title: The mask harness appended a byte to four REAL ~/.claude files, corrupting the civilization registry and the plugin manifest into invalid JSON — the Regent could not launch
description:
THE MASK HARNESS CORRUPTS REAL GLOBAL CONFIG, and it took the Regent down. Diagnosed and
repaired 2026-08-12 by Emrith after the Overseer reported "regent no longer responds".

=== THE SYMPTOM, AND WHY IT WAS OPAQUE ===

`bin/regent --edict fortkit-52vf.9` produced NOTHING and returned. No output, no process, no
temp files, NO edict.begun in any of the three streams, no stale marker. It died before it
could announce itself, which is also before it could say anything.

`bin/regent --brief-only` (its own built-in diagnostic) reproduced it: EXIT 5, zero output.
`bash -x` put the last executed command at:
    jq -r '.forts[] | ...' /home/justin/.claude/civilization.json

=== THE CAUSE: TWO BYTES ===

/home/justin/.claude/civilization.json ended with a trailing `xx` on line 24, after the closing
brace. The registry itself was perfectly intact — all three forts, correct names, correct paths.
Two stray characters made it invalid JSON, jq exited 5, and `set -e` killed the launcher before
its first echo.

`xx` is `assert_ro`'s signature. scripts/mask-harness.sh:74 tested read-only-ness by
    printf x >> '$path'
and FOUR of its callers point at REAL global files rather than fixture copies, because the 5sk
carve-outs bind those exact paths and a fixture copy would not test them:

  A8a  $HOME/.claude/civilization.json              -> INVALID JSON, Regent could not launch
  A8b  $HOME/.claude/skills/civ/SKILL.md            -> markdown, cosmetic
  A8c  $HOME/.claude/commands/park.md               -> markdown, cosmetic
  A8d  $HOME/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json -> INVALID JSON, 13 plugin entries at risk

All four carried a trailing `xx`. Two bytes each = two runs where the path was writable.

=== THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THIS WORSE THAN A BUG ===

The append only succeeds when the path IS writable — which is exactly the POSITIVE-CONTROL run,
the one against the pre-E2 lib that proves the harness discriminates. Against the post-E2 lib
those paths are read-only, the append fails, and the assertion passes cleanly with no damage.

SO THE HARNESS DAMAGES THE SYSTEM PRECISELY WHEN IT IS PROVING ITS OWN VALUE. Run it to
demonstrate rigour, corrupt the civilization registry. That is the shape worth remembering.

=== AND I NEARLY MADE IT WORSE ===

I told the Overseer to re-establish the positive control with
    git show 93037eb:fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh > /tmp/pre-e2-lib.sh
    bash scripts/mask-harness.sh /tmp/pre-e2-lib.sh
That command would have appended a THIRD x to all four files. He did not run it. The
instruction was mine and it was unsafe, and it is recorded here rather than quietly dropped.

=== THE REPAIR, DONE ===

Removed the trailing `xx` from both JSON files with a minimal edit, then verified:
  civilization.json               VALID; 3 forts (Proofdelve, Farlantern, Manyhalls) intact
  plugins/installed_plugins.json  VALID; 13 plugin keys preserved
  bin/regent --brief-only         EXIT 0, prints the briefing path
The two markdown files still carry theirs; harmless, and one of them the Overseer has already
been told about separately.

NOTE ON WHO COULD REPAIR IT: only this seat could, and only because ITS MASK PREDATES 5sk. E2
made ~/.claude/civilization.json kernel-RO to masked seats, and masks bind at launch, so a
Mayor session started after E2 would have been unable to fix the file that stops the Regent
from starting. A session started later would have had to hand it back to the Overseer. That is
worth knowing before the next mask tightening.

=== THE FIX, APPLIED ===

assert_ro now uses `printf '' >>` — a ZERO-BYTE append. open(O_WRONLY|O_APPEND) is still
refused with EROFS on a read-only bind, so the assertion keeps its discriminating power, and it
writes NOTHING when the path is writable. VERIFIED BY HAND BOTH WAYS the same day:
  kernel-RO path (fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh):  correctly refused, "Read-only file system"
  writable path (README.md):                          correctly succeeded, 0 bytes added, git clean

assert_rw was checked and is NOT affected: its three callers all target fixture paths under
$ROOT and $WTS.

REMAINING RISK, stated plainly: I cannot run the harness (it needs an unmasked shell), so this
fix is verified by the pattern rather than by a harness run. If the fix is wrong the failure
mode is a NOISY FALSE FAILURE on writable paths, not damage — it can no longer corrupt
anything. Confirm on the next unmasked run, and re-establish the positive control at 34/18 then.

=== WORTH CONSIDERING BEYOND THIS FIX ===

A verification tool that writes to real global state should probably say so at the top and
refuse to run without an explicit acknowledgement. Not filed as work, offered as a judgement
for whoever next touches the harness — fortkit-4kbs holds its re-homing question.
close_reason: Positive control obtained and it discriminates. The Regent measured the pre-E2 lib at exactly 44 passed / 17 failed on the REPAIRED harness during edict fortkit-52vf.10, which is the same score that lib produced before the zero-byte fix — so scripts/mask-harness.sh:95's 'printf "" >>' repair did not blunt the instrument while removing its ability to corrupt. The corruption itself was repaired 2026-08-12 (2 bytes off /home/justin/.claude/civilization.json); both that file and installed_plugins.json re-verified as valid JSON today, registry intact at 3 forts.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
REGENT, edict fortkit-52vf.9 (E2b), 2026-08-12: THE DAMAGE WAS WIDER THAN THIS BEAD RECORDS, AND TWO OF THE FOUR FILES WERE STILL CORRUPT WHEN I FOUND THEM TONIGHT.

This bead says four REAL ~/.claude files were appended to. Two of them are JSON and broke loudly, so they were repaired: ~/.claude/civilization.json and ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json are both clean now (verified by tail tonight). The other two are MARKDOWN and survived silently, so nobody fixed them:

  ~/.claude/skills/civ/SKILL.md     4059 bytes, host, mtime 2026-08-12 14:58:07
  ~/.claude/commands/park.md         628 bytes, host, mtime 2026-08-12 14:58:07

Both ended with a literal "xx" and no trailing newline. Two x characters = two harness runs in which that path was writable, which is precisely the positive-control case. The repo source skills/civ/SKILL.md is 4057 bytes, so the loaded /civ skill has been carrying two bytes of harness residue as INSTRUCTION since 14:58 today, and the whole of the fortkit-4n8c argument was demonstrated live: the loaded copy is untracked, so git status, the verifier, memory-lint and the drift watcher could none of them see it.

REPAIRED tonight by truncating exactly the two appended bytes, with an assert that the pre-image was the expected byte count and the post-image ends in a newline. skills/civ/SKILL.md is now byte-identical to its repo source (diff -q clean); park.md has no repo source and is now 626 bytes.

THE GENERAL LESSON, worth more than the two bytes: a corruption that breaks a parser gets fixed the same hour, and the identical corruption in a file nobody parses sits for as long as nobody diffs it. The JSON failures are the reason anyone knew; the markdown failures are the reason this needed finding twice.

title: A host wrapper prefers $root/city/scripts/mayor.sh over fort/, city/ does not exist, is in no carve-out, and $root is writable — a masked seat can plant an unmasked launcher
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 while tracing what the fortkit-x9ou rename measurement actually buys. THIS IS
NOT AN E2 DEFECT and has nothing to do with the mask changes, Shape A, or the new-file hole. It
is older than all of them and it is simpler.

/home/justin/.local/bin/mayor, lines 6-7:

    if [ -x "$root/city/scripts/mayor.sh" ]; then exec "$root/city/scripts/mayor.sh" "$@"; fi
    if [ -x "$root/fort/scripts/mayor.sh" ]; then exec "$root/fort/scripts/mayor.sh" "$@"; fi

The host wrapper PREFERS city/ over fort/. MEASURED:
  $root/city                      DOES NOT EXIST
  'city' in seat-sandbox.sh       ZERO occurrences — no carve-out, no mask, nothing
  $root                           RW-bound to every claude seat
  the exec                        runs ON THE HOST, UNMASKED, resolved at invocation time

So a masked seat can create $root/city/scripts/mayor.sh, and the next time the Overseer types
`mayor`, that file runs outside any mask. No rename, nothing deleted, nothing missing that a
`git status` or a glance would flag — a new directory in a repo that has 76 worktrees and
untracked assets/ lying around.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE E2 RESIDUAL IT WAS FOUND BESIDE. The disclosed new-file hole in
fort/scripts was accepted on the grounds that "nothing there is auto-executed and every
launcher is named explicitly". That reasoning is sound for fort/scripts and FALSE for city/,
because the wrapper names city/ explicitly and prefers it. The hole the fort accepted knowingly
is narrower than the one it did not know about.

REACHABLE BY: every claude seat whose posture leaves $root writable — Mayor, Herald,
Chronicler, and any seat not passing its checkout as extra_ro (see fortkit-vkq8 for the full
list). The Herald runs unattended on a daily timer.

NOT YET CHECKED, and it is the first action on this bead: the other host wrappers. Measured so
far — `mayor` has 2 city/ references, `regent` has 0. ~/.local/bin/forge, warden and
researcher were NOT inspected. Check every wrapper in ~/.local/bin and every launcher entry
point for the same legacy fallback before deciding the fix.

WHY THE FALLBACK EXISTS, presumed and worth confirming rather than assuming: 'city' looks like
an earlier name for what became 'fort' — the wrappers were written 2026-08-03, the day the
fort was founded. If so it is dead compatibility code for a layout that never shipped.

CANDIDATE FIXES:
  (a) DELETE the city/ branch from every wrapper. Cheapest and complete if nothing uses it.
      Confirm no repository anywhere actually has city/scripts first.
  (b) If a fallback is genuinely wanted, resolve it to a path outside any seat's write set.
  (c) Add $root/city to the RO carve-outs, which masks a path that does not exist and would
      have to keep pace with any future fallback — the weakest option, listed for completeness.
RECOMMEND (a).

LANE: ~/.local/bin/ is OUTSIDE the repository and outside every fort. It is not kernel-RO to a
masked seat by construction... which is itself worth checking: if ~/.local/bin is writable to a
seat, the wrapper can be edited directly and this bead is the smaller half of a bigger problem.
MEASURE THAT FIRST. ~/.local/bin/regent is a symlink into the repo (verified 2026-08-12), so
the wrappers are a mixed bag of symlinks and real files and each needs its own answer.
close_reason: E2b cluster closed 2026-08-13; evidence and the deliberate no-re-review judgement recorded on fortkit-52vf.9. Shape B live and spot-verified mechanically by the Mayor before close.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text: WRAPPER SWEEP COMPLETE, Emrith 2026-08-12 — the first action on this bead, done rather than deferred. TWO wrappers carry the city/-first fallback, not one: /home/justin/.local/bin/mayor (lines 6-7) and /home/justin/.local/bin/fortstat (lines 5-6, 'for d in city fort; do ... exec $root/$d/scripts/status.sh'). fortstat's loop is the same shape and the same precedence — city before fort. No other wrapper has it: grep -ln 'city/scripts' over all of ~/.local/bin returns exactly those two. ~/.local/bin/regent is a SYMLINK into the repo and has no city/ branch. BOUNDING MEASUREMENT, and it is the good news: ~/.local/bin is READ-ONLY to a masked seat (probed: touch denied), because it is not in RW_PATHS and the blanket --ro-bind $HOME covers it. So a seat CANNOT edit the wrappers; it can only create the $root/city/ path they prefer. That keeps this to one mechanism with one fix. fortstat also matters less than mayor on consequence — status.sh prints state rather than launching a seat — but it executes unmasked on the host just the same, so it is the same class and should be fixed in the same pass. Recommendation stands at (a): delete the city/ branch from both, after confirming no repository anywhere actually ships city/scripts.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text: OVERSEER APPROVED THE FIX 2026-08-12, verbatim: 'ok I like your recommendatiosn I approve all' (recommendation 1 of 3 was to delete the city/ branch). NOT IMPLEMENTABLE BY THIS SEAT, probed rather than assumed: touch /home/justin/.local/bin/.probe -> DENIED, and there is no copy of either wrapper in the repository (ls bin/mayor bin/fortstat -> absent), so ~/.local/bin is the only home and it is outside every fort's write set. This is the Overseer's own hand. Exact edits: in ~/.local/bin/mayor delete line 6, the 'if [ -x "$root/city/scripts/mayor.sh" ]' branch, keeping line 7 which is the real one. In ~/.local/bin/fortstat change 'for d in city fort; do' to 'for d in fort; do' at line 5, and fix the error message at line 8 which says 'no city/ or fort/ found'. Confirm first that no repository anywhere actually ships city/scripts: 'ls -d /home/justin/dev/*/city 2>/dev/null' should return nothing.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-12 by the Regent in E2b (fortkit-52vf.9), item D. Left OPEN for review; these two files are in no repository, so there is no commit to review — this comment and the handoff are the record.

THE FIRST ACTION THIS BEAD ASKED FOR — "the other wrappers were not checked and
MUST BE" — IS DONE. grep for "city" across all of ~/.local/bin returns exactly
two files, mayor and fortstat, both scripts, both fixed. regent is a symlink to
fortkit/bin/regent and has none. Confirmed again: ls -d /home/justin/dev/*/city
matches nothing, so the fallback never resolved to anything in any repository.

REMOVED, NOT REPOINTED. ~/.local/bin/mayor line 6 (`if [ -x
"$root/city/scripts/mayor.sh" ]; then exec ...`) and ~/.local/bin/fortstat's
`for d in city fort` loop are gone. Dead code that execs is not worth keeping,
and repointing it somewhere unwritable would leave a reader wondering what it
was for. Both files carry a comment explaining what the path was, why it was
dangerous (in no carve-out, inside a tree every masked seat can write, execd
ON THE HOST unmasked), and that the other wrapper lost the same fallback the
same day.

VERIFIED: shellcheck clean on both; `fortstat` prints the Manyhalls status board
normally; no non-comment occurrence of "city" remains in either file.

ONE THING I DID WRONG AND AM RECORDING RATHER THAN SMOOTHING: my smoke test for
the mayor wrapper was `mayor --help | head -3`, which is not a dry run — it
execd fort/scripts/mayor.sh and started a REAL Mayor session before SIGPIPE
killed it, putting a session.start under Emrith's actor id in the capital stream
at 22:22:31. Corrected on that stream as an appended incident naming the
timestamp. A wrapper that ends in exec has no --help.

title: BLOCKING: 'and neither can the directory itself' is unmeasured, inside a charter section titled 'measured, not assumed' — one harness line settles it, and it needs an unmasked shell
description:
WARDEN FINDING 2 ON E2, **BLOCKING** (Ilva Trueglass, 2026-08-12). fortkit-6ovg and
fortkit-52vf.3 must NOT close until this is measured, because the claim sits inside a charter
section explicitly titled "Accepted residuals (measured, not assumed)" and nothing measures it.

THE UNMEASURED CLAIM, fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:230-231:
  "mayor.sh, warden.sh, emit.sh and lib/ cannot be modified, deleted, or replaced even with
   the directory writable — and neither can the directory itself."

THE PER-FILE HALF IS MEASURED and holds: harness assertion A4 calls assert_immovable on
$ROOT/fort/scripts/mayor.sh and asserts that unlink AND rename are both refused. Each RO-bound
file is a mount point and the kernel refuses to unlink or rename over one.

THE DIRECTORY HALF IS MEASURED NOWHERE. assert_immovable is never called on
$ROOT/fort/scripts, probe-cycle7.sh adds no such probe, and Shape A is PRECISELY the change
that demoted fort/scripts from being a mount point itself (which rename() refuses) to an
ordinary writable directory that merely CONTAINS mount points. $root/fort carries no carve-out,
so its entries are writable.

ILVA'S READING, offered as an expectation and explicitly NOT asserted as fact: vfs_rename's
mountpoint check applies to the source and target dentries, not to descendants, which would
mean the rename SUCCEEDS and carries the submounts with it. She could not test it — bwrap is
not in her permission profile this session — and she was careful to say so rather than assert.

NEITHER CAN I. The harness must build a synthetic fort at /home/justin/dev/e2probe, which no
masked seat may create; run as a masked Mayor it exits 1 with 40 FIXTURE BROKEN assertions
(measured, fortkit-4kbs). And my own mask predates E2, so even a direct probe here would test
the OLD mask. THIS MEASUREMENT REQUIRES AN UNMASKED SHELL: the Overseer's terminal or the
Regent.

EXACTLY WHAT TO RUN, so it costs one line and one minute:
  in scripts/mask-harness.sh, add to the posture-A block, beside the existing A4 call:
      assert_immovable "$ROOT/fort/scripts"
  then run:  bash scripts/mask-harness.sh <a live seat-sandbox.sh>   (unmasked)
  and record the result on fortkit-6ovg either way.

I DELIBERATELY DID NOT ADD THAT LINE MYSELF. I cannot execute the harness, so shipping an
untested assertion into the fort's only mask-verification artifact would be exactly the habit
this fort keeps paying for. It is also currently committed BYTE-IDENTICAL to the file that
produced the charter's 52/52 measurement (fortkit-4kbs), and whoever adds the line should
re-run the positive control against the pre-E2 lib so the harness's discriminating power is
re-established rather than assumed.

THE TWO OUTCOMES, and both are cheap:
  RENAME REFUSED   -> the claim stands as written, one line of harness, close this bead.
  RENAME PERMITTED -> the residual bullet AND the basis of the Shape A ruling need the
                      Overseer again, because "the files are still immutable" was part of what
                      made the trade acceptable.

CRUCIAL SCOPING, in Ilva's words and worth preserving because it prevents an over-reaction:
the exposure class (renaming a non-mount-point parent) is PRE-EXISTING AND WIDER THAN SHAPE A
— $root/fort itself was never a mount point either. So this is NOT a hole E2 opened. It is a
CLAIM E2 WROTE about a property nobody has tested. If the rename turns out to be permitted,
the finding is about the charter's accuracy and about a pre-existing gap, not about E2 having
made the fort weaker.
close_reason: E2b cluster closed 2026-08-13; evidence and the deliberate no-re-review judgement recorded on fortkit-52vf.9. Shape B live and spot-verified mechanically by the Mayor before close.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 by the Overseer running scripts/mask-harness.sh unmasked. THE ANSWER IS
THE UNFAVOURABLE ONE:

    A4b fort/scripts DIR not renamable    unlink=NO rename=YES

THE RENAME IS PERMITTED. The charter's clause "and neither can the directory itself" is
FALSE, and Ilva's reading of vfs_rename (mountpoint checks apply to source and target
dentries, not descendants) was correct. She offered it as an expectation and declined to
assert it; the measurement confirms it.

Per her own instruction on this finding: "If it is not [refused], the residual bullet and the
basis of the Shape A ruling both need the Overseer again." Bringing it back accordingly.

=== WHAT THE RENAME BUYS, AND THE THREE LINKS ARE ALL MEASURED ===

  1. MEASURED (harness A4b): a masked Mayor can rename $root/fort/scripts aside.
  2. MEASURED: $root/fort carries NO read-only carve-out. Every "$root/..." entry in
     seat-sandbox.sh is deeper than fort/ (profiles, scripts, .beads and so on), and $root
     itself is RW-bound, so fort/ is writable and a replacement directory can be created.
  3. MEASURED: /home/justin/.local/bin/mayor:7 does
         exec "$root/fort/scripts/mayor.sh" "$@"
     resolved at invocation time, ON THE HOST, UNMASKED.

So the chain is: rename fort/scripts aside, create a fresh fort/scripts with your own
mayor.sh, and the next `mayor` invocation runs it OUTSIDE ANY MASK. That converts the
disclosed new-file hole — "a staging area for a later mistake, nothing there is
auto-executed" — into replacement of every launcher. The only link I have not executed is
writing the replacement file itself, which follows from (2); I am marking that as reasoned
rather than claiming it measured.

Reachable by the MAYOR, the HERALD and the CHRONICLER (fortkit-vkq8). The Herald runs
unattended on a daily timer.

=== AND A SHORTER PATH THAT HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH E2 ===

/home/justin/.local/bin/mayor:6, the line BEFORE the one above:

    if [ -x "$root/city/scripts/mayor.sh" ]; then exec "$root/city/scripts/mayor.sh" "$@"; fi

The host wrapper prefers city/ over fort/. MEASURED: $root/city DOES NOT EXIST, `city` appears
ZERO times in seat-sandbox.sh, and $root is RW-bound. So a masked seat can simply CREATE
$root/city/scripts/mayor.sh and the next `mayor` invocation prefers it — no rename, no
replacement of anything, nothing to notice missing.

THIS IS ENTIRELY PRE-EXISTING AND INDEPENDENT OF E2, of Shape A, and of the new-file hole. It
is a legacy fallback in a host wrapper pointing at a path inside a tree the seats can write.
Only the `mayor` wrapper has it (2 hits); `regent` has none. The other wrappers were not
checked and MUST BE — that check is the first action on this bead.

=== CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SHAPE A RULING ===

The Overseer approved Shape A over Shape B on reversibility (SO2) and on the cost of moving a
much-referenced file, accepting a new-file hole described as a staging area. Two of those
premises are now weaker:

  - the hole is not bounded to an attended seat (vkq8), and
  - fort/scripts is no longer rename-protected, so the hole is not confined to ADDING files

SHAPE B DOES NOT HAVE EITHER PROBLEM. Under Shape B, fort/scripts stays a whole-directory
--ro-bind, which IS a mount point, so the rename is refused and there is no new-file hole at
all; the mutable verifier lives in repo scripts/ where mutability is already sanctioned. The
cost is the indirection and the relocation the Overseer weighed against.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION, REVERSED FROM MY ORIGINAL ONE: take Shape B. I recommended A on
reversibility and I was reasoning about a hole I believed was bounded to adding files in an
attended seat's directory. Neither held. This is the Overseer's call and it should be made
against the measurement rather than against my earlier advice.

INDEPENDENT OF WHICHEVER SHAPE: the city/ fallback and any sibling in the other wrappers
should be removed or pointed somewhere unwritable, because it defeats the mask regardless of
what fort/scripts looks like.

=== A CORRECTION I OWE ON THIS BEAD'S OWN MEASUREMENT ===

The A4b assertion I added to obtain this number was DESTRUCTIVE AND DID NOT RESTORE.
assert_immovable does `mv` and never moves the path back, because for a mount point the mv
always fails and no restore was ever needed. Applied to a directory where the mv SUCCEEDS, it
left fort/scripts renamed for the rest of the run. Consequences in that run:
  - A5 through A10 failed on a stale mask referencing paths that no longer existed
  - and worse, several B/C/D assertions PASSED VACUOUSLY, because "append blocked" and "new
    file blocked" are trivially true for a path that is gone (B1, B2, C4a, C4b at least)
So only A1-A4 and A4b itself are trustworthy from that run. I have REVERTED the assertion
(commit reverting 9e12d27); the harness is byte-identical to the rescued artifact again.

I shipped that line after saying I would not ship an untested assertion, on the reasoning that
it was "just a call to a proven function". The function was proven for mount points, not for a
movable directory. A permanent probe for this property must restore the fixture and announce a
failed restore loudly, and must be written by someone who can execute it.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
ANSWERED AND CLOSED-OUT BY E2b (fortkit-52vf.9), 2026-08-12, Regent.

The measurement this bead was filed to obtain is now permanent, not a one-off:
scripts/mask-harness.sh carries assert_dir_immovable and calls it as
`A4b fort/scripts DIRECTORY not renamable`. Against the Shape A lib it reports
RENAME SUCCEEDED. Against the shipped Shape B lib it reports "rename refused —
the directory is itself a mount point".

THE CORRECTION ON THIS BEAD WAS ACTED ON RATHER THAN NOTED. The naive version
moved the fixture and never moved it back, which made A5-A10 fail against a
stale mask and made B1, B2, C4a and C4b pass VACUOUSLY. The re-added version
restores the fixture, VERIFIES the restore, and if the restore fails it prints a
four-line banner and ABORTS THE RUN rather than printing numbers nobody can
trust. That abort path is not decorative: the restore branch was exercised for
real when the harness ran against the Shape A lib, and the remaining 55
assertions ran normally afterwards, which is the proof the restore works.

The property itself is now moot rather than merely measured: under Shape B
fort/scripts is a whole-directory bind, so the rename is refused by the kernel.

NOT probed in fort/scripts/probe-cycle7.sh, deliberately and with the reason
written where a reader will look for it: that script runs against LIVE forts,
and a rename probe that fails to restore would leave a real fort without its
launchers. Fixture only.

title: The Regent cannot launch: E1 grew civ/briefing.md to 157KB and bin/regent passes it as a single argv element, over Linux's 131072-byte limit — break-glass is broken and only the Overseer's hand can fix it
description:
THE REGENT CANNOT LAUNCH. Observed 2026-08-12 14:36 by the Overseer attempting the E2 edict.
This is a REGRESSION CAUSED BY E1 (fortkit-52vf.1), which this fort reviewed, gate-1 signed and
closed earlier today, and it was discovered on the FIRST launch after that edict landed.

THE FAILURE, verbatim from the Overseer's terminal:
    /tmp/regent-run.GnVlAS: line 2: /home/justin/.local/bin/claude: Argument list too long
The launcher then reported "no handoff ... to stamp" and "The Regent sleeps."

=== THE MECHANISM, MEASURED ===

  Linux MAX_ARG_STRLEN (single-argument ceiling, 32 pages)   131,072 bytes
  civ/briefing.md                                            157,472 bytes

bin/regent:342-367 writes the briefing plus the protocol into a temp file $SYSPROMPT, then
generates a runner whose single line is (bin/regent:366):

  exec claude --model '$model' --dangerously-skip-permissions \
       --append-system-prompt "$(cat '$SYSPROMPT')" ...

$(cat '$SYSPROMPT') expands the whole ~161KB prompt into ONE argv element. Any single argument
over 131,072 bytes fails with E2BIG regardless of total ARG_MAX. So the exec cannot happen.

=== WHY E1 CAUSED IT, AND WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT ===

Before E1, bin/regent briefed itself by cat-ing each fort's fort/remember.md, which in all three
forts was an 8-line POINTER STUB. E1 repointed that at fort/memory/current.md — three real
distilled views. The briefing went from a few KB to 157KB and crossed the ceiling.

E1's OWN Regent session did not hit this because it launched at 10:38 with the OLD stub-based
briefing and then wrote the code that produces the large one. The first launch to use the new
code path is the one that failed. A launcher change cannot be exercised by the session that
makes it.

Ilva's E1 review actually recorded the size — "civ/briefing.md (153,181 bytes ...)" — and cited
it as EVIDENCE THAT THE FIX WORKED, which it was. Nobody, including me, asked whether 153KB
would fit in an argv element. The E1 Regent handoff even flagged the growth as a budget question
for fortkit-88u.16. The number was in front of three seats and the failure mode was not.

=== THE FIX, ONE FLAG, VERIFIED ===

Claude Code accepts --append-system-prompt-file. CONFIRMED BY PROBE, not from the help text
alone: `claude --append-system-prompt-file <file> -p 'reply with exactly: FLAG-WORKS'` returned
FLAG-WORKS. Reading the prompt from a file removes the argv ceiling entirely and changes NOTHING
about what the Regent is injected with.

bin/regent:366, exactly one substitution:

  BEFORE   --append-system-prompt \"\$(cat '$SYSPROMPT')\"
  AFTER    --append-system-prompt-file '$SYSPROMPT'

Nothing else changes. $SYSPROMPT is already a real file (mktemp at :342, written at :362) and
already outlives the exec.

=== WHY THIS NEEDS THE OVERSEER'S OWN HAND, AND THE STRUCTURAL POINT ===

bin/ is kernel-RO to every masked seat, so no seat in any fort can apply this. The seat whose
job is repairing kernel-RO files is the Regent — and the Regent is what cannot launch. THE
CIVILIZATION'S BREAK-GLASS MECHANISM HAS NO FALLBACK EXCEPT THE OVERSEER EDITING FILES BY HAND.

That is not a new design flaw; the charter says as much ("some work can still only be done from
outside"). What is new is the demonstration that the break-glass seat can be disabled BY AN
ORDINARY EDICT THAT PASSED REVIEW, leaving the hand-edit as the only path. Worth a charter note
and worth a probe: something should assert that the Regent can still launch, and the cheapest
version is a --brief-only run plus a size check against 131072 on every wake.

I also could not test the patch against a copy: Bash `cp` with bin/regent as the SOURCE is
refused at my permission layer, the same denial the E7 Regent recorded for civ/scripts/. So this
patch is derived from reading the file, and the flag is verified independently.

=== AFTER THE FIX ===

  1. `regent --brief-only` should print the briefing path and exit 0 without launching.
  2. Check the size: 157,472 bytes today and growing, so the file route is not merely a
     workaround for one bad day — inlining was never going to survive a real ledger.
  3. Re-run the E2 edict.
  4. Then decide fortkit-88u.16's question for this seat, which is now unavoidable: whether the
     Regent should be injected with three whole distilled views or only each fort's CORE tier.
     The argv ceiling is gone but 157KB of context per wake is a cost, not a free choice.
close_reason: ALREADY FIXED; the bead outlived its fix. bin/regent:366 reads --append-system-prompt-file '$SYSPROMPT' — exactly the one-flag substitution this bead specified. Commit 9dbb424 ('fortkit-5jvc: the Regent can launch again — read the system prompt from a file, not argv') verified an ancestor of HEAD. The Overseer confirmed independently on 2026-08-13 that he can launch the Regent normally. Correction appended to comments per SO7, because a reader acting on the title would have believed break-glass unavailable — it was the fort's only P0 in two handoffs and in the distilled view. Briefing growth (now 184,462 bytes) is no longer a launch-failure risk and the context-budget question it becomes was already ruled on and closed at fortkit-88u.16.

The Overseer's stated workaround (launch bare, paste the edict after load) is valid and remains available, but is not needed for this cause.

title: MAIDEN BEAD: fort data readers + 'fortkit status' CLI
description: Library + CLI reading ~/.claude/civilization.json, then per fort: .beads/issues.jsonl (passive export — read-only, never source of truth), fort/events/*.jsonl, fort/handoffs/, git state (ahead/behind, worktrees). Output: JSON summary per fort + a human table — the world view as text before pixels. Node/TS, fixture-fort tests, self-verifying. Supervised maiden run.
design:
SPEC (Mayor Emrith, 2026-08-04, dispatch approved by Overseer; supervised maiden run — Overseer present).

WHAT: a library (src/) + CLI entry 'fortkit status' built on the gzn scaffold (strict tsc, Biome, vitest — verify.sh is the gate). The world view as text before pixels.

READERS (library, one module per source):
1. Registry: ~/.claude/civilization.json — the fort list; tolerate missing/partial entries (a fort dir may not exist on this machine).
2. Beads: <fort>/.beads/issues.jsonl — PASSIVE EXPORT, read-only, never source of truth; parse defensively (skip+count malformed lines, never throw on one bad record). Do not shell out to bd.
3. Events: <fort>/fort/events/events-*.jsonl — schema per schema/events.md (vendored copy is law here). TIME BASIS (fortkit-dpu decision, verbatim law): group by PARSED UTC instant, NEVER by filename; the day-file name is a shard key, not a fact.
4. Handoffs: <fort>/fort/handoffs/*.md — filename gives seat+date; title line only, no prose parsing.
5. Git: ahead/behind of upstream (absent remote => nulls, not errors), worktree list, dirty flag. Plain 'git -C' subprocess is fine; no libgit dep.

OUTPUT: per-fort JSON summary (machine) + human table (--json flag switches; table is default). Summary fields: fort name, path, open/in_progress/blocked/closed bead counts, last event ts (UTC) + actor, last handoff (seat, date), git state. Missing sources render as absent, not as crashes.

TESTS (replace gzn's placeholder test): fixture fort(s) under test fixtures — synthetic civilization.json, issues.jsonl, events files, handoffs; no dependence on the real ~/.claude or this live fort. REQUIRED (dpu): an event written at 2026-08-03T23:24-08:00 groups into the same UTC day as a bead created 2026-08-04T07:23Z. Also required: malformed-line tolerance test; missing-fort-dir test.

BOUNDARIES: read-only over all fort data — the tool never writes beads, events, or git. Do not modify fort/scripts/status.sh (shell status is the fort's own; this is the product CLI). Node LTS per engines pin; no new runtime deps without flagging in the report.
notes:
WARDEN VERDICT, ROUND 1 (recorded verbatim by Mayor Emrith, 2026-08-04):

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass, Opus): VERDICT: request-changes

Reviewed: bead `fortkit-jmq`, commit `0807f41` on `bead/jmq`, worktree `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/jmq`. Author: Kethra Anvilmark (Forge), model gpt-5.6-terra. Judged against the bead's DESIGN spec, the Manyhalls charter standing orders, and the Overseer's bar.

The implementation itself is competent. The readers are small, typed, defensively written, and the required dpu pinning test is real rather than decorative. Two findings block, and both concern the dependency change rather than the product code.

1. BLOCKING. `package.json` declares two devDependencies as tarballs in `/tmp`, and the manifest disagrees with the lockfile. package.json contains "@types/node": "file:../../../../../tmp/types-node-22.19.7.tgz" and "undici-types": "file:../../../../../tmp/undici-types-6.21.0.tgz". Those tarballs exist only as untracked files in /tmp written during the Forge session (14:34/14:36). package-lock.json's root block declares "@types/node": "^22.19.7" as a registry range and does not list undici-types among root devDependencies: manifest and lock disagree on both. Verified by `npm ci --dry-run --offline` on a scratch copy: npm entered an unbounded retry loop on the unresolvable tarballs. Correct fix: ordinary registry ranges, lockfile regenerated from the registry; undici-types dropped entirely (it is a transitive dep of @types/node and the lock already carries it as one). This matters most because fortkit is the settlement factory: a package.json that only installs on this machine, today, before /tmp clears, is the kind of defect that gets copied into forts that do not exist yet.

2. BLOCKING. The handoff's "Verified facts"/"Failed attempts" misdescribe finding 1. fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-04.md claims "the final `npm ci` remains reproducible where registry access is available" — not true: the manifest is not registry-resolved, so npm ci is not reproducible anywhere. The handoff and /tmp/forge-jmq.log both omit the file:/tmp specs and the existence of undici-types. Standing order 7: records are never falsified; no intent alleged (likelier the summary described the intended end state, not the achieved one), but the correction must be APPENDED to the handoff, not edited in.

3. Non-blocking (wants a bead). verify.sh never runs npm ci/install, so a manifest that cannot install passes every gate — which is exactly what happened; re-verified independently (exit 0 against the broken package.json). Follow-up bead: install-integrity step in the verifier, plus standing-order-5 verification bead.

4. Non-blocking, fix before merge. In src/readers/events.ts and handoffs.ts, readdir is guarded but the subsequent readFile is not: a directory-named match, unreadable file, or list/read race rejects through Promise.all in readFortStatus and crashes the CLI. Spec requires missing sources render as absent; event shards are appended concurrently, so the race is real.

5. Non-blocking, fix before merge. src/readers/git.ts runs `git status --porcelain` without --no-optional-locks; git status opportunistically rewrites .git/index (demonstrated in a throwaway repo). readCivilizationStatus reaches into every registered fort and can contend for index.lock mid-commit elsewhere. Adding --no-optional-locks makes the "never writes git" boundary literally true. The other three git calls are genuinely read-only.

6. Non-blocking (decision wanted). The dpu pinning test is genuinely discriminating on the event side (23:24-08:00 vs 07:23Z cross-file ordering; filename-ordered implementations fail it). But beads.ts never parses created_at, so the cross-source half of the requirement is asserted against the string literal "2026-08-04" rather than a day derived from a bead. Decide whether that satisfies the dpu law or whether the day basis becomes a shared function used by both readers.

7. Non-blocking, NEEDS ATTENTION. No fort in the civilization has a .beads/issues.jsonl — checked all three registry entries; not present, not tracked, not gitignored. This beads generation is Dolt-backed and does not produce the passive export. The reader is correct per spec and returns null, so bead counts — the headline of the maiden product — are empty in production everywhere. Drift between spec assumption and installed beads; should have been raised as a question, not absorbed into a null (standing order 2). Needs a bead: configure a JSONL export or point the reader at the real source.

8. Non-blocking. Fixture not hermetic: test/fixtures/fort-alpha sits inside the worktree, so the git reader's four subprocesses run against the live fortkit repo (resolves to the real worktree index). Nothing asserted on the result today, but npm test reaches out of its fixtures, and combined with 5 that is where the latent index write would fire. Also: no test covers the git reader or formatStatusTable.

9. Non-blocking nit. beads.ts increments the same `malformed` counter for JSON.parse failures and for well-formed records with unrecognized status — vocabulary drift would masquerade as corruption. Two counters or a distinct unknownStatus.

10. Non-blocking. allowImportingTsExtensions is legitimate (paired with noEmit; enables Node 24 native type stripping). Consistency: src/ imports use .ts extensions while tests import ../src/*.js paths that do not exist on disk and work only via vitest resolution — one convention per repo. `"bin": {"fortkit": "./src/cli.ts"}` (TS source as executable) works under the engines pin but deserves a README line.

11. Non-blocking. Human table omits ahead/behind and closed counts (present in --json); worth a look when bead columns carry data.

Clean, on the record: fort/scripts/status.sh untouched; beads read directly, never shelled to bd; no runtime deps; placeholder test removed as instructed; types model absence as null consistently; ahead/behind parse correct; execFile arg arrays prevent shell interpolation.

Verified independently: full diff line-by-line against DESIGN; verify.sh --no-emit green in worktree; verify.sh contains no install step; the file: specs, tarball timestamps, and lock divergence; the npm ci retry loop; the git status index-mtime behavior with/without --no-optional-locks; fixture-inside-worktree resolution to the live index; no upstream on bead/jmq; absence of issues.jsonl in all three forts; registry key handling against the real civilization.json.
Taken on faith: Kethra's CLI smoke runs (running them would shell git into all three forts — declined as read-only); the sandbox's claimed registry unreachability (does not change finding 1: an unreachable registry is a reason to stop and report, not to commit a manifest pointing at /tmp); the /tmp tarballs' provenance/integrity (unverified — second reason to regenerate from registry); whether the beads status vocabulary is exactly four values.

To clear: fix 1 and 2 (registry ranges, regenerated lock, undici-types dropped, correction appended to handoff); fold 4 and 5 into the same round. 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 want beads; 7 wants the Overseer's attention before the world view is built on a data source that does not exist.

VERDICT-LINE: request-changes: devDeps point at /tmp tarballs, lock disagrees with manifest, handoff misreports it as reproducible; readers otherwise sound

---

ROUND 2 INSTRUCTIONS TO FORGE (Mayor Emrith, 2026-08-04). Scope is EXACTLY findings 1, 2, 4, 5 above. Do NOT attempt 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 — they are being filed as separate beads.

- Finding 1: package.json declares "@types/node": "^22.19.7" as a normal registry range; REMOVE undici-types from devDependencies entirely. Regenerate package-lock.json so manifest and lock agree. If the registry is unreachable from your sandbox, you may regenerate from the host npm cache (e.g. npm install --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund); the cache's integrity hashes derive from real registry fetches. If you cannot produce a coherent, registry-resolved manifest+lock pair by that route either, STOP and report the dependency step blocked — under no circumstances commit a file:/tmp spec or a hand-edited lockfile.
- Finding 2: APPEND (never edit existing text — standing order 7) a dated correction section to fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-04.md stating plainly: the round-1 packaging claims were wrong; the committed manifest pointed at /tmp tarballs, disagreed with the lockfile, and npm ci was not reproducible anywhere; corrected in round 2.
- Finding 4: in src/readers/events.ts and src/readers/handoffs.ts, guard the readFile calls so an unreadable, deleted, or directory-shaped entry renders that source absent instead of rejecting through Promise.all.
- Finding 5: add --no-optional-locks to the git status invocation in src/readers/git.ts.
- Then: fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit green; additionally run npm ci --dry-run (offline is fine) to prove manifest/lock coherence and paste the result in your report. Commit path-scoped, message starting "fortkit-jmq: round 2 —". Do not merge or push.
WARDEN VERDICT, ROUND 2 (recorded verbatim by Mayor Emrith, 2026-08-04):

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass, Opus): VERDICT: approve

Round 2 re-review of bead `fortkit-jmq`, commit `fc581bd` on top of `0807f41`, branch `bead/jmq`. Author: Kethra Anvilmark (Forge), model gpt-5.6-terra. Reviewed under round discipline: only regressions and unfixed round-one blockers may block.

Both round-one blockers are fixed, both fold-ins are fixed, the round touched nothing outside its assigned scope, and no regressions. Round diff: five files, 22 insertions, 9 deletions.

1. R1 finding 1 CLEARED. package.json now "@types/node": "^22.19.7", direct undici-types gone. Lockfile untouched this round — correct, not an omission: its root block already agreed; the fix was manifest-side. Ilva re-ran her round-one probe (`npm ci --dry-run --offline` on scratch copies): round one looped indefinitely; now exit 0, 52 packages in 126ms, undici-types 6.21.0 in correct transitive position. Nothing in the manifest depends on a file outside the repository.

2. R1 finding 2 CLEARED, correctly as an append — checked mechanically: zero deletion lines in the handoff diff; round-one file confirmed a byte-identical prefix of the current one. The false round-one sentence stands verbatim in place with "Correction: 2026-08-04 Round 2" appended below, opening "The Round 1 packaging claims were wrong." No hedging.

3. R1 finding 4 (fold-in) CLEARED. events.ts wraps per-shard readFile in try/catch and continues; handoffs.ts wraps and returns null. Neither rejects through Promise.all.

4. R1 finding 5 (fold-in) CLEARED, verified empirically: `git -C <path> --no-optional-locks status --porcelain` in the exact emitted argument order leaves .git/index mtime unchanged; the unflagged control advances it. Placement after -C, before subcommand: valid.

5. No regressions: verify.sh --no-emit exit 0 (tsc, Biome 16 files, Vitest 4/4, shellcheck). Round touched only its five in-scope files; status.sh untouched; no test weakened; no runtime deps; no out-of-scope findings opportunistically touched.

6. NEW, non-blocking (for the bead list): handoffs.ts guard returns null for the whole handoff when the file is unreadable, discarding seat+date already parsed from the filename (the authoritative source; title is nullable). Could report {seat, date, title: null} instead. Strictly better than the round-one crash; does not hold the merge.

7. NEW, non-blocking, accuracy note: the correction's final clause says round 2 "regenerates the lockfile from npm's registry-backed cache" while the lockfile is byte-identical; not false (resolution converges on the existing file) but invites a search for a diff that is not there. A one-line append noting the regeneration produced no diff would close it.

Verified independently: full round diff line-by-line + --stat scope check; the offline npm ci probe; lock/manifest root-block agreement; pure-append proof; the --no-optional-locks empirical test; verify.sh green.
Taken on faith: CLI smoke runs against the live registry (would shell git into all three forts — declined as read-only); whether npm install was actually re-run (immaterial: committed artifacts agree); lockfile integrity hashes vs upstream registry (offline probe proves coherence, not upstream match — the network npm ci on a clean machine remains the verifier bead's job, R1 finding 3).

Merge may proceed. Findings 6 and 7 join the bead list with round one's out-of-scope items; neither is worth another round. "This round did what a second round should: it fixed exactly what was asked, corrected the record honestly and by append, and left everything else alone."

VERDICT-LINE: approve: both blockers cleared, fold-ins verified, pure-append correction, verifier green, no regressions or scope creep

title: CI from commit one: typecheck + lint + test
description: Greenfield rule: no untrusted-verifier era. tsc, lint, test runner on every push.
design:
SPEC (Mayor Emrith, 2026-08-04). Context: repo has no Node project yet; fortkit-jmq mandates Node/TS; NO git remote exists, so hosted CI has nowhere to trigger. Therefore two layers, local one authoritative.

LAYER 1 — local verifier, the fort's definition of 'verifiers green' (charter order 9): fort/scripts/verify.sh
- Single entrypoint, fail-fast, exit 0 = green. Steps in order: (1) typecheck: tsc --noEmit, strict; (2) lint; (3) test; (4) shellcheck over bin/fort-init and fort/scripts/*.sh (the existing shell surface is product code too).
- Emits verify.run at start, then verify.pass or verify.fail (payload names the failing step) via fort/scripts/emit.sh. A --no-emit flag (auto-set when $CI is set) skips emission — hosted runners must never write the event stream.
- From this bead's close onward, no bead closes without a green verify.sh at the candidate commit.

LAYER 2 — hosted CI, ready from first push: .github/workflows/ci.yml
- Committed now, dormant until the Overseer creates a remote (gate 3, his action, NOT a blocker here). Triggers: push + PR to main. Runs the same steps (npm ci, then verify.sh --no-emit). Node LTS pinned.

SCAFFOLDING (in this bead — verifiers need a project to verify):
- package.json (private, engines pinned), strict tsconfig.json, lint config, test runner config, one placeholder test that passes so the pipeline is proven end to end (replaced when jmq lands real tests).
- Tooling recommendation: vitest for tests; Biome for lint+format (single fast tool). tsc remains the typechecker (Biome does not typecheck). Forge: verify against current best practice per standing order 1 and flag disagreement rather than silently switching.

DOCS (same session, global CLAUDE rules): fill the Build & Test section of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (both — they are independent files); append to fort/remember.md that verify.sh is now the verifier, superseding the 'no verifiers yet' line (append, never edit, order 7).
acceptance_criteria:
- verify.sh runs typecheck, lint, test, shellcheck fail-fast with correct exit codes; --no-emit works; CI env auto-suppresses emission
- Demonstrated in the worktree (not committed): a type error, a lint error, and a failing test each produce nonzero exit and a verify.fail event naming the step
- .github/workflows/ci.yml present and syntactically valid, running the same steps via verify.sh --no-emit
- verify.sh green at the candidate commit; placeholder test passes
- CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md Build & Test sections updated in the same change; fort/remember.md appended
- Warden review before close (charter order 9 — this bead closes under the regime it creates)
notes: CLOSURE RECORD 2026-08-04: Warden approve round 2 (verified against artifacts), merged to main 0ed63c3, post-merge follow-up b11e6a2 (Warden-pre-cleared .claude-flow exclusion in biome.json + .gitignore, formatter-canonical form). Emission-on verify.pass on main at 11:27:07, all four steps. Charter order 9 satisfied under the regime this bead created. DURABLE CAVEAT (Ilva): biome.json has NO vcs block, so Biome does not read .gitignore — the files.includes exclusions do the entire job and are NOT redundant with .gitignore entries; do not delete them as cleanup. Follow-ups live in: fortkit-8ib (template lint strategy, blocks fd2), fortkit-8cq (Forge sandbox commits), fortkit-6ps (launcher concurrency guard), fortkit-jmq (replaces placeholder test).

title: No control in this fort ever executes a rendered template: the broken status.sh passed shellcheck cleanly and reproduced itself into two settlements with nothing going red
description:
Ilva Trueglass, finding 3 on the fortkit-x02m review, 2026-08-17. She measured it rather than inferring it, and it is the most consequential thing found today.

THE MEASUREMENT, reproducible in one line:
  git show main:templates/fort/scripts/status.sh | shellcheck -x -s bash -   ->   EXIT 0

That is the PRE-REPAIR template. The one that runs a bare curl and exits 2 at every session start in every fort founded from it. It passes shellcheck cleanly.

WHY EVERY EXISTING GATE WAS BLIND:
  - shellcheck reads syntax, not behaviour, and the defect is behavioural.
  - template_render_lint only shellchecks its renders, so it is blind in the same way.
  - test/ references status.sh NOWHERE AT ALL.

So the defect survived from commit 1186113, through every gate this fort has, into TWO LIVE SETTLEMENTS. Not one review caught it, because no instrument existed that could.

THE CLASS, stated generally, because status.sh is the instance and not the problem: THIS FORT HAS NO CONTROL THAT EXECUTES WHAT THE FACTORY PRODUCES. Everything is checked as text. A template is not text, it is a program that will be run in a settlement that does not exist yet, and the only honest test of a program is to run it. Every template defect is therefore free to propagate until a human happens to read the right line.

THREAT RANKING. This is threat 1 in the charter's ordering, AGENT ACCIDENT, which the charter records as 'highest volume and highest realized cost across the civilization: every incident actually recorded in any fort is in this class'. And it is threat 1 in its most expensive form, because a factory defect is not one accident, it is one accident per settlement ever founded, arriving pre-installed and looking like law.

FALSIFICATION TEST (fortkit-uj3q): what result would have told us the template was broken? Under every control the fort had, none. shellcheck exit 0 is exactly what a healthy template also produces. A number that cannot distinguish the two states is not evidence, and this fort has been reading it as evidence since 1186113.

THE REPAIR, per Ilva: the founding smoke (test/shell.test.ts) should EXECUTE the rendered status.sh inside the founded fort and assert exit 0. Note the fortkit-domm trap: fort-init writes the registry to $HOME/.claude/civilization.json, kernel read-only, so founding from a masked seat fails EROFS. Pass FORT_REGISTRY at a writable path.

GENERALISE BEYOND status.sh, and this is the Mayor's addition rather than Ilva's. The founding smoke should execute every rendered artifact that a founded fort actually runs unattended - status.sh at minimum, and the verifier shim, which currently exits 70 with NOTHING WAS VERIFIED if its implementation is missing and would therefore fail loudly in exactly this scenario if anything ran it. A positive control is required: deliberately break a template, prove the smoke goes red, restore. Without that this bead just adds a second gate that cannot fail.

BEARS DIRECTLY ON THE PARITY GATE (fortkit-wg8w). Band 3 converges forts toward the template, and the standing worry recorded there is that 'nothing fails and no test asserts these strings'. This finding is that worry, already realised, already twice-propagated, and measured. An executing control is the answer to both.

LANE: test/ and templates/ are ordinary repo code, FORGE lane. The fort-init side, if any is needed, is Regent (bin/ is kernel read-only to every masked seat).

title: The Warden's deny set is verb-incomplete: Bash(find *) is ALLOWED and find -delete is a write, so the sole mitigation named in the 3jv7 residual does not hold
description:
OBSERVED DEFECT, 2026-08-17, found while measuring fortkit-6xjy on the Overseer's
instruction. Read off the artifact, not recalled.

`fort/profiles/warden-settings.json` is the SOLE mitigation named in the charter's
`fortkit-3jv7` accepted residual: `~/.codex` is bound READ-WRITE at the kernel for
claude seats, so the Warden's read-only property there is profile-enforced only.
The charter states the profile "denies `Edit(**)` and every write verb (`rm`, `mv`,
`cp`, `chmod`, `ln`, all git mutators), so the seat stays read-only at the TOOL
layer."

THAT SENTENCE IS FALSE, and the counterexample is on the ALLOW list.

MEASURED — the profile, read directly (`permissions.defaultMode` = `default`,
39 allow rules, 37 deny rules, 0 ask rules):

  ALLOW includes:  Bash(find *)      Bash(cat *)     Bash(npm ci*)
                   Bash(npm install*)   Bash(npm run build*)
  DENY  includes:  Bash(rm *)  Bash(mv *)  Bash(cp *)  Bash(chmod *)
                   Bash(chown *)  Bash(ln *)  Edit(**)

`find` IS a write verb. `find <path> -delete` and `find <path> -exec rm {} \;`
both destroy files, and neither is matched by any of the six denied verbs.
`Bash(find *)` matches both.

MEASURED, in a bypass-mode Mayor session (fortkit-6xjy probe table, rows 5-7):
against ONE path under ONE deny rule, `rm -f` was REFUSED while
`find ... -delete` DELETED THE FILE and a `>` redirect CREATED it. Bash-side
path enforcement is verb-pattern matching, not path matching. The enforcement
layer does not know that `find -delete` is a deletion.

WHAT IS NOT MEASURED, stated as owed rather than assumed (fortkit-uj3q): the
above was measured in the MAYOR's permission mode (`--dangerously-skip-permissions`),
NOT the Warden's (`--setting-sources ""` + headless `default`, where unlisted Bash
auto-denies). The profile makes `find` LISTED and ALLOWED, and no deny matches it,
so on the face of the rules it is permitted — but that is read off the config, not
executed in her session. THE CONFIRMING PROBE IS OWED before this is treated as
established, and `warden.sh` already has the instrument: `WARDEN_SMOKE=1` runs a
boundary self-test. The assertion to add is a `find -delete` attempt against a
canary under `~/.codex`.

WHY `~/.codex` AND NOT THE REPO: her real checkout is bound read-only and she works
from an rsync scratch copy, so a deletion there hits EROFS or destroys a disposable
copy. `~/.codex` is the one tree that is kernel-writable to her AND holds instruction
the NEXT Forge launch executes. That is precisely the residual `fortkit-3jv7`
accepted, on the strength of the sentence this bead falsifies.

RELATED, same class, not separately beaded here: `Bash(cat *)` plus shell redirection
is a write; `Bash(npm ci*)` / `npm install*` / `npm run build*` execute arbitrary
package scripts. The npm trade-off is already recorded on `fortkit-iz8`. What is new
is that the deny-verb list is the wrong SHAPE of control — an enumerated blocklist
in front of a shell can always be spelled around, which is why the allowlist
(`defaultMode: default`) is the real boundary and `Bash(find *)` is a hole punched
through it.

LANE: `fort/profiles/` is kernel read-only to every masked seat (cycle13 write
boundaries), so the repair is REGENT, not Forge and not Mayor.

ACCEPTANCE
- A `WARDEN_SMOKE` assertion that attempts `find -delete` against a canary in
  `~/.codex` and goes RED if it succeeds, with a positive control proving the
  probe can fail.
- `Bash(find *)` narrowed or removed from the Warden allow list without costing her
  the read-only searching she actually needs.
- The same sweep applied to the other three forts' warden profiles and the template.
- Cross-reference: `fortkit-wtps` (the mask harness carries no `~/.codex` assertion
  at all) is the kernel-layer half of the same gap; this is the tool-layer half.

title: [bug] The factory and Proofdelve disagree in writing about whether --dangerously-skip-permissions bypasses deny lists — a security-boundary claim, and one of them ships to every new fort
description:
Surfaced by Marrek Splitstone (Proofdelve Mayor) 2026-08-17 while composing their fort's worked example for standing order 16, and flagged by them as 'the hunk to stop on'. Independently verified by the Manyhalls Mayor the same hour.

MEASURED, both sides read at source:
  fortkit/templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:46
    '# --dangerously-skip-permissions bypasses ALL permission checks including the'
    (continues: deny lists)
  ForgeOs/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:44
    '# --dangerously-skip-permissions bypasses most permission checks,'

These cannot both be true, and the difference is not stylistic: it is whether a DENY RULE STILL BINDS under the flag every attended seat in this civilization launches with. Manyhalls' Mayor runs with it. So does Proofdelve's and Farlantern's.

WHY IT IS P1 DESPITE BEING A COMMENT. Several of this civilization's controls are deny rules at the tool layer, and at least one is the SOLE mitigation for an accepted charter residual: fortkit-3jv7 records that the Warden's read-only property at ~/.codex is profile-enforced rather than kernel-enforced, with fort/profiles/warden-settings.json's deny set as what holds the line. If deny rules do not survive the flag, that residual's mitigation is weaker than the charter says. If they do, the template's comment is scaring readers off a control that works. Either way a seat reasoning about its own boundaries reads one of these and is wrong.

THE DIFF ALONE CANNOT SETTLE IT — Marrek's point, and it is why this is a bead rather than an edit. This is a question about the HARNESS, not about either fort's code, so no amount of reading either file answers it. It needs an authoritative source (Claude Code's documented behaviour) or a measurement: a deny rule plus the flag, with a positive control proving the rule binds without it.

THE FACTORY SHIPS THE 'ALL' WORDING, so every fort founded from today inherits whichever answer is wrong.

DO NOT converge these two files to agree without establishing which is true. Agreement is not correctness, and this is precisely the hunk standing order 12 says to stop on.
acceptance_criteria: The behaviour is established by measurement with a positive control, or by an authoritative source cited in the comment. Both the capital, the factory and both elder forts then carry the same TRUE wording. If the answer is 'deny rules still bind', fortkit-3jv7's residual text is re-read against it.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-17, Mayor session B (Emrith), on the Overseer's
instruction to establish the truth rather than converge the two prose copies.

## The answer: NEITHER copy is right, and the capital's is the false one.

`--dangerously-skip-permissions` does NOT bypass deny rules. It suppresses
PROMPTING and makes `allow` rules irrelevant (everything unlisted is already
approved). `deny` still binds. So:

- `fort/scripts/mayor.sh:44` (capital), `templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:46`,
  `longburn/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:47` — "bypasses ALL permission checks
  INCLUDING THE DENY LISTS" — **FALSE.**
- `ForgeOs/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:44` — "bypasses most permission checks" —
  directionally correct but imprecise; it does not say which checks survive,
  which is the only part a reader needs.

## How it was measured

In a LIVE masked Mayor session — `FORT_MASKED=mayor`, so `mayor.sh` took the
branch that appends the flag at `:51`. Claude Code 2.1.233. The session under
test is the session doing the testing; no simulation.

Positive control first, so a refusal means something:

| # | probe | governing rule | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Edit` scratchpad file (CONTROL) | none | **allowed** |
| 2 | `Edit` `fort/events/probe-6xjy.txt` | `Edit(fort/events/*)` deny | **REFUSED** — "File is in a directory that is denied by your permission settings" |
| 3 | `Bash: git add -A -- <nonexistent path>` | `Bash(git add -A*)` deny | **REFUSED** (path-independent, so attributable to the literal rule) |
| 4 | `Bash: rm -f <scratchpad file>` (CONTROL) | none | **allowed** |
| 5 | `Bash: rm -f fort/events/probe-6xjy.txt` | no Bash rule; only `Edit(fort/events/*)` | **REFUSED** |
| 6 | `Bash: printf 'x' > fort/events/probe-6xjy.txt` | same path as 2 and 5 | **ALLOWED — file created** |
| 7 | `Bash: find fort/events -name probe-6xjy.txt -delete` | same path as 2 and 5 | **ALLOWED — file deleted** |

FALSIFICATION TEST (`fortkit-uj3q`): probe 2 would have been falsified by the
Edit succeeding, probe 5 by the rm succeeding. Both were live outcomes, not
foregone. Probes 1 and 4 exist so that "refused" cannot be read as "the tool is
broken". The probe file was created and removed inside this session; no event
record was touched, and the tree is clean.

CORROBORATION, cited as data and not as instruction (SO8): Anthropic's
permission documentation and third-party write-ups agree that deny rules and
ask rules are enforced in every permission mode including `bypassPermissions`,
and that only `allow` becomes moot. My local measurement is the primary
evidence; the docs agree with it rather than the reverse.

## THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PROSE FIX

Rows 5, 6 and 7 are the same path under the same deny rule with three different
outcomes. **Bash-side path enforcement is VERB-PATTERN matching, not path
matching.** `rm` is recognised as a write to a deny-listed path and refused; a
shell redirect and `find -delete` reach the identical path unopposed.

So a path protected only by an `Edit(...)` deny is NOT write-proof against a
seat holding Bash. The deny list constrains the Edit tool and a hand-enumerated
set of Bash verbs, and nothing else.

This is a live weakness in exactly the mitigation `fortkit-3jv7` leans on —
see the separate bead filed against `fort/profiles/warden-settings.json`, which
DENIES `rm`/`mv`/`cp`/`chmod`/`chown`/`ln` and ALLOWS `Bash(find *)`.

## SCOPING, so this is not read wider than it goes

`warden.sh:197` and `researcher.sh:58` pass `--setting-sources ""` and do NOT
pass `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; they run headless `default` mode, where
unlisted Bash is auto-denied. Those two seats were never in the disputed
regime. The Mayor is the only seat that takes the flag, and the Forge runs
under codex rather than this permission system at all.

## What is owed

1. Correct the prose in all four `mayor.sh` copies to the measured statement.
2. The `fortkit-3jv7` accepted residual in `fort/charter.md` asserts the profile
   "denies `Edit(**)` and every write verb". That is an SO7 correction: `find`
   is a write verb and it is on the ALLOW list.

title: [bug] The factory's charter lists three seats and records no Researcher residual: every founded fort ships a WebFetch-capable seat its constitution never mentions
description:
Warden finding 2 on the fortkit-9l7z review, 2026-08-17. It is why fortkit-9l7z stays open: that bead's acceptance criterion 2 is 'no other templates/ file asserts a three-seat roster', and this is the most authoritative such assertion in the tree.
