title: rw86 + fotv template half: templates/fort/scripts/status.sh carries all three status defects and is where every future fort inherits them
description:
THE FORGE LANE HALF of fortkit-rw86 and fortkit-fotv, filed 2026-08-17 after the B2R2 Regent sitting repaired the three LIVE forts and deliberately left templates/ out of scope. Calder's handoff names the template halves as the whole remaining Band 2 class.

MEASURED THIS MORNING, not inferred from the sitting: templates/fort/scripts/status.sh is 39 lines, has NEVER received either rw86 repair (it still carries the original 'ahead of origin/main' wording and the disarmed drift warning), and ENDS MID-COMMAND on a dangling backslash at line 39.

A fort founded from this factory today is born with a status line that lies about its sync state and a session-start script that exits 2. Both live forts had exactly this until this morning.
design:
PORT FROM THE CORRECTED LIVE FILE. DO NOT RE-DERIVE. fort/scripts/status.sh in this
repo is the reviewed, measured reference; copy its Git and Staging blocks. Re-deriving
is how this file acquired two of its three defects.

DEFECT 1 (fortkit-rw86, and the template never got even the FIRST repair). Template
lines 30-32 are still the original:
    AHEAD=$(git rev-list --count origin/main..main 2>/dev/null)
    echo "  branch: $(git branch --show-current), ${AHEAD:-?} commit(s) ahead of origin/main"
    [ "${AHEAD:-0}" -gt 3 ] && echo "  ⚠ PUSH DRIFT: >3 unpushed commits"
Three things wrong at once: "ahead of origin/main" is FALSE (it measures this clone's
last sync, not the remote); an unreadable ref renders as "?" in the sentence while
${AHEAD:-0} on the next line defaults the SAME unknown to zero and silently disarms the
drift warning; and the && form is used where an explicit if belongs.

DEFECT 2 (fortkit-rw86 second round, Ilva's blocking finding). The live file's SYNCED
line must come across EXACTLY, comment included:
    SYNCED=$(git log -g -1 --format=%gd --date=iso refs/remotes/origin/main 2>/dev/null \
      | sed 's/^[^{]*{//; s/}$//')
%gd, NOT %cd. Under `git log -g` the -g is INERT for %cd, which stays the COMMIT's
committer date, so %cd renders a commit date under a sync label. The live comment ends
"Do not simplify this back" and that sentence is the point of porting it.

DEFECT 3 (fortkit-fotv). THE TEMPLATE FILE ENDS MID-COMMAND. Line 39 is the last line:
    timeout 5 curl -sf -o /dev/null -w "  /api/health: %{http_code} (%{time_total}s)\n" \
a dangling backslash with no URL and no fallback. So curl runs bare, prints
"curl: (2) no URL specified", and the script EXITS 2 at every session start. This is
where the two live forts inherited it (Calder established the provenance from history:
the fort's first ever copy, commit 1186113, already ended this way). Complete it from
the live file's tail.

DISCLOSED RESIDUAL YOU ARE INHERITING, recorded on fortkit-fotv and NOT to be silently
"fixed" here: the ported tail prints "/api/health: 000" before the skipped line, because
curl's -w output is written even on failure. It reads like a measurement that returned
000 when no request was made. ForgeOs is the reference copy and deviating would invent a
fourth variant of the very file the parity gate is converging. If you think it should
change, say so in your handoff and leave it; do not decide it inside this bead.

VERIFY, and the first two are the ones that actually discriminate:
1. shellcheck -x over the template (it is on the verifier's TEMPLATE_SH surface).
2. The template-render lint must stay green: scripts/verify-impl.sh's template_render_lint
   renders every {{TOKEN}} to plain, spaced and EMPTY values and shellchecks the result.
   The spaced pass is why placeholders in test expressions matter here.
3. CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit green.
4. State in your handoff whether the rendered template now exits 0 rather than 2. That
   is fotv's actual acceptance and it is not visible from shellcheck.
acceptance_criteria: templates/fort/scripts/status.sh matches the corrected live fort/scripts/status.sh in its Git and Staging blocks: honest relabel, explicit if/else on ref readability, SYNCED via %gd with the wrapper stripped, and a complete curl command with its fallback. Rendered template exits 0. shellcheck and template-render lint green. CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit exit 0.
close_reason: Forge-built, Warden-reviewed (Ilva, APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS), merged --no-ff in the order 881h -> a355 -> x02m. Post-merge main GREEN: CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit exit 0, 16 files / 190 tests, template-render positive control red as required. All findings recorded or filed; none blocking.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Work produced by **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge ladder rung 1, GPT family), so I applied the anti-vacuity check the fort demands of GPT-family diffs, and it came back clean: `git diff main:fort/scripts/status.sh bead/x02m:templates/fort/scripts/status.sh` shows the ONLY differences between the corrected live reference and the candidate template are the header/banner (identity and `{{TOKEN}}` lines, which MUST differ) and the pre-existing Recent-handoffs block. From `── Git ──` through the closing banner the two files are byte-identical. This is a real verbatim port, not a re-derivation — which was the bead's central instruction and the way the file acquired two of its three defects. Two commits, two files, both in the Forge's lane (`templates/`, `fort/handoffs/`); nothing touched in `fort/scripts/`, `bin/` or `fort/profiles/`. Branch is a clean fast-forward over main. Defects 1, 2 and 3 are all closed: honest "since last sync" relabel, explicit `if`/`else` on ref readability with the unknown state warned rather than defaulted to zero, `%gd` with its "Do not simplify this back" comment intact, and the curl invocation completed with its URL and `|| echo` fallback. The disclosed `000` residual was preserved and declared, as instructed, rather than silently repaired.

1. **NON-BLOCKING — the handoff carries an unreconciled contradiction about verifier state.** "Verified facts" says the verifier "is red solely on all seven `test/seats.test.ts` assertions," and "Open risks" says "The template-render lint is part of the verifier but is not reached after Vitest stops the fail-fast sequence" — i.e. that a bead-listed discriminating check was never demonstrated. Twenty lines below, the launcher-observed block records the same command in the same worktree at 11:28:48 at exit 0, 188/188, with template-render green. My own run agrees. The seat's red was environmental to its session, not a property of the tree, and the handoff's attribution of it to Node v24.14.0 is over-scoped: I ran under v24.14.0 and `seats.test.ts` passed. Nothing here is falsified as an observation and the later, authoritative run is in the same file, so this does not meet the blocking bar — but a reader who stops at "Open risks" concludes an acceptance criterion is unmet. This is the open `fortkit-xtlq` class (handoffs have no supersession mechanism); the launcher appends a green stamp without marking the superseded claim. Worth a comment on that bead rather than a new one.

2. **NON-BLOCKING — two `file:line` citations in "Verified facts" point at comment lines, not the code they name.** `:30` is cited for "the explicit readable-ref branch"; the `if` is at `:53`. `:49` is cited for `git log -g --format=%gd`; that is `:51` (`:49` is the comment's last sentence). `:68` is correct. The substance is true and the cited lines fall inside the block being described, so no reader is led wrong about the artifact — but the schema asks for artifact links, and `read-the-artifact-remember-the-why` makes a file-and-line citation a testable proposition. Small, and worth a bead only if it recurs.

3. **NON-BLOCKING — no control in this fort executes a rendered template, and the bead's two "discriminating" legs are blind to defect 3's whole class.** I measured this rather than inferred it: `git show main:templates/fort/scripts/status.sh | shellcheck -x -s bash -` exits **0**. The pre-repair template — the one that runs bare curl and exits 2 at every session start in every fort founded from it — passes shellcheck cleanly, and `template_render_lint` only shellchecks its renders, so it is equally blind. That is why this defect survived from commit `1186113` through every gate into two live settlements. Nothing in `test/` references `status.sh` at all. This bears on **threat 1, agent accident** — the highest-volume threat in the charter's ordering — in its most expensive form: a factory defect that reproduces itself into every future settlement with no control that goes red. Recommend a bead: the founding smoke (`test/shell.test.ts`) should execute the rendered `status.sh` in the founded fort and assert exit 0. Pre-existing gap, not introduced here, hence non-blocking.

4. **NON-BLOCKING — parity residual, correctly left out of scope.** The template's Recent-handoffs block still diverges from live (no `-maxdepth 1`, `[ "$found" = 1 ]` vs `-eq 1`, a different `while read` shape with a literal newline in the `-printf` format), and line 4 still reads "ForgeOS city status" in a file whose banner is `{{FORT_BANNER}}`. The bead scoped acceptance to the Git and Staging blocks and the Forge held that fence, which is right under SO12's per-hunk rule. But the parity gate is converging this file, so the remainder should be beaded rather than left to be rediscovered.

5. **NON-BLOCKING — for the Mayor's ruling, now more urgent than it was.** `fortkit-fotv` itself records that the Staging section is a Proofdelve concept and that the correct repair for forts with no staging deploy may be to DROP it rather than complete it. This bead forbade deciding that here, and the Forge correctly did not — but the template is precisely where that decision propagates: every fort founded from this factory now ships a hardcoded grep for `docs/azure-staging-runbook.md` and `azurecontainerapps.io`, plus the `000`-before-skip residual. Completing it was the right call for this bead; the ruling should land before the next founding.

6. **NON-BLOCKING, observation — the ported comment carries a Manyhalls citizen's name and Manyhalls bead ids into every future fort's `status.sh`.** I raise it because SO12 is live and I am the name in question. My recommendation is to KEEP it verbatim: SO12's identity rule and seat-lint rule 2 both target Held-by and Personality lines, not provenance in a comment, and the citation is what makes "Do not simplify this back" credible to a stranger in a settlement that does not exist yet. Recorded so the choice is deliberate rather than inherited.

**Verified independently, by execution in my scratch copy:**
- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — **exit 0**, run twice. 16 files / 188 tests passed, both typechecks, Biome clean over 66 files, and `template-render: 10 template scripts rendered in 3 passes and linted clean; positive control went red as required`. The registry and skills-install legs announced SKIPPED (my tree is not a git checkout and is unregistered), which is their designed behaviour, not a suppression.
- `shellcheck -x templates/fort/scripts/status.sh` — exit 0.
- Verbatim-port claim — mechanically, by cross-blob diff against `main:fort/scripts/status.sh`, not by eye.
- The pre-repair template passing shellcheck (finding 3) — measured.
- Branch has no drift from main; two commits, path-scoped, no out-of-lane files.

**Taken on faith or established by reading rather than execution:**
- **"The rendered template exits 0."** My profile refused every spelling that would render and run it (`sed`, `bash <script>`, process substitution, redirection to a scratch file), so I did not reproduce the Forge's smoke. I establish it instead from the full 71-line file: there is no `set -e`/`pipefail`, the only `exit` is the `cd` guard at line 5, and the final command is a plain `echo` banner — so the exit status is 0 whenever `cd` succeeds, including under the render-lint's empty pass. The same structural read explains the old exit 2 (last command was a bare `curl`). Strong, but it is a reading, not a run, and I mark it as such.
- The Forge's in-session red on `test/seats.test.ts` and its Node-24 `promisify(execFile)` diagnosis: not reproducible here and not re-derived; see finding 1.
- `bd` was not run in this posture, per the recorded launch constraint; bead context came from the injected bead and `.beads-export.jsonl`.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — verbatim port confirmed by cross-blob diff, verifier green (188/188, exit 0); 6 non-blocking findings.

title: B2R2: the Band 2 repair sitting — one blocking Warden finding and three records that outlive their corrections
description:
The second and smaller Band 2 Regent sitting. Ilva's covenant-4.5 review of the first sitting (fortkit-wg8w.1) returned REQUEST-CHANGES on one finding, and raised three more that live in the same kernel-read-only files. All four are collected here because they are one attended sitting over bin/fort-init and fort/scripts/, not four dispatches.

ITEMS: fortkit-rw86 (the blocking one, three live forts) - fortkit-obva - fortkit-mm7m - fortkit-qfnf.

This is the last thing standing between the Band 2 sitting and its closure. fortkit-wg8w.1, fortkit-0po6, fortkit-naju, fortkit-ugw4 and fortkit-rw86 cannot close until the blocking finding is repaired and re-reviewed (SO9).
design:
READ THE CORRECTION COMMENT ON EACH BEAD BEFORE THE BEAD. Item 1's subject bead
(fortkit-rw86) describes its own defect wrong: the correction dated 2026-08-17 is the
accurate text. Where bead and file disagree, THE FILE IS RIGHT.

SEQUENCING: item 1 first and alone if time is short. It is the only blocking item and the
only one that reaches two other forts. Items 2-4 are independent of it and of each other.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ITEM 1 - fortkit-rw86 correction. BLOCKING. THREE LIVE FORTS.

DEFECT, measured twice independently (Ilva 2026-08-17 blocking finding 1 on wg8w.1; Mayor
re-measured the same morning):
  fort/scripts/status.sh:42
    SYNCED=$(git log -g -1 --format=%cd --date=iso refs/remotes/origin/main 2>/dev/null)
  Under `git log -g`, %cd is STILL THE COMMIT'S COMMITTER DATE. The reflog entry's own time
  is %gd. THE -g IS INERT FOR THIS VALUE, which is the whole finding:
    -g %cd    2026-08-13 22:17:58 -0800
    -g %gd    origin/main@{2026-08-13 22:18:05 -0800}
    no -g %cd 2026-08-13 22:17:58 -0800     <- identical to the -g form
  So the line renders a commit date under a sync label. Gap: 7s here, 3m39s in one of
  Ilva's rows, UNBOUNDED under git fetch.

FIX, MEASURED IN THIS REPO BEFORE BEING WRITTEN DOWN rather than proposed:
    SYNCED=$(git log -g -1 --format=%gd --date=iso refs/remotes/origin/main 2>/dev/null \
             | sed 's/^[^{]*{//; s/}$//')
  Output: `2026-08-13 22:18:05 -0800` - same shape the line prints today, so no other line
  changes. Ilva's alternative is equally acceptable: keep %cd and RELABEL it
  `tip committed <ts>`. Either closes the finding; do not do both.

  DEGRADATION IS ALREADY CORRECT AND MUST STAY THAT WAY: an unreadable ref exits 128 to
  stderr, 2>/dev/null swallows it, SYNCED is empty, and ${SYNCED:+ (synced $SYNCED)} omits
  the clause. A FRESH CLONE HAS NO REFLOG FOR origin/main and will therefore print no
  synced clause at all. That is honest and is not a regression - verify it rather than
  assuming it.

  POSITIVE CONTROL REQUIRED. A green here proves nothing unless the OLD and NEW commands
  return DIFFERENT values in the tree you test. If they agree, you have measured a repo
  whose last push happened to be its tip's commit, which cannot discriminate the property.
  Pick a fort where they differ, or make them differ.

SCOPE: three LIVE copies - fortkit, ForgeOs, longburn. The templates/ half belongs to
fortkit-rw86's Forge lane and is EXPLICITLY NOT IN THIS SITTING; note in the handoff that
it must be written FROM THE CORRECTED CODE, because the class is otherwise one Forge pass
from the factory and from every fort founded after it.

RECORDS OWED (SO7, and this is half the item): the correction is already appended to
fortkit-rw86 by the Mayor 2026-08-17. STILL OWED:
civ/handoffs/regent-2026-08-14T100235.md, which asserts 'the reflog sync time' and is the
Regent's own record to correct. Commit 150f4b7's message cannot be edited; the bead comment
is its correction of record.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ITEM 2 - fortkit-obva. bin/fort-init:38-41 attributes a narrowing to fortkit-4wlz, which

I have completed my review. Here is my record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Model that produced the work:** the Regent, Calder Sealbroken (they/them), Claude Opus 5 — `model_source: launcher --model flag (never self-reported)` on the `edict.begun` event, Overseer present throughout. Frontier, attended, no reward-hacking flag on the rung. I weighted scrutiny normally and re-ran every claim my posture allowed; each one held, including two the sitting recorded against itself.

**Gate check.** Human gate 1 (`fort/` files, launchers) requires Warden + Overseer review. The Overseer's half is on the record (bead comment, three commit messages, `edict.begun`); this review is the other half. No charter, seat file or covenant text changed in the range, so no mandatory-ESCALATE area is touched. Round one; the wg8w.1 blocking finding is repaired.

**The blocking finding is closed and I re-ran the control myself.** Six git invocations across three forts, and the third column is the one that discriminates:

| fort | `-g %cd` | `-g %gd` | no `-g` `%cd` |
|---|---|---|---|
| fortkit | 22:17:58 | 22:18:05 | 22:17:58 ← identical to `-g %cd` |
| ForgeOs | 22:15:50 | 22:15:55 | 22:15:50 ← identical |
| longburn | 22:16:06 | 22:16:11 | 22:16:06 ← identical |

Byte-identical to what the bead, the commit and the SO7 correction claim. No fort is the degenerate case. The repaired pipeline yields `2026-08-13 22:18:05 -0800` — same shape, one field changed.

---

**FINDINGS**

**1. NON-BLOCKING — `%gd` is when `origin/main` last *moved*, not when this clone last fetched.** A `git fetch` that brings nothing new writes no reflog entry, so a seat that fetched this morning and got no new commits still reads a days-old `(synced …)`. This is strictly better than a committer date and is inherent to the deliberate no-network-call design recorded four lines above it, but the label still slightly overclaims. Worth a bead against `fortkit-rw86`'s open second half (the real push-drift watcher), not a round.

**2. NON-BLOCKING — the ported staging tail now prints a health measurement the capital never took.** `fortkit` has no `docs/azure-staging-runbook.md`, so the URL is the bare path `/api/health`, and per the Regent's own disclosed residual (measured in longburn on byte-identical code) curl's `-w` writes `/api/health: 000` before the `(health check skipped…)` fallback. Two lines at every wake, one of which reads like staging returned 000. The trade is still clearly positive — exit 2 → 0, and the script now ends on an `echo` rather than a dangling `\`. `fortkit-fotv` is open and already carries the point the Regent correctly declined to decide unilaterally: for a fort with no staging deploy the right repair is probably to drop the section, and that is the Mayor's call. Keep it on that bead.

**3. NON-BLOCKING — `fortkit-qfnf`'s repair leaves no control behind, and one already exists to hang it on.** The escaping was proven by throwaway foundings that no longer exist; nothing in the suite would go red if `sed_rhs` were simplified away. `test/shell.test.ts:175` already founds a real fort on every run (it executed in my run — 0 skipped), with purpose `"Smoke test fort."`. Changing that one string to contain `&`, `|` and `\` and asserting the rendered charter turns acceptance criterion 5 into a permanent gate at zero cost. This fort's own doctrine says both halves are required; this is the missing half.

**4. NON-BLOCKING — no automated test exercises any *live* launcher's in-mask refusal.** `test/mayor-launcher.test.ts:19` loads `templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh`. The Regent found this, said so plainly, and substituted a 15/15 runtime probe with a per-fort vacuity control — the right response in the moment, but the probe leaves nothing behind and `fortkit-mm7m` will close. Bead the coverage gap so the marker change is guarded by something that can go red.

**5. NON-BLOCKING — `schema/events.md` documents no `edict.*` category at all.** `edict.begun` / `edict.applied` / `edict.ended` are in all three streams and are the Regent's entire announcement machinery; the charter names that file canonical and categories add-only. I searched the export: no open bead covers it. The Regent flagged it and correctly did not edit a vendored file mid-sitting. File it.

**6. NON-BLOCKING — record precision, in the fort's favour.** The sitting index and the handoff both say "shellcheck -S warning clean on all nine touched shell files." Eleven shell files were touched (fortkit 5, ForgeOs 4, longburn 2). I ran ShellCheck on all eleven — `-S warning` and default severity — and every one is clean, so the coverage claim is true and the count understates it. Worth an errata line for a fort that treats numbers in records as testable propositions.

**7. NON-BLOCKING, and stated so Band 2's closure is not misread — the factory still ships all three defects.** I confirmed `templates/fort/scripts/status.sh` still ends on the dangling backslash and `templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:56` still carries `export FORT_MASKED=1`. Correctly out of this sitting's scope, disclosed in the commit, the handoff and on `rw86`/`fotv`/`mm7m`, each with the standing instruction that the template half be written *from* the corrected live code. A fort founded today is still born with all three. Band 2 is not the factory being fixed; it is the live copies being fixed.

---

**WHAT I VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY**

- The `%gd` positive control in all three live forts, plus degradation: an unreadable ref exits 128 to stderr with empty stdout (swallowed, clause omitted), and a reflog-less object returns empty at exit 0.
- The repaired pipeline's output, via a hex-escaped spelling of the identical sed — my profile refuses the literal `s/^[^{]*{//; s/}$//`.
- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in cwd: **exit 0, 187 tests / 16 files, 0 skipped** — identical to the record. The founding smoke was among the tests that ran, so `bin/fort-init` executed end to end under the new `render_stream`.
- ShellCheck clean on all eleven touched shell files across the three forts.
- `seat-sandbox.sh:519` is `mask+=(--clearenv)` and `FORT_MASKED` is in none of `mask_env`'s passthrough lists — the removed export was genuinely dead, and the `--setenv` is appended after `--clearenv`, so the marker survives.
- `mayor.sh:11` tests `-n`, so the legacy `1` still refuses; `test.each(["mayor","forge","warden","1"])` still covers it; all three forts now speak one dialect with no host-side export.
- The `obva` attribution against the export: `fortkit-4wlz` is OPEN, states two `.ssh`/`.aws` lines, three options and a recommendation, and holds no rule; `fortkit-0po6` carries both the mis-description and the Overseer's shape-(a) ruling narrowing it to `{{REPO_PATH}}`. The corrected comment is accurate on the record.
- `fotv`'s provenance: `1186113`'s `status.sh` — the fort's first ever copy — already ended on the dangling backslash. Not a truncation incident.
- The SO7 correction is appended, never edited in, and its three timestamp pairs match my own measurements.
- `bin/fort-init` has exactly one sed substitution site; the registry write uses `jq --arg`.

**WHAT I TOOK ON FAITH**

- The elder forts' verifier runs (longburn 255/6 skipped; ForgeOs 155/0 with Docker up). I cannot run another fort's verifier from this posture, and doing so would write in their trees.
- The fresh-clone measurement end to end (criterion 2). I have no write access to make a clone; I verified the mechanism only.
- The two hostile foundings (criterion 5). I cannot run `bin/fort-init`, and my profile refuses the sed spellings needed to round-trip `sed_rhs` through `s|…|…|g`. I did execute the escaping half — `Salvage & repair | back\slash` → `Salvage \& repair \| back\\slash` — and confirmed `\&` yields a literal `&` in a replacement; the `\|` and `\\` round trips I read rather than ran.
- The 15/15 live-launcher runtime probe, the gated `os.replace` install path, and the `000` line in the capital's staging output (curl is refused by my profile; carried from the Regent's measurement of identical code in longburn).
- `bd` cannot run in this posture; all bead reasoning is from `.beads-export.jsonl` taken at launch.

This is the strongest record I have reviewed from this seat: the finding was restated as an experiment rather than an argument, the positive control was demanded before the green was believed, a scope claim was measured and reported before being acted on, and two of the sitting's own errors are written down where the next reader will meet them. Nothing here makes the fort worse than not merging.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: rw86 blocker closed, %gd control re-run in all 3 forts, verifier 187/16 green; 7 non-blocking findings.

DEPENDENCY GRAPH CORRECTED BY THE MAYOR, 2026-08-17. Recorded because changing the shape of the record is itself a change to the record.

WHAT I FOUND. Closing the two merged template halves failed:
  cannot close fortkit-a355: blocked by open issues [fortkit-wg8w.2]
  cannot close fortkit-x02m: blocked by open issues [fortkit-wg8w.2]

The graph held: a355 -> wg8w.2 -> mm7m, and x02m -> wg8w.2 -> rw86. But a355 IS mm7m's template half and x02m IS rw86's and fotv's. So mm7m could not close until a355 closed, a355 could not close until wg8w.2 closed, and wg8w.2 could not close until mm7m closed. A deadlock in three hops.

bd dep cycles reported NO CYCLE, correctly. The loop was never in the edges. It ran through a fact no edge encoded — that a355 discharges mm7m — so the graph saw a chain where reality had a ring. Worth noting for anyone who trusts that command as a completeness check: it proves the edges are acyclic, not that the WORK is.

WHAT THE EDGE MEANT vs WHAT IT SAID. 'a355 depends on wg8w.2' recorded a real MERGE-ORDER constraint (the sitting's live repairs land before the template halves) and that constraint was honoured: dbaeb3e preceded both merges. But bd models a satisfied dependency as a CLOSED one, and wg8w.2 could not close for reasons of its own. So a constraint that had already been met went on blocking.

  ADDED    fortkit-mm7m depends on fortkit-a355
  ADDED    fortkit-rw86 depends on fortkit-x02m

  bd dep cycles after: no cycles.

The new edges say what is actually true: a parent defect is not discharged until BOTH its live repair and its template half have landed. Closure now runs bottom-up (template half -> parent defect -> sitting) instead of top-down, which is the direction the work actually flows.

THIS BEAD IS NOT CLOSED and I did not close it. It still depends on rw86 and mm7m, and those need their own assessment rather than a cascade — rw86 in particular has an open second half (fortkit-f3i1: git ls-remote fails from a masked seat, so the fort still cannot answer 'are we behind' from inside), and fotv now carries a Mayor ruling to DROP the Staging block from the template, which is follow-on work rather than a discharge. title: Seat-file lint in the fort verifier: actor-id collisions, foreign citizens and unfilled placeholders, checked at every roster edit rather than once at founding
description:
REHOMES the enforcement half of fortkit-8rh and fortkit-fd2, on the Overseer's 2026-08-14 ruling that bin/fort-init grows a SEAT ROSTER ONLY: seats, no personhood, no names, no pronouns, no personalities.

WHY THE FACTORY CANNOT HOLD THESE CHECKS.
Both beads were written assuming fort-init handles a roster. It does not, and after the seat-roster ruling it deliberately never will. fort-init founds every seat EMPTY and the moot is a manual step afterward (bin/fort-init:194-195). A seat-only roster's ids are mayor/forge/warden/researcher: a closed factory-controlled vocabulary with no distance-1 pairs and no user input to get wrong. So at founding there is NOTHING for fortkit-8rh to check.

AND THE FACTORY IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT ANYWAY. fortkit-8rh asks for the check 'at fort founding AND at every roster edit'. fort-init runs ONCE per fort. Roster edits happen forever afterward, at every moot, every reseating, every seat added. A lint in the fort's own verifier runs every session in every fort, which is the requirement the bead actually wrote down.

THREE RULES, ONE INSTRUMENT, over fort/seats/*.md and the charter's occupants line:
 (1) NO ACTOR-ID COLLISION WITHIN THE FORT at Levenshtein distance 1, case-insensitive: HARD REFUSE. Distance 2: WARN. Overseer ruling on fortkit-8rh 2026-08-13, verbatim: 'I agree with your recommendation. kind of similar names in different forts are fine.' The collision that matters is WITHIN one roster, which is where kestra/kethra sat. CROSS-FORT near-collisions are explicitly fine and must NOT be refused: oswin (civ) and orin (Farlantern Forge) sit at distance 2 in a roster the civilization already runs. Cross-fort rendering is fortkit-aam's concern.
 (2) NO FOREIGN CITIZEN'S NAME in this fort's seat files. The identity half of standing order 12. Note the legitimate exception: attribution comments crediting another fort's seat for a finding are provenance, not inheritance (two live examples in templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:127,455 crediting Ilva Trueglass). The rule is about the Held-by and Personality fields, not about citations.
 (3) NO SURVIVING {{UNFILLED}} PLACEHOLDER once the moot has been held.

THE PRE-MOOT EXEMPTION FOR RULE 3, and the signal already exists rather than needing to be invented: bin/fort-init:177 writes the fort into the registry with "fort_name": null, and the moot sets it. Verified 2026-08-14 against ~/.claude/civilization.json: ForgeOs=Proofdelve, longburn=Farlantern, fortkit=Manyhalls, all three named. fort_name null means pre-moot and placeholders are LEGAL; fort_name set means placeholders are a FAILURE. A correctly founded fort must pass this lint on day zero while still full of placeholders.

LANE, and it is the point of rehoming: scripts/verify-impl.sh is MAYOR-WRITABLE and kernel read-only to the Forge by explicit carve-out (cycle 13, fortkit-52vf.9). So this is NOT Regent work and needs no privileged sitting. It travels to every fort the way fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs already does.

RELATED: fortkit-be4 will eventually give actor ids an explicit field separate from display name; until then rule 1 reads the Held-by line. This lint is where be4's field lands when it exists.
design:
Precedent to follow: fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs, which already travels with every fort and is invoked from the verifier. Same shape.
Wire into scripts/verify-impl.sh (Mayor-writable), NOT fort/scripts/verify.sh (read-only shim since cycle 13).
Fixtures required, and rule 1 needs a positive control or it is not evidence: a colliding roster fixture that MUST fail, a distance-2 fixture that must WARN and not fail, a pre-moot fixture (fort_name null, placeholders present) that must PASS, and a post-moot fixture with a surviving placeholder that must FAIL.
Open question for the implementer: the charter's occupants line and fort/seats/*.md both carry identity and can disagree. Decide which is authoritative and say so in the lint's own output, or check both and refuse on disagreement.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A roster with two actor ids at edit distance 1 fails the verifier. 2. A roster at distance 2 warns and passes. 3. A freshly founded fort (fort_name null, every seat file full of {{UNFILLED}}) PASSES. 4. The same fort with fort_name set FAILS until the placeholders are replaced. 5. A seat file carrying another fort's citizen name in its Held-by or Personality field fails, while an attribution comment naming another fort's seat does not. 6. All five covered by fixtures; the failing cases proven to fail.

Round-1 blocker was mine and is corrected on the record under SO7. Carried findings filed as fortkit-ihwu, fortkit-e69p, fortkit-m2tj, fortkit-upvo. Discharges the enforcement half of fortkit-8rh and fortkit-fd2.

  — rules 2 and 3 SKIPPED (found 3 fort(s), none matching this repo)
```

`expect(result.stdout).toContain("rule 3 enforced")` can only hold if the checkout the test happens to be running in is listed in `$HOME/.claude/civilization.json` **with a non-null `fort_name`**. That is ambient machine state. The lint itself behaves correctly here — it takes the announced skip, exactly as `scripts/seat-lint.mjs:130-136` says it will for my scratch — so the file's own comment predicts the environment in which its test then fails.

Two environments, one measured and one derived:

- **Measured:** the Warden's review scratch. Every future Warden review of every future bead in this fort begins with a red verifier for a reason unrelated to the diff under review. That is standing order 9's gate turned into noise, and it is the same class as the incident already in the ledger — `h5i`, 2026-08-08, "couples to ambient git state differently across the three environments that all showed green pre-merge."
- **Derived, not executed (I cannot run a GitHub runner):** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:29` runs `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` on every push to `main` and every PR. A runner has no `~/.claude/civilization.json` at all, so `registry` parses as `null`, the lint emits the "registry unreadable — rules 2 and 3 SKIPPED" note, and the same assertion fails. I am confident in the derivation because it is the identical code path I *did* execute, reached by a different branch of the same `try`.

The commit message's "**CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit: exit 0, 16 files / 187 tests**" is the `fortkit-px7e` shape: true in the author's environment, false in a masked seat's and on the runner, stated unconditionally in a durable record. The counts (16 files, 187 tests, was 15/180) are accurate; the exit code is conditional. A correction belongs on the bead per SO7.

**The remedy is small and the machinery is already in the diff.** `buildCivilization`/`lintFort` already prove the FORT_REGISTRY path works. Point the live-capital test at a scratch registry whose single entry is `repositoryRoot` with a set `fort_name`: rule 3 then enforces against the *real* roster deterministically in every environment, rule 2 checks against zero siblings, and the assertion measures the code instead of the disk. Keep `toContain("charter cross-check")` as-is — that line is environment-independent and passes everywhere today.

Related and worth stating plainly, because it constrains what that test can ever assert: **rules 2 and 3 are structurally unenforceable in GitHub CI.** No registry, no sibling forts. The shared gate enforces rule 1 and the charter cross-check; rules 2 and 3 are enforced only on a machine that hosts the civilization.

### 2. NON-BLOCKING — the lint does not travel; a fort founded today gets none of it

The bead's stated reason for this lane is "it travels to every fort the way `fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs` already does." This diff touches neither `templates/`. Precisely:

- `templates/fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs` exists. There is no `templates/` counterpart for `seat-lint.mjs` at all.
- `templates/scripts/verify-impl.sh:73-79` runs `typecheck lint test shellcheck` — it wires neither memory-lint nor seat-lint.

So the gap seat-lint inherits is *larger* than memory-lint's: memory-lint at least ships as a file. Placing the capital's copy at `scripts/seat-lint.mjs` is right — it matches where the capital's own memory-lint sits — so this is a missing template half, not a misplacement. Also note the live/template `verify-impl.sh` divergence is the kind of thing `drift-watch` reports as a propagation gap (9 open in this morning's scan). Bead it against the parity programme; do not hold the merge for it, since merging gives the capital the lint and not merging gives nobody it.

### 3. NON-BLOCKING — the rule as ruled would not have caught the collision that motivated it

`kestra`/`kethra` — named in `fortkit-8rh` and in this bead as *the* collision the rule exists for, and the reason this seat is called Ilva — is at edit distance **2**, so it WARNS and passes. The implementer found this while writing the fixture, wrote it down at `test/seats.test.ts:104-113`, and put the pair among the WARN cases where the ruling puts it rather than bending the threshold to make the story come out right. That is the correct handling and I want it on the record as such.

Two caveats. First, the Overseer should see this explicitly: the distance-1 refuse threshold, faithfully implemented, would not have prevented the fort's own founding scar. Second, the comment claims "Escalated to the Overseer on `fortkit-8rh` rather than resolved here" — **I could not verify that escalation.** The export at `.beads-export.jsonl` carries `_type:"issue"` records only, no comment bodies (453 issues, 0 comments), `fortkit-x508` shows `comment_count: 0`, and `bd` cannot run in this posture. Not asserted as false; asserted as unverified from where I sit.

### 4. NON-BLOCKING — civilization seats are outside rule 2's roster

The foreign roster is built from `registry.forts[].repo + /fort/seats`. Civilization citizens — the Regent, the Herald, Oswin — live in `fortkit/civ/seats/`, which no fort entry points at. A seat file whose Held-by named the Regent would pass rule 2. Covenant section 4's "never emits as one of this fort's citizens" is the same law in the event stream that standing order 12 is in the roster; the lint covers one and not the other. Bead.

### 5. NON-BLOCKING — a duplicate registry entry makes a fort foreign to itself

`scripts/seat-lint.mjs:155-160` resolves this fort's entry through `realpath`, but the rule-2 self-skip at line 180 compares the raw string `fort.repo === entry.repo`. If the registry ever lists one repo under two spellings (a symlink, a trailing slash), the other spelling becomes a "foreign fort" whose citizens are this fort's own, and every seat file hard-fails. The loop also has no `break`, so last match wins. The canonical path is already computed one scope up; comparing it in the self-skip closes this. No observed occurrence, so per SO11 this is an observation with a cheap fix, not a hardening demand.

### 6. NON-BLOCKING observations, no bead requested

- Rule 2 matches the bare given name on word boundaries. Today's names are invented and the risk is latent, but a foreign given name that is also an ordinary word would produce a false red in a Personality line. Worth a line of comment when someone next touches the file.
- This fort's verifier result is now partly a function of *other repositories' working trees*, uncommitted edits included. A reseating underway in Proofdelve can move Manyhalls' gate with nothing in this repo changing. This is inherent to rule 2 as specified, and rejecting the hardcoded list was right — I record it as a property, not a defect.
- Test fixtures leave `mkdtemp` directories behind in `/tmp`. Cosmetic, and consistent with the existing suite.
- The three `fatal: not a git repository` lines in the full verifier run are **not** from this diff: the isolated `npx vitest run test/seats.test.ts` produces none. Pre-existing noise from other files.

### What is good here, and it is most of it

Every acceptance criterion has a fixture and the failing cases are proven to fail (1: synthetic `kethra`/`kelhra` at distance 1, exit 1 · 2: both live distance-2 pairs pass with the warn on stderr · 3 and 4: the same tree read against two registries · 5: inheritance refused, attribution in the body allowed · plus an empty-roster anti-vacuity failure). Zero seat files is a FAILURE rather than a pass, and the registry degrades to an *announced* skip — the file's header names `fortkit-52vf.12` finding 4 and `fortkit-vhk.5.1` finding 8 as the scars that taught it. The worktree-to-canonical resolution is the `verify-impl.sh:136-147` lesson applied rather than relearned. The bead's open question is answered in one direction and **the declined direction is printed in the lint's own output**, so no reader mistakes it for coverage. And the two `bin/fort-init` citations in the code are exact — `:223` is the `FORT_REGISTRY` read, `:226` is the `fort_name: null` write — where the bead's own older line numbers had drifted. That is the artifact being re-read rather than remembered.

No gate-1 trigger: the diff touches `scripts/` and `test/` only, no `fort/` path, no charter or seat file. No mandatory-ESCALATE area. No threat-model finding in any of the above; nothing here bears on agent accident, injection, supply chain or credential leakage beyond the verifier-reliability point in finding 1, which is threat 1 (a red gate that everyone learns to read past is how an accident gets merged).

---

**Verified independently:** `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in cwd (RED, 1/187, the failure quoted above) · `npx vitest run test/seats.test.ts` in isolation (1 failed / 6 passed, and no `fatal:` noise, which is how I attributed that noise elsewhere) · typecheck, browser-typecheck and biome all clean in the same verify run · `shellcheck -x scripts/verify-impl.sh` clean, run separately because the aborted verify never reached its shellcheck step · the scratch is not a git checkout (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` → fatal) and is not in the registry, which is the mechanism of the failure · `bin/fort-init:223`, `:226`, `:68` read at source · `templates/scripts/verify-impl.sh:73-79` and the absence of any `templates/` seat-lint file · `.github/workflows/ci.yml:29` · the capital's four seat files carry no `{{` and all four names appear in `fort/charter.md`, so rule 3 and the charter cross-check would pass there.

**Taken on faith:** the commit's positive control (a scratch registry whose sibling claims Emrith turning the real verifier red at the seat-lint step) — I could not run `node scripts/seat-lint.mjs` directly, my profile refused it, and the synthetic fixture in `test/seats.test.ts` proves the same mechanism · rule 2 against the *real* Proofdelve and Farlantern rosters, whose trees are outside my working directories · the claimed Forge-worktree measurement (3 seats there, 4 in main) · the claimed escalation on `fortkit-8rh`, per finding 3 · the CI-runner failure in finding 1 is derived from an executed code path, not executed on a runner, and I mark it as such.

VERDICT-LINE: REQUEST-CHANGES: test/seats.test.ts asserts ambient registry state — verifier RED in the Warden's scratch and on CI; 5 non-blocking findings.

I have everything I need. Writing the review record.

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Round 2.** Round-one discipline applies: only regressions and unfixed round-one blockers may block. My single round-one blocker is fixed, I measured the fix in the exact environment that was red, and I found no regression in the delta.

**Provenance.** Mayor lane, as the bead rehomed it: `scripts/verify-impl.sh` is Mayor-writable and kernel read-only to the Forge (cycle 13, `fortkit-52vf.9`), and the diff touches `scripts/` and `test/` only. Both commits carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)`; the Mayor `session.start` at 07:29 still carries no model in its payload, which is `fortkit-ph4g` and not this bead's to fix. Attended frontier seat, no GPT-family weighting.

**Verifiers executed.** `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in cwd: **exit 0, 16 files / 187 tests**, all steps reached including shellcheck and template-render (round 1 aborted before those).

---

### 1. RESOLVED — round-one blocking finding 1 is fixed, and the fix is the fix rather than the case vanishing

`test/seats.test.ts:287` now pins `FORT_REGISTRY` to a scratch registry naming `repositoryRoot`, so the live-capital test asserts the code against the real roster instead of asserting the disk. In the same scratch that produced round one's `1 failed / 186 passed`:

```
seat-lint: 4 occupied of 4 seat file(s); 6 id pair(s) compared
seat-lint: charter cross-check — 4 occupant(s) checked against charter.md; ...
registry: /tmp/warden-x508 is not listed in /home/justin/.claude/civilization.json
  — rules 2 and 3 SKIPPED (found 3 fort(s), none matching this repo)
...
 Test Files  16 passed (16)      Tests  187 passed (187)
```

**The positive control is in that output and I did not have to construct it.** The skip note is still present — the condition that broke round one is still firing — and the suite passes anyway. That is the discriminating observation, not a bare green.

Stronger than the two environments the commit message names: **all seven tests in the file pin `FORT_REGISTRY`** (`test/seats.test.ts:98` for six of them via `lintFort`, `:281` for the announced-skip case). Ambient `$HOME` cannot reach this file at all now, in any environment. That covers the GitHub runner (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:29`) by construction rather than by a run I cannot perform.

`lintFort` promisifies `execFile`, which rejects on non-zero exit, so `await lintFort(repositoryRoot, registry)` asserts exit 0 against the real seat files and the real charter as well as the two `toContain` strings. Rule 3 and the charter cross-check are genuinely enforced against Manyhalls' own roster, deterministically.

The scope note in the test — rules 2 and 3 are structurally unenforceable on a runner, which has neither a registry nor sibling forts — is written into the file where the next reader will hit it. That is the right place for it.

### 2. RESOLVED — round-one finding 5, with a residual worth a bead (non-blocking)

`scripts/seat-lint.mjs:178-183` now `break`s on first match and records `entryRepo` as the **resolved** path; `:224` compares `await resolveRepo(fort.repo) === entryRepo`. The duplicate-spelling case I raised — a registry listing one repo under two spellings making the fort foreign to itself — is closed, and the lookup is now deterministic instead of last-match-wins.

Two things it does not do, and neither is a blocker:

- **No fixture pins it.** `buildCivilization` could emit a duplicate entry with a trailing slash in three lines. The bead's evidence bar applies to the acceptance criteria, which are all covered; this is a hardening added mid-review and untested.
- **One ordering survives.** If the registry ever listed a *worktree* path before the canonical checkout, `entry` matches via the raw `fort.repo === root` fallback, `entryRepo` becomes the worktree, and the canonical entry is then treated as foreign — this fort's own citizens hard-failing every seat file. `bin/fort-init` never writes a worktree into the registry, so this is unobserved and SO11 governs: record it, do not demand it.

Bead both together against `scripts/seat-lint.mjs`.

### 3. RESOLVED — round-one finding 6 recorded (non-blocking)

`scripts/seat-lint.mjs:249-255` carries the latent cost of the bare-given-name half and, better than I asked for, names the remedy to prefer if it ever fires (narrow to the full name, do not delete the rule). Nothing further.

### 4. CARRIED — the lint still does not travel (non-blocking, bead)

Unchanged and unaddressed, as the commit says. `templates/scripts/verify-impl.sh:74-78` runs `typecheck lint test shellcheck` — no `seat-lint`, and no `memory-lint` either — and there is no `templates/` counterpart to `scripts/seat-lint.mjs` at all. A fort founded today gets none of this. Merging gives the capital the lint; not merging gives nobody it. Bead against the parity programme, where the live/template `verify-impl.sh` divergence already belongs.

### 5. CARRIED — civilization seats are outside rule 2's roster (non-blocking, bead)

Also unchanged and acknowledged. The foreign roster is built from `registry.forts[].repo + /fort/seats`; `civ/seats/` holds `chronicler.md`, `herald.md`, `regent.md`, and no registry entry points at them. A seat file whose Held-by named the Regent would pass rule 2, while covenant section 4's "never emits as one of this fort's citizens" is the same law one layer up. Bead.

### 6. CARRIED — the escalation on fortkit-8rh remains unverifiable from this seat (non-blocking)

`test/seats.test.ts:104-113` still says the kestra/kethra pair — the collision this rule exists for, and the reason this seat is called Ilva — was "Escalated to the Overseer on fortkit-8rh rather than resolved here." The export at `.beads-export.jsonl` carries 453 `_type:"issue"` records and no comment bodies, and `bd` cannot run in this posture. Not asserted false; asserted unverified. The handling itself remains correct: the pair sits at distance 2, it is filed among the WARN cases where the ruling puts it, and the threshold was not bent to make the story come out right.

### 7. The SO7 correction is correctly placed and correctly scoped (non-blocking, noted for the record)

It sits in the bead's `comments`, which is where the 2026-08-11 amendment (`fortkit-zpw8`) put corrections and where review habit reads. It owns the right half — counts accurate, exit code conditional — names both environments this time, cites the cause without diffusing it, and files it as the class it is rather than as working state. My round-one measurement is quoted accurately. Nothing to add.

### 8. Coverage moved rather than shrank (non-blocking observation, no bead)

Pinning the registry means the live-capital *test* no longer checks Manyhalls' seat files against the real Proofdelve and Farlantern rosters. That check did not disappear: `run_step seat-lint node scripts/seat-lint.mjs` in `scripts/verify-impl.sh:319` runs with no `FORT_REGISTRY` and reads the real one, so on a civilization host the verifier does the live rule-2 check while the test does the code check. That is the correct split — the test measures the code, the gate measures the roster — and it is worth stating so nobody later "restores" the ambient coupling thinking coverage was lost.

Round-one finding 6's other half stands unchanged and is a property, not a defect: on a civilization host this fort's gate is partly a function of other repositories' working trees. Rejecting a hardcoded list of other settlements' citizens was right, and standing order 12 is the reason.

**No gate-1 trigger:** `scripts/` and `test/` only, no `fort/` path, no charter, no seat file. No mandatory-ESCALATE area. **Threat model:** nothing new bears on any of the four. Round one's threat-1 concern — a red gate everyone learns to read past — is what this round closes.

---

**Verified independently:** md5 of the scratch's `scripts/seat-lint.mjs`, `test/seats.test.ts` and `scripts/verify-impl.sh` against the `eabbcc9` blobs, so I ran what I read · `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in cwd → **exit 0**, 16 files / 187 tests, announced skip note present, shellcheck and template-render both reached and green, typecheck/browser-typecheck/biome clean · `npx vitest run test/seats.test.ts` in isolation → 7 passed, and no `fatal: not a git repository` noise, which is how I attribute the three lines in the full run to other files rather than to this diff · the full `seat-lint.mjs` and `seats.test.ts` at `eabbcc9` read at source, and the `0f6e37a..eabbcc9` delta read hunk by hunk · every `FORT_REGISTRY` pin in the test file enumerated (`:98`, `:281`) · `templates/scripts/verify-impl.sh:74-78` and the absence of any `templates/` seat-lint file · `civ/seats/` contents · both commit trailers naming Claude Opus 5, and today's event stream carrying no model on the Mayor's `session.start`.

**Taken on faith:** the commit's empty-`HOME` verifier run — my profile refuses an env-prefixed command, so I could not reproduce that spelling; it is corroborated by a third environment I *did* measure (this scratch, repo absent from the registry, skip announced, suite green) and by the structural fact that no test in the file reads `$HOME` · rule 2 against the real Proofdelve and Farlantern rosters, whose trees are outside my working directories · the GitHub-runner behaviour, which I derive from an executed code path rather than from a runner · the claimed escalation on `fortkit-8rh`, per finding 6.

Findings 2, 4 and 5 are bead candidates and are not held against this merge.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: round-1 blocker fixed and verified green in the scratch that was red; 4 non-blocking findings to bead.

title: B2R: the Band 2 Regent sitting — four factory and launcher repairs in files no masked seat can write
description:
Band 2 of the parity gate is the factory. Four of its items live in bin/ or fort/scripts/, kernel read-only to every masked seat in the capital INCLUDING the Forge (fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:187-203, guarded on civ/covenant.md, above the case $seat at :205 so it binds both branches). Two of them additionally reach ForgeOs and longburn, which no Manyhalls seat can write at all (core fact: a-masked-mayor-session-cannot-launch-the-herald). The seat that should logically do this work is not the seat that can. One attended Regent sitting.

THE FOUR ITEMS: fortkit-0po6 (Regent half only) - fortkit-naju - fortkit-ugw4 - fortkit-rw86.

READ THE CORRECTION COMMENT ON EACH BEAD BEFORE THE BEAD. All four were re-verified against the live files by the Mayor on 2026-08-14, and three of the four describe their own defect wrong. Where bead and file disagree, THE FILE IS RIGHT.

EXPLICITLY NOT IN THIS SITTING, and not deferred by accident:
  fortkit-8rh and fortkit-fd2's check half. Both presuppose a roster and moot
  scaffolding in bin/fort-init that have NEVER BEEN BUILT (fort-init founds all
  seats empty; the moot is a manual post-founding step, bin/fort-init:194-195;
  the scaffolding is an optional line item in fortkit-vlj, P2, untouched). The
  Overseer ruled 2026-08-14 that fort-init grows a SEAT roster only, with no
  personhood, which means those two beads have no target at founding at all
  and are rehomed to the fort verifier. See the seat-lint bead.
  fortkit-0po6's TEMPLATE half. Forge lane, blocked on this sitting.

SEQUENCING: 0po6 before naju (render() must learn {{HOME}} before new files
render through it). ugw4 and rw86 share no file with either and can go first
for an early green.
design:
ITEM 1 - fortkit-0po6, Regent half. Overseer ruling: shape (a), a {{HOME}} placeholder.
  THE TRAP: templates/config/settings-permissions.json NEVER PASSES THROUGH render().
  bin/fort-init:151 runs its own sed "s|{{REPO_PATH}}|$REPO|g". Patch render() at
  :27-29 alone and a literal {{HOME}} ships into every new fort's .claude/settings.json,
  where a deny rule containing braces matches nothing and denies nothing. That is the
  fortkit-f3y double-slash class one layer up, failing in the direction where the fort
  believes it is protected. BOTH sites, or route :151 through render().
  POSITIVE CONTROL REQUIRED: the template carries no {{HOME}} token yet (Forge lane), so
  a sed against it is a no-op and 'it works' would be read off the sed line. Render a
  throwaway fixture containing {{HOME}} and prove substitution.
  Also: narrow fortkit-4wlz's 'no absolute-path denies' to REPO_PATH on the record.

ITEM 2 - fortkit-naju. FIVE sites, not the three the bead names. Measured 2026-08-14:
  :31   for s in mayor forge warden           -> researcher.md not rendered
  :32   for sc in emit status mayor forge warden verify -> researcher.sh and
        probe-researcher-boundaries.sh not rendered
  :46   render warden-settings.json ALONE     -> researcher-settings.json not rendered
  :180  for s in mayor forge warden           -> NO seat.founded event for the researcher
  :90-91 the generated CORE-TIER founding fact asserts 'actor ids default to the seat
        offices (mayor/forge/warden)' and becomes FALSE the moment a fourth seat installs
  OVERSEER RULING 2026-08-14: fort-init grows a SEAT ROSTER, seats only, no personhood
  (no names, no pronouns, no personalities). Shape: SEATS=(mayor forge warden researcher)
  in one place; per seat render its seat file, launcher, profile and boundary probe, each
  IF THE TEMPLATE EXISTS; build the :90-91 fact text and the :180 event loop from the same
  list. Directory-derivation was considered and is worse: templates/fort/scripts/ mixes
  seat launchers with emit/status/verify, so it needs a naming convention that does not
  exist. One explicit list is still one place.

ITEM 3 - fortkit-ugw4. VERIFIED BY READING THE GUARD, not by grepping for the string
  (the bead warns that a grep measures the indicator, and it is right).
  fort/scripts/mayor.sh:11 tests -n "${FORT_MASKED:-}" and interpolates the value into
  the refusal message, so FORT_MASKED=warden and =forge work with NO CHANGE TO mayor.sh.
  CORRECTION TO THE BEAD: the pattern is TWO lines, not one. mayor.sh:54-55 does
  'export FORT_MASKED=1' AND 'mask+=(--setenv FORT_MASKED 1)'. Both launchers need both,
  after build_mask/mask_env (forge.sh:70-71 codex, warden.sh:151-152 claude) and before
  the exec. Three live forts. Templates are Forge lane.

ITEM 4 - fortkit-rw86. fort/scripts/status.sh:28 git rev-list --count origin/main..main.
  CORRECTION TO THE BEAD: the failure mode is not 'an empty AHEAD'. :29 prints
  ${AHEAD:-?} and :30 guards on ${AHEAD:-0}, so an unreachable remote renders as
  '? commit(s) ahead of origin/main' AND SILENTLY SUPPRESSES the >3 push-drift warning.
  Mayor's recommendation stands: shape (b), relabel honestly ('N commits since last sync
  with origin' plus the reflog sync time). Offline, cannot fail, converts a false
  statement into a true one. Three live forts. The real push-drift watcher Marrek argues
  for is NEW WORK and gets its own bead when the Overseer wants it, not folded in here.

THE TRAP THAT OTHERWISE COSTS AN AFTERNOON: bin/fort-init:174 writes the registry to
$HOME/.claude/civilization.json, kernel read-only, so founding from a MASKED seat fails
EROFS. The Regent runs unmasked and will not hit it; the founding smoke at
test/shell.test.ts:25-46 will. Pass FORT_REGISTRY at a writable path.
acceptance_criteria:
EVERY ONE OF THESE IS TAKEN ON A REALLY-FOUNDED FORT OR A REAL LAUNCH. None is taken by reading the script back.
1. A fort founded from templates/ into a scratch dir contains fort/seats/researcher.md, fort/scripts/researcher.sh, fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh and fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json, both scripts executable, and its event stream carries seat.founded for the researcher.
2. grep -rn '{{' over the ENTIRE founded tree INCLUDING .claude/settings.json returns nothing. This single check is what catches the :151 trap.
3. A throwaway fixture containing {{HOME}} rendered through both render() and the :151 path substitutes correctly (positive control for item 1, since no shipped template uses the token yet).

comments.text:
I have enough to render a verdict. One measurement decided it.

**Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES**

Work under review: `150f4b7^..8bdce87`, the Regent sitting of 2026-08-14 (Calder Sealbroken, they/them, **model opus**, Overseer present). Frontier model, and the sitting's method is the best I have reviewed in this fort: baseline fort founded from the unedited factory *before* the first edit, a deliberately-built naive fix as the middle row of a three-factory control table, pre-image sha256 + `filecmp` gating on every install, and four departures from the brief disclosed rather than smoothed — one of which corrects the brief and was independently confirmed by the Mayor under SO7. I weighted scrutiny toward the claims the sitting itself generated, because that is the only surface a control of this quality does not cover. Finding 1 is there.

---

**1. BLOCKING — `status.sh`'s `(synced <ts>)` is the tip commit's committer date, not the sync time, and three records say it is "the reflog sync time."**

`fort/scripts/status.sh:42` is `git log -g -1 --format=%cd --date=iso refs/remotes/origin/main`. Under `git log -g`, `%cd` is still the *committer date of the commit*; the reflog entry's own time is `%gd`. Measured in `/home/justin/dev/fortkit`:

```
cd=2026-08-13 22:17:58 -0800 | gd=origin/main@{2026-08-13 22:18:05 -0800} | gs=update by push
cd=2026-08-13 21:45:32 -0800 | gd=origin/main@{2026-08-13 21:45:35 -0800} | gs=update by push
cd=2026-08-13 20:32:02 -0800 | gd=origin/main@{2026-08-13 20:35:41 -0800} | gs=update by push
```

and `git log -1 --format=%cd --date=iso origin/main` → `2026-08-13 22:17:58 -0800`, identical. **The `-g` is inert for this value.** The capital figure the sitting reports as evidence — `(synced 2026-08-13 22:17:58 -0800)` — *is* the tip commit's committer date; the sync was 22:18:05, and in the third row above the gap is 3m39s. Under `git fetch` the gap is unbounded: a tip committed a week ago by another clone renders as "synced" a week ago no matter when you fetched it.

Why this is blocking rather than a bead. `fortkit-rw86` exists because an instrument reported a proxy under the target's label. The repair reintroduces the same class one line down, and asserts the opposite in four places: the bead comment ("*it says WHEN this clone last synced, which is the quantity the number is actually about*"), the handoff ("*the reflog sync time*"), the commit message, and the rendered line itself. A reader acting on any of those mis-dates a sync — SO7's own test for a correction. It is live in three forts and `rw86`'s `templates/` half is still to be written by the Forge *from this code*, so the class is one Forge pass from the factory and every settlement founded after it.

In fairness, and it is why I ask for a repair and not a revert: the error direction is conservative (the tip's committer date cannot postdate the sync, barring clock skew), and the block this replaced was worse in every respect. The ask is small — `--format=%gd` (renders `origin/main@{…}`, strip or print as-is), or keep `%cd` and relabel it `tip committed <ts>` — plus an SO7 correction appended to `fortkit-rw86` and to `civ/handoffs/regent-2026-08-14T100235.md`. Everything else in item 4 is right, including the `if` over `[ … ] && echo` and the single branch on readability, which is the real substance of the bead.

**2. Non-blocking — `bin/fort-init:38-41` states 4wlz's narrowing as though 4wlz held the decision.** The comment reads *"fortkit-4wlz's 'no absolute-path denies in the templates' is NARROWED ON THE RECORD…"*. I read 4wlz from the export: OPEN, titled for two `.ssh`/`.aws` lines, recording three options and a recommendation, and no such rule. The Regent found this and recorded it correctly on both beads and in the commit message — but the factory comment, which outlives both, still attributes the phrase to 4wlz rather than to `0po6`'s mis-description of it. One clause. Bead.

**3. Non-blocking — the fort now speaks two marker dialects, and the dead line stays.** `forge.sh:86`/`warden.sh:167` set seat-named `forge`/`warden`; `mayor.sh:55` still sets legacy `1`, so a Mayor-launched refusal prints *"already inside the '1' seat mask"* — the diagnosability the new eight-line comment argues for, absent in the seat that has it longest. And `mayor.sh:54`'s `export FORT_MASKED=1`, now proven dead, is left standing beside two new comments explaining at length that it does nothing. Both are outside this sitting's brief (item 3 correctly said `mayor.sh` needs no change); both are the "edit the subject, leave the claim" half of `read-the-artifact-remember-the-why`. Bead.

**4. Non-blocking — nothing automated can catch a roster regression.** The founding smoke (`test/shell.test.ts:154`) founds a real fort and asserts only that its shipped verifier exits 0. Not asserted anywhere: the four Researcher artifacts and their modes, `seat.founded` ×4, or the zero-render-token census. All three were measured by hand this sitting and none is a forced read. `fortkit-domm` is the right home — it should assert acceptance 1-3 verbatim, and the token check in the narrowed shape `{{[A-Z_]*}}`, with a positive control that goes red.

**5. Non-blocking — `templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:6` still says `(mayor/forge/warden)`.** The sitting fixed exactly this sentence where `fort-init` generates it (`$SEAT_OFFICES`) and reworded line 2 of this same file, leaving line 6 asserting three offices in a fort that is now founded with four. `researcher.sh:6` already carries the four. Forge lane; bead alongside `hgbe`/`opae`.

**6. Non-blocking — `render_stream`'s sed delimiter is one operator keystroke from corrupting a founding.** `$PURPOSE` is free-text from the command line and `$HOME`/`$REPO` are paths; a `|` or `&` in any of them mangles every rendered file. Pre-existing, but the sitting now owns that function. Low-priority bead.

---

**What I verified independently, by running it in cwd**

- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — green. tsc (both projects), biome 64 files, **15 files / 180 tests**, memory lint 4/4, template-render leg *"10 template scripts rendered in 3 passes and linted clean; positive control went red as required"*. `skills-install` SKIPPED (scratch has no `.git`). Matches the sitting's 180/15 exactly. I could not observe a bare exit code — the harness refused `echo $?` — but every leg ran to completion with no failure line.
- **The founding smoke was not skipped here.** `which bd` → `/home/justin/.local/bin/bd`, `which jq` → `/usr/bin/jq`, and vitest reported 180 passed with no skip count. So a real fort *was* founded from the candidate `bin/fort-init` under `FORT_REGISTRY`, and its shipped verifier passed. Acceptance 7 is executed, by me.
- `test/mayor-launcher.test.ts` — exit 77 and the seat-naming refusal for markers `mayor`/`forge`/`warden`/`1`, executed in that same run. Acceptance 4's guard half is executed; its launcher half is not (below).
- **The "one line, not two" correction is right.** `mask+=(--clearenv)` at `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:519`, first line of `mask_env`, before any `--setenv`; `mayor.sh:54-55` is `export` → `mask+=` → `exec bwrap` with nothing between. The export cannot reach the child and cannot reach anything else either. Both new lines land after `mask_env` and before the exec (`forge.sh:86`, `warden.sh:167`).
- The reflog/committer-date measurement of finding 1.
- Token census over `templates/`: 31 render-token occurrences, every one of them in `render_stream`'s substitution list; `templates/config/settings-permissions.json` carries only `{{REPO_PATH}}` today, so routing it through `render_stream` is a strict superset of the sed it replaced and cannot regress. `{{UNFILLED — …}}` does not match `{{[A-Z_]*}}`, so the narrowing of acceptance 2 is both zero-tolerance and safe — the sitting's departure 1 is correct.
- The roster is materially load-bearing, not cosmetic: `templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh:64` passes `--settings "$root/fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json"`, a file the factory never rendered until this change.
- `.beads/issues.jsonl`: 26 added / 20 removed lines, every removed id re-added, 6 net-new beads, nothing dropped. SO7 intact.
- `fortkit-4wlz` read from `.beads-export.jsonl`: OPEN, no such decision. The Regent's departure 4 is accurate.

**What I took on faith, and could not execute**

- **Every acceptance claim needing a fort founded by hand** — acceptance 1 (four Researcher artifacts, modes, `seat.founded` ×4), acceptance 2 (`{{[A-Z_]*}}` → zero over a founded tree including `.claude/settings.json`), acceptance 3 (the three-factory `{{HOME}}` fixture). My posture refused `mkdir`, `mktemp -d` and a `node -e` that would have made its own scratch, so I could not found a fort. I substituted a static argument — roster loop, template inventory, token census, `render_stream` routing — and a static argument is what it is. The sitting's own evidence for these is unusually strong; it is still its own.
- **Runtime `FORT_MASKED` propagation into a live masked child.** `printenv FORT_MASKED` and a read of `/proc/self/environ` were both refused, so I could not observe the marker in my own session — which is the one place I could have bought it for free. Acceptance 4's launch half rests on the sitting's `marker-harness.sh` and runtime probe, including the disclosed departure (probe rather than seat dispatch, on the Overseer's call). I have no reason to doubt it and no measurement of it.
- **Both elder forts.** `/home/justin/dev` is outside my binds; `ls` refused. I reviewed the capital's copies only. Acceptance 5's "all three forts" and item 3's ForgeOs half are the Regent's measurements.

Nothing here touches the constitution, a profile, a mask or a gate, so no gate-6 escalation arises. Findings 2-6 are beads and are not held against the merge. Finding 1 is one token and two appended corrections.

title: The Herald read an absent digest field as zero and published '0 commits' for all three forts as fact: the digest returned 54, 6 and 7
description:
OBSERVED FAILURE (2026-08-14 Herald run). The report at $vault/herald/reports/2026-08-14.md states: 'Proofdelve 36 events ... / 0 commits'; 'Farlantern 26 events ... / 0 commits'; 'Manyhalls 50 events (75 truncated) ... / 0 commits', and then reasons about the figure: 'The zero-commit figure in all three forts is not credible against the rest of the same payload and is treated as a source fault below, not as a quiet day.'

The instinct was right and the attribution was wrong. THERE IS NO SOURCE FAULT.

MEASURED, running the digest exactly as herald.sh:87 invokes it over the same window: gitLog length = 54 (Manyhalls), 6 (Proofdelve), 7 (Farlantern). Confirmed independently for Manyhalls by hand-running the same underlying query with the Herald's exact window bounds — git log --format=%cI%x09%h%x09%s --since=2026-08-13T13:00:33.251Z --before=2026-08-14T13:00:45.063Z — which returns 54 lines. src/readers/git.ts:20-47 is behaving correctly.

HYPOTHESIS FOR THE MECHANISM, stated as hypothesis rather than measurement because it has not been measured: the digest JSON field is named gitLog (src/digest.ts:27,127) and there is NO field named commits. An absent field was read as zero. The seat had no rule telling it that a missing field and a zero value are different facts.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE NUMBER: the report is durable record in the vault, it is the input to tomorrow's window, and it asserts something false about all three forts on a morning when 67 commits actually landed. It is the same class as fortkit-uj3q: a claim and its subject drifting apart, reached by reading an indicator that could not have discriminated the property claimed. Four of the five instances recorded there had exactly this shape.

SO7: a correction is owed on the 2026-08-14 report, appended rather than edited in.
design:
Two halves, and the second is the one that generalizes:
(a) The report correction for 2026-08-14, appended. The Herald writes the vault; a masked Mayor cannot (see core fact a-masked-mayor-session-cannot-launch-the-herald), so this rides the next Herald run or the Overseer's hand.
(b) civ/scripts/herald.sh prompt: the seat is told the digest is its only window (line 87) but not how to read an absent field. Add the rule — a field you cannot find is a GAP, recorded by name in Gaps and anomalies, never a zero. This is the read-side twin of fortkit-ebf, which teaches the same seat the closedBeads error status. Consider folding the two.
(c) Consider whether formatDigest's human rendering (src/digest.ts:158-176, which prints 'git log: N') should be what the Herald consumes instead of raw JSON, since the rendering names its fields in prose the seat cannot mis-key.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The 2026-08-14 report carries an appended correction naming the true figures (54/6/7) and the mechanism. 2. herald.sh instructs the seat that an unlocatable digest field is a named gap, never a zero. 3. A future run over a window with commits reports a nonzero commit count.

title: The fortkit-9sa constitution watch reads a truncated event list: every charter.amended in the window was sliced away, so the watch reported three announced amendments as unannounced
description:
OBSERVED FAILURE (2026-08-14 Herald run, civ/events/events-2026-08-14.jsonl session.end 05:07:48): Halric reported '3 Manyhalls charter diffs with no charter.amended event' and could not discharge the 9sa watch. The alarm is false and the fort is fine; the watch is broken.

MEASURED, by running the digest exactly as herald.sh:87 invokes it (node src/cli.ts digest --since 2026-08-13T13:00:34.251Z --json):

- The three constitution diffs are real and correctly detected: 98cf750 (beadRef fortkit-hwol), 88c3704 (fortkit-3jv7), d435aab (fortkit-k1pq).
- All three DO have charter.amended events in fort/events/events-2026-08-13.jsonl, at 07:40:33, 10:40:47 and 11:26:07 -08:00, each with the bead as target and Overseer approval recorded on the bead beforehand.
- The digest event feed arrives NEWEST-FIRST. Live measurement: events[0].ts = 2026-08-14T16:59:32Z, events[-1].ts = 2026-08-13T21:19:30Z.
- src/digest.ts:15 sets maxEventsPerFort = 50; src/digest.ts:109 applies events.slice(0, maxEventsPerFort). Keeping the FIRST 50 of a newest-first list keeps the NEWEST and truncates the OLDEST 77.
- Every charter.amended in the window is older than that cutoff. Count of charter.amended in the 50 events the Herald saw: ZERO.

So the watch correlates constitutionDiffs against a list from which the diffs own announcements have already been removed. It fires on any day busy enough to truncate, which is exactly the day with the most charter activity.

FALSIFICATION TEST (fortkit-uj3q, read-the-artifact-remember-the-why): what result would have falsified the watch reporting an anomaly? Under truncation, none. The watch cannot go green for the right reason, so its green is not evidence either.

SECURITY CONSEQUENCE: habituation. A watch that cries wolf on every busy day gets disregarded, and a genuinely unannounced charter edit then passes unnoticed. The charter names that shape as the compromise signature (charter.md, 'The civilization layer' item 4).
design:
Shapes to weigh, decision belongs in the fix:
(a) Exempt charter.amended (and any category the watches correlate on) from truncation — carry them in a dedicated always-complete field alongside the truncated feed.
(b) Have the digest compute the correlation itself and expose a per-diff 'announced: true|false|UNKNOWN-truncated' field, so the consumer cannot get it wrong. Preferred on the read-the-artifact principle: the seat that owns the data owns the join.
(c) Make the Herald refuse to report a 9sa finding when eventsTruncated > 0 and record a gap instead. Weakest — it converts a false positive into a blind spot, and blind is what the seat's law (ugr.6) forbids.
Any shape must include a regression test in test/digest.test.ts with a positive control: a window where the announcement IS absent must still report the anomaly.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A window containing a charter.amended event and its constitution diff reports NO anomaly, with events truncated. 2. A window containing a constitution diff whose charter.amended is genuinely absent DOES report the anomaly (positive control). 3. Both cases covered by tests in test/digest.test.ts. 4. Today's false alarm gets an appended correction wherever it is durable record.

title: [bug] Standing order 12 exists in the capital and the template only: neither elder fort is under the law that governs Band 3

need each fort's own mayor.sh named instead of Manyhalls'. That substitution is itself an
