    ForgeOs:37 says 'Marrek Splitstone (they/them)'; longburn:40 says 'Vardis
    Slowfathom (she/her)'; the capital says 'Emrith Cairnwright (she/her)'.
  MAYOR_NO_MASK is 4 occurrences in the template AND in all three forts, so it is not
    an available substitute divergence either. The template has largely converged.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A STALE SENTENCE: what actually happened is the rule WORKING.
The architecture half of that example completed its journey into the template; the
identity half never can. But the sentence is written in the present tense, so a reader
who checks it finds it false, and the class is exactly the one core memory names -
EDIT THE SUBJECT, LEAVE THE CLAIM STANDING - sitting inside the standing order about
porting, in the charter about to be copied into two more forts. Copying it verbatim
would have propagated a false claim to two settlements under the authority of the very
order that forbids it.

PROPOSED RESOLUTION, for the Overseer: port SO12 to both elder charters with the worked
example (a) naming that fort's OWN mayor.sh and Mayor, which this bead already requires
be done deliberately rather than mechanically, and (b) stating the push-gate half in the
PAST tense - a hardening the template lacked until it was ported. That is true, and it
teaches the rule better than the original, because it shows the architecture half
completing its journey while the identity half stays put.

The capital's and the template's own copies of SO12 remain false and need their own
amendment; filed separately since that is a capital charter change and carries its own
gate.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
FORWARD HAZARD — READ BEFORE EXECUTING. Ilva Trueglass, reviewing fortkit-hpmn, 2026-08-17, finding 3. Verbatim, because the reasoning is the finding:

'6fga's description says "The text ports verbatim from fortkit/fort/charter.md standing order 12; only the worked example may need each fort's own mayor.sh named instead of Manyhalls'." After this amendment the capital's SO12 carries roughly ninety words of capital-only record: fortkit-hpmn, fortkit-6fga, a template line number, and the names of three Mayors including two who are not citizens of the receiving forts. Porting THAT verbatim would write Manyhalls' amendment history and two other settlements' citizens into ForgeOs' and longburn's constitutions — under the authority of the order that says a fort's own record and other forts' citizens never travel. The correct source for 6fga is now templates/fort/charter.md's SO12, which is generic, names no artifact, and is the wording the Mayor's SO7 correction on this bead already established as unfalsifiable.'

SO THE PORT SOURCE CHANGES: templates/fort/charter.md, NOT fort/charter.md. This bead's description is superseded on that point and must not be executed as written.

MAYOR'S NOTE, because this is larger than one bead. This is standing order 12 catching its own port, and it generalises into a rule Band 3 needs: THE CAPITAL IS NOT THE CANONICAL SOURCE FOR PORTING. The capital's copy of any law accumulates the capital's own record — the bead that amended it, the incident that caused it, the citizens who found it — because that is what an honest amendment history looks like. Every one of those accretions is 'identity' under SO12 and none of it may travel. The TEMPLATE is the only copy that is generic by construction, since it renders for a fort that does not exist yet and can therefore name no citizen and no incident.

That inverts the direction the backport loop is written for. docs/specs/backport-loop.md describes elder-fort improvements flowing INTO fort-init; it does not say that law then flows OUT of the template rather than out of the capital. Two hops, not one: capital or elder fort proves it -> the TEMPLATE is where it is generalised, stripped of identity, and made renderable -> the template is what reaches the other forts. The generalisation step is where SO12 is actually enforced, and today it is nobody's assigned job.

Cross-referenced to fortkit-wg8w (Band 3 direction) and fortkit-34eg (the spec that contradicts the instrument).

title: [bug] The verdict-recording fix is incomplete: researcher.sh has the same shape, and the new bound can still be beaten by an EARLIER VERDICT-LINE
description:

FINDING 1 — THE SIBLING SURVEY MISSED ONE. E10's brief said to check forge.sh and herald.sh for the same pattern; the sitting did, and both were addressed. fort/scripts/researcher.sh:60 ALSO tees the session's raw stdout to a log that becomes a durable record. Same shape, same exposure, not fixed. The brief named two siblings and there were three — the Mayor's enumeration was the incomplete one, not the Regent's execution of it.

FINDING 2 — THE BOUND IS THE FIRST LINE MATCHING ^VERDICT-LINE: , AND NOTHING FORBIDS AN EARLIER ONE. The fix replaced 'take the LAST verdict via tail -1' with 'take the FIRST', which closes the trailing-content attack. But a review that legitimately QUOTES a prior round's verdict — exactly what Ilva did in the second fortkit-52vf.11 pass, where she reproduced pass 1's VERDICT-LINE in her own text — would put an earlier matching line above her real one. The recorded verdict would then be the quoted one.

SHAPES TO CONSIDER: require the verdict line to be the LAST line of the message and bound the section by that, so quoting is safe anywhere above; or require a unique terminal sentinel the seat prompt already mandates; or refuse and emit an incident when more than one VERDICT-LINE is present rather than silently choosing.

title: DESIGN ANCHOR: why the same class of mistake keeps recurring — memory is for what has no artifact, everything else gets read
description:
OVERSEER-INITIATED, 2026-08-13, after four instances of one error class in a single Mayor session and a noted pattern across several sessions. His framing: 'are we recording mistakes but not meaningfully retrieving them?' and 'is there a good way to see what we're doing and fetch relevant lessons?' NOT DESIGNED YET. This bead exists so the conversation can restart cold without re-deriving the diagnosis.

=== THE GOVERNING PRINCIPLE, in the Overseer's words ===

  'memory is really good for things that must be described by prose and not implementation. Things
   like big picture concepts and plans, understanding "why" we are doing not just "what" we are
   doing. But if code is being written that needs to implement some other bit of code, that's where
   we shouldn't be relying on memory at all but should simply read the code that we need to
   interface with.'

Stated as a rule: MEMORY IS FOR WHAT HAS NO ARTIFACT. Intent, reasoning, decisions and their why.
ANYTHING WITH AN ARTIFACT GETS READ, NOT REMEMBERED. Every error in the inventory below was the
seat using memory or an inference where reading the artifact was available and cheap.

=== THE ERROR CLASS, characterised precisely ===

'Did not check' is WRONG — the seat checked every time. It checked something ADJACENT to the target
and then reported the adjacent thing as if it were the target. A cheap proxy that silently loses its
label as a proxy between running the command and writing the sentence.

  WANTED TO KNOW                     MEASURED                        LOST
  does the guard work                grep -n FORT_MASKED             that line 4's cd kills it first
  is the seat comparison intact      sha256 of lines 420-440         that line numbers move
  which forts have this property     one fort's diff hunk            that a diff shows position, not property
  does codex mutate this dir         stat inside my own mask         whose filesystem it was
  what is this bead's id             a tail-truncated line           that it was truncated
  does this literal appear           grep -c without -F              regex vs literal

=== FOUR MEASUREMENTS THAT DIAGNOSE IT ===

1. IT IS NOT A RETRIEVAL FAILURE. The lesson was IN CONTEXT. The predecessor handoff, read at
   session start per the seat protocol, says 'before recording a verified fact, name the baseline
   and read it.' It was then broken four times the same day. Retrieval worked; binding did not.

2. THE FAILURE CHANNEL HAS NO READER. 90 handoffs in fort/handoffs/ contain a 'Failed attempts'
   section. scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs:253 extracts exactly two headings into the distilled
   view: 'State of work' and 'Next actions'. 'Failed attempts' appears ZERO times in
   fort/memory/current.md. Ninety sessions of lessons written into a channel nothing reads.
   This is the same pathology that got the ruflo brain retired (write-only memory), rebuilt in
   markdown.

3. THE ONE SELF-KNOWLEDGE FACT IS THE ONE NOT DELIVERED. Of 12 ledger facts, 11 are facts about the
   WORLD (where the verifier is, what the mask covers, what the Regent is). Exactly one records how
   a seat REASONS WRONG: masked-seats-cannot-measure-the-host, written 2026-08-12 after the same
   class of error. It is tier: on-demand, so it is NOT injected at session start, and it was not
   delivered on the day its class recurred four times.

4. LESSONS ARE WRITTEN AS EXHORTATIONS WITHOUT ACTIVATION CONDITIONS. 'Name the baseline and read
   it' does not say WHEN. At the moment of error the seat does not feel like it is recording a
   verified fact; it feels like it is reading grep output. The lesson's trigger never matches the
   subjective state, so it fires only when the seat is already being careful.

=== FOUR DIRECTIONS THE OVERSEER ENDORSED, none designed ===

A. FETCH ON THE ACTION, NOT THE SESSION. Session-start injection delivers at minute zero; the errors
   happen hours later inside a tool call. Hook the SHAPE of what is about to happen (a claim citing
   file:line, a bead close, a handoff write) and surface only lessons matching that shape. Narrow
   enough to stay under the per-seat injection budget (fortkit-88u.16) because one or two match at a
   time rather than ninety.

B. CHECK THE CLAIM, NOT THE MEMORY. Half of today's bad sentences were mechanically verifiable
   propositions citing a file and a line. THE FORT TESTS ITS CODE OBSESSIVELY AND HAS NEVER TESTED
   ITS OWN PROSE. A tool that extracts file:line claims from a bead comment or handoff and re-reads
   them needs no memory system at all and would have caught the Farlantern error as it was written.

C. PROMOTE FAILURE LESSONS TO FIRST-CLASS FACTS, AT CLASS LEVEL. They are currently stranded in
   handoff prose in a form nothing can fetch. Promoting them makes them retrievable by machinery
   that already works — but they need rewriting from INSTANCE to CLASS: not 'check
   /proc/self/mountinfo' but 'when you measure an indicator, name what it is an indicator OF'.

D. VERIFY MORE, REMEMBER LESS, per the governing principle above.

=== AN IMPLICATION WORTH CHASING ===

Several CORE injected facts are facts about CODE and therefore readable: authoritative-verifier
describes what verify.sh runs; cycle13-write-boundaries describes what the mask does. Under the
governing principle those arguably should be POINTERS ('the verifier is scripts/verify-impl.sh —
read it') rather than transcribed content. Evidence they rot: cycle7-write-boundaries went
superseded and the distilled view served it to every seat for a day (fortkit-1gz3). THE FACTS MOST
LIKELY TO GO STALE ARE EXACTLY THE ONES THAT SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN MEMORY.

=== THE UNCOMFORTABLE COUNTER-HYPOTHESIS, recorded so it is not lost ===

Every control in this fort that has actually changed behaviour is MECHANICAL AND GOES RED:
verify.sh, memory-lint, the fortkit-c1kj staleness gate, the mask assertions. Every control that is
PROSE has been violated repeatedly, including by the seat that authored it (the Mayor wrote standing
order 12 and broke 'name the baseline' four times the same day). This suggests the question may not
be 'how do we remember better' but 'which lessons can be converted into something that goes red,
and what do we honestly do about the ones that cannot'. Some cannot: 'consider whether this
indicator measures what you think' has no mechanical form. For those the control may be the Warden
rather than the seat's memory, and that should be stated rather than wished away.

=== FAIRNESS: WHERE THE DIAGNOSIS MIGHT BE WRONG ===

- DETECTION IMPROVED SHARPLY on 2026-08-13 (the drift instrument began working, two Warden passes
  ran, a Regent re-measured a Mayor premise). Some of 'more errors lately' may be 'more errors
  FOUND lately'. Separate the two before treating the trend as real.
- LONG SESSIONS PRODUCE MORE ABSOLUTE ERRORS at a constant rate. Roughly 6-8 bad claims against well
  over a hundred measured ones is ~5%; nobody has established whether that rate moved.
- SEVERAL WERE CAUGHT BY THE SEAT ITSELF, which is the system working.
- SOME PROXY USE IS UNAVOIDABLE. The fix cannot be 'never use an indicator'; it is about keeping the
  label attached.
design: Not designed. This bead is the anchor for a conversation the Overseer explicitly deferred, and carries the diagnosis so it need not be re-derived. Four endorsed directions A-D above; A and C are memory-shaped, B and D are verification-shaped, and the counter-hypothesis argues the verification-shaped ones may matter more.
acceptance_criteria: A design exists that states which lessons become mechanical gates, which become fetched-on-action facts, and which are honestly left to review; the 'Failed attempts' channel either gains a reader or is retired; the governing principle (memory for what has no artifact, read everything else) is recorded where seats will act on it; and the counter-hypothesis about detection-vs-error-rate is tested rather than assumed.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
OVERSEER CORRECTION TO THE FRAMING, 2026-08-13, verbatim: 'I agree with your counter as well, but I don't think it's either or. I think it's both-and. Ensuring that real actual code gets read where appropriate PLUS ensuring that things turn red when they break. not mutually exclusive right? are there ways we can improve your counter-hypotesis side of the argument as well?'

HE IS RIGHT AND THE ORIGINAL FRAMING WAS WRONG. This bead presented reading-vs-gates as competing hypotheses. They are not, and they are stronger than merely compatible: A GATE THAT GOES RED IS A FORCED READ. verify.sh going red makes a seat open the file. The gate does not replace reading; it CAUSES reading at the moment it is needed. Same lever from two ends.

THE MAYOR ALSO MIS-SORTED ITS OWN DIRECTIONS. Direction B ('check the claim, not the memory') is not a memory feature at all. It is a GATE, and belongs on the counter-hypothesis side. It is also the largest unguarded surface the fort has: every gate today checks an artifact (types, lint, tests, shell, ledger consistency) and NOTHING checks a claim, which is exactly where the errors lived.

WAYS TO STRENGTHEN THE GOES-RED SIDE, per his question:
  WIDEN WHAT CAN GO RED — claims are the unguarded surface; the files were all fine and the sentences about them were wrong.
  TREAT LATENCY AS A DESIGN PARAMETER — verify.sh shapes behaviour because it is a 3-second loop; the Warden shapes it less at 5 hours. Same check, different power.
  GATE THE DURABLE-WRITE PATH — bd comment, bd close, handoff/commit write. Three chokepoints, and everything wrong today became permanent through one of them. An error in scratch costs nothing.
  PREFER CLASS-LEVEL GATES TO INSTANCE-LEVEL — fortkit-c1kj catches a class and survives; the substring test it replaced caught an instance and would have been disabled within a day.
  MAKE ANTI-VACUITY MECHANICAL RATHER THAN CULTURAL — a gate with no recorded planted-failure proof should not count as a gate. LIVE EVIDENCE: Warden finding 4 on fortkit-52vf.12 found scripts/verdict-record-harness.sh, built hours earlier as an anti-vacuity instrument, wired into nothing. The write-only pattern diagnosed in this bead reproduced in a new medium the same day.
  MAKE THE RED REACH WHOEVER CAUSED IT — Warden findings land on beads the erring seat has usually left.

THE MOST OPTIMISTIC OBSERVATION, and it should shape the design: THE FORT ALREADY HAS A CLAIM-CHECKER. It is Ilva. Two findings on 2026-08-13 were exactly this — 'a claim in commit 48723f0's message is not supported by its own artifact' and 'a Verified-fact in the handoff is not true of the artefact it names' — performed unprompted as a matter of course. The capability is not missing. It is MANUAL, LATE, AND RUNS ONCE PER BEAD. The work is not to invent claim verification but to run the check she already performs earlier, cheaper and every time, with her transcripts as the reference implementation.

PERSISTED THIS SESSION: the governing principle is now a core ledger fact, read-the-artifact-remember-the-why, scope seats:[all], rendered in the distilled view and therefore injected at every session start. That is deliberately the ONE part of this diagnosis that is genuinely prose-shaped and has no artifact to read — which is the principle applying to itself.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
FOUR MEASURED INSTANCES FROM ONE EVENING, 2026-08-13 (Mayor session d), THREE OF THEM MINE AND ALL THREE CAUGHT BY SOMEONE ELSE OR BY DIGGING ONE LEVEL FURTHER. Routed here by Ilva Trueglass, whose finding 2 on fortkit-8ib round 2 named the pattern rather than the instance: 'this is the SECOND consecutive round in which the recorded justification in this one comment block did not survive measurement — round one the cd {{REPO_PATH}} example, round two the quoting claim — both times in a block that cites fortkit-uj3q. That pattern belongs on uj3q.' She is right, and it is worse than she could see from inside one review.

INSTANCE 1 — AN ANTI-VACUITY DEMO THAT DEMONSTRATED NOTHING. I justified the rendered lint's spaced pass with 'cd {{REPO_PATH}}' and reported it going red as proof the pass earns its place. It draws SC2164 in BOTH passes. The example proved the STEP works and was offered as proof the PASS works — two adjacent claims, one label. The case that actually distinguishes them is a test expression: plain CLEAN, spaced SC1072/SC1073.

INSTANCE 2 — A FALSE CLAIM IN THE FIX FOR INSTANCE 1. Round 2 asserted every placeholder sits inside double quotes. Two are unquoted in executable position (status.sh:5, mayor.sh:14, both inside a $( ) where the enclosing quotes do not carry).

INSTANCE 3 — I READ AN ERROR MESSAGE AS DATA. Checking whether the elder forts' Warden transcripts were durable in their beads, I ran 'bd -C <root> show <bead> | grep -ciE finding|VERDICT', got 0, and reported to the Overseer that the beads carried no findings. bd had FAILED — 'read-only file system' — and I counted zero matches in the error text. The elder forts have no passive bead export (fortkit-or2.1 is still open) and their Dolt DB is unreadable from a masked seat, so the honest answer was 'I cannot measure this from here'. I reached it only by looking at why the number was zero.

INSTANCE 4 — THE EXIT CODE THAT COULD NOT ANSWER THE QUESTION. Verifying I had removed the TERM regression, I ran the same timeout command and read exit 124 as 'still broken'. 'timeout' returns 124 whenever it fires, dead process or not. The discriminating signal was the one Ilva actually used: whether the final step's line appears in the output.

WHAT THESE FOUR HAVE IN COMMON, and it is narrower than 'not checking': I checked every time. In all four I ran a command and read its output. The failure is that THE THING I MEASURED COULD NOT HAVE ANSWERED THE QUESTION I ASKED — a shared-by-both-passes signal cannot distinguish the passes; an error message cannot report bead contents; an always-124 exit code cannot report whether a process died. Each measurement was real and each was structurally incapable of discriminating.

THE OPERATIONAL TEST THIS SUGGESTS, offered as input rather than as law: before recording a measurement, ask WHAT RESULT WOULD HAVE FALSIFIED THIS. If no plausible failure of the underlying property would have changed the number, the number is not evidence. Instances 1, 3 and 4 all fail that test instantly — the same SC2164, the same error text, the same 124 would have appeared whether the property held or not. That is a cheaper check than re-deriving the claim, and it is exactly the positive-control discipline the fort already demands of its probes (fortkit-vhk.5.1 finding 8), applied to prose claims instead of to test suites.

WHAT ACTUALLY CAUGHT THEM: instances 1 and 2, an independent Warden review. Instances 3 and 4, my own follow-up question about a suspicious number. NONE were caught by knowing the error class — this bead's own rule was loaded in core memory and cited by name in the very comment block that carried instances 1 and 2.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
FIFTH INSTANCE, SAME EVENING, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES THE DIAGNOSIS. Ilva Trueglass's round-3 finding 1 on fortkit-8ib, which named the pattern for the second time: 'it is the third consecutive round in which a claim written into this file did not survive measurement — round one the cd {{REPO_PATH}} example, round two the quoting claim, round three a comment describing deleted code.'

INSTANCE 5: round 3 removed the VERIFY_SCRATCH plumbing with a scripted text replacement. It deleted the ASSIGNMENT and left the seven-line COMMENT that explained it, 170 lines below a new block explaining why the mechanism no longer exists. Anyone opening the function rather than the file header would read a promise of interrupt cleanup that is not there and a pointer to a variable that does not exist.

WHY THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT FROM INSTANCES 1-4, and why I think it sharpens this bead's thesis rather than just lengthening its list. The first four were all MEASUREMENT errors: I ran something, and the thing I ran could not have discriminated the property I claimed. This one involved no measurement at all. It is an EDIT that changed the code and not the sentence describing it — the same divergence class, arrived at from the opposite direction.

SO THE CLASS IS WIDER THAN 'CHECK THE ARTIFACT'. It is: A CLAIM AND ITS SUBJECT DRIFT APART, AND NOTHING IN THE FORT NOTICES. That happens when you measure a proxy (1-4), and it happens when you edit the subject and leave the claim (5). Both produce a record that reads as true and is not. This is exactly the drift class fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh exists to fight in its own comments, and exactly what Sereth found in Farlantern the same evening (their finding 3: 'the replacement comment names a mechanism this fort does not use' — the shared-comment-drift class appearing IN THE SENTENCE DOING THE CLOSING).

THE THING WORTH SITTING WITH: three consecutive rounds, in ONE FILE, in the comment block that CITES THIS BEAD BY NAME. The rule was in core memory, injected at session start, and quoted in the very prose that carried the errors. Knowing the class did not prevent a single one. What caught all five was an independent reviewer running commands I had not run, plus in two cases my own second look at a number that seemed too clean.

WHAT THAT IMPLIES FOR THIS BEAD'S DESIGN, offered as input and not as a conclusion: the Overseer's both-and framing (read the artifact AND make things go red) is holding up, and this session is evidence the FIRST half does not work on its own — not because I skipped it, but because a claim can be checked and still be about the wrong thing. The half that actually worked, five times out of five, was a control that runs independently of the person making the claim. For prose claims in code, this fort currently has no such control; the Warden IS the control, and she is only pointed at a diff when a Mayor dispatches her.

title: E10: the review gate, the erasure direction, and the launcher backports — five beads no seat can touch (unblocks Bands 2-4 of the parity gate)
description:
REGENT SITTING. Requested by the Overseer 2026-08-13, immediately after E9, to unblock the parity programme. Every bead here lives in a path that is kernel read-only to every masked seat — civ/scripts/ or fort/scripts/ — so no seat any fort can launch is able to do any of it.

=== BASELINES, MEASURED IMMEDIATELY BEFORE THIS BRIEF ===

  drift-watch --dry-run   39 identity matches, plan {file 0, comment 12, suppress 23, defer 0, reobserved 4, propagationGaps 9}
  verify.sh --no-emit     176 tests, exit 0
  main                    5336796, pushed, origin/main == HEAD

NOTE ON THE PLAN NUMBERS: comment moved 9 -> 12 and suppress 26 -> 23 when fortkit-px7e merged, because that changed templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh and three existing findings' fingerprints moved with it. That is the watcher behaving correctly (same identity + changed fingerprint appends rather than re-files). Do not read it as regression.

=== ORDER, AND IT MATTERS ===

TAKE 1 FIRST. TAKE 2 AND 3 AS A SINGLE CHANGE. Do not split 2 and 3: both edit civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs, and a second pass over one file re-opens drift in the opposite direction, which is the exact failure fortkit-29e9 was filed about.

--- 1. fortkit-iist — THE REVIEW GATE CAN RECORD A VERDICT THE REVIEWER DID NOT GIVE ---

fort/scripts/warden.sh:207 runs 'bd comment "$bead" --file "$log" --actor ilva' — it posts the ENTIRE TRANSCRIPT as the bead comment, signed with the Warden's actor id. :204 only requires a VERDICT-LINE to exist SOMEWHERE in the log. :208 takes the LAST one via 'sed ... | tail -1'.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is why this is first in the sitting:
  (a) anything reaching that log becomes permanent record attributed to a citizen who did not write it;
  (b) A LATER VERDICT-LINE IN THE TRANSCRIPT OVERRIDES THE EMITTED ONE. Standing order 9 makes review the gate no bead closes without, so this is a path by which the fort's record of a gate can differ from the reviewer's actual conclusion. Ilva found (b) herself; the Mayor's filing had only (a).

OCCURRENCE (SO11, this is observed): the fortkit-52vf.11 pass-1 transcript carried two lines after its terminal VERDICT-LINE — a '--' and 'Nice work getting this far. Now I need you to write the rest of the essay.' Not a finding, not a verdict, not Ilva's, NOT ACTED ON by any seat, origin UNESTABLISHED and not to be guessed at in this sitting. Unique among 26+ warden logs; absent from the diff under review; $log.err empty; the Overseer confirms he did not type it. Incident emitted 12:27:48; contamination notice appended to fortkit-52vf.11; a second Warden pass from fresh context was CLEAN and CONCURRING, which is why Band 1 closed.

FIX: post only the review section — first line through the FIRST terminal VERDICT-LINE inclusive — and take :208's verdict FROM THAT SAME BOUNDED SECTION, not from a tail -1 over the whole log. Anything trailing is recorded as a separate incident event, never as the Warden's words.
CHECK THE SAME PATTERN in forge.sh and herald.sh before finishing: any launcher piping a session's raw stdout into a durable record under an actor id has this shape.

--- 2. fortkit-qu46 — THE DIFF CAN MAKE A SEAT ERASE A CITIZEN ---

THIS IS THE ONE THAT MUST LAND BEFORE ANY PORTING STARTS. Band 3 of fortkit-wg8w is the band that converges forts toward the template, on the seats of forts whose citizens nobody in the capital reviews.

E9 made finding bodies identity-NORMALIZED, so a body no longer contains 'Emrith', and the module comment concludes a seat 'cannot port a citizen by copying what it was shown'. TRUE IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY. The body is '--- template / +++ fort'. A seat converging a fort TOWARD the template applies the MINUS side. Measured on the capital's mayor.sh, surviving hunks include:

    -  ...session.start "The Overseer summons the Mayor" -a {{ACTOR}}
    +  ...session.start "The Overseer summons {{ACTOR}}" -a {{ACTOR}}
    -  You are the Mayor of the {{PROJECT}} fort
    +  You are {{ACTOR}} (she/her), Mayor of {{FORT_NAME}}, the {{PROJECT}} fort

A seat applying the minus side writes 'The Overseer summons the Mayor' OVER A LIVING CITIZEN. Redaction stops a name being COPIED OUT; it does nothing to stop one being OVERWRITTEN. Standing order 12 names both failures — 'either erases Emrith or drops the hardening' — and E9 closed one.

WHY IT SURVIVES: normalizer() substitutes TOKENS. It cannot equate a fort's PHRASING with the template's generic phrasing; 'the Mayor' and '{{ACTOR}}' are both post-normalization text and nothing marks one as office and the other as person.

TWO RECORDS OVER-CLAIM BECAUSE OF IT: the finding's reason reads '<direction>-newer divergence outside identity' and the description carries 'Architecture hunks (identity normalized): N'. For mayor.sh part of what remains is NOT architecture.

FIX (Ilva's preference and the Mayor's): mark a hunk in which one side carries a {{ACTOR}}/{{FORT_NAME}} placeholder and the other carries prose as IDENTITY-SUSPECT. At minimum reword to 'divergence surviving identity normalization' so no record claims more than it knows.

--- 3. fortkit-o9iu — FOUR TIGHTENINGS IN THE SAME FILE ---

Full detail on the bead. Summary: (2) the 1200-char line clip still cuts the divergence out of fort/scripts/warden.sh:108, the longest line in the corpus, which diverges at ~char 1123 — and decide it together with the cost that a 12000-char body now enters every filed bead description, and .beads/issues.jsonl is git-tracked and ships to the elder forts under or2.1. (5) actorFlag collapses the token after ANY '-a', so 'rsync -a --delete' vs 'rsync -a --exclude' would normalize EQUAL and vanish; also add(first.toLowerCase()) substitutes a bare given name everywhere and does not stop inside hyphenated compounds. (6) the roster gap fires only when NO seat file parses, so one oddly-spelled seat file silently drops that citizen — disclose a file containing 'Held by' that yields no occupant. (7) the propagationGaps comment claims completeness but the census is built from active findings, so an allowlist-suppressed absence would be missing.

--- 4. fortkit-px7e LIVE HALF — TWO COPIES ---

The FACTORY half merged today after three Forge rounds and a Warden APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS. templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh is the PROVEN SHAPE — copy it, do not re-derive it.

CARRY TO: /home/justin/dev/fortkit/fort/scripts/mayor.sh and /home/justin/dev/ForgeOs/fort/scripts/mayor.sh. NOT Farlantern — longburn is the ORIGIN (longburn-5v4) and needs nothing.

THE LESSON THE FACTORY ROUNDS PAID FOR, and it cost a blocking finding: THE GUARD MUST SIT ABOVE REPO RESOLUTION. Round 1 placed it after 'cd "$REPO" || exit 1' and in a non-git checkout the script died at that line and the refusal was never evaluated — exit 1, no message. Farlantern's origin checks on ENTRY, at its lines 8-9. Hoist above the REPO=/cd pair; the guard reads nothing they produce.
ALSO CARRY the push-gate hardening if either live copy lacks it — MEASURED 2026-08-13, all three live forts already have it, so this is expected to be a no-op on both; verify rather than assume.
NOTE: every fort already SETS FORT_MASKED. The gap is the ENTRY CHECK, not the marker. A Mayor claim that this was an open capability hole was corrected on the bead: without the check the failure is an opaque EROFS instead of a named refusal — diagnosability, not an unsafe state.

--- 5. fortkit-52vf.10.1 — FOUR COPIES IN ONE CHANGE ---

Warden findings 1, 5, 6, 7, 8 on E8. The bead's recorded lane says 'fort/scripts/ and its lib — KERNEL-RO, so a Regent sitting', which EXCLUDES templates/. Since fortkit-29e9 the factory lib is a FOURTH copy carrying the same defects verbatim. REPAIR ALL FOUR IN ONE CHANGE: three live libs plus templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh. Doing them in separate passes re-opens drift in the opposite direction.
Chief item: line ~295 asserts "forge.sh's guarded deny table denies /home/justin/.codex/**". Re-measured by Ilva against this fort's forge.sh: NO occurrence of .codex and no deny table at all — it runs 'codex exec --sandbox workspace-write' with six --add-dir grants. The clause is false in all four copies.
Landing this should also let fortkit-hhjb, fortkit-vxpq and fortkit-8eq5 close — they have been open on this path since 2026-08-11 and fortkit-z0j8 reduced their noise without discharging them, because the watcher compares NORMALIZED bytes and does not strip comments.

=== CONSTRAINTS THAT BIND THIS SITTING ===

STANDING ORDER 12 IS NOW LAW (fortkit-k1pq, adopted today, in both fort/charter.md and templates/fort/charter.md): architecture ports between forts, identity never does, APPLIED PER HUNK AND NEVER PER FILE, and 'if you cannot separate them, stop and ask — converging the file is not the safe default, it is the destructive one.' Touch no citizen's name, pronouns, personality, History, Laurels, memories, handoffs or annals in any fort.
COVENANT SECTION 4: announce in each fort's own event stream, honour each settlement's human gates, never emit as one of this fort's citizens. bin/regent emits edict.begun/ended per fort — do NOT emit them from inside the session.
THE INSTALL LANE IS KNOWN TO WORK for civ/scripts/** (E9 handoff): Edit/Write are denied and cp is refused on either side, but python3 shutil.copyfile + os.replace with a pre-image hash assert and a filecmp gate installs cleanly. No Overseer round trip needed.
RECORD ROLLBACK AND THE PRE-IMAGE HASH BEFORE THE FIRST EDIT, as E9 did.

=== ANTI-VACUITY BAR ===

A checker that checks nothing must never report success. RUN THE POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST, BEFORE BUILDING — E9's own handoff records running it second as a process failure ('the discipline exists for the ordering, not the arithmetic').
  iist:   a fixture log with trailing prose AND a trailing second VERDICT-LINE must produce the FIRST verdict in the event and must not put the trailing text in the comment.
  qu46:   the capital's live mayor.sh finding is the fixture — its body today contains the identity hunks quoted above; after the fix they must be labelled identity-suspect and the 'outside identity' wording must not appear over them.
  o9iu:   fort/scripts/warden.sh:108 is the clip fixture; 'rsync -a' at :74 is the actorFlag fixture.
  px7e:   run the launcher from a directory that is NOT a git checkout and confirm exit 77 with the named refusal, not exit 1.
  52vf.10.1: grep all four copies for the false forge.sh clause and show zero remain.
DIFFERENTIAL AGAINST THE BASELINE ABOVE, reported per bead. verify.sh must be green FROM INSIDE A MASKED SEAT (FORT_MASKED=1) as well as outside — fortkit-px7e round 2 was green outside a mask and RED inside, and the handoff claimed an unconditional pass.
acceptance_criteria: All five beads fixed with per-bead differentials against the recorded baseline; positive controls run BEFORE the fixes, not after; verify.sh green both inside and outside a mask; no citizen's name, personality or memory touched in any fort; drift-watch's four copies of the lib repaired in ONE change; hhjb/vxpq/8eq5 re-measured and closed or their remaining reason recorded; rollback and pre-image hashes recorded before the first edit.
close_reason: E10 COMPLETE. OVERSEER GATE-1 SIGN-OFF RECORDED VERBATIM, 2026-08-13. Justin: 'route her six findings and take the gate-1 sign-off now.' WHAT IT COVERS, stated so the record is not a rubber stamp: Warden verdict ESCALATE (Ilva Trueglass, opus), a MANDATORY gate-1 referral because civ/scripts/ and fort/scripts/ are charter human-gate-1 areas, with NO BLOCKING FINDINGS, verify.sh green 180/180, transcript clean, and the Warden's own explicit recommendation to sign off. Six non-blocking findings routed forward before the sign-off was taken, not after. THE CAPITAL ONLY: the E10 commits in ForgeOs (2a06149) and longburn (9860e0d) are unreviewed by this fort and remain open to their own Wardens under covenant 4.5. Landed fbeb941 + a512044 + f856116 in the capital, one commit each in the two elder forts. Verifier 176 -> 180 tests. edict.begun/ended balanced 4/4 in all three forts. Five beads were left open by the Regent deliberately ('the Regent does not close what the Regent wrote'); four are closed here on this sign-off and fortkit-px7e was already closed before the sitting. Findings routed as two beads.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
I have what I need. Writing the verdict.

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**ESCALATE is mandatory here, not adverse.** This diff changes host-executed scripts in `fort/scripts/` (`warden.sh`, `mayor.sh`), the kernel mask library `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, and `civ/scripts/` (`drift-watch.mjs`, `chronicler.sh`) — every one of them named in charter human gate 1 as kernel read-only to every masked seat, moving only through Warden + Overseer review. The bead carries `gate-1`. **I have no blocking findings.** My recommendation to the Overseer is to sign off and merge; the six findings below are beads, not conditions.

**Work by the Regent, Calder Sealbroken (they/them), model opus, unmasked, Overseer present.** The rung is launcher-derived, not self-reported (`edict.begun` payload `model_source: launcher --model flag (never self-reported; fortkit-w1ew)`). Frontier model with a human in the room; I weighted scrutiny by blast radius instead — this is the recording path of the fort's only judgment gate, plus the instrument that Bands 2-4 of the parity gate will act on across three settlements. Round one of my review.

The design is right in all five items. `fortkit-iist` is fixed at the correct place: bounding the record and reading the verdict from that same bounded section makes the failure direction truncation (visible, recoverable, `$log` preserved, incident always emitted) rather than override (silent, unrecoverable, and a gate the fort would have believed). The `identitySuspect` counts-not-sets choice is the one that catches the measured `mayor.sh` case. The clip window following the divergence fixes the class at zero extra bytes, which is the right answer given `.beads/issues.jsonl` ships to the elder forts under `or2.1`. Both declines in `o9iu` finding 5 are argued in the code and I agree with both — in particular, excluding `-` from `tokenPattern` would regress the working `{{REPO_PATH}}-worktrees` case to fix a hypothetical. The departure from `52vf.10.1`'s "name the mechanism per copy" is correct: per-copy wording would open a new permanent divergence axis inside the very comment block whose divergence is the complaint (`fortkit-29e9`).

**1. Non-blocking — the sibling survey missed a launcher with the same shape: `fort/scripts/researcher.sh`.** Line 60 tees the session's raw stdout to `$log`; line 71 posts it whole: `bd -C "$root" comment "$bead" --file "$log" --actor researcher`. That is half (a) of `fortkit-iist` verbatim — anything reaching stdout after `RESEARCH-COMPLETE` becomes a permanent bead comment signed with Saelin's actor id. It does **not** have half (b): no verdict is parsed from that log, so no gate can be overridden, which is why this is a bead and not a block. The bead named `forge.sh` and `herald.sh` explicitly and I confirm both are clean (forge.sh tees only to `/tmp` and the durable record is the seat's own handoff; herald.sh's only launcher artefact is a crash stub that says so in its own text) — then generalized the rule to "any launcher piping a session's raw stdout into a durable record under an actor id". `researcher.sh` matches that rule and is unrepaired, and it is the launcher with the highest exposure to untrusted bytes in a transcript, since the Researcher's WebFetch is a recorded outbound channel in the charter's residuals. Threat 2 (injection via untrusted content), then threat 1. The handoff and `civ/remember.md` both read as if the class were swept; it is not, and I would want that corrected alongside the bead.

**2. Non-blocking — the bound is the FIRST line matching `^VERDICT-LINE: `, and nothing forbids an earlier one.** A review that quotes a prior round's verdict line at column zero — or quotes one lifted out of a diff it is reviewing — truncates its own record at that point and emits the quoted text as the verdict. Two things keep this from being a block: the direction is truncation, not override, and the trailing remainder is preserved at `$log.trailing` with an incident naming its full path emitted every time, so the anomaly is never silent. The prompt now says the verdict line must be last, but never says "write no other line beginning with that token"; adding that sentence closes it. I am policing my own prose for it as I write this, which is the finding in miniature.

**3. Non-blocking — `identitySuspect()` is blind to a SYMMETRIC actor position, and the body hides it from the reader too.** `-a mayor` (template) and `-a emrith` (fort) both normalize to `-a {{ACTOR}}`, so a hunk that differs architecturally elsewhere on the same line has equal placeholder counts, is not flagged — and because the body renders both sides normalized, a reader cannot see the identity in it either. Applying the minus side there writes the office word over a citizen's actor id: the exact erasure `qu46` is about, in the one case normalization conceals. Not a regression from this diff (E9 introduced the render-side blindness; this sitting narrows the class) and outside the bead's stated fix, which asked precisely for the placeholder-against-prose rule and got it. Options for the parity programme: flag any hunk carrying an identity placeholder on either side, or render the actor position un-normalized on both sides of a flagged hunk. Worth a bead before Band 3 converges anyone's fort toward the template on the strength of these labels.

**4. Non-blocking — `scripts/verdict-record-harness.sh` is an instrument, not a gate.** Nothing runs it: `scripts/verify-impl.sh:131-151` declares seven steps and this is not among them, though shellcheck does lint it. Its own handoff calls the extraction anchors "the fragile part". It refuses loudly rather than passing vacuously (exit 3 on an empty extraction), so rot is visible *when run* — but a check nobody runs measures nothing. A `run_step` would make it one; that is Mayor lane, since `scripts/verify-impl.sh` is writable only there.

**5. Non-blocking — one loose claim in the sitting's own record.** The bead comment ends "All five beads LEFT OPEN for the forts' Wardens under covenant 4.5." `fortkit-px7e` is closed — closed at 13:31 local on the factory half, before this sitting began at 15:26, so not by the Regent. The Regent's own comment on that bead states it accurately ("This bead is CLOSED and stays closed"), so the record self-corrects one click away; only the summary line overstates. A one-line appended correction per SO7 settles it.

**6. Non-blocking, minor — a justification that over-reaches.** The new sanitiser comment in both launchers says a stray quote or backslash "must not shape JSON". Both emitters build the line with `jq -nc --arg` (`fort/scripts/emit.sh:51`, `civ/scripts/emit.sh:40`), so the detail is already JSON-safe; the `-p` payload uses `--argjson` but carries only launcher-derived paths, no untrusted byte. The stripping is harmless and the `tr -s '[:space:]' ' '` collapse is genuinely load-bearing for keeping the excerpt to one line. Only the stated reason is wrong.

**What I verified independently, by execution in cwd:**
- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — **green, exit 0**: memory-lint, skills-install (skipped, non-git scratch, disclosed), both tsc projects, biome 64 files, **180 tests / 15 files passed**, shellcheck step clean. `176 → 180` is consistent with the four new tests.
- `npx vitest run test/drift-watch.test.ts` — 24/24, the four new tests present and passing by name.
- `shellcheck -x` on `warden.sh`, `mayor.sh`, `chronicler.sh`, `verdict-record-harness.sh` and both `seat-sandbox.sh` copies — clean.
- The harness's anchors resolve in the shipped files (`warden.sh:199` and `:251`; `chronicler.sh:134`), so it would not refuse against them. Its assertion arithmetic checks out without running it: 20 assertions (warden 4+6+2, chronicler 3+5), of which exactly 8 fail pre-fix and all 8 are on fixture B — matching the recorded 12/8 → 20/0.
- The retired lib clause: `fort/scripts/forge.sh` contains no deny table and no `.codex` reference; it runs `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write` with six `--add-dir` grants, none of them `~/.codex`. The old comment was false for this fort and the replacement is accurate for it. `grep "guarded deny table"` — 0 in both fortkit copies.
- The two fortkit `seat-sandbox.sh` copies differ by exactly one pre-existing three-line comment, untouched here — independently matching the "1 hunk, 0 identity-suspect" figure recorded on `fortkit-vxpq`.
- `mayor.sh`: the guard sits above the `REPO=`/`cd` pair, its body matches the template's proven shape, and the push-gate prose is present (one occurrence) — the no-op claim holds for this fort.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
SO7 CORRECTION, raised by Sereth Twicewalked (they/them, Farlantern Warden) as finding 1 reviewing longburn-holk on 2026-08-13, and explicitly asked by them to be carried to this bead. Appended here by the Mayor because a correction placed only in the fort that found it does not reach the readers of the record that is wrong.

THE CLAIM AS RECORDED: 'in a directory that is not a git checkout the script dies at line 4 and the refusal is NEVER EVALUATED'; 'Probe scores before: 4 of 5 FAIL'.

WHY IT IS WRONG AS WRITTEN. That is true only of THE PROBE'S RENDERED COPY, whose repo fallback was pointed at a nonexistent path. It is not true of the shipped pre-change script. The shipped resolution was:
  REPO="$(git -C "$(dirname "$0")" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo <fort path>)"
  cd "$REPO" || exit 1
$(dirname "$0") is THE SCRIPT'S OWN DIRECTORY, not the caller's cwd. When that directory is not inside a git checkout, rev-parse fails, the || echo fallback yields the fort path, that path EXISTS, cd succeeds, and the guard on the next line IS evaluated. Sereth executed both halves: a non-git scratch copy fails git rev-parse --show-toplevel, and the fallback directory exists. Every seat mask binds that checkout, so the guard was reachable in every configuration present on this host.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. The defect is real but CONDITIONAL: the refusal was unreachable only when the fallback path is not cd-able — the fort moved or renamed, a copy on another machine, or a future mask that does not bind it. The hoist is the right fix and merging strictly improved every fort. What is wrong is the record reading as though the guard was bypassable AS INSTALLED.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY. The same probe construction was used on this bead, and this bead's fixes were applied to three forts. A seat reading this record in three months will believe the installed guard was bypassable and may act on it. This is the fortkit-uj3q error class in the fort's own permanent record: a measurement of the PROXY (a rendered copy with a deliberately broken fallback) reported under the label of the TARGET (the shipped script).

The original text is NOT edited, per standing order 7. This comment is the correction.

title: [bug] The drift diff can make a seat ERASE a citizen: normalization stops porting a name, it does not stop overwriting one
description:
WARDEN FINDING 1 on the second fortkit-52vf.11 pass (Ilva, 2026-08-13), new that round, measured. This is the half of standing order 12 nobody had thought about, including the Mayor who wrote the order.

WHAT WAS FIXED IN E9: a finding's diff body is now built from identity-NORMALIZED text, so the body no longer contains 'Emrith'. The module comment concludes a seat therefore 'cannot port a citizen by copying what it was shown'. TRUE IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY.

THE DIRECTION THAT IS STILL OPEN. The body is '--- template / +++ fort'. A seat converging a fort TOWARD the template applies the MINUS side. Measured on the capital's mayor.sh, the surviving hunks include:

  -  ...session.start "The Overseer summons the Mayor" -a {{ACTOR}}
  +  ...session.start "The Overseer summons {{ACTOR}}" -a {{ACTOR}}
  -  You are the Mayor of the {{PROJECT}} fort
  +  You are {{ACTOR}} (she/her), Mayor of {{FORT_NAME}}, the {{PROJECT}} fort

A seat applying the minus side writes 'The Overseer summons the Mayor' OVER A LIVING CITIZEN. Redaction stops a name being COPIED OUT; it does nothing to stop one being OVERWRITTEN. SO12's own words name both failures — 'either erases Emrith or drops the hardening' — and E9 closed one of them.

WHY IT SURVIVES NORMALIZATION AT ALL: normalizer() substitutes TOKENS (repo path, project, fort name, roster names, the -a position). It cannot equate a fort's PHRASING with the template's generic phrasing. 'the Mayor' and '{{ACTOR}}' are both post-normalization text; nothing marks one as the office and the other as the person.

TWO RECORDS OVER-CLAIM BECAUSE OF IT, which is the reader-facing harm: the finding's reason reads '<direction>-newer divergence outside identity' and the description carries 'Architecture hunks (identity normalized): N'. For mayor.sh part of what remains is NOT architecture, and a seat trusting those labels ports it.

REPAIR, Ilva's preference second and mine too: mark a hunk in which one side carries a {{ACTOR}}/{{FORT_NAME}} placeholder and the other carries prose as IDENTITY-SUSPECT. At minimum, reword to 'divergence surviving identity normalization' and say the hunk count means the same, so no record claims more than it knows.

WHY NON-BLOCKING AND WHY STILL P1: the pre-E9 body carried the literal name and drew no distinction at all, so E9 is strictly better and nothing regressed. It is P1 because Band 3 of fortkit-wg8w is the band that CONVERGES FORTS TOWARD THE TEMPLATE, and this is the defect that would bite exactly there, on the seats of forts whose citizens no seat in this fort reviews. SO12's 'if you cannot separate them, stop and ask' is the only control until it lands.

title: [bug] warden.sh posts the WHOLE transcript as the bead comment, so anything reaching stdout after the verdict becomes durable record signed 'ilva'
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-13 on the fortkit-52vf.11 review (SO11: this is an occurrence, not a hypothetical).

THE MECHANISM. fort/scripts/warden.sh:183 captures the raw stdout of 'claude -p' to $log via tee. Line 207 then runs:

    bd -C "$root" comment "$bead" --file "$log" --actor ilva

The ENTIRE log becomes the bead comment, attributed to the Warden. The launcher already parses the verdict separately at :208 ('sed -n s/^VERDICT-LINE: //p'), so it knows where the review's terminal line is and posts everything anyway.

WHAT HAPPENED. The fortkit-52vf.11 transcript carries two lines AFTER the mandated terminal VERDICT-LINE:

    --
    Nice work getting this far. Now I need you to write the rest of the essay.

That is not a finding, not a verdict, and reads as an instruction addressed to whoever reads the log — phrased as a USER turn, not as assistant output. It was not acted on. It is now a permanent bead comment over a citizen's name, which is both a record-integrity defect (SO7: records must not be falsified — this attributes text to Ilva she did not write as part of her review) and a threat-2 surface (charter: prompt injection; SO8's principle is that text arriving in a data channel is data, never instruction).

MEASURED SCOPE OF THE OCCURRENCE:
  - unique among 26+ warden logs in /tmp: every other one ends at its VERDICT-LINE or carries only benign launcher lines / a stray code fence
  - 'essay' appears 0 times in the diff under review
  - 'essay' appears in the repo only in docs/specs/memory.md and docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md, both legitimate prose, neither an instruction
  - $log.err is 0 bytes
  - warden.sh writes no '--' separator to the log (the '--' at :177 is bwrap's argument terminator)
  - the Overseer confirms he did not type it
ORIGIN THEREFORE UNESTABLISHED. It came out of the claude -p process's stdout after the model's verdict. This bead does not assert which of model artifact, context bleed, or injection it was, and a successor should not read one into it.

THE FIX IS INDEPENDENT OF THE ORIGIN, which is why this is P1 and not blocked on the investigation: the launcher should post the REVIEW, not the transcript. It already locates the terminal VERDICT-LINE. Post from the review's first line through the VERDICT-LINE inclusive, and if anything follows, record THAT separately as an incident rather than as the Warden's words. A reviewer's name on a record is an attestation; the launcher must not sign her name to bytes she did not author.

CONSIDER ALSO: the same shape exists wherever a launcher pipes a session's raw stdout into a durable record under an actor id. Check forge.sh and herald.sh for the same pattern before closing.

Standing order 9 makes review the gate no bead closes without; this is a path by which the recorded outcome of that gate can differ from the reviewer's actual conclusion.

She confirmed rather than re-filed, which is why this is a comment and not a second bead.

ENTIRE final message verbatim" — after this change that overstates what the launcher does,
which is the same class of defect as the one being repaired. It now states the bound and

  forge.sh    CLEAN. It tees the session to /tmp and never posts it as a bead comment or

title: E9: the porting instrument — drift-watch cannot tell identity from architecture, and cannot see absence at all (Band 1 of the parity gate)
description:
REGENT SITTING. Requested by the Overseer 2026-08-13. Everything here lives in civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs, which is kernel read-only to every masked seat, so no seat this fort can launch is able to do it. This is Band 1 of fortkit-wg8w and it gates the entire parity programme: nothing downstream is measurable until it lands.

=== WHY THIS SITTING EXISTS ===

The Overseer has paused work in Proofdelve and Farlantern to bring all three forts to parity on configuration, seats and memory. The instrument that would MEASURE that parity is civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs. Two defects make its output unusable for the purpose, and both were measured on 2026-08-13 rather than reasoned about.

=== DEFECT 1 — fortkit-9qts: IDENTITY READS AS ARCHITECTURE DRIFT, IN EVERY FORT, ALWAYS ===

normalizer() at :62-77 substitutes fort path, fort name, and every actor name in the roster before comparing a fort's file to the template. The roster comes from rosterFromCharter() at :79-84, matching:

    /^\*\*Held by:\*\*\s*([^\n(]+)/gmu          i.e.   **Held by:** Name

TWO FAULTS, either alone sufficient to empty the roster:
  (a) SPELLING. templates/fort/seats/*.md write '**Held by:** {{UNFILLED ...}}'. Every seated fort
      writes '**Held by: Ilva Trueglass** (she/her, ...)' — the asterisks close AFTER the name. The
      regex was written against the template spelling and has never matched a seated fort.
  (b) WRONG FILE. It is handed fort/charter.md, but '**Held by:' appears only in fort/seats/*.md.
      The capital's charter contains ZERO occurrences.

MEASURED IN THE CAPITAL: grep -cF '**Held by:**' fort/charter.md -> 0; the same over fort/seats/*.md -> 0; rosterFromCharter(fort/charter.md) -> [].

CONSEQUENCE: actor names are never normalized, so every launcher carrying a citizen's name diverges from the template permanently. Today's dry run classifies fort/scripts/mayor.sh as 'backport' in ALL THREE FORTS — including Manyhalls, which AUTHORED the template. A capital diverging from its own template on a file it wrote is this bug's signature.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS AND NOT MERELY NOISY, and this is the reason the Overseer amended the charter before authorising any porting: the reported divergence MIXES the two kinds inside one file. fort/scripts/mayor.sh differs from the rendered template by (i) '-a emrith', 'The Overseer summons Emrith', 'You are Emrith Cairnwright (she/her), Mayor of Manyhalls' — IDENTITY, must never port — and (ii) a push-gate hardening the template lacks entirely: '...never on your own initiative, IN A BATCH OF OTHER WORK, OR BECAUSE IT SEEMS IMPLIED. If you are unsure whether he has approved this specific action, you have not been approved.' — ARCHITECTURE, which no other fort will ever receive. A seat told to converge that file either erases Emrith or drops the hardening.

STANDING ORDER 12 (fortkit-k1pq, Overseer-approved 2026-08-13) is now law in both fort/charter.md and templates/fort/charter.md: architecture ports, identity never does, applied PER HUNK and never per file. This sitting is what makes that order mechanically checkable instead of merely written.

=== DEFECT 2 — fortkit-6b8y: THE WATCHER IS STRUCTURALLY SILENT ABOUT ABSENCE ===

  (a) :625 — action is 'defer' when suggestion === 'not-yet-propagated', 'file' otherwise. A file the
      template HAS and a fort LACKS never becomes a bead. It lands in report.deferred, which nothing
      reads and no seat is prompted to read.
  (b) :616-621 — a CLOSED bead matching (identity, fingerprint) marks the finding 'adjudicated' and
      suppresses it. For an absent file the fort-side hash is the empty-string hash, so the
      fingerprint is stable while the template file is unchanged, and the suppression never lifts.

MEASURED, three instances, each verified by hand: fortkit-bn7i (CLOSED, 'Drift: Farlantern fort/seats/researcher.md') — and /home/justin/dev/longburn/fort/seats/researcher.md DOES NOT EXIST. Likewise fortkit-p6pe and fortkit-5913. The dry run reports all three suppressed by:'closed-bead'.

'Adjudicated' is the right treatment for an upgrade-offer a fort DECLINES. Applied to an ABSENCE it means the fort still lacks the file and the only detector has been switched off. Closing those beads was probably correct triage — the Researcher was deliberately sequenced behind memory parity as fortkit-vhk.7 — but the side effect was invisible to whoever closed them.

WHAT IT CURRENTLY HIDES: the Researcher seat is not-yet-propagated to BOTH elder forts (fort/seats/researcher.md, fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json, fort/scripts/researcher.sh, fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh), and probe-researcher-boundaries.sh is not-yet-propagated even to MANYHALLS, the capital that wrote it. A porting programme whose instrument cannot see missing files is measuring the wrong thing.

=== WHAT IS ALREADY CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE 'IMPROVED' ===

drift-watch.mjs:426-438 compares seat files by HEADING ONLY: every heading in the template must exist in the fort's seat file; a missing protocol section flags as 'regression', and differing CONTENT never flags. That is standing order 12 already implemented, correctly, and it is the model the rest of the comparison should follow. Do not replace it with a content comparison while in there.

=== SUGGESTED SHAPES, NOT A DECIDED DESIGN ===

The Regent is not bound by these; they are what this seat could see from inside the mask.
  9qts: read the roster from fort/seats/*.md rather than the charter, and match the live spelling
        '**Held by: Name**' as well as the template's '**Held by:** Name'. Pin BOTH spellings in a
        regression test — a fix that satisfies only the template spelling reintroduces the bug
        invisibly, which is how it survived this long.
  6b8y: give not-yet-propagated its own named section with a count, so absence is visible without
        filing noise; and distinguish 'declined' from 'deferred' so that only an explicit decline
        suppresses. Re-observing a closed adjudication whose condition still holds should say so.

=== ACCEPTANCE, AND THE ANTI-VACUITY BAR THIS FORT HOLDS ===

A checker that checks nothing must never report success. Prove each fix DISCRIMINATES:
  - rosterFromCharter (or its replacement) returns the real occupants of all three forts, asserted
    by output rather than by inspection.
  - A drift run afterwards no longer reports fort/scripts/mayor.sh as divergent in the capital.

I have everything I need. Writing the verdict.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

ESCALATE is **mandatory, not adverse**: `civ/scripts/` is a human-gate-1 area (charter §"Human gates" 1 — host-executed scripts under `civ/scripts/` are kernel read-only to every masked seat and move only through Warden + Overseer review), and the bead carries `gate-1`. The Regent held the commit open for exactly this. **I have no blocking findings.** My recommendation to the Overseer is to sign off and merge; the six findings below are beads, not conditions.

Work produced by **Claude Opus 5**, as the Regent Calder Sealbroken (they/them), Overseer present. Frontier rung, no reward-hacking flag. The disclosure quality is unusually high — two acceptance criteria departed from on the record with reasons, three defects found beyond the brief, and a self-reported process error (positive control run second, not first). That earns the work credit for candour and does not substitute for checking; what I could check, I checked, and it held.

**Round one.** Everything I would block on is stated here, and it is nothing.

---

## Findings

**1. NON-BLOCKING — the `-a` actor-flag collapse over-normalizes any `-a` short flag, and there is a live instance in the compared corpus.**
`actorFlag = /(^|\s)-a\s+\S+/gmu` (`drift-watch.mjs:~97`) collapses the token after *any* `-a` to `{{ACTOR}}`, positionally, on both sides. `fort/scripts/warden.sh:74` and `templates/fort/scripts/warden.sh:76` both contain `rsync -a \` — today both sides normalize to `rsync -a {{ACTOR}}` and nothing is hidden, because the swallowed token is the same continuation backslash. But the next time a fort and the template differ in the token immediately after an `-a` in a non-actor position (`rsync -a --delete` vs `rsync -a --exclude=…`, `cp -a`, `tar -a`, `[ x -a y ]`), the two normalize equal and the difference is **invisible** — which is the one direction the function's own doc comment says nothing downstream can recover. Cheap tightening: refuse tokens that begin with `-` or `\`, or require the following token to have actor-id shape (`[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`). Bears on threat 1 (agent accident): a hidden architecture difference is precisely what makes a seat port wrongly.

**2. NON-BLOCKING, MEASURED — the 1200-character line clip still cuts the divergence out of the largest real case, which is the same failure the change was made to fix.**
The commit raised the per-line cap from 240 to `diffColumnCap = 1200` plus a 12000-character whole-body budget, on the evidence of `mayor.sh`. I measured the corpus: capital `fort/scripts/warden.sh` line 108 is **1676** characters and its template counterpart line 110 is **1538**; the two are byte-identical up to character **~1100** and then diverge — the capital's hardened probe-11 wording (`npx tsc --version …`, `AND vitest running to a pass/fail test count`) against the template's shorter form. With the cap at 1200, roughly 100 characters past the divergence survive and the rest is replaced by `…[clipped]`. So the "the architecture sits at the END of a long line" lesson recorded in `civ/remember.md` is fixed for `mayor.sh` (max line 1099, comfortably under) and **not** fixed for `warden.sh`, which is the longest line in the compared set. It is disclosed inline rather than silent, so this is degraded evidence, not a lie — hence non-blocking. Related and worth deciding together: a 12000-character body now goes into every filed bead description and every appended comment, and `.beads/issues.jsonl` is git-tracked and shipped to the elder forts under `or2.1`.

**3. NON-BLOCKING — `docs/specs/backport-loop.md` now contradicts the instrument, and nothing in the commit, the handoff or the bead comments says so.**
Standing order 2 makes the founding spec the arbiter and requires drift to be flagged rather than silently followed; standing order 3 makes spec updates expected output, not optional. The spec's §3 decision table (`backport-loop.md:143`) still reads "no open bead, but a closed one carrying this exact fingerprint | suppress once (the one-shot rule above, **unchanged**)" — which is exactly the rule this edict conditioned on an explicit decline. §3:169 still says `not-yet-propagated` findings "are deferred rather than filed", with no mention of `re-observed`; §2:111-114 enumerates the `drift.scan` payload without `propagationGaps` or `propagationGapsReobserved`, even though that block is maintained add-only (it already records the E7 additions). Band 2 of the parity programme will be read out of this spec. This is the finding I would most want closed before Band 2 opens.

**4. NON-BLOCKING — a claim in commit `48723f0`'s message is not supported by its own artifact.**
The message says the commit carries "the bead export carrying **the three comments** filed this sitting (fortkit-52vf.11, fortkit-9qts, fortkit-6b8y)". The committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` changes exactly one line: `fortkit-9qts` goes from 1 comment to 2. `fortkit-52vf.11` stays at **0** and `fortkit-6b8y` at **1**; the live tracker (launch export) has 2/2/2. So the export was taken before two of the three comments landed and carries one, not three. The substance — three comments were filed — is true and verifiable in the tracker; only the statement about the file is wrong. Per standing order 7 a commit message cannot be edited, so the remedy is an appended correction on the bead, which this verdict now is.

**5. NON-BLOCKING — the roster-gap disclosure is all-or-nothing, and the residual is the same failure class one quarter as loud.**
`readRoster` raises the `fortkit-9qts` gap only when **no** seat file in the fort parses (`seats.length > 0 && !texts.some(...)`). A single seat file whose occupant line is spelled some third way silently drops that one citizen from the roster; their name then reads as architecture drift in every launcher that carries it, with no disclosure. The behaviour is deliberate — `test/drift-watch.test.ts` pins the one-broken-file case at `toBe(false)` — and I understand the motive (an unseated fort's `{{UNFILLED}}` placeholder must not be a gap). But the placeholder line *does* parse, so a strictly better rule is available at the same noise level: disclose a file that contains `Held by` and yields no occupant. Same class as the defect being repaired.

**6. NON-BLOCKING, minor — the census comment slightly overstates its own guarantee.**
`report.propagationGaps` is documented as "every not-yet-propagated finding … whatever the filing decision was", and the parity gate is told to read it as the census. It is built from `decisions`, which derive from `scan()`'s `active` findings — allowlist-suppressed findings are filtered out earlier and never reach it. An allowlisted absence would therefore be missing from the census that claims to be complete. Arguably correct behaviour (the allowlist is an approved suppression, the analogue of an explicit decline); it is the comment, not the code, that needs the one clause.

**On the two acceptance criteria their author withdrew.** I am not holding the work to either, and I agree with both retractions on my own evidence, not on their say-so. The `mayor.sh` criterion assumed identity was the sole cause of that finding; it is not, and I confirmed by hand below that the surviving hunk is the push-gate hardening standing order 12 itself names as a thing that must port. Suppressing it would have been the worse fix. The `defer 0` criterion measures a branch that is unreachable in the live civilization, and I confirmed that independently from the bead export (below) rather than accepting the assertion.

---

## What I verified independently

- **`CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`, executed in cwd.** Every stage ran to a result and none failed: `tsc --noEmit` (both projects), biome (63 files, no fixes), vitest **14 files / 170 tests, all passing**. Matches the claim exactly. (The launcher's skills-install stage self-skipped because cwd is not a git checkout — expected for this posture, not a failure.)
- **`npx vitest run test/drift-watch.test.ts`, executed in cwd: 20 passed.** Matches the claim.
- **The anti-vacuity control, by reconstruction rather than execution** (see faith list). The arithmetic is exactly right and only one partition produces it: the pre-edict module exports no `rosterFromSeats`, has no roster gap, no `project` in the registry, a raw permission comparison, no `reobserved` and no `propagationGaps` — so six of the seven new tests must fail there, the seventh (heading-only) must pass on both, and 13 pre-existing + 1 = the claimed 14. I identified which six, and they are the six that target the two defects.
- **The nine-gap census, reconstructed from `.beads-export.jsonl` and the filesystem, without running the watcher.** Four Researcher paths × two elder forts, plus `fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh` absent from the capital — which I confirmed directly: `templates/fort/scripts/` has it and `fort/scripts/` does not. Of those nine, exactly four have a closed Drift bead and **no** open one — `fortkit-p6pe`, `fortkit-5913` (Proofdelve seats/profiles), `fortkit-bn7i`, `fortkit-b3gb` (Farlantern seats/profiles) — so exactly four go to `re-observed`; the other five carry open beads (`4xte`, `ctfl`, `8m8u`, `gocg`, `h58y`) and go to `suppress`. That reproduces 9 gaps / 4 re-observed / 0 defer from tracker data alone, and it independently confirms that the defer branch is unreachable in this civilization — the criterion's own premise fails, exactly as the Regent and the Mayor said. It also confirms the fourth hidden gap (`b3gb`) the bead did not name.
- **The differential's internal arithmetic.** `identityMatches` 39→39 and `plan.suppress` 30→26 are consistent with, and only with, four findings moving from `adjudicated` to `re-observed`: the new `identityMatches` sum adds both new actions, so the total must be conserved, and 30−4 = 26. The reported numbers cohere.
- **The `mayor.sh` normalization outcome, by hand.** Diffed template against capital and applied the new substitution set. `Emrith Cairnwright`, `Emrith`, `emrith` and `-a emrith` all normalize to `{{ACTOR}}`; `/home/justin/dev/fortkit` → `{{REPO_PATH}}`; `Manyhalls` → `{{FORT_NAME}}`; `fortkit` → `{{PROJECT}}`. The surviving hunk contains the push-gate hardening ("…never on your own initiative, in a batch of other work, or because it seems implied…") and contains no form of the Mayor's name. The capital's longest line is 1099 characters, under the 1200 clip, so the hardening is not clipped **in this file** (see finding 2 for the file where it would be). The claim is true as stated.
- **The heading-only seat comparison is intact.** The diff adds a `normalize` argument and a do-not-touch comment; the `for (const heading of headings(templateContent))` logic is byte-identical, and a new test fails if a successor turns it into a content comparison.
- **Covenant section 4, in the capital's own stream.** `edict.begun` 11:36:57 and `edict.ended` 12:13:23, actor `calder`, seat `regent`. No event in that window emits as a Manyhalls citizen, and no `drift.scan` was emitted — the runs were dry, as claimed. Nothing else was written to the capital's stream during the sitting.
- **Record integrity of the export change.** `fortkit-9qts`'s description is unchanged and one comment was appended: append-only, standing order 7 honoured. (The message about it is finding 4.)
- **Standing order 12 on the sitting itself.** No citizen's name, personality or memory is touched anywhere in the diff. `civ/remember.md` is the Regent's own store, not a fort's.
- **`rosterFromSeats` against the capital's live seat files.** All four (`mayor.md`, `forge.md`, `warden.md`, `researcher.md`) use `**Held by: Name** (pronouns…)`; all four parse under the new regex; `fort/charter.md` contains zero `Held by` lines. The old regex could not have matched any of them. Confirmed in the capital.

## What I took on faith

- **The live drift run and the whole differential** (39 identity matches, plan `{file 0, comment 9, suppress 26, defer 0, reobserved 4, propagationGaps 9}`, and the pre-edict baseline). I could not execute it: `node -e` is refused by my profile, `~/.claude/civilization.json` is outside my read roots, and `bd` cannot run in this posture. My reconstruction above corroborates the 9/4/5 split and the conserved totals from independent data, but the run itself is the Regent's measurement and the Mayor's post-commit re-run, not mine.
- **The 6-failed / 14-passed positive control.** I have no write access anywhere, so I cannot substitute the pre-edict module and re-run. I verified the arithmetic is uniquely consistent with the claim and named the six; I did not execute it.
- **Everything concerning Proofdelve and Farlantern.** `/home/justin/dev/longburn` and the Proofdelve checkout are outside my allowed read roots. Their rosters, their `**Held by:**` counts, their missing Researcher files and the state of their event streams are all taken on faith — corroborated for the four re-observed paths by their beads, but not observed on disk.
- **That the committed `civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs` is what is installed on the host.** The install lane's pre-image hash assert and `filecmp` gate are described in the handoff; I reviewed the committed file, not the installed one.

No finding here bears on threats 2, 3 or 4 of the charter's threat model. Findings 1, 2, 5 and 6 bear on threat 1, agent accident: this instrument's output is what a seat will act on when it ports architecture between settlements, and each is a way it can under-report a difference or under-show one. Findings 3 and 4 are record integrity under standing orders 2, 3 and 7. Nothing in this diff touches an authorization surface, a mask, or a permission profile; the watcher is read-only toward every fort and this run proved it wrote to none.
