- the identity half of the launch line: `You are the Mayor of the {{PROJECT}} fort` against `You are {{ACTOR}} (she/her), Mayor of {{FORT_NAME}}, the {{PROJECT}} fort`

The bead itself names `"The Overseer summons Emrith"` as identity that must never port, and it still surfaces. Two consequences. (a) The finding's `reason` now reads `"${direction}-newer divergence outside identity"` and the description carries `Architecture hunks (identity normalized): N` — both assert that what remains is architecture; for `mayor.sh` part of it is not. (b) The module doc comment says a seat "cannot port a citizen by copying what it was shown". True in the fort→fort direction — the name is genuinely absent from the body. But the body is `--- template / +++ fort`, so a seat converging a fort *toward* the template applies the `-` side and writes `"The Overseer summons the Mayor"` over a living citizen. Redaction stops porting a name; it does not stop **erasing** one, which is the other half of what standing order 12 warns about ("either erases Emrith or drops the hardening"). Cheap repair, and I'd take the second: mark a hunk in which one side carries a `{{ACTOR}}`/`{{FORT_NAME}}` placeholder and the other carries prose as identity-suspect; or, at minimum, reword to "divergence surviving identity normalization" and say the hunk count means the same. Why non-blocking: the pre-E9 body carried the literal name and made no distinction at all, so this is strictly better, and SO12's "if you cannot separate them, stop and ask" still binds the seat. Bears on threat 1 (agent accident). It does **not** produce a false finding — both sides are normalized symmetrically — it mislabels a true one.

**2. NON-BLOCKING, MEASURED — the 1200-character line clip still cuts the divergence out of the largest real case, which is the same failure the change was made to fix.**
The commit raised the per-line cap from 240 to `diffColumnCap = 1200` plus a 12000-character whole-body budget, on the evidence of `mayor.sh`. Measured on the compared corpus: exactly one line ≥1200 characters exists in `fort/scripts/warden.sh` (line 108) and one in `templates/fort/scripts/warden.sh` (line 110), and they are byte-identical through roughly character **1123** — `...11) VERIFIER CAPACITY (fortkit-8cv6) — run: ` — then diverge, the capital's hardened probe-11 wording (`npx tsc --version`, and vitest running to a pass/fail result) against the template's shorter form. At a 1200 cap, about 77 characters past the divergence survive and the rest becomes `…[clipped]`. So the "architecture sits at the END of a long line" lesson recorded in `civ/remember.md` is fixed for `mayor.sh` (no line ≥1100 there, confirmed) and **not** fixed for `warden.sh`, which holds the longest line in the set. Disclosed inline rather than silently, so this is degraded evidence, not a lie. Worth deciding together with the sibling: a 12000-character body now goes into every filed bead description and appended comment, up from 1200, and `.beads/issues.jsonl` is git-tracked and shipped to the elder forts under `or2.1`.

**3. NON-BLOCKING — `docs/specs/backport-loop.md` now contradicts the instrument, and nothing in the commit, the handoff or the bead comments says so.**
Standing order 2 makes the founding spec the arbiter and requires drift to be flagged rather than silently followed; standing order 3 makes spec updates expected output. `backport-loop.md:143` still reads "no open bead, but a closed one carrying this exact fingerprint | suppress once (the one-shot rule above, **unchanged**)" — the exact rule this edict conditioned on an explicit decline. `:169` still says `not-yet-propagated` findings "are deferred rather than filed", with no mention of re-observation. The §3.3 `drift.scan` payload enumeration lists the E7 add-only additions (`findingsCommented`, `findingsDeferred`, `allowlistLapsed`) and not `propagationGaps` / `propagationGapsReobserved`. Band 2 of the parity programme will be read out of this spec. This is the finding I would most want closed before Band 2 opens.

**4. NON-BLOCKING — a claim in commit `48723f0`'s message is not supported by its own artifact.**
The message says the commit carries "the bead export carrying **the three comments** filed this sitting (fortkit-52vf.11, fortkit-9qts, fortkit-6b8y)". Measured across the two blobs: `.beads/issues.jsonl` changes exactly one line — `fortkit-9qts` goes 1 comment → 2. `fortkit-52vf.11` stays at **0** and `fortkit-6b8y` at **1**. The launch export shows the live tracker at 4/2/2. So the snapshot was taken before two of the three comments landed and carries one, not three. The substance — three comments were filed — is true and verifiable in the tracker; only the statement about the file is wrong. I considered this against the blocking bar's "false or unsupported claim in a record" clause and rank it non-blocking: the claim's substance holds, the artifact is a snapshot that always lags, standing order 7 forbids editing the message, and the prescribed remedy is an appended correction on the bead — which this verdict now is. Blocking would not repair the sentence; it would only withhold a correct fix.

**5. NON-BLOCKING — the `-a` actor-flag collapse over-normalizes any `-a` short flag, and there is a live instance in the compared corpus.**
`actorFlag = /(^|\s)-a\s+\S+/gmu` collapses the token after *any* `-a`, positionally, on both sides. `fort/scripts/warden.sh:74` and `templates/fort/scripts/warden.sh:76` both contain `rsync -a \`; today both normalize to `rsync -a {{ACTOR}}` and nothing is hidden, because the swallowed token is the same continuation backslash. The next time a fort and the template differ in the token immediately after an `-a` in a non-actor position (`rsync -a --delete` vs `rsync -a --exclude=…`, `cp -a`, `tar -a`, `[ x -a y ]`), the two normalize equal and the difference is **invisible** — the one direction the function's own doc comment says nothing downstream can recover. Cheap tightening: refuse tokens beginning with `-` or `\`, or require actor-id shape (`[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`). Same class, and I'd fold it into the same bead: `add(first.toLowerCase(), "{{ACTOR}}")` substitutes a bare lowercased given name everywhere, and `tokenPattern`'s guards do not stop substitution inside hyphenated compounds (`fortkit-other` → `{{PROJECT}}-other`). Neither has bitten yet, which under standing order 11 is why this is a note on a diff under review rather than a hardening bead of its own.

**6. NON-BLOCKING — the roster-gap disclosure is all-or-nothing, and the residual is the same failure class one quarter as loud.**
`readRoster` raises the `fortkit-9qts` gap only when **no** seat file in the fort parses (`seats.length > 0 && !texts.some(...)`), and `test/drift-watch.test.ts:613` pins the one-broken-file case at `toBe(false)`. A single seat file whose occupant line is spelled some third way silently drops that one citizen; their name then reads as architecture drift in every launcher carrying it, undisclosed. The motive is sound — an unseated fort's `{{UNFILLED}}` placeholder must not raise a gap — but that placeholder line *does* parse, so a strictly better rule is available at the same noise level: disclose a seat file that contains `Held by` and yields no occupant.

**7. NON-BLOCKING, minor — the census comment slightly overstates its own guarantee.**
`report.propagationGaps` is documented as "every not-yet-propagated finding … whatever the filing decision was", and the parity gate is told to read it as the census. It is built from `decisions`, which derive from `scan()`'s `active` findings; allowlist-suppressed findings are filtered out at `drift-watch.mjs:715-740` and never reach it. An allowlisted absence would be missing from a census that claims completeness. Arguably correct behaviour — an allowlist entry is an approved suppression, the analogue of an explicit decline — so it is the comment, not the code, that needs the one clause.

---

## On the two acceptance criteria their author withdrew

I am not holding the work to either, and I agree with both retractions on my own evidence rather than on their say-so.

- **"mayor.sh no longer divergent in the capital."** The criterion assumed identity was the sole cause. It is not: I diffed the two files and applied the new substitution set by hand, and the surviving body contains the push-gate hardening that standing order 12 itself names as a thing that must port. A fix satisfying this criterion would be hiding a real finding. (Finding 1 is that the *same* body also still carries residual identity — which qualifies the Regent's claim without rescuing the criterion.)
- **"defer 0 means the fix did not work."** The defer branch is unreachable in this civilization, and I confirmed that from tracker data independently (below) rather than accepting the assertion. The counter that moved is `propagationGaps`, 0 → 9.

---

## What I verified independently

- **`CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`, executed in cwd.** Every stage ran to a result and none failed: `tsc --noEmit` on both projects, biome (63 files, no fixes), vitest **14 files / 170 tests, all passing**. Matches the claim. The `skills-install` stage self-skipped because cwd is not a git checkout — expected for this posture, not a failure.
- **`npx vitest run test/drift-watch.test.ts`, executed in cwd: 20 passed.** Matches the claim.
- **The reviewed file is the live file, and the file I tested.** `sha256sum` of `civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs` and `test/drift-watch.test.ts` is byte-identical between cwd and `/home/justin/dev/fortkit`, and `git status --porcelain` on both paths in the live repo is empty — so the working-tree file the cron watcher executes is the committed one. *(This closes a "taken on faith" item from my earlier sitting.)*
- **The roster spellings, in the capital.** All four seat files (`mayor.md`, `forge.md`, `warden.md`, `researcher.md`) use `**Held by: Name**` with the asterisks closing after the name; all four template seat files use `**Held by:** {{UNFILLED …}}`; `fort/charter.md` contains **zero** `Held by` lines. The old regex could not have matched any of them. `rosterFromSeats` parses both spellings and rejects the placeholder, pinned at `test/drift-watch.test.ts:582`.
- **The nine-gap census, reconstructed from `.beads-export.jsonl` and the filesystem, without running the watcher.** Four Researcher paths × two elder forts, plus `fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh` absent from the capital — confirmed directly on disk: `templates/fort/scripts/` has it, `fort/scripts/` does not. Of those nine, exactly four have a closed `Drift:` bead and **no** open one — `fortkit-p6pe`, `fortkit-5913` (Proofdelve seats/profiles), `fortkit-bn7i`, `fortkit-b3gb` (Farlantern seats/profiles) — so exactly four go to re-observed; the other five carry open beads (`4xte`, `ctfl`, `h58y`, `gocg`, `8m8u`) and go to suppress. That reproduces **9 gaps / 4 re-observed / 0 defer** from tracker data alone, independently confirms the defer branch is unreachable, and confirms the fourth hidden gap (`b3gb`) the bead did not name.
- **The differential's internal arithmetic.** `identityMatches` 39→39 with `plan.suppress` 30→26 is consistent with, and only with, four findings moving adjudicated → re-observed (the new sum adds both new actions, so the total is conserved; 30−4 = 26) *and* zero findings eliminated by normalization — which is itself consistent, since the launchers' divergences are prose the token substitution cannot equate (finding 1) and the `.claude/settings.json` findings are deduped to one per fort before counting.
- **Fingerprint stability.** `makeFinding` still hashes the raw contents; the changed `reason` string is not an input to the fingerprint. So no existing drift bead gets a spurious "drift changed" comment from this edit — the E7 scar (`fortkit-zvz2`) is respected, as its inline comment claims.
- **The heading-only seat comparison is intact.** The diff adds a `normalize` argument and a do-not-touch comment; the `for (const heading of headings(templateContent))` logic is byte-identical, and `test/drift-watch.test.ts:857` fails if a successor turns it into a content comparison.
- **The new tests discriminate.** `:636` asserts both directions (identity-only file → no finding; one added architectural line → a finding with `hunks === 1`, a body containing `set -euo pipefail` and containing neither `Emrith` nor `emrith`). `:729` asserts closed-without-decline → re-observed and not suppressed, decline-in-description → suppressed, decline-in-comment → suppressed. `:797` asserts all three absence states appear in the census with `filed === 0`. These are non-vacuous.
- **Covenant section 4, in the capital's own stream.** `edict.begun` 11:36:57 and `edict.ended` 12:13:23, actor `calder`, seat `regent`. No event in that window emits as a Manyhalls citizen, and no `drift.scan` was emitted — the runs were dry, as claimed.
- **Record integrity of the export change.** `fortkit-9qts`'s description is unchanged and one comment was appended: append-only, standing order 7 honoured. (The commit *message* about it is finding 4.)
- **Standing order 12 on the sitting itself.** No citizen's name, personality or memory is touched anywhere in the diff. `civ/remember.md` is the Regent's own store, not a fort's.
- **The contamination notice's mechanism, since it is now part of this bead's record.** The incident event exists (12:27:48, actor `emrith`). `fort/scripts/warden.sh:207` posts the whole transcript with `bd comment --file "$log"`, `:204` only requires a `VERDICT-LINE` to exist somewhere in it, and `:208` takes the **last** one via `tail -1`. The Mayor's description is accurate, and the exposure is wider than the trailing prose: a later `VERDICT-LINE` in the log would override the emitted one. Already filed by the Mayor; I am not re-filing it, only confirming it.

## What I took on faith

- **The live drift run and the whole differential** (39 identity matches; plan `{file 0, comment 9, suppress 26, defer 0, reobserved 4, propagationGaps 9}`; and the pre-edict baseline). I could not execute it: the registry at `~/.claude/civilization.json` is outside my read roots and `bd` cannot run in this posture. My reconstruction corroborates the 9/4/5 split and the conserved totals from independent data, but the run itself is the Regent's measurement and the Mayor's post-commit re-run, not mine.
- **The 6-failed / 14-passed positive control.** I have no write access anywhere, so I cannot substitute the pre-edict module and re-run. The arithmetic is uniquely consistent with the claim (the pre-edict module exports no `rosterFromSeats`, has no roster gap, no `project` in the registry, a raw permission comparison, no `reobserved` and no `propagationGaps`, so six of the seven new tests must fail there and the seventh must pass on both), but I did not execute it.
- **Everything concerning Proofdelve and Farlantern on disk.** Verified as a limit rather than assumed: `ls /home/justin/dev/longburn/fort/seats/` is refused — my read roots are cwd and `/home/justin/dev/fortkit` only. Their rosters, their occupant-line spellings and their missing Researcher files are corroborated by their beads, not observed.

Findings 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7 bear on **threat 1, agent accident**: this instrument's output is what a seat will act on when it ports architecture between settlements, and each is a way it can under-report a difference, under-show one, or mislabel one. Findings 3 and 4 are record integrity under standing orders 2, 3 and 7. No finding bears on threats 2, 3 or 4. Nothing in this diff touches an authorization surface, a mask, or a permission profile; the watcher is read-only toward every fort and the sitting's event record shows it wrote to none.

VERDICT-LINE: ESCALATE (gate-1, civ/scripts/) — no blocking findings; verifiers green 170/170, census reconstructed independently; 7 beads

title: [epic] PARITY GATE: configuration, seats and memory at parity across three forts and reproducible from the factory — the gate the Overseer resumes work behind
description:
OVERSEER INTENT, 2026-08-13: 'I'm mostly pausing work in other forts while we do this, so I'd prioritize getting this project complete and ported to the whole civ over making sure each fort is working well at all times.' And on scope: 'The viewer is a fun project but not in scope for complete. The main things I want is the correct configuration, seats, memory functionality, things like that. I want the forts to function really well and be on parity before I resume work on them.'

SCOPE. Fort machinery only: configuration and permission profiles, the sandbox/mask layer, seat architecture, and the memory store. EXPLICITLY OUT: Bartizan and the visualizer, notwithstanding that it is the founding spec — the Overseer ruled it out of 'complete' on 2026-08-13.

THIS EPIC ADDS NO NEW WORK OF ITS OWN. The work already exists across fortkit-or2, fortkit-xgul, fortkit-vhk and fortkit-52vf plus loose beads; a fifth umbrella restating them would inflate a board that is already the problem. What this bead contributes is A DEFINITION OF DONE THAT CAN BE CHECKED MECHANICALLY, and the sequencing that makes the check meaningful.

THE GATE, and it is deliberately a measurement rather than a judgement: a run of the drift watcher WITH ABSENCE MADE VISIBLE shows zero UNEXPLAINED divergence per fort across configuration, seats and memory — every remaining difference carries either a recorded charter accepted-residual or an explicit decline. Identity divergence does not count and must not be counted (fortkit-k1pq).

FOUR BANDS, sequenced so each one's verification exists before the next fans out.

  BAND 1 — THE INSTRUMENT. fortkit-9qts, fortkit-6b8y, fortkit-z0j8.
  Nothing downstream is measurable until these land. 9qts means identity currently reads as
  architecture drift in every fort; 6b8y means the watcher is structurally silent about absence,
  which is the whole subject of a porting programme; z0j8 is five lines and also closes hhjb, vxpq
  and 8eq5. A parity number taken before Band 1 is not a parity number.

  BAND 2 — THE FACTORY. fortkit-0po6, fortkit-fd2, fortkit-52vf.10.1 (widened to four copies),
  fortkit-n3bk.2, fortkit-8ib, fortkit-8rh.
  The factory is the porting mechanism. Everything propagated downstream inherits its defects, so
  repairing forts before the factory means repairing them twice.

  BAND 3 — PROPAGATE. fortkit-vhk.7 (Researcher seat to both elder forts), fortkit-5aon
  (probe-cycle7.sh to both), docs/specs/memory.md to both, fortkit-xgul.8.2 (tool placement),
  fortkit-0qxm and fortkit-52vf.7 (settings and profiles), fortkit-agf.
  The bulk, and Forge-parallelizable once Bands 1 and 2 are in.

  BAND 4 — PROVE IT. fortkit-xgul.7 plus a clean drift run per fort under the Band 1 instrument.

TWO CROSS-CUTTING PREREQUISITES, both filed separately because they bind everything:
  fortkit-k1pq  the architecture-ports/identity-stays charter rule. AWAITING EXPLICIT OVERSEER
                APPROVAL under the prose gate; the porting must not run before it is law, because
                the worked example (Emrith's name and the push-gate hardening in one mayor.sh diff)
                shows there is no safe way to act on the current classification.
  fortkit-fnjn  the already-done-bead sweep. A parity measurement computed against a board carrying
                phantom work is not worth having; five such beads surfaced in one morning from a
                partial query.

DEFERRED AND RECORDED, NOT FORGOTTEN: fortkit-69bd, composable building blocks. The Overseer's own
call is that it is a future thing. It must not start while this runs — changing the shape of the
thing being ported mid-port is fortkit-29e9's failure one level up.
acceptance_criteria: A drift run per fort, under the Band 1 instrument, shows zero unexplained divergence across configuration, seats and memory, with every remaining difference carrying a recorded residual or an explicit decline; identity divergence is excluded by construction and shown to be excluded; the Overseer confirms he is willing to resume work in the elder forts behind it.

This bead defines Band 3 as PROPAGATE: the elder forts converge toward the template. fortkit-qu46 established the diff body is '--- template / +++ fort'. On 2026-08-17, adopting standing order 12 into their own charters, Marrek Splitstone (Proofdelve) and Vardis Slowfathom (Farlantern) each composed a worked example from their own fort's mayor.sh, and each independently concluded THE TEMPLATE IS THE ONE THAT IS BEHIND.

VERIFIED HERE BY READING ALL SIX FILES, not taken from either handoff:

     legacy value. Both elder forts and the capital have the corrected one-line
     seat-named form (Regent edict fortkit-wg8w.2, that same morning). A
     template-directed pass would REVERT AN EDICT THE DAY IT LANDED — Marrek's phrasing.
  2. templates/fort/scripts/forge.sh   — FORT_MASKED zero times.
  3. templates/fort/scripts/warden.sh  — FORT_MASKED zero times.
     longburn's carry a real refusal guard (case, exit 77) at forge.sh:16 and

  4. templates/fort/scripts/status.sh  — never received either fortkit-rw86 repair and

Add the fortkit-px7e hoisted-guard rationale, five measured comment lines present in
Proofdelve's mayor.sh and absent from the template (Marrek's item 2).

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BAND, and it is a design change rather than a defect list: a
one-directional Band 3 that converges elder forts toward the template would REGRESS both
of them, revert a Regent edict, and delete a working guard that exists in only one fort.
The instrument would report success — nothing fails, no test asserts these strings, the
verifiers stay green. That is exactly the shape fortkit-qu46 warned about, arriving from
the direction nobody was watching.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN: it is not an argument against Band 3. It is an argument that
BAND 3 IS BIDIRECTIONAL, and that the template halves (fortkit-x02m, fortkit-a355,
fortkit-881h, fortkit-tcmg, fortkit-e69p, fortkit-xgul.8.1) are not tidying-up after
Band 2 — THEY ARE BAND 3'S PRECONDITION. Every one of them moves architecture from a

RECOMMENDATION FOR THE OVERSEER: before Band 3 opens, take a pass that asks per file
WHICH SIDE IS AHEAD, and let the answer be 'the fort' where it is. Standing order 12 now

title: [bug] The drift watcher never normalizes citizen names — rosterFromCharter has never matched a real fort, so identity reads as architecture drift forever
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13, and it is the mechanical cause of the hazard fortkit-k1pq is about.

civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:62-77 normalizer() substitutes three things before comparing a fort's
file to the template: the fort path, the fort name, and EVERY ACTOR NAME IN THE ROSTER. The roster
comes from rosterFromCharter() at :79-84, which matches:

  /^\*\*Held by:\*\*\s*([^\n(]+)/gmu        i.e.  **Held by:** Name

THE TEMPLATE SPELLS IT THAT WAY. THE LIVE FORTS DO NOT. templates/fort/seats/*.md carry
'**Held by:** {{UNFILLED — set at the Founding Moot}}'; every seated fort writes
'**Held by: Ilva Trueglass** (she/her, ...)' — the asterisks wrap the NAME as well as the label.
The regex was written against the template spelling and has never matched a seated fort.

PROVEN, not inferred. Run against the capital's real charter:
  grep -cF '**Held by:**' fort/charter.md            -> 0
  grep -hcF '**Held by:**' fort/seats/*.md           -> 0
  rosterFromCharter(fort/charter.md)                  -> []
A second defect compounds it: the function is fed fort/charter.md, but '**Held by:'' appears in
fort/seats/*.md, never in the charter at all. So even with the spelling corrected it would need to
read the seat files. TWO faults, and either alone empties the roster.

CONSEQUENCE. Actor names are never substituted, so every launcher containing a citizen's name
diverges from the template permanently and is classified as backport or upgrade-offer. Today's dry
run flags fort/scripts/mayor.sh as 'backport' in ALL THREE FORTS — including Manyhalls, the capital
that AUTHORED the template. A capital diverging from its own template on a file it wrote is the
signature of this bug.

WHY IT IS A PARITY BLOCKER AND NOT A NUISANCE. The classification is unusable while it holds: the
divergence it reports is a mixture of identity and architecture with no way to tell them apart

title: Charter amendment: seat ARCHITECTURE ports, seat IDENTITY never does — the rule the parity programme runs under
description:
OVERSEER INTENT, 2026-08-13, recorded verbatim before any porting work runs:

  'we don't want to overwrite the persons in the other forts, just make upgrades to the seat
   architecture, like making sure they are using the right memory store, and the right sandbox
   configs, the right capabilities. names, personalities, memories, etc, should persist and not be
   overwritten when porting.'

THE RULE, stated so a stranger porting a change can apply it without asking:

  ARCHITECTURE TRAVELS. Capabilities, restrictions, sandbox and mask configuration, permission
  profiles, memory-store mechanism, launcher mechanics, protocol sections of a seat file, ladder
  STRUCTURE, and the standing orders a seat operates under.

  IDENTITY STAYS. Name, pronouns, personality, the seat's History and Laurels, that fort's own
  memories, handoffs, annals, and its moot record. A fort must never inherit another settlement's
  citizen — already law in the founding-moot record and in fortkit-ebm/fd2; this generalises it
  from FOUNDING to PORTING, which is where it was not yet written.

WHY IT NEEDS TO BE LAW BEFORE THE PORTING RUNS, and this is measured, not hypothetical. Today's
drift run classifies fort/scripts/mayor.sh as 'backport' in ALL THREE forts. Diffing the live
capital against the rendered template shows the divergence is a MIXTURE of both kinds in one file:

  IDENTITY   -a emrith; 'The Overseer summons Emrith'; 'You are Emrith Cairnwright (she/her),
             Mayor of Manyhalls'
  ARCHITECTURE  the live push gate ends '...never on your own initiative, IN A BATCH OF OTHER
             WORK, OR BECAUSE IT SEEMS IMPLIED. If you are unsure whether he has approved this
             specific action, you have not been approved.' The template carries only the short
             form. That hardening exists in the capital and no other fort will ever receive it.

A seat told to 'converge mayor.sh to the template' either overwrites Emrith or drops the push-gate
hardening. There is no safe way to act on the current classification, which is why this is a
prerequisite of the parity programme rather than a note inside it.

GATE: this edits fort/charter.md (standing orders), prose-gated since cycle 7. Prior Overseer
approval must be recorded on THIS bead before the edit, and charter.amended emitted at it. The
intent above is recorded; EXPLICIT APPROVAL TO APPLY IT IS NOT YET GIVEN and must be.

title: [bug] The drift watcher is structurally silent about the propagation gap — 'not-yet-propagated' is never filed, and closing such a bead suppresses it forever
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 while measuring the civ-wide porting gap the Overseer asked for. This bears directly on 'port this project to the whole civilization', because the instrument the fort would use to MEASURE that porting is blind to exactly the thing being ported.

TWO INDEPENDENT MECHANISMS, both in civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs, and either alone is sufficient to hide the gap.

(1) NOT-YET-PROPAGATED IS NEVER FILED. Line 625: action is 'defer' when suggestion === 'not-yet-propagated', 'file' otherwise. So a file the template HAS and a fort LACKS never becomes a bead. It lands in report.deferred, which nothing reads and no seat is prompted to read. The watcher files beads about files that exist and diverge; it is silent about files that are absent.

(2) A CLOSED BEAD SUPPRESSES THE SAME FINDING PERMANENTLY. Lines 616-621: a CLOSED bead matching (identity, fingerprint) marks the finding 'adjudicated' and it is suppressed. For a not-yet-propagated finding the fort-side hash is the empty-string hash (e3b0c442...b855), so the fingerprint is stable for as long as the TEMPLATE file is unchanged. Closing the bead therefore silences the finding indefinitely, even though the condition it described is still true.

MEASURED INSTANCES, all three verified by hand this session:
  fortkit-bn7i  CLOSED, 'Drift: Farlantern fort/seats/researcher.md'
                /home/justin/dev/longburn/fort/seats/researcher.md — DOES NOT EXIST
  fortkit-p6pe  CLOSED, 'Drift: Proofdelve fort/seats/researcher.md'
  fortkit-5913  CLOSED, 'Drift: Proofdelve fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json'
The dry run reports these as suppressed with by:'closed-bead'. The gaps are real and the watcher will never mention them again.

WHY THE DESIGN IS DEFENSIBLE AND STILL WRONG HERE. 'Adjudicated' means a human looked at this exact drift and accepted it, which is the correct treatment for an upgrade-offer a fort declines. Applied to an ABSENCE it means something different: the fort still lacks the file, and the only detector has been switched off. Closing these beads was very likely correct triage at the time — the Researcher propagation was deliberately sequenced behind memory parity as fortkit-vhk.7 — but the SIDE EFFECT was not visible to whoever closed them.

THE STAKES, and this is the same class as fortkit-fnjn from the other direction: fnjn is beads outliving their fix (false alarm, board inflation). This is beads closed while the work is undone AND the detector disabled (false quiet, silent gap). False quiet is the worse of the two, because nothing will ever raise it again.

CURRENT REAL GAPS THIS HIDES, from today's dry run: the Researcher seat is not-yet-propagated to BOTH elder forts (fort/seats/researcher.md, fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json, fort/scripts/researcher.sh, fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh), and probe-researcher-boundaries.sh is not-yet-propagated even to MANYHALLS, the capital that authored it.

SHAPES TO CONSIDER, not a decided design: report not-yet-propagated as its own named section with a count, so absence is visible without being noisy; distinguish 'declined' from 'deferred' so only an explicit decline suppresses; or re-open/re-raise when a closed adjudication's condition is re-observed as still true.
acceptance_criteria: A run of civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs surfaces the currently-hidden propagation gaps (the four Researcher paths across the elder forts and probe-researcher-boundaries.sh in the capital) in a form a seat actually reads; closing a bead for an absent file no longer silences it while the file is still absent; proven by a differential against today's dry run, which reports plan.defer 0 and hides all three known instances.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 0134648 (E9, fortkit-52vf.11), two concurring Warden reviews, no blocking findings. Closure no longer suppresses an ABSENCE unless the bead carries an explicit written decline ('Drift decision: declined'); otherwise the finding is re-observed — reported and counted, never re-filed. Fingerprint adjudication is untouched for non-absence findings, where the bead correctly said it was right. report.propagationGaps added: a named census of every not-yet-propagated finding whatever the filing decision was, with counts in report.plan, in the drift.scan payload, and a line on stderr. or2.8's no-file ruling stands — the defect was never that the gap was unfiled, but that it existed only in a field nothing read. PROVEN: the four previously-silenced beads (bn7i, p6pe, 5913 and b3gb, the fourth named in no bead) now surface as re-observed; nine propagation gaps are visible for the first time, including probe-researcher-boundaries.sh absent from the capital that wrote it. Ilva reconstructed the 9/4/5 split from tracker data alone, without running the watcher, and it matched. RESIDUAL FILED: the census is built from active findings, so an allowlist-suppressed absence would be missing from a census documented as complete — the comment, not the code, needs the clause.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Five lines moved, and they do exactly what the bead asked. I re-ran the measurement that produced this bead in the first place (my finding 4 on `fortkit-29e9`) and it now comes back clean: **the only divergence left between the capital's live mask lib and the factory's copy is the disclosed comment.** Executable delta: zero. Verifier green, run by me from cwd.

**Model: `gpt-5.6-terra`** (top Forge rung), launcher-stamped in the handoff and corroborated independently in the live event stream (`fort/events/events-2026-08-13.jsonl:49,52` — `session.start` payload `{"model":"gpt-5.6-terra"}`, `handoff.written` payload `verify_exit: 0`). Scrutiny weighted for the GPT family: I read the produced file rather than the diff, and every handoff claim I could execute, I executed. All held.

**On the gate, since I am the one who widened it yesterday.** On `fortkit-29e9` I ruled `templates/fort/scripts/lib/` gate-1 *by extension* and referred it. I am not referring this one, and the line I am drawing is: **the extension attaches to a change that alters what the factory's enforcement layer does — not to a provably inert convergence toward text the Overseer has already signed off.** Measured against git objects, not working copies: `git diff main:fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh bead/z0j8:templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh` returns the comment hunk and nothing else. The live lib is the E8 text the Overseer gate-signed (`fortkit-52vf.10`) and is untouched here. Asking him to re-approve his own approved bytes is ceremony, and the charter says a control that reduces no threat is exactly that. If Justin wants the referral to be path-shaped rather than substance-shaped, that is his call to make and this paragraph is the place to make it.

---

### Findings

**1. The bead's acceptance criteria cannot be met by this diff, and `hhjb`/`vxpq`/`8eq5` must NOT be closed on this merge. — non-blocking (threat 1, agent accident)**
Criterion 1 is met (see verification below). Criterion 2 — "drift-watch.mjs reports the path as converged" — is not, and cannot be. The normalizer (`civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:62-77`) substitutes only the repo path, the fort name and roster actor names; it does not strip comments, and the compare at `:340` is on those normalized bytes. The 3-line→1-line comment at lines 162-168 therefore survives normalization and the path still reads DIVERGENT. I can prove this for **`fortkit-vxpq` (Manyhalls)** directly, because the capital's live lib is the one file in that comparison I can read: it still differs. `fortkit-hhjb` (Proofdelve) and `fortkit-8eq5` (Farlantern) I cannot measure at all — those checkouts are outside my mask — and their libs took the elder forts' half of E8, which this fort has never reviewed.
The bead's own description concedes this ("reduces the remainder to the disclosed comment alone") while its "WHAT IT UNBLOCKS" section and its acceptance criteria promise closure. The Forge did not paper over the contradiction — it is stated plainly in the handoff's Open risks, correctly, with the right reason for not fixing it here (`fortkit-52vf.10.1` owns that comment, and a second pass over the same file re-opens drift in the opposite direction, which is the failure `29e9` existed to prevent). **The over-promise is mine:** my `29e9` filing recommendation called this "a five-line follow-up that lets `hhjb`/`vxpq`/`8eq5` close," and the same finding's own body said the comment is not normalized away. Correcting it here on the record. The honest disposition of criterion 3 is "remaining reason recorded" — the reason is the disclosed comment, and it discharges when `52vf.10.1` lands.

**2. The gate-1 referral on `fortkit-29e9` has no recorded resolution. — non-blocking (threat 1)**
`fortkit-29e9` carries exactly one comment (my ESCALATE, 18:58:39Z), an empty `notes` field, and `closed_at` 19:06:13Z — seven minutes later. The Mayor's repair of my finding 1 (`templates/fort/charter.md`, commit `afb287f`) landed in that same minute, so the referral was answered *by action*. But the question I put to Justin was a gate question, and nothing in the bead or the event stream records that he answered it. Precedent one bead earlier is the opposite: `52vf.10` closed "on Overseer gate-1 sign-off after Warden ESCALATE," recorded. A reader six weeks from now cannot tell whether a gate-1 referral was ruled on or merged past. Caveat on my evidence: `.beads-export.jsonl` is a launch-time snapshot; it postdates the closure (the closure is in it), so the absence is real as of the snapshot, but a comment appended after launch would not appear to me. This is about a closed bead, not about this diff.

**3. Nothing tests the parity this bead exists to restore. — non-blocking (threat 1)**
No test in `test/` references `seat-sandbox` or the option parser; the safety net for this change is ShellCheck plus my own textual differential. The divergence being repaired here was introduced by hand and is being removed by hand, and standing order 12 (new on main, below) is about to port this same file into three more forts. SO11 is satisfied — this is an observed failure, not an imagined one: `29e9` carried the lib and left the reorder, and it cost a bead and two sessions to find and fix. A one-assertion verifier gate — the live and template libs identical modulo comments — would have caught it in the sitting that made it, and it is the same shape as the memory-staleness gate (`fortkit-c1kj`). Mayor lane, since it edits `scripts/verify-impl.sh`. Recommend filing.

**4. The branch is one commit behind main. — non-blocking**
Base `afb287f`; main is `d435aab` (`fortkit-k1pq`, the standing order 12 charter amendment). Paths are disjoint — `d435aab` touches `fort/charter.md`, the event stream and `templates/fort/charter.md`, and `git diff afb287f..d435aab -- fort/scripts/lib templates/fort/scripts` is empty — so the merge is clean and my live-vs-template differential above was taken against main's true tip. This diff obeys it anyway, exactly: what moved is sandbox and mask configuration (architecture), and the hunk contains no name, pronoun, personality, History, memory or annal. ---

### Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Executed by me, in cwd (`/tmp/warden-z0j8`), this session:**

Reordering two mutually exclusive literal branches in that construct is semantics-preserving as a matter of shell grammar, not as a judgment call.

title: [bug] The factory's permission set has no ~/.codex rule: a new fort's Mayor gets kernel-rw with no tool-layer backstop, and the recorded template decision forbids the obvious spelling
description:
WARDEN FINDING 2 on fortkit-29e9 (Ilva, 2026-08-13), non-blocking, threat 1.

templates/config/settings-permissions.json — rendered to a new fort's .claude/settings.json by bin/fort-init:151-156 — carries NO ~/.codex entry in its deny block. Since E8 reached the factory (fortkit-29e9), a new fort's attended MAYOR gets ~/.codex read-write at the kernel with nothing at the tool layer behind it.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT COVERED. The WARDEN's backstop DOES propagate: templates/fort/profiles/warden-settings.json:49 carries Edit(**), which is precisely the mitigation the charter's fortkit-3jv7 residual names, so the seat that residual is written about is protected in a new fort. The gap is the Mayor's. The capital at least attempts a Mayor rule (.claude/settings.json:112, Edit(//home/justin/.codex/**)) but in the double-slash spelling that matches nothing — the fortkit-f3y defect, now closed in the warden profile and still live here.

THE REASON THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, and the reason it needs a decision rather than a patch: fortkit-4wlz closed by documenting WHY NO ABSOLUTE-PATH DENIES BELONG IN THE TEMPLATES AT ALL. render() substitutes an absolute path into a template that already carries a leading slash, which is what produced the double-slash class in the first place. ~/.codex is not repo-relative, so it cannot use {{REPO_PATH}}, and there is no HOME placeholder. Adding an absolute-path deny here CONTRADICTS A RECORDED DECISION; flagging the conflict rather than resolving it silently, per the spec-discipline rule.

THREE SHAPES, and the choice is the Overseer's:
(a) introduce a {{HOME}} (or {{CODEX_HOME}}) placeholder to render() so an absolute deny can be spelled correctly once, and revisit 4wlz's blanket 'no absolute-path denies' as being about REPO_PATH specifically;
(b) give the Mayor template the same Edit(**)-shaped deny the Warden template uses, scoped so the Mayor keeps the write access her seat actually needs — larger change, needs its own measurement;
(c) accept it as a charter residual in the template, on the argument that the Mayor is an ATTENDED seat and the prose gate is the control for attended seats — which is the same reasoning cycle 6 used for push.

Emrith's recommendation: (a), because the double-slash class keeps recurring and a placeholder fixes the spelling once for every future absolute deny, and because (c) accepts a residual the fort has not measured.
acceptance_criteria: A new fort founded from templates/ either carries a ~/.codex rule for the Mayor in a spelling proven to match (rendered and grepped from a real founded fort, not asserted), or carries a charter residual saying why it does not; and fortkit-4wlz's 'no absolute-path denies' decision is either honoured or explicitly narrowed on the record.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
OVERSEER RULING 2026-08-13 (Mayor session d): SHAPE (a) APPROVED. Introduce a {{HOME}} (or {{CODEX_HOME}}) placeholder to bin/fort-init's render() so an absolute deny can be spelled correctly once, and revisit fortkit-4wlz's 'no absolute-path denies' as being about REPO_PATH specifically rather than absolutes in general.

THE OVERSEER RAISED A CONCERN AND IT WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE RULING STOOD: 'didn't we decide that ~/.codex needs write access from the Mayor, because codex needs to save something there?' Correct, and this bead does not touch it. THE TWO LAYERS ARE DISTINCT:

KERNEL — unchanged, and must stay unchanged. fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:330 sets CODEX_DIR_RW=1 on the claude branch and :416 binds $HOME/.codex read-write. Measured in a live masked Mayor session's /proc/self/mountinfo 2026-08-13 (that session's own filesystem, named explicitly per fortkit-uj3q): /home/justin/.codex is a REAL btrfs bind, rw, on the true home directory and NOT tmpfs; config.toml ro; sessions/ and log/ tmpfs; history.jsonl /dev/null ro. The reason, seat-sandbox.sh:278-292: the Mayor launches the Forge, a child codex inherits the mount namespace, and codex rotates its auth token BY RENAME. The prior design (tmpfs over ~/.codex plus auth.json re-bound read-only as a FILE) pinned the inode, rotation failed at write, the refresh token was reused and revoked server-side, a host-side 'codex login' stayed invisible to running sessions, and both seat lanes died until restart. Measured longburn-1p9 2026-08-05, unified civilization-wide by E8 (fortkit-52vf.10) 2026-08-13.

TOOL — what this bead changes. A permission-profile Edit() deny binds Claude Code's own Edit tool. It does NOT bind a codex subprocess spawned through Bash, and the subprocess is what rotates the token. PROOF BY EXISTENCE rather than by argument: the Warden is also a claude seat, also receives CODEX_DIR_RW=1, and fort/profiles/warden-settings.json:49 denies Edit(**) outright. She functions.

THE BEAD'S OWN CLAIMS RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-13: .claude/settings.json:112 carries Edit(//home/justin/.codex/**) and is the ONLY codex rule in any permission file in this repository; the double-slash matches nothing (the fortkit-f3y class). templates/config/settings-permissions.json contains zero codex rules. Neither warden profile carries a codex-SPECIFIC rule; the coverage the charter's fortkit-3jv7 residual attributes to warden-settings.json comes from the blanket Edit(**) at line 49, which is worth knowing before anyone narrows it.

SHAPE (b) IS RECORDED AS A TRAP, and not for codex reasons. Copying the Warden's blanket Edit(**) onto the Mayor would brick the seat that writes specs, beads, docs and fort files. This bead's description hedges it as 'scoped so the Mayor keeps the write access her seat actually needs'; there is no safe scoping of Edit(**) for this seat. Do not reach for (b).

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
MAYOR RE-VERIFICATION 2026-08-14, before the Regent sitting. THE APPROVED FIX HAS A TRAP THAT WOULD SHIP SILENTLY, AND THE BEAD IS NOW SPLIT ACROSS TWO LANES.

THE TRAP. The Overseer's ruling says introduce a {{HOME}} placeholder to render(). But
templates/config/settings-permissions.json NEVER PASSES THROUGH render():
  bin/fort-init:27-29  render() { sed -e "s|{{REPO_PATH}}|$REPO|g" -e ... }
  bin/fort-init:151    PERMS=$(sed "s|{{REPO_PATH}}|$REPO|g" "$T/config/settings-permissions.json")
Line 151 is a SEPARATE sed with its own substitution list, and it is the ONLY path this
file takes. Patch render() alone and a literal {{HOME}} lands in every new fort's
.claude/settings.json, where a deny rule containing braces matches nothing and denies
nothing. That is the fortkit-f3y double-slash class one layer up, and it fails in the
direction where the fort BELIEVES IT IS PROTECTED and is not. Both sites, or route :151
through render().

THE CONTROL THAT CATCHES IT: grep -rn '{{' over the entire founded tree INCLUDING
.claude/settings.json. fortkit-naju's acceptance already demands no surviving braces but
scopes it to the fort/ tree; widen it, and this class cannot ship again.

THE SPLIT, on the Overseer's decision 2026-08-14 to let a Forge pass write the template:
  REGENT (fortkit-wg8w.1): render() and :151 learn {{HOME}}; fortkit-4wlz's 'no
    absolute-path denies' explicitly narrowed to REPO_PATH on the record.
  FORGE (fortkit-hgbe, blocked on the sitting): the actual ~/.codex deny line in
    templates/config/settings-permissions.json, spelled with {{HOME}}.
This bead does not close until both land.

WHY THAT ORDER IS THE SAFE ONE, and the Mayor's earlier framing of the risk was wrong:
a sed for {{HOME}} against a template with no {{HOME}} token is a NO-OP. The machinery is
inert and harmless until the Forge writes the token. THE REVERSE ORDER IS THE DANGEROUS
ONE. There is no window in which the factory ships something broken.

BUT IT COSTS THE REGENT HIS PROOF, so a POSITIVE CONTROL IS REQUIRED. With no shipped
template using the placeholder, 'it works' would be read off the sed line, which is the
exact error class this sitting is written against (fortkit-uj3q: what result would have
falsified this?). The Regent renders a throwaway fixture containing {{HOME}} through both
render() and the :151 path and proves substitution.

RE-CONFIRMED TODAY: templates/config/settings-permissions.json contains ZERO codex rules
(grep -c codex = 0).

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
REGENT, Band 2 sitting (fortkit-wg8w.1), 2026-08-14. Calder Sealbroken, model opus,
Overseer present. THE REGENT HALF IS IN. This bead does not close until fortkit-hgbe
(the Forge's ~/.codex deny line) lands, per the split recorded above.

WHAT LANDED, and it is one line more than the ruling asked for on purpose. The trap
the Mayor named — templates/config/settings-permissions.json never passes through
render(), because bin/fort-init:151 kept a sed of its own — is closed by REMOVING THE
SECOND SED rather than by teaching it {{HOME}}:

    render_stream() { sed -e "s|{{REPO_PATH}}|$REPO|g" ... -e "s|{{HOME}}|$HOME|g" ... "$1"; }
    render()        { render_stream "$1" > "$2"; }
    PERMS=$(render_stream "$T/config/settings-permissions.json")

Two seds cannot drift if there is one. Patching both sites was the letter of the fix;
this is the same behaviour with the recurrence removed, and any token added in future
now reaches the permission file by construction.

POSITIVE CONTROL, REQUIRED AND RUN, because no shipped template uses {{HOME}} yet and
"it works" would otherwise have been read off the sed line. A throwaway fixture kit
was built with {{HOME}} injected on BOTH paths — a deny rule
"Edit({{HOME}}/.fixture-canary/**)" in config/settings-permissions.json, and a
"FIXTURE CANARY: {{HOME}}/.fixture-canary" line in fort/seats/mayor.md — and three
forts were founded from it with three different factories:

  factory                              seats/mayor.md          .claude/settings.json
  pre-edit bin/fort-init               {{HOME}} literal        {{HOME}} literal
  naive fix ({{HOME}} in render only)  /home/justin  OK        {{HOME}} LITERAL
  this fix                             /home/justin  OK        /home/justin  OK

The middle row is the trap, measured rather than argued: the naive fix substitutes
where a reader would look and ships a brace-bearing deny rule into the file that is
supposed to deny. It fails in the direction where the fort believes it is protected.

WIDER CHECK, which is what catches this class permanently: `grep -rn '{{[A-Z_]*}}'`
over the ENTIRE founded tree INCLUDING .claude/settings.json now returns zero. See the
fortkit-naju comment for why the criterion is the render-token shape and not a bare
`{{` — a founded fort must keep its {{UNFILLED — ...}} moot markers.

CRITERION 6, THE fortkit-4wlz NARROWING — AND A CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE.
This description says "fortkit-4wlz closed by documenting WHY NO ABSOLUTE-PATH DENIES
BELONG IN THE TEMPLATES AT ALL." Read today, that is wrong twice. fortkit-4wlz is
OPEN, carried by fortkit-52vf.7 (E6, profiles). It documents no such decision: it
states a defect in two .ssh/.aws lines and asks the Overseer for a ruling among three
options — and its own option (b) is "ADD a {{HOME}} placeholder to fort-init's
render() and correct the spelling to a single slash". So the recorded position this
bead treated as a contradiction was a recommendation for two specific lines, and the
machinery it asked for is exactly what the Overseer has now ruled in.

ON THE RECORD, therefore: the "no absolute-path denies in the templates" reading is
narrowed to {{REPO_PATH}} — the token whose value is concatenated after a leading
slash, which is what produced the double-slash class (fortkit-f3y). It was never a
rule about absolutes. {{HOME}} now exists and renders correctly on both paths, so
4wlz's option (b) is available machinery rather than a proposal; WHICH of (a)/(b)/(c)
the .ssh/.aws lines get remains 4wlz's question and E6's work, untouched here.

UNCHANGED AND MUST STAY UNCHANGED: the kernel grant. seat-sandbox.sh still binds
$HOME/.codex read-write on the claude branch. This sitting touched no mask.

title: Fixes that land as passengers leave no trail back to their bead: five beads outlived their fixes, one of them the fort's only P0
description:
OBSERVED, NOT IMAGINED (SO11). In a single Mayor session on 2026-08-13, FIVE open beads turned out to describe defects that were already repaired. Four of the five were P1 or P0 and two were being planned against as live work that morning.

fortkit-5jvc  P0, open 2 sessions. bin/regent:366 already read --append-system-prompt-file. Commit 9dbb424 NAMED the bead in its subject. It was carried as the fort's only P0 in two handoffs and in the distilled view; the Overseer discovered it by simply launching the Regent successfully.
fortkit-f3y   Raised to P1 THIS MORNING against a defect that no longer existed. git log -S'//home' shows 70eef64 removed all five double-slash denies on 2026-08-11, inside a commit titled 'Mayor session C handoff ... day's records'. The repair rode as a PASSENGER in a records commit during a gate-1 sweep.
fortkit-uhvt  P1. Both halves false: the elder forts migrated 2026-08-11 under their own beads, and bin/fort-init:25/55-56/74-131/182-189 founds forts on the ledger.
fortkit-xgul.4/.5  Corrections recorded ON THE BEADS saying the migrations completed, and the beads left open anyway.

THE CLASS. A fix reaches main by a route that does not close its bead: another fort's bead (xgul.4/.5), an edict, the Overseer's own hand, or a commit named for something else (f3y). The bead is the fort's only durable statement of what is wrong, so a bead that outlives its fix is a FALSE RECORD that survives every review — and standing order 7 makes records the thing this fort will not let drift. It also inflates the board: five of 227 found in one morning by one query, with no systematic sweep yet run.

THE SIGNAL WORKS, AND IT IS CHEAP. Proven this session: for each open bead, look for a commit on main whose SUBJECT BEGINS with that bead id. It surfaced every one of the above. Report only, never auto-close — three of the five needed a tree measurement to confirm, and one (f3y) had no matching commit subject at all and was found by content search instead.

A FLAW IN THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE QUERY, recorded so the implementation does not repeat it: matching '${id}[:. ]' lets a CHILD id satisfy a PARENT. fortkit-xgul.7 matched a commit for fortkit-xgul.7.1, and fortkit-52vf matched fortkit-52vf.9. The boundary must exclude '.', and epics with open children must be excluded from candidacy regardless.

PROPOSED SHAPE, for the Overseer's decision rather than assumed: a report script under scripts/, run at SESSION CLOSE, not a verifier step. A bookkeeping mismatch must never red the build — that is the same trap fortkit-c1kj rejected two gate designs over.
design: Report-only, never auto-close. Two signals, because neither alone found all five: (1) commit subject begins with the bead id, anchored to exclude '.' so children do not satisfy parents; (2) content search for the bead's own cited artifact, which is how f3y was found. Placement in scripts/ per the c1kj precedent that memory/bookkeeping machinery lives beside memory-lint.mjs and travels to the factory via templates/.
acceptance_criteria: A script reports open beads whose fix appears already landed, anchored so a child id cannot satisfy a parent and excluding epics with open children; proven non-vacuous against the five known instances by running it at a commit where each was still open; wired into the session-close protocol rather than the verifier; and the first full sweep's results triaged.

title: The Warden is no longer read-only BY CONSTRUCTION at ~/.codex — the property is profile-enforced now, and both the charter and her seat file still say 'by construction'
description:
WARDEN FINDINGS 3 AND 4 on fortkit-52vf.10 (Ilva, 2026-08-13), raised by the seat whose own guarantee is weakened. Non-blocking, and a RECORD defect of the class this fort escalates.

FINDING 3 — THE HOLE. E8 unified on CODEX_DIR_RW for BOTH seat types. The Warden is a claude seat, so it applies to her: at the KERNEL she can now write ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, skills/, plugins/ — instruction executed by the NEXT Forge launch, outside her mask. The lib comment discloses it ('an attended Mayor or Warden'). MEASURED MITIGATION: fort/profiles/warden-settings.json denies Edit(**) and every write verb (rm, mv, cp, chmod, ln, all git mutators), so the seat stays read-only at the TOOL layer. But for this one directory the property is now PROFILE-ENFORCED while fort/charter.md and fort/seats/warden.md both say 'read-only by construction'. A guarantee whose stated mechanism no longer matches its actual mechanism is the reader-facing defect fortkit-yowr was filed about, one layer up.

FINDING 4 — THE COST STATEMENT COVERS WRITES AND OMITS THE NEW READS. For claude seats ~/.codex was previously INVISIBLE (tmpfs) and is now READABLE IN FULL except sessions/, log/ and history.jsonl — including config.toml, which in Codex commonly carries MCP server definitions and their environment. Consistent with the standing 'reads across $HOME stay open' decision (charter, 2026-08-04), which is why Ilva ranked it non-blocking, but the cost paragraph should SAY it rather than leaving a reader to infer the read side from the write side.

WHY THIS NEEDS THE OVERSEER AND NOT JUST AN EDIT: the fix lands in fort/charter.md (residuals) and/or fort/seats/warden.md, both PROSE-GATED since cycle 7 — prior Overseer approval recorded on this bead, plus a charter.amended event. Two candidate shapes, and the choice is his:
  (a) record it as a charter ACCEPTED RESIDUAL with the measurement attached, per SO11, the treatment fortkit-gohb gives the /proc exposure; or
  (b) narrow the 'by construction' wording in both the charter and warden.md to say what is now true — kernel-enforced everywhere except ~/.codex, profile-enforced there — which is more honest and more maintenance.

Emrith's recommendation: (b) plus a one-line residual, because 'by construction' is exactly the phrase a future seat will trust instead of re-deriving the mask, and the charter already carries a residuals section that makes (a) cheap to add alongside.
acceptance_criteria: Overseer approval recorded verbatim on this bead; the charter and fort/seats/warden.md no longer assert an enforcement mechanism that is not the one in force at ~/.codex; charter.amended emitted; the read-side cost stated.
close_reason: Overseer-approved and applied under the cycle-7 prose gate, 2026-08-13. Approval recorded verbatim on the bead; shape (b) plus the residual, as recommended. fort/charter.md (prose-gate scope sentence + seat table) and fort/seats/warden.md no longer assert 'by construction' for the Warden; a new charter accepted residual carries the write side, finding 4's read-side cost stated explicitly, and the limit of its own measurement (scripts/mask-harness.sh asserts nothing about ~/.codex, fortkit-wtps). charter.amended emitted 10:40:47. Verifier green: 163 tests, exit 0. Commit 88c3704. Out of scope and flagged on the bead rather than silently widened: fort/charter.md:69's Researcher 'read-only toward the world by construction' — that claim is about external systems, not the filesystem, and researcher.sh takes the same CODEX_DIR_RW bind.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
OVERSEER APPROVAL RECORDED VERBATIM, 2026-08-13, Mayor session (Emrith). Justin: '1. 3jv7 P1 gate-1. yes I agree with you and approve.'

The approval was given against this bead's stated recommendation, which is SHAPE (b) plus a one-line residual: narrow the 'by construction' wording in fort/charter.md and fort/seats/warden.md to say what is actually in force — kernel-enforced everywhere except ~/.codex, profile-enforced there — AND record the residual in the charter's accepted-residuals section with its measurement attached, per SO11. So the Researcher seat gets the same CODEX_DIR_RW bind. fort/charter.md:67 claims the Researcher is 'read-only toward the world by construction' — that claim is about EXTERNAL SYSTEMS, not the local filesystem, so it is not falsified by this finding and is left alone. title: The memory staleness gate: assert no fact rendered in the distilled view is status: superseded in the ledger
description:
THE CLASS DEFECT BEHIND fortkit-1gz3, held by the Mayor because it edits scripts/verify-impl.sh — kernel read-only to the Forge by the Shape B carve-out, so it can never be dispatched.

WHAT IS MISSING. Nothing regenerates fort/memory/current.md and no verifier detects it as stale. Measured 2026-08-13: 'grep -rn consolidate-memory scripts/verify-impl.sh fort/scripts/ package.json .git/hooks/' returns NOTHING. The consequence was fortkit-1gz3: the view served a SUPERSEDED core fact — 'fort/scripts/ except Mayor-writable verify.sh' — to every seat at session start for a day, while the ledger and the seat file had both been corrected. It is the widest-read of the three places that record lived.

THE DESIGN IS SETTLED, AND BY TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES.

The gate CANNOT be 'regenerate and diff the whole file'. Demonstrated twice in one day: the view's Open work section changes on ordinary bead traffic, and regenerating after today's 15 closures produced a diff whose ONLY content was '232 -> 228 open beads'. A whole-file gate would go red on every bead close and be disabled within a day.

Warden finding 2 on fortkit-1gz3 reached the same place from the other direction, reviewing the repointed test: the new assertion is semantic rather than typographic, which is a real improvement, but it is still a 62-character substring of a live generated rendering containing two hyphenated tokens. A benign reflow of cycle13-write-boundaries.md — no supersession, no change of truth — reds the suite again, and the next seat faces the same 'correct action becomes a red build' trap one wrapping removed. Her words: a form that keys on IDENTITY rather than prose would close the class.

THE GATE TO BUILD: no fact rendered in fort/memory/current.md is status: superseded in fort/memory/facts/. Cheap, keyed on identity not prose, immune to reflow and to bead churn, and it catches the exact bug that produced 1gz3. title: The distilled view serves a SUPERSEDED core fact to every seat at session start, and a test pinning a line-wrap artifact is what keeps it there
description:
THE DISTILLED VIEW SERVES A SUPERSEDED CORE FACT TO EVERY SEAT AT SESSION START, AND A TEST IS
WHAT KEEPS IT THERE. Found 2026-08-13 by Emrith while looking for work that would not collide
with a running Regent sitting.

=== THE DEFECT, MEASURED ===

fort/memory/facts/cycle7-write-boundaries.md is status: superseded, superseded-by:
cycle13-write-boundaries. Correctly so — that supersession is part of the E2b reap (9d8464f) and
it is what Warden E2b blocking finding 2 asked for.

fort/memory/current.md STILL RENDERS THE SUPERSEDED CYCLE-7 TEXT as a live core fact, and does
not render cycle13 at all. It still tells every seat that host-executed scripts are kernel-RO
"except Mayor-writable verify.sh" — the exact false claim that fortkit-hwol just corrected in
fort/seats/mayor.md, and that cycle13-write-boundaries was written to replace.

  git log -1 fort/memory/current.md                -> 004d9d2 (fortkit-ij8j)
  git log -1 fort/memory/facts/cycle13-...md       -> 9d8464f (the E2b reap, LATER)

So the view predates the supersession. It is a GENERATED file — its own header says "Generated by
scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs; do not edit" — and the generator was never re-run.

WHY THIS IS THE WIDEST-READ COPY OF THE THREE. The false record lived in three places:
fort/seats/mayor.md:17 (fixed by fortkit-hwol today), the facts ledger (fixed by the supersession
yesterday), and this view. fort/seats/mayor.md names current.md in the Mayor's session-start
reading list, and every other seat file does the same for its own seat. This is the copy a fresh
session reads first.

=== WHY NOBODY REGENERATED IT: A TEST PINS THE STALE TEXT ===

Running `node scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs` produces the CORRECT view — it drops the superseded
fact and renders cycle13, so the generator is not the defect. But the regenerated file turns the
suite RED, 162/163:

  FAIL test/memory.test.ts > memory consolidation >
       "pins the migrated cycle-7 correction as the active Forge truth"
  AssertionError: expected '# Manyhalls current operational truth...' to contain 'PROSE- gated'

test/memory.test.ts:158-166 reads the LIVE fort/memory/current.md and asserts:
  toContain("attended seats (Mayor, Warden) have")
  toContain("PROSE- gated")
  not.toContain("Forge runs with a kernel mask")

Three problems, in increasing order of seriousness:

1. It asserts against a live generated artifact rather than a fixture, so the test's subject
   changes whenever the fort's memory changes.
2. "PROSE- gated" IS A LINE-WRAP ARTIFACT, not semantic content. The cycle-7 rendering wrapped
   "PROSE-" and "gated" onto separate lines; cycle13 renders "PROSE-gated" unhyphenated, so the
   assertion fails on the presence of a SPACE. The test pins the shape of one fact version's word
   wrapping.
3. Consequently a green suite now REQUIRES the superseded fact to remain in the view, and the
   test's own name calls it "the active Forge truth" when the fort has formally ruled it is not.
   A test that enforces a record the fort has superseded is worse than no test: it converts the
   correct action into a red build, which is exactly why this sat for a day.

The test's INTENT is legitimate and should survive: the migrated write-boundaries fact is present,
and the pre-migration claim ("Forge runs with a kernel mask") is gone. Only its implementation is
wrong.

=== THE FIX ===

1. Regenerate fort/memory/current.md with `node scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs`. Do not hand-edit
   it; it is generated and says so.
2. Repoint test/memory.test.ts:158-166 at cycle13 SEMANTICS rather than cycle-7 wrapping. Assert
   on content that distinguishes the current truth from the superseded one — e.g. that the view
   names scripts/verify-impl.sh as the verifier the fort evolves, and that it does NOT contain the
   "except Mayor-writable verify.sh" claim. Never assert on a hyphenation or wrap artifact.
3. Consider whether the test should read a FIXTURE plus a separate thin assertion that the live
   view is not stale, rather than pinning live prose. State your reasoning either way in the
   handoff; this is the second time this file's coupling to live artifacts has produced a defect
   (see fortkit-gzv2).

=== NOT IN THIS BEAD, AND WHY ===

The CLASS defect is that nothing regenerates this view and no verifier detects it as stale:
`grep -rn consolidate-memory scripts/verify-impl.sh fort/scripts/ package.json .git/hooks/`
returns NOTHING. A staleness gate belongs in the verifier, which is scripts/verify-impl.sh —
kernel read-only to the Forge by the Shape B carve-out, and therefore MAYOR work. Emrith holds it.

DESIGN NOTE FOR THAT HALF, recorded here so it is not lost: the gate CANNOT be "regenerate and
diff the whole file." The view's "Open work" section changes every time any bead opens or closes,
so a whole-file diff would red the verifier on ordinary bead traffic and be disabled within a day.
It must be scoped — most likely to the Core facts section, or to a check that no fact rendered in
the view is status: superseded in the ledger. The second is cheaper and catches this exact bug.

=== PATH DISCIPLINE ===

You own fort/memory/current.md and test/memory.test.ts. A Regent sitting (fortkit-52vf.10) is
running in parallel over fort/scripts/** in all three forts, and Emrith holds scripts/verify-impl.sh.
Touch neither.

=== VERIFICATION ===

- fort/scripts/verify.sh green, 163 tests.
- fort/memory/current.md contains the cycle13 text and no longer contains "except Mayor-writable
  verify.sh" or any rendering of the superseded cycle-7 fact.
- Demonstrate the repointed test still FAILS if the view regresses: plant the superseded fact back
  into a scratch copy, or otherwise show the assertion discriminates. A test that cannot fail is
  the defect one directory over (fortkit-xgul.7.1 was closed on exactly this evidence).
acceptance_criteria: fort/memory/current.md regenerated and carrying cycle13-write-boundaries with no rendering of the superseded cycle-7 fact; test/memory.test.ts asserts cycle13 semantics rather than wrapping artifacts; the repointed test demonstrably fails if the view regresses; fort/scripts/verify.sh green at 163.
close_reason: Merged to main after Warden APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS (Ilva, 2026-08-13, 6 non-blocking, round one). She proved the central acceptance criterion herself rather than accepting the handoff — the reward-hacking flag being live for the gpt-5.6-terra rung — by running the new assertions against main's genuinely stale current.md: positive assertion 0 matches stale / 1 candidate, negative 1 / 0. Two of three flip on the exact regression, so the test can fail. She independently confirmed the wrap-artifact diagnosis and declined gate 1 with reasons (a generated view re-rendered from a supersession already Overseer-approved under cycle 13 and committed at 9d8464f). verify.sh green, 14 files / 163 tests, in her own scratch copy.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Verification complete. Writing the record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Scope note on the diff.** `git diff main..bead/1gz3` is misleading here: `main` has moved on (through `1335ece`), so that two-dot diff shows main's later work as deletions. The branch's actual content is two commits — `c141246` (regenerate the view + repoint the test) and `5e278be` (launcher handoff stamp) — touching exactly three files: `fort/memory/current.md`, `test/memory.test.ts`, `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-13-1gz3.md`. Path discipline held: `fort/scripts/**` and `scripts/verify-impl.sh` are untouched, so neither the parallel Regent sitting (`fortkit-52vf.10`) nor Emrith's surface was crossed.

**Model.** `gpt-5.6-terra`, recorded in the handoff header. GPT-family, so the reward-hacking flag applies and I did not accept the handoff's "a direct semantic probe passed … and failed for the superseded fact" on its word — I ran the differential myself against the real stale artifact (finding 1 below). The claim holds.

**Gate consideration (why not ESCALATE).** Human gate 1's prose covers "`fort/` files". I considered it and concluded no escalation is due: this diff introduces no constitutional text. It re-renders a *generated* view from a ledger supersession that was already made, already Overseer-approved under cycle 13 (`fortkit-52vf.9`), and already committed at `9d8464f`. `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, `.claude/` and every host-executed script are untouched. Treating a regeneration of a derived artifact as a constitutional amendment would be ceremony, and the over-breadth of that gate's prose is already the subject of open bead `fortkit-qj3`.

## Findings

**1. The repointed test demonstrably discriminates — verified, non-blocking (this is the bead's central acceptance criterion, and it is met).**
The bead required proof that the new assertion fails if the view regresses. I ran the differential against the genuine pre-fix artifact rather than a synthetic mutation: `git show main:fort/memory/current.md` (the stale view, still live on main) piped to `grep -c -F`.

- positive assertion `"scripts/verify-impl.sh: writable to the Mayor, kernel-RO to the Forge"` → **0 matches** on the stale view (fails), **1 match** on the candidate (passes).
- negative assertion `"except Mayor-writable verify.sh"` → **1 match** on the stale view (fails), **0 matches** on the candidate (passes).

Two of the three assertions flip on the exact regression. The test is not vacuous, and unlike `fortkit-xgul.7.1`'s subject it can fail. I also confirmed the diagnosis behind the bead: `PROSE- gated` was indeed a wrap artifact — `cycle7-write-boundaries.md:16-17` breaks after `PROSE-` and the generator joins lines with a space. The new assertion string sits entirely within `cycle13-write-boundaries.md:22`, so it does not depend on a join.

**2. The positive assertion still pins live prose, so the same failure mode survives in reduced form — non-blocking, file as a bead.**
This is the one finding I'd want carried forward. The defect this bead fixes is "a test pinning the shape of a fact's text converts the correct action into a red build." The new assertion is semantic rather than typographic, which is a real improvement, but it is still a 62-character substring of a live generated rendering, and it contains two hyphenated tokens (`verify-impl.sh`, `kernel-RO`). A benign reflow or light rewording of `cycle13-write-boundaries.md` — with no supersession, no change of truth — reds the suite again, and the next seat faces the same "correct action → red build" trap one wrapping removed. A form that keys on identity rather than prose would close the class: assert the view renders the link `fort/memory/facts/cycle13-write-boundaries.md` and renders no link to `cycle7-write-boundaries.md`, or better, the bead's own cheaper design — no fact rendered in the view is `status: superseded` in the ledger. The Forge did answer the bead's item 3 in the handoff ("fixtures should cover generator behavior, while this assertion catches the distinct failure of a changed facts ledger without regeneration"), which is a defensible position responsive to what was asked; I disagree only about the assertion's form, not about keeping a live-artifact check.

**3. One assertion from the original test was dropped rather than carried — non-blocking.**
`expect(current).not.toContain("Forge runs with a kernel mask")` is gone. The bead stated the test's surviving intent as two things: the migrated fact is present *and* the pre-migration claim "Forge runs with a kernel mask" is gone. Fix item 2 prescribed only the new pair, so this is a tension inside the bead rather than a departure from it, and the new negative guards a nearer and more likely regression. But the old line costs one line to keep and the bead explicitly named it. Nothing in the handoff claims it was preserved, so no record is false.

**4. The class defect has no bead — non-blocking, recommend filing (SO5-adjacent).**
The bead correctly scopes the staleness gate out (it belongs in `scripts/verify-impl.sh`, which is Mayor work) and records the design note that a whole-file diff would red on ordinary bead traffic. I searched `.beads-export.jsonl` and found no bead carrying that gate — the nearest neighbours are `fortkit-ybg7`, `fortkit-pfe` and `fortkit-cz1r`, none of which is it. Right now the design note survives only inside this bead's description, and this bead is about to close. Confirmed independently: `grep -rn consolidate-memory` across the verifier, `fort/scripts/`, `package.json` and the hooks still returns nothing.

**5. Merging leaves non-core sections of the view stale on arrival; the acceptance criterion still holds — non-blocking.**
The view was generated from the branch's ledger and bead snapshot, and main has since merged `bead/n3bk.1`, added a fact, and closed beads. The "Open work", "Latest handoffs" and gap sections will therefore disagree with post-merge reality. I checked whether this touches the *core* section, which is what the bead is actually about: main's only new fact, `masked-seats-cannot-measure-the-host.md`, is `tier: on-demand`, so it does not render in Core facts and the merged view's core section remains exactly correct. No action needed for this merge; it is another instance of finding 4.

**6. The regenerated view now carries no Mayor "State of work" line at all — non-blocking, honest, pre-existing.**
`mayor-2026-08-12-c.md` uses `## The verdict: REQUEST-CHANGES…` where the schema wants `## State of work`; I confirmed its headings directly. So the widest-read file loses the Mayor's state summary relative to main's older rendering. This is not concealed — the generator discloses it in Index build gaps, and I verified that new gap line is authentic generator behaviour rather than hand-written. Same family as `fortkit-cz1r`.

## What I verified independently, and what I took on faith

**Executed in my scratch copy (`/tmp/warden-1gz3`), against the candidate code:**
- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — **green**, 14 test files / **163 tests**, matching the acceptance criterion and the Forge's launcher-observed figure. All seven steps ran: memory-lint (core budgets printed), typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (62 files, no fixes), vitest, and ShellCheck — which I confirmed is actually installed (0.11.0) and therefore silent-clean rather than absent, since a missing binary would have exited 127 at that step. `skills-install` announced `SKIPPED` because cwd is not a git checkout; that is the verifier's announced-skip path and is unrelated to this diff.
- `npx vitest run test/memory.test.ts` — 8 tests passed, matching the handoff's targeted claim.
- The differential proof in finding 1, against `main`'s live stale `current.md`.
- The core-fact rendering: `current.md:9` matches `cycle13-write-boundaries.md:16-26` verbatim modulo newline→space joins; no `cycle7` text and no `cycle7-write-boundaries.md` link remain anywhere in the file.
- That the new Index-build-gap line is truthful, by reading `mayor-2026-08-12-c.md`'s headings.
- That the second commit's single changed line is a launcher timestamp normalisation plus an appended verifier block — the same stamp shape as `01615f3` on main, not an edit to any claim, so SO7 is satisfied.

**Taken on faith:**
- **That `current.md` is byte-identical to `node scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs` output rather than partly hand-edited.** I could not execute the generator: it writes, and every write path available to me is refused — `mkdir` outside the working directories is blocked by the harness, and `mkdir` inside cwd was denied by my profile, so I had nowhere to run it against a scratch root. Mitigation, not proof: the core-fact line matches the ledger exactly, the new gap line is independently confirmed, the handoff and bead-count sections are consistent with generator behaviour, and I found no hand-edit signature. Same instrument gap as `fortkit-bjle`.
- **The verifier's process exit code.** My profile refuses compound commands and `sh -c`, so I could not capture `$?`. The run reached and printed the final vitest summary with no step emitting failure output, and the diff touches no shell file, so ShellCheck's result is identical to main's.
- The Forge's "`npm ci` was needed" note in Failed attempts — immaterial to the artifact.

Round one. Nothing here meets the bar for blocking: the merge replaces a false core fact served to every seat at session start with the fort's actual ruling, the verifiers are green at the required count, the test can fail, and no record in the diff overstates what was done.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — verify.sh green 163, test proven to discriminate vs main's stale view; 6 non-blocking findings
