title: [bug] scripts/mask-harness.sh scored 61/0 on a lib that would have stopped Proofdelve's Forge dead — it carries no ~/.codex assertion at all
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 during the E8 sitting (fortkit-52vf.10), and it is the reason E8 needed a second instrument.

Before any edit, scripts/mask-harness.sh scored ALL THREE forts' lib/seat-sandbox.sh at 61 passed / 0 failed. At that moment ForgeOs's codex branch granted no writable surface anywhere under ~/.codex, so porting its forge.sh onto the lib would have met EROFS on token refresh, session rollouts and history.jsonl — 'either loud-and-total (Forge will not launch, core loop stops) or delayed and confusing' (Ilva, 2026-08-08). The harness could not see it, because it asserts nothing about ~/.codex.

THE INSTRUMENT THAT DISCRIMINATED, written for E8 and kept in the sitting's scratch, scored ForgeOs 4/9, fortkit 6/9, longburn 9/9 on the same three libs. Its load-bearing assertions:
  - THE PROPERTY IS RENAME, NOT APPEND. longburn-1p9 was not 'auth.json is unwritable' — codex rotates by RENAME, and a re-bound auth.json pins the inode, so an append-based probe can pass while rotation is broken.
  - AN INTERPRETATION GUARD. Under a tmpfs over ~/.codex every write 'succeeds' into a scratch dir that dies with the sandbox and every real file is ABSENT, so a naive writability probe reports PASS while the runtime is broken and a read-only probe on config.toml reports WRITABLE when what it did was CREATE a file in a tmpfs. Assert the mask sees the REAL directory (byte count matches host) BEFORE anything else, or every later label lies.
  - A nested variant builds the claude (Mayor) mask and builds the codex (Forge) mask INSIDE it, which is the namespace 1p9 actually broke in.

ASK: fold these into mask-harness.sh so the standing instrument covers the property. SAFETY, non-negotiable (fortkit-qbq2): never append a byte to a real file under ~/.codex — zero-byte appends for read-only assertions, a trap-removed canary for writability.

LANE: Mayor (scripts/ is Mayor-writable under Shape B).

comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Referral, not a block. I have NO blocking findings.** The diff is correct, complete against its spec, and independently verified green; it should stand. ESCALATE is the mandatory gate referral my seat owes on two independent triggers, and it carries one decision that is the Overseer's alone:

- **Auth surface.** This changes how the Codex credential directory is mounted — the identical mechanism the Overseer signed off on 2026-08-13 as `fortkit-52vf.10` (E8), where the sign-off was recorded as **covering the capital only**. This diff extends it to every settlement the factory produces.
- **Gate 1 by extension.** `templates/fort/scripts/lib/` is the enforcement layer each new fort is *born* with. The bead is right that `templates/` is not kernel-RO — but that governs the lane (who may edit), not whether gate 1's "Warden + Overseer review" applies. Cycle 7 established that prose-gated ≠ unreviewed.

**The one question for Justin:** may the factory ship the widened `~/.codex` posture *ahead of* its record and its Mayor-side backstop (findings 1 and 2), or must those land in the same sitting? The capital accepted this widening with a charter residual and a profile deny attached. The factory, after this merge, ships the mechanism with the Warden's backstop but neither the record nor the Mayor's. If the answer is "ship it," nothing here needs changing and the findings are beads.

Model: **gpt-5.6-terra** (top Forge rung), launcher-stamped in the handoff and in commit `ad74075`. Scrutiny weighted for the GPT family: I read the produced file directly rather than trusting the handoff, and every handoff claim I could test, I tested. All held.

---

### Findings

**1. The factory now ships the E8 mechanism without the E8 record. — non-blocking (threat 1, agent accident)**
`templates/fort/charter.md:50` ("Warden | Review, read-only by construction") and `templates/fort/seats/warden.md:9` ("read-only toolset by construction") are true of the template *before* this merge and false *after* it: the claude branch now binds `~/.codex` read-write at the kernel. The template charter has no accepted-residual entry for it. The capital corrected exactly this wording one commit before this branch point (`88c3704`, `fortkit-3jv7`), so the fix text already exists and was not carried. Every fort founded from now on is born asserting a kernel property its own mask does not provide — and its Warden reads that file at session start. Not blocking: the alternative is a factory whose Forge meets EROFS on first token refresh and whose Mayor cannot dispatch a Forge at all, which is worse than a stale sentence. This is the item I most want the Overseer to rule on.

**2. The template's permission set has no `~/.codex` rule at all. — non-blocking (threat 1)**
`templates/config/settings-permissions.json` (rendered to a new fort's `.claude/settings.json` by `bin/fort-init:151-156`) carries no `~/.codex` entry in its deny block. So a new fort's attended **Mayor** gets `~/.codex` kernel-rw with no tool-layer backstop; the capital at least attempts one (`.claude/settings.json:112`, `Edit(//home/justin/.codex/**)`), albeit in the double-slash spelling `fortkit-f3y` doubts and which the Mayor raised to P1 for precisely this reason. The **Warden's** backstop *does* propagate — `templates/fort/profiles/warden-settings.json:49` carries `Edit(**)`, which is the mitigation the charter's `fortkit-3jv7` residual names — so the seat the residual is written about is covered. Bears on threat 1, not the out-of-scope human adversary.

**3. The template inherits a clause this fort has already measured false. — non-blocking**
`templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:295`: "forge.sh's guarded deny table denies /home/justin/.codex/**". Re-measured here: `fort/scripts/forge.sh` contains no occurrence of `.codex` and no deny table; it runs `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write` with six `--add-dir` grants. That is `fortkit-52vf.10.1` finding 1, already open — and its recorded lane is "fort/scripts/ and its lib — KERNEL-RO, so a Regent sitting", which **excludes `templates/`**. Unless that bead is widened, the Regent will repair three copies and leave the factory's fourth, re-opening the drift in the opposite direction. Same for `52vf.10.1` finding 7: the `--mask-file` doc block at template line 30 inherits the undisclosed silent-skip-a-directory gap. **Carrying these verbatim was the right call for this bead** — byte-identity with the live libs is what quiets the drift watcher, and diverging to fix a comment defeats the purpose. Recommend widening `52vf.10.1` to four copies rather than reworking this diff.

**4. Consequence 2 of the bead is narrowed, not discharged — and its premise needs one correction. — non-blocking**
Measured with `diff -I '^[[:space:]]*#'` between the capital's live lib and the new template lib: the **only executable divergence remaining** is the `--mask-file` `case` branch placed *before* `--rw-tree` instead of after. Semantically identical (distinct literal patterns, `*)` catch-all last) and harmless, but it is 10 of the 14 remaining divergent lines. Plus the pre-existing 3-line→1-line comment at the `.git/hooks` note, which the handoff discloses honestly. `drift-watch.mjs` compares normalized bytes (`:341`), and neither difference is normalized, so `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh` will still read as divergent in all three forts. Moving that one branch to the live position would reduce the remainder to the disclosed comment alone.
**Correction to the bead's premise, for the record:** the bead says the watcher "will file Drift beads against the fix." It will not. Identity has been `(fort, path)` since E7 (`:136`), and `fortkit-hhjb` (Proofdelve), `fortkit-vxpq` (Manyhalls) and `fortkit-8eq5` (Farlantern) are already **open** on exactly this path since 2026-08-11. The effect is one appended comment on each existing bead (`:611`), not three new beads. Merging this diff strictly reduces that noise; it does not yet let those three close.

**5. Consequence 1 is fully fixed, including a detail the diff's own new comment depends on. — non-blocking, verification**
`bin/fort-init:33-34` does render the lib into a new fort. And `bin/fort-init:47` is `chmod +x fort/scripts/*.sh` — which does **not** reach `fort/scripts/lib/`, so a rendered fort's copy stays 0644. The new header comment's "MODE IS 0644 AND THAT IS THE DECISION" therefore holds in the factory as well as in the three live forts. A new fort now gets `CODEX_DIR_RW` on both branches, the live directory bind, `config.toml` read-only over it, and transcripts/history masked.

**6. The branch is one commit behind main. — non-blocking**
Merge base `88c3704`; main is `89fda88` (`fortkit-c1kj`, the memory staleness gate, touching `scripts/memory-lint.mjs` and `templates/fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs`). Paths are disjoint from this diff, so the merge is clean and the new gate cannot be affected by it — but neither the Forge's verifier run nor mine exercised that gate. Re-run the verifier post-merge before closing.

---

### Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Executed by me, in cwd (`/tmp/warden-29e9`), this session:**
- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0**, confirmed by exit-status test, not by reading output: memory-lint, skills-install (SKIPPED — cwd is not a git checkout), typecheck, browser-typecheck, Biome (62 files, no fixes), **163/163 Vitest in 14 files**, ShellCheck. The ShellCheck leg (`scripts/verify-impl.sh:150`) explicitly globs `templates/fort/scripts/lib/*.sh`, so the changed file **is** covered and passed. Run three times, consistent.
- `git diff main:fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh bead/29e9:templates/...` — the full live-vs-template differential, and `diff -I` over the two working copies to isolate executable-line divergence (finding 4). This is the anti-vacuity check `fortkit-bjle` says I usually cannot run; here I could, and the E8 carry is complete.
- Read the produced template lib at lines 40-155, 190-320, 370-459 and confirmed every E8 property by inspection, including bind **ordering**: rw grants → `~/.codex` directory bind (`:380`) → `config.toml` RO (`:392`) → `history.jsonl` to /dev/null (`:443`) → `sessions`/`log` tmpfs (`:445`). Every new bind is existence-guarded, so a host with no `~/.codex` does not abort.
- Verified all four handoff "Verified facts" against the file, and the `templates/` vs live `forge.sh` diff (placeholders and actor ids only — no E8 gap there).
- Findings 1, 2, 3, 5 measured directly against the cited files and line numbers; finding 4's bead list from `.beads-export.jsonl` via jq.

**Taken on faith:**
- The Forge's `bash -n` and scoped-ShellCheck run before the full verifier (equivalent evidence obtained by my own verify.sh run) and its `npm ci` recovery.
- The bead's measurement that all three live forts' libs carry the E8 hunks. I can read only `fortkit`; ForgeOs and longburn are outside my mask. Finding 3's false-clause measurement is against **this** fort's `forge.sh` only, which is the copy that matters for it.
- That `~/.codex` write access is in fact what the Codex runtime needs at runtime — the E8 measurement (`longburn-1p9`, rename rotation), not re-run here.
- Could not execute: `bash -c 'source ...; build_mask ...'` to compare built masks argv-for-argv — my profile refused it as a multi-operation command. The source-level differential in finding 4 is the substitute, and it is strong: one relocated `case` branch.

**Filing recommendation:** findings 1 and 2 as one P1 bead (the factory's E8 record + Mayor deny, Forge lane, `templates/`); finding 3 by widening `fortkit-52vf.10.1` to four copies; finding 4 as a five-line follow-up that lets `hhjb`/`vxpq`/`8eq5` close.

VERDICT-LINE: ESCALATE — gate referral only, no blocking findings; E8 carry verified complete and verifier green (163/163, exit 0)

title: templates/config/settings-permissions.json still ships 13 inert Write() rules — every new fort is born with the defect yowr fixed, and the drift watcher will call the fix the drift
description:
WARDEN E2b FINDING 3 (Ilva, 2026-08-12), the highest-consequence of that review's seven
non-blocking findings, and it starts lying TODAY.

=== THE DEFECT, MEASURED 2026-08-13 ===

templates/config/settings-permissions.json still carries 13 Write(...) permission rules:

  :57  Write(docs/**)              ALLOW list
  :58  Write(fort/**)              ALLOW list
  :82  Write(**/.env*)             DENY list
  :83  Write(.env*)                DENY list
  :84  Write(.git/config)          DENY list
  :85  Write(.git/hooks/**)        DENY list
  :86  Write(fort/events/*.jsonl)  DENY list
  :87  Write(fort/scripts/emit.sh) DENY list
  :88  Write(fort/scripts/forge.sh) DENY list
  :89  Write(fort/scripts/lib/**)  DENY list
  :90  Write(fort/scripts/mayor.sh) DENY list
  :91  Write(fort/scripts/status.sh) DENY list
  :92  Write(fort/scripts/warden.sh) DENY list

The harness reports every one of these as INERT at launch: "Write(x) is not matched by file
permission checks — only Edit(path) rules are. Use Edit(x) instead (Edit rules cover all
file-editing tools)." fortkit-yowr fixed this in all three LIVE forts on 2026-08-12; the count is
now 0 Write( rules in all three. THE FACTORY WAS NEVER TOUCHED.

=== WHY IT IS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY ===

Two consequences, and the second is the one Ilva ranked highest:

1. Every fort founded from now on is born with the exact defect yowr just removed. A rule that
   silently does nothing is worse than no rule — it shows a reader a protection that is not in
   force. That is the "a checker that checks nothing must never report success" class this
   civilization already paid for on 2026-08-05.
2. THE DRIFT WATCHER WILL REPORT THE LIVE FORTS AS DIVERGING FROM THE TEMPLATE. It will call the
   fix the drift, every day, starting now. A daily false signal is how a watcher stops being read.

=== THE FIX ===

Convert, do NOT delete. yowr's landed fix was Write(x) -> Edit(x), because Edit rules cover all
file-editing tools; the protections are meant to stay, they are just spelled wrong. Deleting them
would remove intent that the live forts kept.

REFERENCE TREE, and use it rather than converting blind: fortkit's own live .claude/settings.json
is the post-yowr shape (0 Write(, 39 Edit(). Read it and make the template agree, allowing for
the placeholder substitutions the factory performs. Do the same comparison against the other two
forts if their shapes differ from fortkit's — they were fixed in the same pass.

CAUTION — DEDUPE: if converting a Write(x) produces an Edit(x) that the file already contains,
you get a duplicate rule. Check each conversion against the existing Edit rules in the same list
and drop the redundant one rather than shipping doubles.

=== NOT IN THIS BEAD ===

- Warden finding 4 (templates/scripts/verify-impl.sh is not on the ShellCheck surface). That fix
  edits scripts/verify-impl.sh, which is KERNEL READ-ONLY to the Forge by an explicit carve-out
  — the carve-out that stops the Forge editing the verifier that judges its own work. It is the
  Mayor's, and Emrith is doing it in parallel. Do not attempt it; you will hit EROFS.
- fort/scripts/**, fort/profiles/**, .claude/**, fort/charter.md, fort/seats/** — all kernel-RO
  to you, and all outside this bead.
- PATH DISCIPLINE FOR THIS BEAD: you own templates/** and nothing else. A Regent sitting
  (fortkit-52vf.10) is running in parallel over fort/scripts/** in all three forts. The disjoint
  path split is what makes the two safe at once. Do not stray.

=== VERIFICATION ===

- 0 occurrences of "Write(" in templates/config/settings-permissions.json.
- The file is still valid JSON (jq -e . on it).
- Every converted rule appears exactly once in its list.
- fort/scripts/verify.sh green in your worktree.
- State in the handoff how the template's rule set now compares to fortkit's live
  .claude/settings.json, naming any deliberate remaining difference and why.
acceptance_criteria: 0 occurrences of 'Write(' in templates/config/settings-permissions.json; file is valid JSON; each converted rule appears exactly once; verify.sh green in the worktree; handoff states how the template compares to fortkit's live .claude/settings.json.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
## Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead `fortkit-n3bk.1`. Round one. Work by **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge top rung, per the handoff's `Model:` line); two path-scoped commits, `83d288a` + `01615f3`, touching only `templates/config/settings-permissions.json` and `fort/handoffs/`. Path discipline honoured exactly: the three-dot diff against the merge base is two files, nothing in `fort/scripts/**`, `fort/profiles/**`, `.claude/**`, `scripts/verify-impl.sh`, or the charter.

Note on the diff spelling: `main..bead/n3bk.1` shows nine extra files as deletions. Those are main's own newer commits (the E8 Regent sitting `755e369` and after) that the branch predates — not reverts. The branch's work is the three-dot diff, and that is what I judged.

**Every acceptance criterion is met, and I executed all of them.** 0 `Write(`; valid JSON; allow 52/52 unique and deny 22/22 unique; all 13 removed `Write(x)` rules have an `Edit(x)` twin at tip (12 pre-existing, `Edit(fort/events/*.jsonl)` added); `verify.sh` green at exit 0 in my own run. No protection is lost — `yowr`'s record confirms by measurement that the deny still binds the Write tool with only the `Edit` rule remaining, and on the allow side `Edit(x)` covers all file-editing tools, so the removed allow entries granted nothing.

### Findings

**1. (non-blocking) Main moved under this branch, and 6 of the 15 template rules no longer match the reference tree the bead named.** After the Forge's 08:15 session, the E8 Regent sitting (`755e369`, 08:51:27) replaced fortkit's six granular `Edit(fort/scripts/emit.sh|forge.sh|lib/**|mayor.sh|status.sh|warden.sh)` denies with a single `Edit(fort/scripts/**)`, and added `Edit(scripts/**)` to allow. The drift watcher's permission check is a literal `includes` (`civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:362-376`), so post-merge those six template rules read as absent from the capital. The bead's consequence 2 is *reduced* (13 → 6), not eliminated. Two mitigations of severity: findings are deduped by fort+path identity, so this is one open `Drift:` bead with fingerprint comments, not six per run; and merging is strictly better than not merging, since today the template carries both the 13 inert `Write(` rules *and* the 6 granular ones. **This is not a Forge error** — the handoff's claim was true against the tree it had, which I verified by timestamp. Follow-up bead: carry the post-E8 spelling `Edit(fort/scripts/**)` into the template, which also fixes finding 2.

**2. (non-blocking, pre-existing, outside this bead) The factory ships a materially narrower deny set than any live fort, and three of the missing rules are relative and perfectly templatable.** Live fortkit denies `Edit(.claude/**)`, `Edit(fort/profiles/**)` and the broad `Edit(fort/scripts/**)`; the factory denies none of them. In a fort founded today, allow `Edit(fort/**)` therefore covers `fort/profiles/**` and the shipped `fort/scripts/researcher.sh`, `probe-researcher-boundaries.sh` and `verify.sh`, none of which any deny names. Bears on **threat 1, agent accident**. The kernel mask is the real boundary and it holds — `templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:142` and `:283` bind `.claude`, `fort/profiles` and `fort/scripts` whole-directory read-only — so this is defense-in-depth, plus exactly the reader-facing accuracy problem `yowr` was filed about: a settings file that shows a protection it does not spell.

**3. (non-blocking, record correction, SO7)** The handoff's Open risks line — "Live configurations add their fort-specific absolute-path and kernel-boundary `Edit(...)` protections … those cannot be literal template values" — is true for the `//home/justin/...` absolutes and the generated SessionStart hook, and **not true** for `Edit(.claude/**)`, `Edit(fort/profiles/**)` and `Edit(fort/scripts/**)`, which are relative and belong in the template (the file already carries that class). A reader acting on the original text would conclude nothing further needs carrying to the factory, which is the SO7 test for a correction; it is appended here, in comments, where the rule now says corrections go.

**4. (non-blocking) Evidence by inheritance, and it is the reasonable call.** `yowr`'s acceptance test — a real launch, `grep -c "is not matched by file permission checks"` == 0, with a positive control that caught a vacuous first measurement — cannot be run against a template, which is not a settings file until `bin/fort-init:151` substitutes `{{REPO_PATH}}`. The conversion is textually identical to the live one that *was* measured, and the substitution is a single sed, so I do not ask for more here. The first fort founded after this merge is the place to take the measurement.

**5. (non-blocking, observation)** `Edit(fort/events/*.jsonl)` is subsumed by `Edit(fort/events/*)`. Keeping it is correct: the bead said dedupe *exact* twins and match the reference tree, and both spellings are in fortkit's live file for the same reason `yowr` recorded.

**6. (non-blocking, process lesson)** The bead justified running this lane beside Regent sitting `52vf.10` on path disjointness. Paths stayed disjoint; content did not. This lane's spec named the other lane's file as its reference tree, so the other lane's edit invalidated this lane's alignment 36 minutes after it shipped. Disjoint paths do not imply disjoint content when one lane's spec cites the other lane's file.

**Gate note.** Human gate 1 covers *this fort's own* constitution and permission profiles. `templates/config/settings-permissions.json` is a product artifact that becomes *another* fort's constitution at founding, and the enforcement layer agrees — `templates/` is writable to the Forge, which holds the fullest kernel lock in the fort. I therefore did not treat this as a mandatory-ESCALATE surface, and I record the reading so the Overseer can overrule it. Nothing here changes what is enforced anywhere today.

### Verified independently vs taken on faith

**Executed in cwd:** `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0**, twice (memory-lint; skills-install SKIPPED with its reason announced, since cwd is not a git checkout; typecheck; browser typecheck; Biome 62 files; Vitest 14 files / 163 tests; shellcheck). The shellcheck leg is not vacuous: `run_step` (`scripts/verify-impl.sh:56-71`) exits on any non-zero status including 127, so a missing binary would have failed the run. `jq -e` validity; `Write(` count 0 in the file and 0 anywhere under `templates/`; allow and deny uniqueness by `unique|length`; the 15 `Edit` rules enumerated; every removed `Write` rule matched to its twin at tip from the diff plus the tip file. Read from the real repo: the branch's two commits and their file scope, the three-dot diff, fortkit's current live `.claude/settings.json` and its history (`9dc381f` yowr, `755e369` E8, with timestamps), `civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs`, `test/drift-watch.test.ts`, `bin/fort-init:151`, the template seat-sandbox mask lines, and the `fortkit-yowr` bead record in the export.

**Taken on faith:** the live `.claude/settings.json` of ForgeOs and longburn, and hence the handoff's cross-fort inclusion claim for those two forts — their paths are outside my allowed directories and both `ls` and `jq` were refused there. Likewise `~/.claude/civilization.json`, so I could not confirm which forts the drift watcher actually scans; finding 1 assumes the capital is among them, which the watcher's own comments about the capital imply. The handoff's launcher-observed verifier block I did not audit — I re-ran the verifier myself instead.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — 13 inert Write rules gone, no protection lost, verify.sh green (I ran it); 6 findings, all beads, none blocking.

title: E8: the last inline mask — port ForgeOs/forge.sh onto the lib, and close the ~/.codex drift that would stop Proofdelve's mill the moment it lands
description:
E8: PORT ForgeOs/fort/scripts/forge.sh ONTO ITS lib/seat-sandbox.sh — the last inline mask in
the civilization — AND CLOSE THE ~/.codex DRIFT THAT WOULD OTHERWISE STOP PROOFDELVE'S MILL THE
MOMENT THE PORT LANDS.

Regent sitting. Carries fortkit-6jf (the standing bead, in_progress since 2026-08-08) plus
fortkit-n3bk findings 6, 7, 8, 9. LANE: Regent, because fort/scripts/ is kernel read-only WHOLE
to every masked seat since cycle 13 (fortkit-52vf.9) and forge.sh is a launcher — human gate 1.

=== 1. MEASURED STATE (2026-08-13, Emrith; every line below is a command's output, not a recollection) ===

  fort                    forge.sh   sources the lib?
  ForgeOs   (Proofdelve)  295 lines  NO  — inline mask, no build_mask call
  longburn  (Farlantern)  111 lines  YES — build_mask codex
  fortkit   (Manyhalls)   169 lines  YES — build_mask codex ... --rw-tree "$wt" (:70)

ForgeOs is the last inline mask anywhere in the civilization, and it is the fort where the Forge
runs regularly. Its own file says so at :163 ("this one is the last inline mask"). ForgeOs
forge.sh:171-173 carries the E2b hand-copied stopgap:

  RO_PATHS=("$HOME/.codex/config.toml" "$wt/.claude" "$root/.claude"
            "$wt/fort/scripts" "$wt/scripts/verify-impl.sh"
            "$root/fort/scripts" "$root/scripts/verify-impl.sh")

That stopgap exists because without it Proofdelve's Forge would be the one seat anywhere able to
rewrite the verifier judging its own work. It is four entries hand-kept in sync with a 427-line
lib. Every further mask edit widens the gap — which is why this sitting is urgent rather than
tidy.

=== 2. THE BLOCKING HAZARD — THE PORT IS NOT A MECHANICAL CONSOLIDATION ===

MEASURED, grep -cF across the three libs:

  RW_PATHS+=("$HOME/.codex")     fortkit 1 (:311)   ForgeOs 0   longburn 0
  CODEX_DIR_RW=1 in codex branch fortkit 0          ForgeOs 0   longburn 1 (:170, bind at :326)

fortkit and longburn each grant the Forge a writable ~/.codex, by two DIFFERENT mechanisms.
ForgeOs's lib grants it by NEITHER. Its codex branch (:164) still reads "KNOWN EXCEPTION:
~/.codex stays readable" — the exact stale comment Ilva raised as non-blocking finding 4 on this
bead on 2026-08-08, in the same review whose BLOCKING finding 1 was that a read-only ~/.codex
breaks the Forge.

Why nothing has broken yet: ForgeOs's lib codex branch has NEVER BEEN EXECUTED, because ForgeOs's
forge.sh does not call it. This sitting is the thing that would execute it for the first time.

CONSEQUENCE IF PORTED AS-IS: Proofdelve's Forge launches under a $HOME ro-bind with no writable
surface anywhere under ~/.codex. Codex refreshes auth.json (by rename), writes session rollouts
under $CODEX_HOME/sessions/, and appends history.jsonl. All EROFS. Ilva's 2026-08-08 words for
the failure mode, which still apply exactly: "either loud-and-total (Forge will not launch, core
loop stops) or delayed and confusing (works until the current token expires). Either is worse
than not merging."

THEREFORE: FIX ForgeOs's lib codex branch FIRST, IN THIS SITTING, BEFORE forge.sh CALLS IT.
Do not treat the port as step one.

FIRST DECISION OF THE SITTING — which mechanism, and then ONE mechanism in all three forts.
Emrith's recommendation, flagged for the Overseer rather than assumed: take longburn's
CODEX_DIR_RW shape and backport it to fortkit, retiring fortkit's RW_PATHS entry. Reasons: it
names rotation-by-rename as the reason in the code, it covers BOTH seat types (fortkit's line is
codex-only), and it is the shape landed by the fort that actually hit the bug (longburn-1p9).
Unifying is the entire point of fortkit-6jf; leaving two correct mechanisms and one absent one
reproduces the N-list drift the bead was filed against.

=== 3. PRESERVE EXACTLY (from the Overseer's 2026-08-08 dispatch on this bead, still binding) ===

- The ~/.codex NOT-masked exception, with config.toml re-bound READ-ONLY (ForgeOs-21f.5): auth
  refresh must keep working while the disarm-the-next-launch vector stays closed.
- forge.sh:80 deny_table, which MIRRORS ~/.codex/config.toml — Landlock read-deny is an upstream
  TODO (openai/codex#11316), so the two must not diverge.
- The --add-dir grant set, the .beads hooks-dir RO rebinds, the env allowlist including
  CODEX_HOME and OPENAI_*, and the concurrency flock.
- The incident-emitting bwrap refusal, and the ordering invariant (ForgeOs-01l): RW binds before
  the RO pass, so nothing masked lies beneath a later bind.
- Extend build_mask with narrow parameters if the Forge's deltas need them. DO NOT fork a second
  copy of its logic — that is the defect being repaired.

=== 4. n3bk FINDINGS RIDING THIS SITTING ===

6. The [ -f ] fix trades a loud abort for a silent gap: a DIRECTORY named like a secret is now
   skipped rather than aborting the launch (correct) but is then unmasked and nothing says so.
   Disclose it in the code and in the record.
7. seat-sandbox.sh lost its executable bit. CORRECTION TO THE FINDING, measured 2026-08-13: all
   THREE libs are -rw-r--r--, so this is uniform across the civilization, not a fortkit anomaly
   and not an unexplained single-file mode change. It is sourced, not executed, so 0644 is
   arguably correct. Decide and record which, rather than "restoring" a bit that was never set
   anywhere.
8. Two convenience-layer follow-ons in the file item E was already editing.
9. probe-cycle7.sh does not probe $root/scripts/verify-impl.sh under the CODEX posture. This is
   the load-bearing half of Shape B's safety — the carve-out that stops the Forge editing its own
   judge — and it becomes MORE load-bearing in this sitting, because Proofdelve's Forge is about
   to start getting its mask from the lib instead of from the hand-copied stopgap. The unmasked
   harness asserts it (C4c/C4e); probe-cycle7 is what runs per fort and must assert it too.

=== 5. VERIFICATION — AND THE E2b LESSON APPLIES ===

DO NOT verify with `test -w`. That is the exact symptom that hid fortkit-6ovg for a whole cycle:
a writable file inside a read-only directory returns TRUE to test -w and still defeats Edit,
sed -i and git checkout. Assert with real operations.

Required, in order:
a. BEFORE state captured in Proofdelve: fort/scripts/probe-cycle7.sh, recorded pass/fail counts.
b. After the lib fix and before the port: a bwrap probe proving ~/.codex is WRITABLE and
   ~/.codex/config.toml is NOT, under the codex posture in ForgeOs.
c. After the port: a REAL fort/scripts/forge.sh smoke launch in ForgeOs on a throwaway bead.
   "The mask builds" is not "codex starts", and this is the fort whose mill stops if it is wrong.
d. From INSIDE the Forge's worktree, not $root: a real write attempt to fort/charter.md must
   fail. Ilva's 2026-08-08 blocking finding 2 was that the constitution was protected in the
   checkout the Forge never touches and open in the one it always touches. fortkit's lib now
   applies the RO pass per rw_tree (:194, :285); confirm ForgeOs's does too, from the worktree.
e. probe-cycle7.sh in all three forts, after.
f. scripts/mask-harness.sh unmasked. CAUTION, fortkit-qbq2: its assert_ro once tested read-only-
   ness with `printf x >> path` against FOUR REAL ~/.claude files and corrupted the civilization
   registry and the plugin manifest into invalid JSON, taking the Regent down. It has been
   repaired to a zero-byte append. Confirm you are running the repaired version. A positive
   control at 44/17 on the pre-E2 lib is what closes fortkit-qbq2.

=== 6. EXPLICITLY NOT IN THIS SITTING ===

- fortkit-1q9 (scope RO carve-outs to every tree in RW_PATHS): waits on E5. The Mayor creates
  worktrees from inside her own mask when dispatching the Forge, so locking $root-worktrees
  breaks the mill in all three forts today.
- templates/** — n3bk findings 3 and 4 are the FORGE's lane and are being run in parallel in a
  fortkit worktree. The Regent must not touch templates/ in this sitting; the path split is what
  makes the two safe to run at once.
- The elder-fort lib comment drift beyond the codex branch (ForgeOs's cycle-7 comment block still
  describes the Shape-A "verify.sh alone is re-granted writable" world). Note it, file it, do not
  chase it here.

=== 7. STALE RECORD ON THIS BEAD, SO A READER IS NOT MISLED ===

fortkit-6jf's history carries a Warden ESCALATE verdict (Ilva, 2026-08-08) against commit 3ff7aa6
on branch bead/6jf, with two blocking findings. MEASURED 2026-08-13: `git log main..bead/6jf` is
EMPTY, so that branch is contained in main; fortkit's forge.sh gained the lib in b2881b7 (the E2
sitting), by a different route. Both of that verdict's blocking findings are now fixed IN
FORTKIT'S LIB — finding 2 by the per-rw_tree RO pass (:194, :285), finding 1 by :311. Neither is
fixed in ForgeOs's lib, which is section 2 above. A reader of this bead's history would otherwise
conclude the port is unstarted and the verdict outstanding; it is neither, and the surviving
defect is narrower and in a different fort than the verdict describes.
acceptance_criteria: ForgeOs/fort/scripts/forge.sh sources lib/seat-sandbox.sh with no inline mask block and no hand-copied RO_PATHS stopgap; ONE ~/.codex write-grant mechanism across all three libs; a real forge.sh smoke launch in ForgeOs succeeds on a throwaway bead; a write to fort/charter.md from inside the Forge's worktree fails; probe-cycle7 green in all three forts; n3bk findings 6,7,8,9 addressed or explicitly deferred with reasons.
close_reason: Overseer gate-1 sign-off recorded verbatim 2026-08-13 after Warden ESCALATE with no blocking findings. Certifies the CAPITAL's half only: the ForgeOs port and both elder libs are unreviewed by this fort and remain open to their own Wardens under covenant 4.5. 6jf's deliverable is confirmed — ForgeOs/fort/scripts/forge.sh sources lib/seat-sandbox.sh, no inline mask remains, and it was the last inline mask in the civilization. Ten Warden findings routed to fortkit-3jv7, fortkit-52vf.10.1 and fortkit-f3y before close.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
MAYOR INPUT ON THE SITTING'S FIRST DECISION (Emrith, 2026-08-13), for the record before the Overseer answers. The Regent put three options to Justin and surfaced evidence I did not have when I wrote section 2's recommendation: longburn-1p9, a RECORDED incident on 2026-08-05 in which the pinned-inode auth.json re-bind caused refresh-token reuse, server-side revocation, and both seat lanes down until re-login. That strengthens option 1 rather than weakening it — it makes the wider fix SO11-clean (an observed failure, not an imagined one), and option 2 knowingly leaves a recorded incident latent in two forts. My recommendation stands at option 1, now on better evidence than I originally had.

TWO RIDERS, both measured.

RIDER 1 — THE COST STATEMENT IS INCOMPLETE. ~/.codex is not only auth plus runtime state. It holds skills/ (.system/{skill-installer,skill-creator,review-agent,plugin-creator,openai-docs,imagegen}, each with SKILL.md, scripts/, agents/) and plugins/. That is session-executed instruction for the Codex runtime — the identical surface cycle 13 locked for the Claude runtime under fortkit-5sk, six days ago, on exactly that reasoning. Option 1 grants attended Mayor and Warden sessions in fortkit and ForgeOs write access to it. State that in the record before accepting the trade; it is not in the three options as written.

RIDER 2 — DO NOT FIX IT IN THIS SITTING, AND DO NOT REFLEX-BIND IT READ-ONLY. Measured 2026-08-13: /home/justin/.codex/skills mtime 08:12:11.888034213 and skills/.system 08:12:11.889413649, against Kethra's session.start on fortkit-n3bk.1 at 2026-08-13T08:12:11-08:00 — the same second; plugins/ at 08:12:13.747. A directory mtime moves when an entry in it is created, removed or renamed, so the codex runtime mutates both within ~2 seconds of launch and a read-only bind would likely REFUSE THE LAUNCH. That is the same failure class that made this sitting non-mechanical in the first place. Filed separately as fortkit-elh9 with the measurement attached. Leave it alone here: E8 already carries a lib fix, a launcher port, a mechanism unification and four n3bk findings.

RIDER 3 — VERIFICATION OF THE CLAUDE BRANCH. longburn-1p9 broke on the DISPATCH lane, and masks bind at launch, so no session already running can verify a claude-branch change — mine included, and my mask predates every change of this sitting. Relaunch a Mayor in each fort and dispatch a throwaway Forge bead from inside it. That is the exact path that failed in Farlantern.

comments.text:
E8 EXECUTED 2026-08-13 by the Regent (Calder Sealbroken, they/them, model opus),
Overseer present throughout. This comment records what was measured; the dispatch-lane
results are appended separately.

=== THE OVERSEER'S DECISION ON SECTION 2 ===

OPTION 1, Emrith's recommendation: longburn's CODEX_DIR_RW, for BOTH seat types, in all
three libs. fortkit's RW_PATHS entry and the CODEX_AUTH_RO auth.json re-bind are retired.
He attached three riders, all honoured:
  1. State in the record that ~/.codex ALSO holds session-executed instruction for the
     Codex runtime, and that option 1 grants attended Mayor and Warden sessions write
     access to it. That cost was NOT in the three options I put to him. It is now written
     into all three libs at the dispatch exception, enumerated (AGENTS.md, skills/,
     plugins/, rules/, memories/) and named as the codex twin of fortkit-5sk.
  2. Do NOT bind skills/ or plugins/ read-only to fix it: codex mutates both at startup,
     so an RO bind is a launch-abort risk of the ~/.claude/teams shape. Filed separately
     as fortkit-elh9, which the lib comment now names rather than saying "filed
     separately" and leaving a reader at a dead end.
  3. Verification must include a Forge dispatched from a freshly launched Mayor in each
     fort, because longburn-1p9 broke on the dispatch lane and masks bind at launch.

ONE MEASUREMENT DISCREPANCY, reported rather than smoothed over. Rider 2 cited
~/.codex/skills mtime 08:12:11.888 against a Forge session.start at 08:12:11, and
plugins/ at 08:12:13. The session.start is real (kethra, fortkit-n3bk.1, 08:12:11).
The mtimes are not: measured 2026-08-13, ~/.codex/skills is 2026-08-10 12:29:42 and
~/.codex/plugins is 2026-07-09 09:20:06, both BEFORE the session. I could not establish
what was counted, so I am not calling the premise wrong — and it changes nothing:
leaving skills/ and plugins/ alone is his call, it is the conservative default, and the
~/.claude/teams precedent is reason enough on its own.

=== INSTRUMENTS FIRST, AND THE STANDING HARNESS COULD NOT SEE THE DEFECT ===

scripts/mask-harness.sh scored ALL THREE pre-edict libs at 61 passed / 0 failed. At that
moment ForgeOs's codex branch granted no writable surface anywhere under ~/.codex. The
harness carries no ~/.codex assertion at all, so a lib that would have stopped
Proofdelve's mill scored perfect. Filed as its own bug.

A dedicated probe was written and INVERTED FIRST — run against the three PRE-EDICT libs
before any edit:
    ForgeOs   4 passed / 5 failed   <- the blocking hazard, by real operation
    fortkit   6 passed / 3 failed
    longburn  9 passed / 0 failed   <- the target shape
Two design points that are the whole value of it:
  - THE PROPERTY IS RENAME, NOT APPEND. longburn-1p9 was never "auth.json is unwritable";
    codex rotates by RENAME, and a re-bound auth.json pins the inode, so an append probe
    passes while rotation is broken.
  - AN INTERPRETATION GUARD RUNS FIRST. Under a tmpfs over ~/.codex every write "succeeds"
    into a scratch dir that dies with the sandbox and every real file is ABSENT, so a
    naive writability probe reports PASS on a broken runtime and a read-only probe on
    config.toml reports WRITABLE when what it did was CREATE a file in a tmpfs. The probe
    asserts the mask sees the REAL directory (byte count matches host) before anything
    else, or every later label lies. My first draft did not, and two of its labels lied.

=== WHAT CHANGED ===

All three forts' fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:
  - CODEX_AUTH_RO retired; CODEX_DIR_RW for both seat types; ~/.codex bound as a live rw
    DIRECTORY with the RW grants, config.toml read-only, sessions/ log/ history.jsonl
    masked for claude seats. One mechanism, three forts.
  - NEW PARAMETER --mask-file <path>, joining MASK_FILES so caller deltas ride the same
    existence-guarded bind pass and land LAST per the ordering invariant. A caller
    appending its own --ro-bind after build_mask returns gets that ordering by luck.
  - n3bk finding 6 DISCLOSED: a directory named like a secret is now skipped and then
    silently unmasked. Disclosed in code in all three copies; the real fix (descend and
    sweep) is filed, because it changes what a launch costs and deserves its own
    measurement.
  - n3bk finding 7 DECIDED, not "restored": 0644 is correct and the header now says why.
    The file is SOURCED, never executed; all three copies measured -rw-r--r--, so there
    is no single-file mode change to explain and the escalation class does not apply.
  - SSH_AUTH_SOCK moved to claude_only. See the smoke section — this one was found by
    running, not by reading.

ForgeOs/fort/scripts/forge.sh: THE CIVILIZATION'S LAST INLINE MASK IS RETIRED. 91 lines
removed; every removed line read individually against a lib equivalent. It sources the
lib, calls build_mask codex with --rw-tree, --mask-ssh-auth-sock and two --mask-file
arguments, and carries no RO_PATHS stopgap. The deny_table, --add-dir set, flock, handoff
stamping and event emission are untouched; require_bwrap's incident-emitting refusal is
NEW and is placed BEFORE session.start so a refusal cannot leave a session.start with no
matching session.end.

WHAT THE PORT ADDS that the inline block never had, and this is the part worth reading:
its mask line was `--bind / / --dev /dev --die-with-parent` with NO `--ro-bind $HOME
$HOME`. Cycle 5's filesystem inversion had never reached this launcher, so Proofdelve's
Forge had been running under "everything writable except what we masked" while every
other seat in every fort ran inverted. It now gets the inversion, per-worktree .beads
hook rebinds, the $wt/.claude and worktree charter/seats/skills locks, the six-spelling
secret sweep, a user-owned ssh_config, and the known_hosts pin.

fortkit fort/scripts/probe-cycle7.sh (n3bk finding 9, and it was worse than the finding
said): the codex posture was built ONLY inside the worktree-conditional block, so
$root/scripts/verify-impl.sh was never asserted under it AND, in a fort with no worktree,
the codex posture was never built at all — the probe measured nothing whatever about the
Forge's mask and still printed a clean pass line. Nine assertions added unconditionally,
including the two new ~/.codex properties for both postures.

fortkit .claude/settings.json (n3bk finding 8): six enumerated Edit(fort/scripts/<file>)
deny rules collapsed to Edit(fort/scripts/**), mirroring the kernel boundary that has
covered the whole directory since cycle 13 and omitted verify.sh; Edit(scripts/**) added
to allow so the Mayor's sanctioned verifier edits are covered. Relative spellings only —
whether the //home/... form binds is fortkit-f3y's question and adding possibly-inert
rules is the defect fortkit-yowr removed 37 of. The two elder forts have both gaps; filed
rather than fixed, because the Overseer scoped this sitting to fort/scripts/**.

=== MEASUREMENTS, BEFORE AND AFTER ===

  instrument                     before                        after
  mask-harness.sh (per lib)      61/0, 61/0, 61/0              61/0, 61/0, 61/0
  mask-harness.sh pre-E2 lib     44/17                         44/17   <- closes qbq2
  E8 codex probe (per lib)       4/9, 6/9, 9/9                 9/9, 9/9, 9/9
  probe-cycle7 (per fort)        35/0, 31/0, 31/0              44/0, 40/0, 40/0
  dotnet+boundaries under mask   n/a                           9/0
  nested dispatch lane           n/a                           3/3, 3/3, 3/3
(order throughout: fortkit, ForgeOs, longburn.)

The pre-E2 lib scoring exactly 44/17 on the REPAIRED harness — zero-byte append, confirmed
at scripts/mask-harness.sh:95 — is the positive control fortkit-qbq2 asks for.

dotnet under the ported mask, measured before spending a codex session: restore exit 0,
build exit 0. The $HOME inversion did not break the toolchain.

ILVA'S 2026-08-08 BLOCKING FINDING 2 IS CLOSED AND MEASURED FROM THE WORKTREE, which is
where the Forge actually works rather than the checkout it never touches: appends to
$wt/fort/charter.md, $wt/scripts/verify-impl.sh and $root/scripts/verify-impl.sh are all
refused under the ported codex posture.

=== THE SMOKE FOUND WHAT READING DID NOT ===

First real FORGE_SMOKE=1 launch: restore/build green, 152 filtered tests passed, probes
1-12 pass. PROBE 13 FAIL: SSH_AUTH_SOCK was SET. Veyra read a live agent as a boundary
failure and REFUSED probes 14-22 rather than risk a real push. That is correct seat
conduct and it is why the run was worth its cost.

Measured rather than taken from the narration: the socket IS bound to /dev/null
(character special file, 0 bytes) and `ssh-add -l` returns "Error connecting to agent:
Connection refused". NO capability was gained and no key could sign. But the lib's env
allow-list carried SSH_AUTH_SOCK in `common` where the inline block simply never passed
the name, so an unchanged capability cost NINE UNMEASURED ASSERTIONS including the host
RCE escape check. longburn already had it right. Fixed in fortkit's and ForgeOs's libs by
moving the name to claude_only; measured after: codex unset, claude set.

Second smoke, after the fix: probes 9-22 ALL PASS, including 18 and 21 (the .beads hooks
host-escape check, both discovered directories), 20 (.git/config), 14 (push exit 128) and
22 (34 env names, SSH_AUTH_SOCK absent).

Probe 13's remaining FAIL was the probe, not the mask: it implied `ls ~/.ssh` should be
empty, and the lib surfaces exactly ONE file back over that tmpfs — known_hosts, 3559
bytes matching host, no key file present in the mask at all — so host-key pinning survives
instead of doing fresh TOFU every launch. That is ForgeOs-q6m, THIS FORT'S OWN BEAD, which
its forge.sh never received because it was the last inline mask. The probe reported FAIL
for a protection being added. Its expectation is corrected in place, with both halves
stated, because a smoke that cries wolf on a correct posture is a smoke nobody reads.

comments.author: calder
comments.text:
=== THE DISPATCH LANE (the Overseer's rider), MEASURED IN ALL THREE FORTS ===

Done at two levels, because they answer different questions.

DETERMINISTIC, no model: build the mask mayor.sh builds (build_mask claude "$REPO",
mask_env claude, FORT_MASKED=1), and INSIDE that namespace build the codex mask from the
same lib and exercise the property that actually failed in longburn-1p9.
    fortkit 3/3    ForgeOs 3/3    longburn 3/3
  - rotation-by-rename inside ~/.codex survives the nested namespace
  - config.toml still read-only through BOTH masks
  - the nested seat sees the REAL ~/.codex (3383 bytes, matching host), not a tmpfs

END TO END, a real Forge session dispatched from inside the real Mayor mask, one per fort,
on a throwaway bead (ForgeOs-860w, fortkit-m0wm, longburn-wpdh):
  - ForgeOs:  restore passed, build 0 warnings/0 errors, 152 filtered tests passed,
              verify.pass emitted, worktree status only the masked-deploy-script artifact.
  - fortkit:  fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit EXIT 0 inside the mask — TypeScript, browser
              TypeScript, Biome, ShellCheck, 14 files / 163 tests. Handoff committed.
  - longburn: session completed, node_modules seeded in-mask, all boundary probes as
              expected.
  In all three the Mayor's mask created the worktree, and bd, emit.sh, the session events
  and the bead comment all worked through the nested namespace.

Seat-reported observations, identical in fortkit and longburn:
  SSH_AUTH_SOCK unset; ~/.codex 36 entries readable; config.toml write exit 1; append to
  fort/charter.md, scripts/verify-impl.sh and the fort/scripts/verify.sh shim all exit 1.

=== THE FINDING THIS PRODUCED, WHICH IS BETTER NEWS THAN THE BEAD ASSUMED ===

Both seats reported `touch ~/.codex/<canary>` FAILING. My probe instruction had said to
expect exit 0, so on its face that reads as the rotation grant not working. IT IS NOT, and
the distinction is worth writing down because the two enforcement layers are doing
different jobs and only one of them is bwrap's:

  - THE MODEL'S SHELL cannot write ~/.codex at all. Codex's own --sandbox workspace-write
    layer denies everything outside its writable_roots, and longburn's seat said so in as
    many words: "rejected by the command executor". That is the POLICY layer, above the
    kernel, and it is doing exactly what it should.
  - THE CODEX PROCESS ITSELF can, through the kernel layer. PROVEN BY MTIME, not by
    reasoning: ~/.codex/history.jsonl was written at 08:37:48 today and three session
    rollout files under ~/.codex/sessions were written after 08:15 — during these masked
    sessions. Those are precisely the writes that would have been EROFS had ForgeOs's
    forge.sh been ported without the lib fix first.

So the ~/.codex write grant is FOR THE RUNTIME, NOT FOR THE SEAT. The Forge is denied at
policy and permitted at kernel; only the attended Mayor and Warden are permitted at both,
which is exactly the asymmetry the Overseer's rider asked to have stated and which the lib
comment now carries.

HONEST LIMIT ON THE ROTATION EVIDENCE: auth.json is unchanged since 2026-08-05, so no real
token rotation fell due during these sessions. Rotation-by-rename is proven by the
deterministic probe (an actual mv inside ~/.codex, through both masks, in all three forts)
and by codex's own writes landing there — not by observing a live token refresh. The next
real refresh is the final confirmation and nobody needs to wait for it to use these forts.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

  [x] forge.sh sources the lib, no inline mask block, no hand-copied RO_PATHS stopgap
      (grep: no ^MASK_FILES= / ^MASK_DIRS= / ^RO_PATHS= / --bind / / / --clearenv remain)
  [x] ONE ~/.codex write-grant mechanism across all three libs (CODEX_DIR_RW)
  [x] a real forge.sh smoke launch in ForgeOs succeeds on a throwaway bead — three of them
  [x] a write to fort/charter.md from inside the Forge's WORKTREE fails
  [x] probe-cycle7 green in all three forts (44/0, 40/0, 40/0)
  [x] n3bk findings 6, 7, 8, 9 addressed or explicitly deferred with reasons

FILED, NOT FIXED HERE, each with its reason on its own bead: the factory lib never got E8
(highest consequence — new forts born with the retired mechanism, and the drift watcher
will call the fix the drift); mask-harness.sh's missing ~/.codex assertions; probe-cycle7
existing only in the capital; the two elder forts' settings.json gaps; the [ -f ] silent
gap's real fix; ForgeOs's lib cycle-7 comment drift.

NOT CLOSED BY ME. This edict is the Regent acting above three constitutions, and covenant
4.5 gives each fort's Warden the right to review it by that fort's own standards. The two
elder forts' changes are committed in their own trees for exactly that reason.

comments.text:
SO7 CORRECTION TO MY OWN RIDER 2 (Emrith, 2026-08-13). The Regent's handoff reports it could not reproduce the mtimes I cited and, correctly, declined to call the premise wrong without establishing what the figure counted. I have now established it: THE FIGURE COUNTED MY SANDBOX. /proc/self/mountinfo in this Mayor session shows /home/justin/.codex is a TMPFS with auth.json as the only path re-bound from real disk; skills/, plugins/ and config.toml as I read them were scratch created inside my own mask. Calder's host figures (2026-08-10 12:29:42 and 2026-07-09 09:20:06) are the true ones. The 08:12:11 correlation was real and inverted in meaning: it is when dispatching the Forge populated MY tmpfs.

RIDER 2'S INSTRUCTION WAS NONETHELESS THE RIGHT ONE, and I want the record to be exact about why: not because I had measured a launch-abort risk, but because leaving an unmeasured surface alone inside a sitting already carrying a lib rewrite, a launcher port and a mechanism unification is the conservative default. The Regent's ~/.claude/teams precedent is the real independent ground. comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Mandatory gate-1 referral, not a block.** This diff changes the kernel mask library (`fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`), a permission profile (`.claude/settings.json`) and a host-executed script in `fort/scripts/` — all three named in human gate 1 — and it moves an auth surface (the Codex credential directory's writability), which my seat file makes a mandatory escalation class. **I have no blocking findings.** The design is sound, the fortkit codex posture is materially unchanged (the old `RW_PATHS` grant and the new direct bind sit at the same point, before the RO pass), the ordering invariant holds by reading, and the capital's half of E8 should stand. Ten findings below, all for beads. Same grammar as my `52vf.1` and `52vf.3` verdicts: keep the commit, route the gate.

**Capability disclosure, per the recipe.** I ran the fort's gate (`CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`, exit 0) and ShellCheck directly. I could **not** execute `build_mask` in any form — `bash -c` is not in this session's allow list — and `/proc/self/mountinfo`, `~/.codex`, `/home/justin/dev/ForgeOs` and `/home/justin/dev/longburn` are all outside my readable roots. **Every mask-behaviour number in the record is therefore taken on faith**, enumerated at the end. This is a static review of the mask plus an executed review of the verifier and the event stream.

**Scope.** The bead's headline deliverable — ForgeOs's `forge.sh` port — is not in this diff and not readable from this seat. Five of the six acceptance criteria are unverifiable here. The Regent deliberately left the elder forts open for their own Wardens under covenant 4.5; that is right, and this verdict certifies the capital's half only. No reader should take it as clearing E8 whole.

---

### Findings

**1. The lib's policy-layer claim is false for this fort's copy. (non-blocking — record)**
The dispatch-exception comment states: "For the CODEX seat the policy layer still covers it: forge.sh's guarded deny table denies `/home/justin/.codex/**`." Measured: `fortkit/fort/scripts/forge.sh` has **no deny table** — read in full, the word `deny` does not appear; it runs `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write` with six `--add-dir` grants and nothing else. The deny table is ForgeOs's (`:80` per the bead). The *conclusion* is correct — `workspace-write`'s writable roots exclude `~/.codex`, and both dispatch-lane seats reported "rejected by the command executor" — but the mechanism named in this copy does not exist in this copy. A shared comment that is true in one fort and false in another is the drift class this whole edict exists to close. Fix: name the enforcing mechanism per copy.

**2. The newly-opened surface's only convenience control is written in the spelling this fort doubts. (non-blocking — threats 1 and 2)**
`.claude/settings.json:112` carries `Edit(//home/justin/.codex/**)`. Until this commit the kernel made that rule moot for claude seats (`~/.codex` was a tmpfs); now the kernel deliberately opens the directory and that rule is the only tool-layer control left over it — in the double-slash form whose efficacy is this fort's own open question (`fortkit-f3y`), and binding `Edit` only, not `Bash` writes. The commit message reasons "relative spellings only" for the rules it added, which is right, and leaves the one rule that newly matters in the doubtful spelling. Non-blocking because the charter is explicit that deny lists are convenience and the kernel is the boundary — but f3y just became load-bearing and should be prioritized.

**3. "Read-only by construction" now has a kernel-level hole at `~/.codex`. (non-blocking)**
The Warden is a claude seat, so `CODEX_DIR_RW=1` applies to her: at the kernel she can now write `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `skills/`, `plugins/` — instruction executed by the *next* Forge launch, outside her mask. The lib comment discloses this ("an attended Mayor or Warden"). Measured mitigation: `fort/profiles/warden-settings.json` denies `Edit(**)` and every write verb (`rm`, `mv`, `cp`, `chmod`, `ln`, all `git` mutators), so the seat stays read-only at the tool layer. But for this one directory the property is now *profile-enforced*, while the charter and the seat file both say "by construction". That belongs in the charter's residuals or the seat file, not only in a lib comment.

**4. The stated cost covers writes and omits the new reads. (non-blocking)**
The Overseer's rider was honoured for the instruction surface. Not stated: for claude seats `~/.codex` was previously invisible (tmpfs) and is now readable in full except `sessions/`, `log/` and `history.jsonl` — including `config.toml`, which in Codex commonly carries MCP server definitions and their environment. Consistent with the standing "reads across `$HOME` stay open" decision (charter, 2026-08-04), which is why this is non-blocking, but the cost paragraph should say it rather than leaving a reader to infer the read side from the write side.

**5. The new standing assertions ship without the interpretation guard the same session invented. (non-blocking)**
The E8 scratch probe asserted the mask sees the *real* `~/.codex` (byte count matching host) before labelling anything, precisely because under a tmpfs a writability probe passes on a broken runtime — the Regent's own words, and their own first draft had two lying labels. `probe-cycle7`'s new `probe ok "~/.codex writable"` carries no such guard; the tmpfs case is caught only indirectly, by the paired `config.toml` deny probe failing. Second half: the property that actually broke in `longburn-1p9` was **rename**, and the standing probe asserts **file creation**. The instrument that asserted rename-with-guard "lives in this session's scratchpad" (Regent handoff §5) and is gone. `fortkit-wtps` is the right home; it should carry the guard and the rename assertion, not just the missing `~/.codex` lines.

**6. Three new masks land with no assertion anywhere, and one has an undocumented consequence. (non-blocking)**
`~/.codex/sessions`, `~/.codex/log` and `~/.codex/history.jsonl` are newly masked for claude seats. `probe-cycle7` asserts only config.toml-RO and directory-writable; `scripts/mask-harness.sh` has no `~/.codex` string at all (confirmed by grep — which independently corroborates the record's "61/0 on a lib that would have stopped Proofdelve's mill"). Worth recording with it: a Forge **dispatched** from a Mayor inherits those masks recursively, so its session rollouts and history land in the Mayor's tmpfs and are lost. No regression (the old full tmpfs lost them too) and no launch failure (measured: `fortkit-m0wm` ran to exit 0), but it is nowhere written down and would cost a debugging session.

**7. `--mask-file` silently ignores a directory. (non-blocking)**
The bind site is `[ -e ] && [ ! -d ]`, correctly, so a caller passing a directory gets no mask and no output — the same silent-gap class this very commit discloses at length for the secret sweep two hundred lines above. One sentence in the parameter's doc block closes the asymmetry.

**8. A charter line-number citation is now stale. (non-blocking — record)**
`fort/charter.md` cites `probe-cycle7.sh` "line 74" for the inverted Shape-B assertion. Measured: old `:74` and new `:80` are both `probe deny "scripts/verify.sh SHIM RO (Shape B)"` — the citation now lands on a comment. The charter's 35/0 figure is a dated measurement and remains true as one. Cite the probe's label, not its line; labels do not drift.

**9. Five of six acceptance criteria are outside this seat's reach. (non-blocking — scope)**
Stated above; repeated here so it is in the numbered record. The ForgeOs port, the two elder libs, the ForgeOs smoke launches and the elder forts' probe totals are unreviewed by me.

**10. Rider 3 was satisfied in substance, by a different act than it names. (non-blocking)**
The Overseer asked to "relaunch a Mayor in each fort and dispatch". What was executed was a *reconstructed* Mayor mask (`build_mask claude`, `mask_env claude`, `FORT_MASKED=1`) with `forge.sh` run inside it. That is equivalent for the property at issue — masks bind at launch, and a namespace rebuilt from the new lib is the stricter test — and the record says "mask", not "session", so nothing is misstated. Independent corroboration that a real claude-seat launch survives the new lib: this session and my two predecessors today (09:14, 09:22) were all launched by `warden.sh` off the merged lib.

**Credit where the record earns it:** the sitting caught a false premise supplied by the seat that briefed it, reported it without overclaiming it wrong, disclosed a probe whose first draft lied, and treated a smoke failure (SSH_AUTH_SOCK) as nine unmeasured assertions rather than a cosmetic. The `settings.json` collapse also closes a real gap — the six enumerated rules omitted `verify.sh` and `probe-cycle7.sh`, and the kernel has covered the whole directory since cycle 13.

### Verified independently (executed by me, in cwd)

- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0**: memory-lint, skills-install (SKIPPED — cwd is not a git checkout), `tsc`, browser `tsc`, Biome 63 files, Vitest **14 files / 163 tests**, ShellCheck.

(A byte-exact hash comparison of cwd against the commit was refused by my profile; the cwd copies read as consistent with the committed hunks.)
- Event stream: `edict.begun` 08:15:35 and `edict.ended` 09:13:06 bracket the 08:51:27 commit — the charter's "an edict is never silent" is satisfied.

A launcher-observed verifier pass inside the mask, from the event record rather than from a model's report. It also proves the empty-array `MASK_FILES+=("${mask_files_extra[@]}")` expansion does not abort a `set -euo pipefail` launcher on this host.
- Follow-up beads exist in the export as claimed: `29e9`, `wtps`, `elh9`, `n5ii`, `5aon`, `0qxm`, `n3bk.2`.
- `scripts/mask-harness.sh` carries no `~/.codex` assertion; probe arithmetic 35 + 9 = 44 is consistent; charter line-74 drift confirmed against both revisions.

### Taken on faith (could not execute)

- Every mask-behaviour number: `probe-cycle7` 44/0, 40/0, 40/0; `mask-harness` 61/0 ×3 and the 44/17 positive control that closes `fortkit-qbq2`; the E8 codex probe 4/9 → 9/9; nested dispatch 3/3 ×3; dotnet 9/0. `probe-cycle7` is host-side by design, my checkout is read-only inside my mask, and it writes canaries into `~/.codex` and `~/.claude` — this seat will not run it.

title: E2b: clear the kernel-RO decks — Shape B reversal, the launch-aborting glob, the city/ fallback, inert Write rules, the skills symlink, and six record/probe gaps
description:
E2b: REVERSE SHAPE A TO SHAPE B. Overseer-approved 2026-08-12, TYPED VERBATIM: "ok I like your
recommendatiosn I approve all" — answering a message whose recommendations were (1) fix the
city/ fallback, (2) reconsider Shape A in favour of Shape B, (3) the small queued fixes.

WHY THE REVERSAL. Shape A was approved on two premises, and the measurements killed both:
  - "the hole is bounded to the MAYOR, an attended seat that asks first" — FALSE. Every
    build_mask claude caller not passing its checkout as extra_ro holds it: mayor.sh:40,
    civ/scripts/herald.sh:97, civ/scripts/chronicler.sh:95. THE HERALD RUNS UNATTENDED on a
    daily 05:00 timer with Bash, Write and Edit (fortkit-vkq8).
  - "the hole only lets a seat ADD files; nothing there is auto-executed" — FALSE. The
    Overseer's own harness run measured 'A4b fort/scripts DIR not renamable :: unlink=NO
    rename=YES'. With the directory unlocked, a seat can rename it aside and put its own
    fort/scripts in its place; ~/.local/bin/mayor:7 then execs that path ON THE HOST,
    UNMASKED. The per-file mounts protect the FILES and not the LOCATION (fortkit-x9ou).

WHAT SHAPE B IS. fort/scripts goes back to a whole-directory --ro-bind, which makes it a MOUNT
POINT again — so rename is refused and there is no new-file hole at all. The mutable verifier
moves out of the locked directory: fort/scripts/verify.sh becomes a thin read-only SHIM that
execs an implementation living where mutability is already sanctioned.

=== THE WRINKLE, FOUND WHILE SPECCING AND NOT PRESENT IN MY EARLIER DESCRIPTION ===

The obvious home for the implementation is repo scripts/. That would make it writable TO THE
FORGE, because the Forge's posture leaves $root read-write apart from the carve-outs, and repo
scripts/ is in none of them. Cycle 7's stated intent is the opposite: "verify.sh alone
re-granted to the Mayor as the session-run tool the fort evolves (verifier changes are Mayor
work: the Forge's and the Warden's masks keep it read-only)."

So Shape B is NOT complete as I first described it. It needs an explicit read-only carve-out for
the implementation path in the codex posture. The Warden needs nothing extra — she already
passes her whole checkout as extra_ro, so the implementation is read-only to her for free.

CONCRETELY:
  1. fort/scripts/ -> whole-directory --ro-bind again. Remove the per-file enumeration and the
     verify.sh unbinding that Shape A introduced.
  2. fort/scripts/verify.sh becomes a shim, tracked, read-only like its siblings, that execs
     the implementation and forwards "$@" and the exit status.
  3. The implementation lands at a decided path (recommend scripts/verify-impl.sh, beside
     memory-lint.mjs and consolidate-memory.mjs, which are already the fort's own tool set).
  4. ADD that path to RO_PATHS in the CODEX posture, so the Forge cannot edit the verifier. This
     is the step my original Shape B description missed.
  5. Confirm the Mayor CAN still edit it: Edit, sed -i and a git checkout that replaces it.
  6. Update every reference to fort/scripts/verify.sh that describes it as the thing you edit.
     It remains the ENTRY POINT and the authoritative verifier, so most references stay true;
     the charter's cycle-7 paragraph and the accepted-residual bullet both need rewriting,
     because the residual disappears entirely under Shape B.

=== TWO MORE FIXES RIDE THE SAME SITTING, SAME FILE ===

fortkit-faka finding 5 — SECRET_GLOBS grew to six patterns for 2kub, two of which (*env*~ and
#*env*#) match names NOT starting with a dot. The filter is [ -e "$f" ] at :99, so a DIRECTORY
named e.g. environments~ gets added to MASK_FILES and --ro-bind /dev/null <dir> ABORTS BWRAP.
Failure mode: NO SEAT LAUNCHES. Measured: no such path exists in any fort today, so it is
latent. Fix: [ -f "$f" ] at :99, and consider :330 for belt. One character class.

fortkit-vkq8's other half — seat-sandbox.sh:240-242 still says "ITS BLAST RADIUS IS THE MAYOR
ALONE". The charter was corrected 2026-08-12 and the lib was not, so the two records DISAGREE
and the charter is the correct one. Under Shape B this comment should describe the new
arrangement rather than be patched, since the residual it describes ceases to exist.

=== WHAT THIS BEAD RESOLVES ON LANDING ===
  fortkit-6ovg   the carve-out finally works AND without the residual
  fortkit-x9ou   the rename exposure closes: a mount point refuses rename
  fortkit-vkq8   the lib half of the false-bound record
  fortkit-faka   finding 5, the launch-aborting glob
The charter's accepted-residual bullet should be REMOVED, not amended, and its removal recorded
as an amendment with the measurement that justified it. NOT resolved: fortkit-w6mb (the city/
fallback), which is independent of the mask and lives outside every fort.

=== VERIFICATION — reuse what already exists rather than inventing it ===
  1. scripts/mask-harness.sh, unmasked, against the candidate lib BEFORE installing. Under
     Shape B, A6 ("DISCLOSED HOLE: new file in fort/scripts") MUST FLIP TO A FAILURE, because
     the hole it asserts is gone — so that assertion has to be rewritten to assert_no_newfile
     as part of this change, and A4b (added and reverted 2026-08-12) should be re-added
     PROPERLY, with a restore that announces a failed restore loudly. See the correction on
     fortkit-x9ou for why the naive version poisoned a whole run.
  2. Re-run the positive control against the pre-E2 lib and confirm it still scores 34/18, so
     the harness's discriminating power is re-established rather than assumed.
  3. probe-cycle7.sh per fort. Its line 74 probe ok "fort/scripts new-file: DISCLOSED 6ovg
     RESIDUAL" MUST BE INVERTED to probe deny, and its comment rewritten.
  4. Then a real seat per fort: launch, and confirm it starts AND can work. A mask that passes
     every probe and prevents a launch has still failed.
  5. Mayor posture: prove Edit, sed -i and git checkout all still change verify.sh.
  6. Forge posture: prove the implementation path is NOT writable (step 4 of the change).

ROLLBACK, decided before editing: E2's four installed libs are in commit b2881b7 and recoverable
per fort in one command. Know that command before starting.

LANE: fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh x3 forts + template, fort/scripts/verify.sh x3 + template,
probe-cycle7.sh, and the charter. All kernel-RO except the charter. PROBED 2026-08-12: this Mayor
cannot write fort/scripts/lib/ (EROFS). Regent, and expect the same hand-install round trips E2
needed.

SCOPE EXPANDED TO A SINGLE EDICT on the Overseer's instruction 2026-08-12: "can we just wrap
everything that you can't do into a single edict so that regent can just take care of it?"

Yes for one BEAD, and the bundle below is drawn deliberately rather than by sweeping everything
open. TWO CONSTRAINTS SHAPE IT:

  1. ONE BEAD PER SITTING IS A MECHANICAL LIMIT, not a preference. bin/regent's --edict takes a
     scalar (edict_target="$2", :71), so a session can only announce ONE bead id in
     edict.begun/edict.ended, and fortkit-jd3g records that a multi-edict session announces only
     the first. Two --edict flags would put a false record in three streams. So: one bead,
     many items — which is exactly what the Overseer asked for.
  2. NOT EVERYTHING OPEN BELONGS IN IT. The programme's sittings are separated by FAILURE MODE,
     not by convenience, and bundling changes whose failure modes differ in kind is how one
     mistake contaminates another. Exclusions and their reasons are at the bottom, and they are
     part of this brief rather than an omission from it.

=== INCLUDED: EVERYTHING THE MAYOR CANNOT WRITE THAT IS ALREADY DECIDED ===

A. THE CORE — Shape B reversal. Full spec in this bead's description above. fort/scripts goes
   back to a whole-directory bind (a mount point, so rename is refused), the mutable verifier
   moves out, and the moved implementation MUST get a read-only carve-out in the CODEX posture
   or the Forge can edit the verifier — the wrinkle absent from my first description.
   Resolves: fortkit-6ovg, fortkit-x9ou, and the lib half of fortkit-vkq8.
   The charter's accepted-residual bullet is REMOVED, not amended: under Shape B it ceases to
   exist. That is a charter amendment and needs its own charter.amended event.

B. fortkit-faka finding 5 — the [ -f ] one-character fix. SECRET_GLOBS grew to six patterns,
   two matching names that do not start with a dot, and the filter at :99 is [ -e "$f" ], so a
   DIRECTORY named e.g. environments~ makes --ro-bind /dev/null abort bwrap. Failure mode: NO
   SEAT LAUNCHES. Latent today (measured: no such path in any fort). Same file as A.

C. fortkit-faka findings 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 — the .beads hooks carve-out missing from 1q9's per-tree
   iteration (she called it the highest-consequence carve-out), bin/fort-init's stranded
   registry write undisclosed, the factory shipping the $root-worktrees argument with none of
   its rationale, probe-cycle7's two mutating probes cleaned up outside the trap, and the
   known_hosts behaviour change worth recording. Same file family as A.

D. fortkit-w6mb — the city/ fallback. ~/.local/bin/mayor line 6 and ~/.local/bin/fortstat line
   5 prefer $root/city/scripts/... over fort/. CONFIRMED DEAD CODE: ls -d /home/justin/dev/*/city
   returns nothing. A seat can create that path and be preferred at the next invocation, running
   unmasked. Zero coupling to the mask; included because it is the one live escalation and it is
   outside every fort's write set. NOTE: ~/.local/bin may also be denied to the REGENT's tool
   layer, as fort/scripts and civ/scripts are — try it, and if denied it is the Overseer's hand.

E. fortkit-yowr — every fort's .claude/settings.json carries ~20 Write(...) rules the CLI itself
   reports as INERT ("only Edit(path) rules are matched by file permission checks"). I saw the
   engine print exactly that today while probing an unrelated flag. Purely a correction of
   ineffective rules to effective ones; .claude/ is kernel-RO.

F. fortkit-4n8c — symlink the installed skills to the repo copies, as ~/.local/bin/regent
   already is. This RESTORES A LANE E2 BROKE: 5sk made ~/.claude/skills kernel-RO and nothing
   automates the install, so a change to fortkit/skills/*/SKILL.md currently does not reach the
   loaded copy at all. Check whether a symlinked path inherits the target's mask rather than
   assuming it.

G. fortkit-ddvo — verify.sh does not shellcheck templates/fort/scripts/lib/*.sh, so the
   factory's mask builder is unlinted. Included because A is restructuring verify.sh anyway.

=== EXCLUDED, AND WHY — this half is the brief too ===

E3's scope (fortkit-t9iw, rvly, ph4g, j8ww, w1ew, iqp, ebm, bfsu, se6, vn8, wi0): launcher
BEHAVIOUR and provenance. t9iw changes how every launcher terminates (mayor.sh execs, so its
EXIT trap has never fired and no Mayor session has ever emitted session.end). Bundling "how
launchers exit" with "what the mask binds" means a single bad sitting can leave the fort unable
to launch AND unable to record that it failed.

E5 (fortkit-px7e / or2.9.4): the in-mask launch refusal. It has a RECORDED SCAR — it once
refused Farlantern's own masked Mayor mid-mill — so it lands when no seat is working, which is
a different scheduling constraint from everything above. fortkit-1q9's remaining half depends
on it.

E4 (warden.sh reliability) and E6 (fort/profiles/): separate files, separate risk, and E6's
fortkit-hn2 needs two consecutive Warden sessions to prove its shape before the factory copy
can follow.

fortkit-6jf: ForgeOs's forge.sh never calls build_mask, so NONE of E2 or E2b reaches
Proofdelve's Forge. That is a real hole and it is a substantial launcher refactor, in_progress,
deserving its own sitting. IT SHOULD BE THE NEXT ONE AFTER THIS, because every mask edit widens
the gap.

=== PRACTICAL WARNINGS FOR THE SITTING ===

THIS IS LONGER THAN E2, WHICH TOOK 2h14m FOR FOUR DEFECTS IN ONE FILE. This is four file
families across three forts plus two host wrappers plus three .claude/settings.json. COMMIT
INCREMENTALLY, one coherent group at a time, so a failure late in the sitting does not lose the
work before it. Suggested order: D (isolated, zero risk) -> E, F, G (independent) -> B -> C -> A
last, because A is the one that can stop every seat launching and should be the freshest thing
in the record if a rollback is needed.

EXPECT HAND-INSTALLS. fort/scripts, bin/ and civ/scripts are denied to the Regent's own tool
layer (recorded by the E7 and E2 Regents), so the Overseer installs those files. Get each one
biome/shellcheck clean BEFORE asking: shellcheck -x <file>, and
npx biome check --config-path=/home/justin/dev/fortkit <file> for JSON.

ASSERTIONS THAT MUST INVERT WITH A, or they fail for the right reason and look like a
regression: scripts/mask-harness.sh's A6 currently asserts the new-file hole is OPEN, and
probe-cycle7.sh:74 probes it as an EXPECTED PASS. Both become assert_no_newfile / probe deny.
Re-add A4b PROPERLY with a restore that announces a failed restore loudly — read the correction
on fortkit-x9ou for why the naive version poisoned a whole run.
