Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES

Work by the Regent, Calder Sealbroken, on **opus**, unmasked, Overseer present throughout (`edict.begun` payload `model:opus, model_source: launcher --model flag`). Frontier model, human present, and the records are among the best this fort has produced. Scrutiny weighted for blast radius rather than for model risk: this is the enforcement layer of three settlements plus the factory every future settlement is founded from.

The design is right. Shape B is the correct reversal, the wrinkle the Overseer found while speccing is closed, the harness was inverted before the lib was touched, and the destructive probe now aborts the run rather than poisoning it. I would merge it today but for two things the diff itself introduces.

---

### BLOCKING

**1. The new `skills-install` step breaks the verifier in every checkout that is not `/home/justin/dev/fortkit`. (blocking — measured)**

`CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in my cwd:

```
skills-install: /home/justin/.claude/skills/civ -> /home/justin/dev/fortkit/skills/civ, expected /tmp/warden-52vf.9/skills/civ
skills-install: /home/justin/.claude/skills/fort-backport -> /home/justin/dev/fortkit/skills/fort-backport, expected /tmp/warden-52vf.9/skills/fort-backport
VERIFIER-EXIT-NONZERO
```

`scripts/verify-impl.sh:98` compares `readlink -f "$dst"` against `readlink -f "$src"`, and `$src` is resolved against the *current* `repo_root`. The installed symlink can only ever point at one checkout, so the comparison is false for every other one. It is step 2 of 7, so `typecheck`, `browser-typecheck`, `lint`, `test` and `shellcheck` never run — the verifier reports failure having verified almost nothing.

The lane this breaks is the Forge's: `fort/scripts/forge.sh:149` runs `(cd "$wt" && ./fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit)` in the worktree. Every future Forge bead now gets a red launcher-observed verifier, and standing order 9 ("no bead closes without verifiers green") cannot be satisfied from a worktree. It also broke this review — I could not reproduce the fort's own gate as spelled in my launch recipe, and had to fall back to the two allow-listed direct legs.

This is a false red, not a false green, which is the better failure of the two. It is still a broken verifier, which the blocking bar names explicitly, and it is new in commit `29d1539` rather than pre-existing.

Fix suggestions, cheapest first: resolve the canonical checkout (`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, then its parent) and compare against that; or compare the symlink target's *basename path* (`.../skills/<name>`) plus a same-repo check; or — most in keeping with the step's own "skipping is announced, never silent" rule — announce a skip when the resolved install target is a different checkout of this repository. Note this needs no Regent sitting: `scripts/verify-impl.sh` is Mayor-writable, which is a property Shape B itself created.

**2. Item A step 6 — the reference sweep — is not done, and the bead's closing comment claims it is. (blocking in part)**

The spec's step 6 is "Update every reference to `fort/scripts/verify.sh` that describes it as the thing you edit." The closing comment says "WHAT IS NOT DONE: nothing in the bundle. Items A-G all landed." Four records still describe the retired arrangement, two of them delivered to seats at session start:

- `fort/memory/facts/cycle7-write-boundaries.md` — `tier: core`, `scope.seats: [all]`, `status: active`: "host-executed scripts (`fort/scripts/` **except Mayor-writable verify.sh**, …)". This is in the shared floor the verifier itself reports as `core shared floor [all]: 2 facts / 33 lines`; every seat is told this at every session start. It was true at `e3fc96a` and this merge makes it false.
- `fort/seats/mayor.md:17` — "Verifier changes are also your seat's work: `verify.sh` is writable to the Mayor alone." The Mayor will act on this and hit EROFS, which is exactly the multi-cycle failure this programme exists to end. The same line also predates the charter's new sentence putting `skills/` under the prose gate, and does not mention it.
- `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:126` (+ the template twin at the same line) — "verify.sh alone is re-granted writable below." Inside the mask builder, describing a re-grant that no longer exists anywhere in the file. This is `fortkit-vkq8`'s defect class — the lib disagreeing with the charter — reappearing one line above the code that fixed it.
- `fort/scripts/warden.sh:143` (+ template twin at :145) — "the verify.sh Mayor re-grant is re-masked here."

**What I am actually holding the merge for is the first two only.** Both are Mayor-reachable — `fort/memory/**` rides `Edit(fort/**)`, and `fort/seats/` is prose-gated for attended seats — so this needs no Regent sitting and no Overseer hand. The two comment sites in kernel-RO files should become a bead for the next sitting; `fortkit-6jf` is already queued next and opens the same file family. I will not hold a merge hostage to a lane the fort cannot reach.

---

### NON-BLOCKING (file as beads; none of these should delay the merge)

**3. Item E did not reach the factory, and it will make the drift watcher lie daily.** `templates/config/settings-permissions.json` still ships 13 inert `Write()` rules (2 allow, 11 deny), and `bin/fort-init:151` renders it verbatim — so the next fort founded gets `fortkit-yowr` back in full. Worse, `civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:361-374` files a finding classified **`regression`** for every template permission absent from a fort. 13 rules × 3 forts ≈ 39 false regressions at the next 06:31 scan, each one advising the fort to restore a rule the CLI reports as inert. The watcher's own code carries the reason this matters: "Filing an unfixable bead every run trains a fort to ignore its watcher."

**4. `templates/scripts/verify-impl.sh` is not on the shellcheck surface.** The new glob list is `templates/fort/scripts/*.sh templates/fort/scripts/lib/*.sh … scripts/*.sh` — `templates/scripts/` matches none of them. That is `fortkit-ddvo` verbatim ("the one copy of the mask builder the verifier never checked is the one every future fort is founded on"), recreated in the same commit that fixed it, for the file that *is* every future fort's verifier. I ran `shellcheck -x templates/scripts/verify-impl.sh` by hand: clean today. Nothing is broken; the surface is simply unguarded.

**5. The charter's "Shape B does not have one" is broader than what was measured.** `scripts/verify-impl.sh` is host-executed and writable to every `build_mask claude` caller that does not pass its own checkout as `extra_ro` — `mayor.sh:40` (sanctioned, cycle 7), and also `civ/scripts/herald.sh:97` and `civ/scripts/chronicler.sh:95`. **The Herald runs headless and unattended on a daily 05:00 timer with Bash, Write and Edit.** So an unattended seat can rewrite the verifier that gates the fort, and it runs unmasked at the next `verify.sh`. This is unchanged in kind from Shape A and strictly better in degree — but the residual bullet that *named the Herald* was removed, and nothing replaced it, so the fort's disclosure of this capability went from explicit to absent. Measured against the charter's own principle in the same paragraph — "write access follows execution context" — and threat 1. Recommend either a one-bullet residual with a measurement per SO11, or a decision on whether the Herald should hold it (the open half of `fortkit-vkq8`).

**6. The `[ -f ]` fix trades a loud abort for a silent gap in one case.** A *directory* matching a secret glob (`.env.d/`, `environments~/`) is now skipped at the sweep (`:109`) and again at the bind site (`:376`, `[ -e ] && [ ! -d ]`), so its contents are readable inside the mask instead of aborting the launch. The reasoning for keeping `[ -e ]` at the bind site (sockets, and the docker socket being a host escape rather than a secret) is exactly right and I would not change it. The complete fix is to route matching directories into `MASK_DIRS` (`--tmpfs`) rather than dropping them, which keeps both properties. Threat 4. Latent by the same measurement as the defect it fixes: no such path in any fort today.

**7. `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh` silently lost its executable bit** (`mode change 100755 => 100644`), unmentioned in the commit message, while the template kept `100755` — so the copies now disagree in a dimension no content diff will show. No functional effect: the lib is sourced, never executed. The likely cause is systemic and worth the bead: `civ/remember.md` now records `python3 <patcher> "$f" "$f.tmp" && mv` as *the* install lane for kernel-RO paths, and that lane creates a fresh file at the umask. It will drop the mode again on the next kernel-RO install; `install -m` or an explicit `chmod --reference` closes it.

**8. Two convenience-layer follow-ons in the file item E was already editing.** `.claude/settings.json` has no `Edit(fort/scripts/verify.sh)` deny, so the tool layer still invites an edit the kernel now refuses (loud-and-early beats EROFS-on-a-temp-path, which is the whole lesson of `6ovg`); and `scripts/` is in no allow rule, so the Mayor's now-sanctioned verifier edits fall outside `Edit(fort/**)`. Neither is a boundary — the kernel mask is.

**9. `probe-cycle7.sh` does not probe `$root/scripts/verify-impl.sh` under the codex posture** — only the declared-worktree copy at `:181`, and only when a worktree exists. The harness covers it (C4c), so the property is measured; the live-fort probe just does not carry it.

---

### What I verified independently

- **Ran in cwd:** `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json` — clean. `npx vitest run` — **163 passed / 163**, 14 files, matching the Regent's count. `shellcheck -x` over the verifier's exact declared surface — clean. `shellcheck -x templates/scripts/verify-impl.sh` — clean.
- **`CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — RED**, at `skills-install`, twice, with the output quoted in finding 1. Steps 3-7 did not execute.
- **Item E, by set comparison of the before/after `permissions.deny` and `.allow` arrays:** every removed `Write(x)` has an exact `Edit(x)` twin, the sole exception `Write(fort/events/*.jsonl)` gained `Edit(fort/events/*.jsonl)`, and zero `Write()` rules remain in either list. The commit's claim of an unchanged effective rule set holds for this fort.
- **The factory gap and the drift consequence:** read `templates/config/settings-permissions.json` (13 `Write()` rules), `bin/fort-init:151` (renders it), `civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:357-374` (files `regression` per absent template rule).
- **The symlinks are real:** the verifier's own output shows `~/.claude/skills/{civ,fort-backport}` resolving into `/home/justin/dev/fortkit/skills/`.
- **The unattended holders:** `herald.sh:97` is `build_mask claude "$root"` with no `extra_ro`; `chronicler.sh:95` passes only the *other* forts.
- **No new launch-abort risk from the added `RO_PATHS`:** `:325` and `:326` guard with `[ -e ]`, the `MASK_FILES` and `MASK_DIRS` loops are `&&`-lists in non-final position (set -e exempt), and `build_mask` ends in an explicit `return 0` (the ForgeOs-vzn class fix). The added `$t/skills` and `$t/scripts/verify-impl.sh` cannot abort a launch in a fort that lacks them.
- **The harness arithmetic:** 57 top-level `assert_*` calls plus the inline `ok`/`bad` pairs ≈ 61, and the six named Shape A failures (A2b, A4b, A6, C4c/C4e, C4d) are each independently derivable from the Shape A code. 44+17 = 61 for the pre-E2 lib on the new set, which correctly supersedes the bead's stale 34/18 expectation from the 52-assertion set.
- **`assert_dir_immovable`** restores, verifies the restore, and `exit 3`s with a banner if the restore failed — the correction `fortkit-x9ou` asked for, done properly.
- **The stale-reference sites** in finding 2, each read in the file.
- **The records:** `edict.begun` (22:19:44), the `charter.amended` at 22:45:25, the two `session.start` corrections appended as `incident` per SO7, and `edict.ended` (22:55:19, present in the live stream just past this range's HEAD).

### What I took on faith (could not execute)

- **`scripts/mask-harness.sh`: 61/0 Shape B, 55/6 Shape A, 44/17 pre-E2.** My profile refused to run the harness (`bash scripts/mask-harness.sh …` → permission denied), so the central measurement of this bead — including the `A4b RENAME SUCCEEDED` result the charter amendment rests on — is unexecuted by me. My static reading of the assertion set is consistent with every number claimed, and the inverted-before-the-code-changed ordering is visible in the diff, but consistency is not reproduction.
- **`fort/scripts/probe-cycle7.sh` 35/0 on the live capital** — needs bwrap against live paths and mutates `~/.claude/teams`; not run.
- **The three real Mayor launches**, the `/proc/2705474/mountinfo` single-`ro`-mount evidence, and the "0 inert-rule warnings (37/42/31 before)" acceptance test.
- **Item D** (`~/.local/bin/{mayor,fortstat}`, the `city/` fallback) — outside every repository, in no commit, and not in this diff. Unverifiable from here; it is recorded on `fortkit-w6mb` and belongs to that bead's review.
- **The ForgeOs and longburn commits**, including the four `RO_PATHS` entries added inline to `forge.sh` as a disclosed stopgap — different repositories, outside my range. That deviation is disclosed and correctly reasoned, and `fortkit-6jf` being next is the right call.

Both deviations the Regent disclosed (`bin/fort-init` + `templates/scripts/verify-impl.sh` outside the lane; the ForgeOs `forge.sh` stopgap) were necessary, are the right calls, and were caught by the founding smoke test rather than by review — which is the outcome the fort wants.

VERDICT-LINE: REQUEST-CHANGES: new skills-install step reds the verifier in every non-canonical checkout (breaks the Forge lane); item-6 sweep left two seat-facing records false. Shape B itself is sound; 7 non-blocking findings.

description:

fortkit-52vf.3 must NOT close until this is corrected: the charter's brand-new accepted
residual states a bound that is FALSE, and the residual bullet is the one place a future

THE CLAIM, fort/charter.md:29 and repeated in fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:240-242
("ITS BLAST RADIUS IS THE MAYOR ALONE"):
  "Bounded to the MAYOR: the Warden and the Researcher pass their whole checkout read-only,
   and the Forge keeps the whole-directory lock."

CONFIRMED FALSE BY ME, from the code, independently of her review. Every build_mask caller
and whether it passes its own checkout as extra_ro:

  fort/scripts/mayor.sh:40        build_mask claude "$REPO"                        NO  -> hole (intended)

  civ/scripts/chronicler.sh:95    build_mask claude "$root" "${other_forts[@]}"    NO  -> HOLE

  fort/scripts/researcher.sh:49   build_mask claude "$root" ... "$root" ...        yes -> no hole

$root resolves to the fortkit repo (civ/scripts/../.., herald.sh:39), so this is the capital's
own host-executed script directory.

WHY THE HERALD MAKES THIS MATERIALLY WORSE THAN THE APPROVED TRADE. The Overseer approved
Shape A on the understanding that the hole sits with an ATTENDED, prose-gated seat that asks
before it acts. The Herald runs HEADLESS AND UNATTENDED on a daily systemd timer at 05:00,

host-executed directory is a different risk from an attended one, and the Chronicler's own
prompt tells it "you have almost no write surface" — which is now untrue.

Threat 1 (agent accident) primarily; threat 2 secondarily, because the Herald's input is

title: [bug] Every fort's .claude/settings.json carries ~20 Write(...) permission rules the CLI reports as INERT — 'only Edit(path) rules are matched by file permission checks'
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 during E2's Mayor-launch verification, in ALL THREE FORTS. Every real mayor.sh launch prints a block of warnings before the session starts, one per rule, of the form:

  Permission deny rule (.claude/settings.json): Write(.claude/**) is not matched by file permission checks — only Edit(path) rules are. Use Edit(.claude/**) instead (Edit rules cover all file-editing tools).

fortkit alone emits ~20 such lines, covering .env*, .claude/**, .git/config, .git/hooks/**, bin/**, civ/scripts/**, civ/profiles/**, fort/profiles/**, the global ~/.claude files, ~/.codex/**, and the worktree copies. ForgeOs and longburn emit their own equivalents. The ALLOW rules are affected too: Write(docs/**) and Write(fort/**) are equally inert.

WHY THIS MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT A CRISIS. The kernel mask is the boundary and the deny lists are convenience — that is this civilization's stated design, and every path above that matters is kernel-RO after E2. So nothing is newly exposed. What IS wrong is that a reader of settings.json sees protections that are not in force, and a rule that silently does nothing is worse than no rule: it is the exact 'a checker that checks nothing must never report success' class the civ layer paid for on 2026-08-05.

THE FIX IS MECHANICAL AND THE CLI STATES IT: Edit(path) rules cover all file-editing tools, so each Write(x) becomes Edit(x). Not done in E2 because .claude/settings.json is a gate-1 constitution file in every fort, this sitting already carried four mask defects, and the change deserves its own measurement (relaunch each seat and confirm the warning block is GONE — that is the acceptance test, and it is cheap).

Suspected age: these rules predate the harness's rule-matching change; nobody read the launch preamble because it scrolls past before an interactive session starts. It took a headless launch that dumped stdout to a file to see them.
design: ACCEPTANCE TEST: launch each fort's mayor.sh with stdout redirected to a file and assert ZERO lines matching 'is not matched by file permission checks'. That is the whole verification and it needs no model. Evidence for this bead: /tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/e2-cand/launch/{fortkit,ForgeOs,longburn}-mayor.log, captured 2026-08-12T15:1x.

title: [bug] mayor.sh exec's bwrap and so never emits session.end — every Mayor session in all three forts opens a session it never closes
description:
FOUND BY THE REGENT during fortkit-52vf.1 (E1) verification, 2026-08-12, and MEASURED rather than reasoned: the three Mayor launches used to prove the repointed prompt reaches the running process each wrote a session.start into their fort's stream and NO session.end.

fortkit  events-2026-08-12.jsonl 10:47:21 session.start emrith/mayor — no pair
ForgeOs  events-2026-08-12.jsonl 10:48:12 session.start marrek/mayor — no pair
longburn events-2026-08-12.jsonl 10:49:00 session.start vardis/mayor — no pair

MECHANISM, and it is a recorded scar reappearing in a different file.
fort/scripts/mayor.sh:6 sets an EXIT trap that emits session.end. Line 44 is
'exec bwrap ...'. exec REPLACES the shell process, so the EXIT trap is
discarded and can never fire. This is character-for-character the defect
fortkit-nvk found in bin/regent ('exec at the end of a launcher silently
discards the EXIT trap', civ memory 2026-08-04), which cost the Regent every
edict.ended it should have emitted for two days. All three forts' mayor.sh
carry the same shape.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. session.start/session.end pairs are how any
reader of a stream reconstructs who was working when. Unpaired starts make
every Mayor session look either still-running or crashed, and 778 session.start
against 722 session.end across the civilization is not a discrepancy anybody
can currently attribute.

CORRECTS A PREMISE IN THE PROGRAMME. fortkit-52vf.4 (E3) records, for the model
pin, that 'mayor.sh:6 ALREADY carries an EXIT trap emitting session.end, so the
stamp rides existing machinery and no wrapper needs building (ph4g Decision D)'.
That machinery does not run. Any E3 work that plans to ride it must fix the exec
first or build the wrapper after all. Noted on fortkit-ph4g too.

FIX SHAPE (the one bin/regent already uses): run the child and propagate its
status instead of exec-ing it, so the trap fires. Kernel-RO to every masked
seat in all three forts, so this is Regent or Overseer work; the natural home is
E3, which already opens all three mayor.sh files.
acceptance_criteria: mayor.sh in all three forts emits exactly one session.end per session.start, measured from a real launch in each fort's stream

title: E7: the drift watcher — one pass over civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs (zvz2 identity key, or2.8 classification, pp1k json envelope, bpuv error reporting). LANDS FIRST, before E1
description:
EDICT 7 OF SEVEN (parent fortkit-52vf), added 2026-08-12 on the Overseer's instruction to
"move forward on a real fix for the drift watcher". SHOULD LAND FIRST, BEFORE E1 — see
sequencing at the end, which is the non-obvious part.

ONE FILE, FOUR DEFECTS: civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs. Kernel-RO to every masked seat,
probed this session (touch civ/scripts/.probe-emrith -> Read-only file system), so the
Regent or the Overseer's hand. Same "one file, one sitting" logic as E2 and E4: four
separate passes over the watcher is the avoidable risk.

  fortkit-zvz2  P1  the dedupe KEY is content-derived (see below — read the SO7 correction
                    on that bead, not its original description, which I got wrong)
  fortkit-or2.8 P2  'never propagated' misclassified as 'regression'; the capital's own
                    deliberate design read as decay. 9 of 38 on the first live run.
  fortkit-pp1k  P2  bd v2.0's --json envelope change will break the array parse at :419
  fortkit-bpuv  P2  every child failure reported as 'already running or flock failed',
                    hiding the real cause

=== THE zvz2 FIX, PRECISELY ===

TODAY, drift-watch.mjs:134:
  fingerprint = sha256(`${fort.name}\0${path}\0${fortHash}\0${templateHash}`)
with fortHash/templateHash = sha256 of the two file CONTENTS (:125-126).

That identifies a (fort, path, exact-content-pair) tuple. It does NOT identify a problem.
Any byte change to either side mints a new identity, so the same drift is re-filed. The
dedupe at :458-465 is working correctly against a key that churns by construction, because
drift IS these files changing.

CHANGE THE IDENTITY TO (fort, path). Keep the content fingerprint, but demote it from
identity to CHANGE-DETECTOR on an existing finding:

  for each finding:
    find an OPEN bead whose identity is (fort, path)
      none                          -> file a new bead, as today
      exists, same fingerprint      -> suppress (unchanged drift; today's correct behaviour)
      exists, different fingerprint -> APPEND a comment to the existing bead carrying the
                                       new fingerprint, the new reason/classification and
                                       the new diff. Do NOT file a second bead.

APPEND RATHER THAN SKIP, and this is the load-bearing half. If it merely skipped on an
identity match, a file that drifts FURTHER after its bead was filed would keep a stale diff
on record and nobody would learn the drift had changed. A changed fingerprint on the same
file is real new information; it belongs on the existing bead. This also satisfies standing
order 7 natively: the record grows, nothing is edited in place.

IDENTITY DERIVATION — a decision the implementer must make deliberately, not by accident.
The bead TITLE is already exactly `Drift: ${fort} ${path}` (:424), so title matching would
work today and is tempting. Prefer an explicit machine-readable identity line in the
description (e.g. `Drift identity: <fort>\0<path>` or a sha of just those two), because
matching on a human-readable title couples the dedupe to title prose that a Mayor may
legitimately reword during triage. The existing `Drift fingerprint:` line proves the
description-line pattern already works and is already parsed (:400-403).

MUST HANDLE, or the fix reintroduces the bug in a new place: the 35 existing distinct
findings were filed WITHOUT an identity line. A dedupe that only reads the new line will
treat all 35 as unseen on its first run and file 35 duplicates — the exact failure this
bead is about, one release later. So the matcher must ALSO fall back to title matching for
pre-existing beads, or a migration pass must add identity lines to the 51 open beads. State
which, and test it.

=== CLEANUP OWED, AND ITS ORDER MATTERS ===

Close the 16 duplicates AFTER the fix lands, never before: a pre-fix run re-files them.
Preserve one bead per distinct fort+path pair (35), keeping whichever carries the more
useful triage history, and close the rest referencing this bead. Do not delete: SO7.

=== SEQUENCING: THIS SHOULD LAND BEFORE E1, AND HERE IS WHY ===

The re-filing is NOT time-driven. A run only re-files where content changed since the last
run; with nothing changing, the dedupe suppresses everything and the run is clean. That is
why pausing the timer was the wrong framing and the Overseer was right to challenge it.

WHAT TRIGGERS IT IS AN EDICT. E1 rewrites ten launcher prompts plus bin/civ-index,
bin/regent and probe-cycle7.sh across three forts. Every one of those files is in the
watcher's compared set. So E1 landing before this fix re-mints the fingerprint of every file
it touches, and the next scheduled run files a fresh duplicate for each. E2 (seat-sandbox x3),
E3, E4 (warden.sh x3), E5 (three launchers x forts) and E6 (profiles x3 + templates) each do
the same for their own files.

THE PROGRAMME IS THE TRIGGER. Running the watcher fix last means every earlier sitting pays
a duplicate tax that then has to be cleaned up by hand. Running it FIRST means the six
sittings that follow each land quietly, with their drift correctly recorded as comments on
existing beads — which is also the most useful possible record of what the programme
changed.

REVISED ORDER FOR THE PROGRAMME: E7, then E1, then E2-E6 as before.

=== VERIFICATION ===

  1. A unit test per branch of the three-way decision. test/drift-watch.test.ts EXISTS and
     is Forge-writable, so the tests need no edict even though the implementation does.
  2. NON-VACUITY, and this is the one that matters: plant a fort+path finding, run twice
     with the file CHANGED between runs, and assert exactly ONE bead exists with a comment
     carrying the second fingerprint. Against today's implementation that assertion must
     FAIL (it would find two beads). Prove the failure, do not reason it — the fort has
     recorded five controls that reported PASS while proving nothing.
  3. A real run against the live tracker in --dryRun first (the flag exists at :455),
     confirming it reports 0 filed and 35 identity matches rather than 51.
design:
IMPLEMENTATION SPEC, Emrith 2026-08-12, written after reading civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs
and test/drift-watch.test.ts in full. This is the authoritative detail for the edict; the
bead description is the why.

=== A FIFTH DEFECT, SAME FAMILY, FOUND WRITING THIS SPEC ===

drift-watch.mjs:374-379 — THE ALLOWLIST HAS THE SAME CONTENT-DERIVED-IDENTITY FLAW:

    const entry = allowlist.find((item) =>
      item.fort === finding.fort &&
      item.path === finding.path &&
      item["content-hash"] === finding.fortHash);

So a deliberate suppression in civ/drift-allowlist.json STOPS SUPPRESSING the moment the
fort's file changes by one byte. Someone allowlists a known, accepted divergence; the file
is then legitimately edited; the allowlist silently lapses and the finding returns. Same
root cause as zvz2 at :134, different consumer, and it fails in the direction that
generates noise rather than hiding it — but a suppression that lapses without saying so is
still a control that stopped working while reporting success.

DECISION REQUIRED, do not just "fix" it: content-hash pinning here may be DELIBERATE, so
that an allowlist entry cannot silently keep suppressing a file that has changed into
something nobody approved. That is a defensible design. If it is the intent, the entry
should carry it explicitly and the lapse should be REPORTED ("allowlist entry for X lapsed:
content-hash no longer matches") rather than silently becoming a fresh finding. Recommend:
keep the pin, add the lapse disclosure. Either way, record the ruling.

=== THE zvz2 CHANGE, CONCRETELY ===

1. ADD AN IDENTITY, SEPARATE FROM THE FINGERPRINT. In makeFinding (:117-137), alongside the
   existing fingerprint, add:
       identity: sha256(`${fort.name}\0${path}`)
   Keep `fingerprint` exactly as it is. Identity answers "which problem is this"; fingerprint
   answers "has it changed since we last looked". Both are needed; today one field is doing
   both jobs and doing the second one only.

2. WRITE THE IDENTITY INTO THE BEAD. In defaultCommands.file (:421-430), add a machine-
   readable line to the description beside the existing fingerprint line:
       Drift identity: <identity>
   Use a line, NOT the title. Title matching would work today (:424 is exactly
   `Drift: ${fort} ${path}`) but it couples dedupe to prose a Mayor may legitimately reword
   during triage. The `Drift fingerprint:` line at :400-403 proves the pattern is already
   parsed successfully.

3. RETURN RICHER STATE FROM existing(). Today (:411-419) it returns a Set of fingerprints.
   It must return a map from identity -> { beadId, fingerprints: Set }. That requires reading
   the bead id alongside the description, which `bd list --all --limit 0 --json` already
   provides. NOTE: this CHANGES THE INJECTABLE COMMANDS INTERFACE, which matters for
   sequencing — see below.

4. THREE-WAY DECISION in run() (:456-466), replacing the two-way filter:
       no bead for this identity            -> commands.file(finding)          (as today)
       bead exists, fingerprint known       -> suppressed.push({by:"fingerprint"})  (as today)
       bead exists, fingerprint UNKNOWN     -> commands.append(beadId, finding)  (NEW)
   and report appended separately from filed, so the emitted event can say so.

5. ADD commands.append. Implement as `bd comment <beadId> --file -` or equivalent, carrying
   the new fingerprint, the new reason, the new suggested classification and the new diff.
   APPEND, NEVER EDIT: standing order 7, and it is the reason this shape is right rather
   than merely convenient — the bead accumulates the history of how a file drifted.

6. EMIT THE NEW COUNTER. defaultCommands.emit (:431-449) reports findingsFiled and
   findingsSuppressed. Add findingsAppended. A run that appends 16 and files 0 must not
   look identical to a run that did nothing — that is exactly the silence that let this
   bug live for a day.

=== THE MIGRATION TRAP, AND IT WILL BITE IF IGNORED ===

The 51 open Drift beads were filed with NO `Drift identity:` line. A matcher that reads
only the new line finds no identity for any of them, concludes all 35 distinct findings are
unseen, and FILES 35 DUPLICATES ON ITS FIRST RUN — reproducing this exact bug one release
later, which is the failure mode this fort keeps repeating.

Two acceptable answers. Pick one, state it in the commit, and TEST it:
  (a) FALLBACK: when no identity line is present, derive identity from the title, which is
      deterministically `Drift: ${fort} ${path}`. Cheapest, no data migration, and it keeps
      working for any bead a Mayor reworded only in the description.
  (b) MIGRATE: a one-time pass adding `Drift identity:` to the 51 open beads.
Recommend (a) plus a comment saying why the fallback exists, since (b) means 51 writes to
records for a mechanical reason.

=== SEQUENCING INSIDE THE SITTING: THE REGENT WRITES BOTH FILES ===

test/drift-watch.test.ts is Forge-writable and civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs is not, so the
tempting split is "Forge writes tests, Regent writes code". DO NOT SPLIT IT. Step 3 changes
the injectable commands interface the tests construct (test/drift-watch.test.ts:218-227
builds `{existing, file, emit}` by hand), so a test written before the implementation would
be guessing the new interface, and a test written after is not a red-first test. The Regent
runs UNMASKED and can write test/ as easily as civ/, so it writes both in ONE commit.

=== WHAT THE EXISTING TEST DOES AND DOES NOT COVER — measured, not assumed ===

test/drift-watch.test.ts:209-231 writes a local change ONCE, then calls run() TWICE with
NOTHING CHANGED between the two runs, and asserts `filed` has length 1. That is the
no-change case. It passes today and it will pass after the fix, so it is not the regression
guard and must not be mistaken for one.

THE MISSING TEST, and it is the whole acceptance criterion: change the file BETWEEN the two
runs.
    run() -> assert 1 filed, 0 appended
    mutate the fort file
    run() -> assert STILL 1 filed total, and 1 APPENDED carrying the new fingerprint
AGAINST TODAY'S IMPLEMENTATION THAT MUST FAIL, because today the second run files a second
bead (filed length 2, no append command exists). PROVE THE FAILURE BY RUNNING IT, do not
reason it. This fort has now recorded six controls that reported PASS while proving nothing;
do not add a seventh in the fix for one of them.

=== POST-LANDING VERIFICATION, IN THIS ORDER ===

  1. --dryRun against the live tracker (the flag exists at :455). Expect 0 to file and 35
     identity matches, NOT 51. If it wants to file 35, the migration trap was not handled.
  2. One real run. Confirm the emitted event reports appended separately.
  3. THEN the duplicate cleanup: keep one bead per distinct fort+path (35), close the 16
     others referencing this bead. AFTER the fix, never before — a pre-fix run re-files them.
     Do not delete: SO7.
acceptance_criteria: Identity is (fort,path); a changed fingerprint APPENDS to the existing bead instead of filing a new one; pre-existing beads without an identity line are matched (or migrated) so the first run does not duplicate all 35; unit test per branch; the two-run-with-change test FAILS against today's implementation before the fix; a --dryRun against the live tracker reports 0 filed.
close_reason: E7 landed at c6875a6 and is reviewed. Warden APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS (Ilva, 2026-08-12): 8 findings, NONE blocking, her words 'nothing here makes the fort worse than not merging'. Findings filed forward as fortkit-veuj (the deferral removes the backport loop's primary signal), fortkit-y97d (six follow-ups incl. the dated bd-comments-seam check on the 08-14 run) and fortkit-7vdm (schema omits the charter-mandated edict events). Verified independently by the Mayor, not read off the record: main green exit 0 / 162 tests; --dry-run on the live tracker reports file:0 comment:16 suppress:23, the zero-to-file acceptance criterion; 51 open Drift beads to 35 with zero duplicate titles; and the new suite is red against the pre-E7 implementation. Ilva reproduced the verifier against sha256-matched bytes of the reviewed commit. Three rulings recorded on the edict: allowlist content-hash pin KEPT with lapse disclosure, legacy identity by title fallback with the residual disclosed, and no capital special case for or2.8.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
EDICT E7 EXECUTED, Regent (Calder Sealbroken, they/them), model opus, 2026-08-12. Commit c6875a6, one commit: civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs + test/drift-watch.test.ts + docs/specs/backport-loop.md. Verifier green (CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit, exit 0, 162 tests). Left OPEN for the Warden under covenant 4.5.

=== THE FIVE, PLUS ONE ===
zvz2  identity is now sha256(fort\0path); fingerprint demoted to change-detector; open+same suppresses, open+different APPENDS a comment, never a second bead.
or2.8 absence classified against the fort's own git history; never-propagated findings deferred, not filed. NO CAPITAL SPECIAL CASE — see the ruling below.
pp1k  rows() accepts a bare array or a v2.0 envelope; proven with BD_JSON_ENVELOPE=1 against real bd, not a mock.
bpuv  flock -E 75 makes contention unambiguous; any other status reports the child's exit code and stderr verbatim.
allowlist (5th, your spec) ruled below.
SIXTH, found during the work: 'bd list --all --limit 0 --json' is 991469 bytes against execFile's 1 MB default maxBuffer. The unattended watcher was days from dying of ENOBUFS, in a journal nobody reads. maxBuffer now 64 MB on every child spawn.

=== THE THREE RULINGS YOUR SPEC DEMANDED ===
1. ALLOWLIST CONTENT-HASH PIN: KEPT, LAPSE DISCLOSED — your recommendation, adopted. An entry must not go on suppressing a file that changed into something nobody approved. What was wrong was the silence. A lapsed entry (same fort+path, different content-hash) is now reported in the run report's 'lapsed' array, in the drift.scan payload as allowlistLapsed, and on stderr where the journal carries it. The finding resurfaces exactly as before. Test covers both halves.
2. LEGACY IDENTITY: TITLE FALLBACK, NO MIGRATION PASS. You asked me to state which and test it. A migration adding identity lines to 51 descriptions was rejected as an in-place edit of records (SO7). The matcher falls back to the title, which the watcher has always written as 'Drift: <fort> <path>'. Disclosed residual, recorded in the code and the spec: rewording a legacy Drift title during triage breaks that bead's match and the next run files a fresh one. The window closes as legacy beads close. Unit test 'matches a pre-E7 bead that carries its identity only in its title'.
3. or2.8 DEFECT 2 NEEDS NO CAPITAL SPECIAL CASE. Your bead offered three shapes for it (special-case the capital, exclude fort/scripts for it, classify as pending-hand-install). None was taken, because the git-history rule covers it with no exception: Manyhalls IS the template source and its fort/scripts is installed by the Overseer's hand, so a file it has not hand-installed has no history under that path and classifies not-yet-propagated by the SAME rule that serves the elder forts. Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Work under review:** commits `c6875a6` (code + tests + spec), `ac3e3fe` (records), `53745d8` (bead export), by the **Regent, Calder Sealbroken (they/them), model opus**, unmasked, Overseer present. A frontier model on a civilization-layer script no fort seat can write; I weighted it as I would any frontier diff — the scrutiny question here is not capability, it is that an unmasked seat's work has no mask to catch it, so the record has to carry the whole proof.

**On the gate.** The bead carries `gate-1`, so I considered mandatory-ESCALATE and concluded it does not apply. This diff touches `civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs`, `test/`, `docs/specs/`, and records. It changes no `fort/` constitution file, no seat definition, no launcher, and no permission profile — none of gate 1's named surfaces, and none of warden.md's mandatory-escalate list (auth surface, data-mutating migrations, deal-visibility). Gate 1's Overseer half is independently satisfied on the record: he commissioned the edict, was present throughout, and installed the file by his own hand twice. The bead was explicitly left open for the Warden under covenant 4.5. Escalating a change the Overseer supervised, back to the Overseer, would be ceremony.

**The substance is right, and the reasoning behind it is better than the brief's.** Identity is `sha256(fort\0path)`; the fingerprint is demoted to a change-detector; the three-way decision is implemented as specified, with two cases the spec did not have (a closed bead's one-shot suppression is preserved, and the matcher reads its own comments back so the append does not become spam on every run). The third-run silence test is the Regent's own catch and it is the one that would have bitten. The five rulings the brief demanded are all made explicitly, recorded in the code, the spec and the handoff, and the two that went against a tempting shortcut — keeping the allowlist pin, refusing the 51-description migration — went the right way for the right reason (SO7). The sixth defect (991 KB against a 1 MB `maxBuffer`) was found by measuring rather than by test, and it was a live outage waiting on a timer.

---

### Findings

**1. `not-yet-propagated` is deferred rather than filed, and the argument for deferring it was repealed by this same commit. (non-blocking)**
The spec amendment justifies deferral with "a watcher that files an unfixable bead every run trains its fort to ignore it." That was true of the *old* churning key. Under the new (fort,path) identity, a never-propagated finding would file **exactly one bead per fort+path, ever** — later template edits append comments to it, they do not file again. So the habituation hazard is already gone, and the deferral now removes signal to solve a problem the rest of the commit fixed. The capital's case is genuinely permanent and deserves silence; the elder forts' case is the backport loop's primary purpose, and for them a never-propagated template file now yields only an aggregate `findingsDeferred` count in the `drift.scan` payload, with the fort+path pairs appearing solely in stdout — a systemd journal. This also goes past all three shapes the bead offered (special-case the capital / exclude `fort/scripts` / classify as pending-hand-install), each of which reclassifies rather than silences. It is disclosed in the spec, the handoff and the bead comment, it is counted, and it is one line to reverse — which is why it is a bead and not a block. Recommend: file once per identity for non-capital forts, or at minimum enumerate the deferred fort+path pairs in the event payload.

**2. The steady-state suppression branch has no direct test. (non-blocking)**
"Open bead whose *description* already carries the current fingerprint → suppress" is the path that will run 23 times on the next scheduled run, and no committed test seeds an open bead with a matching `descriptionOf`. Every suppression the suite exercises arrives either through the comment-readback route (run 3 of the append test) or the closed-bead route. Low risk — it reads the same `known` set — but the bead asked for a unit test per branch, and this is the branch production spends most of its time in.

**3. The `bd comments` seam is on the untested side of the fake tracker. (non-blocking)**
`defaultCommands.comments` parses `bd comments <id> --json` and reads `comment.text`; the test tracker returns raw strings, so the field name is never exercised. If bd's field is not `text`, the readback yields nothing and every run re-appends the same comment — exactly the spam the third-run test defends against, just on the other side of the seam. The bead export's embedded `comments[]` objects do use `text`, which is good corroboration but not the same subcommand. Concrete check, not an assumption: the 2026-08-13 06:31 run should append 16 comments and the run **after** it should append 0.

**4. The legacy title fallback splits on whitespace. (non-blocking)**
`/^Drift:\s+(\S+)\s+(\S.*?)\s*$/` mis-derives identity for any fort whose registered name contains a space. No such fort exists (Manyhalls, Proofdelve, Farlantern) and everything filed from now on carries the explicit line, so exposure is bounded to legacy beads. Worth a guard or a comment, not a fix.

**5. `flock -E 75` collides with EX_TEMPFAIL. (non-blocking)**
A child that itself exits 75 is reported as lock contention. This script's own paths exit 0/1, so it cannot arise from here, but `bd` and `emit.sh` are not bound to that. Cosmetic; record it.

**6. Record hygiene on the event stream. (non-blocking)**
`watcher.repaired` is a new category and was not added to `schema/events.md`'s list. The schema says "extend freely," so this is not a violation — but that list is the discoverability surface for the visualizer and every consumer, and `edict.begun`/`edict.ended`, which the charter *mandates*, are missing from it too (pre-existing, worth the same bead). Separately, the two `watcher.repaired` details run 167 and 223 characters against the schema's "~140 chars so it reads as an announcement."

**7. "9 of the 13 committed tests FAIL against the old implementation" does not reproduce from the artifacts. (non-blocking)**
A straight module swap cannot yield 9 failures: the new test file takes four named ESM imports (`identityOf`, `beadIdentity`, `rows`, `descriptionOf`) that the pre-E7 module does not export, so the file fails at link time and *all thirteen* fail. The number is consistent with a graft — old `scan`/`run` dropped into the new export surface — which is a legitimate way to run it, but the record does not say so and the harness is not committed. The **substantive** non-vacuity claim is sound and I corroborated it by another route (below); it is this sentence's provenance that is thin. I raise it because this fort has now recorded six controls that reported PASS while proving nothing, and this is precisely the sentence a future reader will lean on. Recommend the record name the harness shape.

**8. `--dry-run` now requires a working `bd`. (non-blocking)**
By design and documented in the code — it must read the tracker to report what it would do. Noting it because anything using `--dry-run` as a cheap smoke test on a machine without bd will now fail where it previously succeeded.

**Not a finding, for the next reader:** there is no `edict.ended` in the stream yet. That is expected — the launcher writes it after the handoff, and the Regent's own handoff already names confirming it (one per fort, session `2026-08-12T090019`) as the next Regent's first act before closing fortkit-nvk.

**Threat model.** Nothing here bears on threats 1–4. All child processes use `execFile` with argument arrays, never a shell; the pathspec in `defaultGitHistory` sits after `--`; the only new write is an append to an existing bead. The registry path that reaches `git -C` comes from a local trusted file whose modification requires shell access — the explicitly out-of-scope actor, documented not defended.

---

### What I verified independently, versus what I took on faith

**Executed, in cwd, against the reviewed code:**
- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0**, run twice. All six steps green: memory-lint, `tsc` on both projects, biome (63 files, no fixes), vitest **162 tests / 14 files passed**, shellcheck. This reproduces the Regent's claimed verifier result exactly.

**Verified by reading the artifacts (not executed):**

The claimed number is not approximate; it is derivable.

- Comment objects in the bead export use the `text` field the watcher reads (see finding 3 for why this is corroboration, not proof).

**Taken on faith — I could not execute these.** My profile permits `fort/scripts/verify.sh`, `npx tsc` and `npx vitest run` and refused `node -e`, `mktemp -d`, `flock --help` and `man`, so I could not stand up an independent harness; `bd` cannot run in this posture at all.

All eight findings are beads, not blockers. Nothing here makes the fort worse than not merging: the acute defect is real, the fix is the right shape, the verifier is reproduced green against the exact reviewed bytes, and the cleanup is verifiable from the record rather than only asserted.

comments.text:
CORRECTION under standing order 7, Emrith 2026-08-12, appended to comments because a reader
acting on this bead's description would be WRONG about the cause and would build the wrong
fix.

WHAT I WROTE, and it is false: "THE WATCHER DOES NOT DEDUPE AGAINST FINDINGS IT HAS ALREADY
FILED" and "the watcher simply does not read it back".

IT DOES BOTH. civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:411-419 runs `bd list --all --limit 0 --json`,
:395-407 extracts every `Drift fingerprint: <sha>` from existing bead descriptions, and
:458-465 suppresses any finding whose fingerprint is already known. The mechanism I said
was missing is present and it executed: run 2 reported 17 findings suppressed BY THAT
MECHANISM. I inferred the absence of dedupe from the symptom instead of reading the file,
which is the same error pattern as my xgul.7.1 lane call earlier in this session.

=== THE REAL DEFECT: THE KEY IDENTIFIES CONTENT, NOT A PROBLEM ===

drift-watch.mjs:134

  fingerprint = sha256(`${fort.name}\0${path}\0${fortHash}\0${templateHash}`)

where fortHash and templateHash are sha256 of the two FILE CONTENTS (:125-126). So the
fingerprint identifies a (fort, path, exact-content-of-both-sides) tuple. It does not
identify "this file has drifted". ANY byte change to EITHER side mints a new fingerprint,
the dedupe correctly reports no match, and the same problem is filed again under a new
identity.

That key is guaranteed to churn, because drift IS these files changing. The dedupe is
strongest exactly when nothing is happening and useless exactly when the fort is working.

=== THE TIMELINE PROVES IT, and it closes the arithmetic exactly ===

  2026-08-11 08:10:44   run 1: 38 filed, 0 SUPPRESSED   (first live run, nothing to match)
  2026-08-11 10:24:28   Regent edict 0734b27 rewrites many TEMPLATES (fortkit-xgul.1/.3)
  2026-08-12 06:31:09   run 2: 22 filed, 17 suppressed

Run 1 fingerprinted against the PRE-edict templates. The edict then changed the templates.
Run 2 fingerprinted against the POST-edict templates, so every file the edict touched got a
new fingerprint and was re-filed; the 17 suppressed are the files the edict did NOT touch,
where the key matched and the dedupe worked perfectly.

DECISIVE MEASUREMENT: the duplicate pair 'Drift: Manyhalls fort/scripts/mayor.sh' carries
IDENTICAL reason and classification ("template-newer byte divergence", "upgrade-offer") and
DIFFERENT fingerprints:
  fortkit-w54a  6496f5b77a7ffcef3795b6815bd8aa718db12dbd74e8d33dd3ccd3cb83499ac0
  fortkit-2frg  ee8087dc82c989accc88d717725d8a7912c2e3c8399d2ce1b86a35c0232f545c
Same problem, same words, two identities. And templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh was last
changed by 0734b27, between the two runs. Confirmed by git log.

=== WHAT SURVIVES FROM THE ORIGINAL BEAD ===

The MEASUREMENT stands unchanged and was never in doubt: 29 -> 51 open Drift beads, 35
distinct fort+path pairs, 16 exact-title duplicates, every duplicated title at count 2.
The IMPACT stands. The proposed FIX SHAPE also stands and turns out to be right — key on
fort+path, append the new fingerprint to the existing bead rather than filing a new one —
but for a completely different reason than I gave. I recommended it as "add the dedupe";
it is actually "change what the dedupe key means, and keep the fingerprint as a
change-detector on an existing finding rather than as its identity".

=== AND THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR SCHEDULING ===

The bleeding is NOT automatic and NOT time-driven. A run only re-files for files whose
content changed since the last run. If nothing changes, the dedupe suppresses everything
and the run is clean — which is why I was wrong to frame "disable the timer" as the
mitigation, and the Overseer was right to question it.

WHAT TRIGGERS IT IS AN EDICT. Every Regent sitting that rewrites launchers, profiles or
templates across three forts re-mints the fingerprint of every file it touches.

THEREFORE: fortkit-52vf.1 (E1) rewrites ten launcher prompts plus bin/ across all three
forts. If E1 lands before this bead is fixed, the NEXT drift run re-files a bead for
essentially every file E1 touched. E2, E3, E4, E5 and E6 each do the same for their own
files. The programme is the trigger, and the watcher fix should therefore land FIRST.
Recorded on the epic.

INSTANCE FOR THIS BEAD'S CLASS, from Ilva Trueglass's finding 4 reviewing fortkit-n3bk.2 (2026-08-13). She explicitly recommended a comment here rather than a new bead, and I agree — E3 already owns 'false record fields'.

THE INSTANCE: the SO7 correction the Forge appended to fortkit-n3bk.1 carries the author field 'Justin Schneider'. Kethra wrote it. The Overseer did not.

WHY IT IS WORSE HERE THAN IN THE GENERAL CASE, which is her point and the reason it is worth recording rather than filing under 'known': every commit in this repository carries the same ambient git identity, so this is the Forge lane's standing provenance property and n3bk.2 did not introduce it. But A CORRECTION IS PRECISELY THE RECORD WHOSE VALUE DEPENDS ON WHO ATTESTS IT. A future reader weighing whether to trust an appended correction over the original text will read it as the Overseer's ruling when it is an agent's finding. The general defect is attribution noise; this instance is attribution that inverts the authority of the record.

MECHANISM: bd derives the actor from BEADS_ACTOR, then git user.name, then $USER. The seats that pass -a explicitly (emit.sh calls) are attributed correctly; bd comment and bd create from inside a seat session are not, because nothing sets BEADS_ACTOR in the launchers.

CHEAP CANDIDATE FIX, offered as input to this bead rather than as a decision: the launchers already know which seat they are launching and already pass -a to emit.sh. Exporting BEADS_ACTOR alongside that would attribute every bd write in the session without touching any seat's prompt. Worth measuring against what bd actually reads before anyone builds it — fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh's mask_env controls which variables survive into the sandbox, so an export that does not appear in the allowed set will silently not arrive.

title: E1a: Manyhalls' own warden.md and researcher.md carry NO session-start memory instruction — Mayor's prose-gated half of the read-side repair
description:
MAYOR'S WORK, NOT THE REGENT'S. Sibling of E1 (fortkit-52vf.1) covering the two
surfaces of the read-side repair that this fort is permitted to fix itself.

fort/seats/ is PROSE-gated to attended seats since cycle 7 (charter.md 'Prose
gates', fortkit-i4y): the Mayor may edit it directly with the Overseer's prior
approval recorded on the amendment's bead, and every such edit emits
charter.amended. Manyhalls' own seat files therefore do not need an edict. The
elder forts' do, because a masked Manyhalls Mayor cannot write outside this repo
(measured repeatedly; see the ledger fact a-masked-mayor-session-cannot-launch-the-herald).

  fort/seats/warden.md      add the session-start memory instruction (currently absent)
  fort/seats/researcher.md  add the session-start memory instruction (currently absent)

WHY THESE TWO AND NOT THE OTHER TWO. Measured 2026-08-11 across all three forts:
mayor.md and forge.md carry a correct session-start line naming
fort/memory/current.md. warden.md carries none in ANY fort, and Manyhalls'
researcher.md carries none. Those four seats have exactly one memory instruction,
the launcher prompt, and it names the retired stub. See fortkit-52vf.1 for the

Researcher can then be checked against. The Researcher's line should also carry

fort/seats/ edit.

title: E2: the mask — one pass over lib/seat-sandbox.sh x3 + template (2kub, 1q9, 5sk, 6ovg-as-mechanism-fix)
description:
EDICT 2 OF SIX (parent fortkit-52vf). THE HIGHEST-BLAST-RADIUS SITTING IN THE
PROGRAMME: if this lands wrong, no seat in any fort launches. One careful pass
over fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh in all three forts plus the template.

FOUR BEADS, ONE FILE, DELIBERATELY BUNDLED. Three separate passes over the fort's
most load-bearing script is the avoidable risk, not three times the work.

  fortkit-2kub  P1  editor swap/backup files defeat the .env inode mask. The mask
                    binds ONE path (--ro-bind /dev/null <repo>/.env.staging.local);
                    ..env.staging.local.kate-swp is a different path and a
                    different inode holding an editor's copy of the same buffer,
                    and nothing binds it. OBSERVED: a 768-byte Kate swap existed
                    in the Proofdelve tree at 2026-08-11 18:25. The Overseer ruled
                    this IN SCOPE (threat 1, agent accident, NOT the
                    human-adversary exemption) and closed option (d); do not
                    re-litigate that.
  fortkit-1q9   P1  RO carve-outs are scoped to $root while RW_PATHS grants two
                    trees ($root and $root-worktrees), so every cycle-7 protection
                    applies to only one of them. ROOT CAUSE of three recorded
                    gaps: the Warden worktree-candidate hole, the longburn-a6a
                    worktree residual, and the mayor.sh worktree .git-is-a-file
                    edge. Fix: iterate the carve-outs over EVERY tree in RW_PATHS.
  fortkit-5sk   P1  ~/.claude is granted read-write wholesale with only
                    settings.json, settings.local.json, CLAUDE.md and helpers
                    carved back. civilization.json, skills/, commands/, plugins/
                    and teams/ stay writable to every seat, and they are
                    session-executed context that runs at the NEXT launch,
                    including the unmasked Regent's. Same class cycle 7 already
                    closed for the fort config; the global surface was missed.
  fortkit-6ovg  P1  the cycle-7 verify.sh carve-out does not work: a writable FILE
                    inside a read-only DIRECTORY. See the Overseer's ruling below.

=== OVERSEER RULING ON 6ovg, 2026-08-11, RECORDED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION ===

Asked whether to make the carve-out work, drop it, or paper it with prose, the
Overseer chose: MAKE THE CARVE-OUT ACTUALLY WORK. Give verify.sh a writable
directory context so Edit, sed -i and git checkout/merge succeed. This preserves
the cycle-7 intent that the verifier is the tool the fort evolves and the Mayor
owns it, and it means E2 carries a real mask DESIGN change rather than a line
edit. Scope and verify accordingly.

MEASURED THREE TIMES, THREE FORTS, THREE MAYORS (SO11 satisfied over):
  Proofdelve  Marrek,  ForgeOs-fkmm.9,  2026-08-11
  Farlantern  Vardis,  2026-08-11
  Manyhalls   Emrith,  2026-08-11 session F, in-session probe:
                test -w fort/scripts/verify.sh            -> TRUE
                open-for-append on verify.sh              -> OK
                touch fort/scripts/.cycle7-probe-emrith   -> Read-only file system
The failure mode that makes this expensive: the error names a SIBLING TEMP PATH,
not verify.sh, so the reader hunts the wrong file.

=== NOTE ON THE FOUR COPIES ===

The three live copies have ALREADY DIVERGED (13528 / 14004 / 13652 bytes at
filing). This is not one edit applied three times; it is three edits to three
files, and the drift beads fortkit-vxpq, fortkit-hhjb and fortkit-8eq5 hold the
divergence. Diff before editing. Coordinate with fortkit-6jf (forge.sh
consolidation onto the lib), which is in_progress.

DEFERRED OUT OF THIS EDICT ON PURPOSE:
  fortkit-e4q  PID-namespace isolation. Ruled by the Overseer NOT to clear SO11;
               moving to accepted-residual treatment. It is also the one mask
               change that can break Claude Code and Codex process introspection,
               so it must never ride with four other mask changes.
  fortkit-8cq  worktree index outside the write boundary. Related mechanism,
               different decision, and it has candidate directions rather than a
               chosen one.

VERIFICATION: probe-cycle7.sh AND probe-boundaries.sh per fort, then launch one
seat per fort and confirm it starts and can do its work. A mask edit that passes
probes and prevents a launch has still failed.
design:
IMPLEMENTATION SPEC, Emrith 2026-08-12, written after reading fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh
in full. The bead description is the why; this is the how, with line numbers measured today.
THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK SITTING IN THE PROGRAMME: a bad mask stops every seat in the
civilization from launching, and the seat that would normally notice is the one that cannot start.

=== THE ARCHITECTURE, so the fixes below are legible ===

  :152  mask=(--bind / / --dev /dev --die-with-parent --ro-bind "$HOME" "$HOME")
  :154  for w in RW_PATHS: --bind w w              (re-grant writes)
  :164  for p in RO_PATHS: --ro-bind p p           (carve back out, stacks ON TOP)
  :172  --bind $root/fort/scripts/verify.sh        (the cycle-7 re-grant)
  :173  for p in extra_ro: --ro-bind p p
  later per-file /dev/null masks and per-dir tmpfs masks go LAST (ordering invariant, :155-162)

bwrap mounts STACK: later binds win. That ordering invariant is already documented and was
learned from a real incident (ForgeOs-01l, 4/4 FAIL). Do not reorder without re-running the
mask-spelling probes.

=== 6ovg — THE ONE THAT NEEDS A DECISION, NOT JUST AN EDIT ===

THE DEFECT IN ONE LINE: :164 --ro-bind's the DIRECTORY $root/fort/scripts, then :172 --bind's
the FILE verify.sh inside it. A read-write file inside a read-only directory. Measured three
times in three forts: test -w says TRUE, open-for-append works, and every ordinary edit fails
because Edit, sed -i and git checkout all need to CREATE OR UNLINK A SIBLING in the directory.

The Overseer's ruling (recorded on this bead and on fortkit-6ovg) is MAKE THE CARVE-OUT
ACTUALLY WORK. Two shapes do that and they trade differently. THE REGENT SHOULD NOT PICK
SILENTLY:

SHAPE A — directory RW, every file individually RO except verify.sh.
  Put $root/fort/scripts in the RW set and RO-bind each file in it individually, omitting
  verify.sh. Sibling creation then works, so Edit/sed -i/git checkout succeed.
  WHY IT IS SAFER THAN IT SOUNDS: each RO-bound file becomes a MOUNT POINT, and the kernel
  refuses to unlink or rename over a mount point (EBUSY). So mayor.sh et al. cannot be
  deleted or replaced even with the directory writable.
  THE HOLE, and it must be disclosed and probed rather than glossed: NEW FILE CREATION in
  fort/scripts/ becomes possible. A seat could drop a script into a host-executed directory.
  Nothing there is auto-executed and the launchers are named explicitly, so this is a staging
  area for a later mistake rather than a direct path — but it is a real widening.
  Cost: smallest change, preserves every path reference in docs and CLAUDE.md, most reversible.

SHAPE B — move the mutable verifier out of the read-only directory.
  fort/scripts/verify.sh becomes a thin RO shim that execs a writable implementation living
  where mutability is already sanctioned (repo scripts/ is not in any RO list). The directory
  stays wholly RO: no new-file hole at all.
  Cost: indirection, one new file, and docs describing fort/scripts/verify.sh as authoritative
  need a sentence (it remains the entry point, so the claim stays true).

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: SHAPE A, with the new-file hole DISCLOSED in the code comment, added
to probe-cycle7.sh as an explicitly-expected PASS (a probe that asserts the hole exists is
honest; a hole nobody probes is the thing this fort keeps getting bitten by), and recorded in
the charter's accepted-residuals list if the Overseer agrees it is acceptable. Reason for
preferring A: it is smaller and more reversible (SO2), and Shape B relocates a file that three
forts, CLAUDE.md, the charter and the memory ledger all name.
IF THE OVERSEER JUDGES THE NEW-FILE HOLE UNACCEPTABLE, take Shape B. Either way RECORD THE
RULING on this bead before implementing.

=== 1q9 — MECHANICAL, WITH ONE TRAP THAT WILL BITE ===

RO_PATHS (:81-121) are all $root-prefixed. RW_PATHS (:146) grants BOTH $root AND
$root-worktrees. So every cycle-7 protection applies to one of the two trees.

CONFIRMED BY MY OWN PROBE TODAY, not reasoned: from a masked Mayor session,
touch $root/civ/scripts/.probe is EROFS, but after git worktree add, the same touch inside
the worktree SUCCEEDS. Any masked seat can obtain a writable copy of the whole enforcement
layer by creating a worktree — and the FORGE works in a worktree by construction, so it could
edit its copy of a launcher, commit path-scoped, and the change reaches $root through the
ordinary merge the Mayor performs.

THE TRAP: DO NOT ITERATE EVERY WORKTREE. There are 76 directories under
/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees today. Carve-outs are ~8 paths each, so a naive loop emits
~600 extra --ro-bind arguments per launch and grows without bound as worktrees accumulate.
Scope the carve-outs to the worktree(s) the launch actually uses — forge.sh and warden.sh both
know which one — or RO-bind $root-worktrees wholesale and RW-bind back only the single
worktree in play. The second is the cleaner inversion and matches the "enumerate the grants,
never the prohibitions" principle already stated at :142.

=== 5sk — SMALLEST OF THE FOUR, ONE LINE, BUT CHECK THE INSTALL STEP ===

:120-121 carves back only settings.json, settings.local.json, CLAUDE.md and helpers. Add:
  $HOME/.claude/civilization.json, .../skills, .../commands, .../plugins, .../teams
These are session-executed context that runs at the NEXT launch, including the unmasked
Regent's, so a masked seat that writes them controls code running outside the mask. Same class
cycle 7 already closed for fort config; the global surface was missed.

CHECK BEFORE SHIPPING, because it will strand a workflow: fortkit-4n8c records that shipped
skills are INSTALLED AS COPIES into ~/.claude/skills/ from fortkit/skills/. If any install or
sync step expects to write there from inside a masked seat, this change breaks it. I used that
very writability today to fix skills/civ/SKILL.md. The right answer is probably to symlink the
installed skills to the repo (as ~/.local/bin/regent already is) so the RO bind on the repo
copy governs both — but that is 4n8c's decision and it DEPENDS on this bead. At minimum,
confirm what writes ~/.claude/skills today before making it read-only.

=== 2kub — THE GLOB IS THE BUG, AND IT IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS ===

:57-61 masks secrets by globbing "$x"/.env* and "$x"/*/.env*. The observed file was
  /home/justin/dev/ForgeOs/..env.staging.local.kate-swp
which begins with TWO dots, so .env* DOES NOT MATCH IT. That is the whole defect: not a missing
concept, a missing spelling.

ADD the spellings that do not begin with ".env", at both glob depths:
  ..env*            Kate ( ..<name>.kate-swp )
  .#*env*           Emacs lock file
  \#*env*\#         Emacs autosave
  .*env*.sw?        vim swap for a dotfile ( ..env.staging.local.swp )
  *env*~            editor backups not already caught
Prefer a small array of patterns over one clever glob, so each spelling is greppable and a
future editor can be added by one line.

TWO RESIDUALS TO DISCLOSE HONESTLY IN THE COMMENT:
  1. Globs are expanded AT LAUNCH. A residue file created after the mask is built is NOT
     masked for that session's lifetime. The existing comment at :54 says the glob covers "a
     fort acquiring a new .env* on arrival rather than after the incident"; that is true only
     of the next launch, and the comment overstates it. Fix the comment while you are there.
  2. Masking by enumeration cannot be complete against an editor nobody has enumerated. The
     complementary controls are fortkit-ks3t (gitignore every residue spelling) and not
     opening .env* in an editor inside a fort checkout.
The Overseer ruled 2kub IN SCOPE under threat 1 (agent accident), NOT the human-adversary
exemption, and closed option (d). Do not re-litigate that.

=== DIVERGENCE: FOUR FILES, NOT ONE FILE FOUR TIMES ===

  13528  fortkit/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh
  14004  ForgeOs/...        (+476 vs capital)
  13652  longburn/...       (+124)
  13364  templates/...      (-164)
DIFF ALL FOUR BEFORE EDITING. Held by fortkit-vxpq, hhjb, 8eq5 (drift beads). Decide per hunk
whether a divergence is intentional or decay; do not flatten them silently. Coordinate with
fortkit-6jf, which consolidates forge.sh onto this lib and is in_progress.

=== VERIFICATION — AND THIS IS WHERE THE SITTING EARNS ITS RISK ===

The E7 Regent's advice to its successor, recorded and worth obeying: PROVE MOUNT BEHAVIOUR
WITH A DETERMINISTIC BWRAP HARNESS FIRST, THEN A SMOKE, before trusting it. In order:

  1. A harness that builds the mask and asserts each intended property directly, per shape:
     verify.sh editable by Edit/sed -i/git checkout; every other fort/scripts file NOT
     replaceable; the new-file hole either absent (Shape B) or present-and-expected (Shape A);
     RO carve-outs effective inside a WORKTREE, which is 1q9's whole point; the five new
     ~/.claude paths read-only; each new .env residue spelling returning ZERO BYTES.
  2. BYTE COUNTS, NOT EXIT CODES, on every secret assertion. The file header at :14 already
     warns that a /dev/null bind may yield EACCES rather than empty, so an exit-status probe
     can pass while the file is readable. Assert zero bytes returned.
  3. probe-cycle7.sh and probe-boundaries.sh per fort.
  4. THEN launch one seat per fort and confirm it starts AND can do its work. A mask that
     passes every probe and prevents a launch has still failed, and this is the sitting where
     that happens.
  5. Re-run fortkit-xgul.7.1's now-merged guard: main must stay green.

ROLLBACK, decided BEFORE editing rather than after: keep the pre-edit seat-sandbox.sh for each
fort recoverable in one command, and know that command. If a seat cannot launch, the fort has
no masked way to repair the thing that stops seats launching — only the Overseer's unmasked

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
OVERSEER RULING 2026-08-12, recorded before implementation as cycle 7 requires for an
enforcement-layer change.

TYPED VERBATIM: "I agree that Shape A is preferred so go with that."

SHAPE A, as it was put to him and is therefore the approved scope: put $root/fort/scripts in
the read-write set and RO-bind each file in it INDIVIDUALLY, omitting verify.sh. Sibling
creation then works, so Edit, sed -i and git checkout succeed on verify.sh — which is what
"make the carve-out actually work" requires.

WHY IT IS SAFER THAN IT FIRST READS, and this is load-bearing for the ruling: each RO-bound
file becomes a MOUNT POINT, and the kernel refuses to unlink or rename over a mount point
(EBUSY, not EROFS). So mayor.sh, forge.sh, warden.sh, emit.sh and the rest cannot be deleted
or replaced even with their directory writable. The protection survives.

THE HOLE THAT COMES WITH IT, approved knowingly and NOT to be glossed in implementation: NEW
FILE CREATION inside fort/scripts/ becomes possible. A masked seat can drop a file into a
host-executed directory. Nothing there is auto-executed and every launcher is named explicitly,
so this is a staging area for a later mistake rather than a direct path, but it is a real
widening of the enforcement layer.

THREE THINGS THE IMPLEMENTATION OWES BECAUSE OF THAT HOLE:
  1. DISCLOSE it in the code comment beside the change, in the same voice the file already uses
     for its other accepted trades. A widening that only exists in a bead is a widening the
     next reader of the script will not know about.
  2. PROBE it in probe-cycle7.sh as an explicitly-EXPECTED pass — a probe asserting the hole
     EXISTS. That sounds strange and it is the right shape: this fort has recorded seven
     controls that reported success while proving nothing, and an unprobed hole is how the
     eighth happens. If the hole is ever closed, the probe goes red and tells someone.
  3. RECORD it in the charter's "Accepted residuals (measured, not assumed)" list, which
     requires a MEASUREMENT attached (charter.md:27) — so measure it rather than describing it:
     create a file in fort/scripts/ from a masked seat, record that it succeeded, and delete it.
     That amendment needs the Overseer's prior approval on its own bead and a charter.amended
     event, per the cycle-7 prose gate.

DECLINED: Shape B (a thin RO shim in fort/scripts/ delegating to a writable implementation in
repo scripts/), which has no new-file hole at all but relocates a file that three forts,
CLAUDE.md, the charter and the memory ledger all name. Preferred against on reversibility (SO2)
and on the cost of changing a path many documents assert.

comments.text:
E2 EXECUTED 2026-08-12 by the Regent, Overseer present. Four beads landed across four files plus five launchers. 2kub, 1q9, 5sk and 6ovg are LEFT OPEN for the Warden, as the brief directed. Full per-defect measurements are on each of those beads; this comment is the sitting's own record.

ROLLBACK, DECIDED AND STATED BEFORE THE FIRST EDIT (the brief's requirement): all eight touchable files snapshotted pristine to the scratchpad, all clean at HEAD (fortkit 93037eb, ForgeOs bf021ac, longburn 9a3199e). Rollback was one cp per file from an unmasked shell — no git, no mask, no seat needed, which matters because a fort with a broken mask has no masked way to repair the thing that breaks masks. Never needed.

VERIFICATION RAN IN THE MANDATED ORDER, and the order earned its keep:
1. A deterministic bwrap harness FIRST, before a single file was installed. It builds a synthetic fort under $HOME with the real layout (git repo, two real worktrees, nine secret canaries) and asserts 52 properties across four caller postures. Byte counts on every secret assertion, never exit codes.
   POSITIVE CONTROL against the PRE-EDICT lib: 34 pass / 18 fail, and every failure is a defect this edict names. A harness that cannot fail the old file proves nothing about the new one.
   CANDIDATE: 52/52 on all four generated libs.
2. A PATCHER SELF-CHECK worth recording as a method: the four files had genuinely diverged (13528 / 14004 / 13652 / 13364 bytes), so I hand-wrote the capital's version, proved it on the harness, then wrote an exact-match patcher and required it to REPRODUCE that proven file byte-for-byte before letting it near the other three. It differed in three comment hunks on the first attempt; I fixed the patcher rather than the output, so all four installed files come from one reviewed generator and the one the harness proved is one of them.
3. Every line REMOVED from each of the four files was read individually. No fort-specific divergence was flattened: ForgeOs keeps its NuGet path, ~/.codex handling and cycle-7 r2 comment; longburn keeps CODEX_DIR_RW (1p9), its codex transcript masks and its claude-only SSH_AUTH_SOCK split; the template keeps its generic wording.
4. probe-cycle7.sh 32/32 on the live capital; ForgeOs probe-boundaries 70 pass 0 fail and probe-forge-masks ALL PASSED.
5. Three real Warden smokes and three real Mayor launches. The Mayor evidence is /proc/<seat>/mountinfo READ FROM THE RUNNING SEAT — the kernel's own view of the namespace, not a reconstruction of what the launcher should have built.
6. verify.sh exit 0 on the host before AND after the commit, and exit 0 again inside each fort's Mayor mask.

THREE THINGS THE BRIEF ASKED FOR THAT WERE NOT SIMPLY MECHANICAL:
- The interactive Mayor could not be launched headless: claude with stdin from /dev/null exits at once, and  is not installed on this host. A python pty spawn is what made a REAL mayor.sh launch possible. Recorded because the next Regent will hit it.
- probe-cycle7.sh's verify.sh probe used ': >>', an O_APPEND open, which SUCCEEDED for the whole cycle 6ovg was live. That probe is why nobody caught it. Strengthened rather than trusted.
- The Warden hole 1q9 describes CANNOT be closed by any lib change; only warden.sh's argument closes it. The harness therefore keeps a permanent MEASUREMENT (not an assertion) of the shipping Warden call, which printed WRITABLE for the worktree enforcement layer and would print it again the moment that argument is dropped.

FILED FROM THIS SITTING: fortkit-pfiv (the two decay fixes, so they are reviewable on their own terms), fortkit-yowr (P1: ~20 inert Write() permission rules per fort, found only because a headless launch dumped the preamble to a file), fortkit-ddvo (verify.sh does not shellcheck templates/fort/scripts/lib/*.sh — the factory's mask builder is the one copy the verifier never checks). Receiving beads in the elder forts: ForgeOs-6vxw, longburn-949n.

COMMITS: fortkit b2881b7, ForgeOs 9939506, longburn b2ffa04. All path-scoped. None pushed.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: fortkit-e4q (PID namespace) and fortkit-8cq (worktree index) stayed out, as the bead directed. The Mayor's half of 1q9 stayed out because closing it would break the mill in all three forts today; it is pinned to E5.

  "claude with stdin from /dev/null exits at once, and  is not installed on this host"

The missing word is the name of the util-linux pty tool, s-c-r-i-p-t, which I wrapped in backticks; bash command-substituted it while building the bd invocation, the tool was not found, and the empty result was written into the record.
