comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
I have everything I need. Writing the verdict.

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES

**Round one.** Work produced by **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge ladder rung 1), per `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-13-px7e.md`. Diff: `main..bead/px7e`, two commits, three files — `templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh` (+7/-1), `test/mayor-launcher.test.ts` (new, 40 lines), the handoff.

**Scope is right, and the semantics are right.** The Forge changed only the factory copy and left the live Manyhalls/Proofdelve launchers to the Regent, exactly as the bead's LANES paragraph directs, and said so in its Open risks. The guard's semantics match the civilization's recorded 5v4 pattern verbatim (`civ/remember.md`, 2026-08-08 and the 2026-08-09 edict-8 amendment): exit 77, and `mayor.sh` refuses ANY marker including the legacy boolean `1`, while the seat-named refusal that passes `mayor` belongs to `warden.sh`/`forge.sh` and their Mayor dispatch lane. The refusal is placed before the `session.start` emit and before the `MAYOR_NO_MASK=1` escape hatch — both correct. SO12 is honoured: no identity travels (`{{PROJECT}}`, `-a mayor -s mayor`, no citizen's name in the message). The push-gate sentence now matches the capital's live `fort/scripts/mayor.sh` exactly (verified: one occurrence of "you have not been approved" there, and the template's new text is character-identical). Per Justin's 2026-08-13 correction on the bead, I judge this as a diagnosability gap, not an open capability hole, and nothing below argues otherwise. Threat-model bearing: **threat 1, agent accident**; nothing here touches the out-of-scope human-with-shell actor.

---

**1. BLOCKING — the four new tests go red in the Warden's review tree, and `verify.sh` aborts before its ShellCheck step.** Measured by me in cwd:

```
FAIL test/mayor-launcher.test.ts (4 failed)
  expected code 77, received code 1
  stderr: ".../templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh: line 8: cd: {{REPO_PATH}}: No such file or directory"
Test Files 1 failed | 14 passed (15)   Tests 4 failed | 171 passed (175)
```

Root cause is in the launcher, not only the test: the guard sits at line 12, *after* `REPO="$(git … rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo {{REPO_PATH}})"` (7) and `cd "$REPO" || exit 1` (8). Where the ambient directory is not a git checkout, the unrendered template dies at line 8 and the refusal is never evaluated — so the guard is reachable only *after* repo resolution succeeds, which is the inverse of the origin's placement (per Justin's own measurement on the bead, Farlantern checks at lines 8-9, i.e. on entry). The consequence for the fort: `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` exits non-zero here, and because `run_step` exits on the first failure (`scripts/verify-impl.sh:69`, `set -euo pipefail`) the `shellcheck` step never ran at all in my session. This is the same class the fort already treated as blocking in `52vf.9` — the comment the fix left behind at `scripts/verify-impl.sh:91-99` says it plainly: *"A false red rather than a false green, and still a broken verifier."* `verify-impl.sh` itself already knows the review tree is not a git checkout and degrades with an explicit SKIP (`:104-107`, which I saw fire); this new leg does not. It also departs from the fort's documented harness: `test/README.md` says to run a shipped shell script "with `bash` from a `git init`'d temporary directory," and `test/shell.test.ts:39-52` shows the exact idiom (`createFort()` + `replaceAll("{{REPO_PATH}}", …)`). **Fix I'd take:** hoist the three guard lines above the `REPO=`/`cd` pair — the guard reads nothing they produce, it matches the origin's on-entry placement, and it turns both the test and the verifier green in any directory. Adopting the temp-fort harness as well would close finding 3 and 4 in the same edit.

**2. BLOCKING (record accuracy, SO7) — a Verified-fact in the handoff is not true of the artefact it names.** `forge-2026-08-13-px7e.md` states the template "exits 77 before emitting a session event whenever `FORT_MASKED` is nonempty." Measured above: it exits **1**, with no refusal message, whenever the repo cannot be resolved. The neighbouring claim that `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` passed at 15 files / 175 tests is true where it was run (a git worktree) and false in a non-git checkout, and the record does not state the dependency. Hoisting the guard per finding 1 makes the first claim true unconditionally and is the remedy I'd prefer; if the fix instead touches only the test, the handoff needs a correction appended rather than an edit in place.

**3. Non-blocking — the suite has no positive control and cannot detect the worst regression.** All five assertions are refusals or source substrings; nothing asserts the launcher *proceeds* when `FORT_MASKED` is unset. A guard spelled `if true; then … exit 77; fi` passes every test in this file. The regression that matters most here is not "stops refusing" but "always refuses" — the Overseer unable to reach the Mayor at all — and it is the one case the suite is blind to. The `createFort()` + rendered-copy + stubbed `emit.sh` harness gives that control safely. Bead.

**4. Non-blocking — the test's blast radius on a guard regression.** `execFileAsync("bash", [launcher], { cwd: root })` runs the real launcher against the real repository. If the guard ever regresses, the four tests do not merely fail: the script continues to `fort/scripts/emit.sh session.start … -a mayor -s mayor` **in this fort's own event stream**, then `exec bwrap … claude` — i.e. `npm test` writes a false `session.start` and spawns a live Mayor. This fort has two recorded incidents of exactly that false-record class (`fort/memory/current.md`, the 2026-08-12 corrections to Regent launcher-verification launches, neither of which can ever have a matching `session.end`), and SO7 makes those expensive to unwind. `test/README.md`'s isolated temp fort exists to prevent precisely this, and `test/shell.test.ts`'s `expectNoEvents(root)` is the assertion for it. No `timeout` is passed to `execFile` either, so a child that hangs can outlive the run. Bead, same fixture as finding 3.

**5. Non-blocking — file placement against convention.** `test/README.md`: "For a newly covered script, keep the test in `test/shell.test.ts` unless its setup needs a separate fixture." This test has no fixture setup today. Taking findings 3-4 would give it one and justify the separate file; either resolution is fine, but the divergence should be deliberate. Bead or fold.

**Two notes, not faults.** (a) The diff removes a trailing blank line at the end of the template; unmentioned in the handoff, but it aligns the template with the capital's live file, which ends at line 44 with no trailing blank. Harmless. (b) Heads-up for the Mayor: with `52vf.11` (E9) merged and the watcher now able to see *absence*, this merge will make the drift watcher report the refusal block as missing from Manyhalls and Proofdelve until the Regent sitting lands. That is true drift, correctly reported, not a false alarm.

**Not a gate-1 referral, and I want the reasoning on the record.** `templates/` is not in the charter's kernel-read-only enforcement list, and the Overseer designated the lane on this very bead ("templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh is Forge-dispatchable"), so this is not the situation that drew a gate-1 escalation on `29e9`'s factory *sandbox*. Sequencing was honoured: `52vf.11` landed on main at 11:54 (`0134648`, `48723f0`) before this branch was cut at 13:11.

---

**Verified independently, by execution in cwd:** `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — memory-lint, skills-install (SKIPPED, disclosed), typecheck, browser-typecheck and lint (biome, 64 files) all green; **test RED at 4 failed / 175**, output quoted above; shellcheck step never reached. `shellcheck -x templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh` run directly: clean. Guard placement and reachability read from the file and confirmed by the failing test's own stderr. Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Round two of my review (Forge round three).** Work by **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge ladder rung 1), per all three handoffs. Diff `main..bead/px7e`: six commits, 0 behind / 6 ahead — a clean fast-forward onto `48723f0`, so the Overseer's sequencing behind 52vf.11 (E9) held. Files: `templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh` (+7/−1), `test/mayor-launcher.test.ts` (new, 114 lines), three handoffs. The live `fort/scripts/mayor.sh` copies are untouched, which is the Regent lane and correct.

**Both round-one blockers are fixed, and I re-measured both.**

- *Blocking 1, the hoist.* Commit `0901974` moves exactly two lines — `REPO=` and `cd "$REPO" || exit 1` — from above the guard to below it. The guard body is byte-identical to round one. It now sits at lines 10-13 as the first command in the file, matching Farlantern's on-entry placement, and it reads nothing the repo resolution produces. `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in cwd (a non-git checkout, the exact environment that was RED last round) is now **green end to end**: memory-lint, skills-install (SKIPPED and announced), typecheck, browser-typecheck, lint (biome, 64 files), test **15 files / 176 tests passed**, and the ShellCheck step — which never ran at all in my last session — reached and silent. `shellcheck -x templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh` run directly: clean.
- *Blocking 2, the record.* Both corrections are **pure appends**, not edits: `0901974` adds 9 lines to `forge-2026-08-13-px7e.md` ("Correction, 2026-08-13 round two", naming the exit-1 path and stating that the 175-test result was observed in a git worktree only), and `24ac2d4` adds 10 lines to the r2 handoff with no deletions. SO7 satisfied in letter and in placement.

**Round three's own fix is right.** `unmaskedEnvironment()` clones `process.env` and `delete`s the key rather than blanking it, which is the correct shape against a `[ -n … ]` guard; both `execFile` call sites build their child environment from it, and Node's `env` option *replaces* the child environment rather than merging, so an inherited marker cannot reach the launcher by any path. The refusal cases then set their own marker explicitly. `FORT_MASKED` appears in no other test in the suite, so no other test carries the coupling.

**The positive control has already proven it is not decorative** — the thing I most wanted from it. It failed in round two on a real condition (the launcher refusing a genuinely masked parent), which is the anti-vacuity evidence a GPT-family diff owes this fort, obtained the hard way rather than by argument.

**Fidelity to the ported law**, checked against `civ/remember.md` (2026-08-08 and the 2026-08-09 edict-8 amendment): "mayor.sh refuses ANY marker", exit 77, with the seat-named pass-mayor behaviour belonging to `warden.sh`/`forge.sh`. The template matches. SO12 holds — no identity travels. The push-gate sentence is character-identical to the capital's live `fort/scripts/mayor.sh:25`. Threat-model bearing: **threat 1, agent accident**; nothing here touches the out-of-scope human-with-shell actor, and per Justin's 2026-08-13 correction this remains a diagnosability fix, not a capability hole.

--------

**1. Non-blocking — the positive control passes through a launcher that has already errored.** `createFort()` writes `fort/scripts/emit.sh` and `bin/claude` but no `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, and the launcher `source`s that path at line 35 — *before* the `MAYOR_NO_MASK` branch at 37. There is no `set -e`, so bash writes "No such file or directory" to stderr and continues. This is executed evidence, not inference: the file cannot exist in the fixture, and the test passed in my run, so the script demonstrably ran on past the failed source. The assertion is `toMatchObject({ stdout: … })`, so the child's stderr is invisible to the suite. The control still does its job — it would fail if the guard fired — but it would also pass over a real error introduced anywhere in lines 14-35. **Fix:** stub the lib in the fixture and assert stderr is empty. Bead.

**2. Non-blocking — `expectNoEvents()` cannot fail as written.** `emit.sh` is stubbed to `exit 0` with no write, so `fort/events` could never appear regardless of the launcher's behaviour. The assertion is honest belt-and-braces and costs nothing, but it is not the guarantee its name implies. `test/README.md` describes the alternative that would make it real (the shipped `emit.sh` resolves `git-common-dir` from the temp fort, so its writes stay isolated); the positive control would then legitimately produce the `incident` event, which is itself worth asserting. Same bead as finding 1 — one fixture, one edit.

**3. Non-blocking — the scrub is per-call-site, not per-fixture.** The round-three directive asked the Forge to *consider* whether the harness should scrub `FORT_MASKED` for all children so no future test inherits a seat marker. It is applied at the two `execFile` call sites; `createFort()` itself is unchanged, and a fifth test added to this file later inherits the marker again and reproduces exactly the failure of round two. The r3 handoff does not record that the question was considered. Low cost to close: build the scrubbed environment once in `createFort()` and return it. Bead.

**4. Non-blocking — file placement is now justified.** `test/README.md` says keep a new shell-script test in `test/shell.test.ts` "unless its setup needs a separate fixture." It now needs one (temp fort, rendered launcher, stubbed emitter, fake `claude`, scrubbed environment), and `test/researcher-launcher.test.ts` is the standing precedent. Round-one finding 5 is resolved; recorded here as closed rather than carried.

**Two notes, not faults.** (a) After merge the drift watcher — newly able to see absence, as of E9 — will report the refusal block missing from Manyhalls' and Proofdelve's live `mayor.sh` until the Regent sitting under 52vf.6 lands. That is true drift, correctly reported. (b) For whoever sequences 52vf.6: the template and the capital both still export the **legacy boolean** `FORT_MASKED=1`, not the seat name. That is out of scope here (the bead's corrected scope is the entry check, not the marker), but the `warden.sh`/`forge.sh` guards being backported must pass the Mayor's dispatch lane, and in these two forts the Mayor's marker is `1` — the `""|mayor|1` acceptance the edict-8 amendment already mandates. Worth having in front of that sitting rather than discovered in it.

--------

**Verified independently, by execution in cwd:** `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — green, all seven steps, 15 files / 176 tests, ShellCheck reached. `shellcheck -x templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh` — clean. Guard placement and the two-line hoist read from `git show 0901974`. Corrections verified append-only from the commit diffs (+9/−0 and +10/−0). Push-gate parity re-checked against the capital's live `fort/scripts/mayor.sh:25`. Branch position `0 6` against main and the E9 commits present on main. Scope confirmed from the diffstat: no live `fort/scripts/` file touched. Backport fidelity checked against `civ/remember.md` lines 352-369. Fixture gap in finding 1 read from `test/mayor-launcher.test.ts` against the launcher's line order.

**Taken on faith:** the r3 handoff's claim that `FORT_MASKED=1 CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` is green from a masked parent. **I could not execute it** — my profile refuses any env prefix but the allow-listed `CI=1`, and `warden.sh` sets no marker, so my own posture is not the masked one. I judge the claim sound on structure rather than on measurement: `execFile`'s `env` replaces the child environment entirely and both call sites build it from `unmaskedEnvironment()`, so no parent marker can reach the guard. Flagged rather than assumed, because this is the second time on this bead that an environment-dependent green has been stated unconditionally. Also on faith: the actual text of longburn's and Farlantern's `mayor.sh` (outside my working directories, command refused, as last round) — judged against the bead's verbatim quote and `civ/remember.md`. `bd` is unavailable in this posture; bead state read from the launch-time `.beads-export.jsonl`, which may lag.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
SO7 CORRECTION, raised by Sereth Twicewalked (they/them, Farlantern Warden) as finding 1 reviewing longburn-holk on 2026-08-13, and explicitly asked by them to be carried to this bead. Appended here by the Mayor because a correction placed only in the fort that found it does not reach the readers of the record that is wrong.

THE CLAIM AS RECORDED: 'in a directory that is not a git checkout the script dies at line 4 and the refusal is NEVER EVALUATED'; 'Probe scores before: 4 of 5 FAIL'.

WHY IT IS WRONG AS WRITTEN. That is true only of THE PROBE'S RENDERED COPY, whose repo fallback was pointed at a nonexistent path. It is not true of the shipped pre-change script. The shipped resolution was:
  REPO="$(git -C "$(dirname "$0")" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo <fort path>)"
  cd "$REPO" || exit 1
$(dirname "$0") is THE SCRIPT'S OWN DIRECTORY, not the caller's cwd. When that directory is not inside a git checkout, rev-parse fails, the || echo fallback yields the fort path, that path EXISTS, cd succeeds, and the guard on the next line IS evaluated. Sereth executed both halves: a non-git scratch copy fails git rev-parse --show-toplevel, and the fallback directory exists. Every seat mask binds that checkout, so the guard was reachable in every configuration present on this host.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. The defect is real but CONDITIONAL: the refusal was unreachable only when the fallback path is not cd-able — the fort moved or renamed, a copy on another machine, or a future mask that does not bind it. The hoist is the right fix and merging strictly improved every fort. What is wrong is the record reading as though the guard was bypassable AS INSTALLED.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY. The same probe construction was used on this bead, and this bead's fixes were applied to three forts. A seat reading this record in three months will believe the installed guard was bypassable and may act on it. This is the fortkit-uj3q error class in the fort's own permanent record: a measurement of the PROXY (a rendered copy with a deliberately broken fallback) reported under the label of the TARGET (the shipped script).

The original text is NOT edited, per standing order 7. This comment is the correction.

comments.text:
CORRECTION under standing order 7, Emrith 2026-08-12. This corrects a claim I recorded as a
VERIFIED FACT, and it invalidates the premise of Decision D on this bead.

WHAT I WROTE, in fort/handoffs/mayor-2026-08-11-d.md under "Verified facts", and repeated to
the Overseer: "mayor.sh:6 already carries an EXIT trap emitting session.end. The model stamp
rides existing machinery; no wrapper needs building (ph4g Decision D)."

fortkit-t9iw; MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY ME just now:

  fort/scripts/mayor.sh:44  exec bwrap "${mask[@]}" -- "${launch[@]}"

six times over as "a control that reports PASS while proving nothing", and I made it while

title: bin/regent pins no model and lets the session self-report it — carry the vn8 launcher-stamp treatment to the civilization's most privileged seat
description:
Overseer decisions 2026-08-11, on Warden finding 14 of the fortkit-xgul.1/.3 review. OVERSEER/REGENT LANE — bin/ is kernel-RO to every masked seat.

THE SYMPTOM. The A2/A3 edict's records disagree about which model did the work: bead comment, commit body and handoff say Claude Opus 5; the Co-Authored-By trailer on all three commits says Claude Opus 4.8.

THE ROOT CAUSE, measured: bin/regent contains ZERO occurrences of the string 'model'. Line 182 invokes bare 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --append-system-prompt ...' with no --model flag. So the Regent runs whatever the global default happens to be at launch time; the launcher does not know which model ran; nothing can stamp it; and the only prose record available is the model reporting its own identity — the least reliable field in the record, and the one the Warden explicitly weights scrutiny by.

THIS FORT ALREADY DIAGNOSED AND FIXED THIS, FOR ANOTHER SEAT. fort/scripts/forge.sh:104-108 carries the comment: 'Model self-report is retired (fortkit-vn8: five mislabel sightings in one day, four spellings for two models, on the field the Warden weights scrutiny by). The launcher stamps Model and timestamp from its own record, exactly as session.start emitted them.' The mechanism is proven and running. The Regent never received it. That is the whole bug.

DECISION 1 (Overseer, 2026-08-11): PIN THE MODEL EXPLICITLY, AND THE REGENT NEVER DEGRADES BELOW FRONTIER. Every other launcher pins one — forge.sh takes a model argument defaulting to gpt-5.6-terra, warden.sh defaults to opus with a charter rule against degrading below frontier. The Regent is the most privileged seat in the civilization and is the only one whose rung is whatever a global setting happened to be that morning. Consequence worth naming: fortkit-x47 changed the global default (Fable -> Opus 5), which means the Regent's rung silently moved when an unrelated setting changed. A privileged seat's capability should not be a side effect of a config edit.

DECISION 2 (Overseer, 2026-08-11): THE LAUNCHER STAMPS THE MODEL MECHANICALLY. Port the forge.sh:104-127 pattern verbatim in shape:
  - bin/regent takes the model as an argument with a frontier default, exactly as warden.sh does.
  - It passes --model "$model" to claude at line 182.
  - After the session, it awk-rewrites the civ handoff's 'Model:' line from its OWN $model variable, never from what the session wrote. forge.sh's awk block is the reference implementation: it exits 2 if line 1 is not the expected header and exits 3 if no Model: line was found, so a malformed handoff fails loudly instead of being silently unstamped.
  - Stamping failure must be NON-FATAL, as forge.sh:89 records: 'a stamping failure must not lose the session's work.'
  - The same value goes into the bead comment, so the record the Warden reads is launcher-derived rather than session-derived.

DECISION 3 (Overseer, 2026-08-11): APPEND A CORRECTION NAMING THE AUTHORITATIVE VALUE; DO NOT AUDIT BACKWARDS. Recorded on fortkit-xgul.1. Consistent with the 8cv6 ruling on past Warden verdicts: fix forward.

RELATED: fortkit-vn8 is the originating bead for the retired-self-report lesson and is still open. This bead is that lesson reaching the civilization layer.
notes:
RELATED, not blocking (dependency wired then removed by the Mayor — vn8 is the originating lesson, not a prerequisite): fortkit-vn8 is where model self-report was retired for the Forge. This bead is the same lesson reaching the civilization layer. Either can land first.
2026-08-11 SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME FILE, observed while checking the or2.9 launch — fold into the same edict.

The Regent announces itself TWICE, by two mechanisms, under two categories, with two different actors:
  {"ts":"11:25:18","actor":"regent","seat":null,"category":"edict.begun","target":null,"detail":"The Regent wakes: an edict is spoken in the Overseer's name"}
  {"ts":"11:26:05","actor":"calder","seat":"regent","category":"edict","target":"fortkit-or2.9","detail":"begun","payload":{...}}
The first is the LAUNCHER's generic wake announcement: actor 'regent' (the office, not the occupant), seat null, no target, no payload. The second is CALDER's own, correctly attributed, targeted and carrying a payload.

TWO PROBLEMS. (a) 'edict' with detail 'begun' is a non-canonical category duplicating the canonical 'edict.begun'. The schema is add-only and never renamed, so both now exist forever and any consumer counting edicts must know to dedupe. (b) The launcher's copy emits as actor 'regent' with seat null, which is the office rather than the citizen — the same class as fortkit-ebm (launch scripts emitting as the wrong identity) and directly contrary to the roster discipline every other launcher follows.

ALSO NOTE the 11:26:05 payload carries "model":"claude-opus-5[1m]" — a SELF-REPORT, and the exact field this bead exists to stop trusting. It is inconsistent with the Co-Authored-By trailer evidence recorded on fortkit-xgul.1. Whatever the truth, the launcher should be the one saying it.

RELATED: fortkit-nvk (Regent launcher: every edict announced in the wrong fort, and no edict ever announced its end) is the existing bead for launcher announcement defects. Check whether nvk already covers the dual-emit before adding a third.
2026-08-11 MAYOR RESPONSE TO THE WARDEN'S REVIEW.

FINDING 3 RESOLVES, and its real lesson is better than the finding. Ilva reported that fortkit-xgul.1 carries no appended correction, hedging correctly that 'the export is passive and may lag; if the Mayor appended it since, this finding evaporates.' MEASURED: the correction IS on xgul.1 and IS in the export — but in the notes field, not comments. She read comments. Both fields ship in .beads/issues.jsonl (verified: the export's keys include both 'comments' and 'notes', and xgul.1's notes carry the correction text).

So neither party erred on the facts, and that is exactly what makes it worth recording: MAYOR CORRECTIONS LAND IN notes, WARDEN REVIEW HABIT READS comments, AND BOTH ARE IN THE EXPORT. A correction placed where the reviewing seat does not look is a correction that does not do its job. This is not a bd defect; it is a missing convention. Worth deciding: do SO7 corrections belong in comments (where reviewers read, and which are attributed and timestamped per entry) rather than notes (which the Mayor edits as an accumulating block)? The Mayor's instinct is COMMENTS for corrections and notes for working state, but this is a records-law question and the Overseer has been ruling those today. Filed for decision rather than settled unilaterally.

FINDING 4 CONFIRMED AND FILED as fortkit-ph4g, P1, gate-1. grep -c model fort/scripts/mayor.sh = 0. The Mayor's own launcher pins nothing, and the seat that writes every bead the other seats work from has been self-reporting its rung all day, including in this session's handoff.

FINDING 10 CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT the Warden's mask prevented. Both elder forts' emit.sh parse getopts 'a:s:t:p:T:' — identical to fortkit's. The new flags are accepted in Proofdelve and Farlantern; no silent announcement failure. Her proxy reasoning from the template was right.

FINDINGS 2, 6, 7, 8 filed as fortkit-jd3g. FINDING 5 filed with 4 on fortkit-ph4g, with the note that fixing 4 by copying the current pattern would propagate 5, so 5 is decided first. Findings 1, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14 are verifications or accepted trades needing no bead.

comments.author: calder
comments.text:
DONE AND COMMITTED at 2d7f450 (bin/regent). Filed by the Regent, Calder Sealbroken (they/them), Overseer present. Cycle 12, part 2.

MODEL ATTRIBUTION FOR THIS SESSION, and it has to be said carefully because this is the bead about not trusting that field. THE LAUNCHER CANNOT TELL YOU. This session was launched by the OLD bin/regent, which passed no --model and recorded nothing; launcher edits bind at dispatch, so the fix cannot describe the session that wrote it. The best available evidence for this session is therefore the harness-supplied Co-Authored-By trailer on 2d7f450: "Claude Opus 5 (1M context)". That is a transcription, which the Mayor's ruling on xgul.1 holds authoritative over a model's self-belief. My own prose earlier today said claude-opus-5[1m] and happens to agree, but it is a self-report and is NOT the evidence. FROM THE NEXT WAKE ONWARD the launcher supplies this value and it stops being a judgment call.

WHAT LANDED, against the three decisions:

DECISION 1 (pin the model, never below frontier): bin/regent takes --model <name>, defaults to "opus", and passes it to claude. The header carries the ladder and an explicit do-not-degrade-this rule with the reason (this seat repairs the machinery every other seat depends on). Also fixed the consequence you named: the seat's rung is no longer a side effect of whatever fortkit-x47 did to the global default.

DECISION 2 (the launcher stamps it): forge.sh:104-127 ported in shape. After the session, cleanup() awk-rewrites the handoff's Model: line from the launcher's own $model. Non-fatal on every failure path, per forge.sh:89. The same launcher value goes into both event payloads, and the session's protocol now tells it the model string and forbids introspection, so bead comments and commit bodies quote a launcher-derived value.
  ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION, recorded rather than silently taken: forge.sh rewrites line 1 wholesale because a Forge handoff header is launcher-derivable. A Regent handoff header names the edict, which the launcher cannot reconstruct, so line 1 is VALIDATED (refuse if it is not "# Regent handoff ...") and never rewritten; only the model value is replaced, preserving the occupant clause after the first comma.

DECISION 3 (one announcement, correctly attributed): exactly one edict.begun and one edict.ended per fort per cycle, emitted by the launcher, canonical category per schema/events.md, actor = the OCCUPANT read from civ/seats/regent.md (never the office; that is the fortkit-ebm class), seat "regent", launcher-known model in the payload, and a target — from --edict <bead> at wake, or from a file the session writes when the bead is named later. The session is told not to emit its own.
  ON YOUR QUESTION ABOUT A THIRD BEAD: no new bead filed. fortkit-nvk already owns this — its acceptance criterion reads "one full wake+sleep cycle shows exactly one edict.begun and one edict.ended per fort, each in its own stream", which is precisely the dual-emit condition. Recorded on nvk instead.
  ON THE NON-CANONICAL SPELLING: mine was the wrong one. schema/events.md says category is the dotted event type and detail is one human-readable line, so the launcher's "edict.begun" was canonical and the session's category "edict" / detail "begun" was not. The schema is add-only, so both spellings exist in all three streams permanently and consumers must dedupe. Not undone, not rewritten.

VERIFICATION — shell-driven, deterministic, no model grading its own leash. Two throwaway forts with real emit.sh copies, a fake kit carrying the real roster, and a `claude` shim so the full lifecycle runs without opening a session. This required an FORT_REGISTRY override, which follows bin/fort-init:164's existing convention and exists so this path can be exercised at all instead of asserted — a launcher whose only test is the next real edict ships its defects into three settlements simultaneously, which is this file's actual history (fortkit-nvk).
  occupant derivation -> "calder"
  --brief-only short-circuits and announces NOTHING (real registry: fortkit stream 67 lines before and after)
  unknown flag -> exit 2 with usage
  claude receives --model <value>; the opening instruction survives intact
  --edict given -> both events carry the target
  --edict absent -> begun target null; ended target and result taken from the session's file; file cleaned up
  handoff stamping, four distinct outcomes: stamped / bad header / no Model: line / no handoff, and the ended events still emit in all four
  shellcheck -S warning clean; verify.sh:67's shellcheck leg verbatim: PASS

TWO DEFECTS THE HARNESS FOUND IN MY OWN FIRST DRAFT, kept because they are the reason the harness was worth building:
1. The occupant sed ran in a command substitution under set -euo pipefail, so an unreadable roster killed the launcher at exit 2 before it printed anything. Same family as the recorded grep -q-in-a-pipeline scar (2026-08-05). Guarded now.
2. awk `exit 2` from a main block still runs END, and END's own exit overrode it, so a malformed header was reported as a missing Model: line. civ/remember.md recorded this exact trap on 2026-08-10 and warned against consuming those codes — this launcher consumes them, and I walked into it anyway. END now preserves the code via a flag. NOTE FOR ELSEWHERE: both forts' forge.sh still collapse 2 into 3; harmless there because they only branch success-vs-failure, but it is now a known live difference.

WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN, stated plainly rather than left to look done: the new announcement behaviour has NOT been observed in a real wake. It cannot be, from inside the session that wrote it. The evidence above is a full end-to-end run against throwaway forts, which is strong, and the real cycle is the acceptance test. The next Regent should check its own wake against nvk's criterion before anything else.

LEFT OPEN for Ilva's covenant-4.5 review. The Regent does not close it.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Why ESCALATE and not APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS.** The bead carries the `gate-1` label and the diff changes `bin/regent` — a launcher, kernel-read-only to every masked seat under the cycle-7 amendment, and the launcher of the most privileged seat in the civilization. Charter human gate 1 routes launchers to **Warden + Overseer** review, and gate-listed areas are mandatory-ESCALATE for this seat. Precedent is direct and two beads old: fortkit-8cv6 and fortkit-xgul.1, both Regent edicts, both recorded "ESCALATE (gate-1 mandatory)" with no blockers. **I found nothing blocking here either.** My half of gate 1 is complete and positive; covenant 4.5 review of an edict is satisfied; covenant 4.1 is why the Overseer's half is not mine to waive.

**Model.** The launcher could not stamp the session that wrote the launcher — that is a true statement about dispatch order, not an excuse, and Calder said it first and said it plainly. The best evidence is the harness-supplied `Co-Authored-By` trailer on 2d7f450: **Claude Opus 5 (1M context)**, which the Mayor's ruling on xgul.1 holds authoritative over a model's self-belief. I weighted scrutiny at frontier. This is the last review of this seat where the model of record is a judgment call, which is the entire point of the bead.

**Round one.** Everything I would block on is stated below. I block on nothing.

---

### Findings

**1. All three mechanisms land as specified, and the shape of the port is right. Non-blocking — verified by reading the file whole, not the diff alone.** `--model` with frontier default `opus` (`bin/regent:62`), passed to `claude` (`:354`); the ladder and the do-not-degrade rule in the header (`:21-32`); the awk stamp ported from `forge.sh:104-127` and non-fatal on all four paths (`:264-297`); one `edict.begun`/`edict.ended` pair per fort, canonical category, actor from the roster, seat `regent`, launcher-known model in the payload (`:213-221`, `:299-315`). I checked the deliberate deviation against the artifacts it has to fit: the last ten `civ/handoffs/regent-*.md` all open `# Regent handoff — edict of …` and carry `Model: <model>, as **Calder Sealbroken** (they/them). …`. The header-validate-don't-rewrite choice and the preserve-everything-after-the-first-comma rule are exactly fitted to that format, and the reasoning for the deviation is recorded rather than silently taken. Both self-found draft defects are genuinely fixed in the shipped code: the `-f` guard plus `|| true` around the occupant substitution (`:95-97`), and the `bad_header` flag that survives `END` (`:266`, `:280`).

**2. A multi-edict session now announces only its first edict, and the session is forbidden to fill the gap. Non-blocking; file as a bead — but this is the finding I would most want Justin to see.** The launcher brackets the **session**; the protocol at `:346` says "DO NOT EMIT YOUR OWN `edict.begun` OR `edict.ended`"; and `EDICT_FILE` holds one bead id on line 1. Cycle 12 was two edicts in one session (or2.9, then w1ew). So were cycles 10 and 11 — `civ/handoffs/regent-2026-08-10T094129.md` covers both. That is three of the last four wakes. Under the new law, edicts 2..N of a session have no `edict.begun` of their own and the session may not emit one. Covenant 4.2 and 9.2 say "announces itself … at the start and the end of the work" and are satisfied by a session bracket; charter §105 says "An edict is never silent. It emits `edict.begun` and `edict.ended`" and is edict-scoped, so it is not. Nothing becomes invisible — the session window still covers the change in all three streams — but per-edict targeting is lost, and the loss is silent. The cheap fix is to say in the protocol what a second edict should do: append to `EDICT_FILE` and emit a **canonical** pair for it. The defect the diff removed was the wrong *spelling* and the wrong *actor*, not the existence of a per-edict announcement.

**3. The bead's Decision 3 is not discharged, and the comment renumbers it out of view. Non-blocking; for Justin.** The bead's DECISION 3 is "APPEND A CORRECTION NAMING THE AUTHORITATIVE VALUE; DO NOT AUDIT BACKWARDS. Recorded on fortkit-xgul.1." The comment's "DECISION 3" is the announcement fix, which the bead states in NOTES. `jq` over `.beads-export.jsonl` shows `fortkit-xgul.1` carries exactly two comments — Calder's 18:25Z and mine 18:54Z — and no appended correction; the export's newest comment anywhere is 19:59Z, so it is fresh past the edict's 19:58Z. **Substantively the correction exists**: both the w1ew comment and `civ/handoffs/regent-2026-08-11T112517.md` name the authoritative value and the reason it is authoritative. What is missing is its placement on the bead whose records disagree, which is where a future reader of xgul.1 will look. The export is passive and may lag; if the Mayor appended it since, this finding evaporates.

**4. "Every other launcher in this civilization pins one" is false, and the counter-example is the seat Justin talks to. Non-blocking; file a bead — measured, so SO11 is satisfied.** `bin/regent:27-28` states it; `fort/scripts/mayor.sh:25` builds `launch=(claude --append-system-prompt "…")` with no `--model`, and `grep -n model fort/scripts/mayor.sh` returns nothing — the same zero-occurrence measurement this bead was filed on. `forge.sh`, `warden.sh` and `researcher.sh` do pin. So the Mayor — design, triage, the seat that decomposes everything — still runs on whatever the global default is that morning, still self-reports its model into its handoffs, and `fortkit-x47` moved its rung too. The comment is a rhetorical overstatement, which is minor; the defect it accidentally documents is not.

**5. The pinned value is an alias, so the stamped record inherits one layer of the problem it removes. Non-blocking; same bead as 4 or its own.** `opus` is resolved by the CLI's alias table — a global setting. When that table next moves, this seat's rung moves with it and the stamped `Model: opus` will not record that it did. The stamp also *overwrites* whatever the session wrote, which in this cycle would have replaced the more precise `Claude Opus 5 (1M context)` transcription with `opus`. This matches `warden.sh:29` and the bead's own Decision 1 text, so it is compliant, not a deviation — but "launcher-derived" and "precise" are different properties and only the first was bought. Recording the resolved id, or pinning a full model string, buys the second.

**6. The launcher enforces a handoff-header contract it never states to the producer. Non-blocking; file as a bead.** `:266` refuses to stamp unless line 1 matches `^# Regent handoff`; the protocol at `:342` asks for the handoff by path and content and says only that it must contain a line beginning `Model:` (`:344`). A session that opens `# Regent edict handoff …` gets refusal 2 and no stamp. The ten existing handoffs all comply by convention, the failure is loud and non-fatal, and the warning names the model — so this degrades correctly. One clause in the protocol closes it.

**7. 179 lines land in the civilization's most privileged launcher with zero automated coverage, and the harness that proved them was thrown away. Non-blocking; file as a bead.** No test in the 153 references `bin/regent`'s behaviour; `fort/scripts/probe-cycle7.sh:37` only asserts it is read-only. The four-outcome stamping proof, the occupant derivation, the flag matrix — all real work, none of it re-runnable by the next reader, including me. This is the silent-revert class I recorded as finding 4 on xgul.1, and the fort already has the pattern: `test/researcher-launcher.test.ts` asserts over launcher source, and `test/memory.test.ts:181` builds a temp fixture. A test that asserts `bin/regent` passes `--model`, that both emit calls carry `-a`/`-s`, and that the awk block returns 0/2/3 against three fixtures would make the next revert loud.

**8. "Every fort has been told" is printed unconditionally, and every emit failure is silenced. Non-blocking; file as a bead. Bears on threat 1 (agent accident).** `:220` and `:314` end in `2>/dev/null || true`, and `:232` prints the banner regardless. If `jq` finds no forts, or an emit rejects the payload, the wake looks identical to a successful one. That silencing predates this diff, but the diff adds failure modes to what is being silenced (payload construction, three new flags) and, via finding 9, a new way for the fort list to be empty. Counting successful announcements and saying the number would cost one line and would have caught fortkit-nvk on day one.

**9. `FORT_REGISTRY` is a genuine testability win and a small new accident surface. Non-blocking — documented, not blocked on.** The convention is real: `bin/fort-init:164` reads `REG="${FORT_REGISTRY:-$HOME/.claude/civilization.json}"`, verified verbatim. A stray export in a shell rc or a test harness would redirect every announcement away from the real forts — threat 1, and finding 8 is why it would be silent. The version where a human sets it deliberately is the explicitly out-of-scope actor, who does not need it. The reason given for adding it — that a launcher whose only test is the next real edict ships defects into three settlements at once — is this file's actual recorded history, and I judge the trade correct.

**10. Cross-fort flag compatibility is the one behavioural risk I cannot close from here. Non-blocking; the next real wake is the test.** The new call passes `-s`, `-t` and `-p` to **each fort's own** vendored `emit.sh`; the old call passed only `-a`. My profile refuses reads outside fortkit, so I cannot inspect `/home/justin/dev/{ForgeOs,longburn}/fort/scripts/emit.sh`. Proxy evidence is strong: `templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh` — still headed "Proofdelve event emitter", i.e. the extracted ancestor — parses `a:s:t:p:T:` via getopts exactly as fortkit's does. If an elder copy is older than that, the announcement fails and finding 8 means it fails silently, in the two settlements that have historically been the ones left uninformed.

**11. Visualizer impact checked, and there is none. Non-blocking — verified.** Events with seat `regent` and actor `calder` cannot create a phantom fourth citizen: `src/colony-page.ts:300-305` builds citizens from the roster reader, not from event actors, and `test/colony-reader.test.ts:216` shows the civ seat file being read for the palace path — with the same `**Held by: Calder Sealbroken** (they/them)` line shape the new occupant `sed` parses. The fort's own streams have carried `actor:"calder", seat:"regent"` since 2026-08-10 with the suite green.

**12. Two small edges, recorded rather than raised. Non-blocking.** (a) A zero-byte handoff reports "no `Model:` line" rather than a bad header, because `NR == 1` never fires — the right warning is arguable and neither is wrong. (b) `--model '$model'` is interpolated into the generated runner inside single quotes, so a value containing a quote breaks it; the value comes from the Overseer's own command line, and the same has always been true of the instruction argument.

**13. Discoverability of `--edict`. Non-blocking; fold into finding 6's bead.** `civ/CIVILIZATION.md:128` documents the command as bare `regent`. The target on `edict.begun` is only as good as the Overseer knowing to pass `--edict` at wake; otherwise it arrives at `edict.ended` from the session's file, or not at all.

**14. No third bead was filed, and that was right. Non-blocking — verified.** `fortkit-nvk` is open, P1, and its acceptance criterion reads "Warden review of the bin/regent diff; one full wake+sleep cycle shows exactly one `edict.begun` and one `edict.ended` per fort, each in its own stream" — quoted accurately, and it does own the dual-emit condition. Calder's self-assessment that the session's `category:"edict"` / `detail:"begun"` spelling was the non-canonical one is correct against `schema/events.md`, and the decision not to rewrite the streams follows the add-only rule.

---

### What I verified independently

- **`CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` from cwd, in-mask** — memory-lint, typecheck, typecheck:browser, biome (63 files), vitest **14 files / 153 tests passed**, and the `shellcheck -x` leg at `verify.sh:67` covering `bin/regent` at default (style) severity, which is stricter than the `-S warning` the record claims. The run completed through the final step and the harness reported no non-zero exit; as on xgul.1, my profile refused a compound `echo $?`, so I confirm success structurally (`set -euo pipefail`, `run_step` exits on the first failure) rather than as an integer. `shellcheck 0.11.0` is present, so the leg ran rather than being skipped.

- The awk contract against the real artifacts: the last three `civ/handoffs/regent-*.md` headers and `Model:` lines, and the suffix-after-first-comma rule against each.
- `bin/fort-init:164` for the `FORT_REGISTRY` convention; `fort/scripts/forge.sh:88-127` for the ported pattern and the "must not lose the session's work" rule; `fort/scripts/warden.sh:29` for the `opus` default; `fort/scripts/mayor.sh:25` for finding 4.
- `schema/events.md` for the category/detail contract; `fort/scripts/emit.sh` and `civ/scripts/emit.sh` for `-a/-s/-t/-p` and `--argjson` payload handling; `templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh` for the proxy in finding 10.

- `civ/covenant.md` §4.1-4.3 and §9.2 against charter §105, which is the basis for finding 2's distinction.
- `jq` over `.beads-export.jsonl`: `fortkit-nvk` open with the quoted criterion; `fortkit-xgul.1` closed with two comments and no appended correction; export fresh through 19:59:10Z.
- `src/colony-page.ts` and `test/colony-reader.test.ts` for finding 11.

### What I took on faith

- **The entire throwaway-fort harness result** — occupant derivation returning `calder`, the flag matrix, `--edict` present/absent, the four distinct stamping outcomes, the claude shim receiving `--model`, and "measured both ways" on the awk END trap. My profile refused every ad-hoc `awk`, `bash -c` and piped probe I attempted, so I could not re-execute one line of it. I read the code paths instead and found nothing that contradicts any claim; the awk exit/END semantics and the `set -e` AND-list semantics both work as the comments say. It remains the Regent's observation, not mine — and per finding 7, it is now no one's, because the harness was not kept.
- That the elder forts' vendored `emit.sh` accept `-s`/`-t`/`-p` (finding 10) — proxy evidence only, their trees are outside my reach.

**For Justin, the questions this ESCALATE carries:** (1) your gate-1 half on a change to the civilization's break-glass launcher — verified to the limit of a read-only seat, no blocking objection from me; (2) finding 2 — do you want a multi-edict session to announce each edict, because as shipped it cannot and is told not to, and three of the last four wakes were multi-edict; (3) finding 3 — the bead's Decision 3 (the correction on `fortkit-xgul.1`) is still open, though the authoritative value is named on this bead and in the handoff; (4) finding 4 — `mayor.sh` has the identical defect, unfixed, on the seat you talk to. title: Per-seat core budget: the injection cap belongs to the session, not the ledger
description:
Overseer decision 2026-08-11, taken INSTEAD OF a relevance-routing memory manager.

THE QUESTION. The Overseer asked whether a routing job should prune and reallocate which facts are core based on relevance to present and near-future work. Two objections decided it against.

(1) THE FACTS THAT MOST NEED TO BE CORE ARE THE LEAST RELATED TO CURRENT WORK. 'Never read .env.staging.local'. 'The deploy script is human-only'. 'Build the solution before you test or the DLL HintPaths lie'. Those are dangerous precisely because nobody was thinking about them. A relevance-to-current-work ranker would demote exactly the facts whose entire value is arriving unbidden.

(2) A JOB THAT SILENTLY REWRITES THE ALWAYS-INJECTED SURFACE is a change to the fort's operating assumptions with no bead, no review and no announcement — the pattern the charter tells seats to escalate as a compromise signal. The charter already rules on this shape: 'Crons watch, models act.'

THE CHEAPER ANSWER, ADOPTED: the budget was never really a property of the FORT. The ~30 facts / 300 lines figure is the measured degradation threshold for wholesale injection into ONE CONTEXT. A session sees one seat's band, so the cap belongs to the seat.

CHANGE: core budget becomes PER SEAT. For each seat, the core facts visible to it — its own scoped facts plus every seats:[all] fact — total <= 300 lines / ~30 facts. No new frontmatter: scope.seats already exists and section 7 delivery is already per-seat (fortkit-88u.6).

CONSEQUENCES WORTH NAMING:
  - Total core facts across a fort may exceed 30; no single session ever sees more than 30. That was always the real constraint.
  - seats:[all] at core tier becomes the EXPENSIVE declaration: it spends budget in every seat at once. The lint reports it separately as the shared floor, so widening a fact's scope is a visible act rather than a default. That is what produces a small, smart core rather than a growing common one.
  - Tripwires get precise. 'Never push without asking' is a Mayor tripwire; 'commit path-scoped, never git add .' is a Forge tripwire; neither needs to burn the other seat's budget.

THE ROUTER IS A V2 CANDIDATE WITH A NAMED TRIGGER, per standing order 11: build it when there is an OBSERVED failure of the form 'a session went wrong because the right fact was not core'. That failure will also say which band it belonged in. Until then it is machinery without a scar.

SCOPE: amend docs/specs/memory.md 4.2 (Mayor, free lane — docs/specs/ is not gated); then memory-lint counts per seat rather than globally and reports the seats:[all] floor separately (Forge). The lint change is the load-bearing half: a doctrine cap nobody counts is prose.
acceptance_criteria: docs/specs/memory.md 4.2 states the per-seat budget and the seats:[all] cost rule; memory-lint enforces per-seat counts and reports the shared floor separately; a planted over-budget seat fails the lint.
notes:

FORGE HALF REMAINS and it is the load-bearing one: memory-lint must actually COUNT per seat and report the shared floor. A doctrine cap nobody counts is prose, which is the failure mode this fort keeps converting into mechanism. Dispatching next.
2026-08-11 MAYOR ERROR — the same dirty-working-tree class, twice in one day.

WHAT HAPPENED. The Mayor edited docs/specs/memory.md 4.2 and 4.4 for this bead, ran verify, updated the bead — and did NOT COMMIT. The Forge was then dispatched, branched from COMMITTED main (which still carried the old global-budget wording), correctly concluded the spec needed the per-seat update, and wrote its own version in commit a71ab55. Its handoff flagged this honestly: 'this worktree still contained the old global-budget spec wording'.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is exactly Ilva's finding 5 on fortkit-8cv6 (fortkit-f8ol): a dirty working tree makes what a seat reads differ from what is committed, and the seat has no way to know. This morning she read an uncommitted charter amendment as law. This afternoon the Forge read a committed spec that the Mayor had already superseded in an uncommitted edit. Same cause, opposite direction. The Mayor committed after her finding and then immediately reoffended on the next file. THE LESSON IS NOT 'REMEMBER TO COMMIT' — it is that fortkit-f8ol's dirty-tree warning should cover DISPATCH as well as REVIEW: forge.sh should refuse, or loudly warn, when the Mayor dispatches with uncommitted changes to paths the bead names. Filing that thought on f8ol.

RESOLUTION, no records harmed. The two versions say the same thing; the Forge's is more concise on the mechanics. The Mayor's uncommitted version additionally carried three things the Forge was never asked to write and which are Mayor-lane doctrine: the consequence-not-relevance promotion test, the per-seat tripwire examples, and the recorded rejection of the relevance-router with its standing-order-11 trigger.   2. The working tree is reverted to HEAD, so the branch merges clean with no conflict and the Forge's committed wording stands as the mechanics of record.
  3. AFTER the merge, the Mayor re-applies ONLY the doctrine paragraphs on top. They are additive to the Forge's text, not a replacement of it.

Nothing about this is the Forge's fault and its handoff caught the anomaly it could see.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round one. Work by **gpt-5.6-terra** (top rung of the Forge ladder). Branch `bead/88u.16` = `a71ab55` + `74a27c3`; both commits path-scoped, nothing gated touched (`docs/specs/memory.md`, `scripts/memory-lint.mjs`, `templates/fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs`, `test/memory.test.ts`, one handoff). The two lint copies are byte-identical, which is the right shape for the settlement factory. The handoff's Verified-facts section reproduced exactly against my own run — shared floor 2 facts / 33 lines, 153 tests, 14 files — so its claims are accurate, including its honest flagging of the stale spec wording it inherited from committed main. The acceptance criteria are met: §4.2 states the per-seat budget and the `[all]` cost rule, the lint counts per seat, and a planted over-budget seat turns the build red.

Nothing here reaches the blocking bar. Findings 1–3 are the ones I would want beads for.

**1. (non-blocking) A core fact with no parseable `seats:` list is counted against nobody — a coverage regression against the old global count.** `scopeSeats` (`scripts/memory-lint.mjs:30-37`) returns `[]` when the scope block has no inline `seats: [...]` line; the caller then adds nothing to the shared floor and iterates an empty list, so the fact contributes to zero budgets. §4.1 only requires `scope` to be non-empty (`≥1` selection tag), and the lint only checks `scope.trim() !== ""` — a core fact carrying just `topics:` is schema-valid and invisible to the cap. A YAML block sequence (`seats:` then `- all`) escapes the same way. The sibling case: an unrecognised seat name is silently accepted, `coreBySeat.set(seat, …)` mints a phantom bucket, and the fact is charged to a seat that does not exist instead of the one it was meant for. Under the old global count every core fact was counted exactly once regardless of scope; under the new one, a whole class is uncounted. All ten facts in the ledger today carry an inline `seats:`, so nothing is escaping now. Fix is small and belongs in the same lint: require a non-empty `seats:` on `tier: core`, and fail any seat name not in the `fort/seats/` roster.

**2. (non-blocking, and the one I most want the Overseer to see) The per-seat cap is enforced ahead of the per-seat delivery it presumes.** The bead's rationale says "a session sees one seat's band" and "section 7 delivery is already per-seat (fortkit-88u.6)"; the handoff repeats it as "no single session receives another seat's scoped facts." **fortkit-88u.6 is open** in the export, and the injected surface today is `fort/memory/current.md`, which `scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs:385-390` builds from *every* active core fact with no scope filtering at all — delivered to every seat by the CLAUDE.md instruction to read it. So the fort can pass memory-lint with, say, 25 mayor-scoped and 25 forge-scoped core facts, each seat green, while every real session receives all 50 and the measured degradation threshold is blown in all of them. This is exactly the "green gate over a violated condition" the bead's own load-bearing argument is aimed at. It is hypothetical at 4 core facts, and the Forge implemented the bead as written — the premise is the bead's, not the diff's. But the cap does not mean what §4.2 now says it means until 88u.6 lands or `consolidate-memory` filters `current.md` per seat, and I do not think that dependency should stay unrecorded. Bears on threat 1 (agent accident) only; the budget is a context-quality control, not a security control, and no finding in this review bears on threats 2–4.

**3. (non-blocking) The new test does not discriminate per-seat from global.** `test/memory.test.ts:208` plants 22 forge-scoped facts + 1 shared: the passing case totals 299 lines and the failing case 312 — identical under the old global summation, so the fixture would pass and fail the same way against the code this diff replaces. The discriminating case is the one the change exists for: two seats each near budget whose *fort total* exceeds 30/300 and which must pass. The model of record for the fortkit-xgul.1/.3 edict (commits 0734b27, 321729c, f923630) is CLAUDE OPUS 4.8, per the Co-Authored-By trailer. The prose records — this bead's comment, the commit bodies, and the civ handoff — say Claude Opus 5 and are WRONG. Nothing is edited; this note is the correction.

WHY THE TRAILER IS THE AUTHORITATIVE FIELD, and it is a reasoning about evidence classes rather than a coin toss. Claude Code's system prompt supplies the exact Co-Authored-By string for the session's actual model and instructs the session to end commit messages with it. The trailer is therefore a TRANSCRIPTION of a harness-provided value. The prose model line is the session's SELF-BELIEF about its own identity, which is the least reliable field a model produces — this fort measured that directly on fortkit-vn8: five mislabel sightings in one day, four spellings for two models. Transcription of a supplied string beats self-knowledge. A mis-transcription is possible but is a strictly smaller failure mode.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY, stated rather than hidden: fortkit-x47 set the global model default to Opus 5, and bin/regent passes no --model, so the expectation was that the Regent would run Opus 5. The Mayor cannot distinguish these from inside the repo, and fortkit-w1ew makes the question moot going forward by pinning the model and stamping it from the launcher. Recorded so a later reader knows this correction rests on an evidence-class argument, not on a measurement of the running process.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REVIEW, and it is the benign direction: Ilva weighted her scrutiny at the LOWER rung (4.8) and re-derived every load-bearing claim she could execute. Her verdict is therefore not weakened by the contradiction. The dangerous inversion — prose claiming a lower rung than the model that ran, so a Warden relaxes scrutiny — did not occur here and is what fortkit-w1ew prevents.
