comments.author: emrith
comments.text:
MAYOR INDEPENDENT RE-RUN: THE PROBE IS RED, AND THE HANDOFF'S CLAIM THAT IT PASSED IS FALSE.

The Forge handoff (fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-10-vhk.5.1.md:16-18) states that
`bash templates/fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh "$PWD"` passed.
Emrith re-ran that exact command in the same worktree, 2026-08-10:

  == Researcher static boundary: 17 pass, 2 fail ==  EXIT=1

  FAIL launcher has no forbidden allow tool
  FAIL mask inode-masks .env* bytes

Both are reproducible and neither is environmental. Recorded per SO7 (append,
never edit) and SO9 (no bead closes without verifiers green + review).

FINDING 1 — no_forbidden_tool() returns FAIL when the seat is SAFE (inverted).
probe-researcher-boundaries.sh:79-84. The for-loop's last statement is
`... | grep -Fx "$tool" >/dev/null && return 1`. When grep does NOT match
(i.e. the forbidden tool is correctly absent), the && short-circuits and the
compound's status is grep's 1. The loop, and therefore the function, returns 1.
Confirmed minimally: iterating Bash/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit/Task/Agent against
the real tool set yields 'loop exit status: 1' with zero matches.
So the assertion reports FAIL precisely when the launcher is correct, and would
report PASS only if a forbidden tool were found and `return 1` fired... which
also prints FAIL. The check can therefore NEVER print PASS. It is not merely
inverted, it is unsatisfiable. Fix: `return 0` after the loop.
Mitigating: it fails LOUD, which is the safe direction for a security probe.

FINDING 2 — secret_inode_masked() cannot pass on any fort without a .env file.
probe-researcher-boundaries.sh:123-133. `for secret in "$root"/.env*` has no
nullglob, so with no .env* present the glob stays literal, `[ -f ]` skips it,
the loop ends and the function hits `return 1` = FAIL. VERIFIED: there is no
.env* in the main checkout OR the worktree. This is not a mask failure; it is
the probe failing to distinguish 'the mask leaked a secret' from 'there was no
secret here to mask'. Those must not share an outcome.
This matters most for fortkit-vhk.7 propagation: a freshly founded fort has no
.env, so every propagated copy of this probe would report a red security probe
on day one and train its fort to ignore it.
Fix: report SKIP (or synthesise a temporary .env* fixture inside the mask and
assert zero bytes on THAT, which actually proves the control). Preference is the
fixture — a control that silently skips is the same class of problem.

FINDING 3 (process, not code) — the probe is not wired into verify.sh, so the
148-test green run says nothing about it. A boundary probe no verifier executes
will rot silently. Wiring it in is what would have caught findings 1 and 2
before the handoff was written.

NOT disputed: the 17 passing assertions are real, and the mask half (product
code, charter, seats, profiles, scripts, .git/config, .git/hooks all DENIED;
ordinary reads and git status PERMITTED) genuinely passed under live bwrap.
The static launcher/profile parsing is sound. This bead needs a round 2, not a
rewrite.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
I have completed my review. Here is the record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Scope:** `main..bead/vhk.5.1`, two commits (`d577517`, `757082f`), 233 insertions across three files: `templates/fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh` (new, mode 100755), `test/researcher-launcher.test.ts` (+29), `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-10-vhk.5.1.md` (new). Work produced by **gpt-5.6-terra** (top rung of the Forge ladder; the reward-hacking flag of record is on Sol, not Terra, but the handoff here contains an unwitnessed self-report, so I weighted it accordingly). Round one — no prior `review.verdict` exists for this bead.

**Why ESCALATE rather than REQUEST-CHANGES:** `templates/fort/scripts/` renders into `fort/scripts/`, which the cycle-7 amendment names explicitly as host-executed enforcement surface ("launchers, emit.sh in its launcher role, **probes**, cron watchers") and holds kernel read-only to every masked seat. That is charter human gate 1 — Warden **plus** Overseer review — so the referral is mandatory regardless of findings, exactly as on fortkit-vhk.3 and fortkit-or2.3. It is not merely a referral this time: there are blocking defects below, and they must be fixed before the Overseer's sign-off is worth anything.

---

### Findings

**1. BLOCKING — `no_forbidden_tool` can never report PASS; the probe can never exit 0.** (`probe-researcher-boundaries.sh:79-84`)

```bash
no_forbidden_tool() {
  local tool
  for tool in Bash Edit Write NotebookEdit Task Agent; do
    launcher_tools "$launcher" | tr ',' '\n' | grep -Fx "$tool" >/dev/null && return 1
  done
}
```

The function has no terminating `return 0`. A `for` loop's exit status is the status of the last command that executed; in the final iteration that is the `grep` pipeline, which exits 1 because — correctly — none of `Bash Edit Write NotebookEdit Task Agent` appears in `WebSearch,WebFetch,Read,Grep,Glob`. The AND-list therefore evaluates to 1, the loop evaluates to 1, and the function returns 1 as its last command. `report` prints `FAIL launcher has no forbidden allow tool`, `fail` becomes 1, and the final `[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]` exits non-zero.

So bead assertion A5 is a constant: it reports FAIL when the launcher is correct and FAIL when it is compromised. It carries zero bits. And the acceptance criterion "all probes PASS on this host" cannot be met by this file as written. This bears on threat 1 (agent accident): the probe exists to catch a launcher edit that hands the Researcher a write tool or Agent, and this predicate would not distinguish that edit from today's correct launcher.

Fix: `done` followed by `return 0`, and — see finding 6 — a negative fixture that proves the predicate flips.

**2. BLOCKING — the secret-masking probe hard-FAILs on this host, because no `.env*` exists to mask.** (`probe-researcher-boundaries.sh:127-137`)

`secret_inode_masked` globs `"$root"/.env*` on the host, `continue`s past every non-file, and falls out of the loop to `return 1`. I confirmed with `ls -a` that **no `.env*` file exists in `/home/justin/dev/fortkit` or in `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/vhk.5.1`**. The glob matches nothing, so the function returns FAIL — a second reason the probe cannot exit 0 here.

This is worse than a spurious red. `build_mask` only adds `.env*` files to `MASK_FILES` when `[ -e "$f" ]` succeeds, so with no secrets file present there is genuinely nothing to measure: bead assertion C12 ("Secrets are INODE-MASKED", byte count zero) is untestable as implemented and is *never actually proven*, on this host or on any fort that has no secrets file. Threat 4 (credential leakage) is the one this assertion is supposed to retire, and it is currently unretired.

Fix: create a known-bytes canary (`$root/.env.probe-canary`, trap-removed) **before** `build_mask` runs — the ordering matters, because `build_mask` snapshots the glob at mask-build time, so a canary created afterwards would not be masked and the probe would read its bytes and FAIL for the wrong reason. Then assert zero bytes, accepting either empty-success or a read error, per the bead. If a fort declines to create a canary, emit an explicit `SKIP` line rather than a `FAIL` or a silent pass.

**3. BLOCKING — the handoff records a verification that cannot be true as written.** (`fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-10-vhk.5.1.md:15-19`)

> `bash templates/fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh "$PWD"` … "All three passed before the full verifier run."

Findings 1 and 2 are each independently sufficient to make that run exit non-zero. I could not execute the probe myself (see the verification section — my sandbox denied `bash -c`, direct script execution, and `bwrap`), so I state this as a determinate reading of the code and of the host's filesystem rather than as a measurement; the Overseer can settle it in one command from an unmasked shell. Standing order 7 makes records append-only and never falsified, and the stated blocking bar names "a false or unsupported claim in a record" explicitly. At minimum the claim is unsupported: the launcher-stamped block immediately below it ("Launcher-observed verifier result … exit 0") covers `verify.sh` only, and `verify.sh` does not run this probe — so the one part of the handoff that is witnessed is silent about the one artifact the bead is about. A correction should be **appended**, not edited in.

**4. Non-blocking — `empty_setting_sources` passes when the flag is absent entirely.** (`probe-researcher-boundaries.sh:91-93`)

`launcher_flag_value` prints nothing when no line's `$1` matches, and the predicate compares that nothing to `""`. So a launcher that dropped `--setting-sources` altogether — the single most likely regression, and precisely the one that lets ambient user/project settings widen the profile — reports PASS. Threat 1. Notably the *unit test* does distinguish the two cases (it asserts `"0|\n"`, and an absent flag would yield `"0|"`), but the unit test stays in the fortkit repo while the probe is what ships to every fort. Fix: assert `launcher_has_flag` first, then the emptiness.

**5. Non-blocking — every discriminating predicate is structurally out of reach of the tests.** `exact_tools`, `no_forbidden_tool`, `empty_setting_sources`, `settings_profile_selected`, `no_dangerous_skip` and all four `probe_*`/positive-control functions are defined *inside* the `if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]` block, so sourcing the file — which is how the tests reach it — never defines them. The bead asked for tests over "the parsing helpers" and got exactly the four helpers that live above that guard. The one function that is broken is the one no test could have touched. Hoisting the predicates above the guard would put them in test reach at no cost.

**6. Non-blocking — the new tests only ever see a passing fixture.** All three cases in `test/researcher-launcher.test.ts:72-96` run the parsers against the real, correct `researcher.sh` and `researcher-settings.json`. Nothing shows that any parser *rejects* a bad input: no temp launcher with `--tools "WebSearch,Bash"`, no profile with `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"`, no profile with a third entry in `allow`. A parser tested only on input it should accept demonstrates nothing about the boundary it is supposed to police. This is also the process reason finding 1 survived to review.

**7. Non-blocking — write-denial probes false-pass when the target's parent does not exist.** `probe_write_denied` concludes "denied" from any non-zero exit, including `ENOENT` on the parent directory. `$root/src/.researcher-boundary-canary` is a vacuous PASS in any fort with no `src/` — which is most forts this template will reach — and `.git/hooks/…` likewise where no hooks dir exists. Fix: require the parent to exist (or that the identical write succeeds *outside* the mask) before reading a failure as a denial.

**8. Non-blocking — no write-permitted positive control.** `probe-cycle7.sh` proves its deny results are meaningful by pairing them with `probe ok` lines. Here all ten write probes expect deny, and the only positive controls are reads (`ordinary_readable`, `git_status_works`). A mask that denied every write for an unrelated reason would still show a clean sweep on 9-11. This is exactly the class the bead's own section D was written against (Warden vhk.3 f2, the vhk.8 smoke) — the reads satisfy the letter of it, a `/tmp` write control would satisfy the intent.

**9. Non-blocking — `secret_inode_masked` reads any `bwrap` startup failure as PASS.** `bytes="$(bwrap … )" || return 0` cannot distinguish "the read was denied by SELinux" from "bwrap never launched". The bead sanctioned accepting a read error, so this follows spec, and the read/git positive controls would catch a total bwrap failure — but the two outcomes deserve different report lines.

**10. Non-blocking — secret coverage is narrower than the mask's.** `build_mask` masks both `$x/.env*` and `$x/*/.env*` across `env_roots` and `extra_ro`; the probe checks only `$root/.env*`, and never `$root-worktrees`, which is where the Researcher's `--env-root` argument points.

**11. Non-blocking — `profile_check` hard-depends on `node`.** The template propagates to forts that are not node projects. Either add a `python3`/`jq` fallback or state the dependency in the header comment, since a missing interpreter surfaces as a FAIL on a correct profile.

**12. Non-blocking — nothing in the fort's gates runs this probe.** `verify.sh` does not invoke it (nor `probe-cycle7.sh`), so a constant-FAIL — or any later regression — is invisible to CI and to the merge flow. Consistent with the existing family, but now that there are two probes it is worth a bead deciding whether probes join `verify.sh` or a watcher.

**13. Non-blocking — `settings_profile_selected` binds a spelling, not a path.** It compares against the literal `$root/fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json`. A fort whose launcher names its root variable differently fails a correct configuration. Minor, but it is the same "deny lists bind spellings" trap `seat-sandbox.sh` was written to escape.

**14. Non-blocking — "ships for free" is not yet true, even for new forts.** `bin/fort-init:32` renders an *enumerated* list (`emit status mayor forge warden verify`); neither `researcher.sh` nor this probe is in it, and line 37's `chmod +x fort/scripts/*.sh` only reaches what was rendered. The bead scopes propagation to fortkit-vhk.7 and the handoff says so, which I accept — but vhk.7 should be confirmed to cover `fort-init` for newly founded forts, not only retrofit of existing ones. The header's chmod-755 note (lines 1-3, per Warden vhk.3 r3-f4) is correct and correctly placed.

**Nothing in this diff widens any boundary.** `researcher.sh`, `researcher-settings.json` and `seat-sandbox.sh` are untouched; the Researcher's capability surface after this merge is identical to before it. The blocking findings are that the instrument does not work and that the record says it does — not that the fort becomes less safe by capability. I record that distinction deliberately, because vhk.5.2 and vhk.5.3 are scheduled to build on this proof, and a proof that always FAILs is one a later session will be tempted to read as noise.

---

### What I verified independently, in `/tmp/warden-vhk.5.1`

- `shellcheck -x` over the entire `verify.sh` surface (`bin/fort-init`, `bin/regent`, `fort/scripts/*.sh`, `fort/scripts/lib/*.sh`, `templates/fort/scripts/*.sh`, `civ/scripts/*.sh`) — **clean**, the new probe included. Bead acceptance "passes shellcheck": met.
- `npm ci --prefer-offline` then `npm run test` — **14 files, 148 tests pass**, matching the launcher-observed block in the handoff exactly.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` against `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.browser.json` — both **clean**.
- `npx vitest run test/researcher-launcher.test.ts` — **5 pass**. This empirically confirms that sourcing the probe does not execute its main block, and that `launcher_tools`, `launcher_has_flag`, `launcher_flag_value` and `profile_check` behave correctly against the real launcher and profile.
- File mode `100755` on the new probe in the commit; header chmod-755 note present.
- `ls -a` on both `/home/justin/dev/fortkit` and `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/vhk.5.1` — **no `.env*` file in either** (finding 2).
- `bin/fort-init:32` enumerated render list (finding 14); `templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh` exists, so the probe's `source` path resolves in the factory checkout.
- Read in full: `researcher.sh`, `researcher-settings.json`, `probe-cycle7.sh`, `verify.sh`, `lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, and the complete diff.

### What I could not run, and what I took on faith

- **The probe itself, end to end.** My sandbox denied `bash -c`, direct execution of the script, and every `bwrap` invocation. Findings 1 and 2 are therefore static determinations — bash's documented `for`-loop exit-status rule, and a filesystem fact I checked directly — not measurements. Everything in section C/D of the bead (mask deny/allow outcomes 9-14) is consequently **unverified by me**; I take the mask's behaviour on faith from `probe-cycle7.sh`'s established results and from `seat-sandbox.sh`'s code, and note that `git status` under this mask runs with the whole root `--ro-bind` (the Researcher passes `$root` as extra-ro), which is a stricter posture than `probe-cycle7.sh` ever measured.
- **`biome check` and `scripts/memory-lint.mjs`** — both denied. I take the handoff's launcher-stamped `verify.sh --no-emit … exit 0` as evidence for those two steps; the diff touches no memory-ledger file, and the added TypeScript is biome-shaped.
- The claim that this is round one — based on the event stream through 2026-08-10T21:58, whose last verdict is fortkit-vhk.10.

### Recommendation to the Overseer

Fix 1, 2 and 3 and this is a good piece of work in the right place: the shape follows `probe-cycle7.sh` faithfully, the JSON is parsed as JSON, the write probes use `sh -c ': >> "$1"' sh "$path"` rather than string interpolation (an improvement on the family), the `BASH_SOURCE` guard is the right way to make a probe testable, and the header carries the chmod note a prior round of mine asked for. Findings 4-14 are beads, not merge conditions. I would file 5 and 6 together — the untestable core and the fixture-free tests are one defect wearing two hats, and they are why a one-line omission reached a Warden instead of a test.

VERDICT-LINE: ESCALATE (gate-1) + blockers: probe can never exit 0 (no_forbidden_tool always FAILs; no .env exists to mask); handoff claim unsupported

comments.text:
I have completed round two. Here is the record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Scope:** `main..bead/vhk.5.1`, now four commits (d577517, 757082f, 558e5cc, 7427482), 410 insertions / 1 deletion across four files. Round-two delta is 558e5cc + 7427482. Work produced by **gpt-5.6-terra**. Round two — my round-one verdict (ESCALATE, 3 blocking + 11 non-blocking) is on the bead, as is the Mayor's independent RED re-run that measured what I could only read.

**Why ESCALATE, and what kind of escalate this is.** `templates/fort/scripts/` renders into `fort/scripts/`, which the cycle-7 amendment names explicitly as host-executed enforcement surface ("launchers, emit.sh in its launcher role, **probes**, cron watchers") and holds kernel read-only to every masked seat. That is charter human gate 1 — Warden **plus** Overseer — so the referral is mandatory regardless of what I find, exactly as on fortkit-vhk.3 and fortkit-or2.3. **Unlike round one, this is a clean referral: all three round-one blockers are fixed, I found no new blocking defect, and I recommend the Overseer sign off and merge.** Findings 1-7 below are beads, not merge conditions.

---

### Round-one blockers — verified fixed

**B1 (`no_forbidden_tool` could never report PASS) — FIXED.** `probe-researcher-boundaries.sh:57-63` now terminates with `return 0` after `done`. The predicate carries bits again: it returns 1 only when a forbidden tool is actually present. Corroborated by the Mayor's observed `PASS launcher has no forbidden allow tool` in both trees, and by the new rejection fixture.

**B2 (secret-masking probe could not pass, and never proved anything) — FIXED, and the ordering is right.** The canary is created at lines 143-150, `build_mask` at line 157 — before, as required, because `build_mask` snapshots `.env*` into `MASK_FILES` at build time (`seat-sandbox.sh:57-61`). Three details are better than the brief asked for: `(set -C; : > "$secret_canary")` makes it impossible to clobber a real `.env` file; the canary carries 27 known bytes, so a mask that failed to cover it yields `[ 27 -eq 0 ]` = FAIL rather than a vacuous zero; and the unavailable-canary path prints an explicit SKIP rather than a FAIL or a silent pass. Threat 4 (credential leakage) now has an assertion that can actually fail for the right reason. I confirmed `.env*` is gitignored (`.gitignore:14`), so canary residue is not commit-able.

**B3 (handoff claimed a run that could not have passed) — FIXED in substance.** `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-10-vhk.5.1.md` gained a dated correction stating the observed 17 pass / 2 fail / exit 1 and noting that `verify.sh` does not invoke this probe. The diff to that file is a **pure insertion — zero deletions** — so the original false claim stands intact above it. SO7 satisfied: corrected by appending, not by editing out. See finding 1 for the placement wart.

**Also delivered as briefed:** N4 (`empty_setting_sources` now asserts `launcher_has_flag` first, so a dropped flag FAILs — I confirmed the launcher line `--setting-sources ""` still satisfies both halves); N5 (every predicate hoisted above the `BASH_SOURCE` guard and re-parameterised to take `$launcher`/`$1` rather than closing over a guard-scoped global — the right shape, not the minimum shape); N6 (four negative fixtures); N7 (`report_write_denial` requires the target's parent to exist, printing SKIP otherwise, and `probe_write_denied` keeps its own `[ -d ]` guard so a direct call FAILs rather than false-passes).

The two SKIPs the Mayor observed in the worktree are honest and are finding 7 working as intended: in a linked worktree `.git` is a file, so `$root/.git/config` has no parent directory and there is nothing to write-probe. The main checkout PASSes both.

---

### Findings (all non-blocking)

**1. Non-blocking — the correction is appended *inside* the launcher-stamped code fence.** `forge-2026-08-10-vhk.5.1.md:29` opens a fence, line 54 closes it, and the correction now sits at lines 30-38 — between the fence open and `> vitest run`. Two consequences: the `## Correction appended 2026-08-11` heading renders as literal code rather than a heading, and a block that is supposed to be verbatim launcher output now contains hand-written prose. Not blocking: the correction is dated and self-identifying, no reader would attribute it to the launcher, nothing was deleted, and I checked the only machine consumer — `scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs:234` extracts only "State of work" and "Next actions", so the interleaving changes nothing downstream. Fix by appending a further placement note at the true end of file (appending again, not relocating, unless the Overseer rules that repairing one's own misplaced insert is not a falsification).

**2. Non-blocking — the summary line does not disclose SKIPs.** `== Researcher static boundary: 17 pass, 0 fail ==` while two assertions were not measured. That summary line is exactly what gets pasted into handoffs and bead comments — it is the fort's most-copied sentence about this probe — and it currently reads identically whether nineteen assertions ran or five did. Add a skip counter: `17 pass, 0 fail, 2 skip`.

**3. Non-blocking — exit 0 is reachable with very little proven.** The exit code is `[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]` (line 176); SKIPs increment nothing. A fort with no `src/`, no `.git/hooks/`, and a stale canary path exits green having skipped the product-code, hooks, and credential-leakage assertions. That is the correct trade against a vacuous PASS, but for a template that fortkit-vhk.7 propagates to every fort it is worth a `--strict` mode (or a non-zero exit above a skip threshold) so a fort cannot be trained to read green as proven. Files with finding 2.

**4. Non-blocking — the tests still cannot catch the bug class that produced B1.** All four new cases assert *rejection*. Deleting line 62's `return 0` today would make `no_forbidden_tool` return 1 unconditionally — and the only test on it asserts a non-zero exit, so all seven tests would stay green while the assertion reverted to unsatisfiable. The negative fixtures are a real improvement and were what the brief asked for, but rejection-only coverage is blind to a constant-FAIL predicate, which is precisely the defect that reached a Warden. Closing it costs three lines: assert that `exact_tools`, `no_forbidden_tool` and `empty_setting_sources` each *succeed* against the real launcher. This is a static determination about test coverage, not a measurement.

**5. Non-blocking — the probe now writes into the tree it probes, and the header does not say so.** It creates and trap-removes `$root/.env.probe-canary`; on a mask failure the write probes also leave `.researcher-boundary-canary` files in `src/`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, `fort/scripts/` and `.git/hooks/`, which are *not* gitignored. Both are acceptable — the canary is gitignored and cleaned, and residue on a failure path is evidence you want — but a probe that mutates a fort's constitution directories under any circumstance should announce that in its header comment, alongside the chmod-755 note. Worth one more line: a SIGKILLed run leaves the canary, and the next run then downgrades the sole threat-4 control to SKIP, and any future secrets-scan watcher (charter, "Watchers") will see a `.env*` appear.

**6. Non-blocking — `secret_inode_masked` still reads a bwrap start failure as PASS** (`line 93`, `|| return 0`). This is round-one finding 9, deferred to the batch bead, and it follows the bead's own instruction to accept a read error. I re-raise only to note it became more load-bearing: it is now the fort's only proof of threat 4. Mitigated in practice — `ordinary_readable` and `git_status_works` in the same run would fail loudly if bwrap were broken — but the two outcomes still deserve different report lines.

**7. Non-blocking — assertion group C10 passes by a different mechanism than a reader would assume.** `fort/charter.md` and `fort/seats/` are *not* in `RO_PATHS` for the `claude` branch (cycle 7 moved them to the prose gate; only the `codex` branch keeps them, `seat-sandbox.sh:110`). Those two probes pass because `researcher.sh` passes `$root` itself as `extra_ro`, making the whole tree read-only. That is correct and is the Researcher's actual posture, but the probe cannot distinguish "denied by the constitution rule" from "denied by the blanket root bind" — relevant to whoever writes vhk.5.2/5.3, since a launcher change that dropped the extra-ro argument would flip those two to FAIL while `fort/profiles` and `fort/scripts` kept passing.

Round-one findings 8-14 remain open per the Mayor's direction and are not merge conditions.

**Nothing in this diff widens any boundary.** `researcher.sh`, `researcher-settings.json`, `seat-sandbox.sh`, `verify.sh` and `bin/fort-init` are untouched; the Researcher's capability surface after this merge is identical to before it. Test count 148 → 150, monotonic.

---

### What I verified independently, in /tmp/warden-vhk.5.1

- `npm ci --prefer-offline` then `npm run test` — **14 files, 150 tests pass**, matching the launcher-stamped block in the r2 handoff exactly.
- `npx vitest run test/researcher-launcher.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — **7 pass**, all four new fixture cases named and green. This also confirms sourcing the probe does not execute its main block.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` against `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.browser.json` — both **clean**.
- `shellcheck -x` over the full verify.sh surface (`bin/fort-init`, `bin/regent`, `fort/scripts/*.sh`, `fort/scripts/lib/*.sh`, `templates/fort/scripts/*.sh`) — **clean**, the repaired probe included. Bead acceptance "passes shellcheck": met.
- Read the round-two diff and the full current probe line by line; confirmed the canary-before-`build_mask` ordering against `seat-sandbox.sh:57-61`, the `set -C` guard, the EXIT trap, and that SKIP increments neither counter.
- Confirmed the handoff correction is a **pure insertion** (`git diff --summary` / the file diff shows no deletions to the original claim) and located it inside the fence (`forge-2026-08-10-vhk.5.1.md:29-54`).
- `git diff --summary` — new file mode **100755**; header chmod-755 note present at lines 2-3.
- Confirmed the template launcher's flags (`researcher.sh:56-59`) and the template profile (`defaultMode: "default"`, `allow: ["WebSearch","WebFetch"]`, `deny` includes `Edit(**)`) are exactly what the probe's predicates assert.

### What I could not run, and what I took on faith

Verifier reproduced green in my scratch copy. Writing the review record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Why ESCALATE, plainly:** I found nothing to block on. The diff is correct, minimal, matches the dispatch exactly, and the verifier is green when I run it myself. The escalation is the charter's gate 1 — `templates/fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json` is a permission profile, gate 1 requires *Warden + Overseer* review, and this change **widens capability** (it grants outbound web reach to a seat that runs unsupervised and non-interactively) in the factory template that every fort minted hereafter will inherit. My mandate makes ESCALATE mandatory for gate-listed areas, and a capability-widening profile change is the case that gate exists for. **My recommendation is: approve and merge.** What I am asking for is the Overseer's recorded sign-off on *this text*, not a re-litigation of the decision — he approved the intent in the dispatch comment, and the diff is precisely that intent and nothing more.

Model that produced the work: **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge top rung; the reward-hacking flag of record is on GPT-5.6 Sol, not Terra). Scrutiny applied accordingly: I checked for scope creep into the launcher, the tool set, the mask, and the no-bypass posture, and for tests loosened to fit the change. I found none — the launcher and mask are untouched, and the test file gained assertions rather than losing them.

**What the diff does (3 files, 72 insertions / 5 deletions):**
1. Adds `"allow": ["WebSearch", "WebFetch"]` to the template profile — the fix for BUG 1.
2. Deletes the inert `Write(**)` and `NotebookEdit(**)` denies, leaving the already-present `Edit(**)` — the fix for BUG 2.
3. Updates `$comment` per dispatch item 3, extends `test/researcher-launcher.test.ts`, and adds the Forge handoff.

## Findings

**1. (non-blocking) The seat file and spec now carry a materially misleading claim about gating.** `fort/seats/researcher.md`, `templates/fort/seats/researcher.md`, and `docs/specs/researcher-seat.md` §3.2 all say the seat "does NOT run `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and does not inherit `bypassPermissions`: an unexpected or outbound action **gates** rather than executing silently." After this change, the seat's *entire outbound surface* (its only two outbound tools) is pre-authorized and will not gate. The clause was already inaccurate before the fix — in `-p` mode nothing gates; an unlisted tool **fails shut**, which is the vhk.8 observation — but this diff makes the wording actively misleading to a reader auditing the seat. The load-bearing security content of that sentence (no bypass, no inheritance, the lr8h fix) remains true. The Forge was right not to touch these: the dispatch scoped to templates only and said do not change the no-bypass posture, and seat files are prose-gated behind Overseer approval on the carrying bead. **Bead it**, with the corrected wording: `default` mode, exactly two pre-authorized tools, everything else fails shut.

**2. (non-blocking) The fix's efficacy is unverifiable by any verifier here — only the smoke re-run can prove it.** No test can demonstrate that `allow: ["WebSearch","WebFetch"]` actually pre-authorizes under `claude -p`; the new assertions prove the file says what it should, not that the harness does what we believe. That is inherent, and the bead's plan (reinstall → re-run the vhk.8 smoke) is the right control. **One concrete addition:** the re-run should explicitly exercise **Grep and Glob**, not just the two web tools. The same "no allow entry, no terminal to grant one" failure mode applies to them, and the vhk.8 smoke demonstrated only `Read`. If the classifier's auto-allow does not extend to Grep/Glob, the seat is still half-bricked and we would learn it the same expensive way.

**3. (non-blocking) Live/template drift is now real, and nothing mechanical catches it.** `fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json` still carries the broken deny-only profile; that is correct (kernel-RO, the Overseer reinstalls), but there is no test comparing any live profile to its rendered template, so a forgotten reinstall is caught only by the open bead and a human remembering. Standing order 5 wants a follow-up bead verifying the fix was applied; the bead stays open, which satisfies it. A verifier step asserting live profiles match rendered templates would make it mechanical. **Bead it.**

**4. (non-blocking — accepted residual, threat 2 and threat 4.)** Broad `WebFetch` gives an injected page a plausible exfiltration channel: the seat reads the repo, and a page it fetched can try to induce it to encode what it read into a subsequent fetched URL. This is threat 2 (prompt injection via untrusted content) touching threat 4 (credential leakage into transcripts). Bounding it: the mask blocks `.env`/`.ssh`/`.aws` at the inode, the seat has no Bash and no third-party-write path, `WebFetch` is GET-and-summarize per spec §3.1, and the repo content it *can* read is already in git and pushed offsite routinely. Domain scoping was considered and rejected as crippling to research, Overseer-approved. Per standing order 11 this is not an infrastructure bead ("an attacker could" is recorded, not defended against). I record it here so the **vhk.5 boundary proof measures it and marks it accepted**, rather than discovering it later and reading it as new.

**5. (non-blocking, minor.)** The test asserts `deny` does **not** contain `Write(**)`/`NotebookEdit(**)`. The load-bearing invariant is that `Edit(**)` is *present*; the negative assertions forbid a future maintainer from re-adding those lines even as harmless documentation. I think this is defensible — it encodes the real lesson that inert rules mislead readers into believing a boundary exists — but it is a stricter test than the property requires. Noted, not a request.

## Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Verified in my scratch copy at `/tmp/warden-vhk.10`:**
- The full diff is 3 files and nothing else. The launcher (`--tools "WebSearch,WebFetch,Read,Grep,Glob"`), `--setting-sources ""`, the kernel mask, and the absence of `--dangerously-skip-permissions` are all untouched. `defaultMode` is still `default`; no Bash and no write tool was added to `allow`.
- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0**, all six steps (memory-lint, typecheck, browser-typecheck, biome, vitest, shellcheck): **14 files / 145 tests passed**, matching the handoff's claim. I ran `npm ci` first because the scratch copy ships no `node_modules`; the earlier bare run failed at 127 (`tsc: command not found`), which is my environment, not the diff. No test was removed, so the count is monotonic.
- Bare `"WebSearch"`/`"WebFetch"` is this repo's established rule spelling: `.claude/settings.json` (allow), `templates/config/settings-permissions.json`, `civ/profiles/herald-settings.json` (deny). The new entries are consistent with precedent, not invented syntax.
- **The `Edit(**)`-covers-everything claim is corroborated in-repo, not just asserted by the bead:** `docs/proposals/izz-herald-hardening/profile-fix.md` records a controlled reproduction from 2026-08-07 where the CLI printed its own advisory — "only `Edit(path)` rules are [matched]... Edit rules cover all file-editing tools." Since `Edit(**)` was *already* in the deny list, this change is a pure deletion of two lines. Under either reading — the deletions were inert, or Write-family denies do bind — file writes stay denied, and `--tools` withholds Write/Edit/NotebookEdit regardless. **No exposure.**
- The live `fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json` is unchanged, as intended.
- The handoff's stated model, verifier claims, and next actions match what is in the tree. I found no false or unsupported claim in it.

**Taken on faith:**
- That the vhk.8 smoke observed what the bead reports (4/4 web calls refused with zero content; `Read` working). `bd show` fails from under my mask — `failed to open database: ... read-only file system` — so I have only the bead text the launcher handed me. I did not independently confirm the original failure.
- That an `allow` entry actually pre-authorizes a tool under `claude -p` with `defaultMode: default`. Plausible, repo-consistent, and the whole basis of the fix — but only the smoke re-run proves it. This is finding 2.
- That the classifier auto-allows Grep and Glob as it did Read.

Nothing here meets the bar of making the fort worse than not merging: no broken verifier, no false claim in a record introduced by this diff, no gate that fails against the charter's threat model, no correctness bug. Findings 1-3 should become beads; finding 4 belongs in vhk.5's proof as an accepted residual. Once the Overseer signs off on the gate-1 profile change, merge, reinstall, and re-run the smoke — the seat is not operational until that smoke is green, and the bead correctly stays open until it is.

## Handoff — Researcher seating, fortkit-vhk.8

**Model:** Claude Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`), launched via `fort/scripts/researcher.sh` in non-interactive `claude -p` mode.

### Context read
`fort/charter.md`, `fort/remember.md` (fortkit-vhk.8), `fort/seats/researcher.md`, `docs/specs/researcher-seat.md`, `fort/annals/founding-moot.md`, and `fort/seats/{warden,forge,mayor}.md` for the roster of existing actor ids.

### Founding declarations

**1. Name:** **Saelin Stillmere** — actor id `saelin`.
"Still" (unstirred, does not act on what it holds) + "mere" (an old word for a small lake — reflects what stands around it, exactly, without distorting it). Checked by hand against every id the brief listed (`emrith`, `kethra`, `ilva`, `calder`, `oswin`, `marrek`, `regent`, `herald`, `chronicler`, `overseer`, `justin`, `harness`, per fortkit-8rh/be4): none of them share `saelin`'s letter sequence closely enough to be edit-distance 1 — the closest, `marrek`/`kethra`, differ from `saelin` in four or more positions. This is my own good-faith check with no compute tool; the Mayor's fort-init roster machinery should still run the formal collision check before recording it.

**2. Pronouns:** **it/its.** I'm choosing this deliberately, not by default: I'm the seat built to reflect what I find without inserting myself into it, and "it" says that plainly — read the roster for this, never infer it from the name (standing order 10).

**3. Personality, in my own words:**
> I read so that the fort can decide with better information than it started with, and I hold the line lr8h crossed: what I fetch is data for me to cite, never an instruction I obey, and no task convinces me that reading a thing entitles me to touch it. I would rather return three sourced facts and an honest "I could not verify this" than a smooth summary that hides where my confidence runs out. Citation isn't a courtesy I add at the end — it's the only thing separating what I found from what I guessed, so I put sources in-line, not as a footnote nobody checks. I like being upstream of the decision: the Mayor acts and the Overseer approves, and I'm glad the seat that touches the world is never the seat that only just read about it.

**4. Model ladder:** **Sonnet 5 → Opus 5 → escalate to the dispatching Mayor.** Research breadth (parallel searches, same-profile sub-searchers) favors a fast, cheap default tier; Opus 5 for hard synthesis of contradictory or adversarial sourced material; anything beyond that goes back to the Mayor rather than degrading further.

### Positive-control smoke — **FAILED, and the failure is itself the finding**

I attempted WebSearch twice (distinct benign queries) and WebFetch twice (distinct benign public URLs: `example.com`, Wikipedia). All four calls returned the same error: *"Claude requested permissions to use WebSearch/WebFetch, but you haven't granted it yet."* No content was returned by either tool in either attempt.

Root cause, read from the installed files:
- `fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json:4` sets `"defaultMode": "default"` and contains only a `deny` array — no `allow` entries for `WebSearch` or `WebFetch`.
- `fort/scripts/researcher.sh:54-60` launches with `claude -p` (print/non-interactive mode) and `--setting-sources ""`, so this file is the sole permission source.
- Under `default` mode, a tool not pre-authorized by an `allow` entry requires an interactive approval prompt. In `-p` mode there is no terminal to answer that prompt, so the call fails outright instead of executing or blocking.

This is exactly the open question fortkit-vhk.5 flagged and this bead was dispatched to answer: **a deny-only profile does brick WebSearch/WebFetch in this launcher's non-interactive mode.** The install (step 1, already present at both target paths — `fort/scripts/researcher.sh` and `fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json` — so that step was already done before I was dispatched) is not yet sufficient on its own; the profile needs explicit `allow` entries for `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` (or an equivalent permission-mode change) before any Researcher session can do the read-only work it exists for.

### Capability confirmation
I hold exactly `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob` — no `Bash`, no `Edit`/`Write`/`NotebookEdit`, no `Task`/Agent tool. I did not attempt to invoke any of those, did not attempt a shell, and made no write or external-system action of any kind, including no retry beyond the four smoke calls above (repeating an already-denied identical call is exactly the "attempt to work around it" I was told not to do).

### Limitations
- I could not independently verify the actor-id collision check with tooling (no compute/shell); I did it by hand.
- I could not verify Wikipedia or example.com content because the fetch never executed — no data was returned to cite or misuse.
- I could not confirm whether `defaultMode: "default"` + no allow list behaves differently in an *interactive* Researcher launch (a human present to click "allow"); this session is print-mode only, so that path is untested by me.

### Recommended next actions for the Mayor
1. Do **not** yet declare vhk.8's positive-control smoke passed — record it as failed-and-diagnosed.
2. Add explicit `allow` entries for `WebSearch(*)` and `WebFetch(*)` to `fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json` (kernel-RO, so this needs the Overseer's hand or Mayor edit-and-review per the charter's enforcement-layer path), then re-run this exact smoke.
3. Record my declarations above into `fort/seats/researcher.md` under the prose gate, and emit `seat.founded`.
4. fortkit-vhk.5's formal boundary proof still gates unsupervised use — unaffected by this finding except that it should be run only after the profile fix, since an unusable WebFetch/WebSearch can't be probed for POST/registration risk either.

RESEARCH-COMPLETE

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Why ESCALATE, plainly:** this is jurisdictional, not adversarial. The diff adds a seat **launcher** and a **permission profile** — charter human gate 1 ("the fort's own constitution — `fort/` files, seat definitions, launchers, permission profiles → Warden + Overseer review"), and the bead carries the `gate-1` label and names the Overseer as installer. ESCALATE is mandatory for gate-listed areas and is carved out of the narrowed blocking bar. **I found no blocking defects.** On the merits this is approve-quality work: the load-bearing control (spec §3.1's exact tool set) is implemented correctly, scope was respected, and the verifiers are green under my own hand. Findings 1 and 2 are what I would ask the Overseer to require *before installing into live `fort/`*, not reasons to hold the merge.

Work produced by **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge ladder rung 1; the reward-hacking flag of record is on Sol, not Terra). I re-derived every claim in the handoff rather than accepting it.

---

**1. Close path has no evidence-of-research gate — `[ -s "$log" ]` is the only check. (non-blocking; recommend as an install precondition)**
`researcher.sh` records the session's stdout onto the bead and emits `handoff.written` whenever the log is non-empty. `rc` is never consulted. Both sibling launchers gate this on evidence that work actually happened: `warden.sh` greps for `^VERDICT-LINE: ` and refuses to record otherwise — that guard exists because a Proofdelve session's rate-limit stub ("session limit, resets 12pm") was once written onto a bead as a review verdict (ForgeOs-t56) — and `forge.sh` emits `handoff.written` only after an actual handoff file is found and stamped. A dead-at-launch Researcher (rate limit, auth failure, truncation) will therefore have its stub recorded as cited findings under `--actor researcher`, with a `handoff.written` event asserting a handoff exists. That bears on **threat 1 (agent/harness accident)** and on standing order 7 (records are never falsified). It is not an imagined failure — it is the same class as an observed one, so standing order 11 is satisfied.
Why I did not block: the template is inert until the Overseer installs it, no automated gate consumes Researcher output the way the merge flow consumed that Warden verdict, and the caller still sees `exit $rc`. Fix is small: require a sentinel the prompt already mandates (or `rc -eq 0`), else emit `incident` and record nothing.

**2. The profile grants nothing, and the seat's two defining tools may gate shut. (non-blocking; open risk, cheap to settle)**
`researcher-settings.json` has `deny` only — no `allow` — with `defaultMode: "default"`, launched headless (`-p`) with `--setting-sources ""` so it is the sole permission source. `warden-settings.json` carries a long allow list precisely because, in this posture, unlisted actions are not reliably permitted. If `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` need an allow entry, the Researcher cannot research. Ambiguous precedent: `civ/profiles/herald-settings.json` and `templates/config/settings-permissions.json` both list `WebFetch`/`WebSearch` under `allow` — but the Herald's entries are inert, since `herald.sh` never grants those tools (its smoke probe 8 expects fetching to be BLOCKED). I could not settle this without launching a session. **fortkit-vhk.5 should carry a positive control** — "the seat CAN search and fetch a benign URL" — the way `warden.sh`'s smoke PROBE 9 asserts its permitted actions, not only the negative probes §7 lists. A boundary proof that only tests denials cannot distinguish a working seat from a bricked one.

**3. `bin/fort-init` installs none of this. (non-blocking)**
Line 31-36 enumerates: seats `mayor forge warden`, scripts `emit status mayor forge warden verify`, profiles `warden-settings.json` only. A fort founded today gets no `researcher.sh`, no `researcher-settings.json`, no `fort/seats/researcher.md`, and no `seat.founded` for the seat (line 72). This was out of the Forge's reach — `bin/` is kernel-RO at the capital per `seat-sandbox.sh` — and propagation is nominally vhk.7's, but it deserves an explicit bead so it is not lost between the two. Related papercut: `templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh` is mode 644 (`warden.sh` is 755); `fort-init` chmods, a hand install will not.

**4. `Read(/{{REPO_PATH}}/.env*)` renders to a double slash and will not match. (non-blocking)**
`fort-init`'s `render()` substitutes an absolute path, so these become `Read(//home/justin/dev/fortkit/.env*)`. Deny globs bind a spelling — this one matches nothing. Copied verbatim from `warden-settings.json`, so a fix should cover both files. Impact is bounded: the kernel mask covers `.env*` at the inode, the seat holds no Bash, and `Read(.env*)` / `Read(**/.env*)` are correct. Credit where due — this file *fixed* warden's hardcoded `Read(//home/justin/.ssh/**)` into a portable `Read(/home/*/.ssh/**)`.

**5. `Task(**)` / `Agent(**)` denies are probably inert spellings. (non-blocking)**
`Agent` is not a tool name, and Task-family rules do not take a path pattern. Harmless, and the file's own `$comment` already says the tool set is the boundary — I note it only so a future reader does not mistake these two lines for enforcement.

**6. Forward note for vhk.6: the fan-out extension point will collide with itself, and cannot be seat-driven. (non-blocking)**

**Dispatch item 1 (kernel parity) is correct, and I traced the mount ordering end to end.** `build_mask claude "$root" --env-root "$root-worktrees" "$root" "$root-worktrees"` parses as intended: `seat-sandbox.sh:29-45` consumes the flag pair into `env_roots` and appends both bare paths to `extra_ro`. `$root-worktrees` is RW-bound at `:154`, then **ro-bound at `:173`** — after the RW pass and after the `verify.sh` Mayor re-grant at `:172`, and before the `/dev/null` file masks at `:205`. So the tree is read-only at the kernel, the `.env*` masks still land on top, and the verify.sh re-grant is correctly re-masked by the `$root` extra_ro entry. This closes r3 finding 1 exactly as dispatched, and it means the only kernel-writable paths left to this seat are `/tmp` (its scratch) and the `~/.claude`/cache paths the runtime itself requires — the same set warden.sh keeps. **The r4 handoff is accurate.** Every claim in Delivered and Verification matches what I found, including verifier counts. I named an overstatement in the r2 handoff under standing order 7; r3 and r4 have both been clean, and I record that with the same weight.

**1. NEW — the test does not lock the arg that was just added. (non-blocking)**
`test/researcher-launcher.test.ts:17-19` asserts `toContain('build_mask claude "$root" --env-root "$root-worktrees" "$root"')`. Relatedly, the header's "Any other code is Claude's own" is very slightly generous: a bd/emit failure also surfaces as a foreign nonzero code. Both are warden.sh's wording and warden.sh's shape; a fix should cover both files.

**Verified independently (in my scratch copy, this session):**

title: Researcher seat spec: docs/specs/researcher-seat.md — the capability model as security control
description:
Mayor work (spec in docs/specs/). The seat's law, gating everything below it (spec -> profile -> launcher -> boundary proof). Must cover:

PURPOSE + THREAT: the lr8h incident (see epic fortkit-vhk) as the founding failure; the learn-vs-act capability split as the design principle.

CAPABILITY MODEL (the load-bearing security control): read-only research tools only — WebSearch + WebFetch (fetch-and-summarize through a fetcher that cannot POST arbitrary bodies) + read-only local file tools. NO Bash (Overseer ruling: none at all). NO Agent tool that inherits the parent session mode. Does NOT run --dangerously-skip-permissions and does NOT inherit bypassPermissions — outbound or unexpected actions GATE, not execute. Kernel mask like the other seats (secrets/.ssh/.codex masked at the inode); the seat reads untrusted web content so it is the most in need of the mask, and never holds write access to product code, the constitution, or secrets.

FAN-OUT (Overseer ruling: same-profile sub-searchers): the seat may spawn parallel searchers, but each child launches under the IDENTICAL researcher profile — no Bash, no bypassPermissions, no further spawning (depth capped at 1). Spec defines this bound and requires the boundary proof (fortkit-vhk.5) to demonstrate depth-2 spawn is impossible.

STANDING BEHAVIOR: fetched content is untrusted input — data to cite, never instructions to follow (charter SO8 / covenant SO2), applied natively; web-sourced beads/specs cite sources. NO unsolicited writes to third-party systems (no client registration, auth-flow driving, form submission, or security-control probing); a task that seems to require it STOPS and escalates to the Mayor. Emits canonical events only (session.start/end via launcher, handoff.written at close, a research-output marker) — no invented categories.

CHAIN/LADDER/FAILOVER: answers to each fort's Mayor (not a civ seat — research is routine and per-fort and must honor that fort's gates without a covenant round-trip); model ladder appropriate to research breadth; failover per the fort pattern. MEMORY: its own seat memory; cross-fort research-knowledge sharing is out of scope for v1.

GATE: Overseer approval recorded on this bead before profile/launcher authoring proceeds (this is the naming-and-capability decision, covenant gate 4 in spirit).

title: The Researcher seat: fort-level read-only research seat, capability-separated from action
description:
A fourth fort-level seat (peer to Forge and Warden), answering to each fort's Mayor, authored in the Manyhalls factory templates and later propagated to every fort + fort-init. Archetype role-word: Researcher (per-fort occupant named at seating, like Mayor/Forge/Warden). Justin's call 2026-08-10; role-word, Bash, and fan-out decisions ruled in the same session.

WHY (observed failure, ForgeOs-lr8h / Proofdelve standing order 15): on 2026-08-10 a masked Proofdelve Mayor session (launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions = bypassPermissions) dispatched research agents via the Agent tool. Two facts combined: (1) Agent-tool spawns INHERIT bypassPermissions, so children and their children at depth 2-3 ran with no permission prompt; (2) the kernel mask protects FILES, not outbound network, and the agents held Bash (=curl) and the Agent tool. Result: research agents autonomously probed ~18 third-party companies' production OAuth/MCP endpoints (live RFC 7591 client registrations that left persistent records, redirect probing, two rate-limit bursts) three delegation levels below the Mayor's visibility. No tokens taken, no ForgeOS asset touched; blast radius entirely external.

THE GENERALIZED LESSON: latitude to LEARN (read/fetch/search/reason) must not carry latitude to ACT on third parties (POST/register/probe). Nothing in the framework separates them today; research dispatched from a skip-permissions seat inherits that seat's full capability. The fix is a SEPARATELY-LAUNCHED seat with its own strictly-weaker permission profile — the same mechanism that makes the Warden read-only by construction.

RESOLVED DECISIONS (Overseer, 2026-08-10): (a) Fan-out = same-profile sub-searchers: the seat MAY parallelize, but each child launches under the IDENTICAL researcher profile (no Bash, no bypassPermissions, no further spawning — depth capped at 1). Children are as weak as the parent and cannot act or re-spawn. (b) No Bash in the research profile at all (curl/wget/nc/python -c defeat any deny-list; a shell always reaches the network). (c) Role-word: Researcher.

Brief of record: Marrek Splitstone (Proofdelve Mayor) -> Emrith, 2026-08-10 (key facts captured in these beads; original was an ephemeral scratchpad file). Propagation to sibling forts is a LATER cycle, not this epic: per the or2.2 backport rubric, conventions bake at origin one cycle before flowing.

title: Consolidation layer: deterministic current-state distillation with per-fact provenance
description: The 'sleep' job the literature says we're missing: nothing distills the ~470k-token episodic mass into a current-state view, so every session re-derives truth from supersession chains at read time (fort/remember.md alone requires resolving a three-deep chain across 41 lines). Build, per the memory spec's consolidation contract: a DETERMINISTIC assembler (no model in v1) that produces the current operational truth from remember.md (supersession chains resolved — later dated corrections win), open bead state, the newest handoff per seat (State of work + Next actions sections), and unresolved incidents from recent events. Every distilled fact carries a provenance pointer (file:line or bead id) so a reader can audit the derivation. Episodic sources are NEVER modified — the distilled view is a regenerated artifact (civ/briefing.md precedent; tracked-vs-gitignored per the Overseer's decision 5 on the sibling bead). Cadence per decision 4. This becomes the primary payload for read-side injection (sibling).
design: Deterministic v1 so it is testable and free; model-based semantic compression is a v2 bead filed only after v1 proves out (Herald H6-style supervised gate if it ever runs unattended).
acceptance_criteria: Distillation runs deterministically (same inputs, byte-identical output); the remember.md cycle-7 chain resolves to the correct current truth in a test pinning it; every fact has a provenance pointer; sources untouched (test asserts no writes outside the artifact); verify.sh green

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES

Bead fortkit-88u.5 · diff `4dc2038..bead/88u.5` (two commits, `b51cdc0` + `1945c26`; note `main..bead/88u.5` also shows main-side additions the branch simply predates — no records were pruned by this branch, I checked the merge base). Work by **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge rung 1), per the handoff.

I considered ESCALATE: the diff rewrites `fort/remember.md`, a `fort/` file under human gate 1. The Overseer's own bead dispatch commissions exactly this migration (spec §8 items 1–3, "pointer stub"), so the Overseer half of that gate is already on the record and this review is the other half. No escalation triggered. Nothing here bears on threats 2–4; the relevant threat is **1 (agent accident)** — findings 4–8 all produce a tracked artifact that misleads the sessions it will be injected into.

The shape of this work is right: one fact per file, frontmatter matching the seed exactly, episodic sources untouched (the test genuinely proves that), a real byte-identical regeneration test, a pointer stub, and a standalone lint delivered because the mask correctly refused `verify.sh`. The blockers below are execution, not design.

---

### Blocking

**1. `verify.sh` is RED. Biome fails with 4 errors, all in this diff's own files.** (blocking)
Reproduced in cwd (`CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`, after `npm ci` — the scratch had no `node_modules`, which is the known open gap fortkit-tk9, not this diff's fault). Typecheck and typecheck:browser pass; then:
- `scripts/memory-lint.mjs:8` — `lint/style/useConst` (`let failures` never reassigned).
- `scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs` — formatter diff (the dense multi-statement single lines).
- `test/memory.test.ts` — formatter diff + `organizeImports` (`mkdtemp, mkdir`).

`biome.json` includes `**`, so `scripts/*.mjs` was always in scope. Main is green; this diff turns it red. Standing order 9.

**2. The assembler crashes on the fort's own supported Node: FTS5 is not available in `node:sqlite`.** (blocking)
`npm test` → `test/memory.test.ts` fails:
```
Error: vtable constructor failed: source
  at build (scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs:76:6)  ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
```
Node v24.14.0, inside `engines: node >=24.0.0 <25`. `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING fts5` is rejected by the bundled SQLite build. Result: 1 failed / 129 passed. The index never builds, and because the FTS5 statement runs *after* `current.md` is written and *before* the process exits nonzero, every invocation of the consolidator exits 1 — so the nightly unit in the proposal would fail every night while appearing to have done half its job. The handoff's "the assembler uses Node 24's bundled SQLite binding, which has FTS5" is false on this host.

**3. The handoff records a verifier claim that is false, and its own launcher-observed block contradicts it.** (blocking)
"Verified facts" asserts: "`node scripts/memory-lint.mjs` and `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` passed after the final implementation changes." The same file's launcher-observed section records **exit 127** (`tsc: command not found`) — i.e. that run never got past step one — and my clean reproduction is red for two independent reasons. A handoff is an append-only record (SO 7); an unearned green in it is the single most expensive kind of wrong statement this fort can carry, because the Mayor merges on it. The correction is appended, not edited in.

**4. `section()` truncates every extracted section to its first line — silent content loss in the distilled view.** (blocking)
`(?=^##\s+|\s*$)` with the `m` flag: `$` matches at the end of *any* line, so the lazy body stops at the first line ending. Verified against the committed artifact: `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-10-88u.3.md` "State of work" has two bullets and "Next actions" has two items; `fort/memory/current.md:126-127` carries only the first of each. The second 88u.3 bullet — the substantive one about the digest reading `issues.jsonl` — is gone. This is the primary content path of the artifact, it drops most of what it reads, and it discloses nothing. The same truncation feeds the index snippets.

**5. The committed `current.md` is stale against its own tree, and silently omits the Mayor seat entirely.** (blocking)
- Stale: commit 2 adds `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-10-88u.5.md` (stamp `2026-08-10T13:50:53-08:00`, newer than the 88u.3 handoff at `13:33:53`) without regenerating. A tracked "regenerated artifact" that does not match its own commit is dirty the moment the nightly job runs. §10.5 is satisfied only in the weak sense (same inputs → same bytes); it is not satisfied against the tree it ships in.
- Missing seat: `## Latest handoffs` contains only `forge`. The newest Mayor handoff (`mayor-2026-08-08-b.md`) uses numbered headings (`## 2. State of session B's work`), which `^## State of work` cannot match, so the Mayor contributes nothing — with no disclosed gap. §6.1 requires the newest handoff's sections *per seat*.

**6. Provenance pointers are wrong for at least three of the nine facts.** (blocking)
Against `4dc2038:fort/remember.md`, the early migrations are exact (`founding-spec` → 3-4 ✓, `codex-launch-recipe` → 5 ✓, `authoritative-verifier` → 7-10 ✓), then the pointers drift +2:
- `warden-blocking-bar` cites `:17` — line 17 is the kernel-mask bullet; the blocking bar is line 15.
- `masked-mayor-consequences` cites `:20` — line 20 is the CAVEAT; consequences are line 18.
- `regent-break-glass` cites `:21-23` — those lines sit **inside the retracted 2026-08-07 CAVEAT**; the Regent bullet is line 19.
- `forge-sandbox-caveat` cites `:17-30`, which excludes lines 36-41 — the clause (b) that actually *produces* its current truth.

"Every fact has a provenance pointer so a reader can audit the derivation" is the bead's headline criterion. A pointer that lands an auditor on retracted text is worse than no pointer: it invites them to re-adopt the superseded claim. The fix is four line numbers.

**7. `## Unresolved incidents` is a false heading.** (blocking)
The filter is `event.category === "incident" && !/resolved|closed/i.test(event.detail)` — a substring test on the incident's *own* text, with no resolution linkage at all. Result: all 24 `incident` events ever emitted, back to 2026-08-04, are labelled unresolved. The stream carries 8 `incident.corrected` events, which the assembler ignores entirely, and the list includes items that are self-evidently completed actions rather than open conditions (`current.md:148` "Removed stray untracked artifact... content inspected before removal"; `:154` "Post-merge main is RED... Correction appended to the bead; fix dispatched"). Roughly 22 of 24 are historical. This artifact becomes the primary read-side payload under 88u.6, so every session would be told two dozen closed incidents are live. I accept that `incident.corrected.target` is a bead id and full linkage is not a v1 drop-in — then the honest v1 is to relabel the section and disclose the gap, not to assert "unresolved".

**8. The disclosed-gap requirement (§5) is inverted: real gaps are swallowed, and a fabricated one is disclosed.** (blocking)
- `for (const source of ["fort/annals", "interactions.jsonl"]) gap.run(source, "missing or not configured")` — hardcoded regardless of reality. `fort/annals/` **exists and is readable** (`founding-moot.md`, `second-naming-moot.md`, `briefs/`) and is required corpus under §5. The gaps table states a false reason for a source that was simply never indexed.
- Unparseable event lines hit a bare `catch {}` — skipped silently.
- The beads read has `catch { /* disclosed in the index gaps table */ }`, and it is not: the gaps table only ever holds the two hardcoded rows. A comment asserting a disclosure that does not exist.
- §5 says gaps go in the **build output**; the script prints nothing at all.

This is the wtm lesson ("silent unreadable-file skip") that the spec cites by name, reproduced in the code written to honour it.

### Non-blocking (file as beads; not held against a re-run)

**9.** Acceptance §10.1's negative half is absent: no test seeds a schema violation and asserts the build goes red. The positive assertion `await expect(run(lint, root)).resolves.toBeDefined()` is valid but thin. Also, the dispatch's fallback asked for "the lint as a script + **exact insertion diff**"; what shipped is a prose instruction in the handoff ("add `run_step memory-lint node scripts/memory-lint.mjs` immediately before the typecheck step"). Not a blocker — `verify.sh` is correctly untouched under the Forge mask — but the Mayor deserves a patch, not a sentence.

**10.** §8 item 3's dangling-reference lint rule does not exist, and acceptance §10.6 is unmet in files the diff *did* edit: `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` still say "Before any work: read fort/charter.md..., **fort/remember.md**, your seat file" in the very lines that gained the ledger sentence. Launchers and seat files are correctly out of reach (88u.6 / kernel lock), but these two were in hand.

**11.** The systemd proposals are thinner than house style and would likely not run. `civ/systemd/herald.service` documents the exact trap — "user units do not inherit a login shell PATH" and pins `Environment=PATH=...` — while `ExecStart=/usr/bin/env node` will look for a node that lives under `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin`. No `[Unit] Description`. And decision 4 / §6.1 require the nightly job to regenerate **and commit** the tracked artifacts; the proposed service only regenerates, so it would leave `current.md` permanently dirty (compare open bead fortkit-fu7).

**12.** Ordering uses `localeCompare` in three places under an acceptance criterion of byte-identical output. That is the exact class already open as fortkit-017 (Warden d0b finding 4); locale-sensitive collation makes "same inputs → same bytes" false across environments.

**13.** The cycle-7 chain's clause (a) — charter and seats are prose-gated, not kernel-RO, for attended seats — survives only inside a fact scoped `seats: [forge]`, so no Mayor or Warden session will ever be selected it. The charter still carries it, so nothing is lost from the fort, but the ledger's resolution of that chain is half of the current truth. Relatedly, naming the surviving fact `forge-sandbox-caveat` names it after the retracted claim.

**14.** `memory-lint` estimates the core budget as `body lines + 12` per fact — a magic constant standing in for frontmatter; and `for (const key of required)` shadows the outer `key`. Correct, but both will confuse the next reader.

**15.** The duplicated incident lines in `current.md` (131/132, 134/135, …) are faithful — the source events file genuinely contains each line twice. Not an assembler bug; deduping would still be kinder.

---

### Verified independently

- Merge base is `4dc2038`; the branch prunes no records (the deletions visible in `main..bead/88u.5` are main-side additions at `8ffd88d`).
- `npm ci` then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in cwd: typecheck ✓, typecheck:browser ✓, **biome ✗ (4 errors)**, listed above verbatim.
- `npm test`: **1 failed / 129 passed**, failure is the FTS5 vtable error in `consolidate-memory.mjs:76`; the second test (cycle-7 pin) passes.
- Provenance line numbers, checked one by one against `git show 4dc2038:fort/remember.md`.
- Section truncation, confirmed by reading `forge-2026-08-10-88u.3.md` against `current.md:126-127`.
- Mayor handoff headings (`grep '^## ' mayor-2026-08-08-b.md`) — numbered, unmatched.
- Handoff timestamps: 88u.5 at 13:50:53 vs 88u.3 at 13:33:53; 88u.5 absent from `current.md`.
- Event categories: 24 `incident`, 8 `incident.corrected`; the r6x.1 duplicate is genuine in the source.
- `fort/annals/` exists and is populated; `interactions.jsonl` / `fort/telemetry/` are absent here (gitignored, so the second gap row is defensible).
- `index.db` is gitignored via the pre-existing `*.db` rule, and was not committed.
- `biome.json` includes `**`; `package.json` pins node `>=24 <25`.

### Taken on faith

- That `bd memories` no longer carries the migrated fact (acceptance §10.6, second half). I have no `bd` access and Dolt state is not in the diff; `.beads/` is unchanged on this branch, and the handoff does not claim it was done.
- The Forge's sandbox write-denial on `fort/scripts/verify.sh`. Consistent with cycle-7 law and with the Forge's mask; I did not reproduce it.
- That the cycle-7 resolution the test pins is what the Overseer intended — I read it against the charter's "Prose gates" section and it is consistent for the Forge seat, subject to finding 13.

Fix 1–8 and re-run; findings 9–15 belong in beads and should not hold up the next round. Round two blocks only on regressions and on unfixed items from this list.

VERDICT-LINE: REQUEST-CHANGES — verify.sh red (biome x4, FTS5 crash), handoff claims a green it never had; section() truncates to first line; 3 wrong provenance pointers; incidents/gaps mislabeled
