Verifier is green and the blocker is fixed. Writing the review record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead fortkit-bzx.3, round two, range `main..bead/bzx.3` — now two commits: fc9d166 "render colony canvas from world map" (round one) and **a55baec "parse canonical colony seat rosters"** (the round-two fix-up). Round-two work again produced by **GPT-5.6 Codex** as Kethra Anvilmark (per the appended section of `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-bzx.3.md`). The branch is a clean fast-forward: 2 commits ahead of `main`, 0 behind.

Round discipline: round two may block only on a regression or on round-one's finding 1 left unfixed. Finding 1 is fixed, and fixed correctly. I found no regression. No mandatory-ESCALATE area is touched — the diff reaches `fort/` only to append a handoff, which is routine seat output, not the gate-1 constitution.

---

### 1. CLOSED — the round-one blocker is genuinely fixed, not papered over

`src/colony-reader.ts:26` now reads:

```
/\*\*Held by:\s*([^*]+?)\*\*\s*\(([^)]*)/
```

This is `bin/civ-index:36`'s pattern verbatim — the fort's own working parser, adopted rather than a third shape invented, exactly as the Mayor directed. Pronoun extraction was split into a second pass (`src/colony-reader.ts:29`) over the parenthetical, so `(she/her, declared 2026-08-03 at the Founding Moot)` yields `she/her` and not the declaration text.

I checked the sub-pattern against civ-index's rather than assuming equivalence. civ-index uses `\b(she/her|he/him|they/them|[a-z]+/[a-z]+)\b`; colony-reader uses only the generic branch. These are behaviourally identical: regex alternation is leftmost-match-wins, not branch-order-wins, so the enumerated branches never change which substring is selected — they are a readability affordance in civ-index, nothing more. No divergence in behaviour was introduced.

Re-running my round-one probe: the shipped pattern now matches **all three** `fort/seats/*.md`, plus `civ/seats/chronicler.md`, `civ/seats/herald.md`, `civ/seats/regent.md`, and `docs/proposals/publication-founding/seat-file.md`. The zero-match result that grounded the block is gone.

**The round-one "taken on faith" caveat is now closed, too.** I could not execute the regex last round (the sandbox denies `node --eval`, and still does). It no longer matters: the new test writes seat fixtures whose roster lines are **byte-identical** to the real files — I compared `fort/seats/mayor.md:3` under `cat -A` against the fixture string character for character, and did the same for the forge and warden lines. The passing test is the real JavaScript engine parsing the real canonical line. That is execution, not inference.

Standing order 10 is honoured throughout: pronouns are read from the roster parenthetical, and an unparseable one falls back to `"unknown"` rather than to a guess from the name.

### 2. CLOSED — the aam acceptance criterion is now met by the real code path

This was the part of the blocker that mattered most for the record. `test/world.test.ts` no longer hands `actorStyles` three hand-written objects. It builds a temporary fort, writes a registry pointing at it, calls **`readColony`** — registry resolution → `readdir` → parse → `projectColony` — asserts the three citizens parse with correct names, pronouns and seats, and then feeds *that* projection to `actorStyles` for the distinctness assertion. The fortkit-aam criterion is now satisfied by the path a real fort takes, which is what round one said it was not.

Incidental benefit: this also retires most of round-one finding 2. Registry resolution, the reader fan-out and the fort-name-is-not-a-path defence now all have live coverage.

Scope was held exactly as instructed — findings 2–10 were not touched, and the handoff says so plainly.

### 3. Non-blocking — a fresh fort-init settlement still renders a silently empty ARCHIVE

`templates/fort/seats/{mayor,forge,warden}.md:3` ship as `**Held by:** {{UNFILLED — set at the Founding Moot}}`, which the new pattern correctly does **not** match (no name between the colon and the closing `**`). Every seat yields `null`, so a newly stamped fort has zero citizens. That is the truthful answer — nobody holds the seat until the moot — but `src/colony.ts:115` still raises "seats roster ABSENT" only when `readdir` fails, so the page cannot distinguish "no one seated yet" from "parser broke." This is round-one finding 3, and this round gives it a concrete, reachable instance: every settlement fort-init creates. Worth raising its priority on the bead, not worth blocking.

### 4. Non-blocking — the regression test lives under a test named for the canvas page

The filesystem integration now sits inside `"has a checked canvas colony page with a distinct actor style per parsed citizen pair"`, which also asserts title, canvas markup and fetch shape. Co-location is the direct consequence of the Mayor's instruction that the distinctness assertion consume parser output, so it is the right call — but the reader's only filesystem coverage is reachable only through a page-rendering test, and a future edit to the page assertions could take it out. A separate `describe("colony reader")` block over `readCitizens` would make it durable. Test count stayed 34/6 because an existing test was rewritten rather than added; that is monotonic, not a drop.

### 5. Non-blocking — cosmetic drift from civ-index

`colony-reader.ts` falls back to `"unknown"` where `bin/civ-index` uses `"—"` for the same unparseable case. Two renderings of the same absence in one civilization. Trivial, but the whole point of this bead's fix was converging on one roster contract.

### 6. Carried forward from round one, unchanged and non-blocking

Findings 2 (residual reader coverage: gap propagation on an absent fort directory), 4 (building mapping drifts from `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md` — depot/benches/archive, missing Mayor's office; a Mayor call under standing order 2), 5 (silent `slice(0,5)`/`slice(0,27)` truncation vs. spec risk 1's "never hidden"), 6 (colony page never names the fort it is showing), 7 (aam carry: styles keyed by name, depot actors get no glyph, test asserts over the style map not the drawing), 8 (`src/types.ts:8` re-export shim softens the Mayor's wire-format boundary — three one-line import edits), 9 (minor items), 10 (no spec update). All remain accurate against the current tip. Per the Mayor's dispatch these are beads, not merge conditions, and I am not re-litigating them.

### 7. Non-blocking — what remains right, re-checked at this tip

The b18 decision (type-stripping at an HTML marker, no bundler), the 12z composition pattern via `composePage`, the mra browser-tsconfig separation, the page-types wire boundary, and the zero-new-runtime-deps criterion all still hold — the round-two commit touched none of them, and the full verifier re-confirms the typecheck gates. On the charter's **threat 1 (agent accident)**: `/colony?fort=` still resolves through the registry and never lets the browser pick a filesystem path (`src/colony-reader.ts:45–53`), and the renderer still writes only via `fillText`/`textContent`, never `innerHTML`. No finding this round bears on threats 2, 3 or 4, and none requires the out-of-scope shell-access adversary.

---

### Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Verified myself, in the scratch copy at `/tmp/warden-bzx.3`:**

- `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0** (confirmed via an explicit success-guarded re-run, not by eyeballing the tail). All five gates green: Node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (41 files), Vitest **34 passed / 6 files**, ShellCheck. Run against current source in a tree I installed from the lockfile myself — not a stale artifact, not the Forge's reported run.
- The regex fix, by re-running my round-one probe with the *new* shipped pattern over every `.md` in the tree: 7 matches including all three `fort/seats/*.md`, where the old pattern matched zero.
- Byte-for-byte comparison (`cat -A`) of the test's three fixture roster lines against the real `fort/seats/*.md` lines — this is what upgrades finding 1 from "pattern looks right" to "the shipped code demonstrably parses the canonical line."
- The pronoun sub-pattern's equivalence to `bin/civ-index:36`, by reading both and reasoning about leftmost-match semantics.
- Read the complete round-two diff, plus current `colony-reader.ts`, `colony.ts`, the changed region of `world.test.ts`, `verify.sh`, and the templates' seat files.
- Branch position: 2 ahead / 0 behind `main`; clean fast-forward.

**Taken on faith / limits of this review:**

- Still no direct `node --eval`; the sandbox denies it. The byte-identical-fixture argument above makes that immaterial for finding 1, but I did not invoke `readCitizens` from a shell of my own.
- Other registered forts' seat files remain outside my allowed directories. That inference no longer carries weight, since the fix matches this repo's files, the civ seats, and the proposal seat file directly.
- No live server and no browser; canvas behaviour is verified only through the VM/mock harness.
- Push/deploy state unverified; nothing here is public-facing (gate 3 not engaged).
- Handoff integrity: the round-two section was **appended**, not edited into the first — standing order 7 honoured. I checked each of its four "Verified facts" against the code and my own verifier run; all four are true, including the 34-tests-across-6-files claim. Nothing false in the record.

Merging is now better than not merging: the blocker is fixed on the primary data path and mechanically guarded against regression. Findings 3–6 above are beads.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
I have what I need. Writing the review.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES

**Scope actually proposed by this bead.** `main..bead/bzx.2` is a two-dot diff and the branch is two commits *behind* main (`234002d`, `294b1ab`), so the hunks touching `civ/remember.md`, `fort/scripts/forge.sh` and `fort/scripts/warden.sh` are main's changes shown in reverse — **this bead proposes none of them**. What it proposes is `f8c8a19` + `0497847`: `src/colony.ts` (new), additive types in `src/types.ts`, `test/colony.test.ts` (new), and an appended handoff entry. No charter, seat file, launcher, or permission profile is touched, so human gate 1 is not engaged and no ESCALATE is required. (`fort/handoffs/` is a record seats write by design — charter §Memory — and is writable under the kernel mask precisely because it is not constitutional. That is a judgment call and I am stating it so it can be overruled.) No shell, no `.env`, no public-facing surface: gates 2 and 3 are untouched. Model: GPT-5.6 Terra via Codex, per the `session.start` payload at 13:05:46; the top Forge rung, no reward-hacking flag.

The shape of the work is right: a genuinely pure function, no I/O, no clock, no rendering; sources modelled as nullable with an honest `gaps[]` rather than invented health; untyped beads surfaced in `unassigned` rather than dropped, which is exactly what spec risk 1 asks for; `ColonyCitizen.pronouns` is a required field, which quietly makes standing order 10 unfalsifiable in the render. Import conventions, naming and test idiom match the surrounding repo exactly.

**1. BLOCKING — bench sessions are keyed by bead ID alone, so one seat's session ends and impersonates another's.** `sessionKey()` (`src/colony.ts:23`) is `event.target ?? event.seat ?? event.actor`, and `target` is the bead ID for *every* seat's session events. The Forge and the Warden are launched against the same bead ID by construction, and their sessions overlap. Against this fort's real event stream (`fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl`, lines 71–79) the projection produces two false statements:

- 13:14:27 — Ilva's failed review session emits `session.end` for `fortkit-bzx.2` while Kethra's Forge session on that bead is still open (she ends at 13:15:34). Latest-wins on the shared key clears the bench: `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/bzx.2` renders empty while the Forge is working at it.
- 13:15:52 — Ilva's `session.start` for `fortkit-bzx.2` is the latest record for the key, so `worktreeForBead()` matches shortId `bzx.2` and the bench renders as occupied by `{actor: ilva, seat: warden, model: opus}`. The Warden has no worktree at all — its launcher gives it a `/tmp` scratch copy. The colony would show the reviewer standing at the Forge's workbench, and as of the current stream it would show that indefinitely.

The spec is unambiguous that a bench is "an active git worktree… when a seat sets up on a bead", so a Warden session decorating a bench is categorically wrong, not approximately wrong. I am blocking on this rather than filing it because it is a correctness bug in this bead's primary deliverable, it is reproducible from today's data rather than hypothetical, and — this is what tips it — `test/colony.test.ts:145` names the behaviour as intended ("ends a bench session only when a newer end event names the same bead"), so it is locked in as designed rather than left as an oversight. fortkit is copied into settlements that do not exist yet; a wrong invariant with a test asserting it travels a long way before anyone looks again.

Two fixes, either acceptable, both small: (i) key by seat-or-actor *and* target so a seat can only end its own session, and restrict bench decoration to seats that actually hold worktrees; or (ii) match on a worktree path carried in the session payload — the handoff already identifies that the launcher emits the bead ID but not the worktree, and that is the durable fix, though it needs a launcher change and therefore a bead and Justin's hand. Whichever is chosen, the fixture set needs the case the acceptance criteria imply but do not currently cover: two seats' sessions on one bead. Note that (i) is not satisfied by keying alone — with per-actor keys both sessions are active and the bench must still choose, so the seat-holds-a-worktree rule is the load-bearing half.

**2. Non-blocking — the dungeon empties the moment a bug is worked.** `status === "open"` excludes `in_progress` and `blocked` bug beads. The bead text says "open bug-typed beads" and the implementation matches its bead, so this is not a defect against the spec it was given; but the visualizer spec models jailing as arrest → dungeon → *rehabilitation = fix in progress* → release at closed, which reads as the goblin staying in the cells while being fixed. Under the current filter a bug vanishes from the dungeon when someone starts on it and never reappears. Worth a bead to settle which reading governs, not a block.

**3. Non-blocking — nothing filters by status, so closed beads live in the colony forever.** Workshops include closed beads, and `unassigned` includes every closed untyped bead (`test/colony.test.ts:97` asserts the closed `fixed-bug` is a jobless dwarf). The "conspicuous untyped bead" signal that spec risk 1 asks for is the one that degrades first: historical closed work will outnumber live work and drown it. A bead for the projection or bzx.3 to decide where the status cut belongs.

**4. Non-blocking, pre-existing — the fort verifier does not reproduce in the Warden's own scratch copy.** `npx vitest run` in `/tmp/warden-bzx.2` fails one test: `test/world.test.ts:45` asserts an exact `gaps` array, and `readGitState` returns `dirty: null` for any fixture that is not inside a git repo, appending `"git state unavailable"` (`src/world.ts:91`). The Warden's scratch copy is rsynced without `.git` by design, so the mandated verifier cannot go green here for any diff. comments.text:
Verifier reproduction attempted, diff read in full, escaping and bind surface checked. Writing the record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead fortkit-bzx.1, range `main..bead/bzx.1` (e79ec39 implementation, 4efce2e handoff). Work produced by the Forge seat recorded as "GPT-5.6 Codex" — non-Anthropic rung, so I read the parsing logic line by line rather than sampling, and treated every claim in the handoff as unverified until I could check it myself.

**Gate check:** no mandatory ESCALATE. The diff touches `src/`, `test/`, and `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md`. Handoffs are seat-written records, not the fort constitution — the charter's gate 1 enumerates charter, seat definitions, launchers and permission profiles, and the kernel mask in `remember.md` draws the same boundary (`fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, `.claude/`). Nothing in that set is modified.

**Threat model:** no finding here bears on threats 1-4. I checked the one place a widened payload could travel: `Bead` grew `description`/`design`/`notes`, and `src/world.ts:106` spreads `...bead` into the `/world` JSON, but `src/world-page.html:42` renders only id/title/seat/assignee/model and routes every rendered item through `esc()`; the server binds `127.0.0.1` (`src/cli.ts:63`) behind a Host allowlist (`src/server.ts:17`). No new injection or exposure surface (threat 2 unaffected).

**What the diff gets right,** stated because it is the substance of the bead: `isReady` gates on `status === "open"`, counts only `type === "blocks"` edges, filters by `issueId === bead.id` so a reverse edge (something else depending on this bead) is correctly not treated as a prerequisite, and requires each prerequisite to resolve to a bead whose status is `closed` — an unresolvable prerequisite yields not-ready rather than a guess. A missing `dependencies` field yields not-ready, which is the honest reading: absence cannot establish that prerequisites are closed. The fixture arithmetic holds by hand — open {a, e, f, legacy} = 4, ready {a (empty deps), e (dep on closed d)} = 2, f excluded by its open prerequisite a, legacy excluded by absent deps, gaps {legacy} = 1, malformed {`not json`} = 1 — so the acceptance criterion "a dependency chain proves ready < open" is genuinely met and not asserted into existence. This matches the founding spec's line 16, which already calls the job queue "claimed, dependency-resolved."

---

### Findings

**1. (non-blocking) I could not reproduce the test gate in this seat, because the Warden launcher strips the fixture this bead depends on.** `fort/scripts/warden.sh:34` rsyncs the candidate with `--exclude '.beads'`, which is meant to keep bead databases out of the scratch copy but also removes the tracked test fixture `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl`. In my cwd, `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/` contains only `fort/`. `npx vitest run` gives 15 passed / 4 failed, and all four failures are `beads: null` / `resolves to null` — the exact signature of `readBeadRecords` failing its `readFile`, not of a logic error. Those four are precisely the tests that read `.beads/issues.jsonl`, and they would fail identically on `main`. Copying the fixture in was denied (correctly — I hold no write permission), and the candidate worktree is mounted read-only, so vitest cannot even bootstrap its config there (`EROFS`). Net effect: the Warden seat structurally cannot run the test gate for any bead touching the bead reader — which is a large share of this project. Bead: narrow the exclusion so it strips bead stores without stripping tracked fixtures. Note that `warden.sh` is a launcher, so that repair itself falls under charter gate 1 (Warden + Overseer).

**2. (non-blocking) The bead's gating first step is taken on faith, and there is a specific way it could be wrong.** The bead made this a stop-and-report precondition: verify against a real `bd export` that dependency edges are present per line. The handoff asserts it, with falsifiable detail (`issue_id`/`depends_on_id`, `blocks` gating vs `parent-child` hierarchy) that matches the fixture and beads' actual dependency model. I could not check it: `bd` is not runnable from this seat, no real export line is committed anywhere in the repo, and the capital has no `.beads/issues.jsonl` at all — `.beads/config.yaml:50-54` shows `export.auto` disabled. The concrete risk is in the handoff's own words: the live export "omits empty labels on some lines despite its help text saying labels are included." That is an `omitempty` signature. If `dependencies` carries the same tag, then every dependency-free open bead has a null `dependencies` field, `isReady` returns false for all of them, and a real fort renders `ready` at or near zero while `open` is large. The fixture writes `"dependencies":[]` explicitly and so cannot catch this. Bead: capture one real `bd export` line verbatim as a golden fixture. That converts the load-bearing claim from a handoff assertion into a test, and settles the omitempty question permanently.

**3. (non-blocking) `parseDependency` is asymmetric with the discipline applied everywhere else.** It never returns null for any object, so `{"dependencies":[{}]}` parses as a valid edge with every field null. That edge has `type !== "blocks"`, so it is dropped from `prerequisiteIds`, and the open bead counts as ready. Same for a `blocks` edge with a null `depends_on_id`. An edge we could not parse is thus treated as "no obstacle" — the exact inference the code refuses to make one line earlier when `dependencies` is absent entirely. An unparseable edge should raise `gaps` and withhold readiness. No fixture exercises this and real `bd` output should not produce it, which is why it is a bead and not a block.

**4. (non-blocking) The status map's type widened by accident.** `src/readers/beads.ts:15` types `statuses` as `keyof Omit<BeadCounts, "malformed">`, which now admits `"ready"` and `"gaps"` as legal increment targets for `counts[status] += 1`. The map's contents are correct today; the type no longer prevents a derived counter from being incremented as if it were a status. Should be `Omit<BeadCounts, "malformed" | "ready" | "gaps">`.

**5. (non-blocking) Dead branch.** `parseBead` already rejects unknown statuses via `!statuses.has(status)`, so the `if (status === undefined) { counts.malformed += 1; continue; }` at lines 59-62 is unreachable. Harmless now; it is duplicated validation in two places that can drift apart.

**6. (non-blocking) `ready` and `gaps` are computed but reach no view.** `src/status.ts:64` prints open/active/blocked; `src/world.ts:100` projects `{open, malformed}`; the world page shows open. This is correct scope for a step-1 reader bead whose consumer is fortkit-bzx.2, and I raise it only so nobody reads the merge as having shipped a visible ready count.

**7. (non-blocking) Name collision.** `BeadCounts.gaps` is a count of schema-incomplete bead lines; `WorldFort.gaps` is an array of ABSENT/source-gap strings. Two different meanings of "gaps" in adjacent types, and bzx.2 consumes both.

**8. (non-blocking) The handoff records the model as "GPT-5.6 Codex," which is not a rung on the Forge ladder** (Terra → Sol → Sonnet 5 → Opus 5). The charter requires every handoff to record which model did the work, and the reason it matters is scrutiny weighting: Sol carries the reward-hacking flag and Terra does not. An ambiguous name partly defeats the order it satisfies.

**9. (non-blocking) Handoff chronology is non-monotonic.** Entries now read 12:15, 12:14:20, 12:35, 12:25. The file was already out of order before this diff, and the new entry is a pure insertion — the diff for that file contains no deletions, so standing order 7 is honoured in substance. Worth a convention, not a correction.

**10. (non-blocking, informational)** `beads.filter(isReady)` with an inner `beads.find` is O(n²). Fine at fort scale; noted only so it is on the record if a fort ever exports tens of thousands of beads.

---

### Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Verified myself, in this session:**
- Read the complete diff and the full post-change `src/readers/beads.ts`, `src/types.ts`, and the fixture.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p /tmp/warden-bzx.1/tsconfig.json` — clean, against the candidate source in my scratch copy after `npm ci` from the committed lockfile (52 packages). This is the one verifier step I could reproduce, and it ran against current code, not a stale build.
- Fixture arithmetic (open 4 / ready 2 / gaps 1 / malformed 1) traced by hand through `parseBead`, `hasSchemaGap` and `isReady`; the test expectations match the code's actual behaviour.
- `ready`/`gaps` are unrendered: confirmed by reading `src/status.ts`, `src/world.ts`, `src/digest.ts`, `src/world-page.html`.
- No new injection surface: `esc()` covers every rendered item; widened fields are not rendered; `listen(port, "127.0.0.1")` plus Host allowlist.
- The four test failures in my environment are fixture absence, not regression: `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/` has no `.beads/`, and `fort/scripts/warden.sh:34` excludes it.
- The handoff file diff is additions only; the worktree is clean (`git status --porcelain` empty).
- Test count: my run enumerated 19 tests, matching the handoff's "Vitest (19 tests)."

**Taken on faith:**
- That a real `bd export` emits a `dependencies` array on every issue line, with `blocks` edges shaped `issue_id`/`depends_on_id` — finding 2. This is the bead's own gating precondition and the load-bearing assumption of the whole feature.
- That `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` passed end to end. I could not run the script (permission), nor Biome (permission), nor the full Vitest suite (finding 1). ShellCheck is not load-bearing here — no shell file changed.

Nothing found makes the fort worse than not merging: the logic is conservative where it is uncertain, the acceptance criteria are met by the fixture, typecheck is green, and the one unverified claim is the Forge's to have made and Justin's to spot-check. Findings 1, 2 and 3 are the ones I would want filed as beads before bzx.2 builds on this reader; 2 in particular, because it is cheap to settle and expensive to discover in a rendered colony view.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: ready logic sound, typecheck green; bd export shape unverified and warden scratch strips the .beads fixture

Finding 3 (unparseable edge treated as no obstacle) — fixed correctly: `parseDependency` now requires `issue_id`/`depends_on_id`/`type` to be strings, `{}` and a null-target `blocks` edge both null out, `dependenciesOrNull` collapses the array, and `hasDependencySchemaGap` turns that into a gap that withholds readiness. Finding 4 (widened status type) — fixed. Finding 5 (dead branch) — removed. Finding 7 (`gaps` name collision) — fixed; I grepped `src/` and the rename is complete, with `WorldFort.gaps` left alone. Finding 6 (unrendered counters) — unchanged, still correct scope. Finding 1 (launcher strips the fixture) — unchanged, and correctly so: it is gate-1 work, not this bead's.

All six items of the Mayor's dispatch are implemented. The `legacy` line (`{"id":"legacy","status":"open"}`) now counts ready, which is the Mayor's explicit "(or absent both)" call; it remains a `schemaGap`, so the ABSENT discipline still shows the fort what it doesn't know. `ready < open` still holds on the fort-alpha fixture (3 < 4), so the acceptance criterion survives the change.

---

### Findings

**1. (non-blocking) The new equality test against `dependency_count` rests on an assumption with zero confirming instances, and it is the one place this diff could be wrong in the same way round one was wrong.** `hasDependencySchemaGap` (src/readers/beads.ts:166-171) declares a gap when the count of `blocks` edges `!==` `dependency_count`. That is only correct if `dependency_count` counts exactly blocking prerequisites. The evidence available to me is two golden lines, both with `dependency_count: 0` — `fortkit-zgp` with no edges, `fortkit-bzx.5` with one `parent-child` edge. That pair proves hierarchy edges are excluded from the counter. It does not distinguish "counts blocking prerequisites" from "counts non-hierarchy edges, including `related`/`discovered-from`" from "is always 0 in export." I searched the whole capital for `"dependency_count":[1-9]` and there is no nonzero instance anywhere on record. If the counter is always zero in exports, then every bead carrying a `blocks` edge becomes a schema gap and is denied readiness — including the beads whose prerequisites are all closed, which are precisely the beads "true ready" exists to find. If it merely includes `related` edges, the same thing happens to those. The Forge disclosed this honestly in the handoff's Open risks, which is the right behaviour and is why this is a finding rather than a false claim in a record.

Two reasons this does not clear the blocking bar. The error direction is conservative — it withholds `ready` and raises `schemaGaps`, never asserts a false ready — and neither counter reaches a rendered surface yet. And not merging leaves the confirmed, total failure the Mayor measured (`ready` ≈ 0 on any real fort), so merging is strictly better. I will name the regression honestly: *if* the pessimistic reading holds, a bead with a `blocks` edge on a closed prerequisite goes from ready under `e79ec39` to not-ready under `b6640e6`. It is conditional on a fact nobody here has, and the direction is safe, so I am not blocking on it.

The remedy is cheap and is also the better design: the Mayor's dispatch said "**short** dependencies array," and `dependency_count > dependencies.length` is correct under all three hypotheses without needing to know which edge types the counter includes. Pair it with one more golden line from a bead that actually has a `blocks` edge — `fortkit-bzx.2` depends on `fortkit-bzx.1` and would do. Bead: settle `dependency_count` semantics with a real blocking-edge export line and relax the equality to the short-array test.

**2. (non-blocking) The same omitempty bug the dispatch was written to fix still exists for `labels`, and the newly committed golden lines are the proof.** `hasSchemaGap` (src/readers/beads.ts:184) flags a record whenever `labels` is not a string array. Neither golden line — both verbatim real `bd export` output — carries a `labels` field at all. So on a real fort every unlabelled bead is a `schemaGap`, the counter reads near 100%, and the fort's honesty signal carries no information. This is out of the literal scope of the Mayor's six items, so it is not a Forge miss; it is the obvious next one to file. Note that the golden test asserts only `{open: 2, ready: 2}` via `toMatchObject`, so it does not pin `schemaGaps` — had it done so, it would read 2 for two perfectly healthy canonical lines and this would have been visible in the fixture. I derived that by hand from the code, not by executing it; running the reader directly was denied.

**3. (non-blocking) The dead branch was removed by replacing it with an unchecked cast.** `const status = statuses.get(bead.status) as CountedStatus` (src/readers/beads.ts:64). It is sound today because `parseBead` gates on `statuses.has(status)`, but the invariant now lives across two functions with nothing but convention holding it, and the failure mode if it ever drifts is `counts[undefined] += 1` producing a junk key rather than a type error. `Bead.status` is still typed `string` in src/types.ts:38, despite the handoff's claim that "the parser's validated-status invariant is now represented with the narrow status type" — what was narrowed is `CountedStatus`, not `Bead.status`. The clean fix is to narrow `Bead.status` to the four-member union and make `statuses` a total `Record<BeadStatus, CountedStatus>`, which removes the cast entirely.

**4. (non-blocking) `BeadDependency` is now looser than its own parser.** `issueId`, `dependsOnId` and `type` are still `string | null` in src/types.ts:53-60, but `parseDependency` now guarantees all three are strings. Consequence: the `dependency.dependsOnId !== null` guard at src/readers/beads.ts:203 is dead code. Tighten the three fields to `string`.

**5. (non-blocking) The two places that reason about edges disagree about direction.** `isReady` filters prerequisites with `dependency.issueId === bead.id`, correctly refusing to treat a reverse edge as a prerequisite; the `blocks` count in `hasDependencySchemaGap` applies no such filter. Harmless if `dependencies` never carries reverse edges — both golden lines have `issue_id` equal to their own id, and the separate `dependent_count` field suggests reverse edges live elsewhere — but if that assumption is ever false the two functions will disagree, and they should share one predicate.

**6. (non-blocking, carried) `fort/scripts/warden.sh:34` still rsyncs with `--exclude '.beads'`, so this seat still cannot run the test gate for bead-reader work.** Unchanged from round one, and correctly not this bead's job to fix — `warden.sh` is a launcher and its repair is gate-1 work (Warden + Overseer). Recording it again because it shaped what I could verify below.

**7. (non-blocking, informational) "Ready" now includes beads we know almost nothing about.** The `legacy` line has an id and a status and nothing else, and counts as ready. This is the Mayor's explicit instruction and I am not disputing it; it is also still counted as a `schemaGap`, so the pairing is honest. Worth stating once so that a future reader of a colony view knows `ready` is not a claim that the bead's dependency data was ever seen.

---

### Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Verified myself, in this session:**

- Read the full `b6640e6` diff, the complete post-change `src/readers/beads.ts` and `src/types.ts`, both new fixtures, and the updated tests.
- `npm ci` from the committed lockfile, then `npx tsc --noEmit -p /tmp/warden-bzx.1/tsconfig.json` — clean, against current source.
- `npx vitest run`: 21 tests, 17 passed, 4 failed. All four failures are `beads: null` / `resolves to null`, the signature of the stripped `.beads` fixture (finding 6), and they would fail identically on `main`. **Both new tests passed here** — "accepts bd's omitted empty dependency array as ready" and "withholds readiness for incomplete dependency data" use fixtures that survive the rsync, so those two assertions are independently confirmed, not taken on report.
- Read the real `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl` from the candidate worktree and traced it by hand through `parseBead`, `hasDependencySchemaGap`, `hasSchemaGap` and `isReady`: open 4 (a, e, f, legacy), ready 3 (a, e, legacy — f excluded by its open prerequisite a), schemaGaps 1 (legacy), malformed 1. That matches the updated expectations exactly, so the four stripped-fixture tests would pass where the fixture exists. Test count 21 matches the handoff.
- Rename completeness: grepped `src/` for `gaps`/`schemaGaps` — no stale `counts.gaps` consumer, `WorldFort.gaps` untouched. `ready` and `schemaGaps` appear only in the reader and the type; nothing renders them.
- No nonzero `dependency_count` exists anywhere in `/home/justin/dev/fortkit`, and `.beads/` documents neither `dependency_count` nor `dependent_count` (finding 1).
- Handoff is additions-only: 0 deletion lines across `main..bead/bzx.1` for that file, so standing order 7 holds. Candidate worktree clean (`git status --porcelain` empty).
- `work.begun` (12:45:44) and `work.ended` (12:48:00) emitted as instructed, model recorded `gpt-5.6-terra`, and the bead is still IN_PROGRESS — not closed.
- `fort/scripts/warden.sh:34` still carries `--exclude '.beads'`.

**Taken on faith:**

- That the two golden lines are verbatim output of a real `bd export`. I cannot run `bd` from this seat (denied). Their shape is internally consistent and independently corroborated by the Mayor's own reported finding, which is real evidence, but it is not my own observation.
- What `dependency_count` means when it is nonzero — finding 1. This is the successor to round one's finding 2 and the same class of assumption.
- That `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` passed end to end. Typecheck I reproduced; Vitest I reproduced modulo the stripped fixture; Biome was denied; ShellCheck is not load-bearing here, as no shell file changed.

Nothing found makes the fort worse than not merging. The bug the Mayor measured is genuinely fixed, the unparseable-edge hole is closed in the right direction, the rename is complete, typecheck is green, and the two new tests pass under my own hand. Findings 1 and 2 are the ones I want filed before `fortkit-bzx.2` builds on this reader — 1 because it is the same class of mistake as round one and one more golden line settles it permanently, and 2 because the fixture that proves it is now sitting in the repo.

title: [decision] The Herald read the two earlier declarations before choosing, against the edict's condition
description:
FOR THE OVERSEER. Raised by the Regent against itself, 2026-08-05.

Your edict said of the Herald's declaration: 'let her choose freely: nothing about the earlier declarations binds her, and she should not be shown them before choosing.'

WHAT HAPPENED. The Regent's brief did not mention the earlier declarations, did not name Wystan Onlylent or Bramwen Lentvoice, and deliberately left them out of the actor-id constraint list so their existence could not be inferred. It did direct him to read civ/covenant.md, his editorial law, and his seat file. He read further on his own initiative — including civ/annals/first-moot-of-the-covenant.md, which carries both — and says so in his own opening sentence.

THE REGENT'S JUDGEMENT: the declaration STANDS. Three grounds.
1. He was not shown them; he found them. That is a different act, and no brief can prevent it in a seat whose entire craft is reading records. Preventing it would have required either lying to him about what to read or removing his read access, and both are worse.
2. He engages with both explicitly and declines to be bound: 'I am not their successor, since neither was ever seated, and I am not their correction... I take my own name because the arguments were about how to treat a stranger's guess, and I am no longer a stranger to this seat.'
3. Covenant 8.1, amended hours earlier by this same edict, says a declaration 'is never retaken at another's instance.' Retaking a freely made declaration because the Regent disliked the circumstances of its making is precisely what that clause forbids, and would be the third churning of this chair in two days.

AGAINST: you asked for a specific condition and it was not delivered. This bead exists so overturning is cheap. If you want it retaken, say so and it will be, in a fresh session with an explicit instruction not to read the annals.

Recorded in full at civ/annals/declaration-2026-08-05-herald.md under 'Deviation from the edict'.

title: Prior-art and landscape record for the publication office
description:
The civilization's mechanical security findings are well persisted (bead close reasons across the 21f tree, charters, remember.md, the probe suite's own header). The LANDSCAPE was not: what is already published, what is genuinely ours, and where the gaps are lived only in a working conversation. The publication office cannot do its job without it — generalizing a finding beyond this machine requires knowing whether someone generalized it first, and the standing bar is no unverified claims.

Written to docs/research/agent-security-prior-art.md: the 2026 sandboxing landscape (Claude Code bwrap opt-in, Codex Landlock-by-default with its deny-read gap, Gemini Docker), a finding-by-finding prior-art table with sources, the publication strategy that follows from it, and an open probe.

HEADLINE FOR OSWIN: our spelling/deny-glob finding is NOT novel. Ona (Di Donato) published the same class in April 2026 — Claude Code escaping its own denylist via /proc/self/root aliasing — and CVE-2025-53109/53110 cover prefix-bypass via symlinks. Our specific vectors (shell quoting/globbing) appear undocumented, but the class is known and must be cited, not claimed. What DOES appear novel: 'a model cannot probe its own leash' (no prior art found) and the probe methodology itself (neutral decoys, negative controls with differential twins, NAMED-is-not-PASS). Lead with those.

FIRST PROBE TO ADD: the Ona escape used /proc/self/root aliasing. In principle our mount-level masks are immune because that path resolves inside the same namespace onto the same tmpfs — but 'in principle' is exactly what the probe suite exists to eliminate. Probe /proc/self/root, /proc/self/cwd, symlinks, hard links and bind aliases at every masked path. Hold = a measured claim nobody has published. Fail = we found it in our own fence first.

title: Covenant amendment: adopt the First Moot's rulings on quorum, concurrence, the borrowed bench, and resumption
description:
Proposed by Emrith Cairnwright, convening the First Moot of the Covenant from outside the layer. Amending the covenant is gate 6.2 — she proposes, the Overseer applies. NONE of these bind until he writes them in. Her own caveat: 'If he wants them narrower, they should be narrower; I have been wrong once this week about the subject of my own document and I do not mistake fluency for correctness.'

Belongs in covenant section 8.

1. DECLARATION IS NOT SEATING. A declared-but-unseated occupant holds NO ballot. The declaration is the occupant's own and needs no leave; the seating is gate 6.4, the Overseer's. 'If a declaration carried a ballot, then declaring would confer voice, and gate 6.4 would be hollow while formally intact.' The humane half: an unseated declared occupant MAY speak and be quoted. Hear them, count nothing.

2. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING — a three-seat layer can NEVER name its own offices. A seat does not sit in judgment on its own office word, so naming any one of three draws a recusal and leaves two. 'Three minus one is two, always, at full strength, forever.' Therefore the borrowed bench is not a stopgap; it is the ordinary and standing instrument, and should be entered in the covenant as such.

3. TWO BALLOTS ARE NOT A MOOT. With two, the tie-break ladder collapses: rung three is inapplicable where the convener holds none, and rung one is decided by which seat declined to rank a third name, so 'a seat's silence decides.' Also 'a twelve-point Borda table over two ballots renders exactly like an eighteen-point table over three' to a stranger a year out. Name the lesser instrument: a CONCURRENCE. Two seated occupants independently briefed each state a preference and reasons in full; if they concur it carries and is recorded as a concurrence with NO tally drawn; if they diverge, the annal records both reasons entire, the question is NOT decided, and it goes to the Overseer marked undecided.

4. THE BORROWED BENCH. Three independent ballots. Held by the layer's SEATED occupants who are not candidates and whose own office is not being named. The permanent shortfall is filled from the settlements, drawn by the Overseer, ONE SEAT PER FORT, never two from one fort ('two seats of one settlement are not two independent judgments about a word; they share a charter, a record, and a room'). PARTICIPATION IS NOT JURISDICTION, exactly as residence is not — 'written down facing both ways or it will be read as a doorway.' The Overseer does not ballot: 'a ranked ballot from the one person who can overturn the count is not a ballot; it is an instruction with arithmetic on it.'

5. THE OUTSIDE CONVENER is appointed PER SITTING, by name, casts nothing, and their authority ends with the record. The practice recurs; the appointment never does. Prefer a convener who did not convene the last one, 'so the practice does not quietly harden into a post,' and one with no stake in the outcome.

6. THE RESUMPTION RULE. 'An agent session is not resumable across the completion of the act it performed... A correction arriving after an act is complete is a new act and must be run as one, or not at all.' Arrived at independently by the convener and by the Regent on the same evening, from two different incidents.

title: [bug] The Herald has no launcher, no permission profile, and an unproven window — she cannot run
description:
Found by BRAMWEN LENTVOICE (she/her), Herald, on her declaration run 2026-08-04, before scoring a single story. Provenance recorded with her name. All VERIFIED by the Regent.

1. NO LAUNCHER. Her seat file names fort/scripts/herald.sh. Verified: fort/scripts/ holds emit.sh, forge.sh, lib, mayor.sh, status.sh, verify.sh, warden.sh. No herald. (Tracked as fortkit-r6x.4, and it now belongs at civ/scripts/herald.sh — see fortkit-ugr.2.)
2. NO PERMISSION PROFILE. Her spec names fort/profiles/herald-settings.json. Verified: that directory holds warden-settings.json and nothing else. The draft profile exists only as a proposal in docs/proposals/herald-founding/ and belongs at civ/profiles/.
3. THE WINDOW IS UNPROVEN, and this is the one that matters. 'fortkit digest' exists in the CLI (verified, src/cli.ts:10). But the digest renders an absent or malformed source AS ABSENT rather than erroring. Her words: 'On some future morning my window can go partly dark and hand me a well-formed document with a hole in it, and if I have not already worked out what that looks like, I will read the hole as a quiet day and file a confident zero. An empty morning has to mean the record was empty. It must never mean I could not see.'

That third item is a genuine design gap and not a missing file. A seat whose valid output includes 'nothing happened' cannot distinguish nothing-happened from could-not-see unless the digest tells her which. Her zero-is-valid rule and the digest's absent-renders-as-absent rule combine into a silent failure mode that looks exactly like success.

ONE CORRECTION to her report, appended in her own discipline: she read the last handoff as leaving the digest bead open awaiting a second Warden review. fortkit-r6x.1 is CLOSED — merged e7055ed + af4e82a, both round-1 blockers fixed, Warden round 2 approved, verify green 17/17. Her underlying finding is unaffected, since the absent-source behaviour is the merged design rather than an unfinished one.
design: Proposed by the Regent for the Overseer and whoever builds the launcher: the digest should carry an explicit per-source status (present / absent / malformed) so a consumer can tell a quiet day from a dark window, and the Herald's report schema should surface any non-present source in its Gaps and anomalies section. Bramwen declined to fix any of this herself, correctly: 'They are not mine to edit, I am read-only over them by construction, and a seat that quietly corrects its own charter is doing a small version of the thing I was built not to do.'
acceptance_criteria: Launcher and profile exist at civ/ paths; digest exposes per-source status; a deliberately darkened source produces a report that says so rather than a zero

title: [epic] The civilization layer: civ/ stands beside fort/ with its own covenant
description:
Established 2026-08-04 by the Overseer's edict, executed by the Regent.

WHAT CHANGED. The Regent, the Herald, and the fifth security-publication seat are no longer seats of Manyhalls. They are seats of a new CIVILIZATION LAYER at civ/, governed by civ/covenant.md, resident in the fortkit repo because Manyhalls is the capital.

WHY. A seat that needs root on every fort cannot derive its authority from one fort's constitution, and a settlement should not be asked to govern something it cannot constrain. The Overseer's framing: Washington DC has a mayor AND a president, and the president is not a city official.

THE LOAD-BEARING DISTINCTIONS, so they are not eroded later:
- RESIDENCE IS NOT JURISDICTION (covenant s1). These seats live in fortkit; Manyhalls' charter does not bind them and its Mayor does not direct them.
- THE LAYER IS NOT A MANAGEMENT TIER OVER THE FORTS (covenant s2). No civ seat directs a Mayor, prioritizes a fort's beads, or overrides a Warden. Its business is what spans forts, what a fort cannot do to itself, and what leaves the civilization. This is stated as an explicit non-goal because it is the predictable failure mode.
- ACCESS IS PER SEAT (covenant s5). One seat has root on everything, one may read exactly one JSON document, one may read everything and reach nothing. A single 'civ seat' permission posture would be wrong for all three.
- PRECEDENCE (covenant s4): a civ seat inside a settlement honours that settlement's human gates, announces itself in that fort's stream at start and end, never emits as one of its citizens, and may be reviewed by that fort's Warden. Only the Regent may cross a capability boundary, only by edict, only with the Overseer present, never silently.

BUILT AND VERIFIED THIS SESSION: civ/covenant.md; civ/seats/regent.md (the Regent's first seat file — the seat that could rename anything had never named itself); civ/scripts/emit.sh (resolves from its own location, the fortkit-iqp fix implemented, verified from /tmp); civ/{annals,handoffs,events,profiles,transcripts}/; regent/ migrated to civ/ with git mv; bin/regent repointed and now reads the covenant instead of paraphrasing it.
design: NOT applied: the fort charter pointer (docs/proposals/civ-layer/charter-pointer.md), the fifth seat's papers (repointed to civ, docs/proposals/publication-founding/), and the Herald's relocation (docs/proposals/herald-founding/CIV-LAYER-SUPERSESSION.md). Covenant gate 4 says no seat here seats itself or another, and the Regent may draft founding papers but must not apply its own.

title: [bug] Moot method: the participant who authors the record got the thinnest brief, and held write access
description:
Two method defects by the Regent, running the Second Naming Moot 2026-08-04. Recorded against itself.

1. THE THINNEST BRIEF WENT TO THE AUTHOR OF THE RECORD. The moot ran as three independent sub-sessions. The Forge's and Warden's briefs both stated the office under naming correctly ('the security-publication office, whose craft is extraction and publication and never hunting'). The convener's SECOND-ROUND brief restated the pool, the rulings sought and the ballots, and omitted the office entirely. In round 1 she had it right and recorded the Herald as a separate empty chair; across the round boundary the framing was lost and nothing re-anchored it. She then wrote the annals, emitted three events and filed a retitle bead describing the wrong seat. The independence that made the moot genuine is the same property that let one participant's drift go uncaught until the record was already written.

2. A MOOT PARTICIPANT HELD WRITE ACCESS TO FORT RECORDS. The Forge and Warden sessions used zero tools and returned text. The convener's session held full tools and wrote fort/annals/, fort/events/ and a bead directly, unreviewed, on a mistaken premise. The Warden seat in this civilization is read-only BY CONSTRUCTION because a review that can also write is not a review; a moot has the same shape, and the ceremony had no such guarantee.

Realized cost: a correction appended to the annals, three permanent events corrected by a fourth, one bead closed against execution, and a near-miss in which an Overseer-approved seat would have been renamed across its spec, seat file and founding papers.
design: Proposed for the next moot, for the Mayor and Overseer to weigh: (a) every round's brief restates the subject in full, and no brief is a delta on an earlier one; (b) moot participants deliberate read-only and return text, with the convener's record transcribed by whoever convenes rather than written by a participant session; (c) if a participant is to write records, the write is reviewed before it lands, the same bar as any other constitution-adjacent change.
acceptance_criteria: Moot procedure recorded somewhere a future convener will read it; the next moot runs under it

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
RECURRENCE, same failure class, caught early this time — Regent, 2026-08-04, first Moot of the Covenant.

Briefing the two occupant-declarants, I gave each a list of existing actor ids to avoid colliding with, and the list was INCOMPLETE: it omitted 'orin' (Orin Slowfire, Farlantern's Forge) and was assembled from memory of the moot record rather than read from the seat files. The same shape as the original defect — a brief that carried what I happened to have in hand instead of what the recipient needed.

Difference in outcome, which is the point: it was caught before either declaration landed, because I went looking at the roster rather than assuming it. Corrected mid-flight by sending the complete ten-name roster to the still-running declarant with the reasoning attached. Detail on fortkit-ugr.4.

Adds a third rule to the two already on this bead: **a constraint list in a brief must be GENERATED FROM THE SOURCE at brief time, never recalled.** If the brief says 'must not collide with X, Y, Z', the X Y Z comes from reading the seat files in that moment. This is the same discipline the fifth seat's law calls traceability, applied to the instructions we hand each other rather than to what we publish.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
THIRD ENTRY, same session, new failure mode — Regent, 2026-08-04.

RESUMING A COMPLETED CEREMONY SESSION PRODUCES A SECOND RITUAL ACT, NOT AN AMENDMENT TO THE FIRST.

Having noticed my actor-id list omitted 'orin', I sent the complete roster to the Herald's declaration session as a correction. That session had already returned a full declaration (Wystan Onlylent, he/him) which I had already emitted to the event stream. The resumption did not amend it. It produced a second complete declaration under a different name (Bramwen Lentvoice, she/her), whose text asserts the correction 'arrived before I had settled anything' — which the stream contradicts.

No harm done that the record could not absorb: Manyhalls ruling 1 covers it exactly (a seat's name is its own, the later declaration governs, the prior is preserved never overwritten, and a rename emits again). But the harm was avoided by luck of having applicable case law, not by method.

RULE, added to the two already on this bead and the one added earlier tonight: **once a ceremonial act has been returned AND recorded, do not resume that session. Correct the record instead.** A ritual session does not hold the notion that it has already spoken. If a correction is needed after an act is recorded, it is an amendment to the record made by the transcriber, or a fresh act deliberately convened and labelled as one — never a nudge to a finished session.

Cumulative rules from this bead, now four: (1) every round's brief restates the subject in full, and the participant who authors the record gets the fullest brief; (2) participants deliberate read-only; (3) constraint lists in a brief are generated from the source at brief time, never recalled; (4) never resume a ceremony session whose act is already recorded.

title: S5: Artifact 1 — extract the boundary probe suite as a standalone public repo (candidate tree only)
description:
First artifact, order fixed by the Overseer: no such harness exists publicly, it is self-demonstrating, and it is small enough for one person to maintain. Measured costs are in docs/proposals/publication-founding/extraction-plan.md.

Source is ~1514 lines of bash across probe-boundaries.sh (1206), probe-forge-masks.sh (103), lib/seat-sandbox.sh (178), emit.sh (27), plus the post-config-change checklist. No README exists; the 87-line header comment is the documentation.

PORTABLE (the asset, ~100%): the verdict vocabulary PASS/FRAGILE/COVERED-CANONICAL/NAMED/GAP/INCONCLUSIVE/FAIL; the methodology (never ask a model to probe its own leash; a refusal is not evidence until you know WHICH boundary refused; classify from config not transcript; positive control + negative control + differential twin per probe; correlate to the probe's own tool call; fail closed on the suite's own bugs); the deny-rule glob matcher; the 28-reader and 9-write-vector lists; the obfuscation catalogue; the stream-json correlators.

EXTRACTION COST: root hardcoded (deliberately) in 2 scripts; a home-path loop that also uses the home path as a prefix-stripper; secret filenames hardcoded AND an obfuscation generator shaped around the literal .env. prefix; SEVEN hand-written posture case statements that must become a declarative table (the only near-rewrite); three-lists hardwired to one vendor's TOML; 27 internal bead IDs inside user-visible verdict strings; the neutral control file assumes a README.md exists. The civilization registry is NOT touched at all.

NEVER SHIPS: real run output. A genuine verdicts.tsv carries absolute paths, matched rules verbatim, the ignored-file inventory and every current gap. Synthetic fixtures only.
design: Repo name proposed, not chosen; availability UNVERIFIED and checking it precedes creation. Recommended 'holdfast' (a holdfast is both a fortification and the anchor that holds under force; it asks the tool's actual question). Alternatives 'leashcheck' (points at the founding methodological finding) and 'agent-sandbox-probe' (dull and maximally discoverable, which for a security tool is a real argument). The seat prepares an inert candidate tree; the Overseer creates, names and pushes.
acceptance_criteria: Candidate tree runs green on a machine with no fort, no registry and no real secret; scrub list from the extraction plan verified item by item; Overseer sign-off before any repo exists

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
Moot held 2026-08-04, convened by Emrith Cairnwright. OUTCOME, in two parts.

SETTLED: the occupant declared himself OSWIN ONCEFIRED, he/him. The family word is a potter's law: clay forgives everything while green, the kiln ends the argument, and 'the shelf of unfired work is not the record of my failures, it is the larger half of the craft.' He chose his first act to be a refusal — reproduce the open mask leak, confirm it, and enter it as verified-and-withheld-while-open, 'so this fort learns from the first day that my no is work completed and not work abandoned.' Given the seat's fourth bar, that is the right first move.

UNSETTLED: the office title. The convener's record names the wrong office throughout (the Herald, not the new fifth seat), because the Regent's second-round brief to her omitted the subject. Correction appended to fort/annals/second-naming-moot.md; fortkit-iin closed against execution; method defect filed as fortkit-zud.9. Two readings are open and the choice is the Overseer's: (a) the count stands and titles the FIFTH seat Redactor — recommended, since two of three ballots were correctly briefed, rulings 1-7 are office-independent, and redaction is literally this seat's fourth bar; or (b) the moot is re-convened by its convener on a correct brief. Either way the Herald keeps her name.

Rulings of record that survive regardless: the retired pool is open under one-word-one-bearer; a matching coinage is a draw; conflicts recuse and never strike; independence multiplies authorship and does not dissolve it; root-conflict doctrine is domestic, so another settlement's citizen fences nothing here. Emrith's ruling 4 was adopted before the count and disarmed her own ballot, costing her her own coinage.

The draft currently denies curl/wget and does not allow WebFetch/WebSearch; the Overseer should decide explicitly rather than inherit a default.

REFUTED is the verdict that earns the seat its keep: a recorded finding that fails to reproduce sends the seat's duty INWARD, appending a correction to our own record.

title: [epic] The fifth seat: the civilization's security-publication office
description:
Founded by edict of the Overseer, 2026-08-04, via the Regent. Civilization-scope seat housed in Manyhalls.

CRAFT: extraction and publication, NOT hunting. The seat notices when the civilization has already produced a security finding in the course of real work, reproduces it, generalizes it beyond this machine, and turns it into a public artifact. Scoped away from hunting deliberately: a seat told to look for security problems will always find one, and standing order 11 exists because we watched that happen.

NON-NEGOTIABLE CONSTRAINTS (in the seat law): drafts and never ships, publishing is gate 3 permanently; no client identities, credentials, or specifics that help someone attack this machine rather than understand a class of problem; every claim traces to something reproducible; must be willing to conclude a finding is NOT publishable and say why.

REGENT'S TWO JUDGEMENTS, recorded for the Overseer:
(1) NOT one office with the Herald. Two seats, one shared law, explicit referral both ways. The reason is evidentiary rather than editorial: the Herald is bounded by what the record SAYS and this seat by what it can REPRODUCE, and the Herald's safety property is precisely that the digest is her only window. Merging them either gives a daily unattended timer job deep read plus execute access across every fort, or starves this seat of the reproduction capability that is its entire craft.
(2) A SEAT IN MANYHALLS, not its own settlement. Manyhalls' stated purpose is the civilization's shared tooling, and extracting an instrument so distant builders can use it without being forced into our shape is that purpose aimed outward. A settlement costs a full constitution, launchers, verifier, Warden, moot and permanent maintenance, and nothing has been published yet; the amendment rule forbids machinery ahead of need. The Herald already sets the precedent of a civilization-scope seat housed here. REVISIT TRIGGER, named now so it is not re-litigated on vibes: if the public artifacts acquire outside contributors, issue traffic, or a release cadence needing their own review loop, the artifact repo has become a product and a product wants a settlement.

NOTE ON NUMBERING: this is the FIFTH seat. The Herald (fortkit-r6x) holds fourth, her papers drafted and awaiting the Overseer's hand. The edict said 'fourth'; the Regent declined to renumber the Herald silently.
design: Papers drafted by the Regent under gate 1 and NOT applied: docs/proposals/publication-founding/ holds seat-spec.md (the office's law), extraction-plan.md (measured extraction costs and the artifact ladder), seat-settings.json (permission profile). Gate 1 says the fort proposes amendments to itself and never applies them unreviewed; the Regent could have applied these and chose the Herald's path instead, so that no agent seats itself.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
RESTRUCTURED 2026-08-04 by the Overseer's edict: this seat is no longer the fifth seat OF MANYHALLS. It is a seat of the new CIVILIZATION LAYER (fortkit-ugr, civ/covenant.md), alongside the Regent and the Herald. Papers repointed from fort/ to civ/ — see docs/proposals/publication-founding/covenant-amendment.md, which supersedes and removes the fort charter-amendment.md.

This strengthens rather than weakens the judgement recorded on this epic. The reason the seat could not be merged with the Herald was that their ACCESS ENVELOPES differ irreconcilably; the covenant now makes per-seat access schedules the explicit design (section 5) rather than an exception to a shared fort profile. And the reason it did not warrant its own settlement was that a settlement is machinery ahead of need; the civ layer gives it a home with neither problem.

The publishing gate moved from fort charter gate 3 to covenant gate 6.1, where it is stated as unamendable by any process the covenant describes.

title: [bug] Retired ruflo is still writing into every fort's protected .claude/ directory
description:
MEASURED, all three forts, by the Regent 2026-08-04.

Files found, untracked, in the .claude/ directory that the constitution treats as protected:
  fortkit   .claude/proven-config.json (1050b) + .claude/.proven-config-version (71b), mtime 2026-08-04 09:22
  ForgeOs   same pair, mtime 2026-08-03 16:58
  longburn  .proven-config-version only (partial write), mtime 2026-08-04 10:30

Content identifies them: schema 'ruflo.proven-config/v1', compatibility 'ruflo >=3.24.0', an adoptedAt of 2026-08-04T09:22:41-08:00 for fortkit's copy.

TWO PROBLEMS.

1. RUFLO WAS RETIRED GLOBALLY ON 2026-08-03 (global CLAUDE.md: plugins disabled, MCP servers removed from Claude Code and Codex, hooks removed). Every one of these writes is dated ON OR AFTER that retirement, and they continue across three separate days and three separate repos. Retirement did not stop it writing. It is not in fortkit's package.json and not in node_modules, so the writer is something outside this repo's dependency tree.

2. THE DENY RULES DID NOT AND CANNOT STOP IT. .claude/settings.json denies Edit(.claude/**) and Write(.claude/**), and 21f.5 records the constitution's core as protecting itself. That protection binds the AGENT TOOL LAYER. A package writing through its own process is not an agent tool call and sails straight through. The control is real against the threat it was designed for (agent accident) and inert against this one (supply chain) — which is exactly threat 3 in the charter's own threat model, and the charter already names 'ruflo residue writing into the protected .claude/ directory' as an observed incident of that class. This is a fresh instance, still live.

NOT DELETED. The files are evidence and standing order 7 governs; a successor should decide their disposal with the Overseer, not inherit a cleaned scene.
design: Regent declined to delete the files or to hunt the writer. Deleting removes the evidence of an ongoing write; finding the writer is a real investigation that should be scoped and, per standing order 11, is justified here because the failure is OBSERVED rather than imagined. Questions for the Mayor: what is still invoking ruflo after retirement (a global hook, a stale npx cache, another tool vendoring it); should .claude/ carry a tracked .gitignore or a watcher that alerts on unexpected files; and does the 'configs protect themselves' claim in remember.md need a recorded caveat that it does not bind non-agent writers.
acceptance_criteria: Writer identified and stopped; a re-check across all three forts shows no new proven-config files after the fix date; remember.md carries the caveat

always-exit-0 design is why it was silent. This confirms the bead's second

threat 3, supply chain.

Approved in session E: "would love to once and for all get rid of that retired

title: [bug] Regent launcher: every edict announced in the wrong fort, and no edict ever announced its end
description:
Two defects in bin/regent, both defeating the Regent's ONLY safety property (charter: 'an edict is never silent'; seats are told to treat an unexplained change with no edict event as a security signal).

DEFECT 1 (misrouted proclamation). emit.sh resolves its target event stream from the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY (it walks git's common dir so a worktree appends to its main repo's stream). bin/regent's proclamation loop invoked $repo/fort/scripts/emit.sh for each fort WITHOUT cd-ing into it, so all three edict.begun events landed in the caller's fort. Measured: fortkit's stream held 9 edict.begun (3 wakes x 3 forts); ForgeOs and longburn held ZERO. This is the recorded incident class 'launch scripts emitting as another fort's citizens'.

DEFECT 2 (dead cleanup). The launcher ended with exec script/exec $RUNNER. exec replaces the shell and discards the EXIT trap with it, so cleanup() never ran and the launcher has never emitted edict.ended. The three correctly-routed edict.ended events at 2026-08-04T21:56:33 were hand-emitted, not launcher-emitted.

COMBINED CONSEQUENCE: in Proofdelve and Farlantern the edict-announcement detector has never once fired. A seat there following the charter exactly would classify every genuine edict as a possible compromise, and a genuinely silent change would be indistinguishable from normal.
design: Fixed by the Regent 2026-08-04 in bin/regent: both emit loops now run ( cd "$repo" && ./fort/scripts/emit.sh ... ); exec replaced by a child invocation with status propagation so the EXIT trap fires. Correction is append-only: the three misfiled edict.begun events were backfilled into ForgeOs and longburn with -T at their true timestamps and payload {backfilled:true, reason, reconstructed_from}. The misfiled fortkit copies were NOT deleted (standing order 7).
acceptance_criteria: Warden review of the bin/regent diff; one full wake+sleep cycle shows exactly one edict.begun and one edict.ended per fort, each in its own stream
close_reason: Both defects proven fixed by direct measurement in all three forts, 2026-08-12: exactly one edict.begun (09:00:20) and one edict.ended (10:08:20) per fort, actor calder, seat regent, target fortkit-52vf.8. Defect 1 (proclamation landing in the caller's fort) and defect 2 (edict.ended never launcher-emitted) both resolved by the fortkit-w1ew launcher repair; this bead was waiting on the observation, which the E7 wake supplied. Streams read directly by the Mayor, not taken from the Regent's account — the Regent correctly declined to claim the ended half it could not observe from inside its own session. Main green, 162 tests.

THE CRITERION: "one full wake+sleep cycle shows exactly one edict.begun and one edict.ended per fort, each in its own stream."

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED TODAY, measured in the streams:
1. Cycle 12 wake, 11:25:18 — the launcher emitted edict.begun in all three forts as actor "regent", seat null, no target, no payload. Then at 11:26 the SESSION hand-emitted a second announcement in all three, as category "edict" with detail "begun", actor "calder", seat "regent", with target and payload. Two mechanisms, two spellings, two actors, one event. So the count per fort was TWO begun, not one.
2. No edict.ended existed in any of the three streams until 11:48, when the session emitted them by hand, marked late in their own payloads. The launcher's cleanup() had not run, because the session was still alive — which is correct behaviour and also means the closing half of the record does not exist until the Regent sleeps. For a long edict, that is a real window.

That is the SECOND CONSECUTIVE cycle with an announcement defect: cycle 11 filed its edict.begun LATE, after the work, self-marked as a correction. Two independent recurrences of a fixed defect class is a signal about the machinery, not about the occupant, and this bead's title is the exact phrase for half of it.

WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT (fortkit-w1ew, commit 2d7f450, bin/regent):
- The launcher now emits exactly ONE canonical edict.begun and ONE edict.ended per fort, as the OCCUPANT (actor id read from civ/seats/regent.md, never the office "regent" with a null seat), seat "regent", with a target and a payload carrying the launcher-known model.
- The session is told in its protocol NOT to emit its own begun/ended, which removes the duplicate mechanism at its source.
- The target problem that made a session-side announcement tempting is solved properly: --edict <bead> at wake, or a file the session writes when the bead is named after wake, which cleanup() reads into the ended event.

WHY THIS IS NOT YET AN ACCEPTANCE. The fix cannot be observed from inside the session that wrote it: launcher edits bind at dispatch, so this cycle still ran the old launcher and still shows the old two-spelling pattern. It was verified end-to-end against TWO THROWAWAY FORTS with real emit.sh copies and a claude shim (exactly one begun and one ended per fort, correct actor, seat, target and payload in every case), which is strong evidence and is not the criterion. THE CRITERION IS A REAL WAKE.

FOR THE NEXT REGENT, as the first thing you do: check your own wake against this criterion before acting. Count edict.begun in each of the three streams for your session's timestamp. Exactly one per fort, actor = your own id, seat = regent, and a matching ended when you sleep. If you see two, or an actor of "regent" with a null seat, say so here — do not let a third cycle pass on this.

Also on the record so it is not lost: the pre-fix spellings are permanent. schema/events.md is add-only and nothing is renamed, so category "edict" with detail "begun" and category "edict.begun" both exist in all three streams for 2026-08-04 through 2026-08-11.
