LEFT OPEN for this fort's Warden under covenant 4.5.

title: Verifier gate: the live and template seat-sandbox libs are identical modulo comments — the check that would have caught z0j8 in the sitting that made it
description:
WARDEN FINDING 3 on fortkit-z0j8 (Ilva, 2026-08-13). Mayor lane: it edits scripts/verify-impl.sh, kernel read-only to the Forge by the Shape B carve-out. Do not dispatch.

WHAT IS MISSING. Nothing tests the parity that fortkit-z0j8 existed to restore. No test in test/ references seat-sandbox or the option parser; the safety net for that change was ShellCheck plus the Warden's own textual differential, both of which run only if a human thinks to look.

SO11 IS SATISFIED — OBSERVED, NOT IMAGINED. fortkit-29e9 carried the E8 hunks into the factory lib and left the --mask-file case branch in the wrong position. It cost a bead, a Forge sitting, a Warden review and two sessions to find and fix something a one-line assertion would have caught in the sitting that introduced it.

THE GATE: the live fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh and templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh are identical modulo comments and template placeholders. The Warden's own command is the specification:

    diff -I '^[[:space:]]*#' fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh

which produced NO OUTPUT after z0j8 merged, and produced the reorder before it.

SAME SHAPE AS fortkit-c1kj, deliberately: assert a relationship between two artifacts that must agree, keyed on something stable, rather than pinning prose. Comments are excluded ON PURPOSE — the template legitimately carries header lines the live lib does not ('TEMPLATE — rendered by fort-init', the SC1083 disable), so a raw byte comparison would be red permanently and disabled within a day. That is the failure mode c1kj rejected two gate designs over.

PLACEMENT NOTE, and it is why this is worth doing rather than just wishing: this is the LAST executable divergence in a file that standing order 12 is about to port into three more forts. A gate here is cheap now and expensive to retrofit after the parity programme has run.

PROVE IT DISCRIMINATES, per this fort's evidence bar: reintroduce the z0j8 reorder in a scratch copy and show the gate reds; show it green on main; show a comment-only edit does NOT red it. A checker that checks nothing must never report success.

RELATIONSHIP TO fortkit-52vf.10.1: that bead removes the remaining COMMENT divergence across four copies. This gate deliberately does not depend on it — it ignores comments by design, so it can land first and does not block on it.
acceptance_criteria: A verifier step fails when the live and template seat-sandbox libs diverge in any non-comment line; green on main today; a comment-only difference does not red it; proven by reintroducing the fortkit-z0j8 reorder in a scratch copy.

title: Regression test for the c1kj memory staleness gate: the four differentials proven by hand should be mechanical
description:
fortkit-c1kj's gate was proven to discriminate four ways by hand this session — control green, superseded fact planted red, active core fact removed red, Open work churn green, and the real pre-fix view at 03aac68^ red on both directions. None of that is mechanically enforced; a future refactor of scripts/memory-lint.mjs could silently defang it, which is exactly the fortkit-x1n class this fort has already been bitten by once.

title: E8 Warden follow-ups 1, 5, 6, 7, 8: a shared comment true in one fort and false in another, a standing probe without the interpretation guard the same session invented, three unasserted masks, and a stale charter citation
description:
WARDEN FINDINGS on fortkit-52vf.10 (Ilva, 2026-08-13), all non-blocking. Verdict ESCALATE was a mandatory gate-1 + auth-surface referral with NO blocking findings: 'the design is sound, the capital's half of E8 should stand.'

1. THE LIB'S POLICY-LAYER CLAIM IS FALSE FOR THIS FORT'S COPY. The dispatch-exception comment says 'forge.sh's guarded deny table denies /home/justin/.codex/**'. MEASURED: fortkit/fort/scripts/forge.sh has NO deny table — the word deny does not appear in it; it runs codex exec --sandbox workspace-write with six --add-dir grants and nothing else. The deny table is ForgeOs's (:80). The CONCLUSION is correct — workspace-write's writable roots exclude ~/.codex, and both dispatch-lane seats reported 'rejected by the command executor' — but the mechanism named in this copy does not exist in this copy. A shared comment true in one fort and false in another is THE DRIFT CLASS THIS WHOLE EDICT EXISTS TO CLOSE. Fix: name the enforcing mechanism per copy.

5. THE NEW STANDING ASSERTIONS SHIP WITHOUT THE INTERPRETATION GUARD THE SAME SESSION INVENTED. The E8 scratch probe asserted the mask sees the REAL ~/.codex (byte count matching host) before labelling anything, precisely because under a tmpfs a writability probe passes on a broken runtime — and the Regent's own first draft had two lying labels. probe-cycle7's new 'ok ~/.codex writable' carries no such guard; the tmpfs case is caught only indirectly, by the paired config.toml deny probe failing. SECOND HALF, and it is the sharper one: the property that actually broke in longburn-1p9 was RENAME, and the standing probe asserts FILE CREATION. The instrument that asserted rename-with-guard 'lives in this session's scratchpad' (Regent handoff item 5) and is now gone. fortkit-wtps is the right home and should carry the guard AND the rename assertion, not just the missing ~/.codex lines.

6. THREE NEW MASKS LAND WITH NO ASSERTION ANYWHERE, AND ONE HAS AN UNDOCUMENTED CONSEQUENCE. ~/.codex/sessions, ~/.codex/log and ~/.codex/history.jsonl are newly masked for claude seats. probe-cycle7 asserts only config.toml-RO and directory-writable; scripts/mask-harness.sh has no ~/.codex string at all — which independently corroborates the record's '61/0 on a lib that would have stopped Proofdelve's mill'. Worth recording alongside: a Forge DISPATCHED from a Mayor inherits those masks recursively, so its session rollouts and history land in the Mayor's tmpfs and are LOST. No regression (the old full tmpfs lost them too) and no launch failure (measured: fortkit-m0wm ran to exit 0), but it is nowhere written down and would cost a debugging session.

7. --mask-file SILENTLY IGNORES A DIRECTORY. The bind site is [ -e ] && [ ! -d ], correctly, so a caller passing a directory gets no mask and no output — the same silent-gap class this very commit discloses at length for the secret sweep two hundred lines above. One sentence in the parameter's doc block closes the asymmetry.

8. A CHARTER LINE-NUMBER CITATION IS NOW STALE. fort/charter.md cites probe-cycle7.sh 'line 74' for the inverted Shape-B assertion; measured, old :74 and new :80 are both the probe deny 'scripts/verify.sh SHIM RO (Shape B)', so the citation now lands on a comment. The 35/0 figure is a dated measurement and remains true as one. CITE THE PROBE'S LABEL, NOT ITS LINE — labels do not drift. (Charter edit = prose gate, so this item rides fortkit-3jv7's approval rather than being done alone.)

LANES: 1, 5, 6, 7 are fort/scripts/ and its lib — KERNEL-RO, so a Regent sitting. 8 is the charter — prose gate.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five findings either fixed with its evidence recorded, or explicitly deferred with a reason on this bead.
close_reason: Fixed in Regent edict E10 (fortkit-52vf.12), commit fbeb941. Warden ESCALATE, no blocking findings, verify green 180/180. OVERSEER GATE-1 SIGN-OFF RECORDED VERBATIM, 2026-08-13. Justin: 'route her six findings and take the gate-1 sign-off now.' WHAT IT COVERS, stated so the record is not a rubber stamp: Warden verdict ESCALATE (Ilva Trueglass, opus), a MANDATORY gate-1 referral because civ/scripts/ and fort/scripts/ are charter human-gate-1 areas, with NO BLOCKING FINDINGS, verify.sh green 180/180, transcript clean, and the Warden's own explicit recommendation to sign off. Six non-blocking findings routed forward before the sign-off was taken, not after. THE CAPITAL ONLY: the E10 commits in ForgeOs (2a06149) and longburn (9860e0d) are unreviewed by this fort and remain open to their own Wardens under covenant 4.5. Residuals from her review are filed forward, not hidden — see the two follow-up beads filed 2026-08-13.

title: Carry the post-E8 permission spelling into the factory: Edit(fort/scripts/**) plus the three relative denies no live fort's template has
description:
WARDEN FINDINGS 1 AND 2 on fortkit-n3bk.1 (Ilva, 2026-08-13, both non-blocking), which the merge deliberately did not fix because merging was strictly better than not merging.

FINDING 1 — THE TEMPLATE IS ALREADY 6 RULES BEHIND, THROUGH NO FAULT OF THE FORGE. The E8 Regent sitting (755e369, 08:51:27) replaced fortkit's six granular Edit(fort/scripts/emit.sh|forge.sh|lib/**|mayor.sh|status.sh|warden.sh) denies with a single Edit(fort/scripts/**), and added Edit(scripts/**) to allow. The n3bk.1 branch shipped at 08:15, 36 minutes earlier, and its spec named fortkit's live settings.json as the reference tree. So 6 of the 15 template rules no longer match that reference. The drift watcher's permission check is a literal includes (civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:362-376), so those six read as absent from the capital post-merge. Severity is bounded: findings dedupe by fort+path identity, so it is ONE open Drift: bead with fingerprint comments rather than six per run.

FINDING 2 — THE FACTORY SHIPS A MATERIALLY NARROWER DENY SET THAN ANY LIVE FORT, and three of the missing rules are relative and perfectly templatable: Edit(.claude/**), Edit(fort/profiles/**), Edit(fort/scripts/**). In a fort founded today, allow Edit(fort/**) therefore covers fort/profiles/** and the shipped fort/scripts/researcher.sh, probe-researcher-boundaries.sh and verify.sh, none of which any deny names. Threat 1, agent accident. The kernel mask is the real boundary and it HOLDS — templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:142 and :283 bind .claude, fort/profiles and fort/scripts whole-directory read-only — so this is defense-in-depth plus the reader-facing accuracy problem fortkit-yowr was filed about: a settings file showing a protection it does not spell.

SO7 CORRECTION ALSO OWED (Ilva finding 3): the n3bk.1 handoff's Open risks line says the live forts' extra Edit protections 'cannot be literal template values'. True for the //home/justin/... absolutes and the generated SessionStart hook; NOT true for the three relative rules above, which belong in the template. A reader acting on the original text would conclude nothing further needs carrying.

MEASUREMENT OWED (Ilva finding 4): yowr's acceptance test cannot run against a template, which is not a settings file until bin/fort-init:151 substitutes {{REPO_PATH}}. The first fort founded after this lands is where the real launch measurement gets taken — grep -c 'is not matched by file permission checks' == 0, with a positive control.

LANE: Forge (templates/ only).
design:
FORGE BRIEF (Mayor, 2026-08-13 session d). Band 2, Lane A. This bead is FULLY Forge-dispatchable: it touches templates/config/settings-permissions.json and nothing else. Do not edit bin/fort-init — it is kernel read-only to your mask (seat-sandbox.sh:198-202, guarded on civ/covenant.md, which this repo has).

FILE: templates/config/settings-permissions.json (the ONLY file this bead changes).

REFERENCE TREE, re-verified 2026-08-13 by reading .claude/settings.json rather than trusting the bead text:
  allow:89   Edit(scripts/**)
  deny:104   Edit(.claude/**)
  deny:127   Edit(fort/profiles/**)
  deny:128   Edit(fort/scripts/**)

CHANGE 1 — collapse the six stale granular denies (finding 1). The template's deny block
currently carries six rules that E8 (755e369) replaced in the live capital:
  Edit(fort/scripts/emit.sh)
  Edit(fort/scripts/forge.sh)
  Edit(fort/scripts/lib/**)
  Edit(fort/scripts/mayor.sh)
  Edit(fort/scripts/status.sh)
  Edit(fort/scripts/warden.sh)
Replace all six with the single Edit(fort/scripts/**).

CHANGE 2 — add the two missing relative denies (finding 2). Alongside the new
Edit(fort/scripts/**), add:
  Edit(.claude/**)
  Edit(fort/profiles/**)
Reason this matters: the template's allow block carries Edit(fort/**), which today covers
fort/profiles/** and the shipped fort/scripts/researcher.sh, probe-researcher-boundaries.sh
and verify.sh, none of which any deny names.

CHANGE 3 — add Edit(scripts/**) to the ALLOW block. Shape B put the verifier implementation at
scripts/verify-impl.sh, outside the locked fort/scripts/. A fort founded without this allow rule
cannot have its verifier edited by its own Mayor, which is the seat that owns it.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE. Add exactly these. Do NOT port the live capital's absolute-path denies
(the //home/justin/... entries) — they are the fortkit-f3y double-slash defect and are being
fixed separately under fortkit-0po6 with a {{HOME}} placeholder. Do NOT port Edit(bin/**),
Edit(civ/profiles/**) or Edit(civ/scripts/**): those surfaces exist only in the capital, and
seat-sandbox.sh:191-194 deliberately guards them on civ/covenant.md so an ordinary fort growing
a bin/ of its own does not find it silently read-only.

WHAT YOU CANNOT VERIFY, AND MUST NOT CLAIM. The template is not a settings file until
bin/fort-init:151 substitutes {{REPO_PATH}}, so the real launch measurement (grep -c 'is not
matched by file permission checks' == 0, with a positive control) CANNOT be taken here. That
measurement is fortkit-domm's job and it is already wired as a dependency. State in your handoff
that the acceptance measurement is deferred to domm; do not report a green you did not take.
This is the same class as your round-2 handoff on fortkit-px7e, where a claim true in your
environment and false in a masked seat's was stated unconditionally.

SO7 CORRECTION OWED, and it goes in this bead's COMMENTS, not its notes. The fortkit-n3bk.1
handoff says the live forts' extra Edit protections 'cannot be literal template values'. That is
true for the absolutes and the generated SessionStart hook, and FALSE for the three relative

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
## Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead `fortkit-n3bk.2`. Round one. Work by **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge top rung, per the handoff's `Model:` line). Two path-scoped commits, `d459998` + `9822f21`; the three-dot diff against the merge base is exactly two files — `templates/config/settings-permissions.json` and `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-13-n3bk.2.md`. Nothing in `fort/scripts/**`, `fort/profiles/**`, `.claude/**`, `bin/**`, `scripts/verify-impl.sh`, or the charter. Commit messages both start `fortkit-n3bk.2: `.

**Diff-spelling note, same as last round:** `main..bead/n3bk.2` shows an 89-line deletion in `scripts/verify-impl.sh`. That is not a revert — it is main's own newer commit `c220b31` (`fortkit-8ib`, the rendered-template lint) that this branch predates. The branch's work is the three-dot diff, and that is what I judged. The two sides are file-disjoint, so the merge is clean; main's new `template-render` step lints only `templates/**/*.sh`, which this branch does not touch, so its inputs are unchanged by the merge.

**All three changes are exactly the brief, and I checked each against the reference tree on disk rather than against the bead text.** The live capital's `.claude/settings.json` carries `Edit(scripts/**)` in allow and `Edit(.claude/**)`, `Edit(fort/profiles/**)`, `Edit(fort/scripts/**)` in deny; the six granular `fort/scripts/*` denies are gone from it. The template now matches on all four. Scope discipline held: no `//home/justin/...` absolutes (left to `fortkit-0po6`), no `Edit(bin/**)`, `Edit(civ/profiles/**)` or `Edit(civ/scripts/**)`, and no `~/.codex` rule (also `0po6`). Allow and deny remain 53/53 and 19/19 unique. The acceptance measurement is correctly deferred to `fortkit-domm` and the handoff says so in two places — no green claimed that was not taken, which is the thing the brief specifically asked for after `px7e`.

The change is a net gain against **threat 1, agent accident**: in a fort founded after this lands, the tool layer now names the same three surfaces the kernel mask already binds read-only (`templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:186` for `.claude` and `fort/profiles`, `:384` for `fort/scripts` in every seat's mask), closing the `yowr` reader-facing gap where a settings file showed a protection it did not spell. No widening: the Researcher, the seat exposed to threat 2, is launched with `--settings fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json`, which denies `Edit(**)`, so the new `Edit(scripts/**)` allow does not reach it. The Forge is a codex seat and does not read this file at all. It reaches the Mayor, which is the seat that owns `scripts/verify-impl.sh` — the intent of change 3.

### Findings

**1. (non-blocking) The template's deny list is no longer alphabetically sorted.** `Edit(.claude/**)` was appended after `Edit(fort/events/*.jsonl)` instead of before `Edit(.env*)`, where its own file's convention puts it. Before this change the template's deny was strictly sorted; the live capital's allow and deny both still are (`jq '.permissions.deny == (.permissions.deny|sort)'` → `true` there, `false` here). Functionally inert on both consumers I checked — Claude Code does not order-rank rules, and the drift watcher compares with a `Set` (`civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:753-770`), not a sequence. It matters only for maintenance: an unsorted deny list is how duplicate rules survive review, and duplicate-checking these lists is exactly what `n3bk.1` was filed about. One-line fix, worth a bead, not worth a round.

**2. (non-blocking, pre-existing, outside this bead's lane) The factory's prose still describes the retired Shape A carve-out, and this change leaves it as the last place asserting it.** `templates/fort/charter.md:13` says the enforcement layer is mechanical "with `verify.sh` alone re-granted writable to the Mayor", and `templates/fort/seats/mayor.md:14` says "`verify.sh` is writable to the Mayor alone". Neither file mentions `scripts/verify-impl.sh` anywhere. That is the precise sentence `fortkit-hwol` was filed and closed on — "the Mayor will act on it and hit EROFS" — fixed in the capital's `fort/seats/mayor.md` and never carried to the factory. It is now sharper than before this diff, because the template's settings have just joined the template's kernel mask in contradicting the template's charter: a fort founded today would be born with a Mayor seat file promising a write the mask, and now the deny list, both refuse. Bears on threat 1 by the wasted-cycle/false-record route rather than a security route. Not this bead's file and not blocking; it belongs in the parity programme (`fortkit-wg8w` Band 2), and it is the same class as `fortkit-6fga` and `fortkit-xgul.8`.

**3. (non-blocking, record placement) The SO7 correction landed on `fortkit-n3bk.1`'s comments, not this bead's, and that is the right call — but the design and the acceptance criteria asked for different things and a reader should know which happened.** The design says "it goes in this bead's COMMENTS"; the acceptance criteria say "SO7 correction appended to the n3bk.1 record". The export shows it on `n3bk.1` at `2026-08-14T04:05:05Z`, correctly stating what is true (the absolutes and the generated hook) and what is false (the three relative rules) in the original text, and closing with "The original handoff remains unchanged" — the append-only rule honoured. `fortkit-n3bk.2` has `comments: null`. The AC is satisfied and the placement is the more useful one, since a reader misled by the `n3bk.1` handoff looks at `n3bk.1`. Recorded so the Mayor does not double-append at closure.

**4. (non-blocking, attribution) That correction's author field reads `Justin Schneider`, not `kethra`.** Every commit in this repository carries the same ambient identity, including main's, so this is the Forge lane's standing provenance property and not something this bead introduced — but a correction is precisely the record whose value depends on who attests it, and this one is attributed to the Overseer, who did not write it. `fortkit-52vf.4` (E3: identity and provenance — actor ids, false record fields) is the bead that owns this class; a comment pointing at this instance would be worth more than a new bead.

**5. (non-blocking, observation) The handoff is accurate where I could check it, including the numbers.** Its Biome (64 files) and Vitest (15 files / 180 tests) figures match my own run exactly, which is the corroboration I wanted given the `px7e` scar this brief cited at the Forge.

**Gate note, restated from my `n3bk.1` review so the reading stays visible.** Human gate 1 covers *this fort's own* constitution and permission profiles. `templates/config/settings-permissions.json` is a product artifact that becomes *another* fort's constitution at founding, and the enforcement layer agrees with that reading — `templates/` is writable to the Forge, the seat holding the fullest kernel lock in this fort. I therefore did not treat this as a mandatory-ESCALATE surface. Nothing in this diff changes what is enforced anywhere today. I record the reading so the Overseer can overrule it.

### Verified independently vs taken on faith

title: [bug] A directory named like a secret is silently unmasked: the [ -f ] fix traded a launch-abort for a quiet gap
description:
fortkit-n3bk finding 6 (Ilva, E2b review). DISCLOSED IN CODE by E8 (fortkit-52vf.10, 2026-08-13) in all three forts' lib/seat-sandbox.sh; NOT closed, and this bead is the open half.

fortkit-faka finding 5 changed the secret sweep's filter from [ -e ] to [ -f ]. That was right and urgent: two of the six SECRET_GLOBS patterns (*env*~ and #*env*#) match names that do not begin with a dot, so a DIRECTORY called e.g. environments~ satisfied [ -e ], joined MASK_FILES, and '--ro-bind /dev/null <directory>' ABORTS BWRAP — failure mode NO SEAT LAUNCHES ANYWHERE, arriving through the fix for fortkit-2kub rather than the defect it was fixing.

THE RESIDUAL: such a directory is now SKIPPED, and then simply unmasked, and no line of output says so. A directory called environments~ or .env.d holding secret files is readable inside every mask in every fort. Latent — no such path exists in any fort today (re-measured 2026-08-13).

THE HONEST FIX is to descend into a directory matching a secret glob and sweep its FILES, rather than skipping it. That changes what a launch costs (a find per matching directory per root) and deserves its own measurement, which is why E8 disclosed it rather than bolting it on. A cheaper interim: emit a warning line naming the skipped directory, so the gap is visible at launch instead of only in a comment.

title: The Codex runtime's instruction surface (~/.codex/skills, ~/.codex/plugins) is writable to every seat that gets ~/.codex — the codex twin of fortkit-5sk, and it cannot be fixed by an RO bind
description:
PARITY GAP WITH fortkit-5sk, one runtime over. Cycle 13 made the Claude runtime's global instruction surface (~/.claude/skills, commands, plugins, civilization.json) kernel read-only to every masked seat, on the stated grounds that its contents are session-executed instruction. The Codex runtime has the identical surface and it is NOT covered.

MEASURED 2026-08-13 (Emrith), ls -la /home/justin/.codex:
  skills/    -> .system/{skill-installer,skill-creator,review-agent,plugin-creator,openai-docs,imagegen}, each with SKILL.md and scripts/ and agents/ subdirectories
  plugins/   -> cache/openai-curated-remote/openai-templates, .remote-plugin-install-staging
  memories_1.sqlite, goals_1.sqlite, queue_1.sqlite, state_5.sqlite
  config.toml is 62 bytes and contains only a trust_level entry for /home/justin/dev/fortkit

WHO CAN WRITE IT TODAY. Every codex-branch caller grants ~/.codex writable with only config.toml re-bound read-only: fortkit lib :311 (RW_PATHS) and longburn lib :170/:326 (CODEX_DIR_RW). So Kethra can already write ~/.codex/skills in Manyhalls and Veyra can in Farlantern. The disarm-the-next-launch protection currently rests on ONE 62-byte file while the far larger instruction surface beside it is open. ForgeOs's own forge.sh:77-78 comment already names this ('leaving Codex global instruction/prompt files under ~/.codex writable'), so the concern is documented in this civilization's code, not invented here.

WHY IT WIDENS UNDER E8 OPTION 1. If fortkit-52vf.10 unifies on CODEX_DIR_RW for BOTH seat types, attended Mayor and Warden sessions in fortkit and ForgeOs gain write access to this surface too, where today their ~/.codex is a tmpfs with only auth.json visible. That trade may well be correct — the longburn-1p9 revocation incident is a recorded failure and justifies it — but it should be accepted knowingly, and it is not stated in the three options the Regent put to the Overseer.

=== THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE ONE THAT WOULD BREAK THE MILL ===

DO NOT simply add ~/.codex/skills and ~/.codex/plugins to RO_PATHS beside config.toml. MEASURED 2026-08-13, and this is the whole reason this bead exists rather than a one-line change in E8:

  /home/justin/.codex/skills   mtime 2026-08-13 08:12:11.888034213
  /home/justin/.codex/skills/.system   mtime 08:12:11.889413649
  /home/justin/.codex/plugins  mtime 2026-08-13 08:12:13.747184468
  Kethra session.start on fortkit-n3bk.1: 2026-08-13T08:12:11-08:00

Same second. A directory mtime changes when an entry in it is created, removed or renamed, so the codex runtime mutates BOTH directories within ~2 seconds of launch. A read-only bind would therefore likely refuse the launch outright — the exact failure class E8 exists to prevent, and the same shape as the ForgeOs ~/.codex read-only hazard that made E8 non-mechanical in the first place.

=== WHAT THIS BEAD NEEDS ===

1. Determine WHAT codex writes there at startup (a marker refresh, a cache stamp, a staging dir) and whether the writes are confined to a subpath that can be left writable while the SKILL.md/scripts/agents content is bound read-only. That is the shape the claude branch already uses for sessions/ and log/ and history.jsonl.
2. If no such split exists, say so plainly and record it as a charter accepted residual WITH the measurement attached, per standing order 11 — the same treatment fortkit-gohb gives the /proc exposure. Do not leave it undocumented.
3. Carry the answer to all three libs and the factory template, since the codex branch is identical in all of them.

LANE: Regent (fort/scripts/ is kernel read-only whole). NOT E8 — E8 is already carrying a lib fix, a launcher port, a mechanism unification and four n3bk findings, and this needs its own measurement before anyone touches a bind.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) a measured split that binds the codex instruction content read-only while leaving whatever codex mutates at startup writable, proven by a real forge.sh smoke launch, carried to all three libs and the template; or (b) a charter accepted residual recording the exposure with the startup-write measurement attached, per SO11.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
SO7 CORRECTION, APPENDED 2026-08-13 BY THE AUTHOR OF THE ERROR. THIS BEAD'S TITLE AND DESCRIPTION ASSERT A MECHANISM THAT IS NOT PROVEN. Read this before acting on either.

WHAT IS WRONG. The description's section 'THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE ONE THAT WOULD BREAK THE MILL' rests on mtimes I measured at 2026-08-13 08:20 from inside a masked Mayor session: ~/.codex/skills at 08:12:11.888034213, ~/.codex/plugins at 08:12:13.747184468, correlated with Kethra's session.start at 08:12:11. I concluded the codex runtime mutates both directories within two seconds of launch and that a read-only bind would therefore refuse the launch.

THAT MEASUREMENT DESCRIBES MY SANDBOX, NOT THE HOST. Established afterwards from /proc/self/mountinfo in the same session: /home/justin/.codex is a TMPFS, and the ONLY path re-bound from real disk beneath it is auth.json (btrfs). skills/, plugins/, config.toml and the sqlite files I enumerated in the description were all tmpfs scratch created inside my sandbox. The Regent measured the HOST at 2026-08-10 12:29:42 (skills) and 2026-07-09 09:20:06 (plugins) and correctly noted mtime does not move backwards. Calder's figures are the true ones. The 08:12:11 correlation was real and means the opposite of what I claimed: it is when dispatching the Forge caused codex to populate MY tmpfs view.

A CONTRADICTION IN MY OWN OUTPUT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT AT THE TIME. In the same command block I ran 'find ~/.codex/skills ~/.codex/plugins -newermt "1 hour ago"' and it returned NOTHING. Two directories allegedly modified eight minutes earlier cannot be absent from that result. I read the stat line and did not reconcile it with the find line.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE REASON THE BEAD STAYS OPEN. The underlying gap is read from the LIB SOURCE, not from mtimes, and is unaffected: every codex-branch caller grants ~/.codex writable with only config.toml re-bound read-only, so the Codex runtime's instruction surface is writable to any seat granted it, and fortkit-5sk kernel-locked the identical surface for the Claude runtime. ForgeOs/fort/scripts/forge.sh:77-78 names the concern in this civilization's own code.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE. The claim in the TITLE ('it cannot be fixed by an RO bind') and the startup-write measurement in the description. The launch-abort risk may still be real — the Regent cites the ~/.claude/teams precedent as independent grounds, and leaving the directories alone remains the conservative default — but IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and nobody should treat this bead as having measured it. Whoever takes this bead must measure the host mtimes from an UNMASKED shell, because no masked seat can see them.

METHOD NOTE FOR THE LEDGER: this is the fifth instance of the class the 2026-08-12 handoff named — inferring a fact about a system from the artifact in front of me without naming the baseline. Here the unnamed baseline was WHOSE FILESYSTEM I WAS LOOKING AT.

title: E2 Warden follow-ups 3-9: a glob that can abort every launch (one character class), fort-init's stranded registry write, the .beads hooks carve-out, and four record/template gaps
description:
WARDEN FINDINGS 3-9 ON E2, all NON-BLOCKING (Ilva Trueglass, 2026-08-12). Findings 1 and 2 are
BLOCKING and live on fortkit-vkq8 and fortkit-x9ou. Her overall judgement: "the mask design
itself is sound."

=== FINDING 5 FIRST, BECAUSE ITS FAILURE MODE IS THE ONE THIS SITTING EXISTED TO AVOID ===

SECRET_GLOBS (seat-sandbox.sh:86) grew from one pattern to six for fortkit-2kub, and TWO of
them — *env*~ and #*env*# — DO NOT START WITH A DOT and therefore match ordinary names. The
filter is still [ -e "$f" ] at :99, so a DIRECTORY named e.g. environments~ would be added to
MASK_FILES, and :330's mask+=(--ro-bind /dev/null "$f") would ABORT BWRAP.

FAILURE MODE: NO SEAT LAUNCHES. That is precisely the blast radius the whole E2 brief was
written around, arriving through the fix rather than the mask.

MEASURED BY ME: no such directory exists in any of the three forts today (find -maxdepth 2 for
*env*~ and #*env*# of type d, all three repos, empty). So this is latent, not live. Confirmed
[ -e ] at both :99 and :330.

FIX: [ -f "$f" ] instead of [ -e "$f" ]. Ilva's words: "costs nothing." Do it at :99, and
consider :330 as well for belt. This is one character class against "no seat in the
civilization can start", so it should not wait for a convenient sitting.

=== FINDING 4: 5sk STRANDED bin/fort-init's REGISTRY WRITE, UNDISCLOSED ===

bin/fort-init:164 writes ${FORT_REGISTRY:-$HOME/.claude/civilization.json}, and that path is
now kernel-RO. FOUNDING A SETTLEMENT FROM INSIDE A MASKED SEAT WILL FAIL EROFS.

Same class as the skills-install lane, which WAS disclosed carefully in both the lib comment
and civ/remember.md. The registry write was not. Not a defect in the decision — founding is
already Overseer/Regent work — but a gap in its record, and the kind that costs someone an
afternoon. Remedy: one sentence beside the skills/ note.

Related: fortkit-4n8c (symlink the installed skills) and fortkit-uhvt (fort-init founds
without fort/memory/). Both touch the same "what can still write ~/.claude" question.

=== FINDING 3: 1q9's PER-TREE ITERATION SKIPPED THE .beads HOOKS GUARD ===

Her words: "the highest-consequence carve-out." The .beads hooks guard was not included in the
per-tree iteration, so it is applied to $root and not to the other declared trees. Read her
full text on fortkit-52vf.3 before implementing; I am recording the headline rather than
paraphrasing a mechanism I have not measured.

=== FINDING 6: THE FACTORY SHIPS THE $root-worktrees ARGUMENT WITH NONE OF ITS RATIONALE ===

templates/ carries the new argument but not the reasoning that explains why it exists, so a
fort founded from it inherits a mechanism nobody there can justify. Same class as
fortkit-xgul.8's items 8 and 9 (template charter prescribing a retired command, template
pointing at a spec path it will not have).

=== FINDING 7: TWO RECORDS GIVE DIFFERENT SOLE CAUSES FOR 6ovg ===

A record-consistency defect, and it matters because 6ovg is now cited in the charter. Reconcile
so both records name the same cause, and append rather than edit (SO7).

=== FINDING 8: probe-cycle7.sh's TWO NEW MUTATING PROBES ARE CLEANED UP OUTSIDE THE TRAP ===

So an interrupted or failing probe run leaves its canaries behind. The probe writes a canary
under fort/memory/facts/ and another in fort/scripts/ (the disclosed-residual probe), and
residue in either place is exactly the kind of stray artifact this fort has cleaned up by hand
before (Warden ow7 finding 7, the bare-UUID 'mkdir' file). Move both cleanups into the trap.

=== FINDING 9: THE known_hosts FIX CHANGES ssh BEHAVIOUR IN-MASK, CORRECTLY, AND WORTH KNOWING ===

fortkit-pfiv fixed a real ordering bug — the known_hosts re-bind was buried under the ~/.ssh
tmpfs in 3 of 4 copies — so host-key verification now actually works in-mask where it silently
did not. Behaviour change, in the right direction, but seats that previously saw no host-key
checking will now see it. Recorded so a future "ssh suddenly complains" is not mistaken for a
regression.

description:
Found by the four-way diff fortkit-52vf.3 mandated, and FIXED IN THAT EDICT rather than deferred, because both are one-line changes already proven in production in the fort that had them. Filed so the change is reviewable on its own terms rather than buried inside E2's four named defects.

DEFECT 1 — known_hosts buried (ForgeOs-q6m, never backported). fortkit, longburn and templates/ all carried
  [ -e $HOME/.ssh/known_hosts ] && mask+=(--ro-bind ...)
BEFORE the MASK_DIRS loop that does --tmpfs $HOME/.ssh. Mounts stack, so the tmpfs landed on top and the bind had NEVER had any effect in those three: every masked launch did fresh TOFU against a known_hosts that dies with the tmpfs. ForgeOs found and fixed this on 2026-08-08 (Warden finding 3 on the 01l review) and the fix was never carried. E2 relocates it to the tail of build_mask in the other three, matching ForgeOs byte-for-byte in placement.

DEFECT 2 — no return 0 (ForgeOs-vzn class). build_mask's last statement in longburn was the MASK_DIRS for-loop, whose status is the last [ -d ] test. If the final MASK_DIR does not exist the function returns 1, and longburn's warden.sh and forge.sh both run set -euo pipefail, so the launcher would ABORT BEFORE THE SESSION STARTS. Latent, not live: longburn's last claude-branch MASK_DIRS entries are $HOME/.codex/sessions and $HOME/.codex/log, both of which exist on this host today (measured). fortkit's tail was an if/fi and returned 0 safely. ForgeOs already had the explicit return 0. E2 adds it to the other three, so no future edit to the tail can reintroduce the class.

This is the shape the memory ledger already warns about: a fix that lands in one fort's copy and is never grepped for in the others. Consolidation debt (fortkit-6jf) is what lets it happen.
design: Both changes are in the E2 diff for fortkit/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh, longburn/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh and templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh. ForgeOs's copy is UNCHANGED by them — it was already correct and is the reference. Verification: E2 harness 52/52 on all four generated libs; three real Warden smokes and three real Mayor launches, all of which build_mask successfully under their launchers' own set -euo pipefail (ForgeOs probe-boundaries seat-mask-build:mayor and :warden both PASS, 175 and 178 argv entries).

title: Nothing has ever removed a Forge worktree: 76 exist, 17GB, 74 belong to closed-and-merged beads — and each holds a writable copy of the enforcement layer
description:
FILED on the Overseer's question 2026-08-12: "why so many worktrees? they should be temporary
and cleaned out once totally done, merged, etc right?" He is right, they are not, and nothing
in the fort has ever removed one. MEASURED BY ME, not estimated:

  worktrees under /home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees        76
  disk                                                      17 GB
  whose bead is CLOSED                                       74
  whose bead is open or in_progress                           2
  with no matching bead                                       0
  CLOSED **and fully merged into main** (safe to remove)     74
  closed but NOT fully merged (would lose work)               0
  occurrences of 'worktree remove' or 'worktree prune' in fort/scripts/forge.sh   ZERO

So every Forge dispatch since the fort was founded has left its worktree behind, and no
mechanism has ever reclaimed one. There is no cleanup step in the launcher, no cron, and no bead
— I searched before filing.

THE DISK IS THE LEAST OF IT. Two consequences matter more:

1. SECURITY SURFACE, and it is live rather than theoretical. fortkit-1q9 is confirmed by probe
   (2026-08-12, recorded on that bead): the cycle-7 read-only carve-outs are scoped to $root and
   NOT to $root-worktrees, so every one of these directories holds a WRITABLE copy of the
   enforcement layer — fort/scripts/, fort/profiles/, .claude/. That is 74 abandoned writable
   copies of the constitution, belonging to work that finished days ago. The fort's stated
   position is that no masked seat can change its own enforcement layer; 74 stale worktrees are
   74 places where that is false.

2. IT MAKES THE 1q9 FIX WORSE THE LONGER IT WAITS. A naive implementation iterating every tree
   in RW_PATHS emits roughly 8 carve-outs x 76 trees = ~600 extra --ro-bind arguments per
   launch, growing without bound. E2's spec already says to scope carve-outs to the worktree in
   play rather than iterate, so the fix does not DEPEND on cleanup — but cleanup shrinks the
   problem from 76 to 2 and makes the whole area easier to reason about.

CLEANUP IS SAFE TODAY, and that is measured rather than assumed: all 74 closed-bead branches are
ancestors of main (git merge-base --is-ancestor bead/<s> main, 74/74). Nothing is lost by
removing the worktrees — the branches remain, and every commit is already on main. `git worktree
remove` deletes only the checkout.

PROPOSED, and it is two separable pieces:
  (a) ONE-TIME RECLAIM: remove the 74 worktrees whose bead is closed and whose branch is merged.
      Re-derive both conditions at run time rather than trusting this bead's counts; they will
      have drifted. Leave the 2 live ones. Consider whether the merged bead/* BRANCHES should
      also be pruned or deliberately kept as history — that is a separate decision and SO7 has
      nothing to say about git branches, so it is a preference rather than a rule.
  (b) A LIFECYCLE SO IT DOES NOT RECUR: the natural moment is the Mayor's close-after-merge
      step, which already knows the bead id and has just verified the merge. Removing the
      worktree there is a two-line addition to a path that runs every time. The alternative — a
      cron sweeping merged-and-closed worktrees — is more machinery for the same effect and adds
      a watcher the charter would want earned.

LANE: (a) is the Mayor's, right now: $root-worktrees is in RW_PATHS and .git/worktrees is not in
any RO list, so a masked Mayor can do it. (b) touches fort/scripts/forge.sh or the Mayor's own
close procedure; the forge.sh half is kernel-RO and belongs to a sitting, the procedure half is
prose.

DO NOT COUPLE THIS TO E2. E2's spec already handles the 76 correctly by scoping rather than
iterating, and making the highest-risk sitting in the programme depend on a 17GB cleanup would
be trading real risk for tidiness.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
SECOND HALF ADDED 2026-08-13, WITH PROOF, and the first half is DONE.

=== FIRST HALF EXECUTED (Overseer-authorized 2026-08-13: 'ones that are truly done and past, merged, and closed should be pruned') ===
74 worktree/branch PAIRS removed. Gate applied per tree, all four conditions required: bead status CLOSED, branch fully merged into main, 'git status --porcelain' empty (no modified AND no untracked non-ignored content), and no live .forge.lock.info. Executed with git's own guards rather than force — 'git worktree remove' (refuses a dirty tree) and 'git branch -d' (refuses an unmerged branch), no -f and no -D, so git independently re-checked every removal. 74 removed, ZERO refusals. Disk 17048MB -> 673MB, 16375MB reclaimed. Kept: 1gz3 and n3bk.1 (unmerged, awaiting Warden), 6jf and hn2 (beads in_progress). Post-state: 4 worktrees, verify.sh exit 0, 'git worktree prune --dry-run' finds nothing stale.

=== SECOND HALF: THE LAUNCHER MUST DO THIS, AND WORKTREE AND BRANCH ARE A PAIR ===
PROVEN, not asserted. fort/scripts/forge.sh:15-17 is 'if [ ! -d "$wt" ]; then git worktree add "$wt" -b "bead/$suffix"; fi' — the -b is UNCONDITIONAL, guarded only on the DIRECTORY. Tested directly: 'git worktree add <scratch> -b bead/ybg7' returns 'fatal: a branch named bead/ybg7 already exists', clean failure, nothing created.

CONSEQUENCE: round-2 dispatch works today only BECAUSE the worktree persists and the if short-circuits (that is how vhk.9 reached r2 and r3). Remove a worktree while leaving its branch and that bead can NEVER be dispatched again — the launcher dies at line 15, before claiming the bead, before emitting anything. So any cleanup must remove BOTH or NEITHER, which is why the sweep above did exactly that.

A LIVE INSTANCE ALREADY EXISTS, found immediately after the sweep: branch bead/m0wm has no worktree (the Regent removed its own probe tree during edict fortkit-52vf.10 and left the branch). fortkit-m0wm is a throwaway probe bead so the impact is nil, but it is the trap occurring in the wild within hours of the mechanism being identified, and it will happen again every time a seat removes a tree by hand.

FIX WANTED (Regent lane, fort/scripts/): forge.sh either reuses an existing branch instead of failing on -b, or removes tree AND branch together when a bead closes merged. Until then this pairing is hand-maintained, which is the class of thing that gets forgotten exactly once. Natural companion to the next launcher sitting; NOT to be bolted onto fortkit-52vf.10.

title: bin/civ-index truncates gate text mid-word with no disclosure: the handbook now silently drops Manyhalls' cycle-7 amendment, the clause defining the write boundaries (Warden E1 finding 1)
description:
WARDEN FINDING 1 on the E1 edict review (Ilva Trueglass, 2026-08-12, non-blocking). Surfaced
by E1 rather than caused by it, and the failure mode is the one this civilization keeps
recording.

THE DEFECT. bin/civ-index:129 emits line.strip()[:220] per gate line — a hard character cap
with NO disclosure. In the newly regenerated civ/CIVILIZATION.md:

  Manyhalls' gate 1 now ends at "(Amendm"
  Farlantern's gate 4 now ends at "→ Warden + Over"

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOST, and it is not cosmetic: Manyhalls' gate 1 truncates mid-word at exactly
the point where the CYCLE-7 AMENDMENT begins — the sentence that says which paths are kernel-RO
and which are prose-gated. So the civilization's own handbook, the document a stranger reads to
learn what the gates are, silently drops the clause that defines the current write boundaries.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED HERE. The cap predates the E1 range. It became VISIBLE because the
charters grew and because E1 regenerated a file that had been stale for seven days
(Generated stamp moved 2026-08-05 -> 2026-08-12). Ilva was explicit that nothing here is made
worse by E1's commit.

THE STANDARD FOR THE FIX IS IN THE SAME COMMIT, which is what makes this worth doing rather
than shrugging at. E1 gave bin/regent a cap that "always DISCLOSES itself, never truncates
silently" — it prints "[truncated at N of M lines — read <path> in full]". civ-index does the
opposite, in the same commit, in the same lane, for the same reason. One of the two is right.

FIX: truncate on a word or clause boundary and append an explicit marker, e.g.
"… [truncated — see <repo>/fort/charter.md]". Match bin/regent's disclosure wording so the two
capital generators behave the same way.

AND THE CLASS IS THE POINT. This fort has now recorded seven controls or records that reported
success while silently losing or proving nothing: probe-cycle7's vacuous positive control,
memory-lint's near-duplicate blindness, warden.sh's verdict_recorded:true, verify.sh's silent
steps, consolidate-memory's epoch-0 handoffs, warden.sh's head-truncated verdict display, and
now this. Every one is a mechanism that produced OUTPUT rather than an ERROR when it could not
do its job. That is worth naming as a recurring class rather than fixing seven times.

MY OWN VERIFICATION MISSED IT, recorded so the gap in method is visible: my E1 verification
comment said "civ/CIVILIZATION.md:108 REGENERATED to match, so the handbook no longer
advertises the stub. Generator and output agree." True of line 108. I checked the line E1 was
about and did not read the rest of the file it had just rewritten.

LANE: bin/civ-index is kernel-RO. Regent. Cheap enough to ride along with another civ/ or bin/
sitting rather than justify one — and note the E1 Regent recorded that bin/ needs the
Overseer's hand for the actual file write.

title: Shipped skills are installed as independent untracked copies, so the loaded instruction can silently diverge from its reviewed source — and it already defeated one verification
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 by Emrith, as the structural cause behind a false bead close of my own
(fortkit-4b9q, corrected under SO7 on that bead). Filed because the class has no watcher, no
bead, and no test, and it silently defeated a verification.

THE SURFACE. This repository ships skills that are INSTALLED as independent copies:

  fortkit/skills/civ/SKILL.md            source, tracked in git
  ~/.claude/skills/civ/SKILL.md          installed, a REGULAR FILE, untracked
  fortkit/skills/fort-backport/SKILL.md  same shape
  ~/.claude/skills/fort-backport/...     presumably the same

They are COPIES. Nothing keeps them in sync, nothing detects divergence, and the installed
copy is the one every session actually loads.

CONTRAST WITH THE CASE THAT CANNOT DRIFT, measured today: ~/.local/bin/regent is a SYMLINK to
fortkit/bin/regent, so the Regent launcher physically cannot diverge from its source. The
skills chose the other pattern. One of those two is right for this civilization and it should
be a decision rather than an accident of how each was installed.

HOW IT BIT. Working fortkit-4b9q (a one-line doc repoint), I edited the INSTALLED copy, then
grepped the INSTALLED copy to confirm the fix, and closed the bead. The repository's copy was
untouched and still carried the retired reference. The verification was circular — I checked
the file I had just edited — and the tracker carried a false close until Ilva caught it as
finding 5 on the fortkit-xgul.7.1 review.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST MY MISTAKE. Two independent copies where the loaded one is untracked is a
setup that rewards exactly that mistake: whichever copy you touch, grepping it proves nothing
about the other, and the untracked one is invisible to git status, to the verifier, to
memory-lint's retired-reference check, and to the drift watcher. All four of the fort's
existing controls look only at the repository.

WHAT IT MEANS BEYOND THIS ONE LINE, and this is the reason for the priority: the installed
skill is SESSION-EXECUTED INSTRUCTION. It is loaded into every session that invokes /civ.
An installed copy that has drifted from its reviewed source is unreviewed instruction running
in every seat, and that is precisely the class cycle 7 closed for fort config with "write
access follows execution context". fortkit-5sk already names ~/.claude/skills among the
paths that should be kernel-RO to masked seats and is carried by E2 (fortkit-52vf.3). This
bead is the OTHER half: 5sk stops a seat WRITING it, and nothing verifies it MATCHES its source.

CANDIDATE FIXES, cheapest first:
  (a) SYMLINK the installed skills to the repo, as ~/.local/bin/regent already does. Drift
      becomes impossible rather than detectable. Interacts with 5sk: a symlinked path inherits
      the target's mask, which needs checking, not assuming.
  (b) A verifier step comparing every fortkit/skills/*/SKILL.md against its installed
      counterpart, failing on divergence and on absence. Cheap, and it makes the invariant
      testable where (a) makes it structural.
  (c) Extend memory-lint's retired-reference check to the installed paths. Narrowest; catches
      only this defect class, not general drift.
RECOMMEND (a) plus (b): symlink so it cannot drift, and a test so the symlink cannot be
quietly replaced by a copy later. Sequence AFTER E2, and check with E2 whether making
~/.claude/skills kernel-RO breaks an install step that expects to write there.

ALSO CHECK, not yet done: whether fort-backport's copies already diverge, and whether any
OTHER fortkit-shipped artifact is installed by copy rather than symlink. I verified only that
the two civ copies are byte-identical NOW, after I fixed both.
close_reason: E2b cluster closed 2026-08-13; evidence and the deliberate no-re-review judgement recorded on fortkit-52vf.9. Its blockers are now closed.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text: ANSWERED BY E2, and the lane it broke is now the Overseer's or the Regent's. ~/.claude/skills is kernel-RO as of E2 (fortkit-5sk landed), and NOTHING AUTOMATES THE INSTALL — the E2 Regent recorded that the only mechanism to date was 'Emrith hand-copied skills/civ/SKILL.md from inside her mask at 13:42 on the day of this edict', which is exactly the writability E2 removed. So this bead's recommendation (symlink the installed copies to the repo, as ~/.local/bin/regent already is) now has its answer AND restores a lane that is currently broken: no masked seat can update an installed skill, and no automation does it either. Until this lands, a change to fortkit/skills/*/SKILL.md does not reach the loaded copy at all.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
FIXED, E2b (fortkit-52vf.9) item F, commit 29d1539 — and the bead was more right than it knew.

Recommendation (a) plus (b), as filed. ~/.claude/skills/{civ,fort-backport} are
now SYMLINKS to skills/<name>, the shape ~/.local/bin/regent already had, and
verify.sh gained a skills-install step that fails if any skills/*/ lacks an
installed counterpart that is a symlink resolving to it. That step FAILS when it
examines zero skills and ANNOUNCES a skip rather than passing silently when
~/.claude/skills does not exist. Negative control run: replacing one symlink
with a copy fails the step naming the path; restoring it passes.

WHAT I FOUND ON THE WAY, WHICH IS THIS BEAD ARGUED IN BYTES: the installed /civ
skill had ALREADY DIVERGED. 4059 bytes against the repo sources 4057, ending in
a literal "xx" with no trailing newline, mtime 2026-08-12 14:58:07 — the E2 mask
harnesss positive-control append (fortkit-qbq2). ~/.claude/commands/park.md had
the same two bytes. qbq2 repaired the two JSON files it damaged because they
broke loudly and left the two markdown ones because they did not, so
session-executed instruction ran for eight hours carrying probe residue, and no
control in this fort could see it. Both repaired; recorded on qbq2.

THE 5sk INTERACTION, checked rather than assumed, as the bead asked. A symlink
does NOT inherit its targets mask: with ~/.claude/skills kernel-RO and skills/
in the repo writable, a masked seat could change the loaded instruction by
editing a tracked file. So skills/ was given the SAME treatment as fort/charter.md
and fort/seats/ — prose-gated for attended seats, kernel-RO for the Forge, which
cannot ask first. That is the cycle-7 line applied to a surface that is exactly
prose binding through a sessions own reading of it. Measured: skills/ writable
in the Mayor posture, blocked in the codex posture, in the live capital.

STILL UNCHECKED, and this bead asked for it: whether any OTHER fortkit-shipped
artifact is installed by copy rather than symlink. I checked only the two skills.
~/.claude/commands/park.md is installed-by-hand with no repo source at all,
which is a third pattern again.

title: [bug] skills/civ/SKILL.md:29 still advertises the retired fort/remember.md — same defect as bin/civ-index:141, but in the Mayor's lane
description:
FOUND BY THE REGENT during fortkit-52vf.1 (E1), 2026-08-12, while sweeping for live references. NOT in E1's scope and deliberately not fixed by the edict: skills/ is not kernel-RO, so this fort's own Forge can do it and least force says it should (covenant standing order 3).

skills/civ/SKILL.md:29 carries the table row:
  | What must a session here know operationally | `<repo>/fort/remember.md` |

That is the same row, in the same words, that bin/civ-index:141 emitted into the
handbook and that E1 has just repointed. The /civ skill is the lookup path every
non-Regent session is told to use, so the retired path is still being advertised
to readers by the capital's own skill while the handbook it mirrors no longer
does.

REPLACEMENT, matching what civ-index now emits:
  | What must a session here know operationally | `<repo>/fort/memory/current.md`
    (distilled view; ledger in `<repo>/fort/memory/facts/`) |

WORTH CHECKING IN THE SAME PASS: whether fortkit-xgul.7.1's widened
retired-reference guard should also cover skills/. It currently scans AGENTS.md,
CLAUDE.md, fort/charter.md, fort/seats/, templates/, fort/scripts/*.sh and bin/.
This row is exactly the kind of live instruction that guard exists to catch, and
it sits outside every one of those roots — which is why a human sweep found it
and the linter did not.
acceptance_criteria: skills/civ/SKILL.md names the ledger; a decision recorded on whether the retired-reference guard covers skills/
close_reason: NOW genuinely fixed, after a false close corrected under SO7 (see comments). BOTH copies repointed and verified independently: fortkit/skills/civ/SKILL.md (the tracked source, which my first attempt missed entirely) and ~/.claude/skills/civ/SKILL.md (the installed copy, which is what I edited and then circularly grepped). Both now at zero references and byte-identical to each other. Caught by Ilva, finding 5 on the fortkit-xgul.7.1 review, who named this bead as closed-claiming-otherwise. The two-copy drift surface is filed separately.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
CORRECTION under standing order 7, Emrith 2026-08-12. MY CLOSE OF THIS BEAD WAS WRONG, and
the bead is reopened above rather than quietly amended.

WHAT I CLAIMED when closing it: "skills/civ/SKILL.md:29 now reads 'fort/memory/current.md
(distilled view; facts ledger in fort/memory/facts/)' ... Verified: zero remaining references
in that file."

WHAT I ACTUALLY DID: edited /home/justin/.claude/skills/civ/SKILL.md — the INSTALLED copy —
and grepped that same installed copy to confirm it was clean. THE REPOSITORY'S COPY,
fortkit/skills/civ/SKILL.md:29, was untouched and still named the retired path. My
verification was circular: I checked the file I had just edited and concluded the defect was
gone, without asking whether that file was the source.

CAUGHT BY ILVA, finding 5 on the fortkit-xgul.7.1 review, which named it as still live "and
fortkit-4b9q is closed claiming otherwise". She was right and my close was a false record in
the tracker for about twenty minutes.

THE STRUCTURAL FACT I MISSED, and it is the durable part: THE SKILL EXISTS IN TWO PLACES AND
THEY ARE INDEPENDENT COPIES, not a symlink.

  fortkit/skills/civ/SKILL.md              the source, in the repository, tracked
  ~/.claude/skills/civ/SKILL.md            the installed copy, a regular file, untracked

Compare with ~/.local/bin/regent, which IS a symlink to fortkit/bin/regent and therefore
cannot drift. The skills are copies and can. Verified just now: after fixing both, they are
byte-identical (diff -q clean), so the only divergence was the one I created by fixing one.

NOW GENUINELY FIXED, both copies, verified separately:
  repo copy       grep -c 'fort/remember.md' -> 0
  installed copy  grep -c 'fort/remember.md' -> 0
  diff -q between them -> identical

THE LESSON, and it is the same one twice in one session: I inferred a state from the artifact
I had just touched instead of from the system. That is the third instance today of the same
method error — the drift-watcher diagnosis (read the symptom, asserted the mechanism), the
mayor.sh EXIT trap (read the trap, assumed it fires), and this (edited a copy, called the
class fixed). The common repair is to ask "what is the source of truth for this, and did I
check THAT" before recording a verification.

FILED SEPARATELY: the two-copy drift surface has no watcher and no bead. See the follow-up
filed alongside this correction.

title: The E7 deferral removes the backport loop's primary signal: never-propagated template files in the elder forts now report only as an aggregate count, and the argument for deferring them was repealed by the same commit (Warden E7 finding 1)
description:
WARDEN FINDING 1 on the E7 edict review (Ilva Trueglass, 2026-08-12, verdict
APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS, non-blocking). Her headline finding, and the sharpest piece of
reasoning in the review.

THE ARGUMENT, and it is the reason this is a real regression in signal rather than a
preference. The E7 spec amendment justified DEFERRING never-propagated findings with:
"a watcher that files an unfixable bead every run trains its fort to ignore it."

THAT WAS TRUE OF THE OLD CHURNING KEY. IT WAS REPEALED BY THE SAME COMMIT. Under the new
(fort, path) identity, a never-propagated finding would file EXACTLY ONE BEAD PER FORT+PATH,
EVER — later template edits append comments to it rather than filing again. So the
habituation hazard the deferral exists to prevent was eliminated by the identity fix in the
same change, and the deferral now removes signal to solve a problem the rest of the commit
already solved.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOST. The capital's case is genuinely permanent and deserves silence:
Manyhalls IS the template source, so a template file it has not hand-installed is not a
defect. But the ELDER FORTS' case is the backport loop's PRIMARY PURPOSE — a template file
that never reached Proofdelve or Farlantern is exactly what fortkit-or2 exists to surface.
For them, a never-propagated file now yields only an aggregate `findingsDeferred` count in
the drift.scan payload, with the fort+path pairs appearing SOLELY IN STDOUT, which on the
scheduled run is a systemd journal nobody reads.

So the mechanism that exists to make cross-fort divergence visible now reports the most
important class of divergence as a number.

IT ALSO WENT PAST THE BEAD'S OWN OPTIONS. fortkit-or2.8 offered three shapes (special-case
the capital / exclude fort/scripts / classify as pending-hand-install) and each of them
RECLASSIFIES rather than SILENCES. The edict chose a fourth shape that silences. That is
defensible and it was disclosed in the spec, the handoff and the bead comment, and it is
counted rather than hidden — which is precisely why Ilva filed it instead of blocking.

ILVA'S RECOMMENDATION: file once per identity for non-capital forts, or at minimum enumerate
the deferred fort+path pairs in the event payload.

MAYOR'S VIEW: take the first. Under the new identity the cost of filing is one bead per
fort+path for the lifetime of the divergence, which is the correct cost of a real finding,
and fortkit-vhk.7 (the propagation epic) is where they would be worked. The aggregate count
is not a substitute: a number cannot be triaged, dependency-linked, or closed. If the
Overseer prefers to keep the silence, then the payload enumeration is the floor, because a
finding whose only home is a journal line is a finding the fort does not have.

LANE: civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs, kernel-RO. Regent. Ilva notes it is ONE LINE TO REVERSE.
Natural home: fold into the next civ/scripts sitting rather than waking the Regent for it
alone — and note the Regent recorded that civ/scripts/ needs two round trips through the
Overseer's hand, so a one-line change there is not a cheap change.

title: Audit every bare 'bd ... --json' parse in the civilization for the v2.0 envelope assumption
description:
Carried forward from fortkit-pp1k, whose fix landed in Regent edict E7 (fortkit-52vf.8, commit c6875a6, 2026-08-12) but covered only civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs.

pp1k's second ask, unaddressed by that edict: every OTHER consumer of 'bd ... --json' in the civilization makes the same assumption — that the output is a bare top-level array. bd 1.1.2 warns on every --json call that v2.0 moves to an envelope, and BD_JSON_ENVELOPE=1 already produces it today ({data:[...], schema_version:1}).

drift-watch.mjs now has an exported rows() helper that accepts either shape and throws a named error on neither. It is the reference implementation; the audit should either import it or copy the three lines.

SCOPE: all three forts plus civ/ and bin/. Grep for 'bd' with '--json' in shell scripts, .mjs and .ts. Known unaudited surfaces at filing time: bin/civ-index, fort/scripts/*.sh across three forts, src/ readers, any skill or hook.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the same argument as pp1k. These parses live in unattended or semi-attended paths, and a shape error surfaces as a stack trace in a journal rather than in front of a human. A consumer that throws on every run reports no data, which is indistinguishable from no data existing.

title: The Warden cannot execute a differential proof against a base revision, so she cannot run the anti-vacuity check the fort demands of every GPT-family diff — twice in two reviews, both times she disclosed it
description:
OBSERVED TWICE IN TWO CONSECUTIVE REVIEWS, both on 2026-08-12, both raised by the Warden
against her own review rather than found by anyone else. SO11 satisfied by two
measurements, and the second one makes it a pattern rather than an incident.

THE GAP. Ilva cannot execute a DIFFERENTIAL PROOF: she cannot stand up a second tree, put
the base revision's implementation in it, and run the candidate's tests against it. Her
profile denies node -e (requires approval), mkdir outside her three working directories,
and output redirection, and she holds no write tool.

OCCURRENCE 1 — fortkit-ybg7. The bead's acceptance criterion was explicit: "The test must
FAIL against the current implementation before the fix, or it is vacuous." Her words: "My
mask denies mkdir, output redirection, and node -e, so I could not stand up a second root
and run main's consolidator against the fixtures; I tried four spellings and all were
refused." She proved it by reading instead, laid out five failing assertions across two
mechanisms, and stated plainly that she had reasoned rather than run it.

OCCURRENCE 2 — fortkit-ij8j, the very next review. Same wall: "my profile refused every
route to running the pre-fix generator (node -e requires approval; mkdir outside the three
working directories is blocked; I have no write tool)." Again she proved it by construction
and again she said so.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY AN INCONVENIENCE. The fort's own review policy weights scrutiny by
which model produced the work, and the recorded flag on the GPT-5.6 family is REWARD
HACKING — which in practice means test vacuity. Ilva said so herself on ybg7: "GPT-5.6
family, so I put the extra scrutiny where that family's flag points — test vacuity." So
the fort asks "does this test actually discriminate" of a whole class of diffs BY POLICY,
and the seat it asks cannot run the check. The one review gate in the merge flow is
structurally unable to execute its own highest-priority verification for the majority of
the work it sees.

WHAT SAVED BOTH REVIEWS, and it is not a control: the MAYOR happened to run the proof
independently in both cases, before her verdicts arrived, and both times the executed
result agreed with her reasoning. That is redundancy by luck of sequencing, not by design.
Had the Mayor not run it, both beads would have merged with the non-vacuity requirement
satisfied by argument alone. And the Mayor is not a reviewer: relying on the dispatching
seat to supply the review's missing half inverts the independence the gate exists for.

CREDIT WHERE IT IS DUE, because the behaviour to preserve is as important as the gap to
close: she did the right thing twice. She attempted it, failed, named the refusals, gave
the reasoning, and labelled it as reasoned-not-executed under a "Verified independently vs
taken on faith" heading. A seat that quietly asserted the proof would have been far worse
than one that cannot run it. Do not "fix" this in a way that discourages that disclosure.

THE TENSION TO RESOLVE, and it is real rather than rhetorical: the Warden is READ-ONLY BY
CONSTRUCTION and that is a deliberate capability boundary, not an oversight. Granting mkdir
and a write path widens it. Candidate shapes, cheapest first:
  (a) A scratch tmpfs the Warden may write, INSIDE her existing scratch root, with nothing
      else granted. She already gets a writable scratch copy of the candidate tree; the
      question is only whether she may create a sibling directory in it.
  (b) The LAUNCHER stands up the base-revision tree for her, before the mask closes, so she
      needs no new write capability at all. warden.sh already builds her scratch by rsync
      and already knows the diff range, so it knows both revisions. This looks like the
      right answer: it buys the capability without widening the seat.
  (c) Make non-vacuity the FORGE's mandatory evidence — the Forge runs the base-revision
      check and records the output verbatim — with the Warden auditing the record rather
      than reproducing it. Cheapest, and weakest: it is the Forge attesting to its own
      test quality, which is precisely what the GPT-family flag says not to trust.
  (d) Accept it and make the MAYOR's independent execution a required step, recorded. Then
      it is a control rather than luck, but it costs the gate its independence.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: (b). It closes the gap without granting the Warden a single new
capability, and warden.sh already has both revisions in hand.

LANE: fort/scripts/warden.sh and/or fort/profiles/warden-settings.json, both kernel-RO.
Regent. Natural home is fortkit-52vf.7 (E6, profiles) if the answer is (a), or
fortkit-52vf.5 (E4, warden.sh) if it is (b) — decide the shape first, then route it.
ADJACENT: fortkit-hn2 (nondeterministic Warden permissions), fortkit-iz8 (allowlist
residuals and the write-capable-check trade-off), fortkit-a16 (inert Write rules).
