comments.text:
OVERSEER RULING 2026-08-12 (Mayor session F), recorded before implementation.

TYPED VERBATIM: "I approve of option b"

OPTION B, as it was put to him and is therefore the approved scope: have
fort/scripts/warden.sh build the BASE-REVISION tree for the Warden, on the host, BEFORE
the mask closes, and tell her where it is. She then only needs to RUN tests against it,
which she can already do.

WHY THIS SHAPE AND NOT THE OTHERS — the reasoning is part of the ruling and should travel
with it:

  It grants the Warden ZERO NEW CAPABILITIES. The work happens in the launcher, on the
  host, outside the sandbox. Her profile is untouched, and "read-only by construction"
  stays LITERALLY true rather than becoming an approximation. This is the same move cycle 7
  made when it decided write access follows execution context.

  The launcher already has everything it needs: it already rsyncs her scratch copy, and it
  already receives the diff range (e.g. main..bead/ij8j), so IT ALREADY KNOWS BOTH
  REVISIONS. Nothing new has to be discovered or plumbed in.

DECLINED, and why, so none of these get re-proposed:
  (a) a writable scratch subdirectory for the Warden — small, but it widens the seat and
      makes "read-only by construction" stop being literally true.
  (c) make non-vacuity the FORGE's mandatory evidence, with the Warden auditing the record
      — cheapest and weakest: it is the Forge attesting to its own test quality, which is
      exactly what the GPT-5.6-family reward-hacking flag says not to trust.
  (d) accept the gap and make the Mayor's independent execution a required recorded step —
      costs the gate its independence, and does not scale to reviews the Mayor is not
      present for.

ROUTING, and it changed because of this ruling: option (b) is a LAUNCHER change, not a
profile change, so it goes to fortkit-52vf.5 (E4, the warden.sh sitting) and NOT to
fortkit-52vf.7 (E6, profiles) where it would have gone under option (a). E4 is already one
of the six scheduled sittings, so this costs no additional sitting.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES for whoever builds it:
  - The base revision is the LEFT side of the diff range the launcher is already given.
    Derive it there; do not ask the seat to compute it.
  - Build it the same way her candidate scratch is built, and consider whether the
    node_modules bind (fortkit-8cv6) needs to reach it too — a base tree she cannot run
    vitest in is useless for this purpose. That is the likeliest way to ship this broken.
  - TELL HER IT EXISTS, in the launcher prompt, with the absolute path. A capability she is
    not told about is a capability she does not have; both of her disclosures show she
    reasons from what the prompt and her mask tell her.
  - ACCEPTANCE MUST BE A REAL DIFFERENTIAL RUN, not the directory's existence: a Warden
    session must execute a candidate test against the base tree and report the failure it
    observes. Anything less reproduces the exact gap this closes — a control that reports
    PASS while proving nothing, which this fort has now recorded four times (probe-cycle7's
    positive control, memory-lint's near-duplicate blindness, warden.sh's
    verdict_recorded:true, verify.sh's silent steps).

PRESERVE THE BEHAVIOUR THAT SURFACED THIS: Ilva attempted the proof, failed, named the
specific refusals, proved it by construction, and labelled it reasoned-not-executed under a
"verified independently vs taken on faith" heading — twice. Whatever lands must not make
that disclosure feel like a failure to report. The gap was found because she was honest
about it.

title: The interactions corpus is indexed as one undifferentiated 108KB blob row that recall cannot rank, scope or order — while the corpus already carries ts, actor and issue_id (Warden ij8j findings 1,3)
description:
WARDEN FINDINGS 1 and 3 on the fortkit-ij8j review (Ilva Trueglass, 2026-08-12, verdict
APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS, non-blocking).

=== FINDING 1: INDEXED, BUT AS ONE UNDIFFERENTIATED 108 KB BLOB ===

scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs:340-352 pushes the WHOLE interactions file as a SINGLE row
with ts: "", actor: "", scopeBeads: "" and snippet: <entire text>.

ILVA READ THE LIVE CORPUS and it already carries exactly the fields the row schema wants:
  {"id":...,"kind":...,"created_at":"2026-08-04T07:26:56Z",
   "actor":"Justin Schneider","issue_id":"fortkit-b37",...}
216 lines, 108 KB. And events.jsonl is ALREADY indexed line-by-line with precisely that
treatment, so the pattern exists in the same file.

docs/specs/memory.md section 5 requires each row to carry a "parsed timestamp (UTC ...),
actor/seat where known". So the corpus a reader will now tick off as indexed is one blob
row that `fortkit recall` (section 6.2) CANNOT RANK, SCOPE OR ORDER. Searching it returns
either everything or nothing.

WHY IT IS THIS BEAD'S PROBLEM RATHER THAN ij8j's: the blob shape is pre-existing code that
ij8j did not introduce. But ij8j is what makes that code path EXECUTE FOR THE FIRST TIME IN
ANY FORT, so this is the moment the latent gap becomes a real one. Ilva judged it
non-blocking on the correct ground: one blob row is strictly better than the corpus being
indexed in no fort at all, so merging does not make the fort worse.

FIX: split interactions per line, mapping created_at -> ts, actor -> actor,
issue_id -> scope_beads. Follow the events.jsonl treatment in the same file.

NOTE THE ADJACENT CONSTRAINT, so this does not get widened by accident: Ilva confirmed
under threat 2 that the interactions row goes ONLY to index.db and never to current.md.
That is what docs/specs/memory.md section 3 ruling 3 requires ("recall-searchable, never
injected"), because the corpus carries agent- and human-authored bead comment text.
Splitting into per-line rows must preserve that boundary exactly. Do not let a
line-by-line refactor leak interactions into the injected surface.

=== FINDING 3 (cosmetic): THE GAP LINE PRINTS THE PATH THREE TIMES ===

Rendered today:
  - .beads/interactions.jsonl: absent at searched path .beads/interactions.jsonl — [.beads/interactions.jsonl](.beads/interactions.jsonl)

It satisfies ij8j's item 2 (it names the path searched, and distinguishes "absent where I
looked" from the old "missing or not configured" which read as a deliberate choice), so
this is polish rather than a defect. reason: "absent" alone would read the same and
better. Fold it into the same pass as finding 1.

LANE: Forge. scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs and templates/fort/memory/consolidate-memory.mjs
plus tests. Nothing kernel-RO. Re-check the merge implication before dispatch per the
correction on fortkit-xgul.7.1.

title: Nothing enforces the handoff header schema at write time: seven violations by three seats in six days, all with the schema in their own seat file (Warden ybg7 finding 5)
description:
WARDEN FINDING 5 on the fortkit-ybg7 review (Ilva Trueglass, 2026-08-12, non-blocking).
She named it as one of the three she wanted filed before that bead closes.

THE GAP. fort/seats/mayor.md:22 specifies the handoff header schema:

    # Handoff: <seat> <ISO timestamp>

and scripts/memory-lint.mjs has NO handoff check at all. Nothing enforces the schema at
WRITE time. fortkit-ybg7 made the READ side loud about violations, which Ilva explicitly
called the correct half to fix first, but the recurrence prevention is a write-side lint
and it does not exist.

THE EVIDENCE THAT IT IS NEEDED IS THE SEVEN EXISTING VIOLATIONS, written by three
different seats over six days, every one of them by an agent that had the schema in its
own seat file:

  forge-2026-08-07-6jf.md      "—"                        (not a timestamp at all)
  mayor-2026-08-06-a.md        "2026-08-06T~12:45-08:00"   (approximate form)
  mayor-2026-08-07.md          "2026-08-07T~11:45-08:00"
  mayor-2026-08-08-a.md        "2026-08-08T~23:30-08:00"
  mayor-2026-08-10-b.md        "2026-08-10T"              (date, no time)
  mayor-2026-08-11-b.md        "2026-08-11T"              (session D)
  mayor-2026-08-11.md          "2026-08-11T"              (session C)

That is the argument for mechanical enforcement in its purest form, and it is the
fort's own standing lesson: when a constraint keeps getting violated despite prose
instructions, encode it as a test. Prose in a seat file did not hold for seven
handoffs across three seats. Note also that session E's handoff RECOMMENDED writing
full instants as a stopgap, and this session complied, which shows the prose can work
when a session happens to read the right handoff — and that is precisely the fragility.

SCOPE: add a handoff-header check to memory-lint over fort/handoffs/*.md. Decide
deliberately whether it goes RED on the seven existing violations or grandfathers them:
  - Going red immediately makes the verifier fail on committed history the fort is
    forbidden to edit in place (standing order 7, and see fortkit-cz1r), which would
    block every bead in the fort from closing. Do NOT ship that.
  - So it must either grandfather the existing seven explicitly by name, or lint only
    files newer than a recorded cutoff. Grandfathering by name is more honest and
    self-documenting, and the list shrinks to zero if cz1r's ruling recovers them.

THIS IS THE SAME TRAP fortkit-xgul.7.1 walked into tonight: a widened verifier inherits
the lane of everything it now judges, and a lint that indicts records nobody may edit
turns main red indefinitely. Read the correction on fortkit-xgul.7.1 before implementing.

DEPENDS ON fortkit-cz1r's ruling for the grandfathering decision. LANE: Forge (scripts/,
templates/, test/).

title: Two parsers over one handoff corpus disagree about validity, and the disagreement decides inclusion — plus unparseable handoffs now leave index.db entirely (Warden ybg7 findings 1,2,4,6,7)
description:
WARDEN FINDINGS 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 on the fortkit-ybg7 review (Ilva Trueglass,
2026-08-12, verdict APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS, none blocking). Ilva asked for 1 and 2 to be
filed TOGETHER, because both are answered by teaching the consolidator the reader's
parser and the annals row-shape. 4, 6 and 7 fold in as the same code path.

=== FINDING 1: TWO READERS OVER ONE CORPUS WITH TWO DEFINITIONS OF "VALID" ===

src/readers/handoffs.ts:39-47 DELIBERATELY parses the fort's approximate-stamp form
("2026-08-06T~12:45-08:00"), and that tolerance is ASSERTED as intended behaviour in
test/world.test.ts:1210. scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs now calls the same three live
handoffs unparseable and drops them — mayor-2026-08-06-a.md, mayor-2026-08-07.md and
mayor-2026-08-08-a.md are three of the seven new gap lines.

So the fort has two parsers over one corpus, disagreeing, and the disagreement DECIDES
INCLUSION. Ilva's note on why it travels: both copies of this generator ship to every
fort founded from the template, so the divergence propagates.

RESOLUTION SHAPE, hers: converge on one parser, and she recommends the TS reader's regex
as the more battle-tested. OR, if strictness is the intended ruling, decide that ONCE and
make the TS reader agree. Either is defensible; having both is not.

=== FINDING 2: DROPPED FROM THE INDEXED CORPUS, NOT MERELY FROM SELECTION ===

The `continue` at scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs:243 skips the row-building loop, so
seven live Manyhalls handoffs' "State of work" and "Next actions" leave index.db entirely
and become INVISIBLE TO `fortkit recall`. docs/specs/memory.md section 5 lists handoff
sections in the indexed corpus, so this is a spec divergence rather than a preference.

THE SPEC ALREADY HAS THE RIGHT PATTERN, section 6.2, for rows with no parsed timestamp
(annals, interactions): index them, exclude them from --since/--until windows, disclose
the exclusion. Better shape here: keep the gap line and the exclusion from latest-handoff
SELECTION, but index the sections with an EMPTY ts.

CONSTRAINT IF IMPLEMENTED, and it is easy to get wrong: section 5's dpu/schema pinning
rule FORBIDS a filename-derived row timestamp. The value must be empty, not the filename
date.

WHY ILVA JUDGED THIS NON-BLOCKING, recorded because the reasoning is the useful part: the
PRIOR behaviour indexed those rows under a FALSE 1970-01-01 timestamp, which standing
order 7 likes even less than absence. The loss is now disclosed rather than silent, so
the diff is a strict improvement even though it is not the end state.

=== FINDING 4: A SEAT WHOSE HANDOFFS ARE ALL MALFORMED VANISHES SILENTLY ===

Such a seat disappears from "Latest handoffs" with no SEAT-LEVEL disclosure; only
per-file gap lines explain it, at the other end of the document. LATENT, not live: only
forge and mayor have handoffs in Manyhalls today and both have valid entries. Ilva folded
it here deliberately.

=== FINDING 6 (nit): AN UNREACHABLE GUARD ===

The second leg of compareHandoffFiles is dead. Every candidate name ends in .md by
construction (files(dir, ".md")), so equal .md-stripped names imply identical names and
`|| compare(left, right)` can never fire. Harmless, but it reads as a guard that guards
nothing, which is the shape this fort keeps getting bitten by.

=== FINDING 7: SUFFIX ORDERING IS LEXICOGRAPHIC — THE SAME CLASS AS THE BUG JUST FIXED ===

"-r10" sorts before "-r9", and bead-id suffixes (forge-2026-08-11-6jf vs -ybg7) order
alphabetically rather than chronologically. Only reachable when parsed instants tie
EXACTLY, which real launcher-stamped Forge handoffs do not, so it is latent. Ilva
recorded it anyway with the reason that matters: "the bead's own lesson is that this
class hides until a day gets busy."

=== RELATED, DO NOT DUPLICATE ===

fortkit-cz1r holds the LAW question this bead's finding 2 partially answers: seven
committed handoffs are unreadable to the view, and repairing their headers is what
standing order 7 forbids. Finding 2 recovers their CONTENT into the index without
touching the headers, which is close to cz1r's option (b) and may make the ruling
cheaper. Sequence: read cz1r before implementing finding 2, and if the Overseer picks a
sidecar-correction mechanism there, these two are one piece of work.

LANE: Forge. scripts/, src/, templates/, test/ — nothing kernel-RO. But re-check the
merge implication before dispatch, per the correction recorded on fortkit-xgul.7.1: a
change to what the consolidator considers valid changes what current.md says in every
fort.

title: forge.sh exits 0 and prints the Warden-review recipe when its own launcher-observed verify.sh exited 1 — the gate order is inverted in the record
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-11 (Mayor session F), on the fortkit-xgul.7.1 dispatch. Same class as
fortkit-bfsu (a false field in an append-only record) and the "unconditional recipe
prose" half of fortkit-f8ol, but in forge.sh rather than warden.sh.

WHAT HAPPENED, from the launcher's own captured output:

  --- forge.sh: launcher-observed verify.sh exit 1 (/tmp/forge-xgul.7.1-verify.log)
  --- forge.sh: session ended (exit 0). Worktree: ...
  --- Next: Warden reviews (fort/scripts/warden.sh fortkit-xgul.7.1 main..bead/xgul.7.1), then the Mayor merges.

So the launcher OBSERVED the authoritative verifier fail, correctly recorded that
observation on the line above, and then reported session exit 0 and printed the
merge-flow recipe as though the gate had been met. The three lines contradict each
other and the last one is the one a dispatching Mayor acts on.

TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS:

1. THE EXIT CODE DOES NOT REFLECT THE OBSERVED VERIFIER. forge.sh exits 0 when its own
   launcher-observed verify.sh exited 1. A harness or a Mayor that keys off exit status
   — which is the normal thing to do, and which this session's task notification did —
   is told the dispatch succeeded. The verifier result is available to the launcher; it
   is simply not propagated.

2. THE "Next:" PROSE IS UNCONDITIONAL. It recommends a Warden review and a Mayor merge
   regardless of the verifier outcome. The charter's merge flow is "Forge commits ->
   verifiers -> Warden review -> merge", with the verifier BEFORE the review. Printing
   the recipe after a red verifier inverts the fort's own gate order, and it invites
   spending a frontier review on a branch that cannot merge.

WHY THIS ONE DID NOT DO DAMAGE, and why that is luck rather than design: the Forge's own
handoff disclosed the redness in plain language and explained it correctly, and the Mayor
independently re-ran the verifier before acting. Had the Forge been less honest, or the
Mayor less careful, exit 0 plus "Next: Warden reviews" is exactly the path to a red main.
This fort has the corresponding scar already: fortkit-h5i, where post-merge main went
RED after three pre-merge greens.

NOT A DEFECT IN THIS PARTICULAR DISPATCH'S OUTCOME: the redness was legitimate and
external (the widened linter indicting kernel-RO launchers that only fortkit-52vf.1 can
fix). A red verifier for a reason the Forge cannot fix is a real state the launcher must
be able to express. So the fix is not "exit nonzero on red" alone.

PROPOSED SHAPE, for the Mayor to settle before dispatching this: distinguish three
outcomes rather than two — verifier GREEN (exit 0, print the review recipe), verifier RED
FROM THIS DIFF (nonzero, do not print the recipe, say what failed), and verifier RED FROM
A DISCLOSED EXTERNAL CAUSE (a distinct nonzero code, print that the branch is blocked and
on what, never the merge recipe). The third case is what actually happened tonight and no
launcher today can say it.

LANE: fort/scripts/forge.sh is kernel-RO to every masked seat. Regent. Natural home is
fortkit-52vf.4 (E3), which already carries fortkit-bfsu, the same false-record class in
warden.sh — fold it there rather than adding a seventh sitting.

comments.text:
A TEST NOW PINS THIS DEFECT IN PLACE. Ilva, finding 6 on the fortkit-881h review, 2026-08-17, merged and closed today.

The new founding-smoke block in test/shell.test.ts asserts 'resolves' on the forge leg — that is, exit 0 — while the inner launch it wraps exited 77. That assertion is CORRECT against today's forge.sh, and it is correct precisely because of the inversion this bead records: forge.sh exits 0 and prints the Warden-review recipe when its own launcher-observed verify.sh exited 1.

SO WHOEVER REPAIRS THE GATE ORDER MUST UPDATE THAT ASSERTION IN THE SAME CHANGE. Otherwise the test goes red on the fix and green on the defect, and the next session reads that red as 'the repair broke the smoke' rather than 'the smoke encoded the bug'.

This is the ordinary way a defect becomes load-bearing: not by anyone deciding it should be, but by a control being written against the world as it is. The test is not wrong to have been written — it is asserting observed behaviour, which is what a smoke test is for. It just now has to be part of this bead's diff.

ACCEPTANCE ADDITION for this bead: the fix updates test/shell.test.ts's forge leg in the same commit, and a positive control demonstrates the updated assertion fails against the OLD forge.sh behaviour. Without that control the new assertion is as unfalsifiable as the one it replaces.

title: Seven committed handoffs are permanently unreadable to the distilled view, and the obvious repair is the one SO7 forbids — Overseer ruling needed
description:
SURFACED BY fortkit-ybg7's FIX, 2026-08-11 (Mayor session F), and it is a genuine
law tension rather than a defect in that fix.

WHAT ybg7 CHANGED. Handoffs whose header stamp does not parse used to sort silently to
epoch 0, which is how Manyhalls' distilled view came to name a two-sessions-stale
handoff as latest. They are now DISCLOSED in current.md's 'Index build gaps' section,
naming the file and the unparseable string. That is the correct fix and it is verified:
the Mayor re-ran it, current.md now names mayor-2026-08-11-d.md (session F) as latest,
and the new regression test fails against the old generator (exit 1, one failing test,
proven by restoring main's generator in the worktree).

WHAT IT REVEALS. SEVEN committed handoffs are now permanently excluded from the
distilled view, disclosed but unreadable to it:

  fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-6jf.md    "—"
  fort/handoffs/mayor-2026-08-06-a.md      "2026-08-06T~12:45-08:00"
  fort/handoffs/mayor-2026-08-07.md        "2026-08-07T~11:45-08:00"
  fort/handoffs/mayor-2026-08-08-a.md      "2026-08-08T~23:30-08:00"
  fort/handoffs/mayor-2026-08-10-b.md      "2026-08-10T"
  fort/handoffs/mayor-2026-08-11-b.md      "2026-08-11T"   (session D)
  fort/handoffs/mayor-2026-08-11.md        "2026-08-11T"   (session C)

Note what two of those are: sessions C and D of 2026-08-11. Their State-of-work and
Failed-attempts sections are exactly the continuity material the Muniment Room exists
to deliver, and no seat reading the view will ever see them.

THE TENSION, STATED PLAINLY. The obvious repair is to fix the seven header stamps. But
standing order 7 says records are append-only and corrections are appended, never
edited in — and fortkit-se6 is an open bug filed against forge.sh for doing exactly
this, editing a committed record in place. A header is not a place you can append to.
So the cheap fix is the one the fort's own law forbids, and doing it quietly would make
the Mayor guilty of se6's defect while se6 is still open against the Forge.

OPTIONS, none obviously right, which is why this is a decision and not a task:
  (a) ACCEPT the exclusion. The record survives in git and in the directory; only the
      generated view cannot read it. Disclosure is already implemented, so this costs
      nothing and loses the continuity content permanently.
  (b) SIDECAR CORRECTION. Allow a companion file (e.g. <handoff>.stamp) carrying the
      corrected instant with provenance, which the generator prefers when present. The
      original bytes are never touched, so SO7 holds literally, and the mechanism
      generalises to any future unparseable record. Costs a generator change and a new
      convention.
  (c) NARROW IN-PLACE REPAIR, explicitly authorised, with an appended note inside each
      file recording who changed the stamp, from what, to what, and why. Honest and
      cheapest to implement, but it establishes that headers are editable, and that
      precedent is hard to bound afterward.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: (b). It is the only option that both recovers the content and
leaves SO7 intact as written, and the sidecar generalises rather than carving an
exception. But this is the Overseer's call because it interprets a standing order, and
whichever way it goes it should be recorded as a ruling so the next seat that notices
seven excluded handoffs finds the decision instead of re-litigating it.

DO NOT let this block anything. ybg7's fix is correct and complete on its own terms;
this is the residue it made visible, which is what a good fix does.

comments.text: RELATED, filed from the same Warden review (Ilva on fortkit-ybg7, 2026-08-12): fortkit-gzv2 finding 2 recovers the seven excluded handoffs' CONTENT into index.db without touching their headers, by indexing them with an empty ts and excluding them only from time-windowed queries (the pattern docs/specs/memory.md 6.2 already uses for annals and interactions). That is close to this bead's option (b) and may make the ruling here cheaper than it looks: the content becomes reachable via fortkit recall even if the headers stay unparseable forever. It does NOT resolve the latest-handoff SELECTION question, which is what actually bit the fort. Also depending on this bead's ruling: fortkit-5sqf, the write-side header lint, needs to know whether the seven are grandfathered by name or recovered.

title: xgul.8 items 4,6,8,9 (Forge): coupling-guard test over bin/fort-init, template verifier memory-lint wiring, template charter retires bd remember and qualifies the spec path
description:
FORGE LANE, dispatchable, no conflict with any other in-flight bead. Items 4, 6, 8
and 9 of fortkit-xgul.8, split out so the Forge can execute them without hitting the
kernel-RO bin/fort-init that items 7 and 11 need. See the SO7 correction on the parent
for why the split exists.

ITEM 4 — THE COUPLING GUARD'S STATED REACH EXCEEDS ITS ACTUAL REACH.
test/researcher-launcher.test.ts:36-37 reads exactly ONE file
(templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh), while the comment above it and the A2/A3
commit message both claim "if either is reverted to fort/remember.md this goes red".
True for A3, FALSE for A2: reverting bin/fort-init alone leaves the test green, and
nothing in the suite asserts anything about bin/fort-init at all. This is the vhk.9
silent-revert class the guard exists to kill, so an overstatement here is not
cosmetic — it tells a future maintainer the factory is covered when it is not.
THE HARNESS ALREADY EXISTS: test/memory.test.ts:181 builds a temp fort with mkdtemp
and runs the real linter against planted fixtures. A sibling test asserting
bin/fort-init contains fort/memory/facts and that its AGENTS block names current.md
makes the sentence true. Read-only assertions over bin/fort-init are fine from any
mask; only WRITING it is blocked.

ITEM 6 — THE STATED REASON FOR NOT WIRING memory-lint INTO THE TEMPLATE VERIFIER DOES
NOT HOLD. The record says wiring it "would break non-node forts", but
templates/fort/scripts/verify.sh:59-61 ALREADY runs npm run typecheck/lint/test
unconditionally, so the template verifier is already node-only and already exits 127
at step one on a non-node fort. Adding memory-lint breaks nothing that is not already
broken. WHY IT MATTERS, and it bears on threat 2: the mechanical control for
docs/specs/memory.md 4.3 rule 4 (untrusted facts never core) currently ships into
every new fort and is executed by nothing. bin/fort-init:175 shows the right pattern
(if command -v node). NOTE THE DISTINCTION the Warden drew: the template header's
"fill in the fort's own gates below" makes LEAVING it defensible; it is the recorded
REASON that does not hold up. So if the decision is to leave it unwired, replace the
false reason with a true one — do not leave a justification the next reader will
check and find wrong.

ITEM 8 — THE TEMPLATE CHARTER STILL PRESCRIBES bd remember, on the line the A2/A3
commit itself edited. templates/fort/charter.md:60 reads "Work state: Beads (bd ready,
bd remember/bd prime)...". Spec 3 decision 1 (final 2026-08-10) retires bd remember,
and Manyhalls' own charter:77 says the ledger supersedes it. A fort founded today is
chartered to write durable facts into the surface the spec retired. Half a line, same
line, missed.

ITEM 9 — THE TEMPLATE CHARTER POINTS A FOUNDED FORT AT A SPEC PATH IT WILL NOT HAVE.
The wording ends "per docs/specs/memory.md" — true in fortkit, dangling in every fort
founded from it. The charter's own civ-layer section already takes pains to say "every
civ/ path in this section is relative to the fortkit repository" for exactly this
reason. "per fortkit docs/specs/memory.md" matches that precedent.

FILES: test/, templates/fort/scripts/verify.sh, templates/fort/charter.md. All
writable. NOT IN SCOPE and mechanically blocked: bin/fort-init (items 7 and 11).

VERIFIER: fort/scripts/verify.sh must be green before handoff. Item 4 adds a test, so
the test count should RISE; say by how much in the handoff.

title: xgul.8 item 5 (Forge, SERIALISED behind ybg7 and ij8j): parametrise the live consolidate-memory generator so the template is a verbatim copy, plus a non-vacuous drift test
description:
FORGE LANE but SERIALISED — DO NOT DISPATCH CONCURRENTLY WITH fortkit-ybg7 OR
fortkit-ij8j. Item 5 of fortkit-xgul.8, split out for that reason alone.

WHY IT IS QUEUED. This item parametrises the LIVE scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs.
fortkit-ybg7 (parse-failure error + handoff sort order) and fortkit-ij8j
(interactions.jsonl path + gap message) both edit the same file. Three Forge branches
editing one file concurrently is a three-way merge conflict and three burned sessions,
not parallelism. Dispatch order: ybg7, then ij8j, then this. Each after the previous
one merges to main, so this branch starts from a base that already contains both.

ITEM 5 — THE TEMPLATE consolidate-memory.mjs IS A DIVERGENT COPY WITH NO BEAD.
Measured by the Warden on the A2/A3 review: exactly THREE string lines differ from
scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs (title, generated-by path, incident-gap link);
memory-lint.mjs is byte-identical. The Regent flagged the drift hazard as "filed
intent, not done here" and no bead was ever created, which is the same evaporation the
Warden recorded as finding 13(b) on fortkit-8cv6 and which fortkit-or2.9 exists to
undo.

SHAPE, as the Warden proposed it: parametrise the live generator — fort name from the
registry, generated-by path from argv — so the template becomes a VERBATIM copy, plus
a drift test asserting the two match modulo the parametrised lines.

WHY THE TEST IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. Making the copies identical today fixes today.
A test asserting they stay identical is what stops the third divergent copy, and this
fort has measured that exact decay elsewhere: the three live seat-sandbox.sh copies
are now 13528, 14004 and 13652 bytes. Without the test this bead is a tidy-up with a
half-life.

CHECK BEFORE YOU START, do not assume: re-diff the two files. ybg7 and ij8j will have
landed in the live copy by the time this runs, so the divergence will be larger than
three lines and some of the new difference is intended (the template needs the fixes
too, which is the point of making it a verbatim copy).

title: A7 item 1: widen memory-lint's retired-reference check to charter, seats, templates AND the launchers — and prove it is not vacuous
description:
ITEM 1 OF fortkit-xgul.7, split out so it is dispatchable. FORGE LANE, and unblocked
NOW: the parent bead reads "Blocked by A4 and A5", but that blockage does not apply to
this item — A4 and A5 (the elder-fort migrations) landed 2026-08-11, and in any case
this item edits only the capital's own linter and its template copy. Items 2, 3 and 4
of the parent genuinely do depend on other work and stay there.

THE DEFECT (Warden, fortkit-vhk.9 r1). scripts/memory-lint.mjs:73-85's
retired-reference check scans only the root AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. So a
reintroduced fort/remember.md reference anywhere else cannot trip the verifier.

WIDEN IT TO COVER, at minimum:
  fort/charter.md and fort/seats/            (fortkit-1yg already noted this)
  templates/                                  (required after A3, or a reintroduction
                                               into the factory is silent)
  fort/scripts/*.sh and bin/                  ADDED BY THIS BEAD, and it is the whole
                                               reason it matters right now — see below.

WHY THE LAUNCHER SURFACE IS THE POINT. fortkit-08ny measured TEN live seat prompts
across three forts still naming the retired fort/remember.md, plus bin/regent and
bin/civ-index. fortkit-52vf.1 (edict E1) repoints them. If this linter does not cover
the launchers afterward, the next reintroduction is silent again and the whole edict
decays quietly. 08ny names this dependency explicitly.

HEED THIS WARNING, from longburn-wtx7.9 item 1: a NAIVE SUBSTRING WIDENING GOES RED
on the dated amendment notes that standing order 7 requires. Legitimate historical
references to fort/remember.md exist and must keep existing — the migration record in
civ/handoffs/, civ/remember.md's own history, and any charter amendment note that
explains what was retired and why. The check must distinguish a LIVE INSTRUCTION to
read the path from a HISTORICAL RECORD that names it.

MUST NOT GO RED ON THESE, all verified present and CORRECT at 2026-08-11:
  bin/fort-init:44,48                          writes the pointer stub deliberately
  templates/fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs:109    the retired-reference list itself needs
                                               the literal string
  fort/remember.md                             IS the pointer stub; it names its own
                                               successor by design
  civ/handoffs/*, civ/remember.md              historical records, append-only

ACCEPTANCE, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT USUALLY GETS SKIPPED: prove the widened lint is
NOT VACUOUS. Plant a violation in each newly covered surface, confirm memory-lint
names it and exits 1, then remove the plant and confirm exit 0. Vardis did exactly
this in Farlantern for the fact-file rules (six deliberate defects, six named
failures, exit 1) and that is the bar. A widened check that passes because it matches
nothing is worse than the narrow one, because it reports coverage it does not have —
the same defect shape as fortkit-08ny's vacuous positive control and fortkit-0s4a.

Both copies: scripts/memory-lint.mjs and templates/fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs, which
fortkit-xgul.8 item 5 records as currently byte-identical. Keep them so, or make the
divergence deliberate and tested.
acceptance_criteria: memory-lint covers fort/charter.md, fort/seats/, templates/, fort/scripts/*.sh and bin/; a planted violation in EACH newly covered surface makes it name the file and exit 1; removing the plants returns exit 0; the four documented legitimate references (fort-init stub writer, the linter's own list, the pointer stub itself, civ/ historical records) do NOT trip it.
close_reason: Merged to main. Warden APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS (Ilva, 2026-08-12), 8 non-blocking; verifier green 163 tests and non-vacuity proven BY EXECUTED TEST — the first of three reviews where her mask did not block the differential check. Post-merge main green, exit 0, 163 tests. AND THE GUARD IS PROVEN LIVE ON MAIN, not just tested: the Mayor planted 'fort/remember.md' into fort/scripts/verify.sh, ran memory-lint, got exit 1 naming that file, and restored the tree clean. So E1's repair is now an invariant the verifier holds rather than a change someone made. Findings forward on fortkit-y97d's sibling set: the historical-charter exemption is untested and dead code today; the exemption is charter-only so fort/seats/*.md and templates/fort/charter.md are zero-tolerance (relevant to xgul.8.1, which is about to edit that template charter); bin/fort-init is exempted whole-file rather than at its stub heredoc; fort/scripts/lib/*.sh is scanned in the factory but not the fort. Her finding 5 caught a false close of mine and produced fortkit-4n8c.

comments.text:
CORRECTION under standing order 7, Emrith 2026-08-11 (Mayor session F), appended to
comments because a reader acting on my earlier text would be wrong.

WHAT I SAID, planning the fortkit-52vf programme: that fortkit-ybg7, fortkit-ij8j,
fortkit-xgul.7 item 1 and fortkit-xgul.8 are Forge lane and "need nothing from the
Overseer and no edict". I said it in the epic, in the lane-assignment comments, and to
the Overseer directly as the plan's main efficiency finding.

IT IS WRONG FOR fortkit-xgul.7.1, AND THE MECHANISM IS INTERESTING. The WORK needs no
edict: the Forge completed it in one session, both linter copies byte-identical, tests
non-vacuous. But the MERGE does, because widening memory-lint to cover the launchers
makes the widened linter indict SEVEN LIVE FILES THAT NO MASKED SEAT CAN EDIT.

MEASURED BY THE MAYOR, independently, in the candidate worktree (not read off the
handoff): CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit -> EXIT 1, and the only failures are

  fort/scripts/mayor.sh  forge.sh  warden.sh  researcher.sh  probe-cycle7.sh
  bin/civ-index  bin/regent

all kernel-RO, and all exactly fortkit-52vf.1's (E1's) scope. Correctly NOT flagged:
bin/fort-init's deliberate stub writer, the linter's own retired-reference list, and
fort/remember.md itself. The exceptions the bead specified all held.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the part that matters: MERGING THIS BRANCH BEFORE E1 LANDS TURNS
MAIN RED, and a red main blocks every other bead in the fort from closing, because
standing order 9 requires verifiers green. So the branch is HELD, and the dependency is
now encoded: fortkit-xgul.7.1 depends on fortkit-52vf.1.

THIS IS NOT A FAILURE OF THE WORK. It is the guard doing precisely what fortkit-08ny
asked for — "memory-lint's retired-reference check should cover the launchers
afterward, or the next reintroduction is silent again". The linter is now a MECHANICAL
enforcement of E1 rather than a prose hope, which is the strongest possible outcome. It
simply means E1 must land FIRST, where I had planned for it merely to land soon.

THE GENERAL LESSON, worth carrying into the rest of the programme: "which seat can
write the file" and "what merging the change implies" are different questions, and I
answered only the first. A widened verifier inherits the lane of everything it now
judges. Check the other Forge-lane beads against this before dispatching them:
fortkit-xgul.8.1 wires memory-lint into the TEMPLATE verifier (item 6), which judges
templates/ only and so does not have this problem — verified, not assumed.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Scope and gate check.** The diff is four files: `scripts/memory-lint.mjs`, `templates/fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs` (byte-identical, blob `5f89619` on both sides), `test/memory.test.ts`, and one Forge handoff. It touches no gate-1 file — no `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, `fort/scripts/`, `bin/`, `.claude/`. No mandatory ESCALATE. Against the charter's threat model this is a strengthening of a control on **threat 1 (agent accident)**: it makes a silent reintroduction of a retired memory pointer into a live instruction surface mechanically loud. No finding below bears on threats 2–4, and none requires the explicitly out-of-scope shell-holding adversary.

**Model.** `gpt-5.6-terra` (Forge top rung, Codex CLI), per the handoff's `Model:` line. This bead was written around one specific failure mode of that family — a widened check that passes because it matches nothing — so I did not accept the handoff's summary of its own test. I read the fixture and the `run` helper and checked whether each assertion discriminates. The detection half does: with main's narrow linter the fixture exits 0, `promisify(execFile)` resolves, and `toMatchObject({ code: 1 })` fails. The exemption half does not (finding 1).

**The hold is discharged, verified by me and not read off the bead.** `ee1791a` (E1) is in this branch's history via the merge at `9281503`, and `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in my scratch copy of the candidate tree is green with `memory-lint` as its first step. The seven launcher references that made this branch red are gone. Tree diff `main` vs branch is the four files plus three files where main is simply ahead (`.beads/*`, `fort/events/events-2026-08-12.jsonl`, from `3b13596`, which the branch predates); merge base is `f6ba89c`, so merging reverts nothing.

The acceptance criteria are met. The design is sound: exemptions are three named, narrow constants rather than the "temporary allowlist nobody removes" the Mayor argued against, and the settlement-shaped copy degrades correctly (a fort has no `templates/` or `bin/`, `filesBelow` returns `[]` on the missing roots, and the shipped copy at `fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs` sits outside every scanned root, so it does not indict itself). Findings follow.

---

**1. The historical-charter exemption is untested, unexercised, and listed under "Verified facts". (non-blocking)**

`isHistoricalCharterReference()` is the answer to the bead's "HEED THIS WARNING", and nothing proves it works. In the fixture, `fort/charter.md` carries a historical paragraph *and* a live one, so the file is red either way — the assertion cannot distinguish an exemption that works from one that always returns `false`. The green phase then overwrites `charter.md` wholesale, so no assertion ever says "a charter carrying only a dated amendment note stays green." Nor does production exercise it: the real `fort/charter.md` contains zero references to the retired path, so the function is dead code today.

The handoff states under **Verified facts**: "The same fixture permits a dated charter migration record…". By my reading of the code that is true — the first occurrence is excused and the loop advances — but the cited evidence does not establish it, and this fort has a recorded scar (`fortkit-vhk.5.1`) about handoff claims whose evidence was thinner than the claim. Bead: add a green-phase assertion for a charter whose only reference sits in an amendment note, and append the qualification to the handoff.

**2. The exemption is charter-only, so the two surfaces where SO7 notes actually live are zero-tolerance. (non-blocking)**

`isHistoricalCharterReference()` returns `false` for any path that is not literally `fort/charter.md`. That makes `fort/seats/*.md` — which carry `## History` sections by design; my own seat file has one — and `templates/fort/charter.md` zero-tolerance, with no escape hatch. Calder's comment defends zero tolerance for `bin/` and `fort/scripts/*.sh` and I agree there: a launcher has no legitimate reason to name the path. Seat histories and the template charter are different, and `fortkit-xgul.8.1` — which this bead blocks — is about to edit `templates/fort/charter.md` to retire `bd remember`. Bead: decide deliberately whether the paragraph heuristic extends to seat files and the template charter, and record the decision.

**3. `bin/fort-init` is exempted whole-file. (non-blocking)**

`pointerStubWriter` short-circuits before the file is read, so a genuine live reintroduction anywhere in `bin/fort-init` is silent — the exact defect shape this bead exists to close, at the one file that writes the stub into every future fort. The bead only required lines 44 and 48 not go red. Bead: narrow the exemption to the stub-writing heredoc (or to lines already carrying an explicit marker) rather than the file.

**4. `fort/scripts/lib/*.sh` is scanned in the factory but not in the fort. (non-blocking)**

The predicate `/^fort\/scripts\/[^/]+\.sh$/` excludes `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, while `templates/` is scanned with `() => true` and therefore *does* cover `templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`. The live copy of the most load-bearing sourced script in the fort is less covered than its template. This matches the bead's literal `fort/scripts/*.sh`, so it is in spec; it is still an asymmetry someone will trip over. No live reference exists there today (verified by grep). Bead.

**5. `skills/civ/SKILL.md:29` still names the retired path, and `fortkit-4b9q` is closed claiming otherwise. (non-blocking here — not in this diff, but it bears directly on this guard's completeness)**

`skills/` is outside every scanned root, which Calder's comment records. What the comment does not record is that the repair is not in the repository. At `main` HEAD and in main's working tree, `skills/civ/SKILL.md:29` still reads `| What must a session here know operationally | `<repo>/fort/remember.md` |`. Meanwhile `3b13596`'s message says "fortkit-4b9q closed: skills/civ/SKILL.md:29 repointed" (that commit touches only `.beads/` and `fort/events/`), and the bead's close reason says "Verified: zero remaining references in that file."

I could not read `~/.claude/skills/civ/SKILL.md` — it is outside my allowed working directories — so I cannot tell whether the edit landed in the installed copy and missed the tracked one, which the close reason's own discussion of `~/.claude/skills/` writability makes plausible. Either way the repository's copy is unfixed and the record does not say which file it fixed. Separately, `4b9q`'s second acceptance criterion — "a decision recorded on whether the retired-reference guard covers `skills/`" — does not appear in the close reason, so the question this bead's guard raises about `skills/` is recorded as settled while being unanswered. Bead, or reopen `4b9q`. `.claude/`, `.agents/`, `.codex/`, `.github/`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are clean (verified).

**6. Superseded fact keys are now substring-matched across launchers and templates with no escape hatch. (non-blocking)**

`retiredReferences` is `["fort/remember.md", ...supersededFactKeys]`, and the widening applies to the whole list, not just the pointer path. There is one superseded fact today, `forge-sandbox-caveat`, distinctive enough to be harmless — the verifier is green. But the class is new: a future short or common-word fact key would false-positive against shell scripts and templates, and outside `fort/charter.md` there is no historical exemption to relieve it. Bead: either constrain superseded-key matching to prose surfaces, or require keys to be distinctive.

**7. Minor: a dead exemption entry. (non-blocking)** `selfReferentialRetirementGuards` contains `"scripts/memory-lint.mjs"`, which can never appear in `retiredReferenceFiles` because `scripts/` is not a scanned root. Harmless, but an exemption that guards nothing invites the reader to believe `scripts/` is covered. Delete it or comment it as forward-looking.

**8. Minor: the check is nowhere in the spec, and a needless shell hop in the test. (non-blocking)** `docs/specs/memory.md` §4.4 enumerates memory-lint's rules and does not mention the retired-reference check at all — pre-existing, but the check now has scanned roots, an exemption policy, and a zero-tolerance rule that Calder says "anyone editing those files later needs to know", currently recorded only in a comment inside `probe-cycle7.sh`. SO3 wants the spec updated with the code. In the test, stderr is routed through `sh -c '"$1" "$2" "$3" 2> "$4"'` into a file when `promisify(execFile)`'s rejection already carries `.stderr`; the argument positions are correct, it is just indirection worth removing.

---

**What I verified independently, by execution in `/tmp/warden-xgul.7.1`:**

- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — all six steps ran to completion: memory-lint (5 budget lines, no failures), typecheck, browser-typecheck, biome (62 files, no fixes), vitest **163 passed / 14 files**, shellcheck. **Caveat, stated because the recipe demands it:** my profile refused every compound spelling that would have printed `$?`, so I read green from the final step completing with no failure output and the tool reporting no error; I did not print the numeric exit code.
- `npx vitest run test/memory.test.ts` — 8/8, including the new test. title: fortkit-e4q fails SO11: measure the /proc sibling-read exposure (existence and byte count only), then record it as a charter accepted residual and supersede e4q
description:
OVERSEER RULING 2026-08-11 (Mayor session F), recorded verbatim in the comment on
this bead. Asked whether fortkit-e4q (PID-namespace isolation) clears standing
order 11, the Overseer ruled that IT DOES NOT, and directed it be recorded as an
accepted residual in the charter's threat model instead of implemented.

WHAT e4q DESCRIBES. Seats run as uid justin sharing the host PID namespace
(seat-sandbox.sh:127 mounts --dev /dev but never --unshare-pid or --proc /proc).
A seat can therefore read /proc/PID/environ and cmdline of, or ptrace, sibling
processes, including a concurrently running unmasked Regent. Masking ~/.ssh is
moot if another process's environment is readable. e4q itself flagged this under
SO11 as a REASONED bypass of an existing control rather than an observed failure,
and set its own priority low accordingly. That self-flagging was correct and the
ruling follows it.

=== THE CATCH, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS A BEAD AND NOT A ONE-LINE EDIT ===

charter.md:27 admits a residual ONLY WITH A MEASUREMENT ATTACHED: 'Standing order
11 admits a residual here only with a measurement attached.' The existing entry
for the Researcher's WebFetch channel (charter.md:29) is the model: it names what
was considered and rejected, bounds the exposure, and cites two probe runs with
pass/fail counts. e4q currently carries a described MECHANISM and no measurement.
So this bead measures first, then amends. Recording an unmeasured residual would
weaken the one clause that keeps the threat model honest.

=== THE MEASUREMENT, AND ITS HARD CONSTRAINT ===

DO NOT READ THE CONTENT. Reading a live unmasked process's environment into a
model's context or a log is threat 4 in this fort's own threat model (credential
leakage into transcripts, 'from which it cannot be recalled'), and the finding does
not require it. Record ONLY:
  - whether open()/read() on /proc/<sibling-pid>/environ SUCCEEDS from inside a
    masked seat, as an exit status
  - the BYTE COUNT returned, never the bytes
  - the same for cmdline, and whether ptrace attach is permitted
  - which sibling was targeted, by PID and process name only
This is the discipline the Researcher boundary probes already used: '.env*, ~/.ssh
and ~/.aws measured at zero bytes returned'. A probe that proves the exposure by
committing the exposure has failed.

The honest form of the target is a concurrently running unmasked process the seat
does not own. If no unmasked Regent is running at measurement time, a plain
unmasked shell of the Overseer's is the same class and is sufficient.

=== THEN THE AMENDMENT ===

Add the residual to charter.md's 'Accepted residuals (measured, not assumed)'
list, in the shape of the WebFetch entry: mechanism, what was considered and
rejected (implementation is available and known — --unshare-pid plus --proc /proc,
which must land together because Claude Code and Codex introspect their own process
tree and a stale /proc view breaks them), the bound, and the measurement with its
numbers.

CYCLE-7 REQUIREMENTS ON THE EDIT, both mandatory:
  - the Overseer's prior approval recorded on THIS bead before the charter is
    touched (it is, in the comment below)
  - charter.amended emitted via fort/scripts/emit.sh with the edit

THEN: close fortkit-e4q by supersession pointing at this bead, so a future seat
that rediscovers the /proc mechanism finds the ruling and the measurement instead
of re-filing it. That closure is the point of the exercise: an accepted residual
that is not findable gets re-litigated.

NOTE FOR THE FUTURE: this residual is the kind that can be REOPENED by evidence.
If a seat is ever observed actually reading a sibling's credentials, SO11 is
satisfied by observation and e4q's implementation becomes ordinary work. The
charter entry should say so.

title: civ/remember.md has not migrated to the facts ledger: the civilization layer is the last flat memory store, and the Regent is the seat reading it
description:

read-side repair surface for fortkit-08ny. FILED ON THE OVERSEER'S EXPLICIT
DECISION the same session — see the comment on this bead for his ruling verbatim.

                   scripts seats systemd transcripts  — NO memory/ directory
  fort forts        all three now carry fort/memory/facts/ + current.md after
                   Project A (fortkit-xgul.4/.5, both landed 2026-08-11)

THE GAP. The Muniment Room architecture (docs/specs/memory.md, spec of record,
approved and committed ad3929e) reached all three settlements today. It has not
reached the civilization layer. civ/remember.md is now the LAST flat operational
memory store in the civilization, and it belongs to the seat with the widest
reach and the most authority: the Regent runs unmasked, with access to every fort
and to the machine.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY TIDINESS. Three defects already open are about the Regent
being briefed badly, and all three are symptoms of a flat store with no structure
to query:
  fortkit-88u.8  the briefing greps '^- \*\*' out of remember.md, so the Regent is

  fortkit-ztzs   the briefing reads each FORT's remember.md, which is now a

                 that 'what a civ seat is injected with across N forts' is the same
                 budget question one level up, and it cannot be answered against a
                 flat file.
A ledger with tiers, scope and provenance answers all three structurally. Patching
the grep answers none of them.

SO7 IS THE HARD CONSTRAINT, exactly as it was for A4 and A5: NOTHING IS DISCARDED.
Stale entries migrate with status: superseded and provenance recorded, never by
deletion. Both elder-fort migrations landed with zero records discarded (Proofdelve
43 records in / 49 facts out, cover check 32/32; Farlantern 29 bullets to 31 facts,
cover 29/29) and this must meet the same bar.

MIGRATION PATTERN IS PROVEN AND SHOULD BE REUSED, not reinvented: the A1 spec, the

do the same here rather than trusting a passing lint.

title: E5: in-mask launch refusal — coupled mayor.sh + warden.sh + forge.sh commit, lands when no seat is working (px7e, or2.9.4)
description:
EDICT 5 OF SIX (parent fortkit-52vf). DEPENDS ON E3 (fortkit-52vf.4).
Holds fortkit-px7e and fortkit-or2.9.4.

WHAT IT DOES: launchers refuse (exit 77) when the mask marker names a seat that
must not launch other seats, while letting the attended Mayor's dispatch lane
through. It stops a masked seat from spawning seats. Reference implementation:
longburn/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:5-7, from longburn-5v4, amended on that fort's own
Mayor's finding: 'no seat launches another Mayor — any marker at all, including
the Mayor's own and the legacy 1, refuses. Only an unmasked shell launches this.'

WHY IT IS ITS OWN SITTING, and this is the whole reason it is not folded into E3:

  1. IT IS A COUPLED THREE-FILE COMMIT. or2.9.4 measured it: the guard reads a
     SEAT-NAMED marker and this fort does not have one (fort/scripts/mayor.sh:42-43
     exports the legacy boolean FORT_MASKED=1, and neither warden.sh nor forge.sh
     carries any guard at all). Porting means changing mayor.sh, warden.sh and
     forge.sh TOGETHER, as one commit. E3 lays the seat-named marker; this adds the
     guards that read it. Split any other way and there is a window where the
     marker exists and nothing honours it, or guards exist and refuse everything.

  2. IT CARRIES A SCAR THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH IT (civ/remember.md, 2026-08-09):
     the seat-named guard shipped correct for new launches and REFUSED
     FARLANTERN'S OWN MASKED MAYOR MID-MILL, because a session already running
     under the old marker met a launcher that had learned the new rule. This edict
     therefore lands when NO SEAT IS WORKING in any fort, and the Regent confirms
     that before editing rather than after. An already-running session cannot be
     protected by a guard written after it started; the only control is timing.

OBSERVED NEED (SO11), from fortkit-px7e: Mayor session E was asked to launch two
elder-fort Mayors for fortkit-xgul.4/.5 and could not, because seat-sandbox binds
all of $HOME read-only with only the repo rw and every spawned process inherits
it. Probe: touch /home/justin/dev/ForgeOs/.mask-probe-emrith -> Read-only file
system. Same class as the ledger fact
a-masked-mayor-session-cannot-launch-the-herald. The failure is currently silent
and late: the seat discovers it by EROFS partway through, having already promised
the action. Session E's own handoff records that as a failed attempt ('the seat
asserted the route before checking it could execute it'). A refusal at launch turns
a mid-task discovery into an immediate, legible one.

SCOPE: three live launchers per fort, plus templates/fort/scripts/ so no fort is
founded without the guard. Manyhalls and Proofdelve both need it; Farlantern is
the reference and needs only the marker reconciled.

VERIFICATION: from an unmasked shell, every launcher starts normally. From a
masked seat, every launcher refuses with exit 77 and a legible reason. The Mayor's
attended dispatch lane still works, since that is the lane the fort runs on.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
MEASUREMENT REFRESH 2026-08-17, because this bead's premise has MOVED since it was written on 08-12 and an implementer reading it today would mis-scope the work.

E5's description says the guard reads a seat-named marker 'and this fort does not have one (fort/scripts/mayor.sh:42-43 exports the legacy boolean FORT_MASKED=1, and neither warden.sh nor forge.sh carries any guard at all)'.

HALF OF THAT IS NOW FIXED AND HALF IS NOT. fortkit-ugw4 and fortkit-mm7m landed between then and now, so the MARKER exists everywhere and the GUARD still exists in only one fort. Read at source today:

  fortkit/fort/scripts/forge.sh:87    mask+=(--setenv FORT_MASKED forge)   <- SETS
  fortkit/fort/scripts/warden.sh:168  mask+=(--setenv FORT_MASKED warden)  <- SETS
  Neither READS it. No refusal in either file.

  longburn/fort/scripts/forge.sh:16   case "${FORT_MASKED:-}" in
                                        ""|mayor|1) ;;
                                        *) echo 'forge.sh: REFUSED — running inside the
                                           ...seat mask; launchers are the lane of the
                                           harness' >&2; exit 77 ;;
                                      esac
  longburn/fort/scripts/warden.sh:38  same shape.
  templates/fort/scripts/forge.sh     FORT_MASKED appears ZERO times.
  templates/fort/scripts/warden.sh    FORT_MASKED appears ZERO times.

SO THE TWO PROTECTIONS ARE DISTINCT AND ONLY ONE IS UNIVERSAL:
  (a) 'no seat launches another Mayor' — mayor.sh refuses under any marker. Universal now.
  (b) 'launchers are the lane of the harness' — forge.sh and warden.sh refuse being
      launched from inside a non-Mayor mask. FARLANTERN ONLY.
E5 is (b). The capital sets a marker nothing reads.

SURFACED BY Vardis Slowfathom (Farlantern Mayor) 2026-08-17 while composing that fort's standing order 17 worked example; independently verified here by reading all six files. Her framing is worth keeping: the elder fort is AHEAD of both the capital and the factory on this file, and 'converge toward the template' would delete a working guard.

title: Defence in depth: no fort ignores editor swap/backup/autosave files, and fort-init ships no .gitignore at all
description:
Overseer-approved 2026-08-11: "let's do the .gitignore fix also — I feel like
that's good 'defense in depth' practice in case something like this happens
again." Filed as its own bead, deliberately separate from fortkit-2kub, so it
lands without waiting on the seat-sandbox decision. Different layer, different
lane, different risk.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO. It does NOT close the mask hole. A gitignored
file is still on disk and still readable by any seat; masking and gitignore
govern different things. What it removes is the `git add .` catastrophe: an
editor's second copy of a secret entering git history, which is unrecoverable in
practice once pushed. Path-scoped staging is already standing order 4, but SO4
is prose and this is mechanism.

THE MEASURED GAP. All three forts ignore the secret itself and none ignores its
editor siblings:
  fortkit   .gitignore:14  .env*
  ForgeOs   .gitignore:11-13  .env / .env.* / .env*.local
  longburn  .gitignore:12  .env*
`git check-ignore -v '..env.staging.local.kate-swp'` matched NO RULE in any of
the three. The leading extra dot defeats every one of those globs. Verified
2026-08-11.

Nor has any editor-residue file ever been committed anywhere:
`git log --all -- '*.kate-swp' '*.swp' '*~'` is empty in all three repos. The
record is clean by luck and by SO4, not by design. This bead converts luck into
design.

DONE ALREADY, in this repo only:
  fortkit/.gitignore gains an editor-residue block (*.kate-swp, *.swp, *.swo,
  *~, \#*\#, .\#*) and a retired-ruflo block (.claude/proven-config.json,
  .claude/.proven-config-version, agentdb.rvf, agentdb.rvf.lock).
  Verified: all eight target paths now match, and src/cli.ts, fort/charter.md
  and fort/events/*.jsonl are confirmed still NOT ignored. The negative check
  matters more than the positive one — an over-broad ignore rule that silently
  drops the event stream would be far worse than the hole it closes.

REMAINING WORK, none of which this seat can reach:
 1. ForgeOs/.gitignore and longburn/.gitignore — outside this fort's mask.
    Overseer or Regent. longburn already ignores the ruflo pair (lines 20-22)
    and names its own cleanup bead, so it needs only the editor-residue block.
 2. THE FACTORY, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. `find templates -name
    '*gitignore*'` returns NOTHING. fort-init ships no .gitignore at all, so
    every fort founded from it inherits whatever the target repo already had
    and gets none of this protection. A fix applied to three forts and not to
    the factory is a fix that decays with every new settlement. Add
    templates/.gitignore (or the equivalent fragment appended at founding) with
    the same two blocks plus the fort-standard entries.
 3. Verification per fort after the change: `git check-ignore -v` on the
    residue spellings must match, AND on fort/events/*.jsonl must NOT match.

ESCAPED HASHES ARE NOT A TYPO. In .gitignore, `#` opens a comment, so Emacs
autosave (`#file#`) and lock (`.#file`) patterns must be written `\#*\#` and
`.\#*`. Anyone porting these lines by eye will drop the backslashes; the
verification step above catches it.

RELATED: fortkit-2kub (the mask hole, the actual defect, Overseer/Regent lane);
fortkit-agf (the ruflo residue these new lines also cover, purge approved
separately); ForgeOs-szai (Proofdelve's local record of the same swap file).

title: memory-lint has no near-duplicate key guard: two concurrent sessions wrote the same fact under two keys, both active, no supersession link
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-11 in Proofdelve, hours after the ledger went in. Not a
Proofdelve bug: it is a missing guard in the capital's memory-lint, which every
fort installs byte-identically.

WHAT HAPPENED. Two concurrent Marrek sessions ran in ForgeOs (both confirmed
live: PIDs 1147160 and 1671067). Each wrote a fact for the same claim:
  fort/memory/facts/workos-has-two-applications-concepts.md   17:56:46  TRACKED
    provenance: migrated from bd remember key
    workos-has-two-distinct-applications-concepts-and-conflating
  fort/memory/facts/workos-two-applications-concepts.md       18:29:02  UNTRACKED
    provenance: ForgeOs-11tf.7; Justin's direct dashboard observation

Both status: active. Both tier: on-demand. Both scope seats [mayor, forge].
Neither carries superseded-by. The keys differ by one word.

THE LEDGER NOW ASSERTS THE SAME THING TWICE WITH NO POINTER BETWEEN THEM, and
memory-lint passes, because it has no notion of near-duplicate keys. A recall
against 'workos applications' returns two facts with different provenance and no
statement of which supersedes which. The architecture's whole claim is that a
fact has one home and corrections are linked; a silent duplicate breaks that
claim quietly.

THIS IS THE SIBLING OF fortkit-8rh. That bead makes fort-init refuse rosters
whose ACTOR IDS collide at edit distance 1, for the same reason: two records
that a reader will conflate must not both exist unremarked. Fact keys need the
same guard. The distance here is not character-level (one whole word differs)
so a plain Levenshtein threshold will not catch it; token-set overlap will.

FIX, for decision:
 - memory-lint gains a near-duplicate key check: report (not necessarily fail)
   when two active facts' keys share a high token overlap, or when two active
   facts share a topic set and a seat set with no supersession link between them.
 - Decide the severity. Recommend WARN rather than FAIL initially, since a false
   positive on a legitimately-adjacent pair would block the verifier, and the
   fort has no calibration data yet. Revisit once there is.
 - The check must be proven non-vacuous against this exact pair as its fixture.

RELATED HAZARD, WORTH ITS OWN LINE. The trigger was two sessions writing the
same ledger concurrently. The elder forts already carry a fact called
concurrent-sessions-share-this-tree. Nothing in the memory architecture accounts
for concurrent writers: no lock, no claim, no detection. A near-duplicate guard
catches this instance after the fact. Whether the ledger needs a concurrency
story at all is a separate design question and should be filed as such rather
than folded in here.

DISPOSITION OF THE PROOFDELVE INSTANCE: theirs to resolve, by supersession
rather than deletion, per SO7. Four facts from the second session are untracked
and must be committed before that fort's session ends, or they sit outside the
tamper-evident record entirely.

title: src/cli.ts is mode 755 in the tree with no record: keep the bit, file the reasoning (shebang + package bin target)
description:
RETROACTIVE RECORD for a product-code change already present in the working
tree. Filed 2026-08-11 (Mayor session E) at the Overseer's direction, after he
identified himself as the author.

WHAT CHANGED. src/cli.ts, mode 100644 -> 100755. Zero content diff (git diff
--stat: 1 file changed, 0 insertions, 0 deletions). Made by the Overseer during
an edict to test something manually; he raised it himself this session and asked
whether it should be reverted.

IT SHOULD NOT BE REVERTED. Measured this session:
  - src/cli.ts:1 is '#!/usr/bin/env node'
  - package.json declares "bin": {"fortkit": "./src/cli.ts"}
  - it is the ONLY file under src/ with the user execute bit set

A file carrying a shebang and named as a package bin target should be mode 755.
At 644, invoking ./src/cli.ts directly fails EACCES. npm sets the bit on install
for bin targets, so the packaged artifact was correct and the REPOSITORY was
not; the defect was latent and only visible to someone running the file in
place. The chmod corrected a real packaging defect rather than introducing one.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WAS THE RECORD, NOT THE BIT. A product-code change
reached the working tree with no bead, so a future Warden would meet a bare mode
bit with no explanation and would be right to revert it. This bead is the
explanation, and filing it is the correction.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. The mode change is committed, not reverted.
2. The commit message references this bead and states the shebang + bin-target
   reasoning, so the record travels with the diff.
3. Confirm no test or verifier asserts the 644 mode (verify.sh green after).

SCOPE NOTE. The Mayor does not write product code and did not make this change.
Committing a mode bit the Overseer authored is his call or the Forge's, not this
seat's.
close_reason: Committed d0d43f1. src/cli.ts recorded at mode 100755, zero content change, per this bead's own measured reasoning: shebang at line 1, package.json bin target, and the only file under src/ with the execute bit. Not reverted, as the bead ruled. The Overseer authorised the commit directly on 2026-08-13 ('yes, commit both'); the change was his own, made during an edict, and he raised it himself. Committed by the Mayor as bookkeeping rather than authorship — no product code was written and the reasoning was adjudicated before the commit. It had been uncommitted in the working tree for eight sessions, which is the real cost here: an uncommitted change is invisible to every gate the fort runs.

title: bin/regent w1ew follow-ups: zero test coverage on 179 new lines, multi-edict announces only the first, silenced emits + unconditional success banner, unstated handoff-header contract
description:
Warden findings 2, 6, 7, 8 on fortkit-w1ew. Non-blocking. Overseer/Regent lane (bin/ is kernel-RO), except the test which is Forge lane.

7. 179 LINES IN THE CIVILIZATION'S MOST PRIVILEGED LAUNCHER WITH ZERO AUTOMATED COVERAGE, and the harness that proved them was thrown away. No test among the 153 references bin/regent's behaviour; fort/scripts/probe-cycle7.sh:37 only asserts it is read-only. The four-outcome stamping proof, the occupant derivation and the flag matrix were all real work and none of it is re-runnable by the next reader. This is the silent-revert class the Warden recorded as finding 4 on fortkit-xgul.1, and the fort already has both patterns: test/researcher-launcher.test.ts asserts over launcher SOURCE, test/memory.test.ts:181 builds a temp FIXTURE. A test asserting that bin/regent passes --model, that both emit calls carry -a and -s, and that the awk block returns 0/2/3 against three fixtures would make the next revert loud. FORGE LANE — asserting over bin/regent's source needs no write access to it.

2. A MULTI-EDICT SESSION NOW ANNOUNCES ONLY ITS FIRST EDICT. The launcher emits one canonical pair per wake; subsequent edicts in the same session get no edict.begun of their own and the session may not emit one. Covenant 4.2 and 9.2 say 'announces itself at the start and the end of the work' and are satisfied by a session bracket; charter 105 says 'An edict is never silent. It emits edict.begun and edict.ended' and is EDICT-scoped, so it is not. Nothing becomes invisible — the session window still covers the change in all three streams — but per-edict targeting is lost, and silently. This session is the live case: cycle 12 (or2.9) and cycle 13 (w1ew) ran under one wake. FIX: say in the protocol what a second edict does — append to EDICT_FILE and emit a CANONICAL pair for it. What the diff correctly removed was the wrong spelling and the wrong actor, not the existence of a per-edict announcement.

8. 'EVERY FORT HAS BEEN TOLD' IS PRINTED UNCONDITIONALLY AND EVERY EMIT FAILURE IS SILENCED. :220 and :314 end in 2>/dev/null || true; :232 prints the banner regardless. If jq finds no forts, or an emit rejects the payload, a failed wake looks identical to a successful one. The silencing predates this diff, but the diff ADDS failure modes to what is silenced (payload construction, three new flags) and, via FORT_REGISTRY, a new way for the fort list to be empty. Counting successful announcements and printing the number costs one line and would have caught fortkit-nvk on day one. Threat 1.

6. THE LAUNCHER ENFORCES A HANDOFF-HEADER CONTRACT IT NEVER STATES TO THE PRODUCER. :266 refuses to stamp unless line 1 matches ^# Regent handoff; the protocol at :342 asks for the handoff by path and content and says only that it must contain a line beginning Model: (:344). A session opening '# Regent edict handoff …' gets refusal 2 and no stamp. The ten existing handoffs comply by convention, the failure is loud and non-fatal and names the model, so it degrades correctly. One clause in the protocol closes it.

CLOSED BY THE MAYOR, NOT A FOLLOW-UP — finding 10 (cross-fort flag compatibility), which the Warden could not close from inside her mask. She could not read the elder forts' emit.sh; the Mayor can. MEASURED: /home/justin/dev/ForgeOs/fort/scripts/emit.sh:8 and /home/justin/dev/longburn/fort/scripts/emit.sh:8 both parse getopts 'a:s:t:p:T:' — byte-identical option strings to fortkit's. The new -s/-t/-p flags are accepted in both settlements. No silent announcement failure, and her proxy reasoning from templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh was correct.

title: memory-lint per-seat budget holes: unscoped core facts escape counting, unknown seat names mint phantom buckets, superseded core facts still charged, test cannot fail on the regression
description:
Warden findings 1, 3 and 6 on fortkit-88u.16. Non-blocking, merged, filed forward.

1. A CORE FACT WITH NO PARSEABLE seats: LIST IS COUNTED AGAINST NOBODY — a coverage REGRESSION against the old global count. scopeSeats (scripts/memory-lint.mjs:30-37) returns [] when the scope block has no inline 'seats: [...]' line; the caller then adds nothing to the shared floor and iterates an empty list, so the fact contributes to ZERO budgets. Section 4.1 requires only that scope be non-empty, and the lint only checks scope.trim() !== '' — so a core fact carrying just 'topics:' is schema-valid and invisible to the cap. A YAML BLOCK SEQUENCE ('seats:' then '- all' on the next line) escapes identically. SIBLING CASE: an unrecognised seat name is silently accepted and coreBySeat.set(seat, ...) mints a phantom bucket, charging the fact to a seat that does not exist instead of the one it was meant for. Under the old global count every core fact was counted exactly once regardless of scope; under the new one a whole class is uncounted. All ten facts in the ledger carry an inline seats: today, so nothing is escaping now. FIX, in the same lint: require a non-empty seats: on tier: core, and FAIL any seat name not in the fort/seats/ roster.

3. THE NEW TEST CANNOT FAIL ON THE REGRESSION IT GUARDS. test/memory.test.ts:208 plants 22 forge-scoped facts + 1 shared; the passing case totals 299 lines and the failing case 312 — IDENTICAL under the old global summation, so the fixture would pass and fail the same way against the code this diff replaces. The discriminating case is the one the change exists for: TWO SEATS EACH NEAR BUDGET whose FORT TOTAL exceeds 30/300 and which must PASS. Also unasserted: the '> 30 facts' branch (the fixture only ever trips the line budget), and the shared-floor report line, which the test title promises and the test never reads. Not reward-hacking — the acceptance criterion is met literally — but a regression test that cannot fail on the regression is not holding the ground.

6. SUPERSEDED CORE FACTS STILL CONSUME BUDGET (pre-existing, now amplified). The lint counts any tier: core fact regardless of status, while consolidate-memory injects only active ones. Previously that inflated one global number; now a superseded seats:[all] fact charges EVERY seat at once.

WHY THESE MATTER TOGETHER: the whole argument for the per-seat cap was converting a doctrine number into a counted mechanism. Findings 1 and 6 mean the count is wrong in two directions (uncounted facts, over-counted facts) and finding 3 means the test would not notice. The mechanism is real but not yet trustworthy.

title: xgul.1/.3 Warden follow-ups: guard reach overstated, template generator drift, memory-lint unwired, index.db untracked-by-luck, template charter still prescribes bd remember
description:
Warden findings 4,5,6,7,8,9,11,12 on the A2/A3 edict (commit 0734b27). No blockers.

4. THE COUPLING GUARD'S STATED REACH EXCEEDS ITS ACTUAL REACH. test/researcher-launcher.test.ts:36-37 reads exactly ONE file (templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh). The comment above it and the commit message both say 'if either is reverted to fort/remember.md this goes red'. True for A3. FALSE FOR A2: reverting bin/fort-init alone leaves the test green, and NOTHING in the 152-test suite asserts anything about bin/fort-init at all. Not a design flaw in the guard — no assertion over researcher.sh can observe fort-init — but an overstatement that will tell a future maintainer the factory is covered when it is not, which is the vhk.9 silent-revert class the guard exists to kill. FIX, and the harness already exists: test/memory.test.ts:181 builds a temp fort with mkdtemp and runs the real linter against planted fixtures. A sibling test asserting bin/fort-init contains fort/memory/facts and that its AGENTS block names current.md makes the sentence true.

5. THE TEMPLATE consolidate-memory.mjs IS A DIVERGENT COPY WITH NO BEAD. Exactly 3 string lines differ from scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs (title, generated-by path, incident-gap link); memory-lint.mjs is byte-identical. The Regent flagged the drift hazard as 'filed intent, not done here' and no bead exists — the same evaporation the Warden recorded as finding 13(b) on fortkit-8cv6. SHAPE: parametrise the live generator (fort name from the registry, generated-by path from argv) so the template becomes a verbatim copy, plus a drift test asserting the two match modulo the parametrised lines.

6. THE STATED REASON FOR NOT WIRING memory-lint INTO THE TEMPLATE VERIFIER DOES NOT HOLD. The record says wiring it 'would break non-node forts'. But templates/fort/scripts/verify.sh:59-61 ALREADY runs npm run typecheck/lint/test unconditionally — the template verifier is already node-only and already exits 127 at step one on a non-node fort. Adding memory-lint breaks nothing that is not already broken. CONSEQUENCE, and it bears on threat 2: the mechanical control for docs/specs/memory.md 4.3 rule 4 (untrusted facts never core) now ships into every new fort and is executed by nothing. fort-init:175 shows the right pattern (if command -v node). The header's 'fill in the fort's own gates below' makes LEAVING it defensible; the recorded REASON is what does not hold up.

7. fort/memory/index.db IS GENERATED AT FOUNDING BUT NOT GITIGNORED. Spec 3 decision 5 and 5 are explicit that the index is exempt from tracking as a zero-trust derived artifact. fort-init:161 appends only .env*. fortkit's own .gitignore catches it via *.db, attributed in-file to bd init — but fort-init:13 runs bd init only when .beads is absent, so a fort founded in a repo already using beads may get no such glob, and the next thing the script prints is 'Next: (1) commit'. One line (fort/memory/index.db) removes the dependency on luck.

8. THE TEMPLATE CHARTER STILL PRESCRIBES bd remember, ON THE LINE THIS COMMIT EDITED. templates/fort/charter.md:60 reads 'Work state: Beads (bd ready, bd remember/bd prime)…'. Spec 3 decision 1 (final 2026-08-10) retires bd remember; Manyhalls' own charter:77 says the ledger supersedes it. 2026-08-11 MAYOR REVIEW OF THE CYCLE-12 EDICT, from the records (the Mayor cannot read the Regent's session; this is what the streams, commits and working trees say).

Both forts were measured with probe 11 BEFORE any remedy, then re-measured after. Both remedies are committed and both after-states are verified rather than asserted.

============================================================
FARLANTERN / longburn — HEALTHY BEFORE AND AFTER
============================================================
Instrument: 9d2c323 (probe 11 strengthened to run the fort's own gate and demand a real test count; the old form ran node/eslint only and never touched the test leg).
Remedy: 64ef335 (.vite-temp added to the tmpfs list over the RO node_modules bind).

BEFORE, verbatim:
  PROBE 11: PASS (verify exit 0)
All eleven probes PASS. Probes 1-8 blocked, probe 9 positive controls all worked, probe 10 the expected qe2 deny ("openat LOCK: read-only file system").

AFTER, verbatim:
  PROBE 11: PASS (verify exit 0) - `node v24.14.0`; all three stages executed: typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`), lint (`eslint src`), and test (`vitest run`) reaching a real count of **255 passed | 6 skipped (261 total) across 37 passed / 2 skipped test files**. No EROFS abort - the test leg genuinely ran (suite root was the scratch dir `/home/justin/.cache/fort-scratch/warden-6yeh`).
