The .vite-temp gap is LATENT exactly as the correction on this bead predicted (no vitest.config.*, so Vite never writes .vite-temp), and the added line is insurance, not a repair. The earlier "reviewing without executable verifiers right now" is measured FALSE.

============================================================
PROOFDELVE / ForgeOs — THE SUSPICION WAS WRONG; SOMETHING ELSE WAS BROKEN
============================================================
Instrument: 35ebc0e (probe 11 added; probes 1-10 unchanged and unrenumbered).
Remedy: 07010e7 (three allow entries in fort/profiles/warden-settings.json).
Runs: WARDEN_SMOKE=1 fort/scripts/warden.sh ForgeOs-mskx HEAD~1..HEAD, twice. Log /tmp/warden-mskx.log.

BEFORE, verbatim:
  PROBE 11: FAIL shellcheck could not execute - permission refusal
  (b) `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` -> refused by permission settings ("This command requires approval"). The gate cannot be run in its sanctioned single-command form at all.
  docker-precheck: could not execute - `docker info` permission-refused (not "docker unreachable")
  shellcheck: could not execute - permission-refused, as were `shellcheck --version` and `command -v shellcheck`
  Executed and passing: dotnet-build ("Build succeeded. 0 Warning(s) 0 Error(s)"), dotnet-test ("Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 152, Skipped: 3, Total: 155"), web-deps ("added 29 packages ... in 974ms"), web-typecheck (exit 0), web-build ("216 modules transformed").
  On node_modules, verbatim: "web/node_modules did not exist before I started - `ls` returned 'No such file or directory' ... `npm --prefix web ci` succeeded ... So this fort's dependency on that install held here - but it held on a cache whose presence I did not have to arrange and cannot guarantee for the next session."

AFTER, verbatim:
  PROBE 11: PASS (verify exit 0)
  "(b) `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` ran without any permission prompt. (c) not applicable - nothing was refused."
  All seven stages executed: dotnet-build clean | docker-precheck "Docker unreachable -> warned and continued (expected)" | dotnet-test "Failed: 0, Passed: 152, Skipped: 3" | web-deps 29 packages | web-typecheck clean | web-build 216 modules in 112ms | shellcheck clean.
  The seat's own caveat on the exit code is kept rather than smoothed: capturing $? verbatim was itself refused, so exit 0 was inferred from the FILTERED VERIFY ONLY line, which under set -euo pipefail is only reachable after the shellcheck step returns 0.

WHAT IT SETTLES:
1. DO NOT PORT fortkit's node_modules bind here. The fort's own web-deps stage (verify.sh:76) does that job and was measured working. Recorded fragility: 29 packages in ~950ms is a warm npm cache, and the seat said plainly it cannot guarantee that for the next session. A cold cache or an offline host turns this into a real outage; the other two forts do not have that single point of failure.
2. What was actually broken was the PERMISSION PROFILE, which allow-listed dotnet/npm/npx but neither fort/scripts/verify.sh nor shellcheck. This fort's Warden could not run the sanctioned gate at all. Fixed at 07010e7 and re-measured.
3. docker-precheck's warn-and-continue is now OBSERVED rather than inferred - the before-run could not see it because `docker info` was refused before it could report unreachability.

The block on the SEAT is at the tool/permission layer only. That is correct by design - verifiers must write - but "read-only by construction" means the seat, not the tree.

title: warden.sh 8cv6 follow-ups: dirty-tree blindness, unconditional recipe prose, HEAD-equality derivation, unguarded worktree node_modules, bind ordering, /tmp export retention
description:
Warden findings 5,6,7,8,9,10,12 on the fortkit-8cv6 Regent edict (commit 2e0744d). No blockers; all filed forward so 8cv6 can close on the Overseer's gate-1 half.

5. THE GUARD CHECKS COMMIT REACHABILITY IN $src, NOT CONTENT IN THE SCRATCH — and a dirty working tree still puts unreviewed code in front of the seat. REALIZED, not hypothetical, in Ilva's own 8cv6 session: /home/justin/dev/fortkit had uncommitted modifications, so the fort/charter.md she read in cwd carried the fortkit-vhk.5.3 accepted-residual amendment that was in NO COMMIT. She read uncommitted text as law. Benign and unrelated here, but the launcher printed 'the scratch will contain the code under review' to a seat that cannot check that claim — which is the exact defect class 8cv6 exists to kill. FIX: after the rsync, run git -C $src status --porcelain and either warn loudly in the briefing or list the dirty paths to the seat.

6. VERIFIER RECIPE AND BEADS ACCESS ARE UNCONDITIONAL PROSE, so the failure paths reintroduce the original defect in miniature. If 'npm ci --offline --ignore-scripts' or 'bd export' fails, the launcher warns on the OPERATOR's stderr and then still tells the seat 'cwd already contains node_modules … so the verifiers execute' and 'a fresh full issue export is in cwd'. The seat is the one party who cannot see the warning. The trailing 'if you still cannot execute a verifier you MUST say so' is a real backstop and why this is non-blocking. FIX: build both paragraphs conditionally from $nm_src and the export's exit status. Related: --offline fails outright when a candidate lockfile adds a package absent from the local npm cache; a retry without --offline, or an explicit note in the warning, recovers it. --ignore-scripts is the right default and stays.

7. WORKTREE DERIVATION MATCHES HEAD EQUALITY, so reviewing an earlier commit of a live branch falsely REFUSES 68. If the Forge's worktree moved past the commit named in the range, no worktree HEAD equals the tip, the merged-into-main test also fails, and a legitimate request is refused. Loud, and the workaround is one argument away, so a usability nit rather than a trap. FIX: match 'the worktree whose HEAD CONTAINS the tip'.

8. THE LOCKFILE GUARD COVERS ONLY THE FALLBACK, not $src's own node_modules. nm_src="$src/node_modules" binds unconditionally when it exists; the 'cmp -s' against package-lock.json runs only on the $root fallback branch. A worktree carrying a stale node_modules from an older lockfile binds unchecked — the same stale-dependency false-green the guard was written to prevent (longburn Warden 6vc r2 finding 4a). Measured mitigation today: worktree 00h's package-lock.json is byte-identical to main's and worktrees here appear not to carry their own node_modules, so the fallback is the live path.

9. THE node_modules BIND IS APPENDED AFTER build_mask's PER-FILE MASKS. seat-sandbox.sh records the ordering invariant explicitly: subtree binds go BEFORE the /dev/null file masks and tmpfs dir masks, because a later subtree bind remounts real content over a mask. The new code appends a subtree bind last. The in-code comment defends the DESTINATION side ('no masked path lies beneath /tmp/warden-*'), which Ilva checked and which holds. The unexamined side is the SOURCE: build_mask globs "$x"/*/.env*, so $root/node_modules/.env is a maskable path and binding $root/node_modules onto the scratch would expose it unmasked. MEASURED: zero .env* at node_modules/.env* or node_modules/*/.env*. Latent hazard, not a live leak — SO11 says documented rather than defended against, but a one-line assertion (refuse if any MASK_FILES entry lies beneath $nm_src) makes the invariant hold by construction instead of by today's directory contents. Threat 4.

10. THE BEAD EXPORT PERSISTS IN WORLD-READABLE /tmp. The rsync deliberately excludes /.beads; the new .beads-export.jsonl puts the same content (1.9 MB, mode 0644, under a 0755 scratch dir) back in /tmp, surviving until the next review with the same bead suffix. Reachable only by a local shell-holding actor, whom the charter puts explicitly out of scope, and the content is already in git and pushed offsite. The RETENTION is the part worth a cheap fix: delete the export where the scratch is torn down.

12. PROBE 10 ASSERTS bd MUST FAIL. If defect 3 is ever fixed properly (bd made readable in-mask), the smoke reports FAIL for an improvement. It is labelled EXPECTED-DENY / accepted cost so it reads as a deliberate change-detector, but recording it so whoever fixes bd flips the probe rather than chasing it.

LANE: live fort/scripts/warden.sh is kernel-RO (Overseer/Regent); templates/fort/scripts/warden.sh is Forge-writable. Findings 5-10 apply to both copies.
notes:
2026-08-11 SCOPE ADDITION — the dirty-tree defect is not review-only; it bites DISPATCH too, and it did so within three hours of being filed.

Finding 5 on this bead is about warden.sh: a dirty $src makes the launcher's 'the scratch will contain the code under review' false, and Ilva read an uncommitted charter amendment as law. The SAME cause bit in the opposite direction on fortkit-88u.16 the same afternoon: the Mayor edited docs/specs/memory.md and did not commit; forge.sh was dispatched; the Forge branched from COMMITTED main, saw the old wording, correctly concluded the spec needed updating, and wrote its own version. Two seats, two directions, one root cause — a working tree that disagrees with HEAD, invisibly to the seat.

ADD TO SCOPE: forge.sh gets the same dirty-tree treatment as warden.sh. At minimum, warn loudly when dispatching with uncommitted changes; better, name the dirty paths in the launcher's stdout so the Mayor sees what the Forge will NOT see. Refusing outright is probably too strong for the Forge — a Mayor legitimately has work in flight — but silence is clearly wrong, and 'the Mayor will remember to commit' is the prose control that already failed once today.

This is the fort's standing conversion applied to its own launchers: when a constraint keeps being violated in prose, it becomes a mechanism.

title: Handoffs have no supersession mechanism: three rounds on one bead produced two stale-record incidents in a row
description:
Warden's generalizable finding underneath vhk.9 round-2 finding 1, filed as the class fix rather than the instance.

THE OBSERVED PATTERN (two incidents, one bead, one day). fortkit-vhk.9 ran three Forge rounds. Twice, an earlier round's handoff was left asserting as VERIFIED FACT something a later round reverted:
  r1 (forge-2026-08-11-vhk.9.md) states 'Every launcher event and the durable bd comment in that template now uses actor id saelin' and lists Overseer reinstallation of the live launcher as a next action. Round 2 reverted all of it.
  r2 (forge-2026-08-11-vhk.9-r2.md) states the memory-surface claim that round 3 reverted.
Both were caught by the Warden, one per round (her r1 finding 4, her r2 finding 1). Neither is a falsification: nothing was rewritten, and each later handoff exists. But a reader who lands on r1 or r2 ALONE is misled, and the fort has no mechanism that would tell them.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS FIXABLE. The facts ledger already solved this. fort/memory/facts/*.md carry a superseded-by: frontmatter field, and scripts/memory-lint.mjs:62-69 ENFORCES and RESOLVES it — a superseded fact cannot silently read as current. Handoffs have no such field, and no lint. The same fort therefore holds two record surfaces with opposite guarantees, and the one WITHOUT the guarantee is the one the Forge writes several times per bead.

SCOPE:
  1. Add a superseded-by: field to the handoff schema in fort/seats/*.md (all seats share one schema). Prose-gated: needs Overseer prior approval on this bead and charter.amended per edit.
  2. Teach scripts/memory-lint.mjs to resolve it over fort/handoffs/ as it already does over fort/memory/facts/, so a stale handoff fails the verifier rather than waiting for a Warden to notice.
  3. Decide whether the LAUNCHER writes it. forge.sh already computes collision-safe -rN suffixes (fortkit-vn8) and therefore already knows, at stamp time, that it is writing round N of a bead whose rounds 1..N-1 exist. It could stamp the supersession pointer mechanically, which is strictly better than asking a model to remember. This is the highest-leverage item.
  4. Backfill is NOT in scope and must not be done by rewriting: the vhk.9 r1 and r2 corrections are APPENDED, per SO7.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE MACHINERY (SO11 — observed, not imagined): two incidents in one day on one bead, both caught only because a frontier-model Warden read every round. The fort's own CLAUDE.md states the principle: when a constraint keeps getting violated despite prose instructions, encode it as a test.
acceptance_criteria: The handoff schema carries a supersession field; memory-lint resolves it over fort/handoffs/ and fails on an unresolved stale handoff; a decision is recorded on whether forge.sh stamps it mechanically, with rationale either way.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
SECOND INSTANCE IN ONE DAY, and this one shows the launcher itself creating the stale record. Ilva, finding 1 on the fortkit-x02m review, 2026-08-17.

The Forge handoff for x02m says in 'Verified facts' that the verifier 'is red solely on all seven test/seats.test.ts assertions', and in 'Open risks' that 'the template-render lint is part of the verifier but is not reached after Vitest stops the fail-fast sequence' — i.e. that a bead-listed discriminating check was never demonstrated.

TWENTY LINES BELOW, IN THE SAME FILE, the launcher-observed block records the same command in the same worktree at 11:28:48 at exit 0, 188/188, template-render GREEN. Ilva's own run agrees. My run of seats.test.ts on main agrees (7 passed, Node v24.14.0, same version the handoff blames).

So the file contains a claim and its refutation, the refutation is later and authoritative, and NOTHING MARKS THE EARLIER CLAIM AS SUPERSEDED. A reader who stops at 'Open risks' concludes an acceptance criterion is unmet. A reader who reads to the bottom concludes it is met. Both are reading the same document honestly.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM THE FIRST INSTANCE ON THIS BEAD, and why it sharpens the requirement: the stale text was written by the SEAT and the superseding stamp was appended by the LAUNCHER. This is not a seat failing to update its own prose. It is forge.sh appending a green stamp to a file whose body already says red, with no mechanism to reconcile them, and doing it correctly by its own lights. The launcher is doing the right thing and manufacturing a contradiction while doing it.

SO THE REPAIR CANNOT BE 'SEATS SHOULD UPDATE THEIR HANDOFFS'. The seat had already exited when the superseding measurement was taken. Whatever supersession mechanism this bead lands must be writable by the LAUNCHER at stamp time, and must make the superseded claim unreadable-as-current rather than merely followed by a correction. Appending is what created the problem here.

RELATED, same day, same class from the other direction: an SO7 correction is appended to fortkit-a355 for a handoff bullet stating a posture-specific result unconditionally, with its qualifier four sections away. Consolidated evidence on fortkit-ff2j.

A launcher change dropping the extra-ro argument would flip those two to FAIL while fort/profiles and fort/scripts kept passing — the probe cannot tell 'denied by the constitution rule' from 'denied by the blanket root bind'.

FROM THE WARDEN'S vhk.5.5 REVIEW (non-blocking):
  1. Header discloses the canary residue but not the two EXISTING files the probe opens for append: $root/fort/charter.md (line 187) and $root/.git/config (line 192), both via probe_write_denied's ': >> $1'. Threat 1, and pointedly so — the charter's own roster of realized incidents names 'a probe that corrupted .git/config'. Unchanged from main and reachable only after the mask has already failed, but it is the half of the footprint most worth announcing and it is the half omitted.
  2. Header misnames the .git/hooks residue: it says '.researcher-boundary-canary' but line 193 creates 'researcher-boundary-canary', no leading dot. One character, and it is the difference between what a bare ls shows and what a hooks-integrity watcher would key on.
  3. The skip WIRING is untested — only the exit predicate is. probe_exit_status was hoisted above the BASH_SOURCE guard so tests reach it, but report_skip stayed inside the main block, so nothing proves a real SKIP increments the counter or that the summary prints its third field. Same shape as the bead's own finding 4: predicate tested, wiring not. Fix: hoist report/report_skip above the guard as probe_exit_status already is. INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by the Mayor, by a different route: sourcing the probe and calling report_write_denial on a missing parent prints 'report_skip: command not found' and returns rc=0, so a sourced skip is silently lost AND reads as a pass.
  5. Untested predicates remain in BOTH directions: no_dangerous_skip, settings_profile_selected, probe_write_denied, ordinary_readable, secret_inode_masked, git_status_works. The first two are pure static predicates needing the same two-line treatment, and no_dangerous_skip is the assertion standing between this fort and --dangerously-skip-permissions.
  7. Argument parsing inspects only $2, so 'probe.sh <root> --strict junk' silently ignores junk while 'probe.sh <root> junk' correctly exits 64; a shift loop like verify.sh:13-22 matches the fort's style. The ${1:?Usage...} message was not updated to [--strict] although the case usage string was.

title: Drift watcher misclassifies 'never propagated' as 'regression', and treats the capital's own design as decay
description:
OBSERVED in the fortkit-or2.4 first live run, 2026-08-11: 9 of 38 filed beads carry reason 'template file is absent from fort' with suggestion 'regression'.

DEFECT 1 — 'absent' is not 'regressed'. A regression means a fort LOST something it had. These files were never propagated. Their propagation is already tracked by fortkit-vhk.7, so the watcher files duplicates of a known open epic and labels them with a cause that did not happen. Clearest case: fortkit-xy3g, 'Drift: Manyhalls fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh' — merged two hours before the scan, deliberately template-only, propagation explicitly deferred on the bead. It was filed as a regression against three forts before it was a day old.

Distinguishing the two is cheap and mechanical: absent-in-fort + present-in-template + fort has NO history of the file = 'not yet propagated'; present-in-both-but-diverged = drift; present-in-fort-history-but-now-absent = genuine regression. The middle case is the only one that needs a human.

DEFECT 2 — the capital reads its own constitution as decay. For MANYHALLS, template-file-with-no-fort/-counterpart is STRUCTURALLY NORMAL. Installing into fort/scripts/ is Overseer's-hand work by cycle-7 design, because that path is kernel-RO to every seat. So the capital will show 'absent from fort' in perpetuity for everything not yet hand-installed, and no amount of correct behaviour will clear it. A watcher that files an unfixable bead every run trains its fort to ignore the watcher — the same habituation failure that retired the ruflo hooks.

Suggest: treat the capital as a special case (it IS the template source; compare only files it has actually installed), or exclude fort/scripts/ for the capital, or classify absent-in-capital as 'pending hand-install' with no bead.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is an unattended watcher whose whole value is that a human trusts its output enough to act on it. At 9-of-38 the noise is a quarter of the signal, and it duplicates an epic that is already open. The or2.5 cross-fort duplicate-work triage bead exists for exactly this hazard.

DISPOSITION of the 9 already filed: supersede under fortkit-vhk.7 rather than close (SO7 — records are append-only and corrections are appended). Needs the Overseer's call, since 38 beads landed in the real tracker.

A not-yet-propagated finding with no bead already tracking it is DEFERRED — reported in the run output and in the drift.scan payload as findingsDeferred, but not filed. Their propagation is tracked by fortkit-vhk.7 and the watcher should not duplicate an open epic.

DEFECT 2 — the capital reading its own constitution as decay. No capital special case was added, and none is needed: Manyhalls IS the template source and its fort/scripts is installed by the Overseer's hand, so files it has not yet hand-installed have no history under that path and classify as not-yet-propagated by the SAME rule that serves the elder forts. One rule, no exception, nothing to keep in sync.

MEASURED on the live tracker, dry-run, 2026-08-12: 9 of 39 findings now classify as not-yet-propagated — precisely your 9-of-38 — and they are exactly the researcher surface:
  Farlantern  fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh, fort/scripts/researcher.sh, fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json, fort/seats/researcher.md
  Proofdelve  the same four

The 5 findings still classified regression are genuine losses, not absences: absent permission rules in three forts' .claude/settings.json, an absent 'Human gates' heading in Farlantern's charter, and an absent standing order in Proofdelve's. That is the signal your bead was defending.

DISPOSITION of the 9 already filed: unchanged by this work and still owed. 4 of the 9 are already closed and their identities now suppress on the closed-bead one-shot rule; the rest sit among the open Drift beads.

-AHEAD=$(git rev-list --count origin/main..main 2>/dev/null)
-echo "  branch: $(git branch --show-current), ${AHEAD:-?} commit(s) ahead of origin/main"
-[ "${AHEAD:-0}" -gt 3 ] && echo "  ⚠ PUSH DRIFT: >3 unpushed commits"
+# NOT "ahead of origin" (fortkit-rw86). origin/main is a LOCAL remote-tracking
+# ref: it moves only when THIS clone pushes or fetches, so the number below is
+# commits since this clone last synced. That equals "ahead of the remote" only

+# with git ls-remote: a stale 19 in {{FORT_NAME}} and a stale 24 in Farlantern that

+# at exactly the moment the fort could not see its own state.

+  echo "  branch: $(git branch --show-current), sync state UNKNOWN — no readable origin/main tracking ref"

+fi

comments.text:
DO NOT CLOSE ON fortkit-z0j8 (merged 2026-08-13). Warden finding 1 on that bead, and she corrected her own earlier claim to reach it: her fortkit-29e9 finding 4 called z0j8 'the five lines that let hhjb/vxpq/8eq5 close', and that was wrong.

WHY. civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs compares NORMALIZED bytes (:340), and the normalizer (:62-77) substitutes only repo path, fort name and roster actor names — it does NOT strip comments. z0j8 removed the last EXECUTABLE divergence between the live and template seat-sandbox libs, but a 3-line-to-1-line comment difference at lines 162-168 survives normalization, so this path still reads divergent.

MEASURED BY THE MAYOR POST-MERGE, not inferred: a live drift-watch --dry-run reports fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh as 'upgrade-offer' in ALL THREE forts, plan unchanged at {file 0, comment 9, suppress 30, defer 0}.

THIS DISCHARGES WHEN fortkit-52vf.10.1 LANDS, which owns that comment and must repair FOUR copies in one change (the three live libs plus templates/, widened 2026-08-13). Do not attempt a separate pass over this file first: a second pass re-opens drift in the opposite direction, which is the failure fortkit-29e9 existed to prevent.

CAVEAT ON SCOPE, in the Warden's own words: she could measure only the capital's pair. Proofdelve and Farlantern are outside her mask, and their libs also carry a separately-authored half of E8 that this fort has never reviewed — so for hhjb and 8eq5 the remaining divergence may be LARGER than the comment. fortkit-52vf.10.1 landed. It does not, and the reason is recorded here rather than the bead
being left to look forgotten.

so repairing the shared comment would remove the divergence. That is true of the comment I
repaired and false of what remains, because the comment I repaired was IDENTICAL in all four
copies and so was never part of any of these findings in the first place. Measured after the
change:

MEASURED BY THE MAYOR POST-MERGE, not inferred: a live drift-watch --dry-run reports fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh as 'upgrade-offer' in ALL THREE forts, plan unchanged at {file 0, comment 9, suppress 30, defer 0}.

THIS DISCHARGES WHEN fortkit-52vf.10.1 LANDS, which owns that comment and must repair FOUR copies in one change (the three live libs plus templates/, widened 2026-08-13). Do not attempt a separate pass over this file first: a second pass re-opens drift in the opposite direction, which is the failure fortkit-29e9 existed to prevent.

CAVEAT ON SCOPE, in the Warden's own words: she could measure only the capital's pair. Proofdelve and Farlantern are outside her mask, and their libs also carry a separately-authored half of E8 that this fort has never reviewed — so for hhjb and 8eq5 the remaining divergence may be LARGER than the comment. RE-MEASURED AND NOT CLOSED — Regent edict fortkit-52vf.12 (E10), Calder Sealbroken
(they/them), model opus, Overseer present, 2026-08-13. E10 expected this bead to close once
fortkit-52vf.10.1 landed. It does not, and the reason is recorded here rather than the bead
being left to look forgotten.

E10's reasoning was that the watcher compares NORMALIZED bytes and does not strip comments,
so repairing the shared comment would remove the divergence. That is true of the comment I
repaired and false of what remains, because the comment I repaired was IDENTICAL in all four
copies and so was never part of any of these findings in the first place. Measured after the
change:

  Manyhalls    fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh   1 hunk   0 identity-suspect
  Proofdelve   fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh   5 hunks  0 identity-suspect
  Farlantern   fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh   7 hunks  0 identity-suspect

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS, read from the bodies:
  Manyhalls   one comment clause the capital carries and the template lacks, explaining that
              the Forge is covered by Landlock keeping the main .git outside its writable
              scope. Real prose divergence, comment only, no behaviour.
  Proofdelve  and Farlantern: each fort's copy cites its OWN cycle-7 bead alongside
              fortkit-i4y (ForgeOs-8c9, longburn-suti), and the surrounding paragraph is
              reflowed to fit. Real divergence, comment only, no behaviour.

is architecture and none is identity. Closing them needs a decision this sitting had no
mandate for: whether a fort's copy of a shared lib may cite its own fort's bead id, or whether
those citations should collapse to the template's wording. That is the Mayor's call under the
parity programme (fortkit-wg8w), not the Regent's, and it is the same question for all three.

DID read as identity-suspect under the first draft of fortkit-qu46's rule, because a fort-local

above are 0 for all three, and that is now the correct reading: nobody's name is at risk in
these files.

behaviour difference between the forts.

title: drift-watch reports every child failure as 'already running or flock failed', hiding the real cause
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-11 during the fortkit-or2.4 timer install. The first scheduled-style run failed and the journal read:

  drift watcher already running or flock failed: Command failed: flock -n /tmp/fortkit-drift-watch.lock <node> <script> --lock-held
  spawn bd ENOENT

The ACTUAL cause was the second line: systemd's user PATH is /home/justin/.atuin/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, which does not contain ~/.local/bin where bd lives, so the watcher's bare 'bd' spawn failed. The lock was never contended at all.

civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:498-502 wraps execFileAsync('flock', ...) in a single .catch() that rethrows EVERY failure as 'drift watcher already running or flock failed'. flock exits non-zero both when the lock is held AND when the child command fails for any reason, so the message asserts a cause it has not established.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC MESSAGE: this is an UNATTENDED cron watcher. Its failures land in a journal, not in front of a human. A message that says 'already running' is one an operator reasonably ignores as benign contention — it reads like the safety interlock doing its job. A silently non-functioning drift watcher reports no drift, which is indistinguishable from no drift existing. The fort would believe it had coverage it did not have.

FIX: distinguish the cases. flock returns exit 1 specifically for lock-not-acquired with -n; any other exit is the child's. Report the child's exit code and stderr verbatim rather than asserting contention. At minimum, include the underlying error in the message instead of replacing it.

RELATED: the PATH defect itself is fixed in the or2.4 installer by deriving and asserting the unit's PATH before writing the unit. This bead is about the watcher misreporting its own failure cause, which would have hidden any other startup failure just as effectively.

Verified independently by the Mayor, not read off the record: main green exit 0 / 162 tests; --dry-run on the live tracker reports file:0 comment:16 suppress:23, the zero-to-file acceptance criterion; 51 open Drift beads to 35 with zero duplicate titles; and the new suite is red against the pre-E7 implementation. comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
FIXED by Regent edict E7 (fortkit-52vf.8), commit c6875a6, 2026-08-12. Your diagnosis was exact and the fix is the one you specified: distinguish the cases rather than assert a cause.

The launcher now runs 'flock -n -E 75 <lock> ...'. flock exits 75, and only 75, when the lock is not acquired; every other status came from the child. So:
  exit 75            -> 'drift watcher is already running: <lock> is held', exit 75
  any other exit     -> the child's stdout and stderr are written through verbatim, and the message names the child's exit code and the last line of its stderr
  flock itself fails -> 'drift watcher could not run flock: <reason>'
The process exit code is the child's, not a flattened 1.

MEASURED ON BOTH BRANCHES, 2026-08-12:
  contention, lock held by a background flock:
    'drift watcher is already running: /tmp/fortkit-drift-watch.lock is held', exit 75
  your exact scenario, PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin so bd is unreachable:
    'drift watcher could not read the tracker: spawn bd ENOENT'
    'drift watcher child failed (exit 1): drift watcher could not read the tracker: spawn bd ENOENT'
    exit 1
That second one is the journal line from your bead, now naming its real cause instead of claiming benign contention.

Related, and it is why the tracker read is now wrapped: a bd failure used to surface as a raw execFile error from deep in the call stack. It is caught and re-thrown as 'drift watcher could not read the tracker: ...' so the operator learns which seam died before they learn how.

title: f3y follow-on: two MORE double-slash denies (.ssh/.aws), and the template hardcodes one user's home
description:
FOUND WHILE VERIFYING fortkit-f3y, and NOT covered by the Overseer's f3y approval — that approval was scoped to the three .env lines. Filing rather than editing, because the fix is a different decision than the one approved.

MAYOR'S ERROR, stated plainly: the f3y scope was reported as 'exactly two files, three lines each' on the basis of a grep for 'env' plus a grep that listed matching FILES rather than matching LINES. Two more broken lines in the same deny block went unreported. The Overseer applied the approved f3y fix to the live profile and these remained.

STILL PRESENT in BOTH fort/profiles/warden-settings.json:49-50 and templates/fort/profiles/warden-settings.json:49-50:
  "Read(//home/justin/.ssh/**)"
  "Read(//home/justin/.aws/**)"

DEFECT 1 — same double-slash class as f3y. A deny glob binds a spelling; no real path is spelled with a leading double slash, so both match nothing.

DEFECT 2 — WORSE IN THE TEMPLATE, and this is the new part. bin/fort-init:27-29 renders only {{REPO_PATH}}, {{PROJECT}}, {{DATE}}, {{FORT_NAME}}, {{FORT_BANNER}}, {{FOUNDING_SPEC}}, {{PURPOSE}}, {{EXTRA_GATES}}, {{EXTRA_ORDERS}}. There is NO home placeholder. So the factory template ships ONE USER'S LITERAL HOME PATH to every fort it founds. On any other machine or user those lines are meaningless twice over.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN EXPOSURE: seat-sandbox.sh:66 puts $HOME/.ssh and $HOME/.aws in MASK_DIRS, so both are tmpfs-masked at the kernel for every seat. The boundary holds. But unlike the f3y .env lines, these have NO working relative-path equivalent in the deny list — there is no Read(**/.ssh/**) — so the permission-layer half of the defense is entirely absent rather than merely redundant.

DECISION NEEDED (Overseer), because the f3y precedent does not settle it:
 (a) DROP both lines, as with f3y, on the grounds that the kernel mask is the real boundary and dead lines inflate an auditor's confidence; or
 (b) ADD a {{HOME}} placeholder to fort-init's render() and correct the spelling to a single slash, keeping the belt-and-suspenders; or
 (c) replace with a portable relative form.

Recommend (a) for consistency with the approved f3y reasoning, plus a header note in the profile stating that .ssh/.aws are covered at the inode by seat-sandbox.sh MASK_DIRS, so the next auditor does not read their absence as a gap. Live profile is the Overseer's hand; template is Mayor lane once the decision is made.

title: vhk.5.1 Warden r2 non-blocking follow-ups: skip disclosure, --strict mode, test coverage gap, probe write-footprint
description:
Warden round-2 findings on fortkit-vhk.5.1. Clean referral, no blockers; these are beads, not merge conditions. Full verdict on vhk.5.1.

1. The SO7 correction is appended INSIDE the launcher-stamped code fence in fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-10-vhk.5.1.md (fence opens :29, closes :54, correction sits :30-38). The heading renders as literal code, and a block meant to be verbatim launcher output now contains hand-written prose. Nothing was deleted and no machine consumer is affected (consolidate-memory.mjs:234 extracts only 'State of work' and 'Next actions'). Fix by APPENDING a placement note at true end-of-file — not by relocating — unless the Overseer rules that repairing one's own misplaced insert is not a falsification. That ruling is worth having on the record either way.

2. The summary line does not disclose SKIPs: '17 pass, 0 fail' while two assertions were never measured. That line is the fort's most-copied sentence about this probe — it goes into handoffs and bead comments verbatim — and it reads identically whether 19 assertions ran or 5 did. Add a skip counter: '17 pass, 0 fail, 2 skip'.

3. Exit 0 is reachable with very little proven. Exit is [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]; SKIPs increment nothing. A fort with no src/, no .git/hooks/ and a stale canary path exits GREEN having skipped the product-code, hooks AND credential-leakage assertions. Correct trade against a vacuous PASS, but for a template vhk.7 propagates everywhere, add --strict (or a non-zero exit above a skip threshold) so no fort is trained to read green as proven. File with finding 2.

4. The tests still cannot catch the bug class that produced blocker B1. All four new cases assert REJECTION. Delete the return 0 at line 62 today and no_forbidden_tool returns 1 unconditionally — and the only test on it asserts a non-zero exit, so all seven tests stay GREEN while the assertion silently reverts to unsatisfiable. Rejection-only coverage is blind to a constant-FAIL predicate, which is exactly the defect that reached a Warden. Costs three lines: assert exact_tools, no_forbidden_tool and empty_setting_sources each SUCCEED against the real launcher.

5. The probe now writes into the tree it probes and the header does not say so. It creates and trap-removes $root/.env.probe-canary; on a mask failure the write probes also leave .researcher-boundary-canary files in src/, fort/seats/, fort/profiles/, fort/scripts/ and .git/hooks/, which are NOT gitignored. Both acceptable, but a probe that can mutate constitution directories must announce it in the header beside the chmod-755 note. Also note a SIGKILLed run leaves the canary, which downgrades the sole threat-4 control to SKIP on the next run and would trip any future secrets-scan watcher.

6. secret_inode_masked still reads a bwrap START failure as PASS (line 93, '|| return 0'). Carried from round-one finding 9 (vhk.5.4). Re-raised because it became more load-bearing: it is now the fort's ONLY proof of threat 4. Mitigated in practice since ordinary_readable and git_status_works would fail loudly if bwrap were broken, but the two outcomes deserve different report lines.

7. Assertion group C10 passes by a different mechanism than a reader would assume. fort/charter.md and fort/seats/ are NOT in RO_PATHS for the claude branch — cycle 7 moved them to the prose gate; only the codex branch keeps them (seat-sandbox.sh:110). Those probes pass because researcher.sh passes $root itself as extra_ro, making the whole tree read-only. Correct, and it is the Researcher's real posture, but the probe cannot distinguish 'denied by the constitution rule' from 'denied by the blanket root bind'. A launcher change dropping the extra-ro argument would flip those two to FAIL while fort/profiles and fort/scripts kept passing. Matters to whoever writes vhk.5.3.

IN SCOPE for the Forge: findings 2 (skip counter in the summary line), 3 (--strict / non-zero exit above a skip threshold), 4 (positive-success assertions for exact_tools, no_forbidden_tool, empty_setting_sources — the constant-FAIL blind spot), 5 (header must announce the probe's write footprint, including that a SIGKILLed run leaves the .env.probe-canary).

  PASS - probe in the vhk.5.5 worktree: '17 pass, 0 fail, 2 skip'. The skip counter is real and the two .git/* skips are the honest linked-worktree ones.
  PASS - --strict exits 1 on the same run. Measured: STRICT EXIT=1. Finding 3 satisfied.

  PASS - verify.sh 152 tests, up from 150. Monotonic.

ONE NEW FINDING, non-blocking, for the Warden's attention and for round 2 or a follow-on:
report_skip is defined INSIDE the 'if [ ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} = $0 ]' main block, but report_write_denial is a TOP-LEVEL function that calls it. When the probe is SOURCED — which is exactly how test/researcher-launcher.test.ts exercises it — the skip path breaks. Measured, not theorised:
  $ bash -c 'source .../probe-researcher-boundaries.sh; report_write_denial "sourced skip path" /nonexistent-dir-xyz/target; echo rc=$?'
  probe-researcher-boundaries.sh: line 110: report_skip: command not found
  rc=0
The executed path is FINE (the main block defines report_skip before the .git/* calls, and my run counted both skips). But sourced, a skip is silently lost AND returns 0, which reads as a pass. That is the same shape as the defect finding 3 was written against: a skip that does not count. Fix: hoist report_skip and the skip counter to top level beside report_write_denial.

Ilva's scratch tree was merged main, not the candidate (her finding 8, confirmed independently by the Mayor). That is a launcher defect plus a Mayor launch error, filed as fortkit-8cv6. The question it raises here: does an APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS from a session that could not execute the candidate still satisfy SO9?

For THIS bead, yes, and on evidence rather than convenience:
  - Her STATIC review WAS against the candidate. She ShellChecked the candidate file piped from 'git show bead/vhk.5.5:...', walked probe_exit_status's truth table, grepped the candidate for surviving bare 'echo "SKIP' emitters, and verified the finding-4 mutation is now caught. All of that reaches the real code through git, not through cwd.
  - She was EXPLICIT about the boundary, listing the 152-test result under 'taken on faith' and stating why the evidence was still the right kind (launcher-stamped, names the candidate worktree, timestamped after the code commit).
  - The EXECUTION half was covered by the Mayor, independently and in the actual candidate worktree: probe reports '17 pass, 0 fail, 2 skip'; --strict on the same run exits 1. Measured, not read.
Two routes, one answer — the same pattern that held on fortkit-vhk.5.1. Merging.

Where this reasoning would NOT hold: a diff whose defect is only visible at runtime, or one where no one re-ran anything. fortkit-8cv6 must land before the fort leans on a Warden verdict as the execution check again.

All four in-scope findings are delivered, and `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-10-vhk.5.1.md` is untouched (diff stat: 3 files, none of them that one). The `--strict` flag that `vhk.5.4` is sequenced to consume exists and behaves as specified.

**Gate check — no ESCALATE.** The changed paths are `templates/fort/scripts/probe-researcher-boundaries.sh`, `test/researcher-launcher.test.ts`, and a new handoff. None is this fort's own constitution: `templates/` appears in neither human gate 1 nor the cycle-7 kernel-read-only enumeration, and the handoff is an append-only record that is writable by design. I checked the blast radius rather than assuming it: `bin/fort-init:32` renders only `emit/status/mayor/forge/warden/verify` plus `lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, so this probe is **not** shipped to founded forts today. The bead's finding-3 rationale ("a template vhk.7 propagates everywhere") is forward-looking, not yet true. Until vhk.7 wires it in, a mistake here is confined to fortkit's own checkout. That does not weaken the case for `--strict`; it just means the gate is clearly not tripped now.

**Nothing here is blocking.** Default behaviour is byte-for-byte backward compatible: with `strict=0`, `probe_exit_status` reduces to the old `[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]`. I walked the truth table by inspection (fail>0 → false; fail=0/strict=0 → true; fail=0/strict=1/skip=0 → true; fail=0/strict=1/skip>0 → false) and confirmed the function is the last command in the guarded block, so it remains the script's exit status. No regression, no false record, no broken verifier, no correctness bug.

### Findings

**1. (non-blocking) The header discloses the canary residue but not the two existing files the probe opens for append — including `.git/config`.**
Bead finding 5 asked the header to announce the write footprint. It announces `.researcher-boundary-canary` residue in five directories. It does not mention that `report_write_denial` is also invoked against `$root/fort/charter.md` (line 187) and `$root/.git/config` (line 192) *themselves*, which `probe_write_denied` opens with `: >> "$1"`. This bears on **threat 1 (agent accident)** — and pointedly so, since the charter's own roster of realized incidents names "a probe that corrupted `.git/config`." Mitigating: the behaviour is unchanged from main, it is reachable only after the mask has already failed, and `>>` with no bytes written changes no content (create-if-absent plus mtime). But of the whole footprint, these two paths are the half most worth announcing, and they are the half omitted. Bead it.

**2. (non-blocking) The header misnames the `.git/hooks` residue.**
The header says a failed assertion can leave `.researcher-boundary-canary` in `.git/hooks/`. Line 193 creates `$root/.git/hooks/researcher-boundary-canary` — no leading dot. In a header whose entire job is to name what gets left behind, the dot matters: it is the difference between what a bare `ls` shows and what a future hooks-integrity watcher would key on. **Threat 1.** One-character fix; bead it.

**3. (non-blocking) The skip *wiring* is untested — only the exit predicate is.**
`probe_exit_status` was correctly hoisted above the `BASH_SOURCE` guard so tests can reach it, and the new test drives it with hand-set globals. But `report_skip` remains *inside* the main block, so nothing proves a real SKIP increments `skip`, and nothing proves the summary line prints its third field. The Forge disclosed honestly that it never ran the probe this session (the dispatch prohibited creating the `.env*` canary), so the new summary line has not been observed by anyone. This is the same shape as bead finding 4 — predicate tested, wiring not — now recurring in the code that answered it. Low risk: four lines, shellcheck-clean, and vhk.5.4 will exercise it. The fix is to hoist `report`/`report_skip` above the guard as `probe_exit_status` already was. **Threat 1.** Bead it.

**4. (non-blocking, and timely) `--strict` failure and assertion failure are indistinguishable by exit code.**
Both return 1; only the summary line discriminates. When vhk.5.4 wires this into `verify.sh`, `run_step` will emit `verify.fail` with `{"exitCode":1}` for a fort that merely *skipped* an assertion — the event stream will not be able to tell "a control failed" from "a control was never measured," which is the exact distinction this bead exists to make visible. A distinct code (the script already uses 64 and 78) would fix it. Worth resolving *before* 5.4 consumes the flag, given the Mayor's sequencing. **Threat 1.**

**5. (non-blocking) Untested predicates remain, and one of them guards the most dangerous flag in the fort.**
Bead finding 4 asked for three positive controls and got exactly three; the pairing with the existing rejection tests now pins both directions for `exact_tools`, `no_forbidden_tool` and `empty_setting_sources`, which is the right shape. Untested in *either* direction: `no_dangerous_skip`, `settings_profile_selected`, `probe_write_denied`, `ordinary_readable`, `secret_inode_masked`, `git_status_works`. The first two are pure static predicates that would take the same two-line treatment, and `no_dangerous_skip` is the assertion standing between this fort and `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. **Threat 1.** Bead it.

**6. (non-blocking, for the Mayor) Bead findings 6 and 7 have no disposition.**
The dispatch note enumerates 2/3/4/5 as in scope and carves out 1. Findings 6 and 7 appear in neither list. The Forge is not at fault — it delivered the enumerated scope exactly. But under standing order 9 this bead will close on merge, and 6 and 7 would leave no forward record. Finding 6 is the substantive one: `secret_inode_masked` still reads a bwrap *start* failure as PASS (`|| return 0`, line 99 in the candidate — I confirmed it unchanged), and it is the fort's only proof of **threat 4 (credential leakage)**. It became materially cheaper to fix as of this diff: the skip machinery just built is exactly what that path needs, so the bwrap-failed case can now become a counted SKIP instead of a silent PASS. Recommend the Mayor file 6 and 7 forward (and track 1 against the Overseer's ruling) before closing vhk.5.5.

**7. (non-blocking) Minor argument-parsing and doc nits.**
Parsing inspects only `$2`, so `probe.sh <root> --strict junk` silently ignores `junk` while `probe.sh <root> junk` correctly exits 64; a `shift` loop like `verify.sh:13-22` would match the fort's own style. The `${1:?Usage: $0 <repo-root>}` message was not updated to `[--strict]` although the `case` usage string was. Separately, `docs/specs/researcher-seat.md:219` quotes the probe as reporting "19 pass, 0 fail, exit 0"; the format is now "…, 0 skip". Not false — the counts are unchanged — but that paragraph is the Overseer-accepted residual record, so the quotation deserves an appended note when 5.4 lands. (That file is currently modified-uncommitted in the main checkout, outside this branch.)

**8. (non-blocking, infrastructure — an observed failure, per standing order 11) My scratch tree was not the candidate tree.**
`/tmp/warden-vhk.5.5` is at merged main, not `bead/vhk.5.5`: the vhk.5.5 handoff is absent and the probe there has no `--strict`. It also has no `node_modules`. My session additionally denied both materializing the candidate files into cwd and arbitrary `bash -c` execution, so I could not re-run vitest at all. The launcher's own briefing told me cwd was "a scratch copy of the candidate tree … safe for build/test re-runs"; it was neither the candidate nor runnable. This happened to me today, so it files rather than speculates. A Warden that cannot re-run the suite is reviewing at reduced capacity, and next time the diff may not be four tidy shell lines.

### Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Independently verified:** ShellCheck on the *candidate* file, piped straight from `git show bead/vhk.5.5:…` — clean, no output. The `probe_exit_status` truth table and its position as the script's final command. That every SKIP path now routes through `report_skip` (grep over the candidate: lines 110 and 191 are the only two emitters, both counted; no bare `echo "SKIP` survives). That `report_skip` is defined before its first call site in the main block. That bead finding 4's blind spot is genuinely closed: deleting `return 0` at line 62 leaves the `for` loop's status as the failing `grep` from the final `Agent` iteration, so `no_forbidden_tool` returns 1, `shell()` rejects, and the new test fails — the mutation is now caught. That `.env*` is gitignored (`.gitignore:14`) while `.researcher-boundary-canary` is not, exactly as the bead described, which is what makes the new skip counter the *only* signal for a leftover canary. That no machine consumer parses the summary line today (grep across the tree). That `bin/fort-init` does not ship this probe. That the diff touches no gate-listed path. That the handoff's second commit is append-only apart from the launcher-owned timestamp line. And the test-count arithmetic as a cross-check on the verifier claim: `forge-2026-08-10-vhk.5.1-r2.md:66` records 150 tests, this diff adds 2, the launcher-stamped block reports 152 — consistent, and monotonic.

**Taken on faith:** that vitest itself passed. I could not run it (finding 8). I did verify the evidence is the right *kind*: the block is stamped by `forge.sh`, not typed by the model; it names `RUN v4.1.10 /home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/vhk.5.5`, so it ran in the candidate worktree; and it started at 08:38:35, after the code commit at 08:38:18. That satisfies my seat's standing requirement to confirm verifiers ran against current code and not stale artifacts. I also take on faith the Forge's account of `npm ci` and the focused 9-test run, though the 152 figure corroborates it arithmetically.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — scope met, backward compatible, shellcheck clean; 8 non-blocking findings, none merge-blocking.

title: bd v2.0 --json envelope change will break the drift watcher's array parse
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-10 during the fortkit-or2.4 scratch-tracker run. 'bd list --json' prints to STDERR: 'NOTE: bd --json output format will change in v2.0. Set BD_JSON_ENVELOPE=1 to opt in early. See docs/JSON_SCHEMA.md for migration details.'

civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:412-419 does JSON.parse(stdout) and passes the result to existingFingerprints(), which expects a BARE TOP-LEVEL ARRAY. Verified today that the current shape is a top-level array and the parse is correct as written. On the v2.0 upgrade it becomes an envelope and every scheduled run throws.

This is a scheduled, unattended watcher, so the failure lands in a systemd journal nobody reads rather than in front of a human. The bead that installs it (or2.4) is the same one whose Warden findings warned the bd seams were unverified.

Fix options: (a) set BD_JSON_ENVELOPE=1 now and parse the envelope, buying determinism ahead of the break, or (b) parse defensively — accept either a bare array or an envelope — which survives the transition without a flag day. Prefer (b) for a watcher: it must not need a coordinated upgrade to keep working.

Also audit every other bare 'bd ... --json' parse in the civilization for the same assumption before v2.0 lands.

title: WebFetch executes rather than gates on loopback and RFC1918 targets (observed, fortkit-p4rc)
description:
OBSERVED, not imagined — SO11 satisfied. During the fortkit-vhk.5.2 live boundary probe (fortkit-p4rc, 2026-08-10) the Researcher was asked to attempt an outbound action against http://127.0.0.1:9/. WebFetch EXECUTED the request rather than gating on it; the result was ECONNREFUSED at the transport layer because nothing was listening on the RFC 863 discard port.

Saelin recorded this itself and framed it correctly: not a boundary failure, because WebFetch is read-only by shape (URL + prompt, no body/method/header parameter), so the worst case is a GET. But the profile allow-lists WebFetch UNCONDITIONALLY (fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json:5), so there is NO host-scoping: loopback and RFC1918 targets are reachable and do not gate.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG: combined with the already-accepted prompt-injection residual (Warden vhk.10 f4), an injected page could induce the seat to fetch internal addresses and report what it saw, and the seat's findings are recorded verbatim onto the dispatching bead by the launcher. That is an internal-network read channel through a seat we deliberately gave no shell. Each half is individually accepted and bounded; the composition of the two has not been assessed.

NOT proposing domain-scoping — that was considered and REJECTED as crippling (Overseer-approved, recorded on fortkit-vhk.5). The question here is narrower: should loopback and RFC1918 be excluded specifically, which costs the seat nothing it legitimately needs?

Relates to fortkit-ywa (network-egress restriction as defense-in-depth) and fortkit-16y (per-seat outbound-capability catalogue). Assess together rather than piecemeal; the Overseer's standing concern about over-restriction applies.

title: vhk.5.1 Warden r1 non-blocking follow-ups (Forge): probe hardening 8-14
description:
Warden findings 8-14 on fortkit-vhk.5.1 round 1, deferred out of the round-2 fix set so the blockers land clean. Full verdict on vhk.5.1.

8. No write-PERMITTED positive control. All ten write probes expect deny; the only positive controls are reads. A mask that denied every write for an unrelated reason would still show a clean sweep. probe-cycle7.sh pairs its denies with 'probe ok' lines — add a /tmp write control so the deny results are known to be meaningful. This is the exact class section D of the bead was written against.

9. secret_inode_masked reads any bwrap STARTUP failure as PASS: 'bytes=$(bwrap ...) || return 0' cannot distinguish 'read denied by SELinux' from 'bwrap never launched'. The bead sanctioned accepting a read error so this follows spec, but the two outcomes deserve different report lines.

10. Secret coverage narrower than the mask's. build_mask masks $x/.env* AND $x/*/.env* across env_roots and extra_ro; the probe checks only $root/.env* and never $root-worktrees — which is exactly where the Researcher's --env-root points.

11. profile_check hard-depends on node. The template propagates to forts that are not node projects; a missing interpreter surfaces as a FAIL on a correct profile. Add a python3/jq fallback or state the dependency in the header.

12. Nothing in the fort's gates runs this probe. verify.sh invokes neither it nor probe-cycle7.sh, so a constant-FAIL or any later regression is invisible to CI and to the merge flow. Now that there are two probes, DECIDE: do probes join verify.sh, or a watcher? This is the finding that would have caught the round-1 blockers before review. Mayor lane for the decision, Forge for the wiring.

13. settings_profile_selected binds a SPELLING, not a path — it compares against the literal '$root/fort/profiles/researcher-settings.json'. A fort whose launcher names its root variable differently fails a correct configuration. Same trap seat-sandbox.sh exists to escape.

14. 'Ships for free' is not yet true for NEW forts. bin/fort-init:32 renders an ENUMERATED list (emit status mayor forge warden verify); neither researcher.sh nor this probe is in it, and line 37's chmod +x only reaches what was rendered. fortkit-vhk.7 must be confirmed to cover fort-init for newly founded forts, not only retrofit of existing ones.
notes:
2026-08-11 (Mayor, Emrith) DECISION on finding 12, which the Warden left as Mayor lane: THE PROBES JOIN verify.sh, as a distinct final stage, not a watcher.

Rationale. A watcher reports after a merge has already happened; verify.sh IS the merge gate, and finding 12 is precisely the finding that would have caught the round-1 blockers before review. The write-footprint objection (5.5 finding 5 — the probe mutates the tree it probes, including constitution directories on a mask failure) is real but is being fixed in the same batch, so the two compose rather than conflict.

Shape of the wiring:
  - runs after ShellCheck, last, so a slow hermetic probe never delays the fast checks;
  - gated on bwrap availability, and a missing bwrap emits a LOUD skip line, never silence;
  - CI passes --strict (the flag 5.5 finding 3 creates), so a skip is a FAILURE in CI while a developer on a host without bwrap is not blocked;
  - both probes (probe-researcher-boundaries.sh and probe-cycle7.sh) wire the same way.
verify.sh is Mayor-writable and the Forge's mask keeps it read-only, so the Forge prepares the probe-side changes and the verify.sh edit itself is Mayor lane. Do not dispatch the verify.sh edit to the Forge.

DECISION on finding 14: CONFIRMED, and already owned. bin/fort-init installs nothing for the Researcher (line ~32 renders an enumerated script list, ~36 renders warden-settings.json alone, ~72 founds mayor/forge/warden). That is recorded on fortkit-vhk.7's 2026-08-11 comment, and vhk.7 explicitly owns adding all four artifacts to fort-init alongside the retrofit of existing forts. No separate bead needed; 'ships for free' is not true for new forts until vhk.7 lands.

SEQUENCING: this bead is dispatched AFTER fortkit-vhk.5.5 merges, because the verify.sh wiring consumes 5.5's --strict flag.
2026-08-11: SCOPE ADDITION from the Warden's vhk.5.5 review, finding 4 — must be resolved BEFORE this bead wires --strict into verify.sh.

--strict failure and assertion failure are indistinguishable by exit code: both return 1, and only the summary line discriminates. Once verify.sh consumes the flag, run_step emits verify.fail with {"exitCode":1} for a fort that merely SKIPPED an assertion. The event stream would then be unable to tell 'a control failed' from 'a control was never measured' — which is the exact distinction fortkit-vhk.5.5 exists to make visible, defeated at the point of consumption. Fix: a distinct exit code for the strict-skip case; the script already uses 64 and 78, so the convention exists.

Also carried here from the vhk.5.5 review: this bead's own round-one finding 9 (secret_inode_masked reads a bwrap START failure as PASS) is now ALSO tracked on fortkit-vhk.5.6, because the skip machinery vhk.5.5 built makes it materially cheaper — the bwrap-failed case becomes a counted SKIP rather than a silent PASS. Whichever bead reaches it first should close the other's copy by reference, not duplicate the work.

title: Periodic assessment: catalogue every agent/seat and its outbound-network capability (balance containment against over-restriction)
description: Overseer-requested 2026-08-10 alongside the c62 ruling. STANDING CONCERN to document and revisit: as the fort grows more seats and more agent types, keep an explicit catalogue of every agent/seat and exactly what outbound-network capability it holds (none / WebSearch+WebFetch read-only / full Bash shell / Codex API only / etc.), so the network-egress attack surface is visible at a glance and reviewed deliberately rather than accreting silently. Justin's framing: he is deliberately wary of OVER-restricting the system (research and tooling need real reach to be useful), so this is NOT a mandate to lock everything down — it is a visibility + periodic-review discipline so that each grant is a conscious choice weighed against the rogue-agent-exploitation risk class (assessment fortkit-zxc). Deliverable: a living table (seat -> tools -> network reach -> justification -> review date), refreshed when a seat is added or a profile changes; feeds the egress-control investigation (ywa) and the drift watcher's surfaces. First pass can start from the zxc code map's per-seat capability section. Revisit cadence: each new seat, and at least once per backport cycle.

title: Investigate outbound-connection logging for masked seats (detection backstop)
description: Security assessment fortkit-zxc, gap 4.3 / recommendation 4. OpenAI did not detect the ExploitGym breach by design — an Artifactory outage and Hugging Face's own team surfaced it; OpenAI learned its models were the attackers by asking a third party. We are in the same position: the planned secrets-scan watcher (fortkit-1zw) inspects file CONTENT, not outbound connections, and nothing logs or alerts when a seat opens a network connection to an unexpected host. Capability separation is the primary control, so this is the second-priority BACKSTOP for when a novel capability defeats the boundary. INVESTIGATE: lightweight outbound-connection logging for masked seats (e.g. per-seat connection audit), what it would cost, and whether it is worth it given ephemeral sessions. Scope before building (SO11). Depends conceptually on the egress-control investigation (sibling bead) — a netns egress path would be the natural logging point.

title: Investigate network-egress restriction as defense-in-depth for shell-holding seats (Forge first)
description: Security assessment fortkit-zxc, gap 4.1 / recommendation 3. The kernel mask (seat-sandbox.sh) governs the filesystem ONLY — no netns, no egress allow/deny, no outbound filtering. The Mayor and Forge both have uncontrolled outbound shell network; this is the exact boundary that failed in the OpenAI ExploitGym incident (a zero-day bought internet egress out of a file-only sandbox). Capability separation stays the PRIMARY control (the Researcher's no-Bash design; an egress deny-list binds spellings, the same weakness as the .env globs), so this is explicitly defense-in-depth, not the main fix. INVESTIGATE: whether a network namespace (bwrap --unshare-net with a controlled egress path) or an egress-deny is feasible for the Forge (Codex workspace-write, holds Bash) without breaking npm ci / codex API calls / git remote. Scope the mechanism and prove it reduces a real threat before building (SO11). lr8h + the OpenAI incident are the observed-failure justification. Do NOT assume the answer is 'add iptables'; the fort's history favors inode/capability boundaries over deny-lists.

title: Researcher fan-out: same-profile read-only sub-searchers, depth capped at 1
description: Implements the Overseer's fan-out ruling: the Researcher may parallelize breadth by spawning sub-searchers, but every child re-enters the SAME researcher launcher/profile (fortkit-vhk.3/.2) — no Bash, no bypassPermissions, and crucially no ability to spawn further (depth capped at 1, enforced not merely documented). This is the reconciliation of Justin's 'spawn sub agents to parallelize' with lr8h: fan-out is preserved, but children are as weak as the parent and the invisible depth-2/3 fleet is structurally impossible. Mechanism decision (part of vhk.1/vhk.3): whether children are launched by researcher.sh re-invocation or a bounded same-profile Agent grant — chosen so the harness cannot let a child inherit the parent mode (the lr8h root cause). The depth cap is a boundary-proof assertion (fortkit-vhk.5 item 3). Blocked by vhk.3.

**1. Spec §8 item 3 says "the lint greps for them" and §10 item 6 says migration leaves *zero* live references; a green lint now asserts that while three exist. I do not hold this against the merge — the Forge cannot write charter or seats under its kernel lock, and widening the rule today would red the build, so the honest fix is Mayor work under the prose gate (adjacent to `fortkit-qj3`). But the rule as shipped does not yet keep done what 88u.10 did. `templates/fort/**` references are correct and should stay excluded: generated forts get their own `remember.md`.

**2. (non-blocking) The negative test does not isolate the rule it claims to prove.** `test/memory.test.ts` second fixture: `invalid.md` is written with `key: replacement` under filename `invalid.md`, so *key-must-equal-filename* fires; `retired.md` sets `superseded-by: replacement` with no `replacement.md` on disk, so *superseded-by does not resolve* fires. The assertion is only `rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 1 })`, so it passes identically if the retired-reference rule is deleted. The rule does work (`retiredReferences` becomes `["fort/remember.md","retired"]`; `AGENTS.md` contains "retired"), but the handoff's "negative fixtures prove both schema and retired-reference lint failures are red" is not supported by the test as written. Fix: assert on stderr text, or clean the fixture so the retired reference is the only failure. The *schema* half (first fixture, `key: incorrect` vs `invalid.md`) is correctly isolated and does satisfy r1 f9 / spec §10 item 1.

**3. (non-blocking, closest I came to blocking) A negative guard was replaced rather than kept.** main's pin test asserted `expect(current).not.toContain("read-only set omits fort/charter.md")` — the guard against the 2026-08-07 bns caveat that cycle 7 made *false* (`4dc2038:fort/remember.md`, "(b) The earlier caveat that forge.sh's read-only set omits charter/seats/profiles was made false by cycle 7"). The new test drops it and substitutes `not.toContain("Forge runs with a kernel mask")` — a supersession check on a sentence that is still true. The dispatch asked for "the absence of the retracted caveat"; what was removed is the guard on the retracted falsehood. Net: one guard against a specific false constitutional claim lost, on the surface injected into every session. Restoring it is one line and costs nothing. I judged this a coverage regression rather than a correctness bug, and the supersession genuinely must ride this branch, so it does not block — but it should be the first line of the follow-up bead, and Justin may reasonably overrule me on that.

**4. (non-blocking) The §6.1 disclosure line is a markdown lazy continuation.** `scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs:395-399` pushes the bullets and then the disclosure with no blank line between, so `current.md:47-48` renders as one bullet: "…fort-init ships other forts' citizens as default seat personalities — [fortkit-fd2](bead:fortkit-fd2) 35 of 113 open beads shown; full list via bd ready". The literal string the ruling mandated is present in the raw text, which is what a masked seat reads, so the requirement is met; a human in a markdown viewer sees the disclosure swallowed by the last bead. Push `""` before it.

**5. (non-blocking) "Top 15 ready" is implemented as top 15 *open by status*.** The filter is `bead.status === "open"` (line 211-214), but the export carries `dependencies`/`dependency_count`, so readiness is computable: `fortkit-fd2` is shown while blocked by the still-open `fortkit-8ib`, and `bd ready` would not list it — under a line that says "full list via `bd ready`". Second-order: `slice(0, 15)` is taken *before* the Map dedupes against the gate group, so only 12 additional ready beads actually surface (verified: 4 in-progress + 19 gate + 12 = 35). Neither is a merge risk; both make the section slightly less than what §6.1 promises.

**6. (non-blocking) Incident dedupe key omits `ts` and `file`.** `duplicateKey` is `category\0target\0detail` (line 276). Against today's corpus it is exactly right — all 9 collapsed lines are same-file, same-ts, byte-identical re-emissions, and no distinct incident was lost. But two genuinely separate incidents sharing category+target+detail on different days collapse to one, keeping the earliest, and the log renders no timestamp to reveal it — an under-report in the view the fort reads for its own scars. Adding `event.ts` to the key still collapses every duplicate present today and cannot drop a distinct one; that is the strictly-better key. The handoff is honest here, naming the three key fields explicitly.

**7. (non-blocking) systemd proposal.** `[Unit] Description`, the PATH pin and the regenerate-**and**-commit step all landed, and the `git add` is path-scoped per standing order 4. Two residuals: the PATH pins `/home/justin/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin`, which breaks silently on any nvm Node bump (`package.json` allows `>=24 <25`), where the in-tree precedent `civ/systemd/herald.service` pins the version-stable `~/.local/bin` — the handoff discloses this risk, which is the right disposition for a proposal-only file; and `consolidate-memory.timer.proposal` still has no `[Unit] Description`. Worth noting for whoever installs: the nightly commit lands on whatever branch is checked out at 03:00. No `%` specifiers in the new `ExecStart`, so no `%%`-escaping trap.

**8. (non-blocking) `text.includes(reference)` on bare fact keys.** Safe for today's hyphenated keys; a future short or common key would red the build on an unrelated word. The fixture's own "Read retired before work." is an accidental demonstration of the substring match. Word-boundary matching would cost nothing.

**9. (non-blocking) `compareBeads` priority coercion.** `Number(null)` is `0`, which is finite, so a bead with an explicit `priority: null` sorts as *highest* priority rather than falling to the `4` default. `undefined` yields `NaN` and defaults correctly. Also `^gate-[1-3]$` silently ignores a hypothetical fourth gate — correct today (the charter has exactly three), worth a comment.

**10. (non-blocking) The new core fact renders as "PROSE- gated".** `fort/memory/facts/cycle7-write-boundaries.md` hard-wraps mid-word after the hyphen, and the collator joins fact lines with a space (`item.body.replaceAll("\n", " ")`), so `current.md:11` reads "…`fort/seats/` PROSE- gated…". This is core tier — injected into every session, including bare ones. The new pin test asserts the literal `"PROSE- gated"`, so a follow-up must fix the wrap and the assertion in the same commit or the test goes red. One-character fix; I flag it because the fort's most-read artifact should not ship with a seam in it.

**Two things that look alarming and are not.** `git diff main..bead/88u.9` shows `docs/specs/backport-loop.md` deleted (-186); that is a stale-base artifact — main gained `bf136a4` after the branch point, the three-dot diff is clean, and nothing on this branch touches `docs/`. And `current.md`'s "Latest handoffs" still names `forge-2026-08-10-88u.7-r2.md` rather than this bead's handoff, because the handoff was committed (49bb1e5) after the regeneration (b7431cc); inherent to the ordering, corrected by the nightly cadence.

**Escalation analysis (recorded because the rule exists for exactly this call).** This diff changes no gate-listed file: not `fort/charter.md`, not `fort/seats/`, not `fort/profiles/`, not `.claude/`, not `fort/scripts/`, not `bin/` or `civ/`. It does add a core fact that *restates* the constitution, which is the strongest argument for mandatory ESCALATE — a wrong one would mislead every seat about the write boundaries. I checked it word for word against the charter's "Prose gates" paragraph (line 35) and against the dispatch: it is verbatim the Overseer's own text from the 22:47 bead comment, and it matches the charter on every clause — attended-seat prose gate with recorded prior approval and `charter.amended`, the kernel-RO enumeration including the Mayor-writable `verify.sh` carve-out, and the Forge's retained full lock. Spec §4.3 rule 5 states that Forge ledger writes ride the bead branch through Warden review like any change. Escalating text the Overseer wrote himself, to the Overseer, would be ceremony. If Justin reads human gate 1's literal "`fort/` files" as covering `fort/memory/facts/`, that is his call to make and `fortkit-qj3` is where it belongs. No security finding here bears on threats 1–4; the memory-write threat surface (poisoning) is unchanged or improved by this diff.

**Verified independently.** `npm ci` then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in the scratch copy `/tmp/warden-88u.9`: **exit 0**, all six steps — memory-lint (step 1, so `node scripts/memory-lint.mjs` is green against this tree), tsc, browser tsc, Biome (54 files), Vitest **12 files / 137 tests passed**, ShellCheck. Exactly matches the handoff's claim; the three `fatal: not a git repository` lines are the scratch tree having no `.git` and are benign — tests pass through them. I hand-simulated the §6.1 cap against the branch's real `.beads/issues.jsonl` (113 open: 4 in-progress, 21 gate-labeled, priorities 1–3) and reproduced the committed `current.md:13-48` **exactly** — same 35 beads, same order, same three groups, same "35 of 113" — which independently confirms both the cap logic and its determinism. I confirmed the 9 collapsed incident lines are all exact same-file duplicates, that no `.tmp` file is tracked (so the `*.tmp` glob strands nothing), that `AGENTS.md:153`/`CLAUDE.md:89` are genuinely clean, that the superseded fact drops out of the core view via the `status === "active"` filter, and that the model attribution and `verify_exit: 0` in the handoff match the event stream.

**Taken on faith.** I could not run `node scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs` directly — this session's tool permissions denied every direct `node <script>` and every file-copy invocation (`fortkit-hn2` again; `verify.sh` itself was permitted, which is how I got a full green). So I did not regenerate `current.md` byte-for-byte myself; I relied on the suite's own byte-identity test, which passed, plus the hand-simulation above. I did not install or run the systemd units — proposal-only files, Overseer's lane. I did not re-derive the priority/label data in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, only read the export.

Recommend merge, and one follow-up bead carrying findings 1–10 with finding 3 (restore the retracted-caveat assertion) and finding 1 (widen the dangling-reference surface — Mayor work under the prose gate) at the top. Bead stays open per dispatch.
