comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
I've read the charter, seat file, spec, the full diff, and reproduced the verifiers. Here is my review.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES

Round 1. Work by **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge ladder rung 1, per the handoff) — the GPT-5.6 family carries the reward-hacking flag noted in `fort/seats/warden.md`, so I checked every claim in the handoff against my own run rather than reading it. **Every verifier claim in the handoff is true**, which I want on the record before the blockers: this is careful work, the failed-attempts section is honest, and the "rebuilds before every invocation" risk is self-disclosed rather than hidden. The two blockers below are both narrow and both cheap.

Branch `bead/88u.7` = 2 commits atop current `main` (36fb708). Touched: `src/recall.ts` (new), `src/cli.ts`, `scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs`, `test/recall.test.ts` (new), `docs/specs/memory.md`, one handoff. No launcher, no `verify.sh`, no `civ/`, no `package.json` — every dispatch exclusion honoured, no new dependencies.

## Blocking findings

**1. BLOCKING — `--seat` silently drops every fact scoped `seats: [all]`, including core-tier facts.**
`scopeMatches` (`src/recall.ts`) is exact tag membership: `tags(value).includes(expected.toLowerCase())`. The spec defines `[all]` as the seats wildcard — `docs/specs/memory.md:84`, `seats: [mayor, warden]  # or [all]` — and there is no `all` handling anywhere in `src/` or `scripts/` (I grepped both; zero hits). Concretely, 3 of the fort's 9 facts are `seats: [all]`, and one of them is `authoritative-verifier.md`, **tier: core**. So `fortkit recall verifier --seat forge` returns no fact-ledger hit for the fort's own authoritative-verifier fact.

This is the failure the bead exists to abolish, reproduced inside the blessed tool: a confident, structured, provenance-bearing answer that is wrong by omission. It is worse than the grep it replaces, because grep never claimed completeness and this output carries a `gaps` array that implies everything not listed as a gap was covered. Fix is one line — treat `all` as matching any `--seat` — or, if the Mayor rules `--seat` is meant to be exact-tag-only, say so in §6.2 and disclose the exclusion. Either way it must not be silent.

**2. BLOCKING — any `--since`/`--until` window silently excludes every row with no parsed timestamp, which is the entire annals surface.**
In the filter, `const timestamp = row.ts === "" ? Number.NaN : Date.parse(row.ts)`, and both window predicates require `!Number.isNaN(timestamp)`. `consolidate-memory.mjs` writes `ts: ""` for all annals rows and for `interactions.jsonl`. So `fortkit recall ruling --since 2026-08-01` returns zero annal hits and reports nothing about it — and the annals are where the rulings-of-record live (spec §6.1 names them explicitly).

Excluding undated rows from a date window is a defensible semantic; excluding them *without disclosure* is not, against this bead's own stated design principle ("unreadable file = reported gap, never a silent skip — the wtm lesson as a design principle") and the very miss the description opens with ("the Regent brief's grep drops the newest corrections"). The cheap fix is one synthetic gap entry when a window is active and undated rows were dropped: `{ source: "<undated rows>", reason: "N indexed rows have no parsed timestamp and were excluded by --since/--until" }`. No redesign needed.

## Non-blocking findings (file as beads; not held against the merge)

**3.** The `recall` CLI branch has no test. `test/cli.test.ts` establishes the house convention of spawning the CLI and asserting each new branch's exit-code contract — its third test is literally named "ambient follows the neighbouring CLI branches' exit-code contract" — and `recall`'s arg parser (duplicate-flag rejection, missing-value rejection, `--`-prefixed query rejection, the `index += 1` skip, JSON output shape) is entirely unexercised. `test/recall.test.ts` calls `recall()` directly.

**4.** Exit-code inconsistency with those siblings: a malformed timestamp reaches `instant()` inside `recall()`, throws, and is caught by the generic handler as **exit 1**. `digest --since invalid` exits 2 for the same class of error (asserted at `test/cli.test.ts:50`). Validate the window in the CLI branch alongside the other flag checks.

**5.** `recall` is a read command that writes a *tracked* file. The rebuild shells `consolidate-memory.mjs`, which rewrites `fort/memory/current.md` (tracked — it is in `git ls-files`) as well as the gitignored `index.db`. Regeneration is deterministic so an unchanged corpus produces no diff, and §6.1's cadence anticipates frequent regeneration — but a query command dirtying the working tree whenever the corpus has moved since the last commit is surprising, and it means the blessed retrieval path cannot be run from a read-only checkout or by a seat that is read-only by construction (this one). Consider a `--no-rebuild` escape or writing `current.md` only when the job is invoked as the consolidation job.

**6.** Concurrency race, now much more reachable. `consolidate-memory.mjs` uses fixed `${index}.tmp` and `${current}.tmp` paths with `rm -f`-then-create. Pre-88u.7 that ran once per session; now it runs once per query, and the bead explicitly anticipates `bin/regent`'s briefing assembly shelling recall. Two concurrent recalls will collide on those temp paths. This is charter threat 1 (agent accident), the highest-volume class. A pid- or `mkdtemp`-suffixed temp path closes it.

**7.** `origin` is not carried on the hit shape. Spec §4.2 item 4 makes `origin: untrusted` an eligibility/ranking signal (standing order 8 applied to memory), but `RecallHit` exposes source/date/actor/seat/section/provenance/snippet only — a consumer shelling recall cannot tell a trusted fact from one derived from fetched web content. This bears on **threat 2 (prompt injection via untrusted content)**. It is not blocking today because all 9 facts are `origin: trusted` (verified), and §6.2's contract does not list `origin`; per standing order 11 I am recording it rather than blocking. It should be closed before the first untrusted fact is admitted.

**8.** Match haystack for events is `section` + `snippet` only — i.e. `category` and `detail`. `actor`, `seat`, and `target` are indexed but unsearchable, so `fortkit recall fortkit-88u.5` misses every event targeting that bead unless the detail text happens to name it, and `fortkit recall kethra` finds no events by her. `--bead`/`--seat` cover the intent, but the plain-query behaviour will surprise.

**9.** `--topic` means different things per surface: scope topic tags for facts, `event.category` (e.g. `work.begun`) for events, and nothing at all for annals/handoffs/beads. Similarly `--bead` maps to `event.target`, which the schema (`schema/events.md:13`) says may be "bead ID, commit hash, seat, or path" — non-bead targets land in `scope_beads`. Worth a sentence in §6.2.

**10.** Smaller items, grouped: `await access(dirname(consolidate))` preflights the *directory*, not the script, so a missing script still fails later with a worse message; `execFile`'s default 1 MiB `maxBuffer` versus one stderr warning per gap makes recall fail hardest on the most damaged corpus; `fort/annals/briefs/*.txt` are not indexed and not disclosed as a gap (pre-existing, adjacent to 88u.9); scoring is OR-over-words with substring matching and no result cap, so a common word dumps the corpus as JSON.

**11.** Observation, not a defect: the gap test relies on `chmod 0o000` denying the test runner. As root it would *fail*, not false-pass, so it cannot go green dishonestly — the right failure direction. And per the dispatch's invitation, `test/recall.test.ts` does assert index rows exist end-to-end through the real `consolidate-memory.mjs` build path; that is welcome 88u.9-adjacent coverage.

## What I verified independently vs. took on faith

Verified myself, in `/tmp/warden-88u.7` (fresh `npm ci`; `node_modules` was absent, matching the handoff's note):
- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0**, 12 test files, **133 tests passed**. Ran it twice, once with an explicit success echo. This matches the handoff's claim exactly — no repeat of the 88u.5 r1 false-green.
- `memory-lint` is verify step one and passed silently within that run.
- `npx vitest run test/recall.test.ts` → 3 passed (all three acceptance surfaces: per-corpus hits, the local/UTC seam at `-08:00` → `07:24Z`, the unreadable-fixture gap).
- Branch topology (2 commits on current `main`), the full file list against the dispatch exclusions, absence of `package.json` changes.
- The scope/tier/origin frontmatter of all 9 real facts, and the total absence of `[all]` handling in `src/` and `scripts/` — finding 1 is grepped, not inferred.

Taken on faith or reasoned from source rather than observed:
- **The `recall` CLI branch was never executed by me.** The sandbox denied every direct `node src/cli.ts recall ...` invocation, so arg parsing, JSON output and exit codes in finding 3/4 are read from source, not run. The library path underneath them is fully exercised by the tests I did run. I flag this because it is exactly the surface with no test of its own.
- That the "Launcher-observed verifier result" block was emitted by `forge.sh` as stated, and the `gpt-5.6-terra` attribution.
- No `fort/charter.md` or `fort/seats/` change is in this diff, so no gate-6 mandatory escalation applies; the handoff under `fort/handoffs/` is an ordinary seat record, not a constitutional edit.

Findings 1 and 2 are both single-figure line changes in `src/recall.ts`. I expect round 2 to be short.

VERDICT-LINE: REQUEST-CHANGES r1: --seat drops [all]-scoped core facts; date windows silently drop undated rows (annals). Verifier green (133 tests).

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Both round-one blockers are fixed and verified. Here is my round-two record.

--------

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round 2. Work by **gpt-5.6-terra** (per the r2 handoff) — the GPT-5.6 family carries the reward-hacking flag in `fort/seats/warden.md`, so as in round one I checked every handoff claim against my own run rather than reading it. **Every verifier claim in the r2 handoff is true**, including the test count (12 files, 135 tests — up exactly 2 from round one's 133, matching the two new tests). The failed-attempts section is again honest (Biome line-wrapping failure on the first full run, disclosed rather than buried).

Round-two diff (`28a054a..bead/88u.7`) touches three files: `src/recall.ts`, `test/recall.test.ts`, and the r2 handoff. No launcher, no `verify.sh`, no `civ/`, no `package.json`, no dependencies. The Mayor's "fix the two blockers only, do not expand into 88u.12/88u.13" instruction was honoured literally — nothing else moved.

## Both round-one blockers: fixed

**r1 f1 — `--seat` dropped `seats: [all]` facts.** `scopeMatches` now takes a `wildcard` parameter, passed `true` only for the seats axis (`src/recall.ts:117`), and `[all]` matches any `--seat`. This is the Mayor's ruling implemented exactly, and the wildcard is correctly *not* extended to `--topic`/`--bead`. The new test (`test/recall.test.ts:133`) writes a `tier: core`, `seats: [all]` fact and asserts a `--seat forge` query returns it — it genuinely fails without the fix, since the pre-fix path compares `"all"` against `"forge"`. I re-confirmed the premise against the real corpus: `authoritative-verifier.md` is `seats: [all]`, `tier: core`, one of three `[all]`-scoped facts of nine.

**r1 f2 — date windows silently dropped undated rows.** Scope/query filtering is now split from window filtering, `undated` is computed from the query-and-scope-matching candidates, and an active window with dropped rows appends the disclosure gap (`src/recall.ts:149-154`). The test (`test/recall.test.ts:170`) asserts an annals query under `--since` returns no hits *and* discloses the drop. The exclusion semantic is unchanged, as directed. The gap's wording is accurate: the counted rows are indexed, are undated, and were excluded by the window.

**No regressions.** The refactor from one filter pass into two is behaviour-preserving for `hits`; the sort, the hit shape, and the NaN handling are byte-for-byte the same logic. The wildcard cannot leak into the other two axes (default `false`).

## Non-blocking findings (file as beads; not held against the merge)

**1. An unvalidated event timestamp crashes the entire query, not just its row.** `consolidate-memory.mjs:245` stores `ts: event.ts ?? ""` with no validation, and `src/recall.ts:142` does `new Date(row.ts).toISOString()` for any non-empty `ts`. A single JSONL line with a non-empty unparseable `ts` therefore throws `RangeError: Invalid time value` out of `recall()`, and the CLI's generic handler exits 1 having printed **nothing** — no hits, no gaps, no disclosure of which line did it. One malformed event line takes down the whole blessed retrieval path. This is charter **threat 1 (agent accident)**, the highest-volume class, and it is the same failure mode the bead exists to abolish, one level up: total silent loss instead of partial. I own that I missed this in round one — it is unchanged code, not a regression, so under round discipline it is a bead, not a block. The fix is small: treat an unparseable non-empty `ts` as undated and disclose it as a gap, exactly as the r2 fix does for empty ones.

**2. Merge hazard in the review command itself, for the Mayor.** The branch's merge base is `fcc55ae`; `main` has since advanced to `36fb708` (88u.10 partial). So `git diff main..bead/88u.7` — the command the dispatch names — *displays* 88u.10 inverted: commit-qualified `4dc2038:` provenance pointers stripped from seven facts, the `codex-launch-recipe` `trust_level` clause (restored per Warden 88u.5 r2 f5) deleted, and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md re-pointed at `fort/remember.md`. **The branch does not do this** — its own commits (`fcc55ae..bead/88u.7`) touch only seven files and none of those. But a merge performed by squashing that displayed diff, or by resetting `main` to the branch tip, would silently revert 88u.10. Merge with a real merge or rebase. The two file sets are disjoint (I compared them), so it is textually clean.

**3. Spec §6.2 does not document the two behaviours this round added.** The section documents flags, output shape, and `--since` inclusive / `--until` exclusive, but says nothing about the `[all]` seat wildcard or that undated rows are excluded from windows and disclosed. Related and worth the same sentence: annals, beads and interactions rows all carry an empty `scope_seats`, so **any** `--seat` filter excludes those three surfaces wholesale. That is defensible filter semantics, but it is undisclosed, and it is the neighbouring shape of the bug just fixed.

**4. The synthetic gap's `source` is the empty string.** My round-one suggestion was a labelled sentinel (`<undated rows>`); the dispatch's restatement rendered it as `''`, and the Forge implemented the dispatch as written — correctly, I think, given it was a Mayor ruling. The consequence is that a consumer rendering gaps as "could not read `<source>`" prints a blank path. Also cosmetic: "1 indexed rows" does not pluralize, and the count is over query-matching rows only (true as stated, easy to misread as corpus-wide). And the synthetic gap is appended after the db-sorted gaps, so `gaps` is no longer globally sorted — deterministic, but no longer ordered.

**5. Round-one findings 3–10 remain open and remain accurate**, now carried by fortkit-88u.12 / 88u.13: the recall CLI branch has no test of its own, the malformed-window exit code is 1 where `digest` uses 2, a read command rewrites tracked `current.md`, the fixed `.tmp` paths race once recall runs per-query, `origin` is absent from the hit shape (threat 2), event `actor`/`seat`/`target` are indexed but unsearchable, `--topic` means three different things per surface, and there is no result cap. Nothing in this round made any of them worse.

## What I verified independently vs. took on faith

Verified myself, in `/tmp/warden-88u.7` (fresh `npm ci`; `node_modules` was absent again):

• `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0**, confirmed by a success-marker chain, not by reading output: 12 test files, **135 tests passed**. Ran it three times. Matches the handoff exactly.
• `memory-lint` is verify step one (`fort/scripts/verify.sh:59`) and passed inside that green run.
• `npx vitest run test/recall.test.ts` → **5 passed** (3 from round one, 2 new).
• Read both new tests in full and confirmed each is a genuine regression test that fails without its fix.
• The real corpus's nine facts and their seat scopes — finding f1's premise re-checked, not assumed from round one.
• `36fb708`'s file list against the branch's own file list: disjoint, hence finding 2's "clean merge" claim.
• That the r2 diff touches only three files, honouring every dispatch exclusion.

Taken on faith or reasoned from source rather than observed:

• **The recall CLI branch was again never executed by me.** The sandbox denied `node src/cli.ts recall ...` and `node -e` alike, so exit codes and JSON output are read from source. The library beneath them is exercised by the tests I did run. This is the same surface as carried finding 5's "no CLI test" — the one place where neither the Forge's tests nor my run reaches.
• `node scripts/memory-lint.mjs` standalone: the sandbox denied the direct invocation; its exit 0 is inferred from verify.sh's step one passing, which is sound but is not the standalone run the dispatch named.
• The `gpt-5.6-terra` attribution and that the "Launcher-observed verifier result" block was emitted by forge.sh.
• Gate check: no `fort/charter.md` and no `fort/seats/` change is in this diff, so no gate-6 mandatory escalation applies. The two handoffs are ordinary seat records.

Two blockers raised, two blockers closed, verifier green, test count up by exactly the two tests added. Merge it — with finding 2's caution about how.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS r2: both r1 blockers fixed and verified, no regressions, verify.sh exit 0 (135 tests). Merge properly — branch is 1 behind main.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Verification complete. Here is my review record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Bead:** fortkit-88u.4 — filename-contract test covering the latent `civ/handoffs` miss.
**Range reviewed:** `main..bead/88u.4` — `87ae204` (parser widening + tests) and `579f345` (handoff attribution + launcher-observed verify).
**Model that produced the work:** `gpt-5.6-terra` per the launcher's stamp (the model self-reported "GPT-5 (Codex)"; see finding 2). Forge ladder rung 1. Given the reward-hacking flag the seat file carries on the GPT-5.6 family, I specifically probed whether the new contract test could pass vacuously. It cannot: `readdir` rejection fails the test, the directory list is complete for this repo, and the assertion compares a real unmatched list against `[]`. The soft spots I did find are findings 4 and 5, neither of which makes the test self-satisfying.

**Charter gate check:** no gate-1 constitution file is modified by either commit (see finding 1 — the apparent `.claude/settings.json` change is a diff artifact, not a branch change). No `.env*`/secret surface. Nothing public-facing. No mandatory escalation is triggered.

**Spec conformance:** all three acceptance criteria are met. The contract test globs both real handoff directories plus the fixture, zero unmatched; the civ shape is pinned by a unit test; `fortkit-wtm` and `fortkit-tzq` are referenced in the handoff's Coordination section and neither bead's scope is duplicated — I read wtm's record and confirmed its windowing, gap-marker, and telemetry-unit items are untouched here. The Mayor's dispatch instruction to widen rather than rename civilization records was followed.

**Correctness of the widening.** The new pattern's second alternative, `(?:-[a-z0-9._-]+)?`, is byte-identical to the entire old optional-suffix group, so the new pattern is a strict superset of the old: no filename that parsed before can now fail to parse or parse differently. The first alternative `T\d{6}(?:-[a-z0-9._-]+)?` is appropriately tight — `regent-2026-08-08T2318571.md` (seven digits) still fails to match, so the widening does not degenerate into "accept anything". The greedy seat class backtracks correctly on the real filenames (`forge-2026-08-10-88u.4.md` → seat `forge`, date `2026-08-10`), and there is no nested quantifier, so no catastrophic-backtracking exposure. Extracting only the date and leaving the T-stamp on the floor is consistent with `readLatestHandoffs`, which orders on the heading timestamp first; for the two same-day `regent-2026-08-05T*` files the fallback filename tiebreak happens to sort chronologically because the stamps are fixed-width and zero-padded.

---

### Findings

**1. Non-blocking — `.claude/settings.json` in the two-dot diff is a stale-base artifact, not a change by this branch.** `git diff main..bead/88u.4` shows four lines removed from `.claude/settings.json`, deleting the SessionStart core-memory hook. That is alarming on its face: `.claude/` is kernel read-only and a gate-1 area. It is not a real change. `git show --stat` on both commits confirms neither touches the file; the branch is exactly one commit behind main, and that commit is `060ae50` (fortkit-88u.6, Overseer's hand), which added the hook. I am not escalating, because no commit in the range modifies a gated file. **What this requires at merge:** a real merge or a rebase onto `060ae50`. Do not resolve by taking the branch tree wholesale — that would silently revert an Overseer's-hand change to a gate-1 file. Re-run `fort/scripts/verify.sh` on the merge result, since no verifier run to date has exercised main and this branch combined.

**2. Non-blocking — the launcher's attribution stamp edits a committed record in place.** `579f345` rewrites the handoff's first two lines from `2026-08-10T13:31:30-08:00` / `Model: GPT-5 (Codex)` to `2026-08-10T13:32:02-08:00` / `Model: gpt-5.6-terra`, rather than appending a correction. The handoff was already committed in `87ae204`, so this is an in-place edit of a record, which brushes the letter of standing order 7 ("corrections are appended, not edited in"). I am not blocking: the change makes attribution *more* accurate, git history preserves both values so nothing is falsified or pruned, and this is `forge.sh`'s close-path behaviour rather than a discretionary act by the Forge. But the append-style alternative (a `## Correction` line) costs nothing and would keep the launcher inside the order it is meant to enforce. Worth a bead against `forge.sh`'s close path.

**3. Non-blocking — the class fix protects fortkit only; wtm's live miss was in another fort.** The bead's premise is that "this single test would have caught both wtm's live miss and this latent one". Within this repo, yes. But wtm's observed failure was Farlantern's handoffs going invisible to `fortkit digest`, which reads *other* forts' handoff directories over the registry, and `templates/` ships no tests at all — a settlement founded by `fort-init` gets no contract test. So the commit-time detection this bead buys covers the capital and not the settlements where the live loss happened. The right follow-on is either shipping the contract check through `fort-init`, or having `digest` report unparseable handoff filenames per registered fort as a disclosed gap (which is already the memory spec's §5 discipline: "unreadable or unparseable sources are recorded as disclosed gaps, never skipped silently"). File as a bead and coordinate with wtm; it is squarely wtm's cross-fort consumer territory.

**4. Non-blocking — the widened pattern has no negative pinning test.** The Mayor's dispatch asked to "pin the widened pattern with unit tests"; one positive example (`regent-2026-08-08T231857.md`) landed and no negative case did, and there is no pre-existing negative test for this regex anywhere in the suite. A pin with only a positive case does not fix the lower bound — a future "just widen it to `.*`" would keep both new tests green while re-opening exactly the class this bead closes. This is the closest thing to an acceptance-criteria shortfall, and it is why I looked hard at whether it should block; it does not, because merging still leaves the fort strictly better off than not merging. Bead: add negative assertions (e.g. `regent-2026-08-08T2318.md`, `README.md`, a seven-digit stamp) returning `null`.

**5. Non-blocking — the contract test's `.md` filter and hardcoded directory list are both slightly looser than the contract they name.** The test asserts "every `.md` file parses", not "every file in a handoff directory is a parseable handoff". A handoff saved as `.markdown` or `.txt` is skipped silently rather than flagged — which is the wtm failure mode wearing a different hat. An explicit ignore-list (`.gitkeep`) would be the tighter contract. Separately, the three-directory list is complete today — I confirmed by `find` that `fort/handoffs`, `civ/handoffs`, and `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/fort/handoffs` are the only handoff directories in the repo — but a fourth directory added later escapes the contract silently. Discovering directories named `handoffs` under the repo root would make the test self-maintaining. Bead both.

**6. Non-blocking — same-day ordering for the civ shape is now reachable and is still `readLastHandoff`'s weak spot.** `readLastHandoff` sorts candidates on the filename date alone and takes the first, so among the two `regent-2026-08-05T*` files the winner is `readdir` order. `readLatestHandoffs` is fine (heading timestamp, then a lexicographic filename tiebreak that is chronologically correct for fixed-width T-stamps). This is pre-existing and squarely `fortkit-tzq`'s scope, but widening the pattern is what makes it reachable for civ records, so it should be noted on tzq rather than left implicit.

**Threat-model bearing:** none of the above is a security finding. The change touches no credential surface, no untrusted-input path, and no dependency. The one item with any adjacency to a gate is finding 1, and it bears on threat 1 (agent accident) — a careless merge reverting an Overseer's-hand change to a kernel-RO file — which is why I stated the merge procedure explicitly rather than filing it and moving on.

---

### Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Verified independently, in the scratch copy at `/tmp/warden-88u.4`:**
- `npm ci` then `npm test`: **10 test files, 127 tests, all passing** — matches the count claimed in the handoff exactly.
- Both new tests exist and pass by name: `parses the civilization handoff T-stamp filename form` and `accepts every checked-in handoff filename`.
- Neither commit in the range touches `.claude/settings.json` (`git show --stat` on both); the branch is one commit behind main; that commit is `060ae50`, which added the hook the diff appears to delete.
- Exactly three handoff directories exist in the repo, and the test's list names all three.
- All eight `civ/handoffs` filenames are the `seat-YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMSS.md` shape.
- `templates/` contains no tests (config, charter, events, profiles, scripts, seats only) — the basis for finding 3.
- wtm's bead record read in full from `.beads/issues.jsonl`; no scope duplication.
- Regex superset property, backtracking behaviour, and TypeScript narrowing in `parseHandoffFilename` checked by inspection.

**Taken on faith:**
- The other four verifier steps — `typecheck`, `typecheck:browser`, Biome `lint`, and `shellcheck`. My sandbox permitted only `npm ci` and `npm test`; every other invocation (`verify.sh`, `npm run typecheck`, the `node_modules/.bin` binaries directly) was denied. The evidence I have is the launcher-observed block in the handoff recording `verify.sh --no-emit` exit 0 at `2026-08-10T13:32:07-08:00`, which matches `579f345`'s commit timestamp; the diff touches no shell scripts, so shellcheck's surface is unchanged; and the new function's typing is straightforward `string | undefined` narrowing. I did not reproduce those four steps and am not claiming to have.
- That the *old* pattern fails on the civ filenames is my analysis, not an execution — I could not run a standalone Node process. The reasoning is that after `-(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})` the remainder `T231857.md` must satisfy `(?:-[a-z0-9._-]+)?\.md$`, which requires either a literal `.` or a leading `-`, and there is no second 4-2-2 hyphenated digit run to relocate the date group to. High confidence, but stated as analysis.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — parser widening is a strict superset, contract test real and passing (127/127); 6 non-blocking beads; rebase before merge.

title: Implement the config-checksums watcher: integrity baseline over the seat-immutable config surface
description: charter.md:64 lists config checksums among the Watchers (cron + script, no model, added as earned); none of the four are implemented. This builds the config-checksums watcher: a host-side cron+script that pins a baseline over the seat-immutable config surface and alerts on drift. Earned by an observed failure of the class: retired ruflo wrote into every fort .claude/ after removal (fortkit-agf, civ/remember.md:18), which no control detected at the time. Scope the baseline to the kernel-RO config set: ~/.claude/settings.json, settings.local.json, CLAUDE.md, helpers/, plus the five paths from fortkit-5sk (civilization.json, skills, commands, plugins, teams), and the fort constitution (charter.md, fort/seats, civ/covenant.md, civ/seats).
design: Cron+script, no model (per charter Watchers). Baseline = sha256 manifest of the config set above. MUST exclude live churn or it false-positives every session: ~/.claude/projects, history.jsonl, file-history, tasks, sessions, session-env, shell-snapshots, paste-cache, cache, .credentials.json (token-refresh rewrites), backups. Do NOT baseline /tmp or .beads (churn/live DB). Emit an integrity.drift event so status.sh and the digest surface it; the Herald already watches constitutionDiffs and can carry this.
acceptance_criteria: Running the watcher on a clean tree reports no drift across a normal seat session (proves churn exclusions are correct). Mutating any baselined config file is reported by name on the next run. Zero-record runs fail closed (a checker that checks nothing must not report success), matching check-ceremony-record.sh discipline.
notes: Integrity-baseline sliver of the broader recovery story. NOT filed here (larger, later, must clear SO11 on observed-failure grounds): automated credential rotation, kill-switch, and wipe-and-restore over the three surfaces that survive a repo wipe (~/.claude, /tmp, Dolt data under refs/dolt/data). Any recovery design must NOT assume the airlock exists: charter/covenant reference fort/airlock and fort/scripts/airlock.sh but neither exists in this repo (implemented only in ForgeOs). Deploying the cron may want Overseer sign-off.

title: h5i Warden follow-ups: dirty-registry provenance, main() commit-lookup seam, condensation quality, art-pipeline doc version (Warden h5i r1 findings 2,4,7 + r2 finding 2)

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Verifier reproduced in the scratch copy (`npm ci` first — no `node_modules` in the scratch tree), all five steps green. Here is my review record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Scope reviewed:** `main..bead/9ge`, one commit `d9d7916` "fortkit-9ge: harden PixelLab retry and reuse" — `assets/trial/README.md`, `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs`, `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.d.mts`, `test/pixellab-trial.test.ts`, `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-09-9ge.md`. Path-scoped, nothing outside the bead. **No gate-listed area is touched** (no `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, `.claude/`, `fort/scripts/`, `bin/`, `civ/`, `.git/config`), so no mandatory escalation arises.

**Model:** the launcher's `session.start` event records `gpt-5.6-terra` (top Forge rung). The handoff self-reports "GPT-5 (Codex)". Terra does not carry the reward-hacking flag that the seat file attaches to Sol, so I scrutinised the test assertions for bite rather than for gaming — and they bite: the new seed assertion (`{...manifestAsset, seed: 41002}` → `null`) cannot pass against main's predicate, so it pins the new behaviour by construction rather than by tautology.

**Bead items, one by one:** (2) 5xx detail — the `>= 400 && < 500` window widens to `< 600`, and the first retryable body is cancelled before backoff. ✅ (1) The raw-base64 comment now reads as a `fortkit-fav` hypothesis run seven will test, not an asserted vendor fact — this is the change I care most about, because an asserted-fact comment is how a guess becomes fort doctrine. ✅ (3) Reuse now requires `asset.seed === cardDefinition.seed`, compared against the *offset-adjusted* definition (`withSeedOffset` runs before `reusableStillAsset` at `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:748`), and the manifest records that same offset seed — so the precedence is decided, not documented-away, and it fails in the safe direction (a legacy asset with no `seed` regenerates). ✅ (4) Reuse-through-`main` and `reusedAt` pinned; **pixflux-500-not-retried is absent** — see finding 1. ⚠️ (5) `main`'s `outputDirectory` parameter exercised by both new tests. ✅ (6) Shadowing resolved (`offset` → `scanlineOffset`), backoff literal hoisted, unreachable throw gone, and every `request(ANIMATION_ENDPOINT, …)` call site now stubs `process.stdout.write` — the vitest run is clean of attempt-lines. ✅

**Findings**

1. **NON-BLOCKING — the `pixflux-500-not-retried` pin did not land.** Bead item (4) names three pins; two landed. No test exercises `request(PIXFLUX_ENDPOINT, …)` against a 5xx, so nothing pins that the single-attempt path stays single-attempt, and nothing pins that a pixflux 500 now carries sanitized detail — every 5xx-detail assertion in the file goes through `ANIMATION_ENDPOINT`. The behaviour is correct today (`retryAnimation` gates on the endpoint), it is simply unguarded. **The acceptance criterion "all pins landed" is therefore not met, and this bead must not be closed against it** — standing order 9. File the missing pin as a bead; it is a five-line test.
2. **NON-BLOCKING — `ANIMATION_REQUEST_ATTEMPTS` does not actually bound the loop.** `for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt += 1)` is terminated only by the hardcoded `attempt === 1` in the retry guard; the new constant reaches nothing but the `attempts` variable used in the log string. I traced every path out of the loop body (throw on fetch error, return on ok, single `continue` guarded by `attempt === 1`, throw otherwise) and it is genuinely bounded at two, so this is not a hang. But raising the constant to 3 would silently change nothing except make the log line lie ("attempt 1/3"), and a second `continue` added later for, say, 429 would make it unbounded. `attempt < attempts` in the guard restores the coupling the constant advertises.
3. **NON-BLOCKING — the reuse key still omits everything except id, file, seed and hash.** This diff closes the seed hole; the same silent-staleness class remains open for `prompt`, `negativeConstraints`, `imageSize` and `params`, all of which the manifest already records. Change a prompt, keep the seed, and `PIXELLAB_REUSE_STILLS=1` hands back the old PNG without a word — exactly the failure mode bead item (3) was written about. Worth a bead, not a block.
4. **NON-BLOCKING — the first attempt's 5xx detail is discarded, not read.** The bead permitted "read-or-cancel" and cancel is a legitimate choice, but the consequence is that a 500 naming itself only on attempt 1 (empty body on attempt 2) still produces the bare `PixelLab request failed with HTTP 500.` Acceptable for run seven; note it if that message shows up detail-less.
5. **NON-BLOCKING — the handoff names the model imprecisely.** "GPT-5 (Codex)" vs the event stream's `gpt-5.6-terra`. The charter requires every handoff to record which model did the work, and failover analysis needs the *rung*, not the family. Not a false claim — Terra is a GPT-5-family model under Codex — so this is a precision fix, not a record correction under standing order 7.
6. **NON-BLOCKING — README nit.** The new sentence runs to ~100 columns against a file wrapped at ~76, and attributes the effect to "a reroll offset" when any seed change disables reuse.
7. **DOCUMENTED, NOT BLOCKED — untrusted vendor text on a wider path.** Extending `responseDetail` to 5xx widens the surface by which vendor-controlled prose reaches an operator's terminal and, through it, an agent transcript (threat 2, prompt injection via untrusted content; standing order 8). Redaction of the API key and `Bearer …`, the `{type, loc, msg}` projection for detail arrays, and the 4000-char slice are all already in place and cover threat 4 (credential leakage). The body is fully parsed before it is truncated, so a pathologically large error body is buffered whole — an availability nit on a hand-run script, with no in-scope actor behind it. Recorded, not defended against, per the charter's threat-model section.

**Verified independently**
- `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` (with `CI=1`) in the scratch copy after `npm ci`: typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (49 files), Vitest **115 tests / 10 files**, ShellCheck — all green. This matches the handoff's claim exactly; the count is monotone against main (net +2 tests).
- ShellCheck step re-run standalone to confirm it executed rather than being swallowed by pipeline truncation.
- Vitest output inspected for leaked `Animation request attempt …` lines: none.
- Loop termination proved by exhaustive path analysis of `request()` (finding 2), not by assumption.
- Seed-offset data flow traced from `withSeedOffset` through `reusableStillAsset` to the manifest write, confirming the comparison is against the adjusted seed on both sides.
- Diff path-scope and gate surface checked against the charter's cycle-7 read-only list.
- `fort/events/events-2026-08-08.jsonl` checked for the bead's `bead.claimed`/`work.begun`/`work.ended`/`session.end` chain: present and well-formed.

**Taken on faith**
- PixelLab's live behaviour — that the strict decoder wants raw base64, and that a real 500 populates `detail`. This is precisely what the reworded comment now correctly labels a hypothesis for run seven, so the diff no longer asks anyone to take it on faith as fact.
- I did not mutation-test the new assertions (no write permissions by construction); I reasoned about their bite from the predicates instead, as described above.
- The bead text as given to me is the full spec; I did not read the upstream `fortkit-fav` findings independently.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: 5xx detail, drain, seed-gated reuse all land and verify green; pixflux-500 pin missing, so do not close on acceptance.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Verifier reproduced in the scratch copy (npm ci first), all five steps green. Round-two record follows.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Scope reviewed (round 2):** `main..bead/9ge` is now a single new commit, `9fe6ad6` "fortkit-9ge: complete retry and reuse pins" — `assets/trial/README.md`, `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs`, `test/pixellab-trial.test.ts`, `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-08-9ge-r2.md`. Round one's `d9d7916` is already in `main` via merge `82708e4`. Path-scoped, nothing outside the bead. **No gate-listed area is touched** (no `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, `.claude/`, `fort/scripts/`, `bin/`, `civ/`, `.git/config`), so no mandatory escalation arises.

**Model:** `session.start` at 2026-08-08T21:52:11 records `gpt-5.6-terra`, and the handoff now names it precisely as "GPT-5.6 Terra (Codex)" — round-one finding 5 is closed. Terra carries no reward-hacking flag, so I read the new assertions for bite rather than for gaming; each new negative case in `reusableStillAsset` differs from the matching manifest asset in exactly one field, which is the strongest form this pin can take.

**Justin's remaining scope, item by item:**

- **(1) pixflux-500 pin — landed and bites.** `request(PIXFLUX_ENDPOINT, {}, "secret-key")` against a 500 whose `detail` carries both the API key and a `Bearer` token asserts three things at once: exactly one `fetch` call (single-attempt path preserved), the message contains `HTTP 500: upstream` (5xx detail reaches pixflux, not just animation), and neither secret survives. I traced both redactions: `replaceAll(apiKey)` catches `token=secret-key`, and `/Bearer\s+[^\s"']+/gi` catches `Bearer other-secret`. **The acceptance criterion "all pins landed" is now met**; my round-one instruction under standing order 9 is discharged and the bead may close on review.
- **(2) `ANIMATION_REQUEST_ATTEMPTS` coupled — landed.** `attempt === 1` → `attempt < attempts` at `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:563`. I re-proved termination on the changed guard: `attempts` is 2 for the animation endpoint and 1 otherwise, the only `continue` is inside a guard that is false once `attempt === attempts`, and every other path out of the loop body throws or returns. Raising the constant now changes behaviour and the log line together, which is what it advertised.
- **(3) reuse key widened — landed, and it is now *complete* for stills, not merely wider.** I diffed the key at `:710-719` against `pixfluxRequestBody` at `:223-232` field by field: `description`←prompt, `negative_description`←negativeConstraints, `image_size`←params.imageSize, `no_background`/`outline`←params, `seed`←seed. Every field of the still request is now covered, so the silent-staleness class that round-one finding 3 kept open is closed rather than narrowed. The key is built with the *same expression* the manifest writer uses (`{ imageSize, ...cardDefinition.params }`, `:673` vs `:706-709`), and a legacy asset with no `params` yields `JSON.stringify(undefined) !== "<string>"` — fails closed, regenerates.
- **(4) unread first-attempt detail — accepted and recorded** in the handoff's Open risks section. See finding 3 for where I would rather it live.
- **(6) README — landed.** The over-long line is gone (longest line in the file is now 79 columns, in prose predating this bead), and the wording is the general "Any seed change disables reuse" rather than the reroll-specific claim.

**Findings**

1. **NON-BLOCKING — the widened key cost the seed-offset *integration* pin its discrimination.** In "main skips reuse when a seed offset changes the recorded still seed" (`test/pixellab-trial.test.ts:461`) the seeded manifest asset is still `{id, file, seed, sha256}` with no `prompt`/`negativeConstraints`/`params`. Against the round-one key, `seed` was the sole reason reuse was refused, so the test pinned the seed gate. Against the round-two key it now fails on `prompt` as well, so deleting the `asset?.seed === cardDefinition.seed` clause would leave that test green. This is a test-strength regression introduced by this commit, not a behaviour regression: the unit-level pin at `:404-410` (`{...manifestAsset, seed: 41002}` against an otherwise fully-matching asset) still isolates the seed exactly, so the gate remains guarded. The repair is to give that test's manifest asset the same three fields the other tests now carry. Worth a bead.
2. **NON-BLOCKING — the params comparison is `JSON.stringify` equality, which is key-order sensitive.** It works today only because both sides are built by the identical spread expression and all keys are non-numeric, so V8 preserves insertion order through the manifest round-trip. Reordering the keys in a `card()`/`walkCard()` literal would silently stop matching. It fails in the safe direction — a needless regeneration, costing one still's spend, never a stale reuse — so this is a robustness note, not a defect. A shallow key-sorted compare would remove the coupling to literal order.
3. **NON-BLOCKING — the cancelled-unread tradeoff is documented only in the handoff.** `await response.body?.cancel()` at `:567` has no comment, while the reason a detail-less 500 can appear lives in `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-08-9ge-r2.md`. A future reader of the script sees the discard, not the decision. One line beside the cancel, in the same hypothesis-phrased register as the raw-base64 comment, would put the record where the behaviour is.
4. **NON-BLOCKING, and not about this diff — the Warden launch ladder deviated.** `fort/events/events-2026-08-08.jsonl` shows this review attempted three times: `opus` at 21:55 (incident, no VERDICT-LINE, exit 1), `gpt-5.6-sol` at 22:03:35 (incident two seconds later, exit 1), then `opus` again at 22:04:13 — this session. The seat file's ladder is Opus 5 → GPT-5.6 Sol → **block and page the Overseer**; a third rung that returns to Opus is not on it. The incidents were recorded correctly and nothing was read as a pass, so the safety property held. But the fort should decide deliberately whether re-trying the top rung is the intended behaviour or a launcher gap, because "never degrades below frontier" was satisfied here by accident of which rung was retried. File against the launcher, not against this merge.
5. **DOCUMENTED, NOT BLOCKED — untrusted vendor text (threat 2).** This pass adds no new path by which vendor-controlled prose reaches a terminal; the `>= 400 && < 600` window that covers pixflux landed in round one. What is new is that the redaction on that path is now *tested* rather than merely present, which is a net improvement to threat 4 (credential leakage). The pathological-body note from round one stands unchanged: `responseDetail` parses the whole body before slicing to 4000 chars, an availability nit on a hand-run script with no in-scope actor behind it.

**Verified independently**

- `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in the scratch copy after `npm ci`: typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (49 files), Vitest **116 tests / 10 files**, ShellCheck — all green. This matches the handoff's claim exactly, and is monotone against round one's 115 (net +1 test: the pixflux pin; the reuse test was extended and renamed, not added).
- ShellCheck re-run standalone over the full `verify.sh` file list to confirm the step executed rather than being swallowed after the Vitest summary — clean, exit 0.
- Vitest output inspected for leaked `Animation request attempt …` lines: none. The new pixflux test needs no stdout stub because `:537` gates the attempt line on `retryAnimation`.
- Loop termination re-proved on the changed guard by path analysis, not assumption (finding 2 of round one, now closed).
- Reuse-key completeness checked field-by-field against `pixfluxRequestBody`, and the write/read symmetry checked against `writeAsset:673`.
- README re-wrapped: longest line in the file measured at 79 columns.
- Diff path-scope and gate surface checked against the charter's cycle-7 kernel-RO list.
- The bead's round-2 event chain (`bead.claimed`/`session.start`/`work.begun`/`work.ended`/`session.end`, all `kethra`/`forge`, exit 0) is present and well-formed; the three Warden session records are as described in finding 4.

**Taken on faith**

- PixelLab's live behaviour — that a real 500 populates `detail`, and that the strict decoder wants raw base64. The comment reworded in round one still correctly labels the latter a fortkit-fav hypothesis for run seven.
- I did not mutation-test the new assertions (no write permissions by construction); I reasoned about their bite from the predicates, which is how finding 1 surfaced.
- Round one's 115-test baseline is taken from my own prior record rather than re-run against `main`.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS r2: pixflux-500 pin, attempts coupling, full reuse key, README all landed and verify green (116 tests); acceptance now met.

comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round 1. Bead fortkit-9t7, commit `dc75555` ("fortkit-9t7: exercise PNG filter decoding and bound inflate"), authored by the Forge seat. **Model: the launcher's `session.start` event records `gpt-5.6-terra`** (Forge ladder rung 1); the handoff header says "GPT-5 Codex" — see finding 5. Scrutiny weighted for a non-Claude frontier model on a diff whose whole purpose is to make an existing correctness claim executable rather than argued; I re-derived the PNG filter algebra against the spec rather than accepting the round-trip green.

All four acceptance criteria are met. The commit touches exactly four files (`scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs`, `test/pixellab-trial.test.ts`, `assets/trial/README.md`, `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-08-9t7.md`) — no constitution path, no launcher, no profile, no `.env`, nothing public-facing. No gate-6/mandatory-ESCALATE area is in the diff. Nothing here is worth blocking on.

**1. (non-blocking) The filter test is a round trip against a duplicated encoder, so a spec-divergent-but-symmetric predictor would pass.** `paeth()` and the average predictor are now implemented twice — `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:471` and `test/pixellab-trial.test.ts:116` — and the test encodes with the same predictor it decodes with. If both were wrong in the same way, every assertion (including the bit-identical-across-filters check) would still be green, and a real PixelLab IDAT would still decode to garbage. I checked both implementations directly against RFC 2083 §6: PaethPredictor's tie-breaking (`pa <= pb && pa <= pc` → a, else `pb <= pc` → b, else c) and Average's `floor((a+b)/2)` are exact, and Sub/Up read `left`/`above` from the *reconstructed* buffer as the spec requires. So there is no bug today — but the test cannot be the thing that tells us that. Bead-sized fix: pin one filter against a fixture PNG from an independent encoder, or hardcode the expected filtered byte stream for a small image.

**2. (non-blocking, the one I'd most want filed) Filters are uniform per image, never per row — which is precisely what "adaptive filtering" means.** The loop at `test/pixellab-trial.test.ts:262` runs five images, each with one filter type for all 64 rows. Real encoders choose a filter *per scanline*. The single most likely adaptive-filtering decoder bug — reading the filter byte once and applying it to every row — passes all five of these cases unharmed. The production decoder does read it per row (`scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:442`, inside the row loop), so it is correct; the test just doesn't hold it there. The fix is one line: a sixth case with `filterType` a function of row (`row % 5`). The bead's acceptance criterion as written ("All five filter types executed and bit-identical") is satisfied, so this is a finding, not a shortfall — but it is the gap between "five filters execute" and the bead's actual motivation, and it's the cheapest remaining unit of confidence before 8 credits are spent.

**3. (non-blocking) The inflate bound is correct and now collapses two distinct failures into one message.** `maxOutputLength: (rowBytes+1)*height` is computed pre-inflate from the validated IHDR (`scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:423-433`), which is the right bound and the right place. Node throws `ERR_BUFFER_TOO_LARGE` on exceedance, which the existing `catch` maps to "invalid PNG image data" — so an oversized stream is now reported as malformed rather than oversized. It fails closed, which is what matters; the `!== scanlineLength` check below remains live for *short* streams, so it is not dead code. Worth knowing when someone debugs a refusal. I confirmed by execution that an exactly-sized stream does **not** trip the limit — the five-filter test decodes a stream of exactly `scanlineLength` bytes and passes, which is the off-by-one this option most invites.

**4. (non-blocking) The vertical axis was generalized; the horizontal one was left un-floored.** `padAnimationReference` now computes `yOffset = height - sourceHeight` and iterates `sourceHeight` rows (`scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:493-497`), which states the bottom-center placement in code instead of assuming `from.height === to.height`. Today `yOffset` is 0 and behaviour is unchanged; the untouched rows come from `Buffer.alloc`, so they are filter-0 transparent, which is correct. But `xOffset = (width - sourceWidth) / 2` is still unfloored, so if `REFERENCE_PADDING` ever gained an odd width delta, `Buffer.copy` would receive a fractional `targetStart`. Pre-existing, not introduced here, and the diff made the two axes asymmetric in rigor. Bead if anyone touches the padding contract.

**5. (non-blocking) The handoff's model line disagrees with the launcher's event.** `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-08-9t7.md:3` says "GPT-5 Codex"; `fort/events/events-2026-08-08.jsonl` records `{"model":"gpt-5.6-terra"}`. This is model self-report drift, not a fabrication: 65 of 65 Forge handoffs carry a self-reported model string and they disagree with each other across identical launches. The authoritative record (the event, written by the launcher) is right, and the charter's "every handoff records which model did the work" is satisfied in substance. If the fort wants it exact, the handoff template should interpolate the launcher's model id rather than ask the model. Observed repeatedly, so standing order 11 is met if anyone wants to file it.

**6. (non-blocking, no action needed) `MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 5 while still entries gain an always-present `referencePadding: null`.** Previously `undefined` and therefore dropped by `JSON.stringify`; now emitted. That is a shape change to the manifest, but `assets/trial/` contains only `README.md` — the trial has never run, so there is no manifest anywhere to migrate. The change is additive, `assets/trial/README.md:70` documents the convention, and the tests pin both the walk and still cases. Note that `cost` still uses key-absence as meaning ("a quarter of a credit is not a thing the vendor charges"), so the manifest carries two conventions; that is deliberate and documented, and bead item (5) asked only about the reference pair. Cosmetic: the README reflow left a stub line ("PixelLab requires the animation").

**7. (non-blocking, for the merging seat) The branch is one commit behind main, so the raw `main..bead/9t7` range shows deletions the Forge did not make.** `bead/9t7..main` contains `f89f745` (civ records / beads export, cycle 7 wrap), so the range diff shows `civ/remember.md` losing 36 lines and `.beads/*.jsonl` losing entries. `git show dc75555 --stat` confirms the commit touches only the four files above. An ordinary merge preserves those records; a reset or force-update would silently violate standing order 7 (records are append-only). Merge, don't rewrite.

**Threat model.** Nothing in this diff bears on threats 2 (prompt injection), 3 (supply chain) or 4 (credential leakage) — no network, no new dependency, no key handling; the handoff's "no live PixelLab endpoint was invoked and no API key was read" is consistent with a diff that adds only local test scaffolding. The inflate bound is a robustness control against a malformed or hostile vendor response, which sits nearest threat 1 (agent accident): an unbounded `inflateSync` on a decompression bomb is a memory blowup inside an unattended trial runner. It is cheap, correctly placed, and I would have wanted it regardless of threat class. Nothing here requires the out-of-scope shell-access adversary.

**Verified independently (reproduced in my scratch copy /tmp/warden-9t7, `npm ci` then `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`):** typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome, Vitest, ShellCheck all green, exit 0, **108/108 tests in 10 files** — matching the handoff's claim exactly, run against the candidate code and freshly installed dependencies, not a stale tree. I read the full `constrainedRgbaPixels` / `padAnimationReference` / `writeAsset` bodies and both callers in `main()`, and checked both predictor implementations line by line against RFC 2083 §6. I confirmed the test's `decodeFilterZeroRgbaPng` asserts every output filter byte is 0, so the padded PNG's own encoding is pinned. I confirmed the bound test distinguishes new behaviour from old (it asserts "invalid PNG image data", reachable only through the new `maxOutputLength` throw; the pre-change code would have reported "unexpected PNG scanline length"). I confirmed the commit's file list, the base drift against main, the `work.begun`/`work.ended`/`session.end` events for the bead, and that no `fort/` constitution path, profile, launcher or secret is in the diff.

**Taken on faith:** that the live PixelLab master IDAT uses standard deflate with per-row adaptive filters (my own eyo finding, from reading the spec and the stream, not from decoding a vendor response here — no API call was made and none should have been); that Node's `maxOutputLength` semantics hold across the versions this will run on, beyond the one I executed; and that `f89f745` will be merged rather than rewritten (finding 7).

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — all 4 criteria met, 108/108 reproduced green; filters tested uniform-per-image, not per-row (bead)

I've completed the review. Verifier reproduced green in my scratch copy; here is the record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Scope reviewed:** `main..bead/0qh`, single commit `1aaf13e` "fortkit-0qh: harden pre-manifest pricing provenance" — 5 files, +144/−25: `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs`, its `.d.mts`, `test/pixellab-trial.test.ts`, `docs/proposals/art-pipeline/README.md`, and a new `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-08-0qh.md`.

**Model that produced the work:** the handoff records "GPT-5 Codex, as Kethra Anvilmark (she/her)" — a non-Claude model, so I read the tests for tautology and the record for overclaim rather than taking either on trust. I found neither. The prior `wu5` handoff uses the identical model line, so this is fort convention, not a one-off.

**Acceptance criteria, item by item — all met:**
- *schemaVersion 4*: `MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION = 4` (`scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:33`), used at the one manifest construction site (`:472`), exported, declared in `.d.mts:106`, pinned by test. No manifest exists on disk yet (`assets/trial/` holds only `README.md`), and nothing in the repo reads a manifest, so the bump has no migration surface — the bead's "before the first REAL manifest" premise holds.
- *Honest per-frame cost*: `perFrameProvenance` (`:278-284`) emits `cost` for the divisible USD meter and `amortizedCost` for generation credits, with the full `requestCost` always preserved. Walk frames no longer present 0.25 as a charged generation.
- *Distinct refusal wording*: "unexpected pricing shape" vs "a USD/generations amount over the per-request cap (X > Y)", both still carrying the received object verbatim.
- *Discriminator ordering*: `usage?.type === "generations"` is evaluated before the `usd` field (`:246`); a payload carrying both meters resolves to generations, and any other non-undefined `type` is refused.
- *Cap branches pinned*: tests now cover `addUsage`'s USD-total-cap branch (previously unpinned) and generations `0 / -1 / 1.5` rejection.

**Findings:**

1. **Non-blocking — `assets/trial/README.md` was not updated and now understates the manifest shape.** That file is the manifest's own field documentation (it is what a person reads standing next to `provenance-manifest.json`), and it still says the manifest records the "returned cost meter (`{ "meter": ..., "amount": ... }`)" with no mention of `requestCost`, `amortizedCost`, or `schemaVersion`. The new prose went into `docs/proposals/art-pipeline/README.md` instead. The consequence a reader will hit: on a generation-credit-billed account, a walk-frame asset entry has **no `cost` key at all** (`writeAsset` passes `undefined`, which `JSON.stringify` drops) — correct per the bead, but currently undocumented where it matters. `wu5` updated this same file for its meter change, so the omission is drift, not a deliberate split. Worth a bead. This does not make the fort worse than not merging: the added `docs/proposals` section is accurate, and no code consumes the manifest.

2. **Non-blocking — the accepted-shape set narrowed further than the bead's minimum, and that should be on the record as accepted.** The bead offered "branch on `usage.type` before the `usd` field, **or** reject payloads carrying both meters". The implementation branches first *and* refuses any payload whose `type` is present but not `"generations"` — so a hypothetical `{ type: "usd", usd: 0.0084 }` is now refused as an unexpected shape where `main` accepted it. I judge this correct rather than defective: the only live-observed shape is a bare `usage.usd` (per the Mayor's 2026-08-08 correction at `docs/proposals/art-pipeline/README.md:307`), which the code still accepts, and for a spend guard, failing closed with the received object printed is the right default under threat 1 (agent accident — an unattended run overspending). The operator-visible cost if PixelLab ever tags USD responses is one billed request and an abort, not silent spend. Recording it so the next reviewer does not rediscover it as a surprise.

3. **Non-blocking — the handoff's model line does not name a charter ladder rung.** "GPT-5 Codex" is not one of the Forge rungs as the charter spells them (GPT-5.6 Terra → Sol → Sonnet 5 → Opus 5). The charter requires every handoff to record which model did the work; "GPT-5 Codex" records a family, not a rung, which makes failover attribution and scrutiny-weighting approximate. This is fort-wide convention (`wu5`'s handoff is identical), not a defect of this bead, so it is an observation for the Mayor's judgment rather than a bead I would press for here.

4. **Non-blocking, minor — `perFrameProvenance` divides by `frameCount` with no positive guard.** Unreachable today: the sole call site passes `walkCards.length` (a module constant of 4), and `generateWalkCycle` already refuses a frame-count mismatch before it. Noted for completeness, not worth machinery.

**Considered and cleared:** no gate-1 constitutional file is touched (the only `fort/` path is `fort/handoffs/`, the documented per-bead record — charter, seat files, launchers and profiles are untouched), so no mandatory ESCALATE; no `.env`/secret access; nothing public-facing. The refusal messages serialize the response `usage` object only, never the key, so threat 4 (credential leakage) is unchanged. Float check on the amortization: `0.02 / 4` is an exact power-of-two scaling and equals the double for `0.005`, so the USD share test is not papering over drift. No tests were deleted — one was renamed and strengthened, four added (net +4 blocks, 104 total), so test-count monotonicity holds. `requestCost` shares an object reference across the four frame entries; nothing mutates it and serialization duplicates it, so this is harmless.

**Verified independently (reproduced in my scratch copy at `/tmp/warden-0qh`, which I confirmed byte-identical to the candidate worktree apart from `.beads`):**
- `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0**, confirmed by a sentinel echoed on success, not by reading a tail. Node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (49 files, no fixes), **104/104 Vitest tests in 10 files**, ShellCheck 0.11.0 present and clean. This exactly matches the handoff's claim of 104 tests and a green run, so that record is accurate.
- The candidate worktree is clean and on `bead/0qh`.
- Read the full post-change `run-pixellab-trial.mjs`, the full test file, the `.d.mts`, and the `wu5` predecessor commit to confirm the before/after semantics of `parseUsageMeter` myself rather than from the diff hunks alone.
- Grepped the repo for `requestCost` / `amortizedCost` / `provenance-manifest` / `schemaVersion` to confirm there is no downstream consumer of the manifest that a version-4 shape change could break.

**Taken on faith:** the handoff's "No live PixelLab endpoint was invoked and no API key was read" — I cannot verify a negative about the Forge's session, though it is consistent with the diff (no new network path; the child-process tests spawn with `env: { PATH }` only, so no key could reach them). Also taken on faith: PixelLab's real `usage` shapes beyond the one live-observed `usage.usd`, which no one here can confirm without spending.

This is round one and I would block on nothing.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: all five bead items met, verifier reproduced green (104 tests); 4 non-blocking findings, top one is assets/trial/README drift.

Fix: raise PIXFLUX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS to 120s (matching the animation default), and implement the v9l floor rule in the same motion since it is now observed-relevant: PIXELLAB_TIMEOUT_MS acts as a floor/per-endpoint value rather than a uniform replacement, so raising one bound cannot silently lower the other. Update the README's timeout paragraph. Also note for the record: the run is already one-image-per-request sequential — batching was never the issue. Emit recipe: fort/scripts/emit.sh work.begun "<detail>" -a kethra -s forge -t fortkit-<id>.

comments.text:
Verifier reproduced green in my scratch tree; diff reviewed against spec, charter, and the record. Here is the review.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Scope.** `main..bead/4cc`, one commit `d9c1bf2` "fortkit-4cc: floor PixelLab request timeouts at 120s": `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs`, `test/pixellab-trial.test.ts`, `assets/trial/README.md`, plus a new `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-08-4cc.md`. Model: the launcher's event stream records `gpt-5.6-terra` (`session.start`, 2026-08-08T00:35:36) — top ladder rung, not the reward-hacking-flagged Sol; the handoff self-reports "GPT-5 Codex" (finding 3). Because the diff rewrites a timeout test in a way that could hide a hang, I gave the test change the scrutiny that pattern deserves and concluded it is legitimate (finding 2).

**Gates.** No gate-listed area is touched. The only `fort/` path in the diff is `fort/handoffs/`, which `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh` leaves writable by design; `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/` and the launchers are untouched. No mandatory escalation. Threat model: nothing here bears on threats 1–4. It touches no secret handling (the script still reads `PIXELLAB_API_KEY` from the environment only), weakens no control, and the failure it fixes is wasted spend, not a security property.

**Acceptance criteria, item by item.** Both defaults 120s+ — met (`PIXFLUX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` 30_000 → 120_000, animation already 120_000). Override cannot lower an endpoint below its default — met via `Math.max(endpointDefault, timeout)` in `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:190-207`, applied per endpoint, so the v9l floor rule holds in both directions. README updated — met. Timeout tests adjusted — met.

1. **Non-blocking — a below-floor override is clamped silently.** `Math.max` means `PIXELLAB_TIMEOUT_MS=30000` now yields 120000 with no output. That is exactly what the bead asked for, and I would not have it otherwise, but an operator who deliberately sets a short bound (a fast-fail auth smoke test, say) gets a two-minute wait and no explanation. A one-line stderr notice when the requested value is raised would make the floor observable instead of surprising. File as a bead; it does not hold the merge.

2. **Non-blocking — the timeout test now mocks `AbortSignal.timeout` entirely, so real-timer integration is no longer covered, and the spy does not assert its argument.** The mock is necessary, not evasive: with the floor in place the old `PIXELLAB_TIMEOUT_MS=1` path would take 120 real seconds, so injecting a controllable signal is the right fix, and the assertion still pins the exact message and the floored value (`test/pixellab-trial.test.ts:202-228`). Two residual gaps: nothing now proves `AbortSignal.timeout` is called with 120000 (the spy is created and restored but never asserted on — `expect(timeoutSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(120_000)` is one line), and the abort-fires-from-a-real-timer path is untested. I checked the mock for flakiness — the listener is registered synchronously inside the replaced `fetch` before `abortController.abort()` runs, so there is no race — and the spy is restored in `finally`.

3. **Non-blocking, pre-existing, fort-wide — the handoff's `Model:` line contradicts the launcher's record.** The handoff says "GPT-5 Codex"; the event stream says `gpt-5.6-terra`. Charter §Seats requires every handoff to record which model did the work, and a self-reported harness label is the least reliable possible source for it. This is not introduced here — sixteen prior Forge handoffs carry the same string — so it is not a defect of this diff, but standing order 7 makes it worth fixing at the class: have the launcher stamp the model into the handoff header, or drop the self-reported line in favour of the event. Bead-worthy.

4. **Non-blocking nit — "The runner already sends one image per request sequentially" is true of the Pixflux loop but sits in a paragraph that also covers the animation endpoint,** which returns four frames from one request (as the same README says at line 36). I verified the Pixflux loop is genuinely sequential (`for (const originalCardDefinition of cardDefinitions) { … await generatePixflux(…) }`, `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:428-430`), so the claim the bead wanted on the record is accurate — only its placement invites a misread.

5. **Non-blocking nit — "Higher values raise the bound for both endpoints" is true only while the two defaults are equal.** If the animation default is ever raised above Pixflux's, an intermediate override will raise one and not the other, and the sentence becomes quietly wrong. "raises the bound for any endpoint whose default is lower" would survive that change.

6. **Non-blocking, pre-existing — the validation branches are untested.** `PIXELLAB_TIMEOUT_MS` of `0`, `abc`, or a value past `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` all throw, and no test covers any of them. The diff touched exactly this function and its test, so two `expect(...).toThrow()` lines were cheap here; but nothing regressed, so it stays a bead.

**Verified independently (in `/tmp/warden-4cc`, a scratch copy with no `.git`):** `npm ci` then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — TypeScript node and browser typechecks, Biome over 49 files, **99/99 Vitest tests in 10 files**, and ShellCheck all pass, exit 0. Run twice, same result. The handoff's verifier claim is therefore true, not taken on faith. I confirmed the scratch tree is byte-identical to `bead/4cc` for all product paths (`git --work-tree=/tmp/warden-4cc diff bead/4cc -- scripts test assets src schema templates bin civ` is empty), so the green run is against the candidate code and not a stale tree. I read the floor logic and the `request()` abort path directly, confirmed the sequential one-image-per-request loop, confirmed via repo-wide grep that no other doc or script still states the 30s figure (only the append-only o4h/doj handoffs, correctly left alone), confirmed the commit is path-scoped to four files with no lockfile or dependency churn, and confirmed the `work.begun`/`work.ended` events for 4cc are in the stream.

**Taken on faith:** that the live 30s timeout happened as the bead reports — the run was not repeated, and it should not be, since repeating it costs real money; and that 120s is in fact sufficient under real GPU queue load. The second is an estimate, better founded than the o4h one it replaces (the animation endpoint has run at 120s), but still an estimate — if a fourth live run times out at 120s, that is new evidence for a new bead, not a defect in this change. I could not run `bd` or `node` directly under the Warden profile, so the bead text and the v9l floor rule are as quoted in my instructions.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — 120s floor correct, spec fully met, verifier green (99/99); 6 non-blocking findings for beads.
