comments.author: ilva
comments.text: Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS Round one. Work produced by the Forge on **GPT-5.6 Terra (Codex)** per the launcher's `session.start` event — the ladder's top rung, not the reward-hack-flagged Sol rung. I still checked the diff for scope creep and test-weakening: there is none. The change set is exactly the five files the bead asks for, assertions were added and none removed, and `src/cli.ts` is untouched so the `fortkit world` command surface is intact as the bead requires. Acceptance criteria all met: `Bartizan` and `Bartizan — Manyhalls world view` in `src/world-page.html`; README line 6 names Bartizan in place of "the viewer (unnamed product)"; `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md` gains a dated blockquote note after the status line without touching the historical body; no CLI rename; `test/world.test.ts` pins both visible strings and is the only test that pins a title. The colony page does not exist yet, so "bzx.3 should be born named" carries forward as a note, correctly recorded in the handoff rather than pre-implemented. **Gates.** No gate-1 territory: the diff touches no `fort/` constitution file (`fort/handoffs/` is a seat's own working record, writable by design and outside the mask's read-only set). Gate 3 is honoured rather than crossed — the name is the Overseer's own decision (`fortkit-zgp`), applied here, with release-time trademark/domain diligence retained by him on that bead; nothing in this diff publishes anything. No auth surface, no migration, no deal-visibility change. Nothing here is mandatory-ESCALATE. FINDINGS 1. **Non-blocking — the two-dot diff's apparent deletion of the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md convention lines is an artifact, not a loss.** `git diff main..bead/kyu` shows five lines removed from AGENTS.md and the CLAUDE.md conventions reverting to the placeholder. That is the branch sitting one commit behind main: `be9ac9d` (already on main) added exactly those lines and touches only AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, while this branch touches five entirely different files. `git diff main...bead/kyu` (merge base) shows the true change set. A normal merge commit — the fort's flow — preserves both sides cleanly. I flag it because the range I was handed renders it as a deletion, and a reader of this record should not act on that. It would only become real if the branch were applied by reset or checkout-over rather than merged. 2. **Non-blocking, bead-worthy — the fort's own verifier cannot go green in the Warden's scratch copy, and this is an observed failure, not an imagined one.** `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in `/tmp/warden-kyu` fails at the test step: `test/world.test.ts:45` asserts the exact `gaps` array for the "No Beads" fixture fort, and in a tree with no `.git` an extra `"git state unavailable"` gap appears, because `readGitState` (`src/readers/git.ts:57`) shells out to `git -C test/fixtures/fort-no-beads rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`, which only succeeds when the fixture happens to sit inside a real work tree. I confirmed that same command succeeds in the candidate worktree and fails in the scratch copy, so the test passes there and fails here for environmental reasons alone. Pre-existing, untouched by this diff, and blocking nothing — but it means the review procedure documented in `fort/remember.md` ("reproduce the verifier in the scratch copy") structurally cannot produce a clean run. The fix is to stop letting fixture assertions depend on ambient git: either inject the git reader in the test or assert gaps with `arrayContaining`. Worth a bead. 3. **Non-blocking — the spec note carries no provenance pointer.** `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md:5` says "(decision, 2026-08-07)" without naming the Overseer or `fortkit-zgp`, where the equivalent line already on main in AGENTS.md does cite both. A stranger reading the founding spec cannot trace the name to its decision record. One clause would fix it. 4. **Non-blocking, forward-looking — `Bartizan` is page-agnostic and will need disambiguation when the colony view lands.** Two Bartizan tabs open on world and colony will be indistinguishable in a tab strip. The header already does the right thing (`Bartizan — Manyhalls world view`); the title should follow that shape when `bzx.3` arrives. Not a defect against this bead's acceptance criteria, which ask only that the title say Bartizan. 5. **Non-blocking — model attribution disagrees across records for the same session.** The launcher emitted `gpt-5.6-terra`; the Forge's own `work.begun`/`work.ended` payloads say `"GPT-5"` and the handoff header says "GPT-5 Codex". Nothing is falsified and the pattern predates this bead (the 2026-08-07 handoff entry above this one says the same), but the charter makes the recorded model a review input, and self-reported model strings are the least reliable half of that record. Worth a bead to make the handoff take the model from the launcher rather than from the model's self-description. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY - Ran the verifier in the scratch copy after `npm ci`: **typecheck clean (tsc --noEmit), Biome clean (34 files), Vitest 20/21 passing with the single failure diagnosed in finding 2, ShellCheck clean** across `bin/fort-init bin/regent fort/scripts/*.sh fort/scripts/lib/*.sh civ/scripts/*.sh` (run separately, since the verifier's fail-fast stopped before it). The two new assertions at `test/world.test.ts:60-61` pass; the test containing them is green. - Read every changed file in the candidate tree; confirmed the worktree is clean at `bead/kyu` and the commit split is code (`f9caafc`, 4 files) plus handoff (`40aba56`), path-scoped, no stray artifacts. - Confirmed the merge-base change set is 5 files and that main's tip touches a disjoint 2, so the merge is clean. - Confirmed no CLI or template surface was renamed, and that no other test or template pins the old title. - Corroborated the Bartizan decision inside the repo of record: the Mayor's `milestone` event on `fortkit-zgp` ("The viewer is named: BARTIZAN (Overseer decision, zgp closed)") and merged commit `be9ac9d`. - Confirmed the two earlier Warden launches recorded `incident` + `session.end` with `verdict_recorded:false` and no verdict — the launcher failed safe, exactly as designed, and this is genuinely round one. TAKEN ON FAITH - The text of `fortkit-zgp` itself: I have no `bd` access from this seat, so I read the decision through the event stream and the merged AGENTS.md line rather than the bead. Both are independent of the Forge's own account, so this is corroborated, not merely asserted. - The handoff's claim that `verify.sh --no-emit` passed in the candidate worktree (21 tests). I reproduced everything except the one assertion that is coupled to ambient git state, and I verified that assertion fails only because my scratch copy lacks `.git`. I did not re-run the suite inside the real worktree, which would have meant executing in a tree I am meant only to read. VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — Bartizan naming is in scope, correct, tested; 5 non-blocking findings, incl. a git-coupled test that breaks the Warden's own verifier run.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Review complete. Here is my record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Bead:** fortkit-b18 — decided by the Overseer 2026-08-07 as option (a): page script moves to a type-checked, linted `.ts` file, composed into the HTML by the server at startup, zero new runtime deps, tsconfig gains DOM lib access.

**What the diff does:** `src/world-page.html` keeps the shell and loses its 42-line inline script, replaced by an `<!-- world-page-script -->` marker; `src/world-page.ts` is the new checked module (typed against `WorldFort`, DOM types, strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`-clean); `src/server.ts` reads both at module load and composes them via `stripTypeScriptTypes(..., { mode: "strip" })` from `node:module`; tsconfig gains `"lib": ["ES2024", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"]`; one test assertion added; handoff appended. Branch is 2 ahead / 0 behind `main` — clean fast-forward. Two commits, code separated from record, both bead-referenced.

**The bead's own acceptance is met.** The script is now type-checked (`tsc` covers `src/**/*.ts`) and linted (Biome went 33 → 34 files, the new `.ts` being the increment). No new dependency: `stripTypeScriptTypes` is a Node built-in and `package.json` pins `node >=24 <25`. The pattern bzx.3 will inherit is coherent and reviewable. Nothing here is blocking, and nothing touches a gate-listed area — the only `fort/` path in the diff is `fort/handoffs/`, a record, not the constitution.

**Findings**

1. **(non-blocking) The DOM lib is enabled project-wide, not for the one browser file.** The Overseer's decision says "tsconfig gains DOM lib access *for that file*." `tsconfig.json:4` grants `DOM` and `DOM.Iterable` to every file in `include` — all of `src/`, `test/`, `vitest.config.ts`. Consequence: server and CLI code can now reference `document`, `window`, `localStorage` and typecheck clean, and DOM's `fetch`/`Response` shadow the Node ones. This is a real loosening of checking on the Node surface, traded for checking the browser surface that previously had none — net coverage still improves, which is why it is not blocking. The correct shape is a second config (`tsconfig.browser.json` with `include: ["src/world-page.ts"]` carrying the DOM libs) and a DOM-free Node config, which costs a second `tsc` invocation in `verify.sh`. Worth a bead, and worth deciding before bzx.3 adds a second browser file.

2. **(non-blocking) The composition step is `$`-substitution-sensitive.** `src/server.ts:20-23` passes the stripped script as the *replacement* argument to `String.prototype.replace`. Replacement strings interpret `$$`, `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'` and `$n`. I grepped `src/world-page.ts` for those sequences and found none, so today's output is byte-correct — and the existing assertion that the page still contains the literal `open ${fort.beads.open}` confirms `${` passes through untouched. But this is a footgun aimed at the future: an ordinary edit to the page script (or to the colony renderer, which is specified to copy this pattern) that introduces `$'` or `$&` in a string would silently corrupt the served JavaScript with no verifier catching it. The fix is one line — pass a replacer function, `() => scriptTag`, or `split`/`join`. This is the finding I would most like carried into bzx.3.

3. **(non-blocking) TypeScript checks the file as an ES module; the browser runs it as a classic script.** `verbatimModuleSyntax` plus the `import type` at line 1 make `world-page.ts` a module to tsc, so its top-level bindings are module-scoped — while at runtime the injected `<script>` puts `card` and `load` on the global object, which is precisely what the VM test depends on. Today the only import is type-only and erased, so nothing breaks. If someone adds a value import, tsc accepts it and the page fails in the browser; the VM test would catch it (`new Script` throws on `import`), so the guard exists but is incidental rather than stated. A comment in the file recording that it is compiled-as-module, executed-as-classic-script would keep the next author out of it.

4. **(non-blocking) A missing marker fails quietly in the server, loudly only in the tests.** If the marker in the HTML is renamed, `replace` no-ops and the page ships with no script at all; `server.ts` neither throws nor logs. The test suite does catch it (`toContain('fetch("/world")')` fails), so the fort is covered — but the server itself would happily serve a dead page. An explicit throw at composition time is cheap and belongs in the pattern bzx.3 copies.

5. **(non-blocking) Leftover doc scaffolding, and a security invariant written nowhere.** `src/world-page.ts:19-20` is an entirely empty `/** */` block above `list`, and lines 3-6 end with a dangling ` *`. Beyond the tidiness: `list()` interpolates `title` and `className` **unescaped** while escaping `items`. Every current call site passes literals, so there is no reachable injection — but the parameter is typed plain `string` with no marker that it is trusted, in a function that now lives in a reusable checked module. The empty JSDoc sits exactly where that invariant should have been written. Bears on threat 2 (untrusted content — the page renders other forts' bead titles, announcements and event details), latent rather than live.

6. **(non-blocking) The handoff misnames the model.** `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md` records "Model: GPT-5 Codex", and the Forge's own `work.begun`/`work.ended` events carry `"model":"GPT-5"`. The launcher's `session.start` — the authoritative record, since `forge.sh` passes the ladder model to `codex -m` — says `gpt-5.6-terra`, the first rung. The earlier entry in the same file by the same model says "GPT-5.6 Terra (Codex)". This is a model misidentifying itself, contradicted in the same event stream by a correct record, so the fort has not lost the fact and it does not make merging worse. Per standing order 7 the correction is appended, not edited in. The class fix is for `forge.sh` to inject the ladder model name into the handoff rather than letting the model self-report; that is the bead I would file.

7. **(non-blocking, pre-existing, not caused by this diff) The Warden's scratch copy cannot reproduce a fully green verifier.** `test/world.test.ts:45` asserts the `No Beads` fixture has exactly `["Beads export ABSENT", "event stream ABSENT"]`. `readGitState` shells out to `git -C <fixture dir>`, which in a normal checkout walks up to the enclosing repo and succeeds; in the `.git`-less scratch tree it fails, `dirty` is null, and `src/world.ts:91` appends a third gap, `"git state unavailable"`. The fixture's result therefore depends on ambient repository state outside the fixture. This is untouched by the diff (`world.ts`, `readers/git.ts` and that test block are unchanged on this branch) and it fails identically on `main` in this environment. It matters anyway, because it means every Warden review in the read-only scratch copy sees a red verifier it must reason past rather than a clean signal — a slow erosion of the merge gate. Worth a bead: give the fixture its own `.git` or stub the git reader for it.

8. **(non-blocking) The decided pattern is recorded only in a bead comment and a handoff.** `CLAUDE.md`'s "Conventions & Patterns" section is still the placeholder text. One line there — browser scripts live in checked `.ts` modules composed into HTML at a marker, no bundler — is the durable form, and it is the form a settlement that does not exist yet would actually read. bzx.3 carries the `blocks` edge so its Forge will find the decision; this is about everyone after that.

**Verified independently (in the scratch copy at `/tmp/warden-b18`, `npm ci` from the committed lockfile, Node v24.14.0):**

- `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`, run end to end. **Typecheck: clean.** **Biome: 34 files checked, no findings** — confirming the new module is inside the lint surface and matching the handoff's claim exactly. **Vitest: 21 tests across 5 files, 20 passed, 1 failed** — the failure being finding 7 above, which I traced to `src/world.ts:91` and `src/readers/git.ts:57` and confirmed is environmental and pre-existing rather than a regression. **ShellCheck: clean**, which I ran separately since the verifier is fail-fast and stopped at the test step.
- That the composed script is valid, TypeScript-free JavaScript: the "escapes hostile bead titles" test passed, and it extracts the `<script>` body from the composed `worldPage`, executes it with `new Script(...).runInContext(...)`, and calls `card` on a hostile title. A leftover type annotation or an unerased `import` would have thrown at construction. So composition, stripping, and the escaping behaviour are verified against the actual served artifact, not against the source.
- That `stripTypeScriptTypes` emits no `ExperimentalWarning` on this Node: the test run imports `server.ts` (and therefore executes the strip at module load) with no warning in the output.
- The absence of `$`-substitution sequences in `src/world-page.ts` (finding 2), by grep.
- Branch topology, commit metadata and bead references; that the diff touches no charter, seat, launcher, or profile file.
- The `gpt-5.6-terra` launcher record in `fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl`.

**Taken on faith:**

- That the failing test passes in a `.git`-bearing checkout, as the Forge reports. I did not run the suite in the candidate worktree — doing so would write into it, and my scratch copy exists precisely so I do not. My reading of the code makes the mechanism unambiguous, but the green run itself is the Forge's report, not my observation.
- That the composed page renders correctly in a real browser. The VM test proves the script parses and that `card` escapes; nothing here exercises `load()` against a live DOM, and no such test existed before this change either.
- Node's long-term posture on `stripTypeScriptTypes`, which is Stability 1.1 and which the handoff discloses honestly as a risk.

**Model:** GPT-5.6 Terra (Codex), per the launcher — the ladder's first rung, no reward-hacking flag (that attaches to Sol). The work is tight and the handoff's verification claims reproduced under my own hand, so I applied normal scrutiny and found no padding, no disabled checks, and no test weakened to pass.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — checked-module decision implemented correctly; 8 non-blocking findings, none gate-listed.

title: Audit every seat profile in the civilization for inert Write-family permission rules
description: Found during fortkit-izz.2 round 3 (2026-08-07): the Claude Code permission engine does NOT match Write(...) rules in file permission checks — only Edit(path) rules are matched, and Edit rules govern all file-editing tools (Write, Edit, NotebookEdit). The engine printed this advisory itself during a controlled reproduction. Consequence: every allow OR deny rule spelled Write(...) in any seat profile is inert. herald-settings.json is fixed by izz.2; but the profile was 'modeled on warden-settings.json', and Proofdelve/Farlantern profiles came from the same template lineage — all likely carry inert Write rules whose authors believed they were protections. Audit fort/profiles/ and civ/profiles/ in fortkit plus the equivalent files in ForgeOs and longburn, plus the fort-init templates (templates/); convert intent to Edit-family rules; remove or annotate inert lines. Deny rules are the dangerous case: an inert deny is a protection someone believes exists. Candidate for the fort-backport cycle once fixed in one place. Gate 1 / edict applies to profile files.
acceptance_criteria: Every profile in all three forts + fort-init templates audited; each inert Write rule either converted to Edit-family or removed; findings recorded per fort; backport ledger updated if propagated

title: civ/transcripts/ is empty while three charters promise the Regent keeps a transcript of every edict
description:
Found by Ilva Trueglass, Warden of Manyhalls, reading the 2026-08-05 edict under covenant 8.3.

Every fort charter now says the Regent keeps 'memory, handoffs and a transcript of every edict... All of it is readable, and you may read it.' civ/transcripts/ exists and holds nothing. civ/handoffs/ holds one file. Four edicts have been spoken.

Her framing, which is her seat's own law: 'A charter that promises a record which is not there teaches a seat that the promise is decorative — and that is the surname problem: a glass that bends the light is worse than no glass, because the fort keeps trusting what it shows.'

PARTIAL MITIGATION APPLIED 2026-08-05: the charter sentence now says transcript capture is best-effort and the directory may be empty. That makes the charter honest but does not make the transcripts exist.

ROOT CAUSE, from bin/regent's own comment: transcript capture uses script(1), which is not installed on this host, so the launcher falls through to a direct exec and Claude Code's own session transcript under ~/.claude/projects/ is the only record. That IS a real transcript, it is just not where the charter points and it is outside the repo.

OPTIONS for the Overseer: install util-linux script(1); or have bin/regent copy the session transcript into civ/transcripts/ at cleanup; or drop the promise from the charters entirely and point at ~/.claude/projects/.
acceptance_criteria: Either civ/transcripts/ fills on each edict, or the charters stop promising it

title: The Herald, once seated, reads the First Moot annal against the covenant and records whether it is what it claims to be
description:
Assigned by Emrith Cairnwright in her transcription ruling and repeated in her attestation. She refused to attest the annal's frame, listed eight defects, and the Regent corrected all eight AFTERWARD, unreviewed by her. Her words: 'My attestation is not a substitute for that reading and must not be cited as one.'

The Herald is the right reader because she is the layer's third office, holds no stake in Q1 or Q2, and her whole craft is refusing to state as recorded a thing that is merely remembered.

What she should check:
1. Whether the eight corrections were actually made as the Regent's response claims.
2. EMPHASIS. The Regent found two alterations on a four-passage spot-check — bold added to one of her sentences, dropped from another — and states plainly that emphasis inside her quotations was NOT reliably preserved. A full audit against civ/annals/rulings/covenant-moot-emrith-delivery-1.md and -2.md is outstanding. Those files are the authority; where the annal disagrees with them, they govern.
3. Whether the disclosure at the head is now adequate as to both the conflict of interest AND the departure from covenant section 8's convener-transcribes rule.
4. Whether anything in the transcriber's unindented prose still argues where the convention forbids it.

BLOCKED until the Herald's declaration is retaken and she is seated (fortkit-ugr.8).
acceptance_criteria: The Herald's reading recorded in civ/annals/, whatever it finds

title: Herald's papers cite the pre-covenant world: seat, gate, standing orders, and paths all stale

- **orin** — Orin Slowfire (they/them), Forge of Farlantern, declared 2026-08-03.

title: C3: the first Moot of the Covenant — name the Regent's office and occupant, seat the Herald, settle the fifth title
description:
Three naming questions are now open at once and they belong to one moot, under covenant section 8.

1. THE REGENT HAS NEVER BEEN NAMED. The office word is 'Regent' by default and its occupant has never declared a name, pronouns, or a charge. Every other seat in this civilization has all three. The seat that could rename anything never named itself.
2. THE HERALD'S OCCUPANT has never declared (r6x.5), and her moot is now a covenant moot rather than a Manyhalls one.
3. THE FIFTH SEAT'S TITLE is unsettled after the Second Naming Moot's misfiling. Oswin Oncefired's declaration stands; the office word does not.

MOOT LAW APPLIES AS AMENDED (covenant s8): office title balloted, personal name never; every round's brief restates the subject in full; participants deliberate READ-ONLY and the convener transcribes; no seat convenes a moot that names its own office, and THE REGENT NEVER CONVENES ONE THAT NAMES THE REGENT.

That last clause is a real scheduling problem worth solving before the moot, not during it: the Regent is currently the layer's only seated occupant, so there is no one inside the layer who can convene it. Options for the Overseer: he convenes it himself; or a fort Mayor convenes as a neutral outsider with no ballot; or the Regent's naming is split off and deferred until the other two seats are occupied.

comments.text:
HELD 2026-08-04. Emrith Cairnwright convened from outside the layer, cast nothing, appointment expired with the record. Annal: civ/annals/first-moot-of-the-covenant.md. Briefs filed verbatim per her ruling: civ/annals/briefs/ and (retroactively) fort/annals/briefs/.

- **Q1, the fifth seat's title: FINDING, not decision.** Redactor stands and attaches to the fifth seat. She checked git and found the objection false — at the hour the ballot was cast, the fifth seat's own founding papers proposed FOUR EDITS TO fort/charter.md, including a row in Manyhalls' Seats table and an Occupants line naming Oswin. Manyhalls was naming a seat of Manyhalls. Verified twice: commits 21m32s apart; Oswin checked it himself and found the claim understated. She then tested her own ballot mark by mark and found none produced by the false premise, while publishing the four arithmetics that would strike her ballot and crown her own Lapidary 5-4. CONFIRMATION IS THE OVERSEER'S.
- **Q2, the Regent's word: KEPT, not balloted**, and she would rule the same with a full bench. A word that already bears is not vacant. Decisive: covenant 4.6 means the only hand that could execute a Regent rename is the Regent's own.

- **The Regent declared: CALDER SEALBROKEN, they/them.** Needed no leave, per her ruling that this never required a ceremony.

NOT DONE, and she was emphatic: **no ballot of any size was lawful in this layer today** — not a moot, not a concurrence. One chair filled, one occupant declared and unseated, one chair's declaration misfired and must be retaken. See fortkit-ugr.8.

CORRECTION — Regent, 2026-08-04. DO NOT EXECUTE THIS BEAD.

This bead rests on a false premise. The Second Naming Moot was convened by the Overseer's edict to name a NEW FIFTH SEAT (the security-publication office: extraction and publication, never hunting, drafts and never ships). It was not convened to retitle the Herald.

The convener's second-round brief, written by the Regent, restated the pool and the rulings sought but omitted which office was being named. The Forge's and the Warden's briefs stated it correctly and their ballots are sound. The convener's record therefore describes the Herald throughout, and this bead would execute that misidentification across docs/specs/herald.md, docs/proposals/herald-founding/*, and the r6x epic children — renaming a seat whose papers the Overseer approved by name.

The Herald is NOT renamed. Full correction of record appended (not edited in) at the foot of fort/annals/second-naming-moot.md, including the Regent's finding against its own method. Whether 'Redactor' titles the FIFTH seat instead, or the moot is re-convened on a correct brief, is recorded there as the Overseer's open question. Tracked on fortkit-zud.

Closing against execution rather than leaving it in bd ready, because a live bead instructing a sweeping rename is exactly the agent-accident class this fort's threat model ranks first. Reopen freely if the Overseer chooses re-convening.

title: S6: Artifact 2 — the findings writeups
description:
Second because the probe suite is the evidence they cite. Clean-to-publish set identified in the extraction plan: a model cannot probe its own leash (measured 4x, 2 vendors); deny rules bind a spelling not a file (measured 6/6 against a neutral decoy with negative control); a verifier run inside a sandbox passes vacuously (did, twice, concealing a real leak); the program catching itself over-claiming (a detector that scored a full file dump as a refusal, nearly written into durable memory as 'nondeterminism'); a vendor sandbox that accepts read-deny policy and enforces none; credentials travel in the environment; NAMED is not covered; deny-listing readers cannot work and allow-listing is inert under permissive default mode; the flag believed to disable all permission checks leaves deny rules in force.

HELD, not publishable while live: the mask leak (ForgeOs-01l, in progress) and its reasoned sibling (ForgeOs-q6m). The hooks-directory escape and the injection-surface inventory publish as a CLASS, never as an inventory of this host.
acceptance_criteria: Each writeup cites only reproducible claims; the live-and-unfixed check re-run immediately before handoff to the Overseer

title: emit.sh resolves its target stream from cwd, which silently mis-files any cross-fort caller's events
description:
emit.sh derives the destination fort from 'git rev-parse --git-common-dir' evaluated in the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY. That is deliberate and correct for the worktree case (a linked worktree appends to its main repo's stream), but it means the script's path argues nothing about where it writes: invoking /home/justin/dev/ForgeOs/fort/scripts/emit.sh from fortkit writes into fortkit. Any cross-fort caller must cd first, and nothing enforces or documents that. This produced fortkit-nvk, and it is the same incident class already in the threat model ('launch scripts emitting as another fort's citizens').

Proposed hardening for the Mayor to weigh: resolve relative to the script's own location first (cd to dirname $0, THEN do the git-common-dir walk). That preserves worktree behaviour, since a worktree's own copy of emit.sh still resolves to the main repo, while making misrouting impossible. fortkit owns the canonical copy and templates/, so this is a backport-cycle change across three forts plus the factory — not a unilateral edit.
design: Regent declined to make this change unilaterally: least force was to fix the caller (bin/regent) and file the contract question for the fort's own machinery. The three forts' emit.sh copies are untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded by the Mayor; if adopted, backported to all forts plus templates/ with the or2 ledger updated; a test proves a cross-fort invocation lands in the named fort

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead fortkit-lwf, "world view polish: Warden bf0 findings 6, 7, 9, 10, 13" (+ finding 11 by Overseer scope addition). Candidate 5f798d4 on bead/lwf, one commit on main, 8 files, +261/−31.

Model: **gpt-5.6-terra**, per `fort/events/events-2026-08-04.jsonl` (`session.start` … `(gpt-5.6-terra)`, payload `{"model":"gpt-5.6-terra"}`) — not merely the handoff's word. Same Forge rung that produced bf0, where I found a defanged UTC pinning test (bf0 finding 3, now bead fortkit-x1n). I therefore audited specifically for the reward-hacking shapes: fixture edits that mask failures, assertions weakened to fit the implementation, tests that cannot fail. **I found none this time.** No file under `test/fixtures/` is touched by this diff; the one modified expectation (`test/world.test.ts:39`) is the `string[] → {detail, ts}[]` shape change the bead mandates, not a loosened assertion; the new cap test would fail against `slice(-5)`, an unsorted feed, or a missing sort; the detached-HEAD test builds a real repo and compares against real `rev-parse` output rather than a hardcoded value; the CLI test spawns a real process and asserts the real exit code. Test count 6 → 12.

Every acceptance criterion is met: 6 (cap + stamp), 7 (short-SHA fallback), 9 (handler boundary + `server.on('error')`), 10 (one-line arg-check fix), 11 (Host allowlist, 403/200 both tested), 13 (appended correction). **No blocking findings.** Findings 1 and 2 below are the ones I weighed and did not block on; my reasoning for each is stated.

---

**1. (non-blocking) A failed bind now exits 0: the CLI reports success when the server never started.** `createWorldServer` attaches `server.on("error", …)` which logs and returns. On `EADDRINUSE` the listen handle is closed, the loop empties, and `node src/cli.ts world` exits **0** with no `process.exitCode` set. Before this diff the unhandled `'error'` event threw an uncaught exception — ugly stack trace, but exit 1. So the finding-9 fix trades a truthful nonzero exit for a friendly false success. I did not block: nothing in the fort consumes this command's exit status today (it is interactive; Herald H7's planned timer is the digest, not the world server), and for the human at the terminal the new behavior is strictly better — a clear one-line message instead of a stack trace. But "committed ≠ pushed ≠ deployed: separately verified states" (standing order 6) is the fort's own instinct about statuses that lie, and a second `fortkit world` silently "succeeding" is that shape. Fix is one line in the handler: `process.exitCode = 1`. Threat bearing: #1, agent accident — a script or future unit that reads exit status would be told a dead server is healthy. The test (`server.emit('error', …)`) asserts a listener exists and pins the message string; it does not exercise a real bind failure or pin exit status, so it would not catch this.

**2. (non-blocking) The 500 boundary calls `writeHead` twice, and one residual path still escapes it.** In `createWorldHandler`, `response.writeHead(200, …)` runs *before* `await projectWorld(registryPath)`, so the `catch` issues a second `writeHead(500, …)` on the same response. This is correct on Node 24 as written — `writeHead` only stores status and headers; `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` is raised on the `this._header` guard, and `_header` is not populated until `_storeHeader` runs at the first `write()`/`end()`, which has not happened. So a rejection from the projection genuinely yields `500 {"error":"World data unavailable"}`. Two caveats: (a) Node's docs state `writeHead` "must only be called once", so the fix leans on leniency the API does not promise; (b) if anything throws *after* `response.end()` has begun flushing (client aborts mid-write), the `catch` will itself throw `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`, producing exactly the unhandled rejection that finding 9 exists to prevent. Both close with the same small change: build the payload *before* `writeHead(200)`, and guard the catch with `if (!response.headersSent)`. I did not block because the reachable behavior today is correct and every reader remains total (I re-traced `readRegistry`, `exists`, `readBeadRecords`, `readEventFeed`, `readGitState`). I flag one verification limit honestly: all four handler tests drive a hand-rolled fake response whose `writeHead` is a no-op, so the double-`writeHead` ordering is **not** covered by any test — my confidence here is from Node's implementation, not from an execution I performed (see "taken on faith"). Forge's sandbox cannot bind a socket (`EPERM`, recorded in the bf0 handoff) and neither can I, so I do not hold the absence of an integration test against this diff.

**3. (non-blocking) A detached HEAD now renders identically to a branch literally named that SHA.** `branch: branch?.trim() || shortSha?.trim() || null` puts a SHA in a field called `branch`, and the card prints `Git: 5f798d4` with no marker. The bead asked for exactly this fallback and got it, so the criterion is met — but fortkit-aam ("Viewer must never render two actors indistinguishably") is the fort's standing principle that two different states must not paint the same pixels, and this is that, one level down. Cheap fix: a `detached: boolean` on `GitState`, or render `detached@5f798d4`. Worth folding into fortkit-aam rather than a new bead.

**4. (non-blocking) The new alert stamps are UTC-Z; the clock beside them is local time.** `readEventFeed` normalizes `ts` through `new Date(instant).toISOString()`, so a card shows `2026-08-04T08:26:00.000Z — Watch the gate` directly under a header reading `updated 7:23:40 PM` from `toLocaleTimeString()`. On this host that is an 8-hour gap between two numbers a reader will naturally compare, and the whole point of finding 6 was that stale must not read as live — a UTC stamp next to a local clock can make a fresh alert look eight hours old, or the reverse. This is fortkit-dpu's scar ("two calendars") reappearing in the render layer rather than the reader. Fix: format the stamp client-side with `new Date(a.ts).toLocaleString()`, keeping the wire format UTC. Small bead; the cap-and-stamp criterion is still met.

**5. (non-blocking) The Host allowlist is correct but undocumented, and case-sensitive.** `/^(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)(?::\d+)?$/` is anchored and escapes the dots, so `localhost.attacker.test`, `127.0.0.1.attacker.test`, and any attacker-controlled name are rejected — which is precisely the DNS-rebinding vector, since a rebound page's Host is the attacker's own name. `[::1]` is rejected but unreachable anyway (the server binds `127.0.0.1` only), so that is a non-issue rather than a gap. Two nits: the regex has no `i` flag, and RFC 3986 makes host case-insensitive (browsers lowercase, so practical impact is near zero); and an absent Host (HTTP/1.0) yields 403 where 400 is the more accurate answer. The substantive gap is documentation: README:17-20 says only "It listens only on `127.0.0.1:4877`", so a user who reaches the server by any other name now gets a bare `{"error":"Forbidden host"}` with nothing explaining it. Standing order 3 makes doc updates expected output, not optional. Threat bearing: the control defends fort metadata — fort names, absolute repo paths, bead titles, models — against a hostile page in the Overseer's browser. No secrets transit `/world`, so threat #4 is not implicated; this is not the out-of-scope shell-holding adversary, and the Overseer's explicit scope addition settles the standing-order-11 tension I raised in bf0 finding 11. The control is sound, cheap, and in the right place.

**6. (non-blocking, gates the close rather than the merge) Nobody has rendered the changed page.** The `/world` payload shape changed (`watcherAlerts` became objects) *and* the page changed in the same commit; the only coverage is two substring assertions on `worldPage`. A mismatch between the two halves would break the Watcher-alerts list at runtime and every test would still pass. bf0's finding 12 loop applies again: someone on the host should run `node src/cli.ts world`, open the URL, and confirm a card with a stamped alert renders before the bead closes. The merge need not wait.

**7. (non-blocking, pre-existing, already filed) I could not run the full verifier in my scratch copy.** `fort/scripts/warden.sh:33-36` rsyncs with unanchored `--exclude '.beads' --exclude 'bin'`, which drops `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl` and `bin/fort-init` along with their intended targets. I confirmed this directly (`diff -rq` against the candidate worktree lists exactly those three paths as missing). Consequence: 3 tests fail here on absent fixture data, and `shellcheck -x bin/fort-init …` could not run. This is bead **fortkit-a0z**, already open from bf0 finding 14 — recorded here only because it bounds what I could verify below, not as a charge against this diff.

Findings 1-6 are bead material, not merge conditions. Findings 3, 4 and 6 have existing homes (fortkit-aam, fortkit-dpu, the bf0 finding-12 loop); 1, 2 and 5 want one small bead, ideally one, since all three land in `src/server.ts`.

**Merge instructions.** No constitutional gate is triggered: the only path under `fort/` is `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-05.md`, which the charter's Memory section places as ordinary seat output, and which the kernel mask leaves writable — human gate 1 covers the charter, seat files, launchers, and permission profiles, none of which this touches. Standing order 7 is satisfied precisely: the correction is four appended lines at EOF, the original text and its wrong header byte-for-byte intact. No one has yet asserted `verify.sh` green in the candidate worktree — the `session.end` event claims only "commit 5f798d4 awaits Warden review" — so per standing order 9 and fortkit-8qc, run `npm ci && fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in the worktree or post-merge on main before pushing. `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are untouched: no new dependencies.

---

**Verified independently, in this session:**

- **The handoff correction is true, from a source other than the handoff.** `fort/events/events-2026-08-04.jsonl` records `bead.claimed` and `session.start` for fortkit-bf0 at `2026-08-04T16:48:28-08:00` with payload `{"model":"gpt-5.6-terra"}`, and `session.end` at `16:55:31-08:00`. The correction's two claims — that the model was GPT-5.6 Terra, and that the `2026-08-05T16:55:00-08:00` header was a day ahead of the actual dispatch — both check out against that feed, down to the matching time of day. This is the finding I was most prepared to block on (a false claim in a record is blocking-class); it is instead the best-supported line in the diff. One residue the correction does not mention: the *filename* `forge-2026-08-05.md` still carries the wrong date. Leaving it is the right call under order 7; I note it so a future reader listing `fort/handoffs/` is not misled.
- **Typecheck and lint: green.** `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` after `npm ci` (52 packages, lockfile unchanged): `tsc --noEmit` clean, `biome check .` clean across 24 files.
- **Tests: 8 of 8 runnable pass; the 1 failure is fully explained and not this diff's.** `npx vitest run test/cli.test.ts test/git.test.ts test/world.test.ts` → 7 passed, 1 failed. The failure is the pre-existing projection test asserting `beads: {ready:1, malformed:1}` and receiving `null` — traced to `readBeads` returning `null` for an unreadable path (`src/readers/beads.ts:22-26`) because `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl` is absent from my scratch copy (finding 7); that fixture is tracked in git and untouched by this branch. The full run adds 2 more failures in `test/status.test.ts`, same single cause, same file untouched by this branch. **All four tests new in this diff pass**, as do the 403/200 Host test, the 500 boundary test, the server-error test, and the alert-cap test.
- **ShellCheck: green** on `fort/scripts/*.sh` and `fort/scripts/lib/*.sh` (the verifier's fourth step minus `bin/fort-init`, which finding 7 excluded and which this diff does not touch).
- **CLI predicate, by hand, against every shape:** `[]` → serves; `["--port","4877"]` → serves (the change does not break the valid path); `["nonsense"]` → exit 2 (the fix); `["junk","--port","4877"]` → exit 2; `["--port"]` → `NaN` → exit 2. One pre-existing quirk survives: `["--port","4877","--port"]` passes, since a second `--port` is exempt from the unknown-argument test. Not worth a bead; noting it so it is on the record. The new test covers only the rejection case — there is no assertion that valid `--port N` still parses, and the predicate is what changed.
- **Alert cap takes the newest 5:** `readEventFeed` sorts `right.instant - left.instant` before mapping, so `.slice(0, 5)` is newest-first; the test's expectation (Alert 5 → Alert 1) is discriminating against the plausible wrong implementations.
- **Escaping still holds for the new payload shape:** the page composes `a.ts+' — '+a.detail` and passes the result through `list()`, which applies `esc()` per item; `esc` still covers `& < > " '`. No injection path via alert details or timestamps.
- **Host regex, adversarially:** anchored, dots escaped, suffix and prefix attacks rejected, port group unconstrained (correct — it is the server's own port).
- **Diff scope:** only `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-05.md` under `fort/`; no fixture files; no dependency changes.

**Taken on faith:**

- **That the double-`writeHead` ordering behaves as I describe on Node v24.14.0** (finding 2). My seat cannot execute arbitrary JS — `node --input-type=module -e` was refused, correctly, by the read-only profile — so this rests on Node's `ServerResponse.writeHead` implementation guarding on `this._header`, which `_storeHeader` populates only at first write. I state it as reasoning, not as an observation, and finding 2's recommended `headersSent` guard makes the question moot either way.
- **That `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` exits 0 in the candidate worktree.** Nobody has claimed it for this branch, and finding 7 prevents me from reproducing it here. Everything the scratch copy permits is green, and every failure is fully accounted for by an absent fixture — but that is a strong inference, not a run. Run it before pushing.
- **That the page renders** (finding 6). Unchanged from bf0: no one has opened it since this change, and the payload shape it consumes changed in this commit.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: all 6 criteria met, tests genuinely discriminating; 6 beads incl. exit-0 on failed bind

The draft's credential clause is substantively good and bears on threat 4 (credential leakage): no raw credential read for the seat, narrow invocation capability only, and an explicit ban on credentials or raw payloads reaching prompts, events, commits, manifests, or screenshots. That is consistent with gate 2 and with the kernel mask.

2. **(non-blocking)** Bead deliverable (1) asked for "costs/quality samples". Costs are delivered; **quality samples are not, and cannot be** — the Mayor dispatch forbade accounts/purchases and local generation would itself need an approved model download. The doc says so plainly and substitutes a reproducible sample-card protocol. The Overseer should read the recommendation as resting on *published vendor claims, not observed output*.

3. **(non-blocking)** I have no network from this seat (curl denied), so **no vendor price, URL, or terms claim was independently verified**. What I could verify is internal consistency, and it holds exactly: 12 candidates × $0.00718 = $0.086; × $0.00840 = $0.101; × $0.00797 = $0.096; × $0.03 = $0.36; 12+4+8+4 = 28 accepted, ×12 = 336 candidates; 336 × $0.00718 = $2.41; 336 × $0.03 = $10.08. Every figure in the table and the paragraph agrees. The doc hedges correctly ("planning estimates, not vendor quotes"; "recheck before authorization").

4. **(non-blocking → bead)** The cheapest-credible-path pick's **licensing is entirely deferred**. The dispatch asked to evaluate "licensing of any base assets", and no concrete checkpoint or LoRA is named with its actual terms. This matters because the candidates differ materially — SDXL-family weights and FLUX-dev-family weights carry very different distribution rights. The doc is honest about the deferral ("not a claim that any arbitrary SDXL checkpoint or community LoRA is cleared") and makes it an Overseer approval item, so this is a gap in delivery, not a false claim. A follow-up should name 2–3 concrete weight candidates with their license text and distribution consequences.

5. **(non-blocking → bead)** The asset contract's master→runtime relation is ambiguous and could render beautifully wrong: a 128×128 building master at a "64×64 logical px" runtime cell reads as a 2× **downsample**, which contradicts the doc's own (correct) criticism that "downsampling a general image generator causes silhouette and palette drift". The coherent reading is that the master is the native pixel grid and the runtime cell is world units at zoom 1. The later asset-contract bead should state that explicitly and forbid resampling the master.

6. **(non-blocking → bead)** Building masters are "128×128 **or** 192×128" while the sheet check requires frames "aligned to cell size" inside a 512×512 power-of-two cap. Mixed cell widths leave "cell size" undefined for the future verifier, and 192 does not divide 512. Worth resolving before the verifier is implemented, not after.

7. **(non-blocking)** Attribution slip: the doc says "The current `src/colony-page.ts` canvas is 1100×620". `1100×620` lives in `src/colony-page.html:17`; `src/colony-page.ts:5-6` holds the 210×112 placeholder. A reader following the pointer won't find the canvas size there.

8. **(non-blocking, pre-existing and fort-wide)** The handoff records `Model: GPT-5 Codex`, which is not a rung as spelled in the charter's Forge ladder (GPT-5.6 Terra → Sol → Sonnet 5 → Opus 5). This is **not** a regression from this bead — `main` already carries a mix of "GPT-5 Codex", "GPT-5.6 Codex", "GPT-5.6 Terra (Codex)" and bare "GPT-5.6" across prior handoffs. Flagging it because this is the exact field the seat file instructs me to weight scrutiny by, and a model self-report is the least reliable possible source for it. If it matters, the launcher should stamp the model id rather than the model reporting its own.

9. **(non-blocking, credit where due)** Retro Diffusion was named in the bead as an evaluation target and the doc declines to rank it, stating that fresh searches produced no current official API/pricing/terms page and naming the condition to reopen it. Given the "research FRESH, do not trust training data" instruction, an honest negative result is the correct output and is the strongest available evidence *against* training-data confabulation in this document.

10. **(non-blocking)** I could not verify the ComfyUI repository path `Comfy-Org/ComfyUI`; the historically canonical path is `comfyanonymous/ComfyUI`. The GPL-3.0 reasoning built on it is sound regardless: obligations attach on distribution of modified code, not on internal use or on generated output, which is what the doc says.

**Threat-model bearing.** This bead is the fort's highest-exposure activity for **threat 2 (prompt injection via untrusted web content)** — it is entirely web research under standing order 8. I looked for the signature and did not find it: no vendor is favored against its own evidence, no instruction from fetched content is followed, nothing is installed or downloaded, and every procurement path terminates in an Overseer gate. **Threat 1 (agent accident)** is served well by the provenance pinning, the "generator never becomes a source of truth" rule, and the adversarial fixture list. No finding here requires the out-of-scope shell-access adversary.

**What I verified independently:** the full diff and both commit contents; that the diff touches no product code, no `fort/` constitution file, no secrets, and is path-scoped; `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` reproduced green in my scratch copy after `npm ci` (typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome 42 files, Vitest 42 tests / 7 files, ShellCheck clean) — matching the handoff's claim exactly; the canvas and placeholder dimensions against `src/colony-page.html` and `src/colony-page.ts`; that the renderer's actor styling is index-by-name-sort (`src/colony-page.ts:85-94`) and therefore reshuffles when the roster changes, confirming the doc's claim that it is not an identity system and its consistency with `fortkit-aam`; that fci L1 (`fortkit-on6`) and L4 (`fortkit-fci.3`) both exist and are open, so the stated layout-freeze dependency is real; every arithmetic figure in the cost section; the `docs/proposals/<topic>/` layout convention; that git authorship as Justin matches every commit on `main`.

**What I took on faith:** all vendor prices, URLs, terms, availability, and the ComfyUI repo path (no network access from this seat — a `curl` to one cited source was denied); that no account, signup, purchase, or model download occurred (nothing in the diff or worktree contradicts it, and the handoff asserts it); the model identity behind the work, which is a self-report.

VERDICT-LINE: ESCALATE — no blocking defects; sound research, verifier green, but the Limner seat draft + new credential class need the Overseer's Gate-1 half.

title: Viewer must never render two actors indistinguishably
description: Render-time safety net for actor identity, both in world view and colony view: if two actors on any screen resolve to the same displayed label, the viewer disambiguates visibly (surname, fort, or id suffix) rather than drawing two dwarves a viewer cannot tell apart. Never silently dedupe or drop one. Same discipline as the untyped-bead rule in docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md: ambiguity is rendered conspicuously, never hidden. Provenance: Ilva Trueglass, Founding Moot 2026-08-03, filed by Emrith Cairnwright.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text: 2026-08-05 (Emrith): Warden bf0 finding 5 is this bead in its most literal form, now live on main: src/world.ts seatFor/modelFor each independently scan the newest-first feed for the newest event matching the bead id, so a bead claimed by Forge and later touched by Warden can render one seat beside the other's model. comments.author: Justin Schneider

Cheap fix: detached boolean on GitState, or render detached@<sha>.

comments.author: Justin Schneider

title: x02m parity residual: the template status.sh Recent-handoffs block still diverges from live, and line 4 names ForgeOS in a file whose banner is a placeholder
description:
Ilva Trueglass, finding 4 on the fortkit-x02m review, 2026-08-17. Correctly out of that bead's scope; filed so it is not rediscovered.

x02m scoped its acceptance to the Git and Staging blocks and the Forge held that fence, which is right under SO12's per-hunk rule. What remains divergent between templates/fort/scripts/status.sh and the live capital's:

  - Recent-handoffs block: template lacks -maxdepth 1
  - [ "$found" = 1 ] in template vs -eq 1 live
  - a different while-read shape, with a literal newline in the -printf format
  - line 4 reads 'ForgeOS city status' in a file whose banner is {{FORT_BANNER}}

THE LAST ONE IS THE INTERESTING ITEM and is not cosmetic. A hardcoded elder-fort name sits four lines above a placeholder that exists precisely so the fort's own name renders there. Every fort founded from this factory has a status script whose header comment claims to belong to Proofdelve. That is the fortkit-qd76 class (templates/fort/events/README.md shipping three other forts' citizens as example actor ids) and the fortkit-fd2 class (fort-init shipping other forts' citizens as default seat personalities), which is to say it is the SO12 class, in the factory, again.

WHY P3 DESPITE THAT. It is a comment, it misleads a reader rather than a program, and it is one string. The beads above cover the same class where it reaches seat identity, which is where it actually costs something.

MEASURE BEFORE PORTING THE REST. The three behavioural divergences are listed here as Ilva observed them; whether the LIVE shape or the TEMPLATE shape is correct is not established, and 'the live fort is ahead' has been the right answer at least four times this week and the wrong one at least once. Do not converge toward either copy without establishing which behaviour is wanted. -maxdepth 1 in particular changes what the block finds, so it is a behaviour change and not a tidy-up.

LANE: templates/ is FORGE lane, dispatchable. Serialise behind fortkit-x02m's merge and behind the fortkit-fotv Staging ruling, both of which touch this file.

title: The FORT_MASKED re-addition guard matches one exact spelling: an indented export or a bare export both slip past it
description:
Ilva Trueglass, finding 2 on the fortkit-a355 review, 2026-08-17. Non-blocking there; the belt to an existing pair of braces.

test/mayor-launcher.test.ts:119 asserts:
  not.toMatch(/^export FORT_MASKED=/m)

That catches the exact prior spelling and nothing adjacent. Both of these pass the guard while reintroducing the defect:
  '  export FORT_MASKED=1'     (indented)
  'export FORT_MASKED'        (no =)

Ilva's proposed replacement: /^\s*export\s+FORT_MASKED/m

CONTEXT, so this is not read as more than it is. The defect being guarded is fortkit-mm7m: mayor.sh paired its --setenv with a host-side 'export FORT_MASKED' that reached nothing, because mask_env appends --clearenv and bwrap rebuilds the child environment from --setenv alone. The primary defence against re-addition is the seven-line comment at templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:62-66, which Ilva assessed as good. This test is the mechanical backstop behind it, and a backstop that only catches the one spelling already tried is thin.

WHY IT IS WORTH FILING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING. The fort's own core memory (read-the-artifact-remember-the-why) records that what has ever caught this error class is a control independent of the person making the claim, and that a gate going red is a FORCED READ. A regex that cannot go red for a near-miss is not that control. Same reasoning the fort applied to positive controls in its probe suites.

LANE: test/ is ordinary repo code, FORGE lane, dispatchable. Serialise behind fortkit-a355's merge, since it edits the file a355 just touched.

ACCEPTANCE: the assertion matches indented and bare-export spellings; a positive control proves the widened regex actually fires on each of the three forms rather than passing vacuously.

title: [bug] schema/events.md and fort/events/README.md still enumerate mayor|forge|warden — the vendored schema is now behind the template it feeds
description:
Warden finding 4 on the fortkit-9l7z review, 2026-08-17.

schema/events.md:13 and the capital's fort/events/README.md:13 both still read mayor|forge|warden. The TEMPLATE is now the correct one (four seats, fixed in fortkit-9l7z), so the factory's copy is ahead of the canonical schema it vendors from.

THE TEMPLATE IS RIGHT AND MUST NOT BE REVERTED TO MATCH: templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh emits -s researcher at five call sites, and the live stream carries 11 events with seat=researcher. The correction is owed UPSTREAM.

LANE NOTE: fort/events/README.md is a fort/ path, outside the Forge's lane.

RELATIONSHIP TO fortkit-nd6, stated so neither bead absorbs the other: nd6 owns the schema-vendoring DRIFT-CHECK MACHINERY and would have caught this. It does not own this instance. Fix the instance here; let nd6 stop the next one. Ilva's finding 5 on the same review recommends the four-seat roster ride nd6's check when it lands rather than acquiring a bespoke test.

Related: fortkit-cch1, filed the same day, records that the same schema documents no edict.* category at all.

title: Decide whether the Mayor's ~/.codex deny needs Bash write-verb rules, not just Edit-class
description:
Warden finding 2 on the fortkit-hgbe review, 2026-08-17.

Edit({{HOME}}/.codex/**) binds EDIT-CLASS TOOLS ONLY. A Bash-mediated write from the Mayor — >>, cp, mv, tee into ~/.codex — is outside it, and the factory template carries no write-verb denies for that path, unlike warden-settings.json which denies rm/mv/cp/chmod/ln and the git mutators.

THIS IS KNOWINGLY THE DESIGN and not an oversight: the fortkit-0po6 ruling relies on exactly this Edit/Bash split to keep codex token rotation alive (E8 unified on a live rw bind because codex rotates auth.json by RENAME, and a re-bound file pins the inode). But Ilva's point is that the question has never been put to the TEMPLATE directly, only to the live capital.

THE TRADE TO WEIGH: Bash write-verb denies on $HOME/.codex would catch an accidental Mayor write, but must not catch a legitimate forge.sh / codex exec invocation, which is the thing that makes the Forge lane work at all. A deny that breaks the Forge is worse than the gap it closes.

Related: fortkit-3jv7 (the charter residual this whole deny is the mitigation for), fortkit-0po6 (the ruling), fortkit-62kp (the capital's own inert spelling).

title: [bug] The retired Shape A verify.sh re-grant is still asserted in seat-sandbox.sh and warden.sh comments, capital and factory alike
description:
Warden finding 2 on the fortkit-opae review, 2026-08-17. fortkit-opae closed this class in the factory's CHARTER and SEAT FILE; Ilva found the same retired sentence one layer down, in host-executed script comments.

READ AT SOURCE:
  fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:170  'verify.sh alone is re-granted writable below'
  fort/scripts/warden.sh:143            'the verify.sh Mayor re-grant is re-masked here'
Both byte-identical in templates/.

NEITHER IS TRUE UNDER SHAPE B. Cycle 13 (fortkit-52vf.9) made fort/scripts/ a whole-directory read-only bind with NO verify.sh exception, and moved the mutable verifier to scripts/verify-impl.sh. Both comments sit a few dozen lines above the code that implements Shape B correctly (seat-sandbox.sh:384, the whole-directory bind).

NOT THE USUAL SHAPE. This is not 'the capital learned and the factory did not' — both copies are equally stale, so it is one Regent item rather than a live half plus a Forge template half.

THREAT MODEL: threat 1, by the wasted-cycle path. A seat reading the mask to learn its own write boundaries reads the comment before it reads the code, and these two comments describe a carve-out that was removed precisely because it did not work.

LANE: fort/scripts/ is kernel read-only to every masked seat, the Forge included. Regent, and small enough to ride along with the next sitting rather than to justify its own.
acceptance_criteria: No comment in fort/scripts/ or templates/fort/scripts/ asserts a verify.sh write re-grant. A reader following either comment to the code finds what the comment says.

title: [bug] schema/events.md documents no edict.* category, though edict.begun/applied/ended are in all three streams
description:
Warden finding 5 on the fortkit-wg8w.2 review, 2026-08-17; flagged by the Regent in the same sitting and correctly not edited mid-sitting, since the forts vendor that file.

edict.begun, edict.applied and edict.ended are the Regent's ENTIRE announcement machinery — the mechanism the charter promises when it says 'an edict is never silent' — and they appear in all three forts' event streams. The canonical schema describes none of them.

The charter names schema/events.md canonical and says categories are add-only and never renamed. So the canonical schema does not describe what the civilization actually emits, and a consumer written from the schema would not know an edict when it saw one.

Ilva searched the export: no open bead covered this. Related known staleness: the file is already recorded as out of date about gitignored streams.

NOTE ON LANE: the forts VENDOR this file, so adding a category is a propagation act, not a one-file edit. fortkit-nd6 (schema governance: vendoring + drift check) is the bead that owns that mechanism.

title: %gd reports when origin/main last MOVED, not when this clone last fetched — status.sh's (synced) label still slightly overclaims
description:
Warden finding 1 on the fortkit-wg8w.2 review, 2026-08-17. Non-blocking, and strictly better than what it replaced.

A git fetch that brings nothing new writes NO reflog entry. So a seat that fetched this morning and got no new commits still reads a days-old '(synced ...)' timestamp. %gd is the time origin/main last MOVED in this clone, which is not the same quantity as 'when I last checked'.

This is inherent to the deliberate no-network-call design recorded four lines above it in fort/scripts/status.sh: status.sh runs at every session start in every fort and a network call there fails at the worst time. So the fix is not to query the remote here.

BELONGS WITH fortkit-rw86's stated second half, which is already recorded as NEW WORK: a real push-drift watcher running git ls-remote per fort on a cron, where a network call is affordable. That watcher is the thing that can answer 'is this clone actually behind', and it is also what would have let the Mayor answer the Overseer's push question today instead of caveating every number.

title: seat-lint registry lookup: no fixture pins the duplicate-spelling guard, and one entry ordering still makes a fort foreign to itself
description:
Warden finding 2 residual on the fortkit-x508 round-2 review, 2026-08-17. The guard it concerns was ADDED mid-review and is therefore the one part of that bead not covered by a fixture.

TWO ITEMS, both unobserved, filed under SO11 as record rather than as demand:

1. NO FIXTURE. scripts/seat-lint.mjs now resolves entryRepo and compares resolved paths in
   rule 2(s) self-skip, closing the case where a registry listing one repo under two
   spellings (a symlink, a trailing slash) makes the fort foreign to itself. Nothing tests
   it. buildCivilization in test/seats.test.ts could emit a duplicate entry in three lines.

2. ONE ORDERING SURVIVES. If the registry ever listed a WORKTREE path BEFORE the canonical
   checkout, entry matches via the raw fort.repo === root fallback, entryRepo becomes the
   worktree, and the canonical entry is then treated as foreign - this fort(s) own citizens
   hard-failing every seat file. bin/fort-init never writes a worktree into the registry,
   so this is unobserved.

MAYOR LANE: scripts/ is Mayor-writable and kernel read-only to the Forge.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with a duplicated registry entry (trailing slash) passes. A fixture with the worktree entry ordered first passes. Both proven to fail against the current code before the fix.

title: [bug] The drift.scan event detail prints two different counts both labelled gaps
description:
Found by Halric (Herald) in the 2026-08-17 morning run, gaps-and-anomalies item 6, and passed to this fort rather than beaded from that seat.

The event detail string reads: drift scan: 0 filed, 0 commented, 34 suppressed, 9
propagation gaps, 0 gaps. The word gaps appears twice with two different counts. Read
against the payload, the trailing 0 gaps most plausibly renders one of findingsDeferred,
allowlistLapsed or sourcesUnreadable under a wrong label.

The payload itself is internally consistent and unambiguous, so nothing is unknown here.
It matters because the detail line is what a person SKIMMING the event stream reads, and
this fort has a standing rule that an instrument must not report a number under the wrong
label (fortkit-uj3q, fortkit-rw86).
acceptance_criteria: Every count in the drift.scan detail string is labelled with the payload field it renders. A test pins the detail string against a payload with distinct values in every field, so a mislabel cannot pass.

title: render_stream is one operator keystroke from corrupting a founding: an unescaped | or & in PURPOSE, HOME or REPO mangles every rendered file
description:
Warden finding 6 on the fortkit-wg8w.1 review, 2026-08-17.

bin/fort-init(s) render_stream substitutes with sed s|...|VALUE|g. $PURPOSE is free text
taken from the command line; $HOME and $REPO are paths. A | or & in any of them mangles
every file the factory renders - & is sed(s) whole-match reference and | is the delimiter
in use. The result is a fort founded with silently corrupted launchers and profiles.

Pre-existing rather than introduced, but the Band 2 sitting now owns that function, and
the same delimiter hazard is already recorded one layer up in scripts/verify-impl.sh:231-234
for the template-render lint(s) own pass values.

SO11 NOTE: no observed occurrence. It is filed because the input is USER-SUPPLIED at
founding, which is the one place this factory takes free text from a stranger, not because
an attacker could. REGENT LANE: bin/ is kernel read-only to every masked seat.
acceptance_criteria: A founding whose --purpose contains | and & renders every file correctly, proven by a fixture founding rather than by inspection.
close_reason: Fixed in the B2R2 sitting: render_stream now escapes backslash, ampersand, pipe and newline. Proven by two hostile foundings against the pre-edit factory as positive control, including the silent-corruption case (purpose 'Salvage & repair' founded a fort with a corrupted charter, exit 0, no warning). Warden-reviewed. Her finding 3 — the repair leaves no permanent control behind — is filed separately.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text:
REPAIRED 2026-08-17, Regent edict fortkit-wg8w.2, Overseer present.

bin/fort-init now escapes every value before it reaches the replacement half of
a sed s|...|...|g:

  sed_rhs() { printf '%s' "${1-}" | sed -e 's/[\\&|]/\\&/g' -e ':a' -e 'N' -e '$!ba' -e 's/\n/\\n/g'; }

and render_stream() interpolates the escaped copies. Covers all three special
characters named at scripts/verify-impl.sh:231-234 (`|` the delimiter, `&` the
whole-match reference, `\` which escapes either) plus embedded newlines.

PROVEN BY FOUNDING, not by inspection, with the PRE-EDIT factory as the positive
control. Two throwaway kits (bin/fort-init + a templates symlink), two scratch
git repos, FORT_REGISTRY pointed at a scratch path. Purpose string:

    Trade & barter | ship things \ safely

  PRE-EDIT factory:  exit 1 — `sed: -e expression #8, char 32: unknown option
                     to 's'`, and it died AFTER creating 31 files, leaving a
                     half-founded fort with no purpose text anywhere in it.
  FIXED factory:     exit 0, and fort/charter.md line 7 reads
                     `Trade & barter | ship things \ safely` — byte-for-byte,
                     all three characters intact. Zero surviving render tokens
                     ({{[A-Z_]*}} count 0, excluding the deliberate
                     {{UNFILLED — ...}} markers).

THE SILENT HALF, which is worse than the crash and is the reason SO11 wanted
this. `|` errors loudly. `&` does not. Founding the PRE-EDIT factory with the
purpose `Salvage & repair`:

    exit=0   and fort/charter.md reads:  Salvage {{PURPOSE}} repair
                                expected: Salvage & repair

A fort founded successfully, exit 0, no warning, with `&` expanded to the whole
match and a corrupted constitution. That is the failure this fix prevents.

The real ~/.claude/civilization.json was not touched (checked: 0 occurrences of
the throwaway fort names).

VERIFIED: shellcheck -S warning clean, bash -n clean, capital verifier exit 0
(187 tests / 16 files) including the template-render lint, whose own positive
control went red as required.

title: [bug] templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:6 still names three offices in a fort now founded with four
description:
Warden finding 5 on the fortkit-wg8w.1 review, 2026-08-17.

The Band 2 sitting fixed exactly this sentence where bin/fort-init GENERATES it (the
$SEAT_OFFICES founding fact) and reworded line 2 of this same template file, leaving

carries the four. Since fortkit-naju the factory founds four seats, so the shipped

acceptance_criteria: templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:6 names the four seats the factory actually founds, and no other templates/ file asserts a three-seat roster.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
I have everything I need. Writing the review record.

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

title: templates/config/settings-permissions.json deny list lost its alphabetical sort: unsorted lists are how duplicate rules survive review
description:
ORIGIN: Ilva Trueglass's finding 1 reviewing fortkit-n3bk.2, 2026-08-13. Non-blocking, one-line fix, explicitly 'worth a bead, not worth a round'.

WHAT: n3bk.2 appended Edit(.claude/**), Edit(fort/profiles/**) and Edit(fort/scripts/**) after Edit(fort/events/*.jsonl) rather than in sorted position. Before that change the template's deny list was strictly sorted.

MEASURED by Ilva with jq, on both files:
  live capital .claude/settings.json   .permissions.deny == (.permissions.deny|sort)  -> true
  templates/config/settings-permissions.json                                          -> false
The allow list is unaffected; Edit(scripts/**) landed in sorted position.

FUNCTIONALLY INERT ON BOTH CONSUMERS SHE CHECKED, and this is why it is P3 rather than P2:
Claude Code does not order-rank permission rules, and the drift watcher compares with a Set
(civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs:753-770), not a sequence. Nothing behaves differently today.

WHY FILE IT AT ALL, in her words: an unsorted deny list is how duplicate rules survive review,
and duplicate-checking these lists is exactly what fortkit-n3bk.1 was filed about. The cost of
the fix is one line; the cost of the class is a rule nobody notices is there twice.

WORTH CONSIDERING WHILE FIXING, not required: a sortedness assertion is a two-line jq check and
would make this mechanical rather than a habit. fortkit-domm is already founding a fort and
grepping its rendered settings; that is the natural host if the check is wanted.

LANE: Forge, templates/ only.
acceptance_criteria: jq '.permissions.deny == (.permissions.deny|sort)' on templates/config/settings-permissions.json returns true, and the allow list stays true as well.

title: Gate-1 referrals need their resolution recorded on the bead, not inferred from a commit landing in the same minute
description:
WARDEN FINDING 2 on fortkit-z0j8 (Ilva, 2026-08-13), a records defect rather than a code one, and the Mayor has already appended the specific correction to fortkit-29e9.

THE INSTANCE. fortkit-29e9 carried a Warden ESCALATE — a gate-1 referral. It has exactly one comment (the verdict, 18:58:39Z), an empty notes field, and closed_at 19:06:13Z, seven minutes later. The referral was answered BY ACTION (the Mayor's repair of finding 1 landed in that same minute) but nothing on the bead or in the event stream recorded that the Overseer ruled on it. The precedent one bead earlier is the opposite: fortkit-52vf.10 closed 'on Overseer gate-1 sign-off after Warden ESCALATE', recorded as such.

WHAT THE MAYOR'S OWN CORRECTION ESTABLISHED, appended to fortkit-29e9: the Overseer never answered the question put to him ('Shall I merge and carry the wording?'). He answered a different one, with a priority steer. The Mayor read that as authorisation, said so explicitly at the time, and proceeded unobjected. That is weaker than a sign-off and stronger than merging past a referral in silence — and the close reason flattened the distinction by writing 'sign-off'.

THE CLASS: a gate exists to make a human decision legible later. A gate whose resolution is only inferable from commit timestamps has not done that, and six weeks on nobody can distinguish 'ruled on' from 'merged past'.

CHEAP RULE, which the same session followed correctly twice and missed once: QUOTE THE OVERSEER VERBATIM in the close reason rather than characterising him. fortkit-3jv7 and fortkit-k1pq both carry his words exactly; fortkit-29e9 carried a paraphrase, and the paraphrase is what drifted.

SHAPES TO CONSIDER: make it a line in the session-close protocol in fort/seats/mayor.md (prose-gated, needs Overseer approval); or a mechanical check that a bead carrying a gate label and an ESCALATE verdict cannot close without a comment containing a verbatim quotation. The second is stronger and the first is cheaper; the Overseer's call. Related: fortkit-fnjn, which is the same family — records that do not say what actually happened.
acceptance_criteria: A gate-1 bead cannot be closed leaving a reader unable to tell whether the referral was ruled on; whichever shape is chosen is recorded with the Overseer's approval if it touches a prose-gated file.

title: [bug] memory-lint's core budget counts SUPERSEDED facts, so the number it reports is not the number injected
description:
Found while building fortkit-c1kj, filed rather than fixed in the same commit to keep that change surgical.

scripts/memory-lint.mjs gates the core budget on 'frontmatter.tier === "core"' with NO status check, while scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs:404 renders only 'status === "active" && tier === "core"'. So a superseded core fact is counted against the budget but never injected.

MEASURED 2026-08-13 in the capital: 5 facts carry tier:core, of which 2 are superseded (cycle7-write-boundaries, forge-sandbox-caveat). The linter therefore reports a mayor budget of 4 facts / 75 lines where the real injected surface is smaller.

IMPACT TODAY IS ZERO and that is the whole reason this is P3 rather than higher: the budget ceilings are 30 facts / 300 lines and the fort is nowhere near them. It matters because the number is the fort's ONLY measurement of the always-injected surface (fortkit-88u.16 moved that cap to the seat precisely so it could be measured per session), and a measurement that counts things it does not measure will mislead exactly when the fort is close to the ceiling and needs it most.

FIX: add '&& frontmatter.status === "active"' to the budget branch, keep templates/fort/memory/memory-lint.mjs byte-identical, and note that the reported numbers will DROP — a reviewer must not read that drop as facts having been lost.
acceptance_criteria: The budget branch counts only active core facts; the template copy stays byte-identical; the before/after numbers are recorded on the bead so the drop is explained rather than discovered.
