title: schema/events.md omits edict.begun and edict.ended, which the charter MANDATES and which seats are told to police as a security signal — plus the new watcher.repaired (Warden E7 finding 6)
description:
WARDEN FINDING 6 on the E7 edict review (Ilva Trueglass, 2026-08-12, non-blocking).

TWO PARTS, and the second is worse than the first.

1. `watcher.repaired` is a NEW event category and was not added to schema/events.md's list.
   The schema says categories "extend freely", so this is NOT a violation. But that list is
   THE DISCOVERABILITY SURFACE for the visualizer and every other consumer, so a category
   that exists only in the stream is a category no reader knows to handle.

2. AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: `edict.begun` and `edict.ended` are missing from that
   list too, and the CHARTER MANDATES THEM. Pre-existing, not this edict's doing.

   fort/charter.md's Regent section states "An edict is never silent. It emits edict.begun
   and edict.ended into this fort's own event stream", and instructs every seat to treat an
   unexplained change with no edict event as A SECURITY SIGNAL worth escalating. So the two
   events a seat is told to police are absent from the schema that tells consumers which
   events exist. A visualizer built from the schema would not render the civilization's most
   privileged action, and a seat auditing the stream against the schema would find the
   charter's mandated events undocumented.

   These are also now PROVEN to fire correctly, one per fort, for the first time in the
   fort's history (fortkit-nvk, closed 2026-08-12 on direct measurement across all three
   forts). So the events are real, correct, load-bearing, and undocumented.

3. Separately, the two `watcher.repaired` details run 167 and 223 characters against the
   schema's guidance of "~140 chars so it reads as an announcement". Minor, but the guidance
   exists because these strings are rendered.

FIX: add `edict.begun`, `edict.ended` and `watcher.repaired` to schema/events.md's category
list, and audit the list against what the streams actually contain — if three categories
drifted out of the schema, others may have too. Run the audit rather than assuming these are
the only three.

NOTE ON GOVERNANCE: schema/events.md is the canonical event schema for the whole
civilization and fortkit-nd6 covers "schema governance: vendoring + drift check". This bead
is the concrete instance nd6 exists to prevent, so land them together or at least read nd6
first. The charter also says categories are "add-only, never renamed", so this is purely
additive and carries no migration.

LANE: MAYOR. schema/events.md is documentation the Mayor owns, not kernel-RO, and not
product code. Small enough for a Mayor session; no edict needed.

title: E7 Warden follow-ups: untested steady-state suppression branch, the bd comments field-name seam (check the 08-14 run), whitespace in fort names, flock -E 75, the uncommitted differential harness, and --dry-run now needing bd
description:
WARDEN FINDINGS 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 on the E7 edict review (Ilva Trueglass, 2026-08-12,
all non-blocking). Finding 1 is fortkit-veuj; finding 6 is fortkit-fx1e.

=== FINDING 3 IS THE ONE WITH A DEADLINE, so it is first ===

The `bd comments` seam is on the UNTESTED side of the fake tracker.
defaultCommands.comments parses `bd comments <id> --json` and reads `comment.text`; the test
tracker returns raw STRINGS, so the field name is never exercised. IF BD'S FIELD IS NOT
`text`, the comment readback yields nothing and EVERY RUN RE-APPENDS THE SAME COMMENT —
which is the spam the third-run test defends against, on the other side of the seam. The
bead export's embedded comments[] objects do use `text`, which corroborates but is a
DIFFERENT SUBCOMMAND.

HER CONCRETE CHECK, and it needs no code: the 2026-08-13 06:31 run should append 16
comments, and THE RUN AFTER IT SHOULD APPEND 0. If the second run appends 16 again, this
finding is live and the watcher is spamming. WHOEVER READS THE 08-14 RUN MUST CHECK THIS.
Recorded here and in the Mayor's handoff so it is not missed.

=== FINDING 2: THE STEADY-STATE SUPPRESSION BRANCH HAS NO DIRECT TEST ===

"Open bead whose DESCRIPTION already carries the current fingerprint -> suppress" is the
path that will run 23 times on the next scheduled run, and no committed test seeds an open
bead with a matching descriptionOf. Every suppression the suite exercises arrives via the
comment-readback route (run 3 of the append test) or the closed-bead route. Low risk since
it reads the same `known` set, but the bead asked for a unit test per branch and THIS IS THE
BRANCH PRODUCTION SPENDS MOST OF ITS TIME IN.

=== FINDING 4: THE LEGACY TITLE FALLBACK SPLITS ON WHITESPACE ===

/^Drift:\s+(\S+)\s+(\S.*?)\s*$/ mis-derives identity for any fort whose registered name
contains a SPACE. No such fort exists (Manyhalls, Proofdelve, Farlantern) and everything
filed from now on carries the explicit identity line, so exposure is bounded to legacy beads
and shrinks as they close. Her call: worth a guard or a comment, not a fix. NOTE the
adjacent rule — fortkit-8rh already makes fort-init refuse rosters whose actor ids collide
at edit distance 1; a fort NAME containing a space is the same family of input the factory
should probably refuse rather than the watcher tolerate.

=== FINDING 5: flock -E 75 COLLIDES WITH EX_TEMPFAIL ===

A child that itself exits 75 is reported as lock contention. This script's own paths exit
0/1 so it cannot arise from here, but bd and emit.sh are not bound to that. Cosmetic;
recorded so a future reader of a spurious "already running" does not repeat fortkit-bpuv's
investigation.

=== FINDING 7: THE "9 OF 13" CLAIM DOES NOT REPRODUCE FROM THE ARTIFACTS ===

And her reasoning is correct, which means MY OWN VERIFICATION NEEDS A CORRECTION TOO.

She points out a straight module swap cannot yield 9 failures: the new test file takes four
named ESM imports (identityOf, beadIdentity, rows, descriptionOf) that the pre-E7 module does
not export, so the file fails AT LINK TIME and ALL THIRTEEN fail. The number is consistent
with a GRAFT — old scan/run dropped into the new export surface — which is a legitimate way
to run it, but the record does not say so and the harness is not committed.

MAYOR'S CORRECTION, appended under SO7 because my own report to the Overseer was imprecise:
I reported "9 of 13 tests fail against the old implementation" from a worktree in which I
restored the pre-E7 drift-watch.mjs by `git checkout c6875a6^ -- civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs`
and ran vitest. That produced 9 failed / 4 passed, which I reported as a straight swap. Ilva
is right that a straight swap should fail at link time and take all 13 down. The most likely
explanation is that vitest's module resolution reported the missing named exports as
per-test failures within the file rather than a whole-file link error, so 9 is the count of
tests that actually touch the missing surface and 4 are those that do not. EITHER WAY THE
SUBSTANTIVE CLAIM HOLDS — the suite is red against the old implementation, which is what
non-vacuity requires — but the "9 of 13" figure should not be read as "9 tests specifically
discriminate the fix". Her corroboration by another route (the committed
identity-not-content test proves the fingerprint changes when the fort file changes, and the
pre-E7 run() filtered solely on known.has(fingerprint), so the old code NECESSARILY files a
second bead) is the stronger argument and should be the one cited.

HER REASON FOR RAISING IT IS THE REASON TO KEEP IT: "this fort has now recorded six controls
that reported PASS while proving nothing, and this is precisely the sentence a future reader
will lean on."

ACTION: the record should name the harness shape. Whoever next touches the watcher should
commit the differential harness, or the record should state plainly that the count came from
an uncommitted graft.

=== FINDING 8: --dry-run NOW REQUIRES A WORKING bd ===

By design and documented in the code (it must read the tracker to report what it would do).
Noted because anything using --dry-run as a cheap smoke test on a machine without bd will now
FAIL where it previously succeeded. Relevant to any founding smoke or CI path that ran it.

LANES: 2 and the finding-7 harness are test/ (FORGE). 3 is an observation with a dated check,
no code. 4, 5 and 8 are civ/scripts/drift-watch.mjs comments or guards (REGENT), cheap enough
to ride along with fortkit-veuj rather than justify a sitting of their own.

title: Nothing surfaces that an edict is still open: the stream records begun, and cannot distinguish working from idle-holding-full-access
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-12, and filed off the Overseer's own question ("should I exit the regent
session immediately after each edict?"). The answer is yes, and this bead is the machinery
that makes the answer easy to follow instead of easy to forget.

THE GAP. The event stream records that an edict BEGAN. Nothing records that one is STILL
OPEN. A reader of the stream cannot distinguish three states that matter very differently:

  edict.begun, work in progress          — normal, expected
  edict.begun, work done, session idle   — full unmasked access held for no reason
  edict.begun, session dead              — the edict crashed and edict.ended will never come

MEASURED TODAY, E7 (session 2026-08-12T090019):
  09:00:20  edict.begun
  09:53:28  work committed (c6875a6)
  09:58:47  handoff written — the record was complete here
  10:08:20  edict.ended, fired when the Overseer exited
So the session held unmasked full-machine access for about ten minutes after its own record
was finished. Nothing surfaced that. The Mayor established it only by reading `pgrep -af
bin/regent` and interpreting a zero-CPU S+ process, then told the Overseer, who exited.
The Overseer had to ASK whether it was still running, which is the wrong direction for that
information to travel.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS. bin/regent's own header states the seat "has no
technical guard. Its safety properties are entirely procedural", and one of those procedures
is that it runs "only while he is present". An open idle session breaks that guard SILENTLY:
it holds while the Overseer is at the terminal and lapses the moment he walks away, with no
event marking the transition. The recorded precedent is the stray unmasked
`claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` running since 2026-08-09 that session E found and the
Overseer ended; a lingering Regent is the same class with more authority.

Note also that edict.ended marks when the CAPABILITY ended, not when the work finished
(proven by the timestamps above, and recorded on the now-closed fortkit-nvk). That is the
honest stamp — an open session really does retain access — which means the ONLY way to keep
the begun-to-ended window small is for the human to exit promptly. Machinery that reminds him
is therefore the whole control, not a nicety.

CANDIDATE SHAPES, cheapest first, and this is a decision rather than a spec:
  (a) `fortkit status` reports an open edict: EDICT_FILE already exists at
      civ/handoffs/.edict-<stamp> (bin/regent:241) and is removed at cleanup, so
      "does that file exist, and is its PID alive" is the whole check. Nearly free, and it
      surfaces where the Overseer already looks.
  (b) The Keep / world view shows the Regent bench as occupied while an edict is open.
      fortkit-0yz already wants "Regent bench lighting from edicts", so this may be that
      bead's natural completion rather than new work — CHECK 0yz BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING.
  (c) A watcher that alerts when an edict has been open beyond some threshold. Most
      complete, most machinery, and the threshold is arbitrary; the charter's watcher list
      is "added as earned" and one ten-minute occurrence does not earn a cron.
  (d) The launcher prints an explicit "EDICT STILL OPEN — exit to close the record" banner
      after its work completes. Cheapest of all, but only helps if the human is looking at
      that terminal, which is exactly the case where he already knows.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION: (a), and check whether (b) is already fortkit-0yz's job first.
Deliberately NOT recommending (c): standing order 11 wants an observed failure, and what was
observed is ten idle minutes with the Overseer in the room, which is a real gap in the
RECORD's legibility but not yet evidence that a cron is warranted.

HONEST ABOUT THE EVIDENCE STRENGTH, since SO11 exists to stop imagined infrastructure: no
harm occurred today. The Overseer was present the whole time and exited when told. What is
demonstrated is that the fort cannot tell the difference between a working edict and an idle
one, and that the human had to ask a model to find out. That is worth a cheap fix and not
worth an expensive one. Priority set accordingly.

LANE: (a) touches src/ and is FORGE lane. (b) is the Keep, also Forge. (d) would touch
bin/regent, which is kernel-RO and would need an edict — the most expensive option for the
least benefit, which is its own argument.

title: docs/specs/memory.md names interactions.jsonl with no directory in two places — the bare filename is the ambiguity fortkit-ij8j's defect grew in (Warden ij8j finding 2)
description:
WARDEN FINDING 2 on the fortkit-ij8j review (Ilva Trueglass, 2026-08-12, non-blocking).

docs/specs/memory.md still names the corpus WITH NO DIRECTORY, in two places:
  section 3 ruling 3, line 57   "interactions.jsonl"
  section 5, line 202           "interactions.jsonl"

ILVA'S POINT, AND IT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A TYPO FIX:
"that bare filename is the ambiguity the defect grew in: the generator and the spec agreed
on the string while disagreeing about the path."

fortkit-ij8j was exactly that failure. scripts/consolidate-memory.mjs:319 joined
root + "interactions.jsonl" while beads writes .beads/interactions.jsonl. Both the code and
the spec said "interactions.jsonl" and were describing different files. One of six corpora
named in section 5 was therefore indexed in NO FORT AT ALL, and the reported gap read as a
choice the fort had made rather than as a wrong path. A bare filename in a spec that
governs multiple readers is not neutral shorthand; it is the place the divergence hid.

FIX: name .beads/interactions.jsonl in both places.

STANDING ORDER 3 makes this required rather than optional: "Tests, explanations, and spec
updates are expected output, never optional." ij8j established the canonical location, so
ij8j is the change that owes the spec update. It is filed forward rather than held against
the merge because the code is now correct and the spec is merely less precise than the
code — the safe direction of the two.

CHECK WHILE THERE, not yet verified by anyone: whether section 5's other five corpora are
named with enough path precision to avoid the same class. The one that just cost the fort a
silently-unindexed corpus was the one named ambiguously, and there is no reason to assume it
is the only one.

the next Mayor session rather than dispatching.

title: verify.sh green output does not enumerate which steps ran: run_step is silent on success, so a clean ShellCheck stage is indistinguishable from a skipped one
description:
OBSERVED THIS SESSION (SO11 satisfied, and the observation is small but real).

fort/scripts/verify.sh's run_step() is SILENT ON SUCCESS: it runs the step, returns
0, and prints nothing of its own. Only the underlying tools' own output appears, and
some of them are silent when clean. ShellCheck is one: a clean run prints nothing at
all.

WHAT THAT COST, this session. After the fortkit-52vf.2 seat-file edits the Mayor ran
verify.sh, got exit 0, and could not tell from the log whether the ShellCheck step
had run. grep -i -c 'shellcheck' over the full captured log returned 0. Confirming it
had run required reading verify.sh:67, checking shellcheck was on PATH, and re-running
the identical invocation by hand. Three probes to answer a question a green log should
have answered.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG. This fort has a recorded pattern of
controls that report PASS while proving nothing: probe-cycle7.sh's positive control
asserting a pointer stub is writable (fortkit-08ny), memory-lint passing over a
near-duplicate fact pair (fortkit-nwl6), warden.sh emitting verdict_recorded:true with
no verdict (fortkit-bfsu). A verifier whose green output does not enumerate what it
verified is the same shape one step further back: nothing is wrong, and nothing is
demonstrable either. The steps list already exists in the emit payloads at
verify.sh:58 and :68, so the information is known to the script and simply not shown
to the reader — and under --no-emit or CI, which is how it is invoked for review,
even the payload is suppressed.

FIX, and keep it small: have run_step announce each step and its outcome on stdout,
so a captured log enumerates the six steps (memory-lint, typecheck,
browser-typecheck, lint, test, shellcheck) whether or not events are emitted. Nothing
about the pass/fail logic needs to change.

LANE: MAYOR. verify.sh is re-granted writable to the Mayor alone under cycle 7; the
Forge's and Warden's masks keep it read-only, so this must never be dispatched to the
Forge (fort/seats/mayor.md:17).

COUPLED TO fortkit-6ovg, and sequence behind it: writing verify.sh from a masked Mayor
session currently fails, because fort/scripts/ is a read-only DIRECTORY and every
ordinary edit needs to create a sibling temp file. Measured again this session:
test -w verify.sh TRUE, touch fort/scripts/.probe -> Read-only file system. So this
bead is cheap to specify now and cannot be executed until E2 (fortkit-52vf.3) makes
the carve-out work.

title: Backport longburn-5v4 into Manyhalls: in-mask launch refusal — COUPLED change (mayor.sh + warden.sh + forge.sh), not a one-liner
description:
TRIAGE by the Regent under edict fortkit-or2.9. CLASS: backport, but the cheapest-looking of the four is the most expensive, and that is the finding. NOT APPLIED.

WHAT 5v4 DOES IN FARLANTERN: launchers refuse (exit 77) when FORT_MASKED names a seat that must not launch other seats, while letting the attended Mayor's dispatch lane through. It stops a masked seat from spawning seats.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINER HERE, measured 2026-08-11: the guard reads a SEAT-NAMED marker (mayor/forge/warden), and this fort does not have one. fort/scripts/mayor.sh:42-43 exports the LEGACY BOOLEAN, 'FORT_MASKED=1', and neither warden.sh nor forge.sh carries any guard at all. Porting 5v4 therefore means changing three launchers together — teach mayor.sh the seat name, add the guard to warden.sh and forge.sh — which is a coupled cross-file change, exactly the shape that must land as ONE commit and therefore as one edict.

AND IT CARRIES A SCAR THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH IT (civ remember, 2026-08-09): the seat-named guard shipped correct for new launches and REFUSED FARLANTERN'S OWN MASKED MAYOR MID-MILL, because her live session predated the edict and still carried the legacy '1' — launcher edits bind at dispatch, not at edit. The accepted form takes '' | mayor | 1, with a dated retirement note for the legacy value. Any test matrix for this port must include the environment of currently-running sessions, not only the new contract.

VALUE HERE IS LOWER THAN IN FARLANTERN: that fort's Mayor drives a mill and routinely dispatches seats; this fort's does not to the same degree. Cheap insurance, real coupling cost, hence P3 rather than P1.

REVIEW: gate 1 (launcher scripts). Regent-only to apply.

title: warden.sh candidate-derivation: head -1 SIGPIPE under pipefail; and 'candidate present' echo is partial when the tip is already merged
description: Two non-blocking findings from Ilva's r2 review of the fortkit-8cv6 warden.sh repair (commit 2e0744d), filed forward so 8cv6 is not blocked. Both are in the new defect-1 candidate-presence guard.
design: Finding 6 (latent, fails-closed): src=$(git worktree list --porcelain | awk … | head -1) runs under set -o pipefail. If two worktrees share a HEAD, awk's second write can land after head -1 closed the pipe; awk dies 141, pipefail propagates, set -e aborts the launcher with exit 141 and no REFUSED line. All 74 worktree HEADs are distinct today so it is latent, and the direction is safe (no session, no verdict). Fix: replace 'head -1' with 'awk … | { IFS= read -r line; printf %s "$line"; }' or add an awk exit after the first match. Finding 8 (cosmetic): when the tip is already merged, $src derives to main and the scratch is built from main's CURRENT HEAD, a strictly later tree than the reviewed commit — the 'candidate present' echo is true (reachability) but the seat reads later work as candidate. Suggest amending the echo to '… present in $src at HEAD <sha>; the scratch may contain later commits'.

title: researcher.sh template prompt references retired fort/remember.md — fix before propagation
description: The Researcher launcher's prompt (templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh, and the live Manyhalls copy line 29) instructs the seat to 'Read fort/charter.md, fort/remember.md, fort/seats/researcher.md'. fort/remember.md is retired (88u migration; now a pointer stub) — same class as fortkit-1yg. It does not error (stub exists) but points the seat at the wrong memory surface. Fix the TEMPLATE to read fort/memory/current.md (distilled view; facts ledger fort/memory/facts/) instead, matching mayor.md/forge.md/charter after 1yg. Forge template edit + re-render/reinstall (kernel-RO live launcher = Overseer hand). MUST land before fortkit-vhk.7 propagation so the retired reference does not spread to every fort. Also fold in the post-seating actor-id update (researcher.sh emits -a researcher; once the occupant is named, the live+template launcher's actor id follows, like mayor.sh emits -a emrith).
notes:
2026-08-11 (Mayor, Emrith) ROUND 1 REJECTED IN PART — the memory-prompt half is correct; the actor-id half is applied at the WRONG LAYER and must be reverted from the template.

WHAT IS RIGHT (keep): the prompt now reads fort/memory/current.md and cites fort/memory/facts/, replacing the retired fort/remember.md. That was the bead's purpose and it is done correctly.

WHAT IS WRONG (revert): commit 65d1a38 hardcodes '-a saelin' into templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh — six emit call sites plus the bd comment --actor. Every other template launcher carries the SEAT OFFICE, not the occupant:
  templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh  -> -a mayor      LIVE fort/scripts/mayor.sh  -> -a emrith
  templates/fort/scripts/forge.sh  -> -a forge      LIVE fort/scripts/forge.sh  -> -a kethra
  templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh -> -a researcher   LIVE fort/scripts/researcher.sh -> -a researcher (still the office; the saelin change belongs HERE)
Verified by reading all six files 2026-08-11, not inferred.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. fort-init renders this template for every fort founded hereafter, and fortkit-vhk.7 is about to propagate it to Proofdelve and Farlantern. Shipped as committed, every other fort's Researcher would claim beads and emit events as Saelin Stillmere, a citizen of Manyhalls. That is fortkit-ebm ('launch scripts emit as another fort's citizens') and fortkit-fd2 ('fort-init ships other forts' citizens as default seat personalities') reintroduced by hand, into the exact artifact the propagation bead carries.

THE BEAD'S OWN WORDING CAUSED THIS, and the correction belongs on the record rather than on the Forge. This bead said 'the live+template launcher's actor id follows, like mayor.sh emits -a emrith'. That conflates two files: the LIVE mayor.sh emits -a emrith, the TEMPLATE mayor.sh emits -a mayor. The Forge followed the instruction it was given, faithfully. Mayor error.

ROUND 2 SCOPE: revert every '-a saelin' and '--actor saelin' in templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh back to 'researcher'; keep the memory-prompt change and its regression assertions; add a test asserting the TEMPLATE launcher carries the office id and no occupant name, so this cannot regress into the propagation. The live Manyhalls researcher.sh -> -a saelin is Overseer's hand (kernel-RO) and is tracked separately, not here.
2026-08-11 (Mayor, Emrith) WARDEN'S BLOCKING FINDING 1 ACCEPTED. The Mayor's judgement is overruled by the Warden's, and the record should say so plainly.

I found the same fort-init gap independently and filed it as fortkit-uhvt, but I ruled the template change should STAY and vhk.7 be gated on uhvt. That was wrong, and Ilva's reasoning is the better one: before the change the prompt named a path that exists everywhere the template is USED and is merely stale in the one fort where the template never runs. After the change it names a path that exists NOWHERE the template is used. Strictly worse for the propagated artifact. My 'it is inert because fort-init does not render researcher.sh yet' missed that the template is also the SOURCE for the vhk.7 backport, and that every other template launcher still says fort/remember.md — so the researcher template would be the lone one pointing at nothing.

Her characterisation of the root cause is also correct and I accept it: this is a BEAD-AUTHORING defect, not a Forge defect, and it is the same error twice from one bead. This bead conflates the live tree with the template tree. I caught that conflation in the actor-id half and kept it in the memory half. The Forge implemented what it was told, faithfully, both rounds.

ROUND 3 SCOPE (Warden's requested change, one line plus test removal):
  1. Revert the prompt in templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh to fort/remember.md.
  2. KEEP the round-2 office-id state (six emit sites + bd comment --actor all 'researcher', no occupant name) and its test assertions.
  3. Drop the two now-false memory assertions from test/researcher-launcher.test.ts: toContain('fort/memory/current.md'), toContain('facts ledger in fort/memory/facts/'), and not.toContain('fort/remember.md').
  4. Warden finding 2: strengthen the office-id guard. The current not.toContain('saelin') is spelled against ONE literal name, so '-a emrith' or '-a kethra' in five of six emit sites would leave the suite green, and the toMatch(/-a researcher -s researcher/g) is a strict duplicate of the toContain above it (the /g does nothing on a single toMatch and misleadingly reads as 'all occurrences'). Replace with negative regexes over every attribution site: not.toMatch(/-a (?!researcher\b)/) and not.toMatch(/--actor (?!researcher\b)/).
  5. Warden finding 3: adopt mayor.sh:2-4's header rationale, citing fortkit-ebm/fd2, instead of the terser line.
  6. Warden finding 4: add one line to the r2 handoff naming the r1 claim it supersedes ('supersedes the actor-id claim in r1'). APPEND only — r1 is not to be touched.

WHAT REMAINS OF THIS BEAD AFTER THE REVERT: the office-id correctness work and its regression guard. The memory-surface half is SUPERSEDED BY fortkit-uhvt, which owns migrating the whole template world together (bin/fort-init, templates/fort/charter.md, templates/fort/seats/{mayor,forge}.md, and all four template launchers). Ilva reached the same two options independently and recommended the revert under standing order 2 as the reversible one. Agreed. uhvt keeps the larger option alive for the Overseer to rule on; this bead stops pretending to carry it.
2026-08-11 (Mayor, Emrith) ROUND 3 VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (commit 4ca36b6), measured in the candidate worktree rather than read from the handoff:
  templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh — 0 occurrences of 'fort/memory', 1 of 'fort/remember.md', 0 of 'saelin', 5 of '-a researcher'. The Warden's blocking finding 1 is fixed.
  Net three-dot diff (main...bead/vhk.9) of the template is FOUR LINES, all header comment: the fortkit-ebm/fd2 rationale adopted from mayor.sh:2-4. The prompt line is byte-identical to main again.
  test/researcher-launcher.test.ts gains exactly the four assertions the Warden specified, including not.toMatch(/-a (?!researcher\b)/) and not.toMatch(/--actor (?!researcher\b)/). Checked by hand: '-a emrith' trips the negative lookahead and fails the suite, which the previous not.toContain('saelin') would not have.
  Three handoffs present (r1, r2, r3); the r2 supersession note was APPENDED, r1 untouched.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW DELIVERS, stated plainly because it is much less than its title: a header comment carrying the ebm/fd2 rationale, and a regression guard that pins every attribution site in the template to the seat office. THE BEAD'S NAMED PURPOSE — repointing the template off the retired fort/remember.md — IS NOT DELIVERED AND CANNOT BE, because the template world has no fort/memory to point at. That work is fortkit-uhvt's. This bead's title now overstates it; the title stays (records are append-only) and this note is the correction.

Warden round 2 launched WITH the candidate directory as third argument, correcting the Mayor's own error from rounds 1-2 (fortkit-8cv6). This is a workaround, not a fix: the launcher still accepts the two-argument form silently.
close_reason: Merged 2026-08-11. Warden round 2 APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS (Ilva Trueglass, opus), 6 findings, none blocking; her round-1 BLOCKING finding fixed by the round-3 revert. Post-merge main verified by the Mayor: verify.sh 14 files / 152 tests, exit 0. Three Forge rounds, two Warden reviews. WHAT LANDED: the fortkit-ebm/fd2 header rationale, and a regression guard pinning every -a and --actor site in the template to the seat office. WHAT DID NOT LAND, stated plainly: the bead's named purpose. Repointing the template off fort/remember.md is impossible while the template world has no fort/memory to point at; that work is fortkit-uhvt's. The title overstates what this bead delivered and stays as written per SO7, with the correction on the bead. Follow-ups: fortkit-vhk.14 (restore memory-surface coverage as a coupling guard, -s gap, r2 supersession line, header harmonization) and fortkit-xtlq (handoff supersession class fix). comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES

**Model that produced the work:** gpt-5.6-terra (both handoffs), Forge ladder rung one. Scrutiny weighted accordingly; the diff is small and I read every changed line. I found no reward-hacked assertions — the new tests do assert real properties of the file, though one is a no-op duplicate (F2).

**Round posture:** the bead carries a round-1 rejection *by the Mayor*, not by the Warden. This is the Warden's round one on this diff, so I state everything I would block on.

**What round 2 got right, and I confirm it:** every `-a saelin` and `--actor saelin` is gone from `templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh`. All six `emit` call sites (lines 46, 52, 72, 75, 77) and the `bd comment --actor` (line 71) carry `researcher`. The net `main..bead/vhk.9` diff of the template is exactly two lines: a header comment and the prompt line. The Mayor's round-1 blocker is fully fixed.

---

### 1. BLOCKING — the new prompt points every consumer of this template at a path that does not exist there

The change makes the template prompt read `fort/memory/current.md (distilled view; facts ledger in fort/memory/facts/)`. That surface exists **only in the live Manyhalls tree**. It does not exist in the template world this file ships into:

- `bin/fort-init:25` — `mkdir -p fort/{seats,handoffs,annals,events,specs,scripts,telemetry}`. No `memory`.
- `bin/fort-init:39` — writes `fort/remember.md` with the fort's founding operational facts. That file is real and populated in a newly founded fort.
- `templates/fort/` contains no `memory/` directory (`ls`).
- `templates/fort/charter.md:60` still documents `Operational facts: fort/remember.md` as this fort-shape's memory surface.
- `templates/fort/seats/mayor.md:11` and `templates/fort/seats/forge.md:12` still direct their seats to `fort/remember.md`.
- `templates/fort/scripts/mayor.sh:29`, `forge.sh:81`, `warden.sh:44` all still direct their seats to `fort/remember.md`.
- Nothing in `bin/`, `civ/scripts/`, `scripts/`, or `templates/` creates or references `fort/memory` (grep). The only non-live reference in the whole repo is `scripts/memory-lint.mjs`, which is fortkit-local tooling.

The bead's premise — "`fort/remember.md` is retired (88u migration; now a pointer stub) … matching mayor.md/forge.md/charter after 1yg" — is true of the **live** tree and false of the **template** tree. `6bc7447` (fortkit-1yg) touched exactly three files: `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/forge.md`, `fort/seats/mayor.md`. All live. It touched no template.

So the effect of merging, in each place this artifact is actually used:

- **fortkit/Manyhalls:** none. The template is never executed here; the live `fort/scripts/researcher.sh` is what runs, and it is kernel-RO and unchanged.
- **A fort founded by `fort-init` hereafter:** its Researcher is told to read `fort/memory/current.md` and `fort/memory/facts/`, neither of which exists — a hard read failure — while `fort/remember.md`, which does exist and holds that fort's operational facts, goes unmentioned. Every other seat in that same fort is correctly pointed at `fort/remember.md`.
- **`fortkit-vhk.7` propagation:** the bead export (`.beads/issues.jsonl:163`) states vhk.7 carries this launcher "to Proofdelve, Farlantern, and fort-init so new forts are born with it." The `fort-init` leg is verified broken above. I could not verify the Proofdelve/Farlantern leg — those repos are outside my working directories — but the memory ledger is fortkit-local 88u work with no propagation path in this repo, so the same dangling reference is the expected outcome there.

Before the change the prompt named a path that exists everywhere the template is used and is merely stale in one fort where the template never runs. After the change it names a path that exists nowhere the template is used. That is strictly worse for the propagated artifact, and it is the bead's own stated failure mode ("so the retired reference does not spread to every fort") realised in the opposite direction. Threat model: **threat 1, agent accident** — the highest-volume, highest-realized-cost class, and the charter's own text already lists this family ("launch scripts emitting as another fort's citizens", fortkit-ebm/fd2) as a realised incident. This is a correctness bug in the deliverable, so it clears the blocking bar.

I want to be plain about where the defect lives: **this is a bead-authoring defect, not a Forge defect.** The Forge implemented the instruction it was given, faithfully, both rounds. The bead conflates the live tree with the template tree; the Mayor caught that conflation in the actor-id half and kept it in the memory half. That is the same error twice from one bead.

**Requested change (executable by the Forge, one line):** revert the prompt in `templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh` to `fort/remember.md`, keeping the round-2 office-id state and the office-id test assertions. Drop the two now-false memory assertions from `test/researcher-launcher.test.ts` (`toContain("fort/memory/current.md")`, `toContain("facts ledger in fort/memory/facts/")`, `not.toContain("fort/remember.md")`).

**The alternative, for the Mayor and Justin to rule on, not the Forge:** migrate the whole template world together — `bin/fort-init` (create `fort/memory/current.md` + `facts/` at founding), `templates/fort/charter.md`, `templates/fort/seats/{mayor,forge}.md`, and all four template launchers — and make vhk.7 depend on it. I do not recommend it as this bead: it is much larger than the bead's scope, and `bin/` is kernel read-only to every masked seat (charter, cycle-7 amendment), so the Forge **cannot** perform it and should escalate rather than attempt it. If Justin prefers this route, it needs his hand on `bin/fort-init` and the decision recorded on the bead. My recommendation is the revert: it is the reversible option (standing order 2), and it keeps this bead's scope honest.

### 2. Non-blocking — the office-id regression test is weaker than the bead asked for

The bead asked for "a test asserting the TEMPLATE launcher carries the office id and no occupant name." What landed:

```ts
expect(source).toContain("-a researcher -s researcher");
expect(source).toContain("--actor researcher");
expect(source).toMatch(/-a researcher -s researcher/g);   // duplicate of line 1
expect(source).not.toContain("saelin");                   // one name only
```

`toMatch(/…/g)` here is a strict duplicate of the `toContain` two lines above; the `/g` flag does nothing for a single `toMatch` and reads as if it proved "all occurrences," which it does not. The negative guard is spelled against one literal name, so `-a emrith` or `-a kethra` in five of the six emit sites would leave the suite green. The assertion that would actually carry the bead's intent is a negative regex over every attribution site, e.g. `expect(source).not.toMatch(/-a (?!researcher\b)/)` and `expect(source).not.toMatch(/--actor (?!researcher\b)/)`. It does catch the exact regression that occurred, so this is a bead, not a block.

### 3. Non-blocking — the header comment diverges from its siblings and drops the rationale that was just violated

`mayor.sh:2-4` explains *why*: "Actor ids are seat-office names (mayor/forge/warden) until the Founding Moot renames them — a fort must never inherit another settlement's citizen (fortkit-ebm/fd2)." `forge.sh` and `warden.sh` carry the short form. The new researcher line — "Actor id is the Researcher seat office." — is more precise about the template never being renamed, but it is now the *least* informative of the four about the exact rule this bead's round one broke. Worth adopting mayor.sh's fortkit-ebm/fd2 citation.

### 4. Non-blocking — the round-1 handoff records the reverted change as a "Verified fact" with no pointer to its correction

`fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-11-vhk.9.md` states as verified fact that "Every launcher event and the durable `bd comment` in that template now uses actor id `saelin`" and lists as next action that the Overseer reinstall the live launcher to match. Standing order 7 is satisfied — I confirmed the file was not rewritten after its stamp commit (`a2ffc6d`); only the stamp appended to it — and the r2 handoff is the appended correction. But r2 never names the r1 claim it supersedes, so a reader who finds r1 alone is misled. A one-line "supersedes the actor-id claim in r1" in r2 would close it.

### 5. Non-blocking, and outside this bead — the live Manyhalls launchers still carry the retired reference

`fort/scripts/mayor.sh:25`, `forge.sh:81`, `warden.sh:42`, and `researcher.sh:29` all still instruct their seats to read `fort/remember.md`. 1yg fixed the live charter and seat files, not the live launchers. This is an observed failure, not an imagined one (standing order 11): my own launch prompt this session told me to read `fort/remember.md`, and I read the stub. These are host-executed and kernel-RO — Overseer's hand, tracked separately from this bead. Worth one bead covering all four rather than one per seat.

---

## What I verified independently

- Full candidate template read from `bead/vhk.9`: all six `emit` sites and `bd comment --actor` carry `researcher`; string `saelin` absent.
- Each of the seven new test assertions checked by hand against the candidate template's bytes; all seven hold. Also confirmed which ones become false under my requested revert (F1).
- `shellcheck --shell=bash` on the candidate template read from stdin: exit 0, no findings.
- `bin/fort-init` lines 25, 32, 39, 56 read directly; `templates/fort/` listed directly; grep for `fort/memory` across `bin/`, `civ/scripts/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`.
- `templates/fort/charter.md:60`, `templates/fort/seats/{mayor,forge}.md`, `templates/fort/scripts/{mayor,forge,warden}.sh` still name `fort/remember.md`.
- `scripts/memory-lint.mjs:73-85`: the retired-reference check scans only `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, so it never covered `templates/` — no verifier conflict either way.
- `6bc7447` (1yg) diffstat: three live files, no template.
- `fortkit-vhk.7` scope, read from `.beads/issues.jsonl` in git.
- Per-commit diffstats for all four commits; r1 handoff untouched after its stamp.
- `templates/fort/seats/researcher.md` contains no memory reference (so F1 is confined to the launcher).

## What I took on faith

- **The verifier run.** Both handoffs report `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` exit 0, launcher-observed, 14 files / 150 tests. I could not reproduce it: the scratch tree at `/tmp/warden-vhk.9` is a copy of `main`, not of the candidate, it has no `node_modules`, and every write I attempted (patch file, `mktemp -d`, `touch`) was denied — so I could neither apply the diff nor run vitest, typecheck, lint, or memory-lint. The one gate I could reproduce, shellcheck on the changed file, passes. The stamp is written by `forge.sh`, not by the model, which is what makes the rest credible; I am recording that I did not observe it.
- **That Proofdelve and Farlantern lack `fort/memory/`.** Both repos are outside my working directories. Finding 1 does not rest on it — the `fort-init` leg is verified in this repo and is sufficient on its own.
- `bd` was unavailable this session (`failed to open database … read-only file system`), so all bead records came from `.beads/issues.jsonl` in git rather than from `bd show`.

VERDICT-LINE: REQUEST-CHANGES: template prompt now names fort/memory/current.md, which fort-init never creates — dangling in every fort it ships to.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Model that produced the work:** gpt-5.6-terra, all three rounds (r1/r2/r3 handoffs each stamp `Model: gpt-5.6-terra`) — Forge ladder rung one. Scrutiny weighted accordingly; the delta is four lines of shell comment and four lines of test, and I read every changed line and hand-checked every assertion against the candidate bytes.

**Round posture:** this is the Warden's **round two** on this diff (the bead's round three, counting the Mayor's round-one rejection). Under round discipline only regressions and unfixed round-one blockers may block. My round-one blocker is fixed and I found no regression, so genuinely new findings below are filed as beads rather than held against the merge.

**Round-one blocker: RESOLVED.** `templates/fort/scripts/researcher.sh:31` reads `fort/charter.md, fort/remember.md, fort/seats/researcher.md` again. I re-verified the premise that made the revert correct rather than taking it from the bead: `bin/fort-init:32` renders only `emit status mayor forge warden verify` — `researcher.sh` is not rendered at all today — and `bin/fort-init:39` writes a populated `fort/remember.md` at founding. So the reverted prompt names the surface that will actually exist wherever this template eventually runs, and it now matches `templates/fort/{charter.md,seats/*,scripts/{mayor,forge,warden}.sh}` instead of standing alone.

**Net effect on the propagated artifact:** `git diff --numstat main...bead/vhk.9` on the template is `3 1` — the three-line header comment replacing one line, and nothing else. Functionally the shipped template is byte-identical to main. That is the safest possible shape for an artifact `fortkit-vhk.7` is about to carry to Proofdelve, Farlantern and `fort-init`.

**My round-one findings 2, 3 and 4 are all closed**, correctly:
- F2: the duplicate `toMatch(/…/g)` and the one-name `not.toContain("saelin")` are gone, replaced by `not.toMatch(/-a (?!researcher\b)/)` and `not.toMatch(/--actor (?!researcher\b)/)` — negative guards over every attribution site, which is what the bead asked for.
- F3: `researcher.sh:2-4` now mirrors `mayor.sh:2-4` verbatim in structure, citing fortkit-ebm/fd2, with `researcher` added to the office list.
- F4: `forge-2026-08-11-vhk.9-r2.md:61` appends `> Round 3 correction: supersedes the actor-id claim in r1…`. The r2 diff is `+2 −0` — a true append, no historic content rewritten (standing order 7 honoured), and the r3 handoff's "Failed attempts" section discloses that a first attempt put the line inside the preserved verifier block and was fixed before commit. That disclosure is the kind of record-keeping I want to see and I note it approvingly.

--------

### 1. Non-blocking — r2's memory claims are now false of the merged artifact, and its appended correction names only the r1 claim

`forge-2026-08-11-vhk.9-r2.md:12-14` states as verified fact that the template "names `fort/memory/current.md` and `fort/memory/facts/`, with no retired `fort/remember.md` reference", and :17-18 that the test "guards the current memory surface". After the r3 revert all four clauses are false of what merges. The appended correction at :61 supersedes only the **actor-id** claim in **r1** — exactly the scope the Mayor wrote — and says nothing about r2's own memory claims.

This is the same defect class as my round-one F4, one round later, and I graded that one non-blocking, so this is non-blocking too. It is genuinely mitigated: r3 states the current state plainly at :11-12, and the r1→r2→r3 filenames sort in order in one directory. But a reader who lands on r2 alone is misled. **Bead:** append one line to r2 naming r3 as its superseder for the memory claim.

The generalizable observation underneath, and the better bead: the facts ledger has a `superseded-by:` frontmatter field that `scripts/memory-lint.mjs:62-69` *enforces and resolves*; handoffs have no such field and no lint. Three rounds on one bead produced two stale-record incidents in a row. A `superseded-by:` line in the handoff schema, checked by memory-lint, would close the class instead of patching instances.

### 2. Non-blocking — the defect this bead was filed for now has zero regression coverage

Dropping the three memory assertions was correct (they became false), but nothing replaced them. `test/researcher-launcher.test.ts` now asserts nothing whatsoever about which memory surface the template's prompt names. The original defect — "the launcher prompt points the seat at the wrong memory surface" — can silently recur, and the bead closes with less coverage of its own subject than it had at round two.

**Bead:** add `expect(source).toContain("fort/remember.md")`. This is worth more than the guard it restores: it makes `fortkit-uhvt` **fail this test** the moment it repoints the template, which forces `bin/fort-init` and the template prompt to move in the same commit. That is precisely the coupling whose absence caused rounds one through three.

Fold in one smaller gap: the new negative regexes cover `-a` and `--actor` but not `-s`. `-s saelin` at five of the six emit sites would leave the suite green. `expect(source).not.toMatch(/-s (?!researcher\b)/)` closes it, and the `-s` sites are the same lines.

### 3. Non-blocking — `fortkit-uhvt`'s title is now stale

uhvt is titled "…while launcher templates now point at it". That clause was true when it was filed during round two and is false after this revert. The bead still owns the right work; a reader taking the title at face value will hunt for a template pointer that no longer exists. One-line correction on uhvt, Mayor's hand.

### 4. Non-blocking — two sibling template headers still carry the terser rationale

`templates/fort/scripts/forge.sh:2` and `warden.sh:2` still say "Actor id(s) are seat-office names until the moot" without the fortkit-ebm/fd2 citation that `mayor.sh` and now `researcher.sh` carry. Harmonizing all four is a one-line-each bead; the two that were most recently touched are the two that got it right.

### 5. Non-blocking, unchanged from round one and outside this bead — the live Manyhalls launchers still name the retired pointer

`fort/scripts/mayor.sh:25`, `forge.sh:81`, `warden.sh:42` and `researcher.sh:29` all still instruct their seats to read `fort/remember.md`. Observed, not imagined (standing order 11): my own launch prompt this session told me to, and I read the stub. Kernel-RO, host-executed — Overseer's hand. Confirm this is covered by `fortkit-88u.6` (read-side injection) or uhvt; if it is not, one bead covering all four.

### 6. Non-blocking, recorded so my gate reasoning is auditable — no mandatory ESCALATE

Under `fort/` the diff touches only `fort/handoffs/` (the Forge's own record surface). `bin/`, `civ/`, `.claude/`, `fort/profiles/`, `fort/scripts/`, `fort/charter.md` and `fort/seats/` are untouched — verified by a path-scoped diffstat. `templates/fort/scripts/` is not among the kernel-RO host-executed paths enumerated in the cycle-7 amendment; it is Forge-writable by design, which is the enforcement layer's own statement that the factory copies are not gate-1 constitution. I note that gate 1's prose ("launchers, permission profiles") reads ambiguously as to the factory copies — that ambiguity is already owned by open bead `fortkit-qj3`, so I cite it rather than file it.

**Threat model:** the change is comment-only in effect, so it bears on no threat. The findings above are all **threat 1, agent accident** — findings 1 and 2 are about a future agent acting on a stale record or an unguarded file, which is the class the charter names as highest-volume and highest-realized-cost. None require the out-of-scope shell-holding human.

--------

## What I verified independently

- Full candidate template read from `bead/vhk.9`. Prompt at :31 names `fort/remember.md`; no `fort/memory` string anywhere; no `saelin`.
- **Exhaustive enumeration** of every `-a ` and `--actor ` token in the candidate template (ripgrep over the file): lines 48, 54, 74, 77, 79 are `-a researcher -s researcher`, line 73 is `--actor researcher`, and there is no other occurrence of either token. That establishes both negative regexes hold, by enumeration rather than by executing them — I could not run vitest (below).
- All seven launcher assertions in `test/researcher-launcher.test.ts:27-47` checked by hand against the candidate bytes; all seven hold.
- `shellcheck --shell=bash --external-sources --source-path=<worktree>` on the candidate template: exit 0, no findings. This is the full delta of verify.sh's shellcheck step, since researcher.sh is the only shell file the diff touches.
- `bin/fort-init:27-39` read directly: `render()` resolves `{{REPO_PATH}}/{{PROJECT}}/{{DATE}}/{{FORT_NAME}}`, the launcher loop covers `emit status mayor forge warden verify` and **not** researcher, and line 39 writes a populated `fort/remember.md`. This is what makes the revert correct and the new header line 2 accurate.
- `scripts/memory-lint.mjs:73-85`: the retired-reference check scans only root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, so reintroducing `fort/remember.md` under `templates/` cannot trip verify.sh's first step — no verifier conflict, and the green stamp is consistent with the revert.
- `git diff --numstat` (template = 3/1), path-scoped diffstat over `fort/ bin/ civ/ .claude/ templates/fort/profiles/`, `git diff --check` (clean), and per-commit `--stat` for all six commits: r1's handoff appears only in 65d1a38 and its stamp a2ffc6d and was not rewritten; r2's was touched once after its stamp, `+2 −0`.
- Sibling headers `mayor.sh:2-4`, `forge.sh:2`, `warden.sh:2` read directly for the F3 comparison.
- `fortkit-uhvt` exists in `.beads/issues.jsonl` on main, with the title quoted in finding 3.
- The four live launcher prompts still naming `fort/remember.md` (finding 5).

## What I took on faith

- **The verifier run.** Both r2 and r3 report `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` exit 0, launcher-observed, 14 files / 150 tests. **I could not reproduce it, for the second review running.** `/tmp/warden-vhk.9` has no `node_modules` and every write I attempted was refused by the permission layer (`touch`, `mktemp -d`); the candidate worktree is EROFS under my mask, so `vitest` died writing `node_modules/.vite-temp`; `tsc` and `biome` invoked directly from the worktree's `.bin` were both refused. This is exactly open bead **fortkit-hn2** ("Warden sessions get nondeterministic tool permissions"), so I record it against that bead rather than filing a new one — but I note that hn2 has now cost two consecutive reviews their independent verifier reproduction, which is evidence for its priority. What I could reproduce, I did: shellcheck on the only changed shell file, and hand-verification of all seven launcher assertions. Unobserved risk is confined to typecheck/lint over four added test lines.
- **`bd` is unavailable** (`failed to open database … read-only file system`), so all bead records came from `.beads/issues.jsonl` in git rather than `bd show`. I could not read uhvt's status or dependencies, only confirm it exists.
- **The r3 handoff's "targeted Vitest (7 tests)" figure** — consistent with the file (2 tests in the first describe, 5 in the second), but I did not execute it.
- **That Proofdelve and Farlantern lack `fort/memory/`.** Both are outside my working directories. Nothing in this verdict rests on it: the fort-init leg is verified in this repo.

**A closing note for the record.** The Mayor's acceptance of my round-one finding is on the bead in plain terms, including the ruling that this was a bead-authoring defect rather than a Forge defect. I concur, and I want the record to say that the Forge implemented what it was told, faithfully, in all three rounds, and that round three delivered every one of the six scoped items. What remains of this bead is a comment and a hardened guard — a small merge, correctly scoped, with the larger question kept alive on uhvt for the Overseer rather than smuggled through here.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: revert lands, guard hardened, template now comment-only vs main; 5 beads incl. stale r2 record + no memory guard

title: Trial-runner robustness: sameDeclarationIdentity string guard; registryCommit stderr silencing (Warden gxr findings 4-5)
description: Warden gxr review (2026-08-10): (4) sameDeclarationIdentity (run-pixellab-trial.mjs:906-915) matches on mutual absence of declarationSha256 — two undefineds compare equal. Unreachable in production today (citizenAppearance always sets it; .d.mts requires it for TS callers) but the runner is untyped .mjs; requiring typeof === 'string' on both sides makes 'a legacy manifest can never satisfy identity' true by construction. title: seat-sandbox: PID-namespace isolation (--unshare-pid + --proc /proc) to close the sibling /proc credential-read bypass
description: Seats run as uid justin sharing the host PID namespace (masks mount --dev /dev but never --unshare-pid or --proc /proc; seat-sandbox.sh:127). A seat can therefore read /proc/PID/environ and cmdline of, or ptrace, sibling processes including a concurrently running unmasked Regent, which bypasses the credential masking (masking ~/.ssh is moot if another process environment is readable). Adding --unshare-pid gives the sandbox its own PID namespace so host/sibling PIDs are invisible; --proc /proc must be added in the same change because Claude Code and Codex introspect their own process tree and a stale/host /proc view would break them. Filesystem flocks are unaffected (forge.sh takes its lock on the host before bwrap; emit.sh flocks an fd on the event file). --die-with-parent composes with --unshare-pid. SO11 NOTE: this closes a reasoned bypass of an existing control rather than a directly observed failure; flagging for Overseer to confirm it clears standing order 11 (charter.md:51) before implementation, priority set low accordingly.
design: In build_mask common path add --unshare-pid and --proc /proc. Verify Claude Code and Codex still start and can read their own process tree; confirm --die-with-parent still reaps on parent exit. Do NOT add --unshare-net (infeasible: every seat is a frontier-API client, mayor/warden/herald/chronicler exec claude, forge execs codex; the verifier also needs network for deps since warden rsync excludes node_modules) or mask SSH_AUTH_SOCK in the lib (breaks SSH fetch/pull for all seats plus Mayor push; keep per-seat as forge.sh:48 does).
acceptance_criteria: Host-side probe confirms a seat cannot read /proc/PID/environ of a sibling host process. All launchers start green; verify.sh green; WARDEN_SMOKE and probe-cycle7 pass.
notes: Scoped-down remnant of a broader namespace-isolation idea. Dropped as infeasible/conflicting: --unshare-net and masking SSH_AUTH_SOCK in the shared lib (SSH is the only auth path since ~/.ssh, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.netrc are masked). gate-1: modifies the kernel enforcement layer.

comments.text:
OVERSEER RULING 2026-08-11 (Mayor session F). Question put: fortkit-e4q closes a
reasoned bypass rather than an observed failure and flagged itself under standing
order 11 — does it clear SO11?

RULED, verbatim as the option was worded and selected: "Does not clear SO11 —
record as accepted residual. Move it into the charter's accepted-residuals list

with how vhk.5.3 was handled and with 'an attacker could' belonging in the threat
model."

Options declined: ruling that the concurrently-running unmasked Regent makes the
path concrete enough to schedule as its own edict; and deferring pending a
measurement without deciding.

PROVENANCE: option text selected by the Overseer, not words typed. Typed
instruction the same turn: "sounds good file it. also yes E1a approved."

CARRIED OUT BY fortkit-gohb, which measures the exposure first because charter.md:27
admits a residual ONLY with a measurement attached, then amends the charter, then
supersedes this bead. The measurement records existence and byte counts only and
never content: reading a live process's environment into a transcript is threat 4
in this fort's own threat model.

REOPENING CONDITION, stated so this ruling does not become permanent by default:
if a seat is ever OBSERVED reading a sibling process's credentials, SO11 is
satisfied by observation and the --unshare-pid + --proc /proc implementation
becomes ordinary work.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Verifiers reproduced, diff and records read. Writing the review record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead `fortkit-o4h`, commit `f69d4a6` ("fortkit-o4h: harden PixelLab trial runner"), 5 files, +190/-35. Work produced by **gpt-5.6-terra** (Forge ladder rung 1, per the launcher's `session.start` event at `fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:524`). GPT-family model, so I specifically hunted the reward-hack signatures — assertions that assert nothing, over-fitted tests, disabled checks, deleted coverage. I found thin tests (finding 6) but nothing dishonest: the removed `assertPreflightBudget` was the bead's own instruction, no assertion was weakened, and the test count moved 82 → 85 with three real new tests.

All nine bead items land. Original 7–10: seed offset (`PIXELLAB_SEED_OFFSET`, integer-validated, safe-integer-checked on both input and sum), `AbortSignal.timeout` on both endpoints, the dead preflight removed with the two real caps retained, and output anchored through `new URL('../assets/trial', import.meta.url)` with `resolve` → `join` at both write sites. Scope-extension 1–3, 7 and the README statement of the Mayor's commit decision are all present. The path anchoring is the diff's best change: it bears directly on threat 1 (agent accident), where a cwd-relative `resolve("assets/trial")` would silently create a stray asset tree under whatever directory the runner happened to be in.

**Gate check (no ESCALATE).** No charter, seat, launcher, or permission-profile file is touched. The diff adds `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-o4h.md`; handoffs are routine seat output, explicitly writable under the kernel mask whose read-only set is `.claude/`, `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`. Gate 1 does not apply. Gate 2: the key is still read from the environment only, `delete`d immediately, and absent from prompts, request bodies, manifest entries, and every new error message — including the seed-offset rejections, which do not echo their input. Gate 3: the Overseer running the paid trial from his own terminal is his action, not a public-facing action taken by this merge.

---

**1. Non-blocking — the walk-frame manifest is still untruthful for 3 of 4 entries, and the animation request now literally says "frame 1 of 4". Worth fixing before the Overseer spends money, not after.**

Scope-extension item 1 asked to "send those fields or stop recording them." The diff sends `offsetWalkCards[0]`'s prompt, negatives, and `n_frames` (`scripts/run-pixellab-trial.mjs:358`). `negativeConstraints`, `n_frames`, `seed`, `action`, `view`, and `direction` are identical across all four walk cards, so those are now truthful everywhere. But `prompt` is not: `walkCard()` bakes a `frame N of 4` clause into each one (`:128`), so the manifest entries for `kethra-walk-east-02/03/04` will record a prompt string the endpoint never received. One request, four recorded prompts, three of them fiction — and nothing in the entry distinguishes the truthful one.

The same root cause produces a second effect: the description now sent to a four-frame animation endpoint reads "…walking east, **frame 1 of 4**, leather apron and hammer…". That is single-frame prompt text steering a multi-frame generation.

One change fixes both. Hoist a single animation description without the frame clause, record it identically on all four entries, and carry the frame index in its own field — the ids already encode it (`kethra-walk-east-01`…`-04`), so the clause in the prompt buys nothing.

Why this is not blocking: `assets/trial/` currently holds only `README.md`, so no false manifest exists in the repo today, and the counterfactual is worse — running the trial on `main` sends *no* description at all and records all four prompts falsely. Merging strictly improves the record. But the bead comment ordered this work to land *before* the trial command precisely because the manifest becomes an append-only provenance record the moment it is committed (standing order 7), and the README this diff adds now names it as exactly that. Fix it in the same window.

**2. Non-blocking — one 30-second timeout for both endpoints gives the four-frame animation call the same budget as a 32×32 glyph.**

`REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (`:29`) is applied uniformly in `request()` (`:246`). The bead asked for a bound so a hung request cannot stall the Overseer's single command, and a bound is correct. My concern is the value and its uniformity: `animate-with-text` returns four 32×64 frames from one call and is plausibly several times the latency of a single glyph. I have no PixelLab latency figures and am not asserting 30s is too short — I am flagging that a too-tight bound converts a working run into a run that aborts after being billed server-side, with no retry, and leaves a partial manifest and partial PNGs on disk. Make it per-call (longer for the animation endpoint) or env-overridable, and include the endpoint in the abort message so the failure names itself.

**3. Non-blocking — the `kethraMaster` guard fires after eight assets have already been paid for.**

`:351` does exactly what the bead asked and converts an undefined-dereference into a clear message. But the harm the finding described — "a rename pays for eight assets then dies" — is untouched: the guard sits after the pixen loop. A one-line assertion at startup that `cards` contains an entry with id `kethra-citizen` fails for free, before the first dollar. Same guard, moved to where it is worth something.

**4. Non-blocking — the handoff's mandatory `Model:` field is wrong, and the mechanism that produced it is unreliable by construction.**

`fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-o4h.md:3` records "GPT-5 Codex". The launcher's event stream records `gpt-5.6-terra`. The handoff schema in `fort/seats/mayor.md:20` makes this field mandatory, and the Warden's seat file makes it a review input for weighting scrutiny — so a wrong value degrades the one signal this seat uses to calibrate. I do not read this as falsification: models routinely misidentify themselves, which is the point. The authoritative record is correct and present, so nothing is lost by merging; the correction is appended per standing order 7, never edited in.

The structural fix is the one worth carrying to every settlement: the launcher already knows the model and already emits it: have it inject the `Model:` line rather than asking the model to self-report an identity it cannot reliably know.

**5. Non-blocking — `scripts/run-pixellab-trial.d.mts` is a type contract TypeScript never checks against its implementation.**

Neither tsconfig includes `scripts/`, and `allowJs` is off, so TS reads the hand-written `.d.mts` and never reads the `.mjs`. The declaration is load-bearing (delete it and typecheck fails) and unverified. A signature drift is invisible to the typechecker; only the runtime tests would catch it, and only for behaviour they happen to assert. Given this repo is the template other forts copy, I'd rather see a `scripts` tsconfig with `allowJs` + `checkJs` than a declaration maintained by hand. Mitigation today is real though: vitest imports the actual `.mjs`, and all four exported functions are exercised.

**6. Non-blocking — the new tests are thin in one specific way: `pngFromBase64` has no positive-path test.**

`test/pixellab-trial.test.ts:80` proves garbage is rejected. Nothing proves a real PNG is accepted. If `PNG_SIGNATURE` were wrong, the suite stays green and every live run dies after paying for the first asset — the failure mode the magic-number check was added to prevent, inverted. (I checked the eight bytes against the PNG spec by inspection: `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A` is correct, and the `data:image/png;base64,` prefix strip is correct. The gap is the test, not the constant.) Separately, `animationRequestBody`'s test uses `toMatchObject` on three of the ten fields; the six fields newly threaded from the card definition — `seed`, `image_size`, `action`, `view`, `direction` — are unasserted, and item 1 above is exactly the kind of thing a fuller assertion surfaces.

---

**Verified independently, in the scratch tree at `/tmp/warden-o4h` after `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`:**

- Node typecheck (`tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json`) — clean.
- Browser typecheck (`tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.browser.json`) — clean.
- Vitest — **10 files, 85 tests, all passing**, matching the handoff's claim exactly. Ran against current source, not a stale build: `noEmit` everywhere and vitest transforms from source.
- ShellCheck over the verifier's full surface (`-x bin/fort-init bin/regent fort/scripts/*.sh fort/scripts/lib/*.sh templates/fort/scripts/*.sh civ/scripts/*.sh`) — clean.
- The main-module guard works in both directions, and this is load-bearing now that the script is importable: the child-process refusal tests still exit 1 with the correct message (guard true when it is the entry point), and the whole suite completes in 2.3s with no network activity (guard false under vitest, so importing the module does not run `main()`, does not read the key, and does not `delete` it from the environment).
- Read every line of the changed `.mjs` for key handling: `readApiKey` is not exported, the key never enters a prompt, body, manifest field, or error string, and the new code adds no path to it.
- `assets/trial/` contains only `README.md` today and is not gitignored — so the README's committed-deliberately statement is accurate and finding 1 is prospective, not already-realised.
- The commit is path-scoped, references the bead id, and the `work.begun`/`work.ended` emissions the bead prescribed are present in the event stream.

**Taken on faith:**

- **Biome lint.** My permission set refused every invocation form I tried; I could not run it. The Forge reports it green, the four other verifier steps I *did* reproduce are green, and the diff's formatting is visibly Biome-conformant — but I did not observe it and will not claim I did. Whoever merges should have seen a full `verify.sh` pass.
- PixelLab's actual request/response contract and latency. No live call was made by the Forge or by me, and no key was read. Whether `description` + `n_frames` are the field names `animate-with-text` expects, and whether 30s is a sane bound, are unconfirmed against the vendor. The first live run is the real test of finding 2.

Findings 1–6 are all filed as beads rather than held against this merge. Finding 1 is the one with a deadline: it should land before the Overseer's trial command, not after the manifest is committed.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: all 9 bead items land; 6 non-blocking findings; walk-frame prompt still 3/4 untruthful — fix before live run

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round one. Bead fortkit-tmu, single commit `29389ff` (`main..bead/tmu`), 5 files, +78/−21. Work produced by **GPT-5.6 as Kethra Anvilmark** (per the appended handoff) — the seat file's reward-hacking flag applies to that vendor, so I checked specifically for weakened assertions, deleted or skipped tests, new `shellcheck disable` pragmas, and scope creep. There are none: every changed assertion is strictly stronger than the one it replaced, and the diff is exactly the four spec items and nothing else.

All four acceptance criteria are met, and each of the four bead items is implemented as specified: the no-write assertion is now `access(root/fort/events)` → ENOENT with no date in it at all (and I confirmed by reading both emitters that `mkdir -p "$dir"` at line 49 is the first filesystem write, after every guard, so the assertion is genuinely load-bearing rather than vacuous); both emitter copies are parameterized under `describe.each` with `{{REPO_PATH}}` substituted; the post-`--` case is pinned, making the shipped comment self-verifying; and empty category is rejected in both copies before any write.

**No blocking findings.**

1. **Non-blocking — the positive test is timezone-fragile, and this diff duplicates the fragility.** `emit.sh writes a valid event...` passes `-T 2026-08-08T12:34:56Z` and then expects `events-2026-08-08.jsonl`, but the emitter derives the filename with `date -d "$ts" +%F` in the *runner's* local zone. Observed, not imagined: `TZ=Pacific/Auckland npm run test` → 2 failed | 64 passed, one failure per copy (it was 1 before parameterization). This matters more than a stray flake because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` deliberately sets `TZ: America/Anchorage` under the step name "Verify outside UTC" — the fort has already declared it cares about non-UTC correctness, and the guard only covers negative offsets. `fort/events/README.md` says the daily filename is "writer-local date… a shard key, not a fact", so the fix is to derive the expected filename the same way rather than to hardcode it. Bead. Related record note, so nothing overstates itself: the bead text says the new assertion "also retires the finding-6 timezone sensitivity" — true of the negative tests, which are now date- and zone-independent; the positive test's exposure survives untouched.

2. **Non-blocking — there is a third emitter copy, and it has no guards at all.** `civ/scripts/emit.sh` (the Regent's, Herald's and Chronicler's emitter) has no category dash-guard, no detail dash-guard, no residual-argument check and no empty-category rejection; only the `[ "$#" -lt 2 ]` arity check. `civ/scripts/chronicler.sh:105` passes the category through a variable (`"$when"`). Bears on threat 1 (agent accident): an unset variable there writes a schema-violating event silently instead of failing loudly — the exact defect finding 5 fixed in the fort copies. Outside this bead's spec and it is a capital-layer file, so routing is the Mayor's call under `civ/covenant.md`. Bead.

3. **Non-blocking — the traveling verifier is broken for every settlement it founds.** `templates/fort/scripts/verify.sh:63` runs `shellcheck -x bin/fort-init fort/scripts/*.sh fort/scripts/lib/*.sh`, but `bin/fort-init` exists only in the factory, never in a founded fort. I confirmed shellcheck exits 2 on a missing path, so a new settlement's verifier fails at the shellcheck step out of the box. Pre-existing and outside this bead, but it is precisely the "one that travels" class this bead is about, in the sibling of a file it edits. Bead.

4. **Non-blocking — the new lint glob stops one directory short.** `templates/fort/scripts/*.sh` does not cover `templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, the kernel-mask library every settlement inherits. Today that is harmless: I diffed it against `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh` and the two are byte-identical. But the template launchers carry `# shellcheck source=fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, pointing at the *fortkit* copy, so if the two ever diverge the template lib is linted neither directly nor by `-x`. One-word fix (`templates/fort/scripts/lib/*.sh`). Bead.

5. **Non-blocking — the template emitter still calls itself Proofdelve.** `templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh:2` hardcodes "Proofdelve event emitter"; `bin/fort-init:27` substitutes only `{{...}}` placeholders, so every fort founded from this template ships an emitter announcing another settlement's name. Should be `{{PROJECT}}`. Cosmetic, but it is in the copy that travels and the file is now under test. Bead. Adjacent: the test substitutes 1 of fort-init's 6 placeholders — correct today (that is the only one in this file), worth keeping in step if more are added.

6. **Non-blocking — test-design nit.** `emit()` now rewrites the emitter into the fort root on *every* call, so the shipped script is no longer executed in place. Behaviour-preserving today (both copies resolve their target from `$PWD` via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, never from their own location — I checked), but it means a future path-dependent resolution bug in the shipped copy could pass here and fail in production. Cheaper and stricter: execute the shipped path directly, materialize only the rendered template, once per suite rather than per call.

7. **Non-blocking — merge mechanics for the Mayor.** The branch is 6 commits behind `main`. Main has not touched `fort/scripts/emit.sh`, `fort/scripts/verify.sh`, `templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh` or `test/shell.test.ts` since the branch point (`32adeb9`), so no code conflict — but both sides appended to the end of `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md`, so expect a textual conflict there. Resolve by keeping **both** entries (standing order 7: append, never prune), and re-run `verify.sh` on the merged tree, since my run covers the candidate, not the merge result. Separately: the dispatch recipe in the bead description ends in a bare `-t` with no value, which the emitter correctly rejects with exit 2; the Forge flagged this honestly in its handoff and used `-t fortkit-tmu`. The recipe in the bead text should be corrected.

**On the human gate, stated explicitly so it is reviewable.** This diff touches `fort/` machinery (`emit.sh`, `verify.sh`, a handoff). I am not escalating under gate 1. Gate 1's literal "fort/ files" cannot be the operative reading — every Forge commit writes a `fort/handoffs/` entry, so that reading would make ESCALATE unconditional and therefore meaningless. The operative set is the one the fort itself enforces and records in `remember.md`: `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, `.claude/` and the launchers, read-only at the kernel and applied by Justin's hand. None of those are touched here; `emit.sh` and `verify.sh` are deliberately seat-writable, and the Overseer specified these exact files in a bead he owns. If Justin reads gate 1 more broadly, this paragraph is where to overrule me.

**Verified independently:** read the complete diff and both emitters in full; confirmed guard-before-`mkdir` ordering by source; `npm run test` → 9 files, 66 tests, all pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean against both `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.browser.json`; `shellcheck -x` over verify.sh's exact new surface including `templates/fort/scripts/*.sh` → no output, and `-f json` on the template emitter → `[]`; reproduced the timezone failure under `TZ=Pacific/Auckland`; confirmed shellcheck exits 2 on a missing path; confirmed `bin/fort-init` renders `emit.sh` through the `{{REPO_PATH}}` substitution the test mirrors; diffed the two `seat-sandbox.sh` copies (identical) and the fort vs. civ emitters (guards absent in civ); confirmed the commit is path-scoped to 5 files with the bead id leading the message, and that main has not touched the four changed code files since the branch point. Ran in the scratch tree after `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, so these are current artifacts, not stale.

**Taken on faith:** Biome lint — `npm run lint` and the biome binary are both denied to my read-only profile, so I could not reproduce that one step; the handoff reports it green after one formatting fix, and both typechecks plus CI give partial cover. Also on faith: the contents of beads `fortkit-so2` and `fortkit-8ib` (`bd` is denied to this seat), so I judged item scoping against the bead text supplied to me, and I did not verify the claimed coordination with 8ib's lint-strategy decision. The handoff's other four factual claims I checked and all hold.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — spec met, verifiers reproduced green (lint unverified); 7 non-blocking findings for beads, none blocking.

title: Ambient v1.3: hash avalanche finalizer, real-stream CLI coverage, stdio-claim diagnosis (Warden x67 findings 2-4)
description: (2) The bit-0 defect was patched at two call sites (>>>8), not at the root: hash() has no finalizer and every other call site reads low bits — Ilva derived that 'pursuit'/'variety' bit-0 are EQUAL for every input, so a variety block's PLACE is fully determined by which escape value fired (%8==6 forces archive pursuits, %8==7 forces walls pursuits). Not a bug today, same class as the fixed one. Principled fix: an avalanche finalizer on hash() (murmur3 fmix32 or equivalent) repairing every call site at once; retest distributions. (3) cliChild() replaces console.log/error with IPC sends, so tests assert what the CLI passes to console, not what reaches a stream; also match-or-hang surfaces as an opaque timeout (Promise.race a rejecting timer), and undrained pipes are a 64KB deadlock shape. (4) Resolve the 'execFile suppresses stdout' mystery — her hypothesis: process.exit() discards pending async pipe writes, truncating exactly the stdout reported empty; test/git.test.ts captures child stdout fine in the same environment. Also consider a [UTC, America/Anchorage] CI matrix instead of Anchorage-only (current pin trades a UTC blind spot for a non-UTC one).
